Smith presented Council with the following options for the Celebration of Lights: - Keep as is along Marina Drive - Move displays throughout the city in the various parks - Move to Cypress Basin Park After some discussion regarding the pros and cons of each option, Council informed staff to move the displays throughout the parks. Downtown parking - allowing residents to park with no 2-hour time limit and Jerry Cox parking lot adding 2-hour parking to the front row After discussion regarding residents being allowed to park along the street with no 2-hour time limit, Council decided that these units are existing and never had parking included therefore they choose not to change at this time. Other discussions included possible paid parking or a future parking garage where the landlord works out an agreement for a paid parking spot. Council also informed staff to leave the Jerry Cox parking lot as is. Pedal Pub Pedal Pub requested to create an Ordinance to have beer and wine only while on the Pedal Pub throughout that specific Entertainment Zone. There was much discussion regarding SC state law not allowing open containers within vehicles with motors. Pedal Pub will do further research on other South Carolina entities that allow such uses. Copperhead Road and Pitch Landing Road Development Hucks said that this item is to discuss potential annexation of property located on Pitch Landing and Copperhead Road. The parent parcel is contiguous to the city limits by way of the Warden Station tract, but like Warden Station, it is outside of the City’s utility service area, which makes this request different from most annexations that Council typically considers. Currently, the property is zoned Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (minimum lot size of ½ acre), SF20 (20,000 sq. ft. lot size) and SF40 (40,000 sq. ft. lot size). If annexed, the City would 109 -- 109 of 174 -- August 17, 2026 11 assume land use jurisdiction and other responsibilities for the property, even though the City would not be providing city utilities to the property. A preliminary conceptual plan shows approximately 129 single-family lots concentrated primarily outside the mapped flood zone. The plan also identifies 39.7 acres of wetlands and 27.2 acres of open space. The applicant has indicated that the flood areas would be proposed for Conservation Preservation zoning upon annexation. The remainder would be requested to come into the City as Medium-Density Residential, or R-2. This plan is just conceptual in nature and has not been submitted for any type of formal review. This concept appears to show a small flood-fill area, so the final extent of any proposed floodplain impacts would still need to be verified through engineering and applicable permitting processes. Additionally, there is a piece of the parcel that currently fronts Highway 701 S, making the entire property contiguous, that would need to be a part of the annexation request; otherwise, the remaining parcel shown here does not satisfy the requirement to be contiguous. Hucks said that the applicant was present to provide more detail, but the main reason for this workshop was to determine whether Council was receptive to considering a formal annexation request, and if so, what information and commitments would be expected before the request moves forward, such as infrastructure requirements or agreements that would need to be a part of the annexation. APPLICANT(S): DCD Investments LLC PIN(s): 369-12-03-0002 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Single Family Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-20) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Light Industrial (LI) BACKGROUND: The applicant is requesting annexation of the subject property in connection with proposed development of the property, which will require connection to City utility services. The property is located on Liz Lane and at the end of Webb Lane. The applicant intends to develop the property as an outdoor storage facility limited to storage of recreational vehicles. A substantial portion of the property is encumbered by a power transmission easement. A Santee Cooper electrical substation is located across Liz Lane from the subject property. The powerline easement may provide some separation between the proposed development area and portions of an adjacent residential neighborhood. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: Most adjacent properties are located within Horry County’s jurisdiction and are zoned Single Family Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF20) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). Adjacent City parcels are zoned City of Conway Residential (R), Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), and Highway Commercial (HC). The surrounding area includes established residential properties, undeveloped land, the power transmission corridor, and the electrical substation located across Liz Ln. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map designates the subject property as Low-Medium Density Residential (R-1). This designation generally supports detached single-family residential development and other uses compatible with low- to medium-density residential development. Per Section 3.2.3 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the R-1 district is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential 130 -- 130 of 174 -- STAFF REPORT First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (A) development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding areas. The requested Light Industrial (LI) zoning classification is not consistent with the Future Land Use Map designation. However, several characteristics distinguish the property from a typical residential development site. The approximately 5.79-acre parcel is located across Liz Lane from a Santee Cooper electrical substation and existing utility infrastructure provide some physical separation between the proposed development area and portions of the adjacent residential neighborhood. The applicant intends to use the property solely for the outdoor storage of recreational vehicles. That use is anticipated to generate less daily traffic, noise, and operational activity than many other uses permitted in the LI district. Appropriate access, screening, buffering, lighting, and operational standards will nevertheless be important due to the proximity of residential properties. Although the requested zoning is inconsistent with the future land use map, the property’s physical constraints, relationship to the existing electrical infrastructure, and the relatively low-intensity nature of the proposed use may provide support for consideration of the LI zoning classification. Staff notes, however, that zoning applies to the property rather than to a particular applicant or development proposal. Approval of the requested LI zoning would allow any use permitted within the LI district, subject to applicable UDO requirements, and would not limit the property exclusively to recreational vehicle storage. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION (and public hearing): If First Reading of the Ordinance to annex the property is approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the requested zoning upon annexation at their October 8, 2026 meeting. TRC RECOMMENDATION / COMMENTS: Any development of the property will require compliance with applicable City requirements for access, screening, buffering, landscaping, lighting, stormwater management, and fire access. Improvements located within the power transmission easement will require approval from the easement holder (Santee Cooper). RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (A) to annex the subject property. title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 9.8.26
text: September 8, 2026 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2026 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem Beth Helms, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jason Perzan, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kelli Thomas, Deputy PIO; Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Becky Graham, HR Deputy Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Katie Dennis, Planner; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 30 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Blain gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (H), granting a non-exclusive franchise agreement to Backwater Bites Mobile Food Truck to operate at the Marina, 4 Elm Street (PIN 367-08-01-0003). B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (D) to annex approximately 0.13+/- acres of property located at 124 Quail Run (PIN 383-09-04-0058) C. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (K), to rezone approximately 0.13 +/- acres of property located at 124 Quail Run from Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district (PIN 383-09-04-0058). D. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (C) to annex approximately 9.7 +/- acres of property located at 2899 E. Hwy 501 (PIN 400-04-02-0002). -- 1 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 2 E. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (L), to rezone approximately 9.7 +/- acres of property located at 2899 E. Hwy 501 from Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PIN 400-04- 02-0002). F. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (B) to annex approximately 1.74+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 and Gardner Lacy Rd, including 101 and 103 Gardner Lacy Rd (PINs 399-01-04-0001, 400-04-03-0001, and 400-04-03-0002). G. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (M), to rezone approximately 1.74 +/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 and Gardner Lacy Road, including 101 and 103 Gardner Lacy Road from Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PINs 399-01-04-0001, 400-04-03-0001, and 400-04-03-0002). H. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (A) to annex approximately 2.56+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501, across from Sioux Swamp Dr. (PIN 326-14-04-0010). I. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (N), to rezone approximately 2.56 +/- acres of property located on Hwy 501, across from Sioux Swamp Drive from Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) & Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PIN 326-14-04- 0010). J. Approval of a Resolution authorizing an appointment to the Solid Waste Technical Advisory Committee K. Approval of a Special Event – Chicora Car Club Car Show – October 10, 2026 L. Approval of August 17, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve the September 8, 2026 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Longevity Awards – August 2026 – 10 Years: Johnny Lewis, Public Utilities; and 20 Years: Jamison Dixon, Public Works – Blain and Emrick presented the longevity awards. B. Presentation of a Proclamation honoring Careteam Plus – Blain presented a Proclamation honoring Johanna Haynes, Executive Director/CEO of Careteam Plus and proclaiming that September 8, 2026 is Johanna Haynes’ Day. -- 2 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 3 PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST READING: A. Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-21 (A), granting a non- exclusive Franchise Agreement for Mister Softee Mobile Food Truck to operate at property located along Peanut Road (PIN 367-01-04-0036). Dennis stated that the applicant is requesting approval for a new Franchise Agreement for Mister Softee. The applicant currently has an active Franchise Agreement which includes Collins Park and the Riverfront Park with the operation times being sunup to sundown 7 days a week. The applicant also agreed to cease operations on days of city approved festivals or special events without prior written permission from the event organizer. For this application the applicant has requested to set up on the vacant lot off Peanut Road near the water tower and operate from sunup to sundown 7 days a week at this location as well. Although staff is not opposed to this request staff does have some concerns. These concerns include the proximity to a heavily traveled vehicular right of way on a daily basis as well as an active pedestrian right of way during holiday festivities and other events, the proximity to an event venue that is most commonly used for weddings and the possibility of conflicting noise from the applicant’s vehicle, as well as the queuing area for the consumers as they wait to order. The applicant did fulfill the requirements of mandatory public notice across three consecutive issues of a local newspaper and the requirements for a public hearing have also been met. There was some discussion as council had concerns with operating during events such as the Farmers Market, location on parcel, 4’ queuing area, number of locations for a food truck to operate, and the distance between food trucks. There was no public input. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Blain to defer first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-21 (A) until more information is obtained from the applicant. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (A), to annex approximately 5.79+/- acres of property located on Liz Lane and Webb Street (PIN 369-12-03-0002). Hucks said that this item is for first reading of the ordinance to annex the subject property on Liz Lane currently zoned Horry County SF20. The annexation is being requested at this time in connection with the proposed development of the property that will require connection to city utilities. The applicant is proposing to develop an outdoor storage facility on the property that will be limited mostly to recreational vehicle storage. This property does have some unusual site characteristics. A substantial portion of the property is encumbered by a power transmission easement, and a Santee Cooper electrical substation is located directly across from this property on Liz Lane. The easement and existing -- 3 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 4 utility infrastructure would provide some separation between the developable area and the adjacent residential neighborhood. Hucks said that tonight’s action is limited to first reading of the annexation ordinance. However, while the requested zoning of Light Industrial is not consistent with the city’s future land use map, which designated the property as Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1), the physical constraints of the property, its relationship to the existing electrical substation, and the low intensity nature of the proposed use may provide some support for considering a nonresidential zoning classification at this location. Hucks said that it is important to note that the zoning would apply to the property – not just to the proposed use, so any use in the Light Industrial district would be applicable to the property, subject to the standards of the UDO and not restricted exclusively to the proposed use of recreational vehicle storage. However, any development of the property will have to comply with the city’s requirements for access, buffering, screening, landscaping, lighting, stormwater, and fire access. Any improvements within the transmission easement would also require approval from Santee Cooper. Hucks stated that if first reading of the ordinance to annex is approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the request and make a recommendation regarding the proposed zoning of Light Industrial at ats October 8 meeting. The request would then be returned to council for further consideration. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property. There was some discussion regarding the easement issue. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (A) annexing property located on Liz Lane and Webb Street. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (B), to annex approximately 0.82+/- acres of property located at 1187 Hwy 501 Business (PIN 367-12-04-0002). Hucks stated that the property is currently vacant and zoned Horry County Highway Commercial. The applicant is requesting the city’s highway commercial zoning upon annexation. The annexation is being requested in connection to proposed commercial development that will require a connection to city utilities. Plans for the project were initially submitted to Horry County for review; however, because the development will require city services, and the adjacent property was recently annexed making this property also contiguous, the applicant must request annexation before a connection to city utilities can be provided. If successfully annexed, the property will be subject to the city’s applicable site plan review and permitting requirements. The property is within the Red Hill community, along a predominantly commercial and industrial portion of the Highway 501 business corridor. Most adjacent properties are zoned Horry County Highway Commercial, with a Heavy Industrial property located directly behind the site. Nearby properties within the city limits are zoned Highway Commercial, Forest Agriculture, and Light Industrial. The requested zoning of Highway Commercial upon annexation is consistent with the city’s future land use map, the property’s current county zoning, and the established development pattern along this portion of the Highway 501 Business corridor. Hucks said that if first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property is approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing and make a -- 4 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 5 recommendation of the proposed zoning at its October 8 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommended approval. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (B) annexing property located at 1187 Highway 501 Business. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (C), to annex approximately 0.60+/- acres of property located at 2997 E. Hwy 501 (PIN 400-04-03-0003). Hucks stated that this request for annexation is for property located at the intersection of Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy Road, which contains an existing Domino’s Pizza restaurant. The property is currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial, and the requested zoning upon annexation is City Highway Commercial, so the existing use would maintain a comparable zoning classification once annexation is complete. The surrounding portion of Highway 501 is primarily commercial and light industrial in nature. Adjacent properties in the county’s jurisdiction are zoned Highway Commercial and Light Industrial. While the city’s future land use map classifies the property as industrial, similar recent annexations in connection with the same future development of the immediate area have been zoned Highway Commercial upon annexation. Hucks said that if first reading of the ordinance annexing the property is approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing and make a recommendation regarding the proposed zoning at its October 8 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of first reading. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-11-02 (C) annexing property located at 2997 E. Highway 501. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: − Deborah Butler – spoke to council regarding the Smith Jones Park – requesting to expand camera coverage, increase police presence, update signage and enforce hours. Also requested a partnership with the city and to schedule a workshop to discuss. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to close public input. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: • This Friday is the 25th Anniversary of 9/11. In addition to the city’s normal tribute, we will be adding our color guard and some additional recognitions, all beginning at 8:46 a.m. Some of the new activities will take place at the Terrace, while others are of course, at the Main Street Bridge. This is one of the most powerful things that we, as a city, do. • Halloween decorating is underway. We started a little bit last week but will be making a major push over the next three weeks. The Big Boogining, the official kickoff event, is October 1 st , with the lineup for the costumed march to start at the new end of the Riverwalk and end at the Town Green. Also, the city’s 3rd party consultants, Spirit of -- 5 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 6 Conway, have been working hard to bring in sponsorships for this year’s Halloween and Christmas seasons. Emrick thanked OrthoSC for being the city’s first presenting sponsor of both Halloween and Christmas. • The Mayor’s Youth Council swearing in is Thursday with 7 new members. • The WWII Memorial at Collins Park will have its ribbon cutting on Monday, November 9th at 11 a.m. • The mayor had a young resident reach out to her about the newly paved section of New Road and how she had seen several turtles that had been run over by cars. She asked if we could put up slow turtle crossing signs and even sent an example of what those signs could look like. Emrick showed on screen and said that there are now four signs on the New Road section asking drivers there to slow down and watch out for turtles. Blain requested a ceremony to honor that resident. • The city has had a number of complaints about the stormwater ponds and other debris left by DR Horton in the Kingston Bay subdivision. We are actively working with both DR Horton and SCDES to make sure that any issues that need to be addressed are. However, like with all matters of enforcement, sufficient time to cure violations must be given prior to writing tickets or more punitive responses. And when there has been a demonstrable effort made toward correction, we allow the offending party leeway to make the corrections. It is not an example of us sitting on our hands and letting bad things happen, it is us trying to work toward a solution that is quicker and more efficient for everyone. • We have a few Workshops tonight, including discussions about the Conway Outpost expansion plans, a potential new franchise agreement offering river tours, further rentals at 5 th and Main, and an update to some of our Fire Stations. We also have two Executive Sessions, one dealing with an old Annexation Agreement and the second about appointments of Boards and Commissions. COUNCIL INPUT: Hardwick − Announced that she is excited to see the holiday decorations. − Asked for an update in the future on the DR Horton and the Country Club Road issues. − Said that it has been a great beginning of school and to continue to watch out for the children and school buses. White − Requested police presence periodically at the community garden. Butler − Requested a conversation about the uniformity of the police vehicles, specifically SRO. − Requested a conversation about the Smith Jones Park as she said that she believes in collaboration and that all citizens need to feel safe. Blain − Commended intern, Drew Sorbello and asked everyone to join in singing Happy Birthday to him. -- 6 of 8 -- September 8, 2026 7 WORKSHOP: Conway Outpost – Tommy Guido presented council with a new proposed plan on the opposite side of the marina store from the boat landing. There was discussion regarding the parking spaces, trees, roof pitch and matching the existing structure, and landscaping. Staff advised Guido to work with Planning on applying to CAB. Discussion regarding Franchise Agreement with Waccamaw River Tours – Rick Lanigan of Waccamaw River Tours introduced his business. Lanigan said that his narrated boat tour has been in existence in Socastee for 13 years. It is a 1 ½ hour eco tour on a 12x40 pontoon boat that seats approximately 46 passengers. He would like to do 1 to 2 trips a day for schools, events, possible happy hour, etc. The boat has a restroom. Lanigan would like to leave in and out of the marina and would need floating docks that are ADA accessible. Council was very interested in the tours. Staff directed Lanigan to Planning to discuss a Franchise Agreement. Discussion on rentals at Fifth and Main – Hillary Howard, Conway Downtown Alive asked council to cease with outside private party rentals at Fifth and Main as there have been numerous incidents in the past involving police and fire. Howard said that they would continue to allow non- profits and government entities to have events at the location. Council agreed to cease with private party rentals. Fire Station Redesign – Chief Perzan presented examples of a few fire stations depicting new doors, and/or windows. Council directed Perzan to go with the red doors and black windows. EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Helms made a motion, seconded by Jordan to enter into Executive Session for the following: (A) Discussion of a Contract regarding an Annexation Agreement [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (2)]; and (B) Consideration of appointments to boards, commissions and committees [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70(A) (1)]. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. RECONVENE FROM EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms to leave Executive Session. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. POSSIBLE ACTION ON MATTERS DISCUSSED IN EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by White to allow the administrator to begin negotiations regarding an annexation agreement. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to reappoint Becky Hubbard, ATAX; Andy Altman, Board of Zoning Appeals; Sandra James, Board of Zoning Appeals; and Lesley Hill, Board of Zoning Appeals. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. -- 7 of 8 -- -- 8 of 8 --

DATA See attached handouts. RECOMMENDATION Authorize approval of Memorandum of Understanding with Coastal Carolina University Department of Public Safety, North Myrtle Beach Police Department, Horry County Police Department, Horry County Sheriff’s Department, Surfside Beach Police Department, and the 15th Judicial Circuit Solicitor’s Office to assist Conway PD for the month of October for Halloween events. 4 -- 4 of 270 -- 5 -- 5 of 270 -- 6 -- 6 of 270 -- 7 -- 7 of 270 -- 8 -- 8 of 270 -- 9 -- 9 of 270 -- 10 -- 10 of 270 -- 11 -- 11 of 270 -- 12 -- 12 of 270 -- 13 -- 13 of 270 -- 14 -- 14 of 270 -- 15 -- 15 of 270 -- 16 -- 16 of 270 -- 17 -- 17 of 270 -- 18 -- 18 of 270 -- 19 -- 19 of 270 -- 20 -- 20 of 270 -- 21 -- 21 of 270 -- 22 -- 22 of 270 -- 23 -- 23 of 270 -- 24 -- 24 of 270 -- 25 -- 25 of 270 -- 26 -- 26 of 270 -- 27 -- 27 of 270 -- 28 -- 28 of 270 -- 29 -- 29 of 270 -- State of South Carolina ) ) County of Horry ) MUTUAL AID AND LAW ENFORCEMENT SUPPORT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF CONWAY AND THE 15th JUDICIAL CIRCUIT SOLICITOR’S OFFICE Whereas, the Law Enforcement and Support Act (the Act), beginning at §23-20-10 et seq. of the State of South Carolina Code of Laws, §23-20-30 provides "Any county, incorporated municipality or other political subdivision of this Stat may enter into mutual aid agreements for the proper and prudent exercise of public safety functions. All agreements must adhere to the requirements contained in §23-20-40"; and Whereas, §23-20-20(4) of the Act defines a Mutual Aid Agreement as "any agreement entered into on behalf of a law enforcement agency in this State for the purpose of providing the proper and prudent exercise of public safety functions across jurisdictional lines, including, but not limited to, multijurisdictional task forces, criminal investigations, patrol services, crowd control, traffic control and safety and other emergency service situations. Such agreements must not be permitted for the sole purpose of speed enforcement"; and Whereas, §23-20-20 also defines the following as: (1) "Law enforcement agency" means any state, county, municipal or local law enforcement authority that enters into an agreement for the procurement of law enforcement support services. (2) "Law enforcement provider" means any in-state or out-of-state law enforcement authority that provides law enforcement services to a law enforcement agency pursuant to this chapter. The primary purpose of this PD is to establish a flexible, master-planned framework capable of accommodating the specialized operational, architectural, and site-design standards of a diverse mix of commercial and premier multifamily occupants. By utilizing a PD format rather than rigid individual districts, the development can integrate varied occupant user prototypes, specialized parking logistics, and distinct site-geometry requirements into a more functional, cohesive ecosystem that standard UDO text cannot dynamically support. Further, the PD format facilitates a more environmentally sensitive site layout by clustering development density onto less impactful upland zones. This framework ensures, to the extent feasible, the preservation of existing on-site undisturbed wetlands as high-value, integrated passive open space and spatial buffers, exceeding the environmental outcomes typical of piecemeal baseline development. Code Ann. § 6-31-10 et seq.), local governments may enter into Development Agreements with property owners or developers to establish the terms and conditions governing development of property. Development Agreements provide certainty regarding certain development rights and applicable regulations while providing a mechanism for establishing infrastructure responsibilities, public benefits, environmental protections, and other obligations associated with development of the property. Under the Act, the permissible term of a DA is related to the acreage of the property. WITNESSETH: WHEREAS, the legislature of the State of South Carolina has enacted the “South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act,” as set forth in Sections 6-31-10 through 6-31-160 of the South Carolina Code of Laws (1976), as amended (the “Act”), attached hereto as Exhibit “A”; and WHEREAS, Section 6-31-10(B)(1) of the Act recognizes that “[t]he lack of certainty in the approval of development can result in a waste of economic and land resources, can discourage sound capital improvement planning and financing, can cause the cost of housing and development to escalate, and can discourage commitment to comprehensive planning”; and WHEREAS, Section 6-31-10(B)(6) of the Act also states that “[d]evelopment agreements will encourage the vesting of property rights by protecting such rights from the effect of subsequently enacted local legislation or from the effects of changing policies and procedures of local government agencies which may conflict with any term or provision of the development agreement or in any way hinder, restrict, or prevent the development of the project. and WHEREAS, the City seeks to protect and preserve the natural environment and to secure for its citizens’ quality, a well-planned and designed development and a stable and viable tax base; and WHEREAS, __________, as trustee of the John Quincy Harrison Trust, (the “Owner”) is the legal owner of the Property (as hereinafter defined) and has given permission to Developer, pursuant to the terms of a valid and binding contract to purchase the Property, to enter into this Agreement with the City; and WHEREAS, the development of the Property and the program for its development presents an opportunity for the City to secure quality planning and growth, protection of the environment, and to strengthen the City’s tax base; and WHEREAS, Developer desires to develop certain real property owned by Developer and Owner, consisting of approximately 120.64 acres, , more or less, located in Horry County, South Carolina, as more particularly shown and depicted on Exhibit “B” attached hereto (the “Property”) for the construction and development of a residential development as generally shown on the master plan attached hereto as Exhibit “C” (the “Master Plan”); and WHEREAS, the City, at the request of the Developer, has annexed the Property and simultaneously approved under an amendment to the zoning ordinances of the City an application for zoning of such Property to the Medium Density Residential (“R-2”) and Conservation Preservation (“CP”) zoning district under the ordinances of the City of Conway, together with this Agreement, on or about the ____ day of ________________, 2026; and WHEREAS, the City desires to insure that in the event the Property is developed in accordance with the zoning referenced herein and above that adequate and appropriate public benefits are provided; and WHEREAS, Developer desires to obtain from the City assurances that (i) the proposed zoning of the Property to R-2 and CP will be approved by the City; (ii) upon its application for development permits, Developer may proceed with the development and construction of the Property or in any portion or phase thereof, in accordance with the zoning designation defined as of the Effective Date; and (iii) such development rights will be vested for the duration of the development of the Property pursuant to the terms of this Agreement; and WHEREAS, this Agreement is being made and entered into between Developer and the City, under the terms of the Act, for the purpose of providing assurances to Developer that it may proceed with its development plan under the terms hereof, consistent with its annexation and approved zoning without encountering future changes in law which would materially and adversely affect the Developer’s ability to develop the Property under its approved zoning, and for the purpose of providing important public benefits and improvements, protection to the natural environment and long term financial stability as well as an increased and more viable tax base to the City; and NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the terms and conditions set forth herein, and incorporated herein by this reference, the mutual covenants of the parties contained herein and other good and valuable consideration agreed to by both the City and Developer, including the public and economic benefits to both the City and Developer by entering this Agreement, and to encourage well planned development by Developer, the receipt and sufficiency of such consideration being hereby acknowledged, the City and Developer hereby agree as follows: 1. INCORPORATION. The above recitals are hereby incorporated into this Agreement, 156 -- 156 of 270 -- 3 together with the South Carolina General Assembly findings as set forth under Section 6-31-10(B) of the Act. 2. DEFINED TERMS. Terms not otherwise defined herein have the meaning set forth in the Act, the provisions of which are incorporated herein by reference. The Code shall mean the South Carolina Code of Laws, 1976, as amended. 3. DEFINITIONS. As used herein, the following terms mean: “Act” means the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act, as codified in Sections 6-31-10 through 6-31-160 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina (1976), as amended; attached hereto as Exhibit “A”. “Code of Ordinances” means the Code of Ordinances for the City, as amended and in effect as of the date hereof, as the same may be amended from time to time, a complete copy of which is on file in the City’s office. “Developer” means Ashton Charleston Residential L.L.C., all its/their permitted assigns, and all successors in title or lessees who undertake developer of the Property as a Developer or who are transferred Development Rights and Obligations. “Developer Default” for purposes of this Agreement, Developer Default shall mean Developer has breached the specific obligations of this Agreement, and, following prior written notice from the City, has failed to cure such breach within thirty (30) days of the date of written notice from the City. Pursuant to the Act, the failure of the Developer to meet the development schedule shall not, in and of itself, constitute a material breach of this Agreement. “Developer Default Remedy” notwithstanding any other remedy that may be available to the City at law, or in equity, as a result of a Developer Default, Developer and the City agree that the City may elect to (i) withhold issuance of building permits until such Developer Default is cured; (ii) seek injunctive relief to stop any such continuing Developer Default, or (iii) any other remedy available at law or in equity. “Development Rights and Obligations” means the rights, obligations, benefits and approvals of the Developer(s) under this Agreement. “Development Schedule” means the development schedule attached hereto as Exhibit “E”. “Development Work” means the periodic operation of development activities on the Property, which include, but are not limited to clearing, grading, erosion control, site work, and landscaping under the terms of a written contract with the Developer. “Effective Date” means the date on which the last of the parties has executed this Agreement. “Horry County Stormwater Design Manual” means the Horry County Stormwater Design Manual as amended and in effect as of the Effective Date, a complete copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit “G” or further amended from time to time pursuant to this Agreement. “Jurisdictional and Non-Jurisdictional Waters of the State of South Carolina and the 157 -- 157 of 270 -- 4 United States” means those areas identified by the United States Army Corps of Engineers (“Corps”) and/or the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (“DES”) or any other applicable governmental authority as wetland areas subject to the regulation of the Corps and/or DES. “Master Plan” means the conceptual master plan attached hereto as Exhibit “C”. “Project” means the residential development envisioned by the Master Plan and approved by the City pursuant to this Agreement and the Code of Ordinances, as the same may be amended from time to time pursuant to this Agreement. “Property” means those parcels of land more particularly shown and depicted on Exhibit “B” attached hereto. “Term” means the duration of this Agreement as set forth in Section 4 hereof. “UDO” means the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance as amended and in effect as of the Effective Date, a complete copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit “H”, or further amended from time to time pursuant to this Agreement. 4. TERM. The Developer represents and warrants that the Property consists of at least 25 acres more or less of “highland” within the meaning given that term by the Act. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date of this Agreement and shall terminate on the date which is five (5) years from the Effective Date except as provide herein. Notwithstanding such termination date, provided that the Developer is not in default (after being provided with notice and opportunity to cure as set forth below) of this Agreement, Developer has diligently pursued development of the Property, and the Project has not been completed, at the conclusion of the initial five-year term, the termination date of this Agreement shall automatically be extended for one (1) additional five (5) year term. At the conclusion of the initial five (5) year extension of the Term, provided that the Developer is not in default (after being provided with notice and opportunity to cure as set forth below) of this Agreement, Developer has diligently pursued development of the Property, and the Project has not been completed, at the conclusion of the initial five-year extension of the Term, the termination date of this Agreement shall automatically be extended for one (1) additional five (5) year term. Notwithstanding the terms and provisions in this Section or elsewhere in this Agreement to the contrary, if a court of competent jurisdiction hereafter determines that the length of the Term, or the provision for extension of the Term set forth above, exceeds the maximum term allowed under the Act and if all applicable judicial appeal periods have expired without such determination being overturned, then the Term of this Agreement relative to all or specific affected portions of the Property shall be reduced to the maximum permissible term under the Act, as determined by a court of competent jurisdiction. 5. FAILURE TO OBTAIN TITLE. Notwithstanding any other provision in this Agreement, if legal ownership has not transferred from the Owner to Developer by December 31, 2027, as evidenced by the recording of a deed in the office of the Horry County Register of Deeds, this Agreement shall automatically terminate, and all obligations of both the City and the Developer shall likewise terminate. 6. DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPERTY. The Property shall be developed in accordance with this Agreement, including the Code of Ordinances, and other applicable land development 158 -- 158 of 270 -- 5 regulations required by the City, State, and/or Federal Government. The City shall, throughout the Term, maintain or cause to be maintained a procedure for the processing of reviews as contemplated by this Agreement and the Code of Ordinances. The City shall review applications for development approval based on the development standards adopted as a part of the Code of Ordinances, unless such standards are superseded by the terms of this Agreement, in which case the terms of this Agreement shall govern. 7. VESTED RIGHTS. This Agreement establishes the zoning classification for the Property as R-2 AND CP, in accordance with the UDO as existing on the Effective Date of this Agreement and continuing throughout the Term of this Agreement, as defined herein. As of the Effective Date, such zoning designations and development rights contained in the UDO are deemed vested in Developer, its successors and assigns, subject to the terms of this Agreement, and the agreements, obligations, and commitments contained herein run with the Property and may not be changed or modified except as provided herein or as allowed by the Act. (A) No future changes or amendments to the UDO or other local ordinances, laws, rules or regulations shall apply to the Property after the Effective Date, and no other legislative enactments shall apply to the Property or this Agreement which have an adverse effect on the ability of Owner to develop the Property in accordance with this Agreement or which have the effect of materially increasing the costs of the improvement of the Property, except as may be provided for in this Agreement or Section 6-31-80 of the Act. (B) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties specifically agree that this Agreement shall not prohibit the application of any building, housing, electrical, plumbing or gas codes, nor of any tax or fee of universal application throughout the City to both new and existing development specifically bound to be necessary to protect the health, safety and welfare of its citizens. (C) Furthermore, the parties acknowledge that the improvements to be made to the Property remain subject to the current requirements of the building codes, land development regulations and the current guidelines for approval by the City as of the Effective Date. 8. CONVEYANCES OF PROPERTY AND ASSIGNMENT OF DEVELOPMENT RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS. The City agrees with Developer, for itself and its successors and assigns, including successor Developer(s), as follows: (A) Conveyance of Property. In accordance with the Act, the burdens of this Agreement shall be binding on, and the benefits of this Agreement shall inure to, all successors in interest and assigns of all parties hereto, except for Excluded Property, as such term is defined below. For the purposes of this Agreement, “Excluded Property” means property that is conveyed by the Developer to a third party and is: (i) a single-family residential lot for which a certificate of occupancy has been issued; (ii) a parcel for which certificates of occupancy have been issued and on which no additional residential structures can be built under local ordinances governing land development; (iii) any other type of lot for which a certificate of occupancy has been issued and which cannot be further subdivided into one or more unimproved lots or parcels under local ordinances governing land development; or (iv) a single-family residential lot which has been subdivided and platted and is not capable of further subdivision without the granting of a variance. Excluded Property shall at all times be subject to the Code of Ordinances of the City, and those 159 -- 159 of 270 -- 6 incorporated in this Agreement. The conveyance by Developer of Excluded Property shall not excuse Developer from its obligation to provide infrastructure improvements within such Excluded Property in accordance with this Agreement. (B) Assignment of Development Rights and Obligations. The Developer, or any subsequent developer, shall be entitled to assign and delegate the Development Rights and Obligations to a subsequent purchaser of all or any portion of the Property. The City understands that any such assignment, partial assignment or transfer by the Developer of the Development Rights and Obligations shall be non-recourse as to the assigning Developer. Upon the assignment or transfer by Developer of the Development Rights and Obligations, then the assigning Developer shall not have any responsibility or liability under this Agreement. For purposes of this Section 7, the following activities on the part of Developer shall not be deemed “development of the Property”: (i) the filing of this Agreement and the petitioning for or consenting to any amendment of this Agreement or the Code of Ordinances; (ii) the subdivision and conveyance of any portions of the Property to the City as contemplated under this Agreement; (iii) the subdivision and conveyance of the portion of the Property designated as “Open Space” on the Master Plan to any person or entity so long as the same shall be restricted in use to “open space”; (iv) the subdivision and conveyance of portions of the Property, not to exceed in the aggregate one (1) acre, more or less, provided that such conveyances shall be deed-restricted to single-family residential use; (v) the conveyance of easements and portions of the Property for public utility purposes; (vi) the conveyance of portions of the Property to public entities in the case of any road realignments or grants of road rights of way; (vii) the marketing of the Property as contemplated under this Agreement; and (viii) any other activity which would not be deemed “development” under the Act. 9. MASTER PLAN. The Master Plan attached hereto as Exhibit “C” is the design plan for a residential project for the Property and is submitted herein for descriptive and illustrative purposes only. Notwithstanding anything contrary contained herein, the zoning classification set forth herein shall govern the development of the Property. Design criteria and layout illustrated on the design plan and any other exhibits or materials supporting the development of this Property shall be understood to be flexible, and, as of the Effective Date, incomplete and may be revised, modified and changed by the Developer with the approval of the City, provided such revisions or changes do not conflict with the zoning classification for the Property set forth herein. The final design of development and use as well as types and locations may be shifted, adjusted and added to satisfy market objectives and be consistent with the overall general plan of development, as set forth herein. 10. DEVELOPMENT SCHEDULE. Although the nature of this long-term project prevents the Developer from providing exact completion dates, and market forces may shift and thereby accelerate or slow down development, the general phases of Development are set forth and described in Exhibit “E” (the “Development Schedule”). Developer shall keep the City informed of its progress with respect to the Development Schedule as a part of the required Compliance Review process set forth in Section 16 below. Pursuant to the Act, the failure of the Developer to meet the development schedule shall not, in and of itself, constitute a material breach of this Agreement. 11. EFFECT OF FUTURE LAWS. Consistent with Section 6 herein, Developer shall have vested rights to undertake development of any or all the Property in accordance with the Code of Ordinances and the UDO, as amended and in effect at the time of this Agreement, for the entirety of the Term. Future enactments of, or changes or amendments to the Code of Ordinances and the UDO, which conflict with this Agreement shall apply to the Property only if permitted pursuant to the Act 160 -- 160 of 270 -- 7 and agreed to in writing by the Developer and the City. The parties specifically acknowledge that building moratoria or permit allocations enacted by the City during the Term of this Agreement or any adequate public facilities ordinance as may be adopted by the City shall not apply to the Property except as may be allowed by the Act or otherwise agreed to in writing by the Developer and the City. The parties specifically acknowledge that this Agreement shall not prohibit the application of any present or future building, housing, electrical, plumbing, gas or other standard codes, of any tax or fee of general application throughout the City, provided such fees are applied consistently and in the same manner to all single family properties within the City. Notwithstanding the above, the City may apply subsequently enacted laws to the Property only in accordance with the Act and this Agreement. 12. INFRASTRUCTURE AND SERVICES. The City and Developer recognize that the majority of the direct costs associated with the development of the Property will be borne by the Developer. The Developer certifies that the services will be in place (or if not fully in place, the cost of construction secured by an irrevocable letter of credit or certified check posted pursuant to any applicable federal, state or local regulations (the “Current Regulations”)) at the times provided herein. The Developer shall comply with applicable Laws and all provisions of this Agreement and obtain approvals from the City and other applicable governmental entities before installing any infrastructure. Notwithstanding the provisions referenced above, nothing in this Agreement shall preclude the City and Developer from entering into a separate utility agreement for cost-sharing of water transmission systems or sewer transmission systems when such agreement may be of mutual benefit to both parties. Nothing herein shall be construed as precluding the City from providing potable water to its residents in accordance with applicable provisions of laws. (A) Rights-of-Way. The Developer or a third party shall at its expense develop and provide roads, streets, and other transportation and drainage related facilities and infrastructure within the Project and pursuant to and at such time required by the development plans for the Project and/or the Current Regulations. Such facilities may be transferred by the Developer, in fee or by easement, subject to proper dedication and acceptance by the City. Rights-of-way may also remain privately owned and maintained. (B) Storm Drainage System. All stormwater runoff, drainage, retention and treatment improvements within the Property shall be designed in accordance with the Code of Ordinances and the Horry County Stormwater Design Manual effective as of the date of plan submission. All stormwater runoff and drainage system structural improvements, including culverts and piped infrastructure, will be constructed by the Developer and dedicated to the City. Upon final inspection and acceptance by the City, the Developer shall provide a one-year warranty period for all drainage system structural improvements within the Project. Retention ponds, ditches and other stormwater retention and treatment areas will be constructed and maintained by the Developer and will not be accepted or maintained by the City. To the extent applicable, any stormwater, water service, tap or similar impact fees shall be capped or determined as of the Effective Date and shall not change during the Term of this Agreement except as specifically allowed for herein. (C) Solid Waste and Recycling Collection. The City shall provide solid waste and recycling collection services to the Property on the same basis as is provided to other residents and businesses within the City. Payment for such services to the City by Developer is required in 161 -- 161 of 270 -- 8 return for such service for each owner within the Property. The City reserves the right to contract with a third party, which may include another governmental entity, and the City reserves the right to terminate or discontinue such service(s) to any owner of any portion of the Property until such payment(s) have been made. (D) Police Protection. The City shall provide police protection services to the Property on the same basis as is provided to other residents and businesses within the City. (E) Fire Services. The City shall provide fire services to the Property on the same basis as is provided to other residents and businesses within the City, which services may be provided by way of a mutual services agreement with Horry County, if the City is unable to provide such services directly. (F) Emergency Medical Services. The City shall provide emergency medical services to the Property, on the same basis as it provided to other residents and businesses within the City, which services may be provided by way of a mutual services agreement with Horry County, if the City is unable to provide such services directly. (G) School Services. The City neither provides nor is authorized by law to provide public education facilities or services. Such facilities and services are now provided by the Horry County School District. (H) Private Utility Services. Private utility services, including electric, natural gas, and telecommunication services (including telephone, cable television, and internet/broadband) shall be provided to the site by the appropriate private utility providers based upon designated service areas. All utilities on the Property shall be located underground and shall be placed in locations approved by the City to reduce or eliminate potential conflicts within utility rights-of-way. (I) Streetlights. Developer shall install or cause to be installed streetlights within the Project. To the extent that the City provides the same benefit to other similarly situated neighborhoods within the City, the City shall contribute toward the monthly cost for each streetlight in an amount equal to the costs for the base street light fixture offered by the utility provider. The remaining monthly cost for each streetlight, including additional charges associated with an enhancement street light fixture, if any, shall be borne by the Developer. (J) No Donation of Acreage for Sewer Plant Expansion. The City shall not require, mandate or demand that, or condition approval(s) upon a requirement that the Developer donate, use, dedicate or sell to the City or any other party for public purposes any portion of the Property or any other property owned by the Developer or any affiliate of the Developer for sewer plant expansion by the City, provided, however, that this provision shall not be deemed to preclude the City from requiring additional sewer pump station facilities, to subsequently be dedicated and conveyed to the City. (K) Donation of Land for Greenway and Public Park. The Developer shall convey approximately twenty-one (21) acres of land for the City’s Crabtree Greenway and public park as shown on the attached Exhibit D (the “Park Property”). Developer will convey the land to the City within ninety (90) days of obtaining legal ownership of the Park Property. Conveyance of the Park Property shall be by limited warranty deed, which shall provide for an automatic reverter to 162 -- 162 of 270 -- 9 the Developer if the Park Property ceases to be used as a greenway or public park. In addition, Developer may reserve sewer and drainage easements across the Park Property as necessary to develop the Project. Developer agrees to install a paved walking trail approximately 2600 linear feet long with an 8' width consisting of 2" of asphalt, 6" of base course, and 12" of prepared subgrade along the eastern side of Altman Branch beginning at Highway 378 and terminating on the southern side of Crabtree Canal. Any additional improvements to the Park Property or the Crabtree Greenway shall be the responsibility of the City. (L) Easements. Developer shall be responsible for obtaining, at Developer’s cost, all easements, access rights, or other instruments that will enable the Developer to tie into current or future water and sewer infrastructure on adjacent properties. (M) Ponds and Lakes. As an obligation, Developer shall install pond(s) or lake(s) as shown on the approved Master Plan for the Property. The exact location, alignment, and name of any public road or improvements required both within the Project or off-site, shall be subject to review and approval by the City Planning Commission as part of the subdivision platting process. The Developer shall be responsible for maintaining all public roads until such roads are offered to, and accepted by, the City for ownership and maintenance. Upon dedication to the City, the Developer shall provide a three-year warranty period for such public roads. As an obligation, Jurisdictional and Non-Jurisdictional Waters of the State of South Carolina and the United States within the Project which are not mitigated, filled or otherwise modified, shall be surrounded by an undisturbed water quality buffer of not less than Twenty-Five (25) feet in width. The City finds that the development permitted or proposed herein is consistent with the City’s comprehensive plan and land development regulations and provides public benefits. The purpose of this Agreement is to (i) provide a mechanism whereby the development of the Property can offset the cost of increased demand on the City caused by the development of the Property, and (ii) agree on certain public benefits. 15. Developer shares this commitment and therefore agrees to abide by all provisions of federal, state and local laws and regulations for the handling of storm water. 16. COMPLIANCE REVIEWS. Developer, or its assigns, shall meet with the City, or its designee, at least once per year during the Term to review development completed in the prior year and the development anticipated to be commenced or completed in the ensuing year as compared to the Development Schedule. The City shall provide written notice to the Developer of the date for such compliance review not less than Five (5) business days in advance, provided such notice shall not be applicable to standard reviews and inspections otherwise performed by the City as to the improvement of the Property. The Developer must demonstrate good faith compliance with the terms of this Agreement. The Developer, or its designee, shall be required to provide such information as may reasonably be requested by the City. The Development Schedule attached to this Agreement is only a projection, and Developer’s obligation at each respective Compliance Review shall be to reconcile the projected Development Schedule attached to this Agreement with the actual schedule of development for the Project at each respective Compliance Review. Failure to meet the Development Schedule attached to this Agreement shall not constitute a default hereunder. 17. DEFAULTS. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 5 above, Developer shall continuously and diligently proceed with Development Work on the Property. Developer’s failure to proceed with Development Work on the Property for a period of more than Six (6) months, other than as a result of Force Majeure, as defined in Section 8 above, shall constitute a default hereunder 164 -- 164 of 270 -- 11 on the part of Developer. In the event of a default, the City shall provide written notice to Developer of such default, and Developer shall have a period of Thirty (30) days in which to cure a default by commencement of Development Work with regards to the next portion of the Property to be developed in accordance with phasing plan of the Project. The failure of the Developer to comply with the terms of this Agreement shall constitute a default, entitling the City to pursue such remedies as deemed appropriate, including withholding the issuance of building permits in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement, specific performance and the termination or modification of this Agreement in accordance with the Act; provided however no termination of this Agreement may be declared by the City absent its according the Developer the notice and opportunity to cure in accordance with the Act. 18. ORDINANCE: #ZA2026-09-08 (J) AGENDA SECTION: First Reading ISSUE: First reading of an ordinance to rezone approximately 120.71 +/- acres of property located along Hwy 378 APPLICANT(S): Kingston Engineering, agent PIN(s): 337-00-00-0023 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Medium Density Residential (R-2) and Conservation Preservation (CP) districts BACKGROUND: City Council approved first reading of the annexation ordinance for the subject property at its May 4, 2026 meeting. Planning Commission is now being asked to hold the required public hearing and provide a recommendation to City Council regarding the appropriate zoning upon annexation. The subject property contains approx. 120.71+/- acres and is located along Hwy 378, and is currently within Horry County’s jurisdiction, where it is zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). The property is located within the City’s utility service area, and future development of the property will require connection to City water and sewer services. Concurrent with the annexation request, the applicant has submitted a Development Agreement outlining the proposed development of the property. The applicant intends to develop the site for single-family residential purposes and is requesting Medium-Density Residential (R-2) zoning for the developable portions of the property. The associated Development Agreement is being considered separately and establishes the proposed development framework, public benefits, and other obligations associated with the project. Portions of the property contain mapped flood hazard areas, wetlands, and other environmentally sensitive features. Consistent with the City’s policy of protecting floor-prone and environmentally sensitive areas that may be unsuitable for residential development, staff recommends that these areas be zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation to provide long-term protection of those areas and limit development where environmental constraints exist, and for the 21 acres proposed to be conveyed to the City to be entirely zoned Conservation Preservation as well. The City’s adopted Pathways and Trails Plan identifies a future greenway or trail connection through this property. As proposed, the accompanying Development Agreement contemplates conveyance of approximately 21 acres of property to the City for installation of the trail, and further negotiations to include construction of the trail by the developer prior to conveyance. These proposed public benefits are part of the Development Agreement. 188 -- 188 of 270 -- STAFF REPORT First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (J) SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: The subject property is adjacent to a mix of institutional, residential, commercial, and undeveloped land, including: • To the rear: Conway High School (Institutional – IN) and two vacant parcels zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) • Along Radio Lane: properties zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and Low/Medium-Density (R-1); and All other adjacent properties are located in the County’s jurisdiction and zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map designates the majority of the property as Medium-Density Residential, with a portion of the Highway 378 frontage identified as Highway Commercial (HC). The requested R-2 zoning is generally consistent with the Future Land Use Map for the majority of the property and reflects the applicant’s intent to develop the site for residential purposes. The proposed CP zoning for flood-prone and environmentally sensitive areas is also consistent with the City’s policy of protecting areas that may be unsuitable for residential development. Planning Commission should note that the Hwy 378 frontage is identified as HC on the Future Land Use Map. However, the applicant is not currently proposing commercial development as part of the zoning request or associated Development Agreement. Planning Commission may consider whether the proposed R-2 zoning is appropriate for the frontage based on the applicant’s stated residential development intent, surrounding conditions, and the overall zoning framework proposed upon annexation. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION (and public hearing): Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their August 6, 2026 meeting and recommended approval of the proposed zoning upon annexation. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (J) to zone the subject property R-2 and CP upon annexation. APPLICANT(S): Zhuang Lin PIN(s): 382-02-04-0002 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) BACKGROUND: The applicant is requesting annexation of the subject property to facilitate reconnection to City utility services. A restrictive covenant related to annexation has been recorded on the property since 1997. According to Horry County land records, a new manufactured home was permitted on the property in 2017. The property also contains an existing single-family dwelling and several accessory structures. A significant portion of the property is located within the AE Flood Zone. Although Weldon Lane is a public roadway, the public road does not extend directly to the subject property. Access to the property is provided by a 50-foot right-of-way/easement extending across privately owned properties. Accordingly, the subject property does not have direct frontage on a public roadway. If annexed, the subject property would be the first property along this portion of Weldon Lane to be incorporated into the City limits. Staff has concerns regarding annexation due to the property’s access limitations, its location relative to existing City development, the extent of the property located within an AE flood zone, and the potential challenges associated with extending municipal services and regulatory responsibilities to the property. Based on these conditions, staff does not believe annexation of the property is in the City’s best interest at this time. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: Adjacent properties are primarily located within Horry County’s jurisdiction and zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). Two (2) nearby properties within the City limits are zoned Conservation Preservation (CP). The surrounding area is predominately wooded and low-density in character, with limited residential development. 257 -- 257 of 270 -- STAFF REPORT First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-10-05 (B) COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map designates the subject property as Conservation Preservation (CP), reflecting the presence of flood-prone and environmentally sensitive areas and the general development character of the surrounding area. Per Section 3.2.15 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the CP district is intended to provide open space and recreational opportunities while protecting environmentally sensitive and flood-prone areas from development that could adversely affect the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The requested Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) zoning is not consistent with the future land use map designation for the property. Additionally, a significant portion of the property is located within the AE flood zone, further supporting consideration of the property’s environmental and development constraints. TRC RECOMMENDATION / COMMENTS: None at this time. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Disapprove First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-10-05(B) to annex the subject property.
