title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 8.17.26
text: August 17, 2026 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem Beth Helms, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Justin Jordan, Larry White. ABSENT: Julie Hardwick. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jason Perzan, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kelli Thomas, Deputy PIO; Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Jamie Givens, Public Utilities Superintendent; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Lynn Smith, HR Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 30 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: White gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Approval of MOUs with various agencies to assist Conway Police Department for the month of October B. Approval of Special Event – Coastal Carolina Homecoming Parade – November 6, 2026 C. Approval of August 3, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve the August 17, 2026 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Employee of the Month – August 2026 – Givens presented the Employee of the Month award to Bryan Bird, Public Utilities Construction Inspector/Line Locator. -- 1 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 2 B. Presentation of a Proclamation – America the Entrepreneurial – Blain read the America the Entrepreneurial Proclamation. C. Presentation of the Bullard Save a Life Club Award – Representatives from ED Bullard Co. presented Captain Jeromy Herndon with a challenge coin and the Bullard Save a Life Club Award; and Firefighter Dallas Watts and Firefighter Stephen Gleason with challenge coins for saving an individual’s life while using a thermal Bullard imager on May 30, 2026. D. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 67.49 ± acres of property located on Mill Pond Road, Church Street, Camelot Street, Carolyn Street, and Lochwood Lane to a Planned Development (PD) district and consider a proposed Development Agreement for commercial and multifamily residential development (PINs 338-00- 00-0037, 338-07-04-0015, 338-07-01-0033, 338-00-00-0015, and a portion of 338-08-03- 0064). Hucks stated that this item is for discussion of a proposed redevelopment of approximately 67.5 acres, generally located along Mill Pond Road, Highway 501/Church Street, Camelot Street, Carolyn Street, and Lochwood Lane. The properties are currently zoned Highway Commercial and Low/Medium-Density residential, or R-1, and the applicant is proposed to rezone the properties to a Planned Development District to allow for a coordinated mixed-use redevelopment of the site. The proposal includes a fairly significant commercial component along with multifamily residential development. A development agreement is also being proposed in conjunction with the PD. That agreement is still in draft form and is intended to address the development parameters, infrastructure responsibilities, public improvements, and other obligations and public benefits associated with redevelopment of the property. Hucks said that no approvals are being considered tonight and that this is being brought before Council as an early discussion item so that Council has an opportunity to see the overall concept and provide any feedback before the request moves further through the formal review and public hearing process. Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on both the proposed Planned Development zoning and the proposed Development Agreement on September 3. Assuming they make a recommendation, the items would come back to Council on September 21. Additionally, while not part of Planning & Development’s review, Hucks said she did want to mention that the applicant has indicated that they intend to pursue a TIF district and a Municipal Improvement District, or MID, in connection with the project. Those would be evaluated separately, but they are part of the applicant’s overall redevelopment proposal. There was some discussion regarding wetlands, open space, future tenants, Mill Pond Road, MID or TIF, and workforce housing. PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST READING: A. Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (H), granting a non- exclusive franchise agreement to Backwater Bites Mobile Food Truck to operate at the Marina, 4 Elm Street. Wilkerson stated that Eric Jordan, operating as Conway Outpost LLC, holds a lease agreement with the City of Conway to maintain the marina building, parking lot, and immediate grounds. Section 4-o of the lease outlines the lessee’s intent to -- 2 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 3 introduce a rotation of food trucks to diversify the marina store’s offerings. Per the agreement, all food trucks must comply with current city requirements, including proper location, licensing, and inspection. Mr. Jordan is requesting authorization to operate a mobile food truck, Backwater Bites, seven days a week at 4 Elm Street. In alignment with Section 5-a of the lease agreement, the applicant acknowledges that food trucks will not be permitted to operate during any approved special events in the area. There was no public input. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Blain to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (H), granting a non-exclusive franchise agreement to Backwater Bites Mobile Food Truck to operate at the Marina, 4 Elm Street. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (I), approving a Development Agreement (DA) for approximately 120.71 +/- acres of property located along Hwy 378 in connection with annexation and rezoning of the property into the City of Conway (PIN 337-00-00-0023). Hucks stated that this proposed development agreement is being considered in conjunction with the annexation and zoning upon annexation of the property, which is the following item on the agenda to be considered. Hucks gave a brief overview, saying that a development agreement is authorized under state law and establishes certain rights and obligations of the City and developer associated with development of the property. In this case, the proposed agreement would provide certain vested development rights for an initial 5-year term while also establishing infrastructure responsibilities, environmental protection, public improvements, and negotiated public benefits. The current draft of the agreement addresses a number of those items. Some of the more significant provisions include the conveyance of approximately 21 acres to the City for park and trail purposes, including construction of approximately 2,600 linear feet of an 8-foot wide paved multi-use trail; roadway and utility connections to adjacent properties; transportation improvements that may be required as a result of the traffic study (not yet submitted), SCDOT, or the City; protection of environmentally sensitive areas, and negotiated treatment of the City’s tree preservation and mitigation requirements. Hucks said that the agreement before Council tonight remains a working document. The Developer recently provided a revised draft, and staff and the City’s legal counsel have reviewed it and provided a list of comments and suggested revisions. Several substantive matters still need to be finalized before final consideration. These include the timing and financial assurance for transportation and other required improvements; timing and conditions associated with the park property and trail improvements, the extent of the proposed tree mitigation relief and how future changes to the Master Plan would affect that relief, and several environmental, infrastructure, assignment, and enforcement provisions. The traffic impact analysis has also not yet been provided, so the specific transportation -- 3 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 4 improvements that may ultimately be required as a result of the development are not yet known. Hucks said that Planning Commission held the first required public hearing on August 6 and recommended approval of the proposed development agreement, with the understanding that the details of the agreement would ultimately be negotiated between the developer and Council. Tonight is Council’s required public hearing and consideration of first reading. Staff recommends that Council conduct the public hearing and consider first reading with the understanding that the Agreement remains subject to continued review and final revisions before it is presented for final consideration. There was discussion regarding the need for first reading if the details of the agreement are still being negotiated upon and it was decided that if the issues are not worked out at second reading the Ordinance can be deferred until such time as the details are all addressed. There was no public input. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (I), approving a Development Agreement for property located along Highway 378, PIN 337-00-00-0023. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (J), to rezone approximately 120.71 +/- acres of property located along Hwy 378 from Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Medium Density Residential (R-2) and Conservation Preservation (CP) districts (PIN 337-00-00-0023). Hucks stated that this annexation and zoning request is for the Harrison tract just discussed in conjunction with the Development Agreement. The property consists of approx. 120.7 acres and is located along Highway 378. It is currently zoned Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture. The proposed zoning upon annexation is R-2 and CP. Council approved first reading of an ordinance annexing the subject property on May 4. Planning Commission held the public hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at its August 6 meeting, recommending approval of R-2, and CP zoning for the AE flood zone areas, as proposed. The breakdown of the zoning would be approximately 86.4 acres zoned R-2 and 32.3 acres zoned CP upon annexation. This proposed zoning is intended to work in conjunction with the Development Agreement Council just considered. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of the proposed zoning. -- 4 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 5 Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (J) rezoning property along Highway 378 (PIN 337-00-00- 0023) as presented. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (K), to rezone approximately 0.13 +/- acres of property located at 124 Quail Run from Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district (PIN 383-09-04-0058). Hucks stated that this is for the proposed zoning upon annexation for approximately .13 acres located at 124 Quail Run in the Quail Creek Village subdivision. Council approved first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property on July 20. The property contains an existing single-family residence and is currently zoned Horry County SF-10. The proposed zoning is R-1, which is consistent with the zoning applied to the other properties within this subdivision that have been annexed into the City. The future land use map identifies the property as medium-density residential; however, staff believes R-1 is appropriate given the existing single-family use and surrounding zoning pattern. Planning Commission held the required public hearing on August 6 and recommended approval. Hucks said that staff also recommended approval. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (K) rezoning property located at 124 Quail Run to City of Conway R-1. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (L), to rezone approximately 9.49 +/- acres of property located at 2899 E. Hwy 501 from Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PIN 400-04-02-0002). Hucks said that with Council’s permission, she could present this item and the next item together (Ordinances #ZA2026-09-08 (L) and #ZA2026-09-08 (M). Hucks stated that these involve separate ordinances because not all of the properties are contiguous with one another, but they do have the same applicant and are associated with the same potential future development project. Together, these requests involve approximately 11.23 acres along Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy Road. Council approved first reading of the ordinances annexing the subject properties on July 20. The applicant is now requesting the properties be zoned Highway Commercial upon annexation. The larger property is approximately 9.49 acres at 2899 E. Hwy 501. It’s currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial. The proposed zoning of Highway Commercial is also consistent with the City’s future land use map. The second group of properties consists of approximately 1.74 acres along Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy Road, including 101 and 103 Gardner Lacy Road. These properties are currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial and Limited Industrial. The City’s future land use map designates those properties as Industrial, so the requested zoning of Highway Commercial is not directly consistent with the future land use map; however, the properties are located within an established commercial and light industrial area along the Highway 501 corridor, and staff believes Highway Commercial is compatible with the existing development and zoning pattern in the area. These properties are being assembled as part of a future commercial redevelopment involving several surrounding properties. At this time, however, no site redevelopment plans have been submitted for review. Planning Commission held the -- 5 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 6 required public hearing on both items at their August 6 meeting and recommended approval of the Highway Commercial zoning of the properties upon annexation. Hucks said that staff also recommended approval on both items. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (L) rezoning property located at 2899 E. Hwy. 501 to City of Conway HC; and Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (M) rezoning property located on Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy, including properties at 101 and 103 Gardner Lacy Road to City of Conway HC. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (M), to rezone approximately 1.74 +/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 and Gardner Lacy Road, including properties at 101 and 103 Gardner Lacy Road from Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PINs 399-01-04-0001, 400-04-03-0001, and 400-04-03-0002). See previous motion. E. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (N), to rezone approximately 2.56 +/- acres of property located on Hwy 501, across from Sioux Swamp Drive from Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) & Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district (PIN 326-14-04- 0010). Hucks stated that this property is approximately 2.56 acres along Highway 501, adjacent to property annexed into the City a few years ago, also zoned Highway Commercial upon annexation. Council approved first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property on July 20. The property is currently vacant and zoned a combination of Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture and Highway Commercial. The requested City zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial. This annexation is requested primarily to facilitate the future construction of a public right of way through the property that would provide access to adjacent properties previously annexed into the City. No site development plans have been submitted at this time. The City’s future land use map designates the Highway 501 frontage of the property as Highway Commercial and the remainder as Low/Medium-Density Residential. While the requested zoning is not entirely consistent with the future land use map, it is consistent with the Highway 501 frontage and the existing city zoning pattern in this area. Planning Commission held the required public hearing on August 6 and recommended approval. Hucks said that staff also recommended approval. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (N) rezoning property located on Highway 501, across from Sioux Swamp Drive to City of Conway HC. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. F. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-10-05 (A) to annex approximately 26.98 +/- acres of property located at 605 Century Circle (PIN 383-00-00-0344). Hucks stated the applicant is requesting annexation in connection with a proposed track and field complex for Coastal Carolina University Athletics. Upon annexation, the proposed City zoning is Institutional, which is consistent with the City’s future land use map designation -- 6 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 7 for the property and with the proposed university athletic use. If Council approves first reading of the ordinance annexing the property, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the proposed zoning of the property at their September 3 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-10-05 (A) annexing property located at 605 Century Circle. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. G. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-10-05 (B) to annex approximately 2.23 +/- acres of property located at 1643 Weldon Lane (PIN 382-02-04-0002). Hucks stated that if approved this would be the first property along this portion of Weldon Lane to be annexed and most of the surrounding property remaining in the county is largely wooded, and undeveloped. Although Weldon Lane is a public road, the public roadway does not extend to the property. Access is provided via a 50-ft right of way or easement crossing privately owned properties, so the property does not have direct frontage on a public road. Additionally, a significant amount of the property is within the AE flood zone and the City’s future land use map designates the property as Conservation Preservation. The requested zoning of R-1 upon annexation is not consistent with that designation. Hucks said that due to the limited access, location relative to the existing City development pattern, environmental constraints, and the potential challenges associated with extending city services and regulatory responsibilities into this area, staff recommended disapproval of this requested annexation. There are also two Executive Sessions, one dealing with a contract for Riverfront Development and the second about appointments of Boards and Commissions. Goldfinch discussed the need for impact fees saying that state law handcuffs the city’s ability to utilize that impact fee and thinks the city should take this need to the statehouse and ask for help. Goldfinch said that smart development is to let the people that are moving here and have never contributed to this environment share in that funding. Emrick said that in the Country Club case the impact fee is the wrong tool because you have a developer that took something in good condition and ruined it. The developer is obligated to fix it, and the problem is what they have ruined is not on the city’s property or in the right of way. Emrick said that is an issue and then said impact fees would be to make improvements because of the development not to fix things that have been broken. The parent parcel is contiguous to the city limits by way of the Warden Station tract, but like Warden Station, it is outside of the City’s utility service area, which makes this request different from most annexations that Council typically considers. Currently, the -- 10 of 12 -- August 17, 2026 11 property is zoned Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (minimum lot size of ½ acre), SF20 (20,000 sq. ft. lot size) and SF40 (40,000 sq. ft. lot size). If annexed, the City would assume land use jurisdiction and other responsibilities for the property, even though the City would not be providing city utilities to the property. A preliminary conceptual plan shows approximately 129 single-family lots concentrated primarily outside the mapped flood zone. The plan also identifies 39.7 acres of wetlands and 27.2 acres of open space. The applicant has indicated that the flood areas would be proposed for Conservation Preservation zoning upon annexation. The remainder would be requested to come into the City as Medium-Density Residential, or R-2. This plan is just conceptual in nature and has not been submitted for any type of formal review. This concept appears to show a small flood-fill area, so the final extent of any proposed floodplain impacts would still need to be verified through engineering and applicable permitting processes. Additionally, there is a piece of the parcel that currently fronts Highway 701 S, making the entire property contiguous, that would need to be a part of the annexation request; otherwise, the remaining parcel shown here does not satisfy the requirement to be contiguous. PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) BACKGROUND: The subject property, identified as Lot 8 of the Buccaneers Cove Subdivision near Hwy 544, was transferred to the current owners on April 29, 2026. The annexation request is being submitted to facilitate a name change on the City utility service account. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: Properties located to the side and rear of the subject properties have been within the City limits since the early 2000’s. The parcel directly behind the subject property is zoned Institutional (IN) and contains multi-family units that primarily serve students attending Coastal Carolina University. Buccaneers Cove is mostly developed with single-family residential uses. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map identifies the property as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Per Section 3.2.3 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-1 district is to preserve and expand areas for low- to medium-density detached single-family residential development within the City of Conway. The district is intended to maintain a relatively spacious residential character, promote quiet and livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses incompatible with the surrounding residential environment. The proposed zoning upon annexation is consistent with both the Future Land Use Map and the surrounding development pattern. SECTION 1. FINDINGS OF FACTS: WHEREAS, Section § 5-3-150, Code of Laws of South Carolina (1976) as amended, provides a method of annexing property into a city or town by a petition signed by all persons owning real estate in the area requesting annexation; and WHEREAS, A proper petition has been filed with the City of Conway by one hundred percent (100%) of the freeholders owning one hundred percent (100%) of the assessed value of the contiguous property herein described, petitioning for annexation of the property to the City of Conway under the provisions of SC Code of Laws, Sec. § 5-3-150(3); and WHEREAS, The area comprising said property is contiguous to the City of Conway and meets all statutory requirements for annexation; and WHEREAS, It appears to City Council that annexation would be in the best interest of property owners and the City. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Mayor and Council of the City of Conway, South Carolina, duly assembled and with authority of same, pursuant to Sec. § 5-3-150, Code of Laws of South Carolina (1976), as amended, the following described property is hereby annexed to and made part of the City of Conway, to wit: Approximately 0.55+/- acres of property identified by PIN: 382-13-01-0001 and located at 916 Buccaneers Cove. This annexation includes all waterways, roads, and rights-of-way adjacent to the property. For a more specific description of said property, see attached map(s). SECTION 2. ORDINANCE: N/A AGENDA SECTION: Consideration ISSUE: Recommendation on selection of design professionals to assist in drafting the Transportation Element of the Comprehensive Plan update. BACKGROUND: On May 15, 2026, the City of Conway advertised publicly to select a firm to provide professional design services for the Transportation Element of the Comprehensive Plan update. The City seeks to develop a Transportation Element that establishes a practical, implementable, and forward-looking framework for transportation planning and mobility improvements throughout the community. The City’s goals for this planning effort include, but are not limited to: • Improving connectivity throughout the City for vehicles, pedestrians, bicyclists, and alternative transportation modes. • Enhancing transportation safety and accessibility for all users. • Supporting coordinated growth and land use planning. • Identifying transportation improvements needed to accommodate future development and population growth. • Improving roadway efficiency, traffic flow, and network connectivity. • Expanding and improving pedestrian, bicycle, greenway, and pathway connections. • Supporting economic development and neighborhood accessibility. • Preserving and enhancing the character and quality of life of the Conway community. • Developing practical implementation strategies and prioritized recommendations. • Ensuring the Transportation Element functions as an integral component of the City’s Comprehensive Plan update effort. Proposals were required to be submitted to the City no later than June 20, 2026. Four firms submitted proposals, and were ranked based on the following criteria: • The firm’s qualifications and project team submitted. (Maximum 20 Points) • Applicant’s previous experience with grant-funded projects (Maximum 10 Points) • Demonstrated ability to meet project deadlines. Proposed work schedule. Timeframe for delivery of service. (Maximum 15 Points) 146 -- 146 of 147 -- STAFF REPORT Selection of Transportation Element • Demonstrated ability of key personnel and/or construction management experience. (Max. 15 Points) • Similar projects completed within past three (3) years (Maximum 15 Points) • References of past clients (Maximum 15 points) • Financial responsibility and stability (Max. 10 Points) Firms submitting proposals and their respective scores are listed below (average of scores from review team): 1. Bolton & Menk: 90 2. Collins Engineering and Design: 77 3. WSP: 89 4. Kimley-Horn: 91 Staff reviewed and scored the submittals in July, and Kimley-Horn scored the highest. Should City Council approve the hiring of Kimley-Horn, the City would enter into negotiations for a contract for services. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Staff recommends selection of Kimley-Horn to provide professional design services for the City of Conway Transportation Element and authorize the City Administrator to enter into contract negotiations. 147 -- 147 of 147 --

Hucks presented this item and the next item on the agenda together since they are companion annexation requests for the same project. Hucks stated that these requests are to annex approximately -- 2 of 5 -- August 3, 2026 3 0.62 acres at 908 Buccaneers Cove and approximately 0.55 acres at 916 Buccaneers Cove. The properties are immediately adjacent to one another and are proposed to be incorporated into a Planned Development project already undergoing the annexation and rezoning process. These annexations are being requested so that the entire development site is within the city’s jurisdiction and considered as a single project. Hucks said that if first reading is approved Planning Commission will hold the required public hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at its August 6 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of first reading for both annexation ordinances. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (F) annexing 908 Buccaneers Cove and Ordinance #ZA2026- 09-08 (G) annexing 916 Buccaneers Cove. See previous motion. CONSIDERATION: Consideration of approval on the selection of a firm to provide professional services for the Transportation Element of the Comprehensive Plan update. Hucks said that this item is for consideration of the selection of a firm to assist staff with preparation of the Transportation Element of the City’s Comprehensive Plan. Transportation is consistently one of the most significant issues raised by residents and planning partners. Because of its importance, and because transportation planning required specialized technical expertise, this element of the comprehensive plan would benefit from outside, independent assistance. This selected firm will help the city take a comprehensive, citywide look at transportation and develop practical, prioritized recommendations that will be developed through that planning process. The city received proposals from 4 qualified firms. A staff review team evaluated and scored the proposals based on the criteria included in the solicitation for services, and Kimley-Horn received the highest overall score. Hucks said that staff recommended selecting Kimley-Horn and authorizing the City Administrator to negotiate a contract for services, in accordance with the city’s purchasing requirements. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Jordan, to approve the awarding of the contract to Kimley-Horn and authorized the City Administrator to negotiate a contract for the Transportation Element services. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Goldfinch congratulated staff on bringing forth a valuable tool for the city’s transportation needs. White asked if the city had used this firm before. Hucks said yes. Blain asked if SCDOT would be involved. Hucks said yes, that they would be involved in lots of the conversations to provide advice. Graduation is held at the outset of the evening, and told Council if they planned to attend to arrive by 5 p.m. • There has been a little bit of rain since council last met and it has helped with drought conditions. In mid-July the levels were below 6’, which is about 3’ lower than normal. In January it dropped below 5’ for reading. The levels are back up now to consist of high tide crests slightly above 8’ which is still low, but much closer to normal than we have been for a while. Still in a drought, but the summer rains are finally helping. • During the month of August, the city’s Recreation team is holding free swimming lessons at Smith Jones Pool. To take advantage of these lessons, you must sign up in person at the Sports and Fitness Center. • Emrick said that several months ago, a resident who lives on 10th Avenue came to see him at City Hall about a problem that they had noticed on their section of 10th Avenue. They live on the divided section between Lakeland and Oak Street and had noticed delivery drivers and others travelling on the wrong side of the divided median. They looked at Google Maps, which had incorrect map directions showing it as two separate, parallel roads. Emrick said that he contacted Google, they made the changes and he thought all was well. The same resident came to see him a few weeks after the map update and told him it was still happening even after the map update. After researching it briefly and discussing it with staff, Emrick said that he directed the city Public Works crews to put down three Thermopane arrows on both sides making sure oncoming traffic knew which direction travel was to take place. The homeowner called him to thank him, and all appeared to be fine. Over the last few weeks, however, some have been inundated with angry calls and emails that the six arrows spaced out over three blocks had destroyed the aesthetic beauty of this stretch of road. Emrick said that he has now directed staff to remove the arrows, and trusts that drivers have learned which way to travel down 10 th Avenue. • This year is the 25th Anniversary of 9/11. The city memorializes this day every year with the raising and lowering of the ladder trucks on either side of the Waccamaw Memorial Bridge, while representatives of the American Legion wave flags on the bridge. This year, the police and fire departments are adding some additional elements to the event. • Emrick informed council that at the next meeting during workshop there will be a discussion regarding the parking lot at Jerry Cox as he has had some requests that the front row be 2-hour parking as people are parking all day. • Emrick said that this agenda was one of the shortest, but the next one will not be and that the next meeting is scheduled to interfere with Horry County Schools’ orientations. The subject property is currently part of a larger tract containing split zoning of Conservation Preservation (CP) and Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The split zoning was originally established due to the presence of environmentally-sensitive areas and flood-prone land associated with portions of the tract. Under the City’s Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), split zoning of parcels is generally prohibited except in circumstances involving environmentally sensitive lands, where Conservation Preservation (CP) zoning is utilized to protect those areas. The proposed 10-acre subdivision area appears to be located outside of the environmentally sensitive portions of the parent tract and is intended to be combined with the adjacent Conway Christian School property, which is currently zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Rezoning the proposed subdivision area to R-1 would prevent the creation of a split-zoning condition on the newly combined parcel and maintain consistency with the zoning of the adjoining school campus. A large portion of the remaining tract will continue to contain flood-prone and environmentally sensitive areas currently zoned Conservation Preservation (CP). SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: The subject property is located adjacent to existing Conway Christian School campus and is surrounded by a mix of residential development, school/institutional uses, and undeveloped land. While the proposed R-1 zoning is not identical to the Medium-Density Residential designation shown on the Future Land Use Map, it represents a less intensive residential classification than currently contemplated for the property. The proposed zoning is intended to facilitate the combination of the property with the adjacent Conway Christian School campus, which is currently zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). BACKGROUND: Sec. 5.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) currently permits the non-commercial keeping of livestock or fowl as an accessory use within the Rural Residential (RR), Rural Agriculture (RA), and Forest Agriculture (FA) zoning districts, subject to specific acreage, containment, and operational standards. The ordinance also contains limited exceptions for certain properties zoned FA and educational facilities located within the Institutional (IN) zoning district. As the City continues to grow through annexation and development, portions of the City now include or may include in the future, large residential properties exceeding twenty (20) acres in size. While these properties may be located within zoning districts that permit single-family detached dwellings, the current ordinance does not provide a mechanism for property owners to keep livestock or fowl for personal enjoyment, sustenance, passive agriculture activities, or similar non-commercial purposes unless the property is located within the RR, RA, or FA zoning districts. The proposed amendment would establish an additional allowance for properties containing twenty (20) acres or more and a single-family detached dwelling as the principal use. Such properties would be eligible to keep livestock or fowl regardless of the underlying zoning district, provided the district permits single- family detached dwellings and the property contains a single-family detached dwelling as the principal use. Livestock and fowl permitted under this provision would remain subject to all applicable requirements of Sec. 5.2.5, including standards related to acreage, animal type, containment, setbacks, nuisance prevention, and prohibitions on commercial operations. In addition to the substantive amendment, the proposed ordinance reorganizes Sec. 5.2.5 to improve readability, administration, and ease of interpretation. The current ordinance is organized primarily by animal type, which can make it difficult for property owners and staff to determine where certain permissions, restrictions, and exceptions apply. The proposed amendment restructures the section by zoning district and applicability, incorporates definitions for key terms, consolidates related standards, and clearly identifies exceptions and special circumstances. These changes are intended to make the ordinance more user-friendly while preserving the City’s existing regulations regarding nuisance prevention, animal containment, setbacks, and non-commercial use limitations. 100 -- 100 of 335 -- Staff finds that the proposed amendment provides reasonable accommodation for large residential properties while maintaining the City’s existing standards intended to protect neighboring properties from potential nuisances and adverse impacts. The proposed twenty (20) acre minimum ensures that the allowance is limited to properties of sufficient size to support the keeping of livestock or fowl in a manner that remains compatible with surrounding development patterns. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing and recommended approval of the proposed amendments at their June 4, 2026 meeting. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the Ordinance at its June 15, 2026 meeting. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (S) to amend Article 5 – Supplemental and Accessory Uses, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to the requirements for Noncommercial Keeping of Livestock or Fowl, establishing an exception for parcels twenty (20) acres or greater in size and containing a single-family dwelling. Hucks stated that currently livestock and fowl are generally permitted only within the Rural Residential (RR), Rural Agriculture (RA) and Forest Agriculture (FA) zoning districts, subject to various standards and limitations. In the FA district, the ordinance has an exception carved out that allows noncommercial keeping of livestock or fowl on property 5 or more acres, without a principal structure, for property owners who wish to build accessory structures on the property for the keeping of these animals. As the city continues to annex larger tracts of land, staff has encountered situations where properties containing several acres of land and containing a single-family residence are located in zoning districts that do not currently allow livestock or fowl for personal, non-commercial purposes. The proposed amendment would create a limited exception for properties that: contain at least 20 acres; contain a single-family detached dwelling as the principal use; and are located within a zoning 162 -- 162 of 335 -- June 15, 2026 8 district that permits single-family detached dwellings. Under the proposed amendment, those property owners would be allowed to keep livestock or fowl for personal, non- commercial purposes, regardless of the underlying zoning district so long as the zoning district permits single-family detached dwellings and contains a single-family detached dwelling. Importantly, all existing requirements would remain in place, including standards related to acreage, setbacks, containment, nuisance prevention, animal type, and the prohibition of commercial agriculture operations. The amendment also reorganizes the ordinance for clarity by grouping requirements based on zoning district and applicability, making the section easier for both property owners and staff to interpret and administer. The new brick entrance and archway are nearly complete. • At the last Council meeting there was a concern raised about removing geese in Riverfront Park and other public spaces downtown. Federal permits are required to remove geese without running afoul of the Federal Migratory Bird Treaty Act. The City of Conway is a Bird Sanctuary by ordinance and within the Bird Sanctuary ordinance there is a provision that if the birds congregate in such numbers that they constitute a menace or nuisance there are ways to abate the nuisance. Relocation is also not considered a particularly effective long-term solution, as geese often return to their original habitat or are replaced by other geese attracted to the same environmental conditions. As a result, wildlife professionals generally recommend habitat modification, public education, and population management techniques over relocation. The most suitable solution is to plant more landscaping materials along the seawall in the open grass area of Riverfront Park. The geese are drawn to open field with an unobstructed view of the water. So, obstructing the view may deter them from habituating in Riverfront Park. That is staff’s recommendation currently. The intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations for automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic environment of the City. Although the Light Industrial zoning does not directly match the parcel’s HC Future Land Use designation, staff finds that LI zoning is appropriate based on the property’s longstanding use for tractor and heavy equipment sales and service, the current heavy equipment sales and rental operation, and the presence of nearby properties designated for industrial uses. The proposed LI zoning would avoid creating a legal nonconforming use upon annexation and would provide a zoning classification that more accurately reflects the existing and historic use of the property. STAFF ANALYSIS: While the Future Land Use Map designates this specific parcel as HC, nearby (and adjacent) properties are designated for industrial uses, and the surrounding areas includes a mix of commercial, industrial, and agricultural properties. Staff recognizes that Council has generally expressed a preference for Highway Commercial zoning along the Hwy 501 corridors due to their visibility, access, and importance as major commercial gateways. However, the subject property has historically operated as a tractor and heavy equipment sales and service facility. The current use is substantially similar, if not identical to, the prior use of the property and was established while the property remained under Horry County jurisdiction. The City recently amended the UDO to define Heavy Equipment and to identify the zoning districts in which the use (Heavy equipment sales and service) is appropriate. Based on those amendments, heavy equipment sales and service is more appropriately classified as a light industrial use rather than a typical highway commercial use. If the property were annexed and zoned HC, the existing heavy equipment sales and rental business would become a legal nonconforming use. This would allow the use to continue but would limit the property owner’s ability to expand or modify the use in the future. Staff does not believe creating a legal nonconforming use upon annexation is the most appropriate zoning outcome when the existing use is longstanding, legally established, and more closely aligned with the Light Industrial district. ISSUE: Recommendation to award the contract for construction of the Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Docks to H, K, & W Marine Construction. BACKGROUND: The Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Ferry Project is identified as a priority project in both the Riverfront and Downtown Master Plan for Conway (2017) and the Conway Pathways and Trails Plan (2022). Throughout the planning process, residents consistently ranked a river crossing among their highest priorities through public meetings, engagement sessions, and online surveys. The project also supports the goals outlined in the City's Comprehensive Plan and aligns with Coastal Carolina University's Bicycle Advisory Committee vision of creating a well-connected bicycle and pedestrian network linking downtown Conway with Coastal Carolina University. The project will enhance quality of life by providing a safe, scenic, and accessible connection for pedestrians and cyclists across the Waccamaw River. Today, the only river crossing is the historic Waccamaw River Memorial Bridge (US 501 Business), which is narrow and presents significant safety concerns for pedestrians and bicyclists. This project offers a safe alternative while expanding recreational opportunities and improving access to employment, education, parks, and downtown amenities. The project includes construction of ADA-accessible permanent and floating docks, connected by a passenger ferry capable of transporting pedestrians and bicycles across the approximately 300- foot-wide Waccamaw River. Once across the river, users will travel approximately 1,921 linear feet of elevated wooden boardwalk through wetlands and wooded areas before reaching Depot Road. From there, trail connections will eventually provide access to Waccamaw River Park and ultimately Coastal Carolina University, located less than three miles away. The ferry itself will become more than transportation, it will be an attraction and community icon. The vessel will be named "The Spirit," reflecting Conway's welcoming character while allowing the City to celebrate each season through rotating holiday themes and decorations. The name also lends itself naturally to community branding and marketing with the tagline "Catch the Spirit," reinforcing Conway's identity as a community that celebrates every season. 327 -- 321 of 335 -- The contractor will be responsible for providing all required structural engineering, structural design of the boardwalk and dock system, and any additional geotechnical investigations necessary to support the final design. The South Carolina Department of Transportation is also scheduled to improve and resurface Depot Road. The selected contractor will coordinate construction activities with SCDOT's contractor, King Asphalt, during portions of the project. The City publicly advertised for bids, and the following proposals were received: 1. Cooper Tacia: a. Total Cost: $6,900,899.00 2. H, K, & W Marine Construction: a. Total Cost: $2,486,088.00 3. IPW Construction Group: a. Total Cost: $5,292,727.00 4. Rakes Building & Maintenance Contractors LLC DBA Blutide Marine Construction: a. Total Cost: $2,811,721.00 5. Sellers General Construction LLC: a. Total Cost: $3,318,698.16 Staff reviewed each proposal for responsiveness, qualifications, and project requirements and recommends awarding the contract to H, K, & W Marine Construction as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. Upon approval by City Council, staff will immediately begin contract negotiations and proceed with project execution. Funding for the project has been secured through a combination of State Parks, Recreation and Tourism (PRT) funding, Hospitality Tax funding, and a grant from the Waccamaw Community Foundation. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends awarding the contract for construction of the Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Docks to H, K, & W Marine Construction in the amount of $2,486,088.00 and authorizing the City Administrator to negotiate and execute the necessary contract documents. title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 7.20.26
text: July 20, 2026 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, JULY 20, 2026 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem Beth Helms, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jason Perzan, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kelli Thomas, Deputy PIO; Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance Director; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Lynn Smith, HR Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Allison Williams, Finance Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 35 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Butler gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (A) to annex approximately 1.93+/- acres of property located at 235 Singleton Ridge Rd (PIN 383-10-03-0025). B. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (L) to rezone approximately 1.93+/- acres of property located at 235 Singleton Ridge Rd (PIN 383-10-03-0025) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district upon annexation. C. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (B) to annex approximately 0.96+/- acres of property located at 3372 Hwy 378 (PIN 370-03-02-0003). D. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (M) to rezone an approximate 0.96+/- acres of property located at 3372 Hwy 378 (PIN 370-03-02-0003) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district upon annexation. -- 1 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 2 E. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (F) to annex approximately 1.78+/- acres of property located at 321 Rainwood Rd (PIN 324-07-03-0006). F. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (N) to rezone approximately 1.78+/- acres of property located at 321 Rainwood Rd (PIN 324-07-03-0006) from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF40) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. G. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (G) to annex approximately 0.65+/- acres of property located at 3154 W. Hwy 501 (PIN 326-15-02-0001). H. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (O) to rezone approximately 0.65+/- acres of property located at 3154 W Hwy 501 (PIN 326-15-02-0001) from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district upon annexation. I. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (I) to annex approximately 71.82+/- acres of property located behind Lake Busbee and adjacent to New Rd (PIN 368-00- 00-0019). J. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (R) to assign the Conservation Preservation (CP) zoning designation to approximately 71.82+/- acres of property located behind property commonly referred to as Lake Busbee and adjacent to New Rd upon annexation into the City of Conway (PIN 368-00-00-0019). K. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (P) to rezone an approximate 10+/- acre portion of 110+/- acres of property located on Cultra Rd and Oak Street, and adjacent to Conway Christian School (PIN 325-00-00-0011) from the Medium- Density Residential (R-2) district to the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. L. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (S) to amend Article 5 – Supplemental and Accessory Uses, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to the requirements for Noncommercial Keeping of Livestock or Fowl, establishing an exception for parcels twenty (20) acres or greater in size and containing a single-family dwelling. M. Approval of a special event – Public Safety Day – October 3, 2026 N. Approval of a special event – Rivertown Reindeer Run – December 5, 2026 O. Approval of a Resolution accepting dedication of roadways & drainage and the financial guarantee for the roadway warranty for Maple Grove, Ph 1 subdivision (Autumn Maple Drive, Red Maple Drive, Samarus Court, Acer Court, Crimson Maple Drive) -- 2 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 3 P. Approval of June 15, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve the July 20, 2026 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Employee of the Month - July 2026 – Hucks presented the Employee of the Month award to Charlotte Peterson and Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planners. B. Presentation of Longevity Awards – June 2026 – 5 Years: Daraius Moultrie, Police; 5 Years: Joseph Lajoie, Fire; 10 Years: Bradner Kister, Solid Waste; and 10 Years: Brian Keith, Public Utilities. Emrick and Helms presented the longevity awards (Moultrie, Lajoie and Keith were absent). C. Presentation by Conway Chamber of Commerce – Morgan McDonnell – McDonnell updated Council on Riverfest and thanked the city for all their support. FINAL READING A. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (H) to annex approximately 0.53+/- acres of property located at 550 Dunn Shortcut Rd (PIN 337-08-02-0021). Hucks stated that this ordinance is for final reading of annexation of property at 550 Dunn Shortcut Road. The next item concerns the same property and is an ordinance to zone this property R-1 upon annexation. Hucks said that if council prefers, those items can be presented together. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by White to combine Ordinance #ZA2026- 07-20 (H) and Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (Q). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Hucks said that the annexation request was submitted by the property owner after a name change to the existing city utility account triggered the annexation requirement. The property contains an existing single-family residence and is adjacent to the Woodcreek subdivision. As council may recall, Planning Commission recommended approval of the proposed zoning upon annexation but also requested that council consider the property owners’ concerns. Council approved first reading of the annexation ordinance on May 18 and first reading of the ordinance to zone the property to R-1 was approved on June 15. The property owner has also submitted a letter requesting that council deny the annexation due to the circumstances surrounding the application and the anticipated financial impact. Based on the city’s adopted policies, utility service requirements and consistency with prior annexation decisions, staff continued to recommend approval. Hucks then said that annexation is ultimately within council’s legislative discretion. Goldfinch voiced his opposition in the annexation saying that changing from husband to wife, due to death, on the utility bill was not the intent of the ordinance and said that he feels this was an exception to the rule. -- 3 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 4 Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (H) and Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (Q). Hardwick stated that council should follow the ordinance with consistency to be fair and equal to all, and that policies are in place for a reason. Butler reiterated and confirmed with staff that most of the parcels surrounding this one are all within the city limits and that eventually this parcel will be annexed into the city. Blain agreed with Goldfinch that when the policy was written it was not the intent to require annexation when it involved husband and wife. Helms asked staff to look at changing the ordinance when it involves spouses. Vote: Blain, Goldfinch, Helms, Jordan and White voted yes. Hardwick and Butler voted no. Motion to deny carried 5-2. B. Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-07-20 (Q) to rezone approximately 0.53+/- acres of property located at 550 Dunn Shortcut Rd (PIN 337-08-02-0021) from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. This ordinance was combined with previous item. See above motion. FIRST READING: A. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (G) to rezone approximately 0.24+/- acres of property located at 500 W. Cox Ferry Rd (PIN 382-04-04-0012), from Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF20) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Peterson stated that this request is for zoning upon annexation of approximately 0.24 acres located at 500 West Cox Ferry Road. The property is currently in Horry County and is zoned Residential, no mobile homes allowed, SF20. Upon annexation, the applicant is requesting City of Conway R-1 zoning. Annexation and the subsequent rezoning have been submitted to facilitate a name change for the property’s city utility account, Restrictive Covenants for the property were recorded on April 9, 2026. The property contains an existing single-family residence, and the annexation request was submitted in accordance with the city’s utility policies due to a name change on the city utility service account. The surrounding area is primarily residential. The only adjacent property currently within the city limits is located across West Cox Ferry Road and is zoned R. The city’s future land use map identifies the property as R-1 and the proposed zoning is consistent with the future land use map, the existing residential character of the area, and the surrounding development pattern. -- 4 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 5 Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (G) zoning the property at 500 W Cox Ferry Road to R-1 upon annexation. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (H) to rezone approximately 0.58 acres of property located at 921 Buccaneer’s Cove (PIN 382-13-01-0007), from Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF20) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Alvarez stated that the first reading of this ordinance to annex the property located at 921 Buccaneers Cove was approved at the June 1 council meeting. The annexation request was submitted in accordance with the city’s utility policy requiring annexation for connection to city utility services. The property is currently zoned Horry County SF20 which requires a minimum lot size of 20,000 square feet and does not allow mobile homes. The requested zoning upon annexation is R-1. The request is consistent with the future land use map which designates the property as R-1. It is also consistent with the zoning of adjacent parcels that have been within the city limits since the early 2000s. The parcel directly behind the subject property is located within the city limits zoned Institutional and contains multi- family housing that primarily serves students attending CCU. Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their July 9 meeting and recommended approval of the proposed R-1 zoning upon annexation. Staff also recommended approval of the R-1 zoning. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (H) zoning the property at 921 Buccaneer’s Cove to R-1 upon annexation. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (I) to rezone approximately 1.26+/- acres of property located at 158 Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN 399-01-04-0005), from Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that this is a request to zone the subject property at 158 Gardner Lacy Road to LI upon annexation. The property is currently zoned LI by Horry County and contains an existing commercial building occupied by Southern Sun Awnings, a long-established metal fabrication and shade solutions business. The proposed zoning is consistent with the existing use and the city’s future land use map. Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their July 9 meeting and recommended approval of the LI district upon annexation. Staff also recommended approval. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (I) zoning the property at 158 Gardner Lacy Road to LI upon annexation. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (J) to rezone approximately 10.51+/- acres of property located at 1151 Hwy 501 (Bus.) (PIN 367-00-00-0010), from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) districts to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district upon -- 5 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 6 annexation. Hucks stated that this request is to zone the subject property LI upon annexation. Council approved first reading of the ordinance to annex on June 15. The property fronts Highway 501 Business and Highway 90 and has historically been used for tractor and heavy equipment sales and service. The current heavy equipment sales and rental business was legally established under Horry County’s jurisdiction before the annexation request was submitted. The future land use map designates the property as HC, so the requested zoning is not consistent with that designation. However, the city recently amended the UDO to adopt revised use standards, classifying heavy equipment sales and service as an industrial use, permitted within the light and heavy industrial zoning districts. LI is the least intensive zoning district that permits the existing use. Zoning the property HC would immediately make a legally established longstanding use nonconforming upon annexation and restrict its ability to expand or modify its operations. Staff believes the LI district is appropriate because this is not a proposal to introduce a new industrial use to an undeveloped property on Highway 501 Business. It recognizes the property’s historic and existing use, which predates annexation, and is also compatible with the mix of commercial and industrial uses in the surrounding area. Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their July 9 meeting and recommended approval of the LI district upon annexation, Staff also recommended approval. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (J) zoning the property at 1151 Highway 501 Business to LI upon annexation. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. E. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-08-03 (K) to rezone approximately 0.44+/- (total) acres of property within the Riverwood at Sherwood Forest subdivision, located on Country Club Dr. and Graham Rd (PIN 324-16-04-0082, a portion of PIN 324-16-04-0077, and a portion of PIN 324-16-03-0045) from the Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. Hucks stated that this rezoning request is limited to incorporating a 10-foot strip of the adjacent lot and adjacent landscape buffer areas into the existing open space tract. The affected areas would be rezoned from R-1 to R zoning district so that the entire expanded open space tract has consistent zoning. Initially, the applicant proposed rezoning the entire open space tract to R1; however, at staff’s request, the proposal was revised in the opposite direction maintaining the open space as R and rezoning the small adjoining areas to match it. The request to rezone these areas does not increase density, create additional lots, or modify the approved development pattern. Planning Commission held the public hearing on the request at their July 9 meeting and ultimately recommended approval but asked that staff inquire further on the outstanding roadwork. There were residents who spoke in opposition to the request; citing concerns about the condition of Country Club Drive. Hucks said that staff understand the concerns regarding Country Club Drive, and those issues need to be resolved. However, the rezoning request is unrelated to the outstanding roadwork and does not grant additional development rights that what already exist. Delaying or denying the request does not change the developer’s existing obligations or prevent development that is otherwise approved. Staff believe that the roadway issues should be addressed directly with the developer and SCDOT through -- 6 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 7 a clear completion and restoration plan rather than through this limited zoning request. Staff also recommended approval of the proposed rezoning. Goldfinch said that it sounds like a clear-cut legal issue and that this rezoning cannot be held up to be used as leverage to get something else done. Hucks said that this issue is separate than the roadwork. Hucks said that there is room to meet with DOT and the developer to get a schedule as to when those issues will be done and that staff can look into the financial guarantee that DOT carries to see if something could be done that way. Blain clarified that approval at this level would in no way give additional opportunity to a developer to move forward or it doesn’t help them in any way. Hucks said no that the lots are still created and they can pull building permits and move forward even without this rezoning. This is a downzoning, but staff does support further discussions with DOT and the developer to get Country Club restoration complete. Helms asked if the developer has spoken to DOT and staff. Hucks said that the developer is aware and Harrelson with Public Works has spoken to DOT and they have taken some enforcement action. Harrelson said that the last response that he got from SCDOT was that they sent inspectors out to do stormwater inspections after receiving complaints on Country Club Road. Harrelson said that SCDOT then shut down the developer and the city received an email from SCDOT asking us to stay out of it. Harrelson said that Country Club is a DOT road therefore the city has no jurisdiction or authority as our ordinance stands. Forest Beverly, property owner, said that the process has been drawn out with SCDOT and some of the issues is that it is an old road that has been there a long time and has run into a lot of issues that were not aware that were there. Beverly said that they are scheduled for August 3 and 4 to do the milling and overlay and then the final grading will be done along the sides. Blain asked when the property owner’s work is done, how much is left for SCDOT. Beverly said that DOT is not responsible for any work and they will push to get it signed off , hopefully in the middle of August. Hardwick asked for a timeline of work that has been done on Country Club. Beverly said that the problem is not what you see, it is what is under ground and said they have run into asbestos waterlines, then the process has to start over. Beverly said the road will also be widened so a turn lane can be installed. -- 7 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 8 Helms confirmed that what she is hearing is the property owner is working with DOT and there is a solution. Beverly said that they have run into several plan revisions with DOT but hope to be out of there in a couple of weeks. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. F. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (A) to annex approximately 2.56+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501, across from Sioux Swamp Dr. (PIN 326-14-04- 0010). Hucks stated that this property is contiguous to the city limits, and the applicant is seeking annexation in connection with the proposed development of adjacent properties that were previously annexed into the city. The subject property is intended to provide a right of way connection for that future development. The requested zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial. The future land use map identifies the Highway 501 frontage as Highway Commercial and the remainder as Low/Medium Density Residential. If council approves first reading of the annexation request, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the proposed zoning at their August 6 meeting. Staff recommended approval of first reading of the ordinance to annex the subject property. Motion: Helms made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (A) annexing the property located on Highway 501 across from Sioux Swamp Drive. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. G. Hucks stated that this request is for annexation of 3 parcels at the intersection of Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy Road. These properties are contiguous to the city limits and will require city services. They are intended to be incorporated into a larger development project involving surrounding properties. The requested zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial. The city’s future land use map identifies the properties as Industrial, rather the Highway Commercial. If council approved first reading of the ordinance annexing the property, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the proposed zoning at their August 6 meeting. Motion: Helms made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (B) annexing the 3 parcels located at the intersection of Highway 501 and Gardner Lacy Road. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. H. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (C) to annex approximately 10+/- acres of property located at 2899 E. Hwy 501 (PIN 400-04-02-0002). Hucks stated that this property is being proposed for annexation in conjunction with the previous request, although it is not contiguous to the other properties, so it is being considered separately. This and the previous properties are intended to be incorporated into a larger -- 8 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 9 development project involving surrounding properties. The requested zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial and will be considered by Planning Commission at their August 6 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommended approval. Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (C) annexing 2899 E. Highway 501. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. I. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (D) to annex approximately 0.13+/- acres of property located at 124 Quail Run (PIN 383-09-04-0058). Alvarez stated that this property is located within the Quail Creek Village subdivision near CCU and annexation is being requested to facilitate a name change on the city utility service account. Ownership of the property was transferred to the current owner on June 10, 2026, and restrictive covenants were recorded the same day. The property contains a single-family dwelling and is surrounded by similar residential zoning patterns. Parcels located directly across the street from the subject property are within city limits zoned R-1. Nine other properties within Quail Creek Village have previously been annexed into the City of Conway, with the most recent annexation occurring in January of 2026. The subject parcel is also located within the CCU Neighborhood Overlay District. The property is currently zoned Horry County Residential SF10 which has a minimum lot size of 10,000 square feet. The requested zoning upon annexation is R1 which is consistent with the future land use map. If first reading of the annexation is approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at their August 6 meeting. Alvarez said that staff recommended approval of first reading of the annexation. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (D) annexing 124 Quail Run. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. J. First reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-09-08 (E) to annex approximately 0.34+/- acres of property located at 2857 Hwy 378 (PIN 337-16-02-0028). Hucks stated that the applicant has withdrawn their request for annexation of this request. CONSIDERATION: A. Consideration of a request to approve the proposed name of a residential subdivision, “Minglewood Estates,” located along Hwy 813. Hucks stated that this item is a request to approve the name of a subdivision located on Highway 813, proposed to contain 24 single-family lots. The proposed name is Minglewood Estates. Preliminary plans are currently under review by the Technical Review Committee. The UDO requires that all subdivision names be approved by council. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of the proposed subdivision name. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to approve the subdivision name of Minglewood Estates. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Consideration of an approval of a proposal for the construction of the Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Docks. Hyman stated the Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Ferry -- 9 of 14 -- July 20, 2026 10 Project has been discussed for years and is finally happening. Hyman said that this project will enhance the quality of life by providing a safe, scenic, and accessible connection for pedestrians and cyclists across the Waccamaw River. The project will include ADA accessible permanent and floating docks, connected by a passenger ferry capable of transporting pedestrians and bicycles across the approximately 200-foot wide Waccamaw River. Once across the river, users will travel approximately 2,000 linear feet of elevated boardwalk through the wetlands to Depot Road, eventually to Waccamaw River Park and ultimately to Coastal Carolina University. The ferry itself will become more than transportation; it will be an attraction and community icon. The vessel will be named “The Spirit,” reflecting Conway’s welcoming character while allowing the city to celebrate each season through rotating holiday themes and decorations. The name also lends itself naturally to community branding and marketing with the tagline, “Catch the Spirit,” reinforcing Conways identity as a community that celebrates every season. Hyman said that the city advertised for bids and received 5 with the lowest responsive and responsible bidder being H, K, & W Marine Construction. Hyman said with Councils approval staff will move forward with negotiations with the contractor. Blain asked if the city had any experience with this company. Hyman said no, but references were provided, and the engineer spoke with those references. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms, to approve the awarding of the contract for construction of the Kingston Boardwalk Trail and Docks to H, K, & W Marine Construction as presented and authorized the City Administrator to negotiate and execute the necessary contract documents. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried.
