ORDINANCE: #ZA2026-03-16 (E) AGENDA SECTION: Consent ISSUE: Final reading of an ordinance to rezone approximately 0.43+/- acres of property located at 1322 & 1324 Cottage Lane APPLICANT(S): Sara Jo Lewis PIN(s): 338-10-02-0006, & - 0005 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) PROPOSED ZONING: Highway Commercial (HC) BACKGROUND: The subject properties, Lots 4 and 5 of the Wright SD, have restrictive covenants that were recorded on November 26, 2025. Each parcel contains a single-family dwelling. Properties directly across Cottage Lane and to the rear of the subject parcels are already within the City limits. Annexation is being requested in order to connect to City utility services, following a name change associated with the existing City utility service account. The applicant requested that the properties be zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) upon annexation. However, the City’s Future Land Use Map identifies the area as Highway Commercial (HC). Because of this designation, staff does not support assigning residential to the properties and recommends that the properties be zoned Highway Commercial (HC) upon annexation to maintain consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and the surrounding land use pattern. Although the parcels are currently developed with single-family homes, the HC zoning district would not require removal of the existing residences. The homes would be allowed to continue as legal nonconforming residential uses, but expansion of the residential use in the future would be limited, if not prohibited, under the HC district (i.e. could not expand outside of the existing building footprint). SURROUNDING USES / ZONING: The properties are bordered on two sides by parcels already located within the City limits and zoned HC. Adjacent properties immediately to the sides are vacant lots, while properties across Cottage Lane and to the rear include commercial uses such as fast-foot establishments and other highway-oriented businesses, all zoned HC within the City limits. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations for automobile oriented commercial activities associated with major highway corridors, while reducing traffic congestion and 32 -- 32 of 196 -- STAFF REPORT Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) enhancing the overall aesthetic environment of the City. CITY COUNCIL: Council approved 1st reading of ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) to rezone the properties to HC upon annexation at the February 17, 2026 meeting. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION: Planning Commission held the required Public Hearing and voted to recommend approval of the HC zoning district at their February 5, 2026 meeting. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) to zone the property Highway Commercial (HC) upon annexation. If the vendor wants to operate on public property or on private property under a special event permit, he or she shall obtain notarized written permission from the owner to conduct business. 3. The vendor shall obtain and carry at all times a valid City of Conway Business License. Vendors must obtain an annual zoning compliance. Food truck permits issued under this ordinance will be valid beginning on date of this Ordinance’s enactment until April 30 of the ensuing year. In the following year, a permit shall be from May 1 until April 30 of the ensuing year. 4. The vendor can operate through an approved City of Conway Special Event Permit. The vendor shall not operate in any manner that blocks, obstructs or restricts the free passage of vehicles or pedestrians in the lawful use of the sidewalks or highways or ingress or egress to the abutting property. Vending units shall be in compliance with all ANSI (American National Standards Institute) regulations. 11. The vendor shall be actively engaged in vending operations at all times while occupying any property. 12. The vendor shall pick up all refuse generated by his or her operation before the vending unit is moved. 13. All vending units must be self-contained with a waste receptacle. 14. The vendor shall not discharge items from any vending unit onto the sidewalk, gutter, storm inlets, streets, or planters. 15. The vendor shall keep the area surrounding their vending unit maintained in a safe, clean, orderly, and sanitary condition at all times. Exterior storage or display of surplus refuse, equipment, materials, goods, wares, or merchandise associated with the vending unit shall be prohibited. 18. The vendor shall display, in plain view and at all times, current permits and licenses in or on their vending unit. 19. Any damage to landscape or vegetation caused by the mobile vending operation shall be immediately compensated by the vendor upon request of the City. 20. ISSUE: First reading of Ordinance #2026-04-20 (C), an ordinance granting a distribution right-of-way easement to the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) across property of the City of Conway adjacent to Sherwood Road (PIN 338-00-00-0024). BACKGROUND: The McKeithan Watershed Project, funded by the South Carolina Office of Resiliency (SCOR) in 2025, is approaching its final stages. As construction nears completion, planning is underway for landscaping, recreational features, and site lighting. Public Works staff have recommended the installation of Santee Cooper streetlights along the walkways, as well as electrical connections to support seasonal and holiday decorations. The proposed fixtures would match the lighting currently used in nearby developments and throughout the downtown area, ensuring visual consistency and enhancing public safety. To proceed with this work, the City must grant Santee Cooper a distribution right-of-way. The required easement would extend the full length of the distribution lines and measure 20 feet in width—10 feet on each side of the cable centerline. Establishing this easement provides the necessary clearance for energized lines, ensures access for maintenance vehicles, and protects utility infrastructure. The easement would be perpetual and would authorize Santee Cooper to enter the property as needed to operate, maintain, and service its equipment. Easements are required of property owners within the subject work area, which includes the City of Conway for the property adjacent to Sherwood Road (PIN 338-00-00-0024). APPLICANT(S): Truett Holdings LLC PIN(s): 367-14-03-0008 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Highway Commercial (HC) BACKGROUND: The subject property is located along E. Hwy 501 and is currently within Horry County’s jurisdiction. This parcel contains an existing commercial business (Skyline Signs) as well as a manufactured home located on the same property. Available records indicate the manufactured home has been present on the site since approximately 2006. Staff has not yet been able to confirm whether the manufactured home was originally permitted as a residential use under County regulations. In 2022, Horry County approved a plat combining two of the parcels associated with the property, resulting in the commercial business and the manufactured home being on the same parcel. The manufactured home is currently vacant. According to the applicant, annexation is being required in order to obtain municipal utility services, which the owner has indicated would allow the existing manufactured home to be used as a legal residence. City records indicate that water was last turned on the structure in September 2025 but was disconnected due to nonpayment. Under Horry County’s Highway Commercial zoning district, single-family (site built) residential uses are permitted; however, manufactured homes are not. Under the City’s Unified Development Ordinance, the Highway Commercial district does not permit residential uses at all, and manufactured homes are not permitted uses in the City under any zoning district. DEFINITION / INTENT OF PROPOSED ZONING: Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic environment of the City. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: Properties along this portion of E. Hwy 501 are developed with highway-oriented commercial as well as industrial uses, including retail, automotive services, manufactured home sales, a sign company, and other commercial businesses. 152 -- 152 of 196 -- STAFF REPORT First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (C) Adjacent City zoning is Highway Commercial. The neighboring properties were annexed in 2025 as Highway Commercial (HC) and one fronting Amber Lane as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Adjacent County zoning includes Highway Commercial (HC), Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA), and a mix of residential zoning types. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s Future Land Use Map designates the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic environment of the City. Assigning HC zoning upon annexation is consistent with both the Future Land Use Map and the established development pattern along Highway 501. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION: Planning Commission is scheduled to hold the required public hearing and consider the proposed zoning upon annexation at their April 2, 2026 meeting. STAFF ANALYSIS: Annexation decisions are based on logical municipal growth, service provision, and consistency with the Comprehensive Plan. The zoning district applied upon annexation must follow the Future Land Use Map, which designates the properties along this corridor as Highway Commercial (HC). Staff supports annexation of the property as it would extend the City’s municipal boundaries in a logical manner. However, it is important to note that under the City of Conway UDO, the HC district does not permit residential uses, including manufactured homes. If annexed and assigned HC zoning, the manufactured home currently located on the property would be considered nonconforming to the City’s zoning regulations. As such, the structure could remain on the property as a nonconforming structure, but its use would be subject to the City’s regulations governing nonconforming uses and structures. Whether the manufactured home can used for residential purposes is dependent on how the UDO would treat this nonconforming use. If the structure was “lawfully” established, meaning the structure was legally permitted by the County, then the residential use could continue as a “legal” nonconforming use. If the structure was never legally permitted, it is considered illegal, not nonconforming and illegal uses cannot be continued. Rezoning the property to a residential use would not be consistent with the City’s Future Land Use Map or the established Highway Commercial development pattern along the Highway 501 corridor. 153 -- 153 of 196 -- STAFF REPORT First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (C) Annexation of the property does NOT constitute approval of any specific use of the property. title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 3.16.26
text: March 16, 2026 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, MARCH 16, 2026 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem Beth Helms, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jason Perzan, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kelli Thomas, Deputy PIO; Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance Director; Chris Weatherford, Public Utilities Deputy Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 20 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Butler gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (A) to annex approximately 1+/- acres of property located at 3000 Hwy 378 (PIN 337-16-04-0011). B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (D) to rezone approximately 1.0+/- acres of property at 3000 Hwy 378 (PIN: 337-16-04-0011) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. C. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (B) to annex approximately 0.43+/- acres of property located at 1322 & 1324 Cottage Lane (PINs 338-10-02-0005 & 338-10-02- 0006). D. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) to rezone approximately 0.43+/- acres of property at 1322 and 1324 Cottage Lane (PINs: 338-10-02-0005 & -0006) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district, or alternatively, the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. -- 1 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 2 E. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (C) to annex approximately 0.2 +/- acres of property located at 1326 Cottage Lane (PIN 338-10-02-0007). F. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (F) to rezone approximately 0.22+/- acres of property at 1326 Cottage Lane (PIN: 338-10-02-007) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. G. Final Reading of Ordinance #2026-03-16 (G), an ordinance authorizing the relinquishment of an existing waterline easement and the acceptance of a new 30-foot- wide waterline easement associated with the relocation and upsizing of a City of Conway water transmission line related to Santee Cooper’s substation project, owned by the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) and identified as PINs 369-00-00-0050, 369-00-00-0027 and 369-00-00-0028. H. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (H), an ordinance extending the non- exclusive franchise agreement issued to Randall’s Culinary Creations Mobile Food Truck at the parking lot located at 7 Elm Street. I. Approval of Protocol and MOU between Conway Police Department and South Carolina Department of Social Services J. Approval of a Resolution accepting dedication of roadways & drainage and the financial guarantee for the roadway warranty for the Chapman Village subdivision (Hudson Trail, Eloise Lane, Caisa Court). K. Approval of a Resolution Recognizing the need for the Horry County Solid Waste Authority to expand Landfill Capacity for Residents and Businesses within the City of Conway L. Approval of February 17, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes M. Approval of March 5-6 Budget Retreat Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve the March 16, 2026 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Longevity Awards – February 2026 – 5 Years: Jonathan Brown, Police; 5 Years: Jacob Shook, Police; 5 Years: Matthew Micallef, Police; 25 Years: Darren Alston, Police. B. Employee of the Month for March 2026 – Public Safety -- 2 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 3 C. Presentation of a Proclamation declaring March 2026 as Red Cross Month – Blain presented the Proclamation declaring March 2026 as Red Cross Month to the representatives of the Red Cross that were in attendance. D. Update on Conway Senior Center – Elaine Gore, Director of Horry County Council on Aging informed council of their interests in relocating from the City Senior Center to the fellowship hall at former Jamestown Baptist Church and are prepared to upgrade the fellowship hall following all necessary permission and codes. Gore said that they are prepared to continue to cover their own expenses and looks forward to discussing the proposal. E. Presentation by Resurrected Life Christian Outreach Ministry – Robin Wages – not present. F. Presentation by Health Care Partners – Josh Kay of Mashburn Construction introduced Santino Mayo, CEO of Health Care Partners who gave a brief overview of the services offered. Mayo announced the progress of their new facility and showed a rendering of the building coming soon to Fourth Avenue, Conway. George Williams, board member of Health Care Partners, expressed his excitement about the new building and being able to serve the community. Williams said that they would like to expand the community garden to the adjacent parcel under the oak trees and asked the city to partner with the health center on this endeavor. Kay announced all the partners involved in the project, thanked staff, gave a summary of the rendering of the building and the projected timeline. Lee Belcher of First Citizens said they are honored to be a partner with Health Care Partners in this project. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #2026-04-20 (C), an ordinance granting a distribution right-of-way easement to the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) across property of the City of Conway adjacent to Sherwood Road (PIN 338- 00-00-0024). Harrelson stated that the McKeithan Watershed Project is approaching its final stages and planning is underway for landscaping, recreational features, and site lighting. Staff recommended the installation of Santee Cooper streetlights along the walkways, as well as electrical connections, to support seasonal and holiday decorations. The proposed fixtures would match the lighting currently used in nearby developments and throughout the downtown area, ensuring visual consistency and enhancing public safety. To proceed with this work, the city must grant Santee Cooper a distribution right-of-way. The required easement would extend the full length of the distribution lines and measure 20 feet in width and 110 feet on each side of the cable centerline. Establishing this easement provides the necessary clearance for energized lines, ensures access for maintenance vehicles, and protects utility infrastructure. The easement would be perpetual -- 3 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 4 and would authorize Santee Cooper to enter the property as needed to operate, maintain, and service its equipment. Harrelson said that easements are required of property owners within the subject work area, which includes the City of Conway for the property adjacent to Sherwood Road. Harrelson said that staff recommended first reading. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #2026-04-20 (C) granting a distribution right-of-way easement to the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) across property of the City of Conway adjacent to Sherwood Road. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (A) to annex approximately 0.73+/- acres of property located at 424 Maplewood Circle (PIN 324-06-01-0002). Hucks stated that this item is a request to annex approximately .73 acres located at 424 Maplewood Circle. The current zoning is Horry County SF40, which is single family residential on lot sizes a minimum of 40,000 square feet. The parcel contains a single-family home and a detached garage. The applicant is requesting annexation in accordance with city ordinance regarding new connections to city utilities. The property is adjacent to parcels already located in the city limits, including properties to the side and rear. The future land use map designates this area as R-1, which is also consistent with the surrounding properties that are already in the city limits. Planning Commission will hold the public hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at their April 2 meeting and their recommendation will be forwarded for first reading of an ordinance regarding the appropriate zoning upon annexation. Hucks said that staff recommends approval of first reading of the ordinance to annex the subject property. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (A) to annex the property located at 424 Maplewood Circle. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (B) to annex approximately 0.63+/- acres of property located at 1121 E Hwy 501 (PIN 367-14-03-0011). Hucks stated that this property is currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial and the property contains an older commercial building that is currently used as a tire center. Based on google imagery, the property has consistently been used as either a tire center or a small used car lot since the early 2000’s. This property is owned by the same property owner of 1125 and 1135 E. Highway 501 (next request on the agenda), which has restrictive covenants and which triggered the annexation when the applicant applied for city utilities for that property, since all adjacent properties become subject to annexation upon the requirement of any property owned by the same applicant being subject to annexation. The city’s future land use map identifies this property as Highway Commercial, which is consistent with the future land use map for surrounding properties with frontage along the Highway 501 corridor. This ordinance is for first reading of annexation only. If approved, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at their April 2 meeting. Hucks said that staff recommends approval of first reading of the ordinance to annex this property. -- 4 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 5 Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (B) to annex the property located at 1121 E. Highway 501. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (C) to annex approximately 3.29+/- acres of property located at 1125 & 1135 E Hwy 501 (PIN 367-14-03-0008). Hucks stated that this request is for annexation of the property located at 1125 and 1135 East Highway 501, which is adjacent to the previous property just discussed. This property contains the structure that triggered the annexation requirement. The property at 1135 E. Hwy 501 contains the commercial business, Skyline Signs and the property at 1125 E. Hwy 501 was previously a mobile home dealership until approximately 2017. According to county land records, the current property owners acquired the property at 1125 E. Hwy 501 in 2018, and the two parcels remained separate until 2022 when the county approved a plat combining them into a single tract. As a result, what were previously separate uses on individual parcels now exist on one combined property, including commercial businesses and a mobile home that was used residentially for several years. County records indicate that the mobile home was moved to its current location and registered in 2010, and the structure is currently vacant. The property owner is seeking annexation in accordance with city ordinance to reconnect the mobile home to city utilities, which has been disconnected since September of last year, with the intent of renting the structure as a residence. Unlike the county’s Highway Commercial district, the City’s Highway Commercial zoning district does not permit residential uses, including manufactured or mobile homes. While limited residential uses are permitted under the county’s version of Highway Commercial, manufactured homes are not, so it’s unclear whether the residential structure was originally permitted under county regulations. Staff also noted that a new address of 1129 E. Hwy 501 has recently been assigned to the location of the mobile home, which was previously associated with the 1125 address. Hucks said that if the property is annexed and assigned Highway Commercial zoning upon annexation, the structure would be considered nonconforming, and whether it could continue to be used residentially would depend on whether the use can be verified as a lawful pre-existing use prior to annexation, and how it is evaluated under the city’s nonconforming use provisions. Aside from Skyline Signs, it appears that another business, Safeshield, which provides traffic control services, has equipment and materials stored on the portion of the property addressed as 1125 E. Hwy 501, although their website lists their business being located at 1135 E. Hwy 501. Currently, staff has not located a record of an active business license for the business at either address. If annexed, any businesses operating on the property would be required to comply with the city’s business licensing and zoning regulations. Hucks said that this request is for first reading of annexation only. If approved, Planning Commission will hold the required hearing on the proposed zoning upon annexation at their April 2 meeting and that staff supports annexation as it represents a logical extension of the city limits along the Highway 501 corridor and recommends approval of first reading, -- 5 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 6 There was some discussion regarding the zoning district requirements. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (C) to annex the property located at 1125 & 1135 E. Highway 501. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. E. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (D) to rezone an approximate 7.4-acre portion of 8.76+/- acres of property located at 2487 Hwy 501 E (PIN: 383-14-02-0001) from the Highway Commercial (HC) and Light Industrial (LI) districts to the Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated that this request is to rezone a portion of the property at 2487 Highway 501 E from Highway Commercial to Light Industrial. The property was originally annexed in 2006, and at that time, the parcel was assigned split-zoning, with the first approximately 300 feet along Highway 501 zoned HC and the remainder zoned LI. Since that time, amendments to the City’s Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) included an amendment prohibiting split-zoning of parcels, except in limited cases involving environmentally sensitive areas. The property owner is currently proposing to subdivide a 1.36-acre portion from the parent tract that would retain the HC zoning and access to the existing business, Tyson Signs, on the LI zoned portion of the property. Staff found that allowing subdivision while keeping the existing zoning pattern would increase the degree of split-zoning condition, which would represent an expansion of nonconformity that is not permitted under the UDO. To resolve that issue, the applicant requested to rezone the remaining HC portion, minus the 1.36-acre portion proposed to be split from the parent tract, to LI, which would eliminate the split zoning and result in a single zoning designation across the parcel following subdivision. Hucks said that Planning Commission held the public hearing on the request at their March 5 meeting and recommended approval of the request. Hucks said that staff also recommended approval. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-05-04 (D) to rezone the property located at 2487 Highway 501 E. Vote: Helms, Butler, White, Jordan, Hardwick and Blain voted yes. Goldfinch voted no. Motion carried with a 6-1 vote. CONSIDERATION: A. Consideration of approval of the proposed subdivision name, “Oak Haven,” for a new development located on Westridge Boulevard (PIN 337-13-03-0056). Hucks stated that this proposed development is located on Westridge Blvd, off Highway 378 across from the Holt Gardens development and next to the Westridge subdivision. The proposed development will consist of 10 single-family dwellings on one common property. Plans are currently being reviewed by TRC; however; the ordinance requires city council approval of the proposed subdivision name prior to final plan approval. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of the proposed name Oak Haven. -- 6 of 8 -- March 16, 2026 7 Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve the subdivision name of Oak Haven for a new development located on Westridge Blvd. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Consideration of a Request for Proposal (RFP) to conduct an Employee Classification and Pay Study. L. Smith stated that this was a consideration of a RFP to conduct an Employee Classification and Pay Study to review the city’s current employee classification structure and compensation system. The RFP opening was held on March 4, 2026 and 7 proposals were received. L. Smith said that staff recommended awarding the contract to Evergreen Solutions with the amount of $59,500. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to approve staff’s recommendation to award the contract to Evergreen Solutions. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. Consideration of a Special Event – Spring Fest @ the Outpost - April 18, 2026. Emrick informed council that The Conway Outpost is proposing to host Springfest on April 18, 2026 which will consist of a vendor and food tuck event with 60-80 vendors with 10x10 tents. The applicant is requesting to close off a portion of the parking lot at the marina, and it is the same day as the Horry Electric 5K. Emrick was concerned about the likelihood of heavy boat user traffic in mid-April. The applicant, Shannon Jordan further explained the request stating that the dock would not be closed and that the back parking lot would be used for the Marina parking. Emrick stated that he would put them in contact with Horry Electric to avoid any potential conflicts. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve the special event as presented. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: None CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: • Reminder of the Recreation Department holding the State’s Largest Easter Egg Hunt on March 28th. Separate hunts for children of all ages and abilities will take place. • The City of Conway sponsored Coastal Baseball game is Friday, the 20. Emrick said he hopes to see all of council there in Teal supporting our Nationally ranked home team and you don’t want to miss Justin Jordan is throwing out the first pitch at the game. • Staff will be meeting with the Department of Environmental Services later this week to look at Lake Busbee to assess whether there are any invasive plant species out there that need to be addressed. This is part of a larger effort to support native bird habitats at the Lake. • The Mayor’s Youth Council plans to begin painting their mural at Riverfront Park this week. -- 7 of 8 -- -- 8 of 8 --

The requirements for open space 67 -- 67 of 171 -- January 20, 2026 5 have been amended a few times over the last 10 or so years, and a 2016 amendment included a revision requiring that a fee in lieu of open space be provided when less than one acre of open space is calculated using the formula determining the amount of open space. This was because the amount of open space being required at the time for some of the developments would not have been compliant with the open space suitability standards in effect at that time. How the total amount of open space that is determined has also been amended, to a much simpler formula, which now requires that there be 1,000 sq. ft. of open space for each lot or unit in a proposed development. This means that there would need to be a minimum of 44 lots or units proposed to meet the minimum standard for providing open space onsite (43,560 sq. ft.). Hucks said that in addition to the requirement to submit a fee in lieu of providing open space when less than one acre is required, the applicant is required to submit a written appraisal of the market value of the land to be developed, as if the development has been completed; in other words, post-development value. As part of the applicant’s request for preliminary plan approval, which is considered by Planning Commission, the applicant requested a design modification from the appraisal requirements, requesting that the contracted amount for the property be accepted in determining the dollar amount for the open space fee in lieu. Planning Commission approved the design modification request, and granted preliminary plan approval, contingent upon final review and approval of the Technical Review Committee. Hucks stated that a separate request considered on the same agenda was for the same project, asking for approval of the fee in lieu amount of open space, but in a reduced amount, which is required to receive a recommendation by Planning Commission before being considered by Council, based on the following factors: (1) This is an infill development, an expansion of an existing student housing project that already contains open space amenities, including an outdoor pool, amenity center, a dog park, among other things, that will be available for use by the new residents; and (2) Although the open space areas shown to be provided on this site do not meet the minimum standards, there is some passive open space being provided, in addition to the fee in lieu. Hucks said that Planning Commission considered the second request for the reduced fee in lieu amount at their January 8, 2026 meeting. Part of the discussion included the amount of open space that was already in place for the existing University Suites, which was approved under a different regulatory framework when previously zoned as a Planned Development and the open space was calculated very differently at that time. Because the open space that does exist is considered nonconforming, it cannot be credited toward the requirement for the proposed expansion. The open space ordinance currently in effect sets a standard method for calculating the fee based on the value of the land, the size of the site, and the amount of open space that would otherwise be required, plus a 25% surcharge, which was adopted as part of the most recent amendments to the open space ordinance. Using that method, and the contracted amount that was approved by Planning Commission via a design modification, the full fee in lieu of providing open space onsite is $223,800. Planning Commission considered the applicant’s request to reduce the fee in lieu amount that is calculated, based on the value of the land via the method they approved, and did not reach consensus on the fee in lieu amount. Two motions were made; 68 -- 68 of 171 -- January 20, 2026 6 neither received a majority. It was split 3/3 both times. As a result, the applicant’s request was denied. Hucks stated that the question is not whether open space is required but in applying the policy that is in effect, whether the proposed fee in lieu amount is sufficient for this project. Based on the number of units proposed, the ordinance calculates the amount of open space required to be 24,000 sq. ft.; a little more than half an acre. As previously stated, using the applicant’s own contracted amount, the fee in lieu amount would otherwise be $223,800, when you take into account the 25% additional fee that is required. The applicant is requesting approval of a reduced fee in lieu amount of $52,152.86, based on the reasons previously provided, and citing in their application that the project only lacks 6,991 sq. ft. of “suitable” open space if the requirement for the fee in lieu for less than one acre of open space did not exist. Hucks said that staff’s determination and recommendation is based on a few factors: − The formula for determining the fee in lieu of open space is designed to approximate the cost of acquiring and developing new open space when a project creates demand for new park land. In this case, the city would have to acquire roughly half an acre of land elsewhere. The standard calculation works best for large, standalone developments where residents will rely entirely on new or offsite public facilities, not ones that have private amenities nearby. − This project is a small, infill expansion, not a new, isolated development. Residents will have access to private amenities directly across the street, which already serves a similar population. As a result, the demand this project places on City parks and recreation facilities could be considered much less than what the formula in the ordinance assumes. The assessed fee ($223,800) reflects a hypothetical cost based solely on land value, not actual use or impact. − Applying the full fee in this case could unintentionally discourage infill development in areas the city wants it, pushing development farther out where infrastructure and services are more costly, contributing towards urban sprawl. A reduced fee supports the City’s broader goals of efficient land use, student housing near campuses, and minimizing sprawl, while still complying with the ordinance. Staff’s recommendation is to approve a reduction in the fee in lieu amount to $65,191.008, which includes an additional 25% fee on top of the applicant’s proposed fee of $52,152. ORDINANCE: #ZA2026-03-16 (E) AGENDA SECTION: First Reading ISSUE: First reading of an ordinance to rezone approximately 0.43+/- acres of property located at 1322 & 1324 Cottage Lane APPLICANT(S): Sara Jo Lewis PIN(s): 338-10-02-0006, & - 0005 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Residential, mobile homes allowed (MSF10) PROPOSED ZONING: Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) BACKGROUND: The subject property, identified as Lot 4 1322 Cottage Lane & Lot 5 1324 Cottage Lane’s restrictive covenants were recorded on November 26, 2025. Both properties contain one single-family dwelling. Properties abutting the rear and directly across Cottage Lane from the subject parcel are already within the city limits. Annexation is being requested as a requirement to connect to city services following a name change to the city utility service account. The applicant is requesting Low/ medium Density Residential (R-1) which is not supported by the Future Land Use Map, which identifies the subject properties as being Highway Commercial (HC). The HC zoning district would not prevent the homes from being used as residencies it would simply restrict the ability to expand the use in the future, as the existing residential structures would become legal nonconforming uses under the HC district. SURROUNDING USES / ZONING: The properties are surrounded on two sides by properties already in the city limits and zoned HC. The properties on either side of the parcels are vacant wooded lots with the rear abutting property being commercial uses like fast food establishments among others all zoned HC in the city limits. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. CITY COUNCIL: Council approved 1st reading of ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (B) to annex the properties at their January 5th meeting. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION: Approval Planning Commission held the required Public Hearing and voted to recommend approval of the HC zoning district at their February 5th meeting. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Staff recommends approval of first reading to rezone the subject property R-1 upon annexation. ISSUE: First reading of Ordinance #2026-03-16 (G), an ordinance authorizing the relinquishment of an existing waterline easement and the acceptance of a new 30-foot-wide waterline easement associated with the relocation and upsizing of a City of Conway water transmission line related to Santee Cooper’s substation project, owned by the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) and identified as PINs 369-00-00-0050, 369-00-00-0027 and 369-00-00-0028. BACKGROUND: Santee Cooper constructed a new electrical substation to support increased growth in the area. An existing City of Conway waterline conflicted with the substation footprint and was relocated. During relocation, the City upsized the waterline to a 30-inch transmission main to improve system capacity and reliability. The relocated 30-inch water line has been installed and is currently operational. As a result, a portion of the existing waterline easement is no longer needed, and a new easement is required for the relocated waterline. ISSUE: Purchasing a hydroseeder for the Public Works Department BACKGROUND: A hydroseeder is a machine that mixes grass seed, mulch, fertilizer, and water into a thick slurry and sprays it onto the ground to quickly establish vegetation, control erosion, and create lush lawns, often on large or difficult-to-reach areas where traditional seeding is impractical. It's a faster, more effective, and cost-efficient alternative to broadcasting dry seed or laying sod. Public Works uses a hydroseeder on areas that have been disturbed such as drainage projects, sinkhole repairs, edge of roadways, & banks of ditches that have been cleaned to re-establish stabilization. It also helps in instances when building parking lots or roads using water to help soak subgrade & base material to achieve maximum compaction. The Public Works Department would like to purchase a used 2025 FINN T75 hydroseeder to replace a 2001-year model Easy Lawn hydroseeder. Since May of 2023, $7,294.51 has been spent on repairs for the hydroseeder currently owned. Parts for this model are becoming hard to find, and some are unavailable due to the 25-year age of equipment. The cost of a new FINN T75 hydroseeder is estimated at $65,000. Dobbs Equipment has a used 2025 model available with 128 hours for $54,997.20 after tax. The money would be reallocated from the Street & Stormwater Materials & Supplies accounts. RECOMMENDATION: Approve the purchase of a FINN T75 hydroseeder at the approximate cost of $54,997.20 . 171 -- 171 of 171 --

text: February 17, 2026 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 17, 2026 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem Beth Helms, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jason Perzan, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Braxton Fleming, Public Works Deputy Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kelli Thomas, Deputy PIO; Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance Director; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Kim Wilkerson, Planning and Development Deputy Director and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 25 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Hardwick gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-02-02 (A) to annex approximately 0.22+/- acres of property located at 250 Chevy Chase Drive (PIN 367-13-01-0031). B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-02-02 (C) to rezone approximately 0.22+/- acres of property located at 250 Chevy Chase Drive (PIN 367-13-01-0031) from the Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. C. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-02-02 (D) to rezone approximately 50.64+/- acres of property located on E. Country Club Drive (PIN 339-00-00-0026), from the City of Conway Low/ Medium Residential (R-1) to the City of Conway Conservation Preservation (CP). D. Approval of a Special Event - Waccamaw Sportsmen’s Expo – March 26-28, 2026 -- 1 of 8 -- February 17, 2026 2 E. Approval of a Special Event – Halloween Hustle – October 3, 2026 F. Approval of a bid for the purchase of a CNC Machine for the Construction Services Department (budgeted) G. Approval of January 20, 2026 City Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by White to approve the February 17, 2026 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Longevity Awards – January 2026 – 5 Years – Nickey Richardson, Police; 25 Years – Jason Perzan, Fire – Emrick and Goldfinch presented the longevity awards. B. Proclamation Honoring Black History Month – Blain presented the Black History Month Proclamation to Cheryl Moore Adamson and others in attendance. C. Conway Downtown Alive Annual Visitor Center Update – Hillary Howard – Howard, Executive Director of Conway Downtown Alive gave an annual visitor center update to Council. D. Update on the 2025-26 Mayor’s Youth Advisory Council – Rogers introduced the Junior Mayor of Conway, Skyler Platt. Platt gave council an update on their work which involves a mural at Riverfront Park, Recycling Program at Conway High School, and helped with a Toy Drive and Movie Night at the Terrace in December. Platt said that the youth council hopes to make this years project a fundraising drive but will have more later. Platt said that the youth council has made several recommendations for councils’ consideration at their budget retreat. E. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 5.28 +/- total acres of property located at 2578 Hwy 378 (PIN 337-10-03-0010), from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Heavy Industrial (HI) district. Peterson stated that this property is currently zoned Highway Commercial and the applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the Heavy Industrial district, which is a district intended to accommodate heavy manufacturing, distribution, and processing uses. The applicant has applied for a business license to display and sell heavy equipment. Similar uses that are identified in the UDO, such as storage/shed sales and manufactured or modular home sales, are only permitted with the Light and Heavy Industrial districts. Heavy equipment includes large scale, earth moving construction equipment, such as bulldozers, excavators, cranes, graders, compactors, forklifts, and similar equipment, including attachments for such equipment. As such, the Zoning Administrator determined that the proposed use could not be permitted in the Highway Commercial district, prompting the request to rezone the property. The city’s future land use map designates this property as Highway Commercial, which is intended for auto-oriented commercial development along major arterial roads and -- 2 of 8 -- February 17, 2026 3 highway corridors. The adjacent properties on either side are zoned Highway Commercial, however their existing uses are more industrial in character, as and while not directly across for the subject property, there are properties across Highway 378 that are zoned Heavy Industrial upon being annexed and another property that contains a similar use, but currently in the county’s jurisdiction. Peterson said that Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the request at their March 5 meeting, and their recommendation will be forwarded at the first reading of the ordinance to rezone the property. Blain had concerns that if the property became Heavy Industrial and the intended current use goes out of business at how close it would be to residential. Goldfinch said that it is very close to other industrial, but he has concerns saying that the city has spent a lot of money on getting this gateway corridor looking nice. Peterson said that across Highway 378 and further down are some industrial uses, but the adjacent uses are Highway Commercial and that the future land use map does show this property as Highway Commercial. White asked if the adjacent property owners had been notified. Peterson said yes, all within 200 feet have been notified. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-04-20 (A) to annex approximately 1.08 +/- acres of property located off Cates Bay Hwy (PIN 369-11-04-0004). Alvarez stated that this property is a part of the Horry County Sandridge Park off Cates Bay Highway. The subject property has been owned by Sandridge Community Improvement Council since 1981. It is accessed via a private easement road from Cates Bay Highway, not a public road. The parcel is adjacent to the New Castle subdivision zoned R-1, which is low/medium residential that is within city limits. Additionally, the property abuts the proposed Conway Perimeter Road. The property currently contains picnic tables and a covered picnic structure. The applicant is within the city utility service area and has previously received city services. However, due to a prolonged lapse in service, city public utilities are requiring a new service connection promoting the applicant to request annexation. Should Council approve first reading of the ordinance to annex the subject property, Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the requested zoning at their April 2 meeting. Alvarez said that given the fact that the property is owned by the Sandridge Community Improvement Council and used in conjunction with a Horry County Park and doesn’t have adequate frontage from a public road, staff recommends against annexation of the subject property at this time. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-04-20 (A) annexing the property located off Cates Bay Highway. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. -- 3 of 8 -- February 17, 2026 4 B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (D) to rezone approximately 1.0+/- acres of property at 3000 Hwy 378 (PIN: 337-16-04-0011) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that first reading to annex this property was approved at the January 5 council meeting. The property was previously used as a car dealership, and it was sold in October of last year. Restrictive Covenants have been on file since 1991. As part of the annexation process, the property must be assigned a city zoning district upon annexation. The current zoning of the property is Horry County Highway Commercial, and the requesting zoning upon annexation is also Highway Commercial, which is consistent with the city’s future land use map. Hucks said that Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the proposed zoning of the property at their February 5 meeting and recommended approval. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (D) rezoning the property at 3000 Highway 378 to City of Conway Highway Commercial. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) to rezone approximately 0.43+/- acres of property at 1322 and 1324 Cottage Lane (PINs: 338-10-02-0005 & -0006) from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district, or alternatively, the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that first reading to annex these parcels was approved at the January 5 council meeting. Both properties contain a single- family dwelling and owned by the same individual. Restrictive Covenants were recorded for the parcels in November of 2025. Cottage Lane is one of the most notable donut holes within the city’s boundaries, however, the annexation of these two parcels along with an abutting parcel will almost completely close this gap, leaving just one remaining undeveloped parcel that will be subject to annexation. The applicant requested to annex the properties as R-1, and Horry County’s version of the Highway Commercial district permits single family residential. However, the property is completely surrounded by City of Conway Highway Commercial, and the city’s future land use map identifies the properties as Highway Commercial. Annexation as Highway Commercial does not prohibit the current use of the property but does prohibit expansion of the current use. Hucks said that Planning Commission held a public hearing on the request at their February 5 meeting, in which R-1 and HC districts were considered, and recommended that the property be zoned to Highway Commercial upon annexation. Staff also recommends approval of first reading of the ordinance to zone the property Highway Commercial. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (E) rezoning the property at 1322 and 1324 Cottage Lane to the City of Conway Highway Commercial. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried D. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (F) to rezone approximately 0.22+/- acres of property at 1326 Cottage Lane (PIN: 338-10-02-007) from the Horry -- 4 of 8 -- February 17, 2026 5 County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2026-03-16 (F) rezoning the property at 1326 Cottage Lane to City of Conway Highway Commercial. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried E. First reading of Ordinance #2026-03-16 (G), an ordinance authorizing the relinquishment of an existing waterline easement and the acceptance of a new 30- foot-wide waterline easement associated with the relocation and upsizing of a City of Conway water transmission line related to Santee Cooper’s substation project, owned by the South Carolina Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) and identified as PINs 369-00-00-0050, 369-00-00-0027 and 369-00-00-0028. Dudley stated that this ordinance is the first reading to address the relocation of a city water line due to Santee Cooper’s new electrical substation project off Liz Lane, behind the Food Lion on Highway 701 South. During construction the city’s existing waterline conflicted with the substation footprint and was relocated. As part of the project the city upsized the line to a 30-inch transmission main to improve capacity and long-term reliability. The new line is installed and fully operational. Because the line has been relocated a portion of the original easement is no longer needed. This ordinance allows the city to release the unused easement and accept a new 30-foot easement for the relocated line. Dudley said this simply updates the legal documentation to reflect what is already in place and staff recommended approval of first reading. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #2026-03-16 (G) authorizing the relinquishment of an existing waterline easement and the acceptance of a new 30-foot-wide waterline easement relating to the Santee Cooper substation project as presented. There was some discussion that if staff become dissatisfied, the franchise agreement can be canceled. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. -- 5 of 8 -- February 17, 2026 6 B. Consideration of the purchase of a Hydroseeder for the Public Works Department. Fleming told council that a hydroseeder is a machine that mixes grass seed, mulch, fertilizer, and water into a thick slurry and sprays it onto the ground to quickly establish vegetation, control erosion, and create lush lawns, where traditional seeding is impractical. Fleming said that the Public Works Department would like to purchase a used 2025 FINN T75 hydroseeder to replace a 2001-year model Easy Lawn hydroseeder. Since May of 2023, $7,294.51 has been spent on repairs for the hydroseeder currently owned. Parts for this model are becoming hard to find, and some are unavailable due to the 25-year age of equipment. The cost of a new hydroseeder is estimated at $65,000. Dobbs Equipment has a used 2025 model available with 128 hours for $54,9977.20. The money would be reallocated from the Street & Stormwater Materials and Supplies account. Fleming said that staff does approve of the purchase. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve the purchase of the used hydroseeder as presented for the Public Works Department. ORDINANCE: ZA2025-09-02 (C) AGENDA SECTION: Consent ISSUE: Final reading of an ordinance to annex approximately 107.75+/- acres of property located at or near the intersection of Cultra Rd and Oak St. APPLICANT(S): Development Resource Group (DRG) LLC PIN(s): 325-00-00-0011 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Medium-Density Residential (R-2) & Conservation Preservation (CP) BACKGROUND: The subject property is proposed to be annexed into the City for residential development. The property is within the city’s utility service area, thus requiring annexation to be requested. Surrounding developments – Rivertown Row North, Kingston Bay and Elmhurst, are also zoned Medium-Density Residential (R-2). Midtown Village, which directly abuts this property, is zoned High-Density Residential (R-3). A large portion of the subject property is located within the AE flood zone, which runs through the middle of the parcel (see attached maps). While development is permitted within flood zones, provided the affected property meets the required elevation, staff does not support rezoning portion(s) of property within a flood zone to a district that would permit residential development. In 2023, Council adopted an ordinance that permits parcels containing environmentally sensitive areas to be split- zoned, which is otherwise prohibited, with such areas being zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation of property or when property is proposed to be rezoned. The applicant has agreed to zone the portions within the flood zone to CP upon annexation to ensure that no residential structures are constructed within the flood zone. Out of the 107.75+/- total acres, approx. 42.5 acres will be zoned CP upon annexation, and the remainder as R-2. SURROUNDING USES / ZONING: Surrounding in-City zoning includes Neighborhood Commercial (NC), High-Density Residential (R-3), Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), and Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The area is primarily single-family residential, with limited established commercial uses. There is a gas station/convenience store (Sun House) with a few tenant spaces containing limited commercial uses, including a dog grooming business, immediately adjacent to the subject property. Surrounding County zoning includes mostly residential, including Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF20) on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes, and Residential, including mobile homes (MSF20), also on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes. Abutting property is also zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). The John T. Henry Auction location is near the subject property, which is also zoned CFA. Horry Electric is also nearby, on the opposite side of Cultra Rd, which is zoned Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI). 4 -- 4 of 164 -- STAFF REPORT Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-09-02 (C) COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map provides three (3) future land use designations for the subject property. For the portion with frontage along Cultra Rd, the future land use is shown as Neighborhood Commercial (NC). Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small-scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. A larger portion of the property is shown as Conservation Preservation (CP) on the city’s future land use map. Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the CP district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The portion abutting Midtown Village and Conway Christian School is shown as High-Density Residential on the future land use map. Per Section 3.2.5 of the UDO, the intent of the high-density residential district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. PLANNING COMMISSION: PC held a public hearing on the proposed zoning of the property at their August 7th and September 4th (2025) meetings. Several people were in attendance that spoke in opposition to the request, citing concerns with flooding, traffic, overdevelopment of the area, density, using roads within Midtown Village as the entrance to the proposed development, etc. Planning Commission ultimately recommended unanimous approval of the requested zoning upon annexation. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved first reading to annex the subject property at their August 4th meeting. City Council approved first reading of the ordinance to zone the subject property CP and R-2 upon annexation at their August 15th meeting. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Staff recommends approval of Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-09-02 (C) to annex the subject property. FINDINGS OF FACTS: WHEREAS, Section § 5-3-150, Code of Laws of South Carolina (1976) as amended, provides a method of annexing property into a city or town by a petition signed by all persons owning real estate in the area requesting annexation; and WHEREAS, A proper petition has been filed with the City of Conway by one hundred percent (100%) of the freeholders owning one hundred percent (100%) of the assessed value of the contiguous property herein described, petitioning for annexation of the property to the City of Conway under the provisions of SC Code of Laws, Section § 5-3-150(3); and WHEREAS, The area comprising said property is contiguous to the City of Conway and meets all statutory requirements for annexation; and WHEREAS, It appears to City Council that annexation would be in the best interest of property owners and the City. Dear Planning Director, I am writing to formally express my objection to the proposed annexation and rezoning of approximately 107.75 acres located on Cultra Road and Oak Street from Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) to City of Conway Medium-Density Residential (R-2). My concerns are as follows: 1. Environmental Impact: The development will result in the removal of a significant number of trees, which not only affects local wildlife and natural beauty but also increases the risk of flooding. Trees play a vital role in stormwater absorption, and their removal could exacerbate flooding during hurricanes and severe storms, which are common in our area. 2. Infrastructure Limitations: Conway’s current infrastructure is not equipped to handle the additional traffic and population growth this development would bring. The city has only two, two-lane bridges for daily commuting. These bridges are in disrepair and will only cause further issues for current homeowners in Conway. 3. Traffic and Road Safety: The roads in and around Conway are already congested. Additional residential development will increase traffic volume, leading to longer commute times, higher accident risks, and more wear and tear on public roads. 4. Overdevelopment Concerns: New housing developments are already being constructed on all sides of our community. This proposal adds to the rapid expansion without adequate planning for schools, emergency services, and utilities, which will negatively affect the quality of life for current residents. I urge the Planning Commission and City Council to consider these concerns seriously and to prioritize sustainable development that aligns with the capacity of Conway’s infrastructure and environmental resilience. Thank you for your attention to this matter. ORDINANCE: ZA2025-09-02 (F) AGENDA SECTION: Consent ISSUE: Final reading of an ordinance to rezone approximately 107.75+/- acres of property located at or near the intersection of Cultra Rd and Oak St from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Medium-Density Residential (R-2) district (+/-65.25 acres) and Conservation Preservation (CP) district (+/-42.5 acres). APPLICANT(S): Development Resource Group (DRG) LLC PIN(s): 325-00-00-0011 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PROPOSED ZONING (upon annexation): Medium-Density Residential (R-2) & Conservation Preservation (CP) BACKGROUND: The subject property is proposed to be annexed into the City for residential development. The property is within the city’s utility service area, thus requiring annexation to be requested. Surrounding developments – Rivertown Row North, Kingston Bay and Elmhurst, are also zoned Medium-Density Residential (R-2). Midtown Village, which directly abuts this property, is zoned High-Density Residential (R-3). A large portion of the subject property is located within the AE flood zone, which runs through the middle of the parcel (see attached maps). While development is permitted within flood zones, provided the affected property meets the required elevation, staff does not support rezoning portion(s) of property within a flood zone to a district that would permit residential development. In 2023, Council adopted an ordinance that permits parcels containing environmentally sensitive areas to be split- zoned, which is otherwise prohibited, with such areas being zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation of property or when property is proposed to be rezoned. The applicant has agreed to zone the portions within the flood zone to CP upon annexation to ensure that no residential structures are constructed within the flood zone. Out of the 107.75+/- total acres, approx. 42.5 acres will be zoned CP upon annexation, and the remainder as R-2. SURROUNDING USES / ZONING: Surrounding in-City zoning includes Neighborhood Commercial (NC), High-Density Residential (R-3), Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), and Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The area is primarily single-family residential, with limited established commercial uses. There is a gas station/convenience store (Sun House) with a few tenant spaces containing limited commercial uses, including a dog grooming business, immediately adjacent to the subject property. Surrounding County zoning includes mostly residential, including Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF20) on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes, and Residential, including mobile homes (MSF20), also on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes. Abutting property is also zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). 19 -- 19 of 164 -- STAFF REPORT Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-09-02 (F) The John T. Henry Auction location is near the subject property, which is also zoned CFA. Horry Electric is also nearby, on the opposite side of Cultra Rd, which is zoned Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI). COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map provides three (3) future land use designations for the subject property. For the portion with frontage along Cultra Rd, the future land use is shown as Neighborhood Commercial (NC). Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small-scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. A larger portion of the property is shown as Conservation Preservation (CP) on the city’s future land use map. Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the CP district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The portion abutting Midtown Village and Conway Christian School is shown as High-Density Residential on the future land use map. Per Section 3.2.5 of the UDO, the intent of the high-density residential district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. PLANNING COMMISSION: PC held a public hearing on the proposed zoning of the property at their August 7th and September 4th (2025) meetings. Several people were in attendance that spoke in opposition to the request, citing concerns with flooding, traffic, overdevelopment of the area, density, using roads within Midtown Village as the entrance to the proposed development, etc. Planning Commission ultimately recommended unanimous approval of the requested zoning upon annexation. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved first reading to annex the subject property at their August 4th meeting. City Council approved first reading of the ordinance to zone the subject property CP and R-2 upon annexation at their August 15th meeting. RECOMMENDED ACTION: Staff recommends approval of Final reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-09-02 (F) to zone the subject property Medium-Density Residential (R-2) and Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation. ISSUE: Approve the reallocation of previously budgeted FY 2025/2026 capital improvement funds from the Dog Park Field project to Soccer Field #1 for sod replacement. The field requires new sod to remain functional and meet program demand. Conversely, improvements planned for the Dog Park Field can be deferred without negatively impacting operations or public access in the near term. JUSTIFICATION • Soccer Field #1 supports a high volume of youth and community programming. • Current turf conditions pose safety concerns and increase maintenance challenges. • Sod replacement is time-sensitive to ensure the field is ready for upcoming seasons. • Reallocating existing funds allows the City to address the most pressing need without increasing the overall capital budget. • The Dog Park Field project can be rescheduled for a future budget year when priorities allow. ORDINANCE: N/A AGENDA SECTION: Consideration ISSUE: A Resolution authorizing the fee in lieu of open space for the University Suites expansion, located on Technology Blvd, in accordance with Section 10.3.9 of the UDO. APPLICANT(S): Diamond Shores Surveying LLC PIN(s): 383-10-03-0020 BACKGROUND: The proposed development is an expansion of the University Suites development located on Technology Blvd. The subject property is 1.75 acres in size, and the applicant is proposing to develop 24 units on the vacant property, which is directly across from the original University Suites development. Both parcels were rezoned to the High-Density Residential (R-3) zoning district last year. Planning Commission granted preliminary plan approval, conditioned upon receiving final approval of TRC, at their January 8th meeting. Included in the preliminary plan approval was a design modification request regarding the appraisal requirements used in determining the appropriate fee in lieu amount, in which Planning Commission granted approval of the applicant’s submitted contracted amount of $569,000 in lieu of a written appraisal from a SC licensed real estate appraiser. In accordance with Section 10.3.9, D.2.b, of the UDO, “when proposed developments require less than one (1) acre of open space, the applicant shall pay a fee in lieu of providing such open space on-site in accordance with this section, with the following exception: if the applicant / developer opts to install and dedicate open space, such area(s) shall not be less than one (1) acre in size and meet all applicable criteria…”. The applicant is providing some open space; however, what is provided does not comply with the suitability standards for open space or the minimum acreage. Per Section 10.3.9, B, the minimum open space required is 1,000 sq. ft. per lot or unit. The total number of units proposed is 24 multifamily units, which would require a total of 24,000 sq. ft. of open space, or 0.55+/- acres. Because less than one (1) acre of open space is ‘required’, the fee in lieu of providing open space is required unless the applicant installs the open space meeting the standards for open space and a minimum of one acre in size. Because the open space being provided does not comply with the suitability standards for open space, the fee in lieu request was submitted for consideration, using the contracted amount provided by the applicant of $569,000, as approved via a design modification request by Planning Commission. Per Section 10.3.9, D.2.c.ii, “the fee in lieu amount must be presented to Planning Commission for recommendation and subsequently approved by City Council prior to preliminary plan approval.” 159 -- 158 of 164 -- STAFF REPORT RESOLUTION: University Suites Open Space Fee-in-lieu As part of the request to pay the fee in lieu of providing open space for this development, the applicant is requesting a reduction in the required fee in lieu amount. Using the amount of $569,000, the following formula is used to determine the total fee in lieu amount: (a) value of property that is determined divided by ( / ) (b) total area of development (sq. footage), then multiplied (X) by the (c) required amount of open space area (sq. footage / acreage) = total fee in lieu (a / b X c = $$). Once that is determined, an additional 25% fee should be added to the amount. a = Total value of property: $569,000 b = Total area of development (total sq. footage of property): 76,230 sq. ft. c = Required amount of open space (1,000 sq. ft. per unit): 24,000 sq. ft. 569,000 / 76,230 = $7.46 / per sq. ft. $7.46/sq. ft. X 24,000 sq. ft. = $179,040 $179,040 + 25% fee added to determined amount of the fee in lieu (Section 10.3.9, D.2.c) $179,040 x 0.25 (%) = $44,760 Total fee in lieu based on the ordinance: $223,800 In addition to the approval of the fee in lieu of providing open space, the applicant is seeking a reduction in the open space fee in lieu amount, based on the following factors: • This project is an expansion of an existing development across from Technology Blvd, University Suites, which has amenities, including an outdoor pool, amenity center, a dog park, green space, and a half basketball court, that will be available to be used by the residents of the new expansion. • While the provided open space does not meet the City’s minimum standards for open space suitability, they are proposing to provide some passive open space onsite. Proposed fee in lieu amount: $52,152.86 This amount was determined by the applicant citing a deficit of suitable open space of 6,991 sq. ft. and using the per square footage amount of $7.46 [$569,000 (contracted amount) / 76,230 sq. ft. (sq. footage of property)]. If this is, in fact, an accurate depiction of the total deficit of open space that would be lacking on-site, should the requirement for the fee in lieu when less than one acre is required not be applicable, the proposed amount does not include the additional 25% fee that is required to be added to the total fee in lieu of providing open space, which was recently adopted as part of the open space 160 -- 159 of 164 -- STAFF REPORT RESOLUTION: University Suites Open Space Fee-in-lieu ordinance revisions, to account for increases in costs of materials and labor over time. The amount, with the 25% additional fee, is $65,191.08. Why does the open space provided in the original University Suites development not count? University Suites was developed as a Planned Development, which was approved in 2007. The requirements for open space were different from what they are now. At that time, 15% of the gross acreage of the site was required to be open space. It was not based on the number of units. Based on the acreage of the original portion (6.78 acres), approximately 1.01 acres would have been required. With 68 units in the original development, under today’s standards, 68,000 sq. ft. of open space would be required, or 1.56 acres. As such, the existing open space is considered nonconforming to today’s standards. PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION: Planning Commission was split 3 / 3 as to the amount of the fee in lieu for the open space that should be required. The first motion that was made was to deny the request, which failed with 3 opposed. Another motion was made to approve the fee in lieu amount, but to require a restrictive covenant that guaranteed the residents would have full use of the amenities already in place at the original University Suites, located across the street. This motion also failed, with 3 opposed. As such, the applicant’s request was denied. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff does not want to discourage infill development; especially when the proposed project is located in the appropriate location. Efficient uses of land, such as infill development, maximizes the existing infrastructure in already developed areas rather than expanding the city outward, limiting urban sprawl. This project, designed specifically for student housing, will help meet the demand for student housing closer to college campuses, rather than adding more demand in the surrounding single-family neighborhoods. For these reasons, staff recommends approval of the Resolution to accept a fee in lieu of open space for the University Suites expansion, in a reduced amount of $65,191.008.
