text: June 2, 2025 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, JUNE 2, 2025 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan and Larry White STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Katie Dennis, Planner; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 30 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Mayor Blain gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. Hyman introduced the interns, Natalia Simmons and Sydney Livingston who were in attendance and Peyton Richardson who was not present. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final reading on the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget - Ordinance #2025-06-02 (A) An Ordinance to levy taxes and establish a Municipal Budget for the City of Conway, South Carolina. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #2025-06-02 (C), an agreement to lease City-owned property located at 214 Magrath Avenue (PIN 339-08-04-0027). C. Approval of a Special Event – 2025 Conway Riverfest – June 28, 2025 D. Approval of Reappointment of Municipal Judge E. Final Reading of Ordinance #2025-06-02 (D), amending a Franchise Agreement with the South Carolina Public Service Authority (SCPSA) F. Approval of May 19, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes -- 1 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 2 APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve June 2, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Longevity Awards – May 2025 – 5 Years: Johnathan Finch, Police; 10 Years: Becky Graham, Human Resources; 10 Years: Ricky Steele Jr, Solid Waste; 10 Years: Russell Dozier, Recreation (absent); 20 Years: Bradley Todd, Planning & Development; 20 Years: Jimmy Stover, Hospitality & Beautification; 20 Years: Larry Elleby, Solid Waste; 25 Years: Robert Cooper II, Construction Services; 25 Years: Bobby Wallace, Fleet Maintenance – Emrick and Jordan presented the longevity awards. B. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing National Gun Violence Awareness Day – Blain presented the National Gun Violence Awareness Day Proclamation to Long and others in attendance. C. Presentation of the Tree City USA Award – Ann Huyler, South Carolina Forestry Commission - Ann Huyler of the South Carolina Forestry Commission presented Dennis and Blain with the Tree City USA designation for the 40th consecutive year. D. Discussion of a request to annex approximately 2.22+/- acres of property located at 1091 E Hwy 501 (PIN’s 367-14-04-0001, -0002, & -0003), and rezone from Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that this annexation request is being considered because of a requirement by Public Utilities. The property at 1091 E. Highway 501, known as South Atlantic Monument Company is currently on the same water meter as the residence located on Amber Lane, which has the same property owner, and as a result of the requirement for the property to have a separate water meter installed, annexation must be requested by the property owner, also requiring that all surrounding property owned by the applicant be subject to annexation. The property on Amber Lane will be considered for first reading in conjunction with these properties at the June 16 Council meeting. The requested zoning for these 3 properties upon annexation is Highway Commercial, which is consistent with the city’s future land use map. Hucks said that Planning Commission will hold the required public hearing on the request at their June 5 meeting and staff will forward their recommendation with first reading of the request. E. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 0.33+/- acres of property located at 1307 Grainger Road (PIN 368-01-02-0007) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Low-Medium Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated that the applicants are requesting to rezone the property from the Highway Commercial district to the Low/Medium-Density Residential District (R-1) to construct a single-family residence. The property has an older commercial structure which was previously used as an auto garage and is currently classified as storage/warehousing, and the legal nonconforming residence that once existed on the property has since been removed. Per the legal description on county land records, the property is identified as lot 21 of a plat from 1941; -- 2 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 3 however, it also includes a portion of lot 20, which was never recorded through a platting action, so the legal lot lines differ from what the city’s GIS maps show. Should the rezoning request be approved, the applicants would need to provide a new plat correcting the issue with the legal lot lines as well as demo the commercial structure that currently exists on the property. The current zoning map and the future land use map identify this property, as well as several other properties with frontage on Grainger Road as Highway Commercial; however, some of these properties contain a residential structure and some are currently vacant. Hucks said that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this rezoning request at their June 5 meeting and staff will forward their recommendation with first reading of the request. Blain said that since the owner has not been maintaining the property it has become an eyesore, and she said that she is happy that the city is looking for another use for the property. White asked if letters were sent to residents in the area. Hucks said letters were sent to properties within 200’ usually 15 days prior to the hearing. White then asked the date of the hearing. Hucks said June 5 at 5:30 p.m. in the Planning and Development building. Butler asked how it was zoned Highway Commercial when it is surrounded by residential. Hucks said that it was probably done a long time ago when the land use map or zoning came into play and the property was being used for commercial at that time. Blain said that recently another similar property was discussed that was Highway adjacent to residential lots. Blain asked staff to consider looking at other commercial parcels that are adjacent to residential neighborhoods. F. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 10.97+/- acres of property located at 1808 Rhue St. (PIN 368-00-00-0002) from the Low Density Residential (R-1) district to the Institutional (IN) district. Hucks stated that the Horry County School District is requesting to rezone this property to Institutional to utilize the property as the school district’s Rivertown complex, which will house the Conway areas adult education program, as well as a limited childcare function, a therapeutic learning center for students, the districts JROTC program and other staff. The request is consistent with the city’s future land use map, which also identifies the property as Institutional. Hucks said that Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on this request at their June 5 meeting and staff will forward their recommendation with first reading of the request. Blain said given the use of the building that she was surprised that the parcel was zoned R1. Hucks said schools are allowed in R1. Goldfinch said he had concerns with this parcel becoming Institutional because if the school district ever decided to sell this property, then everything that falls under that zoning could although have an impact on the adjacent residential neighborhood. Hucks said that educational facilities are allowed in R1, but the new uses go beyond the scope such as childcare, which is not allowed in R1. -- 3 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 4 There was some discussion regarding the Professional district. Hucks said that staff would reach out the school district prior to Planning Commission for a list of uses to choose the most appropriate zoning district. Blain said that when developers or owners meet with staff, she hopes that staff would lean to the most restrictive zoning that would allow their use on the property to avoid encumbrances on the residential neighborhoods. Hucks said that staff do and that the land use map did identify it as Institutional so that is the zoning district that staff would recommend, and staff also makes sure that it is not causing any spot zoning issues. Hardwick said that she agrees with Goldfinch but is glad that the school district is planning uses for the property and not leaving it vacant. G. Discussion of an amendment to Article 5 – Special Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for mobile vending. Hucks stated that this proposed amendment was discussed at the budget retreat earlier this year. Since the city adopted standards for mobile food vending back in 2018, the number of requests that staff receive for mobile vending units nearly doubles year after year. In 2018, staff received 6 applications for mobile vending. This number didn’t increase until 2022/2023, when more than 20 applications were received. Last year, staff processed more than 50 applications for mobile food vending within the city limits. For comparison, the City of Myrtle Beach offers only 20 mobile food vending permits each year and Horry County has a cap of 50 each year for the entire county. The mobile vending permit application process is very time-consuming for both staff and the applicant, and due to state regulations for licensing, requirements for approvals by property owners, coordination with other city departments, the inspections that must take place, and the business license approval process, which is a different process from the mobile vending application, in addition to those that request a franchise agreement with the city, and the enforcement issues that staff encounters with non-permitted food vending units, it has become almost a fulltime job for one staff member a large part of the year. Staff proposes a cap of 40 mobile food vending permits each year, which would be on a first-come, first serve basis. Businesses Licenses, in addition to the mobile vending permits, must be renewed each year; however, many of them do not renew their permit or license but continue to operate, which then becomes an enforcement issue for staff. This cap of 40 would include the 3 different types of mobile food vending outlined in the Unified Development Ordinance, which includes transient mobile vending (such as ice cream trucks), where vendors are limited to a max stationary period of 30 minutes per stop, franchise mobile vending (those having an approved franchise agreement to operate on city-owned property), and mobile vending on private property, which would be those set up on commercially zoned private property for periods longer than 30 minutes at a time. This would not pertain to those mobile vending units operating under an approved special event permit for specific dates. It would also not include other types of franchise agreements that the city enters into, such as Peel Scooters or H2O excursions, which do not have the same requirements as mobile food vending units. Having a cap on the number of vending units permitted each year would -- 4 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 5 not only be good for the brick-and-mortar establishments that sell food within the city, but it would also incentivize those who have been previously licensed to have a mobile food vending permit to renew their license and permit each year so that they do not lose their ability to operate in the city limits if the cap is reached before they have submitted their renewal application. Hucks said that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this proposed amendment at their June 5 meeting and staff will forward their recommendation with first reading of the proposed ordinance. White asked if there are decals with the date available. Hucks said yes, that the mobile vending unit is required to have a placard on bright colored card stock paper located on the unit. Goldfinch asked if the city gives any deference to existing establishments that want to have a mobile operation. Hucks said no. Goldfinch thinks that it is worth a discussion. Emrick said that one option is to change the ordinance so that the cap could not apply to any existing brick and mortar. Blain asked how many food vending permits the city does have now. Hucks said 52 and that the cap of 40 was what was discussed at the budget retreat. Blain said that as businesses do not renew then we would fall to 40 and stay. Hucks said yes, and that staff could put the clause that says that the cap would not apply to existing restaurants in the City of Conway. Hardwick asked if staff would need to revisit the number of mobile food vendors since 52 was a full-time job. Hucks said that she thinks staff can manage with 40. H. Discussion of a request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (f.n.a. Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated that this item was previously discussed at the March 17 council meeting. Since then, it has gone to Planning Commission – both in April and in May, and due to concerns of the Carsen’s Ferry community with the proposed amendments that were initially proposed for Tract A of this Planned Development, the applicant is revising the proposed amendment to allow for only single- family residential as the permitted use on this tract. The initial amendment for Tract A, which is currently one of the 2 remaining commercial tracts within the PD, was to create a “mixed-use” tract, with additional commercial uses on the ground floor and residential uses on the upper floor. Currently, the only uses permitted on Tract A are a baked goods store, café or restaurant, candy or confectionary store, and an ice cream store. Carsen’s Ferry, also known as the Rivertown Landing PD, was adopted in 2007, with the intent of developing a mixed-use development on 28.5 acres of land, consisting of multi-family, office and retail space, and civic use space. Since that time, it has been amended 4 other times – in 2010, 2017, 2018, and in 2022. The 2017 amendment was to permit 50 single- family detached homes in lieu of the multifamily initially proposed on 11.4 acres of the PD, with narrow lots, reduced setbacks, and some portions having rear loaded garages that access an alley. The 2017 amendment also removed approximately 5 acres from the overall -- 5 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 6 PD, which was one of the Commercial tracts, and that 5 acres was rezoned to R-2, or medium density residential, and is now part of the Rivertown Row subdivision. In 2018, Commercial Tract B was amended to reduce the commercial acreage and add to the residential tract in order to permit additional single-family residential, which is now phase 5 of Carsen’s Ferry. The applicant held a community meeting with the residents of Carsen’s Ferry in late April, and the residents were concerned with the proposed uses at that time, which was the mixed-use component of having commercial uses that would lead to increased traffic in the neighborhood and the residential on upper floors in relation to the community amenities for the Carsen’s Ferry residents. The current version of the proposed amendment would continue the same style of homes as in previous phases of Carsen’s Ferry and would eliminate any commercial uses on the property. There could be up to 6 additional homes in the PD if the amendment were approved. Hucks said that Planning Commission will consider the amendment at their June 5 meeting, and staff will forward their recommendation with first reading. Goldfinch asked for clarification. Hucks said if this amendment passed there would be no commercial on Tract A and a very limited amount of commercial on Tract B, which is about 2 acres. Emrick said it is not zoned Highway Commercial and has a very limited number of commercial applications, a bakery, ice cream shop, flower shop, candy store, and a restaurant. Hucks said that with inception of the planned development, this was a mixed use planned development, and it has gone from being a mixed-use development to being a single use with the exception of the limited commercial that remains. Hucks said that staff are concerned that the PD is moving closer to creating a situation where there is a planned development that has a single use and that property was meant to be a mixed-use community. Hucks is not saying that would not be a good amendment for Planning Commission to recommend but staff want to be sure that the state requirement for a planned development is being met. Blain asked how much the city can do to make it remain a mixed-use development. Hucks said that council could choose not to approve the amendment and what the uses are now would remain. There was more discussion regarding the HOA and that the residents in Carsens Ferry said that they were only in support of residential. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-16 (A), to annex approximately 0.38 acres located at 286 Wedding Lane (PIN 367-13-01-0030), and rezone from the Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated that this annexation request is being submitted as a result of the requirement to connect to city utilities. It appears to be a -- 6 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 7 rental property and while the property has been owned by the same property owner since 1979, restrictive covenants were not filed until May of 2025. Due to a name change on the account, the owner was required to request annexation due to the property now being contiguous to other property in the city limits. There have been 4 other properties on Wedding Lane to be annexed since 2017, with the most recent one in 2024. The property currently contains a manufactured home. The requested zoning upon annexation is R-1, or low/medium-density residential, which is consistent with the zoning assigned to the other 4 properties that were previously annexed. It is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. Hucks said that staff recommends approval of the request. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White, to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-16 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #2025-06-16 (B), an Ordinance updating Title 4 and Title 9 of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, in its entirety. Rogers stated that state law requires local governments that establish codes of ordinances to recodify from time to time. Staff reviewed Title 4- Public Utilities and Title 9-Offenses. Many of the updates are minor and correct spelling mistakes, modernizing language, or correct scrivener’s errors. Some sections, while still referring to valid offenses or regulations, are removed to avoid redundancy with state law. Other sections are new and address issues that are not currently codified in city ordinance. Rogers gave a summary of the major changes which included: Title 4 – Public Utilities -Section 4-1-5 – This section is updated to require that if a customer has two payments returned in a six-month period, that customer must pay with guaranteed funds (cash, cashier’s check, money order) for one year. -Sec 4-1-13 – This section establishes a restricted fund that has not been funded in many years. Therefore, it is repealed in this update. -Sec 4-1-14 – Definitions are added to clarify other sections of the code. -Section 4-3-6 is added to codify a requirement that property owners maintain clear access to any public utilities infrastructure on their property so that city staff may easily service such infrastructure. Title 9 – Offenses -Section 9-1-21 deals with noise violations. This section is updated to remove references to phonographs and add digital audio equipment. -Section 9-2 – In this section, the acts of swindling and shoplifting are removed, as they are enforced through state law. This will not affect the ability of the police to enforce violations against either offense. -Section 9-3-1 – This section is repealed, as contributing to the delinquency of a minor is a state offense and is redundant in the city code. -Chapter 6 is added to address prohibitions on public property and rights-of-way. -- 7 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 8 -Chapter 7 is added to clarify regulations against loitering. -Chapter 8 is added to apply penalties for violations of Title 9. White asked if an individual had two payments returned and could not afford it due to loss of a job, how could the city help get the water bill paid. Williams said that staff always work with the residents. Rogers said that there is always the discretion of staff but ideally if in that situation to call in advance. Rogers added an amendment and said that Section 4-3-5 references Ordinance No. 9-03- 25 (B) and it should be 91-03-25 (B). Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White, to approve first reading of Ordinance #2025-06-16 (B) with the correction of Ordinance No. 91-03-25 (B) added in Section 4- 3-5. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSIDERATION: A. Consideration of a Special Event - Palmetto Taps Food Truck Friday – June 13, 2025 – Rogers stated that this request is from Palmetto Taps to have Food Truck Friday on June 13, 2025 from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. Palmetto Taps previously sponsored this same type of event with Smashburger back in April. There will be a live band, tents, 3 vendors and anticipate approximately 250 participants in the parking lot adjacent to Palmetto Taps. Rogers said that if council approves the special event as presented that Palmetto Taps would like to also do the same in July and August and those events could be approved at staff level. Helms requested that Palmetto Taps not set up before 12. Hardwick asked if there had been any complaints. Staff said no. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Butler, to approve the Food Truck Friday special event application for Palmetto Taps and authorized staff to approve the same type of event in July and August. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Consideration of a Special Event – Woodland Lakes Food Truck Friday, June – October – Rogers said that Woodland Lakes POA is requesting to have Food Truck Friday on Shovelers Court, a Cul de sac type street, on June 13 and 27, July 11, August 1, September 5, and October 3 from 5 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. There will be a 10x10 tent and they are expecting 2 vendors each date with approximately 50 participants. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms, to approve the Food Truck Friday special event application for Woodland Lakes. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. Consideration of Acceptance of a Bid for Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall Upgrades (Beaty Street) Construction Contract – Harrelson stated that the city received grant funding to improve the Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall through the -- 8 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 9 South Carolina Infrastructure Investment Program which is administered by the South Carolina Rural Infrastructure Authority(RIA) and funded by Federal, State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds through the American Rescue Plan. The City of Conway advertised publicly, and 3 firms submitted proposals. Staff recommended the low bid of Green Wave Contracting Inc. Harrelson said that if City Council approves the hiring of Green Wave, and RIA approves the choice, the City Administrator would enter into negotiations for a contract with Green Wave for services immediately. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Hardwick, to accept the bid for Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall for Beaty Street from Green Wave Contracting Inc. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. Consideration of a Request for Temporary Closure of an Alley – Emrick stated that this request was from Sean Kabos, owner of Crafty Rooster and Chanti’s for temporary closure of the alley behind the former Chan’s Restaurant for repairs to the rear of the building for 2 to 3 days. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch, to allow the temporary closure of the alley behind the former Chan’s as requested and give staff approval if amendable for additional days if the contractor is acting in good faith. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: None CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: − Emrick said that he was wearing his teal jacket, even though it is not Teal Tuesday because he spent a fantastic weekend with over 18,000 friends at Springs-Brooks Stadium watching the Chanticleers sweep the field and win the Conway Regionals NCAA Tournament. Emrick said that Coastal is headed to Auburn on Friday for Super Regionals and is 2 wins away from the College World Series. − Emrick said that at the last meeting he mentioned that the city’s Strategic Plan is completed. The City’s consultants will be at the next meeting to present it to Council. The Plan is broken down into four primary sections: Economic Development; Workforce Development; Infrastructure Development; and Community Development and Quality of Life. It also includes a Grocery Store Retail Study. − Staff are meeting later in the week with the County to discuss coordination on some of the upcoming Ride IV projects. − The first Downtown Get Down is this Friday night at 7 p.m. on the Town Green. − Conway High School’s Graduation is this Friday. − Skate Day is the 14th at the Billy Gardner Recreation Complex. − Emrick said that those in the know are predicting a hot summer and it seems like a safe prediction. The city is taking precautions with our staff to keep them cool and hydrated. The Police are also patrolling with coolers loaded with cold bottles of water and other cold treats to help cool off our residents. -- 9 of 11 -- June 2, 2025 10 − Staff have received a number of great applications for next year’s Mayor’s Youth Advisory Council. However, there’s still time to get an application in. It’s open to rising 9th through 12th graders who will be based at Conway High School during the next academic year. − Emrick said that Council approved of the Chamber of Commerce Riverfest annual event tonight. This year it will be on June 28th. The headline band is Night Ranger. − The mayor sent us a snapshot of a report that was very flattering to the city. Staff tracked down that full report. A survey of 3,011 vacation travelers found that Conway, our Conway, ranks 2nd nationwide as a city where the locals are most likely to greet a stranger. This survey has also been dubbed the Nicest Cities, with Conway second in America. − Emrick said that there is no Workshop tonight, but several Executive Session items. COUNCIL INPUT: Hardwick said that it is an honor to be a Tree City. Hardwick said that CCU Baseball was on fire this past weekend. Hardwick said that there was much excitement in the community with the Savannah Bananas post and the line dancing events scheduled. Hardwick told staff well done. Goldfinch said that he spoke to former Council member Jean Timbes, and she is doing well. White thanked SCDOT for paving 378 and now is requesting that 701 be mowed. Butler added that great things are happening with the Chanticleers. Butler commended the Conway High School Boys Basketball Coach Michael Hopkins, Boys Golf Coach Brian Rogers, Boys Soccer Coach Andre White, and Girls Tennis Coach Patrick Howle for all being named Coaches of the Year. Blain stated that she would like to present those Conway High Coaches with a Resolution. WORKSHOP: None EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Butler, to enter into Executive Session for the following: (A) Consideration of Appointments to Boards, Commissions and Committees [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70(A) (1)]; (B) Discussion of an Economic Development Opportunity [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (5)]; and (C) Discussion regarding Potential Acquisition of Property in the Jamestown Area [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (2)]. RECONVENE FROM EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Helms to leave Executive Session. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. POSSIBLE ACTION ON MATTERS DISCUSSED IN EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Butler to appoint the Boards and Commissioners to the ATAX Committee as follows: -- 10 of 11 -- -- 11 of 11 --

title: CITY OF CONWAY COUNCIL MEETING PACKET 5.19.2025
text: “I pledge to build a stronger and more prosperous community by advocating for civil engagement, respecting others and their viewpoints, and finding solutions for the betterment of my city.” CITY COUNCIL MEETING CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY, SC 29526 MONDAY, MAY 19, 2025 - 4:00 PM PLEASE SILENCE ALL ELECTRONIC DEVICES I. CALL TO ORDER II. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE – Matt Wilson, Ekklesia Christian Church III. CONSENT AGENDA A. ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-19 (D) to rezone approximately 8.5+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN’s 383-10-03-0020 and -0026) from the Planned Development (PD) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district, and a request to rezone 0.02+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN 383-10-03-0027) from the Planned Development (PD) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in March 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Planned Development (PD) district and Highway Commercial (HC). Two of the parcels include the University Suites Planned Development, with the small .02-acre parcel containing the pump station for University Suites. The other property, across Technology Blvd, is zoned Highway Commercial and is located directly behind the Food Lion shopping center. The applicant proposes to construct 24 multifamily units on the 1.75-acre parcel. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to High-Density Residential (R-3). Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Existing surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: These parcels are located behind the Food Lion shopping center, which is zoned HC. It abuts an established single-family residential neighborhood (Coastal Heights), mostly zoned Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10); however, several lots within this development have been annexed into the city over the last few years and are zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The subject properties also abut property zoned Institutional (IN) that is owned by Horry-Georgetown Technical College (HGTC). The properties are within walking distance to a shopping center, several food establishments, medical offices, a hospital, and both HGTC and Coastal Carolina University (CCU). There are already sidewalks along Technology Blvd, and there are several outlets for vehicular access to Hwy 501. Proposed use of property: Two of the three parcels are already developed, with no changes to those parcels currently planned. One of those developed parcels is the pump station for the University Suites development, owned by Grand Strand Water & Sewer Auth. The vacant parcel currently zoned Highway Commercial is proposed to contain 24 multifamily units. A site plan has been provided by the applicant. The request was reviewed by the City’s Technical Review Committee, and no concerns were provided by any city department regarding this request. 15 -- 15 of 89 -- CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their April 3rd meeting and ultimately recommended approval of the request to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3). However, Planning Commission did express concerns with additional traffic on Technology Blvd; particularly at the intersection with Victory Lane and Horry-Georgetown Blvd, as this area is heavily traveled by pedestrians who visit the Abilities Beyond Barriers establishment (formerly known as Horry County Disabilities and Special Needs) and the SC Dept. of Employment and Workforce. Planning Commission discussed the need for a traffic study of Technology Blvd. Staff explained that for this type of rezoning request, a traffic study is not typically required; however, Article 7 – Streets and Circulation, of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) was amended a few years ago, as part of a broader amendment, giving the Technical Review Committee (TRC) the authority to require a traffic study of any proposed major subdivision development that it determines may have an impact on the road network or functionality, at the expense of the developer. When full civil plans are submitted for review, this will be further studied to determine if a traffic study is warranted for the additional units. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their May 5th meeting. ISSUE: Discussion of a proposed amendment to Article 15 – Enforcement, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding penalties for violations of the UDO. BACKGROUND: Recently, a case being heard in Municipal Court involved violations of both the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) and Building Code. In addition, there was discussion between Municipal Court and Planning & Development staff regarding the authority to issue judgements for those found guilty of misdemeanor offenses in violations of the UDO. The Construction Services Dept. (formerly Building Dept.) has a Code Enforcement Officer, who is able to issue a Uniform Ordinance Summons, in accordance with SC Code § 56-7-80, in addition to Law Enforcement Officers; however, only sworn Law Enforcement Officers are able to issue both a uniform ordinance summons AND a uniform traffic ticket. Code Enforcement Officers cannot issue uniform traffic tickets because they do not have the power to arrest. Because Planning & Development does not have an employee “designated” or employed as a Code Enforcement Officer, staff reached out to the Municipal Associations General Counsel for advice. Furthermore, Article 15 – Enforcement, of the UDO, does not include language referencing the penalties for such violations of the UDO. Currently, with regard to violations, the UDO states the following: Section 15.1.3 Remedies “A violation of any section of the UDO shall constitute a misdemeanor, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction.” Section 15.1.4 Penalties for Violation “Violation of the UDO or failure to comply with any requirements states herein shall be a misdemeanor, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction.” There is no language specifying the penalty for the offense other than it being a misdemeanor or a civil infraction. Last year, an ordinance was adopted to amend Article 15 to include civil infractions and the penalties for such infractions, which was recommended by the Municipal Association. In this instance, the Municipal Association has stated that while the UDO does not cover the issue of an exact penalty, the general code provides language that would include “any ordinance or resolution of the city, or rule or regulation or order promulgated by any officer or agency of the city under authority duly vested in him or it, any act is prohibited or is declared to be unlawful or an offense or misdemeanor…” as stated in Title 1, Ch. 3, Art. C, Sec. 1-3-48: General Penalty; continuing violations of the city’s general code. 41 -- 41 of 89 -- The Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) is not contained within the city’s general code; however, it is referenced in Title 5 of the general code. Title 5 – Planning & Development, only includes Building Regulations, which also includes a subsection (Sec. 5-1-7 – Violations and penalties) that specifies the penalties for violations of building codes, citing the following: Sec. 5-1-7. – Violations and penalties “Any person, firm, corporation or agent who shall violate a provision of these codes, or fail to comply therewith, or with any of the requirements thereof, or who shall erect, construct, alter, install, demolish or move any structure, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, or has erected, constructed, altered, repaired, moved or demolished a building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, in violation of a detailed statement or drawing submitted and permitted thereunder, and in like manner, any condition which is permitted to exist after notice to abate, discontinue, or remove such condition, duly given by the Building Official shall constitute a misdemeanor. Each such person shall be considered guilty of a separate offense for each and every day or portion thereof during which any violation of any of the provisions of these codes is committed or continued, and upon any conviction of any such violation such person shall be punished within the limits as provided by the ordinances of the City of Conway or the laws of the State of South Carolina.” Ch. 5, Sec. 5-5-1. – Unified Development Ordinance, of the general code, only specifies that the UDO is adopted herein, in accordance with Title 6, Ch. 29 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina 1976, amended as “South Carolina Local Government Comprehensive Enabling Act of 1994.” For the sake of consistency and clarity, staff proposes amending Article 15 – Enforcement, of the UDO to include language specifying that violations of the UDO are a misdemeanor offense that is subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances (general code). With regard to the authority of staff in Planning & Development to issue uniform ordinance summons, staff was advised that there is very little as to what qualifications are necessary to be appointed as a code enforcement officer, and the only statute on the matter in SC Code of Laws (§ 5-7-32) states “A municipality may appoint and commission as many code enforcement officers as may be necessary for the proper security, general welfare, and convenience of the municipality.” Planning & Development staff may be appointed as code enforcement officers so that they could issue uniform ordinance summons as a way to have control of the ticketing process through the Planning & Development Dept. Staff believes that through the authority given within the UDO, this has been satisfied. Staff can provide additional information from the City’s general code if needed that provides the entire sections referenced in this report. ISSUE: Discussion of a proposed amendment to Article 4 – Use Tables, and Article 6 – Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding standards for single-family in- common development. BACKGROUND: At a Council workshop last year, staff discussed a proposed amendment to the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) that would allow single-family detached dwellings to be constructed on one property, in common, meaning the homes would be owned by the individual property owners, but the actual property would be owned in common by all participating property owners; much like condominium ownership, or an HPR (horizontal property regime). The structures would still be single-family detached structures; only there will be no common egress or common walls, with the only difference between this type of development and a traditional subdivision being that there are no lot lines. Below are images that depict single-family lots: one with lot lines and the other without for each individual lot. Since that workshop, there has been an increased interest in this type of development. More recently, staff received a sketch plan submittal for a type of single-family in common development, which is included for your reference. ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-02 (B), to rezone approximately 1.4+/- acres of property located at the corner of Davidson Rd and Hwy 501 (PIN’s 383-08-02-0003 & -0002) from the Professional (P) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject properties on April 1, 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Professional (P). These properties are lots 1 and 2 on block 8 of the College Park subdivision (see attached plat of College Park). The lots are currently vacant; however, they are encumbered by power transmission line easements, as are several other surrounding lots, which will restrict any type of development. Lot 1 (PIN 383-08-02-0003) is approx. 0.74 acres and Lot 2 (PIN 383- 08-02-0002) is approx. 0.66 acres. The proposed use of the property is not known at this time. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: These parcels front Hwy 501. Lot 1 is a corner lot, adjacent to Davidson Road. There is nothing on either side of these lots, and properties on either side are zoned Professional. Properties directly behind the subject property is zoned R-1; also, part of the College Park Subdivision. While developed in the county, several parcels were annexed into the city limits over the years, including the lots that front Hwy 501. University Baptist Church is located on lots 1-4 on block 9 of College Park. Declaration of Restrictive Covenants Staff was recently made aware of the existence of restrictive covenants for the College Park Subdivision, from when the development was originally created in 1967, recorded in Deed Book 371 at Page 517 (at Horry County Register of Deeds). Building regulations provided in the restrictions is limited to single- family dwellings only, not to exceed two stories in height. Uses are limited to private family residences together with appropriate and approved outbuildings. Further, the restrictions strictly prohibit commercial activity within the College Park subdivision. The restrictions described within the Declaration of Restrictive Covenants are in effect for an initial 20- year period, and then automatically extended for successive periods of 5 years each, unless an instrument signed by the then owners of a majority of lots within the subdivision has been recorded, agreeing to change in the covenants, limitations or restrictions – in whole or in part. There was such an amendment filed in 1996 for lots 1-4 of block 9 of the subdivision, which subsequently allowed a church with amenities to be constructed on said lots. However, the amendment did not include any revisions to any of the other lots within College Park. In fact, page 3 of the amendment states that “except as changed, amended, or modified 64 -- 64 of 89 -- herein, the subdivision Declaration of Restrictions, and any amendment thereto, shall remain in full force, virtue and effect.” While deed restrictions / restrictive covenants are a civil matter, and it is not required by the local planning agency to determine whether such restrictions exist, once we have received notice of their existence, the local planning agency does have the ability to deny plans that would otherwise violate such restrictions. However, they are not enforced by the local planning agency. More specifically: SC Code of Laws, Section § 6-29-1145. Determining existence of restrictive covenant; effect. A. In an application for a permit, the local planning agency must inquire in the application or by written instructions to an applicant whether the tract of land or parcel of land is restricted by any recorded covenant that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity. B. If a local planning agency has actual notice of a restrictive covenant on a tract or parcel of land that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity: 1. In the application for the permit; 2. From materials or information submitted by the person or persons requesting the permit; or 3. From any other source including, but not limited to, other property holders, the local planning agency must not issue the permit unless the local planning agency receives confirmation from the applicant that the restrictive covenant has been released for the tract or parcel of land by action of the appropriate authority or property holders or by court order. C. As used in this section: 1. “actual notice” is not constructive notice of documents filed in local offices concerning the property and does not require the local planning agency to conduct searches in any records offices for filed restrictive covenants. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their May 1, 2025 meeting, and recommended disapproval. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: With the deed restrictions in mind, while the future land use map identifies the properties as Highway Commercial (HC), if rezoned to HC, it’s unlikely a building permit would be issued for commercial development AND given that the HC district does not permit single-family dwellings, should anyone seek to permit such, the zoning district would no longer allow it, regardless of the fact that the deed restrictions only permit the use of single-family dwellings. Without having evidence to the contrary regarding the continued existence of the aforementioned deed restrictions, staff recommends disapproval of the request. 65 -- 65 of 89 -- Dimensional Standards / Other Requirements: Dimensional Standards / Other Requirements Comparison Current Zoning Proposed Zoning Current Zoning Professional (P)1 Highway Commercial (HC) Min. lot size 7,000 sq. ft. / 10,000 sq. ft. / 1,800 sq. ft.2 8,000 sq. ft. title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES.5.19.25
text: May 19, 2025 1 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, MAY 19, 2025 PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan and Larry White (arrived late). STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: Hillary Howard, Tim Poole. There were approximately 30 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Mayor Blain gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-19 (C) to annex approximately 20.4+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 (PIN’s 326-15-03-0002, 326-00-00-0042 and 337-03-01-0026) and request to rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) zoning districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-19 (D) to rezone approximately 8.5+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN’s 383-10-03-0020 and -0026) from the Planned Development (PD) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district, and a request to rezone 0.02+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN 383-10-03-0027) from the Planned Development (PD) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. C. Approval of May 5, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to approve May 19, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. -- 1 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 2 Blain stated that item IV. E. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome and Omphalocele would be postponed to the June 16 meeting. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Employee of the Month for May 2025 – Public Works – Jenerette presented the May Employee of the Month to Chris Turk. B. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing National Cancer Survivors Day – Mayor Blain presented the proclamation to Will Chappell and others in attendance. C. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing Awareness and Support of National Foster Care Month – Mayor Blain presented the proclamation to those in attendance. D. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing National Garden Week – Mayor Blain presented the proclamation to garden club attendees. E. Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome and Omphalocele – postponed to the June 16 meeting. F. Discussion of a proposed amendment to Article 15 – Enforcement, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding penalties for violations of the UDO. Hucks informed Council that over the last year or so, staff have been issuing more citations for violations of the UDO that end up requiring court appearances and decisions from Municipal Court. There have been discussions regarding misdemeanor offenses and those that are found guilty of violating the UDO; specifically, because the UDO does not provide specific language as to penalties for violations of the ordinance. Hucks said that council approved an amendment to the UDO last year to Article 15, that outlined the penalty for those actions deemed punishable as a civil infraction, which related to signs located within rights-of-way. Staff reached out to the legal counsel for the Municipal Association for guidance, and while they are of the opinion that while 1 – the UDO is not contained within the general code; only referenced to say that the UDO is adopted in accordance with state law – under the Planning Enabling Act of 1994, and 2 – there are a few sections of the city’s general code regarding penalties for violations that include any section of the city’s general code, and one section that states “any ordinance or resolution of the city, or any rule or regulation promulgated by any officer or agency of the city,” staff proposes to make a minor amendment to the language in Article 15 to specify that the penalties for violations of the Unified Development Ordinance are a misdemeanor offense that is subject to the penalties in the city’s code of ordinances for the sake of consistency. Hucks stated that this is further complicated because Title 5 of the general code is entitled “Planning & Development;” however, only building codes are included in Title 5 of the general code, which includes a section for violations and penalties, yet only gives authority to the building official to issue or constitute misdemeanors. The proposed amendment -- 2 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 3 would add “subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances” to the end of each sentence that references violations of the UDO. Hucks said that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on the proposed amendment at their June 5 meeting and their recommendation will be forwarded with first reading of the ordinance. Goldfinch asked for further clarification regarding the state law of the $500 penalty limit. Hucks said that the $500 City’s Code of Ordinance penalty, by the time that you take in any charges for court it would total $1,083.50. Hucks said that if you are found guilty, then there is the option of jail time and/or the fine. Emrick said that every day that the violation exists is a fine. G. Discussion of a proposed amendment to Article 4 – Use Tables, and Article 6 – Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding standards for single-family in-common development. Hucks said that this has been previously discussed with council during a past workshop, within the last year or so. Staff have gotten more interest from developers for in-common single-family subdivisions, which is still considered single-family development, only the homes would be built on one parcel rather than separate lots, like a traditional subdivision is. Currently, there are no standards for such a development within the UDO, so the proposed amendment will include standards, such as minimum separation requirements, ingress / egress requirements, which zoning districts would allow the use, off-sets from internal roadways, buffer / landscaping requirements, among other standards. This type of development is similar to a townhome development – which are considered “single-family attached,” that can be built in- common, and the UDO does provide standards for townhome developments that are built in-common, but not for single-family “detached” dwellings. Hucks stated that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this amendment at their June 5 meeting and their recommendation will be forwarded with first reading of the amendment. Blain asked how similar is this to a scheme where another party might be the owner of a large parcel in which privately owned homes could be situated and Hucks explained the different types of ownership. Blain asked if this is getting closer to the idea where the city or county could own the parcel of land. Emrick said that a housing trust would work whether privately owned or held in a trust. Helms asked if this would help the city to solve the price point where it could get down and be more affordable and that the lots are not so big. Hucks said that it could depend on the type of product, as the city does have residential design standards. Hucks told of a neighborhood where people live that own the houses but not the property. PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST READING -- 3 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 4 Public Hearing and First reading on the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget - Ordinance #2025-06- 02 (A) An Ordinance to levy taxes and establish a Municipal Budget for the City of Conway, South Carolina. Williams informed Council that the FY 25-26 City of Conway Comprehensive budget totals $108,979,864. This is a 27% increase over the current year’s budget. This increase is due to the $9 million re-budgeted items as well as $7.5 million for the 701 SCDOT widening project. Williams said that the proposed personnel changes are as follows: cost of living salary increase of 3% for qualifying employees, $5,000 salary increase for qualifying employees, Christmas bonuses will increase to $1,000 for full-time employees, and 23 new full-time positions. Williams said that the property tax millage will increase by the cost-of-living rate of 3% from 95.3 mills to 98.1 mills. The solid waste collection fees will increase by 5% and the stormwater fees will increase by 9%. Water and sewer rates will increase by the CPI rate of 3%. Utility bills will become paperless by January 2026, and a $2 fee will be added to receive a paper bill after January. Planning and Construction Services will add fees to ensure development is paying for itself. Blain asked for the rationale behind the fees. Williams said that fees are increased each year by the cost-of-living rate to keep up with the cost of living. Goldfinch said that the city talked at budget retreat about what can be done to save the cost, going paperless on the water bill will help save the city money. Goldfinch then said that he fears that the headline will be that the city has increased the budget by 27%. Goldfinch said that the city hasn’t, and every year it is nominal tax increases that line themselves with the cost of living. - David Conti spoke in opposition to the budget. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Jordan to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried Blain asked that before second reading, some attention is given to a request by the Chief of Police relative to staffing. Blain would like for Council to hear more about that request before finalizing the budget. Emrick said that at budget retreat it was discussed to have a public safety consultant come in and analyze the police and fire departments and make staffing recommendations. Blain stated that she would withhold and wait on information from the consultant. Motion: Mayor Blain made a motion, seconded by Hardwick, to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-02 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Goldfinch said that the city is giving a 3% raise, and his understanding is that the county is giving a 5% raise to employees and that is something that the city has to compete with from an employee standpoint. Goldfinch said that the city must balance the budget every year. Goldfinch said that the City of Conway does not have the luxury like the City of Myrtle Beach or Horry County from a tourism standpoint to get revenue offset; unfortunately, the city revenue has to come for the most part from the people that live here. Goldfinch said that under state law the city must roll back the millage so that any increase in property assessments is revenue neutral, and if the city did not have to do that the city would never have to increase taxes. -- 4 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 5 White arrived at the meeting. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-02 (B), to rezone approximately 1.4+/- acres of property located at the corner of Davidson Rd and Hwy 501 (PIN’s 383-08-02-0003 & -0002) from the Professional (P) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that this request was discussed at the May 5 council meeting. As staff explained then, while the requested zoning district of Highway Commercial is compatible with the future land use map designation, staff were made aware of the existence of deed restrictions for the property that allows only single-family detached dwellings on properties within the College Park Subdivision, of which these properties are a part of. While they are currently zoned Professional (P), the P district permits different types of residential, including single-family detached dwellings. The original deed restrictions were recorded in 1967. An amendment was done in 1996 that allowed 4 lots in the subdivision to construct a church, which is where University Baptist Church is located today. To staff’s knowledge, there have not been any other amendments since that time. Additionally, both lots in question are encumbered by 2 power line easements, which take up a substantial part of lot 1 and most of the lot 2, limiting the area of the property that could potentially be developed. If the properties were combined, it may add some developable area, but any encroachment into the powerline easements will require an encroachment permit from the easement owner, which seems unlikely. Hucks said that Planning Commission recommended disapproval of the request at the May 1 meeting and staff also recommend disapproval. However, staff has not had any communication from the property owner as to information contrary to what staff has been able to find, Council could defer or table the request to give the applicant time to provide additional information to staff, seek an amendment to the deed restrictions, or withdraw the request for now. If the request to rezone is denied, the applicant may not apply for a zoning change like the current request for a period of 12 months. Goldfinch asked if staff knew why they had not heard from the applicant. Hucks said no and that the person that came to the Planning Commission meeting is not the actual property owner. Hucks said that she spoke to someone a few days ago that said that they thought the property owner wanted to do single family and Hucks said if that is the case a zoning change is not needed. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms, to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-02 (B). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #2025-06-02 (C), an agreement to lease City-owned property located at 214 Magrath Avenue (PIN 339-08-04-0027). Hyman stated that the city has acquired many lots in the floodplain through the FEMA buyout program. The use of the land must be restricted in perpetuity to protect and preserve the natural floodplain. City Council approved the use of private leases to neighboring property owners. These leases would allow the property owners to use and maintain the FEMA lots for personal -- 5 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 6 use with certain conditions. William West Courtney, owner of 1301 Woody Lane, has requested to lease 214 Magrath Avenue, which is located behind his lot. Motion: Mayor Blain made a motion, seconded by Jordan, to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-06-02 (C). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSIDERATION: Consideration of Acceptance of a Bid for Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall Upgrades (Pine Street) Construction Contract. Harrelson stated that the city received grant funding to improve the Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall through the South Carolina Infrastructure Investment Program (SCIIP), which is administered by the South Carolina Rural Infrastructure Authority (RIA) and funded by federal, State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA). Staff reviewed the 5 bids and recommended the lowest bid from GeoWorks. Should Council approve the hiring of GeoWorks, and RIA approves the choice, the City Administrator would enter into negotiations for a contract for services. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White, to accept the bid for Kingston Lake Stormwater Outfall for Pine Street from GeoWorks. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: None CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: - Thursday, at 1 pm, there will be the celebration of City Hall 200, the 200th birthday of the oldest public building in Horry County. - The Myrtle Beach Regional Economic Development Corporation has an Industry Awareness Class. Next week, they are touring some of the city facilities and hearing about the magic behind the holidays in Conway. - The consultants that are building the Strategic Plan for the City are nearly finished with it. Staff is reviewing a draft copy of the plan and hope they will come to Council and present it in June. This one contains some fantastic information and will be used immediately. - The Parks Master Plan is also nearing completion. Staff hopes to have a draft of the plan in July to present at Council. - The National Register Historic District Expansion is now official. The US Department of the Interior approved an additional 54 buildings and 5 structures in the City of Conway. This opens up tax credits for the rehabilitation of all these properties and acknowledges the importance of these buildings and the role they’ve played in the history of Conway. - The Oasis at Smith Jones Park opens Friday at 4 p.m. - Coastal Carolina Athletics has had a heck of a year, especially this spring. Coastal’s Softball team won 41 games this year, won the Sunbelt Championship and played well in Regionals for the NCAA Championship until their season ended Saturday night. Coastal Baseball has won 43 games, won the regular season Sun Belt -- 6 of 8 -- May 19, 2025 7 Championship and will have their first game in the Sun Belt Tournament Wednesday at 5 p.m. The city is almost certain to host a Regional Tournament in June, hosting three other away teams in hopes of getting to Omaha again. The Track and Field team has had multiple honors. The Men’s golf team won the Sun Belt Championship and went to the NCAA tournament for the first time in seven years. - Horry County Schools asked staff to bring in someone to do a third-party review of the city’s Financial Advisor’s numbers that are contained in the TIF Plan. Rob Salvino, Economist at Coastal Carolina University, has agreed to do that review with one of his summer graduate studies classes. Emrick said that he met with Salvino this morning and toured the TIF District. Hopefully, the report will go well and that will further the conversation with Horry County Schools and then Horry County. - There has been an ask from Council to increase the number of internships that the city offers, especially during the summer months. The city has one that began this week, three more that start next week and another lined up for the fall. In addition, the Mayor has one that will be shadowing her and there will be one in the Fire Department. Also, the city will have 42 summer worker interns in Public Works, Hospitality and Beautification and Parks and Recreation. - There is a Workshop tonight to discuss the Future Land Use Map and its identified uses in the Chicora area. There is also an Executive Session to discuss the employment of an employee in the Police Department. COUNCIL INPUT: Helms said that summer is getting hot and wants to make sure all employees are drinking lots of water. Helms said that the pool looks great. Helms said that she had a good field trip with the Police Department. White said he was not going to jump in the pool this year. Goldfinch said that the groundbreaking at Healthcare Partners on Friday was fantastic and he is excited about the redevelopment of this area. Goldfinch said that for the first meeting in June, Council will have a Resolution honoring Maurice Sheffield, Social Studies teacher at Conway Middle School and his teams that placed in the state and went to the nationals. Goldfinch said that the gentleman that spoke about the budget is having his taxes increased by about $23 so that the city can ensure world class public safety responding to emergencies, world class beautification and sanitation, and staff that puts forth incredible vision. Goldfinch encouraged staff to keep up the good work. Jordan said that Conway High School athletics has had a tremendous year, the golf team is playing for a state championship, baseball team had a great run in the playoffs, and some track and field athletes did the same. Jordan gave some kudos to all the young athletes and soon to be graduates. Hardwick gave a shoutout to the Conway High School Hotshots, the clay shooting team as they did extremely well in the state. Hardwick said that there are lots of good things going on in the city and the schools. Hardwick thanked staff for all their hard work during the budget process. -- 7 of 8 -- -- 8 of 8 --

ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (A), granting a non-exclusive franchise agreement to Mister Softee Mobile Food Trucks (three total) to operate within Collins Park and Riverfront Park. BACKGROUND: Section 5.1.16 – Mobile Vending of the UDO sets forth regulations for mobile vending in Conway. This ordinance allows franchise mobile vending on public property in the CBD, CC, WRD zoning districts and City parks, but only with a franchise agreement approved through City Council. A franchise is an extension of the privilege to use the streets, parking and other City owned amenities for which the franchisee does not have a legal right without permission from the governing body. The franchise agreement allows the franchisee to use City property in the requested manner which exceeds or differs from the customary uses. The franchise agreement is a contract between the City and the franchisee which governs the use of the City property. The agreement does not give exclusive use to the franchisee. The hours of operations and approved locations are determined by City Council in the franchise agreement. A certificate of insurance, as well as a release and indemnification agreement, are also required for mobile vending on public property (which the applicant has obtained). Mister Softee has a “pending” City of Conway Business License awaiting the outcome of City Council’s decision. Mister Softee has requested a “Transient” Franchise Agreement to operate the Mobile Food Trucks at the following locations: • Collins Park – 1001 Sixteenth Avenue (PIN# 338-11-02-0050) • Riverfront Park – 8 Elm Street (PIN# 367-08-01-0003) The requested hours of operation are from sun up to sun down, seven days a week. For a franchise agreement to be valid, it must receive two readings at City Council as an Ordinance. To satisfy the requirements of the City Code concerning franchise agreements, the applicant published a public notice in three (3) issues of a newspaper having general circulation in the City stating the nature of the franchise and the date on which the application is to be presented to Council. The public hearing has also been advertised as required. CITY COUNCIL: City Council held the required public hearing and first reading of the request at their April 7th meeting. ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (B) to amend Article 10 – Subdivision and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding the requirements for the renaming of existing streets. BACKGROUND: Currently, the City has no defined process for renaming existing streets that have been dedicated to the city or naming an unnamed street, with the exception of those being created in conjunction with the development of property. However, staff has received a few requests from different residents of the city to rename a city street in which they resided; the most recent one being a resident of McCray Alley, who inquired about renaming the alley to a different name, which they claimed was for public safety reasons. There is a McCray Rd located off Hwy 701 South with a Conway address, in zip code 29527. Changing of a street name that has been dedicated to the City should be limited and rare, as doing so may have a negative impact on emergency response. However, in the very rare instances that may warrant a street name change, it would be beneficial to have a process in which such requests may be facilitated. Staff reached out to Horry County about their process of renaming county roads. Horry County requires a public hearing to be held for any proposed road name changes. In addition, the property (street/road) must be posted, written notification must be provided to affected addressees, and if approved, a plat must be submitted renaming the road and a new street sign must be installed; all of which incur costs. If approved, the fee schedule for the Planning & Development Dept. will also need to be amended to reflect a $250 fee in conjunction with such requests; however, this fee was one of the fees that was included in the proposed fee schedule that was discussed at this year’s budget retreat. The proposed amendment includes a process for the renaming of a City street, which includes a requirement for a public hearing to be held and two ordinance readings by City Council. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their March 6th meeting, and recommended approval of the amendment to Article 10 to adopt a process for renaming streets within the city limits. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their April 7th meeting. State Code 6-29- 760; and WHEREAS, there is currently no process for renaming existing streets that have been dedicated to the city or naming an unnamed street, except for those created in conjunction with the development of property; and WHEREAS, changing the name of an existing street should be limited and rare, as doing so may have negative impacts on emergency response; however, in the rare instances in which the renaming of a street is warranted, there should be a process established in which such requests may be facilitated; and WHEREAS, this amendment to Article 10 establishes such a process, including application requirements, the requirement for a public hearing to be held by Planning Commission, for two (2) readings of an ordinance renaming such street(s) to be approved by City Council, as well as additional requirements once the street name change has been approved; and WHEREAS, following a review by the Planning Commission and the required public hearing, it has been determined that the UDO should be amended relative to revisions to various items within Article 10 of the UDO. Requests to rename a street dedicated to the City may be approved by City Council through adoption of an ordinance to rename the subject street(s), only after Planning Commission has made a recommendation and review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC). The following provisions shall apply: A. Other than the requested street name, alternative names shall be provided in the event that the requested name is not an available street name. Potential street names shall not: 1. Duplicate or be phonetically similar to any existing street name(s); 2. Be named after any person(s) unless such individual is of historical significance; 3. Include offensive, obscene, vulgar or profane language B. Street Renaming Process 1. Application and/or petition shall be completed and submitted with the applicable fee. a. The applicant must be an addressee on the subject street and have a compelling reason for such request; b. The signers of the application/petition must be addressees for individual properties, residents, or businesses located on the subject street. 2. Requested street name(s) must be reviewed by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) and shall be submitted to Horry County Addressing for availability and reservation (if approvable). 3. Public Hearing required. Once the proposed street name(s) has been reserved, the meeting date in which Planning Commission shall consider the request will be set, in accordance with public notice requirements, and as provided for herein: a. Public notice shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the city a minimum of fifteen (15) days prior to the public hearing in which the request will be considered; b. Individual notices shall be sent to the current addressees of the subject street, and such notice shall contain a description of the matter to be heard. 4. Following Planning Commission’s recommendation and the required public hearing, the request will be forwarded to City Council along with such recommendation from Planning Commission and the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Two (2) readings of such ordinance will be required. 5. Street Name Signs shall be the standard City of Conway, size and color and shall be mounted on steel posts with appropriate brackets. The applicant/petitioner shall be responsible for all materials and labor necessary for the street sign. 6. City of Conway GIS will assign new street addresses once sign installation is completed and will be done in accordance with the street addressing standards provided herein (Section 10.3.20). a. New street addresses shall not be assigned to reflect the name change until the street sign(s) have been replaced. b. Address verification letters may be provided by City of Conway GIS upon request; however, it is the responsibility of the affected addressees to notify all appropriate parties of their change of address (i.e. employer, utility providers, financial institutions, governmental agencies, etc.) 15 -- 15 of 161 -- DATE: MAY 5, 2025 ITEM: III.C. ISSUE: Approval of an Amendment to extend the Franchise Agreement between the City of Conway and SCPSA (Santee Cooper) BACKGROUND: A Franchise Agreement between Santee Cooper and the City of Conway has been in place since 1975, whereby Santee Cooper, as a utility, has the authority under State law to enter into this agreement with the City rather than pay a standard business license. The term of the current agreement expires on June 39, 2025. Under the agreement, Santee Cooper will continue to pay 5% of the revenues collected within the City limits of Conway to the City. 60% of the fees are paid into the General Fund of the City, the remaining 40% are paid into the Underground Utility Fund, which are used to remove overhead utilities and relocate them to underground. The proposed action will extend the current agreement by 30 additional years. 2025 Promulgation Statement Information contained in this document is the Emergency Operations Plan for the City of Conway. This plan provides a framework for use in performing emergency functions during a major disaster or emergency incident in the City of Conway. This plan can also be adapted for use with special events within the City. This Emergency Operations Plan includes the four phases of emergency management. They are: Prevention - those activities which eliminate or reduce the probability of an incident, also known as mitigation; Preparedness - those activities developed to save lives and minimize damage; Response - immediate activities which prevent loss of lives and property and provide emergency assistance; and, Recovery - short and long term activities which return all systems to normal or improved standards. This plan is prepared in accordance with the National Incident Management System (NIMS) concepts and terminology. It will be tested, revised, and updated as required.
