Individual notices shall be sent to the current addressees of the subject street, and such notice shall contain a description of the matter to be heard. 4. Following Planning Commission’s recommendation and the required public hearing, the request will be forwarded to City Council along with such recommendation from Planning Commission and the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Two (2) readings of such ordinance will be required. 5. Street Name Signs shall be the standard City of Conway, size and color and shall be mounted on steel posts with appropriate brackets. The applicant/petitioner shall be responsible for all materials and labor necessary for the street sign. 6. City of Conway GIS will assign new street addresses once sign installation is completed and will be done in accordance with the street addressing standards provided herein (Section 10.3.20). a. New street addresses shall not be assigned to reflect the name change until the street sign(s) have been replaced. b. Address verification letters may be provided by City of Conway GIS upon request; however, it is the responsibility of the affected addressees to notify all appropriate parties of their change of address (i.e. employer, utility providers, financial institutions, governmental agencies, etc.) 123 -- 123 of 124 -- DATE: APRIL 7, 2025 ITEM: VIII. ISSUE: Changes to the Fire Department’s sick leave policy. BACKGROUND: The sick leave policy in the Employee Handbook is more applicable for the “8 to 5” workers, and is not as relevant for the 24-hour Fire Department shifts. The shift personnel only work an average of 10 shifts in a month, so the parameters of 3 times in 30 days or 6 times in 90 days creates instances where Fire employees are missing a lot of work time but are still remaining compliant with the policy. The Fire Department would like to propose the following changes to the sick leave policy: “ unauthorized absence or tardiness or a pattern of absenteeism or tardiness (Guide: One time in a thirty-day period, or three times in a ninety-day period)” RECOMMENDATION: Allow the Fire Department to adopt a separate sick leave policy from the City’s Employment Guidelines. 124 -- 124 of 124 --

title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 4.7.2025
text: April 7, 2025 Page 1 of 11 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, APRIL 7, 2025 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director, Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Kym Wilkerson, Planning and Development Deputy Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: Hillary Howard, Serina Regan. There were approximately 25 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Blain gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (A) to annex approximately 1.42+/- acres located on Bohemia Court and Century Circle in the Atlantic Center Industrial Park (PIN 383-11-02-0003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Planned Unit Development (PUD) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. B. Approval of Reappointment of Associate Municipal Judge C. Resolution accepting Dedication of Roadways & Drainage and the Financial Guarantee for the Roadway Warranty for the Kingston Bay, Phase 2, subdivision (Riverboat Way and Black Lake Way). D. Approval of March 17, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve the April 7, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Employee of the Month for April 2025 – Public Service – Fleming presented Traci Salley as the April 2025 Employee of the Month. -- 1 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 2 of 11 B. Presentation of Longevity Awards – March 2025 – 5 Years: John Farace, Fire; 10 Years: Jeff Leveille, IT – Emrick and Butler presented the longevity awards. C. Presentation of a Proclamation Recognizing April as Autism Acceptance Month – Blain presented Patsy Baker and Veronica Ricardo with the Proclamation recognizing April as Autism Acceptance Month. D. Discussion of a request to annex approximately 20.4+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 (PIN’s 326-15-03-0002, 326-00-00-0042 and 337-03-01-0026) and request to rezone from Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest and Agriculture (CFA) zoning district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the applicant is requesting to annex 3 parcels on Highway 501 and to assign the Highway Commercial district upon being annexed. The parcels are currently zoned Highway Commercial and Commercial Forest Agriculture in the County. The properties are currently vacant. The city’s future land use map identifies the properties as Highway Commercial and low-density residential (R-1). Plans for the property have not been provided, but the commercial uses would extend further than is shown on the future land use map. Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their April 3rd meeting, and recommended approval of the rezoning request. This item is proposed to be on the May 5th council meeting agenda for first reading. SECOND/FINAL READING: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) to amend Article 9 – Landscape and Buffering, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding Landscape, Buffer, and Tree Preservation Requirements. Hucks stated that this ordinance received first reading at the February 3 Council meeting. As previously presented, the biggest amendment to the tree preservation ordinance is removing it from the general code and codifying it into the Unified Development Ordinance, since Planning & Development facilitate the Tree Board meetings and permits for tree removals are issued by the Planning Department. Hucks said that other changes include: - Appeals of the decisions of tree board would be appealable to the Board of zoning appeals rather than to City Council; - Reduction in the threshold for what is considered a landmark life oak tree from 30” DBH to 24” DBH; - Remove Crepe Myrtles and Redwood trees from the protected tree list as well as add the Tulip, Red Cedar, and Tupelo trees to the protected tree list; - Added definitions, clarified the tree mitigation process, and removed certain penalties Hucks said that following First Reading, several issues regarding maintenance responsibilities of trees in certain locations were discussed amongst staff, and whether trees in public rights of way were the responsibility of the city, individual property owners, or HOA’s, as streets within residential subdivisions are required to be public and ‘street trees’ are required to be planted in the rights of ways. Article 9 of the Unified Development Ordinance specifies that “street trees” shall be maintained by the property owner and/or the HOA in perpetuity. However, while routine maintenance of street trees may prevent them from becoming a nuisance or a hazard, there may be instances when the city’s fire or -- 2 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 3 of 11 sanitation trucks may have issues with tree limbs or branches in relation to these trucks when servicing the neighborhood. Additionally, the Tree Preservation Ordinance, as it’s currently written in the general code, is currently under the public works chapter of the code, and their policies and procedures for tree pruning varies from the requirements of the Unified Development Ordinance, in that there is nothing specified that separates from required street trees in newer, residential developments, or from long-established residential areas, even those not within a subdivision, with regard to maintenance of trees within rights-of-way. The general code currently states that the arborist may have hazard trees or public nuisance trees on public or private property pruned in the interest of public safety, and that a notification in the form of a door hanger will be used to alert the residents that crews will be in the area within a 3- day period and contact information will be provided on the door hanger including name and phone number for the city’s beautification department. This was specifically discussed at the recent budget retreat as well. This language has likely been in the ordinance since it was last amended in 2007 and has not been the general practice. Typically, if a tree is a hazard, in most cases, something is done as soon as possible to prevent damage to streets, vehicles, or to prevent injury to pedestrians. Also, our staff typically work closely with public works staff to let them know about any specific areas (outside of subdivisions) that need attention, regardless of whether it is city or state road. Staff also receive a lot of requests from residents for trees to either be removed or pruned that are located within the right of way in front of their home OR on their private property but with limbs extending over the right of way. If the tree is on private property and the tree is NOT a landmark live oak tree, no pruning permit is required. If the tree is a landmark live oak, they must receive a pruning permit from our department. The current amendment proposes to strike through the aforementioned language. The previous paragraph in the same section will have language added to specify that the City reserves the right to prune any tree deemed to be a hazard tree or public nuisance tree, whether on public or private property, in the interest of public safety. Additionally, another section will be added to clarify that any property that requires the installation of street trees shall be required to adhere to the requirements for street trees and the proper pruning of such trees. As with any other standard or requirement within the Unified Development Ordinance, violations of the requirements of the ordinance are subject to penalties, as provided in Article 15 of the ordinance. Since first reading staff also updated the recommended plant list in the landscaping requirement section of Article 9 to revise the mature heights and widths of certain trees and removed the invasive species list and instead specified that no invasive species that is identified in the current version of the South Carolina Invasive Species Exotic Plant list will be allowed in the City of Conway. Hucks said that staff recommended approval of final reading of the proposed amendment, with the changes included since first reading. Hucks said that the next item on the agenda is a repeal of the general code. Blain stated that Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) and Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (D) would be combined. -- 3 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 4 of 11 There was some further discussion regarding hazardous trees due to storms, branches over the neighbor’s fence, neglected tree owners, fees regarding removal of hazardous trees, trees cut from Horry County properties that then become annexed into the city. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve final reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) and Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (D). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (D) to amend Title 3 – Public Works, Chapter 4 – Tree Preservation, and Title 5 – Planning and Development, of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, regarding the Tree Preservation Ordinance. See previous motion. FIRST READING AND PUBLIC HEARING: Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (A), granting a non- exclusive franchise agreement to Mister Softee Mobile Food Trucks (three total) to operate within Collins Park and Riverwalk Park. Wilkerson stated that Mister Softee is requesting a franchise agreement to operate within Collins Park and Riverwalk Park. The requested hours of operation are from sunup to sundown, seven days a week, which is determined by City Council. This is a transient mobile food vending so they would be allowed to go and stop for only 30 minutes at a time, and they don’t have to have a designated parking spot due to the type of mobile food vending. Wilkerson stated that they can also go into any residential or industrial zoned districts. White recommended that Mister Softee also consider Smith Jones Park. Blain asked how many food trucks are enough in the city or limiting the type. Wilkerson stated that both colleges welcome food trucks and staff didn’t want to shortchange them. Wilkerson said that there are 4 franchise agreements and 50 mobile food vending trucks. Emrick said that a limit was discussed at budget retreat, and he feels that staff can handle 50 food trucks but there may be an amendment to limit that number in the future. There was no public input. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Helms to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. FIRST READING: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (B) to amend Article 10 – Subdivision and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding the requirements for the renaming of existing streets. Hucks said that last year, city staff received a few requests from the public inquiring about the process for renaming a public street (owned by/dedicated to the city). Currently, the city does not have a process for doing so. The proposed amendment outlines a process that would allow an individual to request to rename a public street. There are certain restrictions for any proposed names, and there will be an application fee due to -- 4 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 5 of 11 the requirement of the city to notify all affected addressees of the request and advertise for a public hearing. Hucks presented a slide that included an overview of the process, which was outlined in the information provided in Councils packet. First and foremost, there must be a compelling reason for the request. Other requirements include: • Providing alternative names, other than the requested name; • Road cannot be named after a person, unless they are historical significance, the road name cannot include offensive or obscene language; • The applicant must be either a resident, property owner, or business owner located on the street; • A public hearing will be required; followed by 2 readings at city council (posting of property and notices sent to all affected parties); • If approved, the applicant is responsible for the signage including materials and labor costs; • Finally, while GIS will provide address verification letters upon requests, it would be up to the addresses to notify all appropriate parties of their change of address. Hucks said that staff presented the issue to Council during a workshop last year, and was directed to move forward with drafting an amendment to the UDO that would outline a process for renaming a public street. However, any renaming of a public street should be limited and rare – mainly when doing so is in the interest of public safety. Hucks stated that Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the proposed amendment at their March 6 meeting and recommended approval of the amendment. Staff also recommended approval. Hucks said that there could possibly be an issue with public safety for McCray Alley as there is also a McCray Road in Horry County with a 29527-zip code. Motion: Hardwick made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-05-05 (B). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSIDERATION: Consideration of a Request to Change the Fire Department’s Sick Leave Policy – Hendrick stated that the sick leave policy in the Employee Handbook is more applicable for the 8-5 workers and is not as relevant for the 24hour Fire Department shifts. The shift personnel only work an average of 10 shifts a month, so the parameters of 3 times in 30 days or 6 times in 90 days creates instances where fire employees are missing a lot of work but are still remaining compliant with the policy. The Fire Department would like to propose that the following changes to the sick leave policy: “unauthorized absence or tardiness or a pattern of absenteeism or tardiness (Guide: One times in a thirty-day period, or three times in a ninety-day period)” Motion: Golfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to allow the Fire Department to adopt a separate sick leave policy from the City’s Employment Guidelines. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: -- 5 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 6 of 11 - Vonna Gengo – spoke regarding the flooding on her property on Buchanan Lane and asked that the drainage and damage to her yard be fixed. - Hillary Howard – thanked the city for helping make the Waccamaw Sportsmen Expo a huge success. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: - On March 21st the State Board of Archives and History approved the city’s application to expand the National Register Downtown Historic District by 54 buildings and 5 structures. The recommendation from the State now goes to the Department of the Interior for consideration and approval before the official listing on the National Register of Historic Places. This expansion will allow for a whole host of newly added properties to quality for tax credit programs for restoration of the buildings and allow them to receive the proper recognition for the historic contributions that their buildings have made to the fabric of Conway. - The United States Army and its state National Guard divisions regularly conduct training exercises to prepare them for potential needs. "Operation Ridge Runner" is a West Virginia National Guard-led, irregular warfare training exercise that validates the readiness of National Guard special operations forces, active-duty counterparts, and allied/partner nations, focusing on irregular warfare scenarios. In coordination with the SC Army National Guard, they are conducting training locally for the next week to simulate working in densely populated areas with conducting surveillance training missions. They have briefed all local law enforcement of their scenarios and provided copies of their credentials to verify identity. These readiness exercises are designed to develop and test their abilities to work in areas they are unfamiliar with while gathering intelligence to assist in their simulated training scenario. - Summer Camp at the Sports and Fitness Center is full, but Camp Blue registration has begun but will fill up fast. - The cover of this month’s Uptown Magazine from the Municipal Association is, of course, Conway. There’s a great article in there about our Trails Plan and implementation. The city was also featured prominently in last month’s magazine about Public Input in the planning process. And in June of last year, the city was included in two different articles on back-to-back pages. - The Recreation Department has been hard at work on Autism Acceptance Month and Easter - o There is an Art Gallery Exhibition ongoing at the Sport and Fitness Complex from now until the end of the month o April 26th is Sensory Friendly Movie Night, A Bug’s Life, at the Terrace o April 27th is the second annual Professional Wrestling Event at the Sports and Fitness Center and this event is Sensory Friendly o Currently ongoing is the Great Conway Easter Egg Hunt! There are 5 remaining Eggs hidden somewhere in the City Parks with Prizes. Only 1 of the original 6 has been found so far! -- 6 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 7 of 11 o This Saturday at 10 am, South Carolina’s Largest Easter Egg Hunt will take place at the Billy Gardner Sports Complex, with 75,000 eggs filled with candy and prizes. o The Sensory Friendly Easter Egg Hunt is April 12th at 11 am on Field B - The Fire Department has a Badge Pinning Ceremony scheduled for 9 am on the 14th at the Public Safety Building - Reminder of the Earth Day event at Collins Park on April 22nd, from 10 am to 2 pm - There is not a second council meeting this month, so our next meeting will not be until May 5th. - Conway Downtown Alive’s Groovin’ on the Green starts May 2nd and continues each Friday in May. - Tonight, there is a Workshop scheduled to further discuss the Chicora rezoning request to allow for subsidized apartments. We also have several Executive Sessions as printed on the agenda. We should move to the conference room for both. Hardwick asked Emrick when the discussion was had about the drainage ditch on Buchanan Lane, if both properties are within the city limits. Emrick said yes, they are now, but when some of the trees were removed, they were not. COUNCIL INPUT: Goldfinch said that March is Colorectal Awareness Month and recommended that all get a colonoscopy when you are at the age as the city’s insurance will pay. Goldfinch agreed with Howard that the Waccamaw Sportsmen’s Expo was great. Jordan said that Saturday at the Recreation Center there were 1500 kids and gave a kudos to staff. Jordan also thanked the staff that have made the sensory friendly options for children. Hardwick gave shoutouts saying that the Jamboree was great, to Conway High School for the Little Shop of Horrors and Playbill, and to Stella’s for hosting Spirit Night for the local schools. Hardwick said that she loved the new Conway Branding that is going on for April Fool’s Day. Blain commended Conway High’s drum line for being showcased as 1 of the 2 high schools that participated in a HBCU event yesterday. Blain thanked staff for everything. WORKSHOP: Chicora Blvd and 701 N Rezoning Hucks said that this request was considered for first reading at the March 17 council meeting and was subsequently deferred so that a workshop could be held. Hucks gave council the background and said that the applicant was present and will go over the new information that he has provided. Nate Broman-Fulks with Taft Mills Group briefed council on their company stating that they do affordable workforce housing using state and federal tax credits. Broman-Fulks showed examples of buildings that they have done in the past and stated that they do competitive tax credit developments. Broman-Fulks said that last year in South Carolina Housing there were over 70 -- 7 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 8 of 11 applications with part of the criteria being the site itself and the nearby amenities and that this site was in the high demand county and scored the highest among the 30 counties in South Carolina. Broman-Fulks went over the Development Plan stating that they are proposing up to 80 apartments, serving households at 70% of area median income and below which is $60,700 for a family of 4, 2 and 3 story residential buildings with 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom units that are proposed to meet the housing needs of working families supporting the Conway community. Broman-Fulks then went over the site plan showing a larger buffer area with landscaping between the apartments and the Chicora neighborhood, density, property manager on site, and amenities. Broman-Fulks said that since the last update while receiving the feedback is the bigger buffer area and taken driveway off Chicora Blvd. Broman-Fulks discussed stormwater and flooding issues saying that they have guidelines that they have to follow and at worst it will be the same as it is now. Broman- Fulks said what commercial uses could be built there with lots of building and parking areas, traffic concerns, traffic impact analysis, and then the use of the site. Goldfinch asked if the proposal could incorporate a mixed use of commercial with the residential. Broman-Fulks said that the mixed use of commercial and residential is not supported in the tax credit structure. Goldfinch said that this project must be in the city’s best interest and not Taft Mills. Broman-Fulks discussed the opportunity saying it is now as the experts ranked this site the highest of all applications in high demand SC counties and that the housing supports businesses and commercial needs in the area and further added that Horry County hasn’t had a new deal funded in 5 years and Conway hasn’t had one awarded in almost 20 years. Hardwick said that she has many concerns about this proposed housing at this location. Hardwick has concerns with teachers being part of this housing at $60,700 for a family of four as next year a teacher, with no years of experience and a bachelor’s degree, starting salary in Horry County will be over $50,000. Hardwick thinks a lot of the residents will come under the voucher system. Hardwick said that she feels this is trying to be sold to the city for our public servants when in reality she doesn’t think they will qualify at this price point. Broman-Fulks said that this is not government housing, private for profit, or a voucher development but a tax credit development. Broman-Fulks then said that however, they will accept a voucher, but it is not a Section 8 development. Hardwick stated that this brings her to the plan that she has the most heartburn with and that is the flooding at this location. Hardwick is concerned with 80 residential units with a family of 4 with most at risk citizens. Hardwick said that she wants workforce housing but doesn’t think this is the location due to the future land use maps and flooding. White asked about the screening process for the residents, especially for retirees moving here. Broman-Fulks said that a third-party property management company would require a background check, credit check and have to show proof of employment. Broman-Fulks said that because of the fair housing lodging it would not be possible to turn down someone because of them living in another state and as long as you abide by the lease you would be able to live there. Emrick stated that the state only recently recognized workforce housing as a fundable source for the state housing trust plan so it is not possible that there would have been one of these in a more recent time. Emrick said that in the last 10 years, the city did approve Leyland Grove, which is a subsidized senior housing and said that he thought the city had been misled in the presentation that -- 8 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 9 of 11 the city has not had one in 20 years. Broman-Fulks said that this is age restricted to seniors and is not typically considered a workforce housing development. Emrick asked if Broman-Fulks definition of workforce housing is 80% AMI. Broman-Fulks said that there is not a clearcut definition. Emrick said that it is typically up to 120%. Emrick said that what he is having heartburn from is that Taft Mills has gone out and asked for support letters for workforce housing, but their definition of workforce housing defers from what the standard is and has misled a lot of the city partners and the city on what this project is. Broman- Fulks said that they have had lots of conversations and dove into detail exactly what is being proposed and that they don’t mislead ones that they will be partners with. It is a tax credit development serving 20%-70% AMI. Emrick then asked for the definition of low-income housing. Broman-Fulks said he did not know. Goldfinch and Emrick said that it is less than 80%. There was more discussion regarding the definitions of low-income housing, affordable housing and affordable workforce housing. Emrick said that there is a standard definition that HUD uses, and his concern is that there are hard and fast definitions of words that Broman-Fulks was using terms loosely to sale the product and sold that product under those loose terms to organizations that the city does a lot of business with. Emrick said that Taft Mills is getting recommendation letters from United Way, the Chamber of Commerce, and others and sold them the product as workforce housing, which is a need that has been identified but is using a model that isn’t workforce housing. Emrick said that the model is low-income housing, but Broman-Fulks is calling it workforce housing. Emrick thinks it is being done intentionally to get those partners to agree to this and if City Council turns it down, then it looks like the city is turning its back on its partners, which is where Emrick said that he has the biggest heartburn. Emrick said that if this is low-income housing using the definition with the percentage of AMI been given, he then asked if Broman-Fulks had looked at the number of low-income housing units within a mile of this location. Broman-Fulks said no. Emrick said that he thinks that is a massive oversight on Broman- Fulks part because the city has a large community of a broken model housing authority structure that is on Boundary Street within a mile that is low-income housing and is a burden on the city. Emrick said that there needs to be a place with people with housing shortfalls. Emrick said that inclusionary housing is the correct model that can be spread throughout communities and are not pigeon holing everyone in one neighborhood. Emrick thinks this will just add to that broken system and just ignores the fact that it isn’t zoned appropriately, and the city doesn’t have enough Highway Commercial as it is. Emrick said that the city has a future land use map that shows that designation and the city is about to do an area plan that includes this area and probably should consider the future before we put it to something that isn’t there. Emrick said that normally when someone has a proposal like this, they would come to City Hall and ask for the support of the city before you even get to the point of a rezoning and the first time Emrick heard of it being subsidized was after it went to the Planning Commission meeting. Emrick added that the city then starts getting support letters for workforce housing and Broman-Fulks says the project will take section 8 housing. Goldfinch said that 2 letters of support that he has talked to were asked to give so that Council would get in their packets. Goldfinch said that the city knows that we have a workforce need and we would just understand it. Those 2 companies said that they don’t even know what Taft Mills does. Goldfinch said that he also feels misled and doesn’t understand the model therefore he can’t -- 9 of 11 -- April 7, 2025 Page 10 of 11 fully appreciate the impacts of what it may have to strain the city’s resources. Goldfinch said that he can’t support anything if he can’t understand what it is. Broman-Fulks said that a housing authority model was not tax credit housing. He further explained the model. There was more discussion on the definitions of low-income housing versus workforce housing. Rachel Sullivan, the Finance Representative of Taft Mills further explained affordable and workforce housing, stating that 30% of your income is considered affordable housing. Hardwick said that the question before us is to rezone from HC to R3. The city also has to look at our future land use map. Hardwick said that she is opposed to rezoning this piece of property because of how close it is to flood zone. Hardwick wants it to remain HC because when that property floods the business can close its door and she opposes housing because when flood waters rise in the middle of the night and people are in their beds. Goldfinch said that going from HC to R3 but only putting 80 units on 8 acres when Taft Mills said that Conway needs so much more of this. If this is in the best interest of Conway and not Taft Mills, then why doesn’t the city go out and find a developer, rezone to R3 and build 250 units to serve even more need that Taft Mills claim exists. Goldfinch says because that is not in Taft Mills business model. Sullivan reiterated that this is the only method that gives funding. Goldfinch said that he believes that this location is better served as a commercial use. There was discussion of R2 instead of R3 zoning. Hardwick asked what Taft Mills gross income was last year. Sullivan said that she did not have that with her. EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to enter into Executive Session for the following: (A) Consideration of Appointments to Boards, Commissions and Committees [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70(A) (1)]; (B) Discussion regarding a Potential Acquisition of Property in the Downtown Area [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (2)]; (C) Discussion regarding a Potential Acquisition of Property in the Jamestown Area [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (2)]; and (D) Discussion regarding Negotiation of a Potential Contractual Agreement [pursuant to SC Code §30-4-70 (A) (2)]. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. RECONVENE FROM EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by White to leave Executive Session. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. POSSIBLE ACTION ON MATTERS DISCUSSED IN EXECUTIVE SESSION: Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to authorize the Administrator to purchase property Downtown. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. -- 10 of 11 -- -- 11 of 11 --

title: CITY OF CONWAY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA 3.17.2025
text: “I pledge to build a stronger and more prosperous community by advocating for civil engagement, respecting others and their viewpoints, and finding solutions for the betterment of my city.” CITY COUNCIL MEETING CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY, SC 29526 MONDAY, MARCH 17, 2025 - 4:00 PM PLEASE SILENCE ALL ELECTRONIC DEVICES I. CALL TO ORDER II. INVOCATION/PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE – Matt Wilson, Ekklesia Christian Church III. CONSENT AGENDA A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (A) to rezone approximately 0.74+/- acres of property located on Sixteenth Avenue, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01- 0049) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (B) to annex approximately 0.37+/- acres of property located at 116 Clemson Rd (PIN 383-10-01-0018) from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. C. Approval of Mutual Aid and Law Enforcement Support Agreement with the City of North Myrtle Beach D. Approval of February 18, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes E. ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (A), to rezone approximately 0.74+/- acres of property located on Sixteenth Ave, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01-0049) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in late December 2024. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential. The property is currently vacant. The proposed use of the property has not been disclosed by the applicant; however, the applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Zoning District of Subject Property: Per Section 3.2.9 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the NC district is intended to provide small scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the NC district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. Village Corridor Overlay(VCO) district: This property is also located within the Village Corridor Overlay (VCO). Per Section 3.4.3 of the UDO, the intent of the VCO shall be used to promote compact, pedestrian-scale development with residential, neighborhood commercial, professional, and office uses. The Village Corridor Overlay zoning shall include all properties fronting on minor arterials and collector streets designated on the zoning map. Additionally, per Section 6.5.3, A. – Purpose, of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), “the VCO is established to provide unified development that promotes a sense of place and provides opportunities to develop projects engineered to be compatible with the carrying capacity of minor arterials and collector streets.” Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: A portion of the property abuts property zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and abuts property zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) on one side that is used commercially (was occupied by a cosmetology school at one time) and the other side is also zoned R-1 but currently vacant. Behind the property is a split-zoned parcel, zoned R-1 and HC, with the frontage of that property being on Elizabeth Street. There is also a 10-ft construction easement that runs along one side of the subject property that appears to have been created when additional right-of-way was deeded to SCDOT in 2007. 4 -- 4 of 169 -- Dimensional Standards / Other Requirements: Dimensional Standards Comparison Current Zoning (R-1) Proposed Zoning (NC) Min. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their February 6th meeting and recommended approval of the request to rezone the property to NC. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their February 18th meeting. WHEREAS, pursuant to Title 6, Chapter 29 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, the City of Conway enacted the Zoning Ordinance of the City of Conway, South Carolina; and WHEREAS, Article 13, Section 13.1.7 of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) provides that regulations, restrictions, and boundaries set forth in the UDO may be amended, supplemented, changed, or repealed in accordance with S.C. Code §6-29-760; and WHEREAS, a petition has been submitted to rezone approximately 0.74+/- (total) acres located on Sixteenth Ave, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01-0049) from the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district; and WHEREAS, the Planning Commission of the City of Conway, on February 6, 2025, held the required public hearing to discuss the request to rezone from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district, and made their recommendation; and WHEREAS, City Council determined that it is in the best interest of the health, safety, and general welfare of the City of Conway and its citizens to approve the rezoning petition as presented. BACKGROUND: The annexation application was submitted by the property owner, Margaret Lisa Wines, as a requirement for a name change to the city utility services account. According to Horry County Land Records, the deed was transferred into the owner’s name on December 2, 2024. The property is within the Coastal Heights subdivision near Hwy 544. There is an existing single-family structure on the property. Restrictive covenants were recorded for this property February 6, 2025. The adjacent property was annexed into the City in 2022. Several other properties within the Coastal Heights subdivision have been annexed over the years; most of them being on Clemson Road, and some located on University and Lander Drive. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies this property as Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). The intent of the R-1 District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their February 18th meeting. RECOMMENDATION Authorize approval of Memorandum of Understanding with North Myrtle Beach Police Department. 25 -- 25 of 169 -- 1 State of South Carolina ) MUTUAL AID AND LAW ENFORCEMENT ) SUPPORT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE County of Horry ) CITY OF NORTH MYRTLE BEACH AND THE CONWAY POLICE DEPARTMENT WHEREAS, the Law Enforcement and Support Act (the Act), beginning at § 23-20-10 et seq. of the South Carolina Code of Laws, § 23-20-30 provides “Any county, incorporated municipality, or other political subdivision of this State may enter into mutual aid agreements for the proper and prudent exercise of public safety functions. All agreements must adhere to the requirements contained in § 23-20-40”; and WHEREAS, § 23-20-20(4) of the Act defines a Mutual Aid Agreement as “any agreement entered into on behalf of a law enforcement agency in this State for the purpose of providing the proper and prudent exercise of public safety functions across jurisdictional lines, including, but not limited to, multijurisdictional task forces, criminal investigations, patrol services, crowd control, traffic control and safety, and other emergency service situations. Such agreements must not be permitted for the sole purpose of speed enforcement”; and WHEREAS § 23-20-20 also defines the following as: (1) "Law enforcement agency" means any state, county, municipal, or local law enforcement authority that enters into an agreement for the procurement of law enforcement support services. (2) "Law enforcement provider" means any in-state or out-of-state law enforcement authority that provides law enforcement services to a law enforcement agency pursuant to this chapter. (3) "Law enforcement services" means any law enforcement assistance or service performed by a certified law enforcement officer; and (4) "Mutual aid agreement" means any agreement entered into on behalf of a law enforcement agency in this State for the purpose of providing the proper and prudent exercise of public safety functions across jurisdictional lines, including, but not limited to, multijurisdictional task forces, criminal investigations, patrol services, crowd control, traffic control and safety, and other emergency service situations. Such agreements must not be permitted for the sole purpose of speed enforcement. 26 -- 26 of 169 -- 2 WHEREAS § 23-20-40 provides (A) All mutual aid agreements for law enforcement services must be in writing and include, but may not be limited to, the following: (1) a statement of specific services to be provided; (2) specific language dealing with financial agreements between the parties; (3) specification of the records to be maintained concerning the performance of services to be provided to the agency; (4) language dealing with the duration, modification, and termination of the agreement; (5) specific language dealing with the legal contingencies for any lawsuits or the payment of damages that arise from the provided services; (6) a stipulation as to which law enforcement authority maintains control over the law enforcement provider’s personnel; (7) specific arrangements for the use of equipment and facilities; and (8) specific language dealing with the processing of requests for information pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act for public safety functions performed or arising under these agreements. (B) Except as provided in subsection (C), a mutual aid agreement entered into on behalf of a law enforcement authority must be approved by the appropriate governing bodies of each concerned county, incorporated municipality, or other political subdivision of this State. Agreements entered into are executed between governing bodies, and, therefore, may last until the agreement is terminated by a participating party of the agreement. (C) An elected official whose office was created by the Constitution or by general law of this State is not required to seek approval from the elected official’s governing body in order to participate in mutual aid agreements. NOW THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE CODE OF LAWS OF SOUTH CAROLINA, SECTION 23-20-10 ET SEQ, THE NORTH MYRTLE BEACH POLICE DEPARTMENT (NMBPD) AND CONWAY POLICE THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS: 1. TEMPORARY TRANSFER OF OFFICERS, SPECIFIC SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED, MODIFICATION AND TERMINATION OF AGREEMENT: (a) CPD shall provide Officers on a temporary basis to provide law enforcement services in the City of North Myrtle Beach, South Carolina during the Memorial Day Bike Event beginning on May 22, 2025 through May 26, 2025. The Agreement shall be effective for the period beginning at 12:00 a.m. on May 23, 2025, and ending at 11:59 p.m. on May 26, 2025. However, the CPD shall not be required to begin providing assistance until May 23, 2025 continuing through May 26, 2025 unless otherwise requested by the City of North Myrtle Beach to 27 -- 27 of 169 -- 3 commence providing services prior to May 23, 2025 during the above referenced effective period. (b) The specific law enforcement services that the CPD shall provide include, but are not limited to, patrol services, crowd control, and traffic control. (c) This agreement shall terminate, as indicated in paragraph 1(a) on Monday, May 26, 2025 at 11:59 pm. This agreement shall not be modified unless both parties consent, in writing, to a modification. The terms of the modification shall be in writing and shall become a part of the original Agreement. 2. AUTHORITY (a) The North Myrtle Beach City Council has approved this Agreement and has authorized the CPD to request the temporary transfer of law enforcement officers from the CPD to the extent of available personnel and equipment not required for the adequate protection of the remainder of City of Conway. The Police Chief or commanding officer of the CPD shall determine the amount of personnel and equipment available for law enforcement aid in North Myrtle Beach. The decision of the Police Chief or the commanding officer of the CPD shall be final. (b) The City of Conway authorizes the Chief of the CPD or his designee to render temporary law enforcement aid to the NMBPD to the extent of available personnel and equipment not required for adequate protection of the remainder of the City of Conway. (c) Law enforcement officers from the CPD acting under this Agreement shall be commanded by superior authority from within the CPD to maintain the peace or perform duties in the municipality of North Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. While in North Myrtle Beach, officers from the CPD shall be under the direction and authority of a designated person from the CPD. The designated person from the CPD with authority over the officers from the CPD shall in turn be under the direction and authority of Chief of Police for the NMBPD or the Chief’s designee. Officers from the CPD transferred to perform law enforcement duties within the City of North Myrtle Beach shall have all powers and authority of a law enforcement officer employed by the City of North Myrtle Beach. The bond for any officer transferred from the CPD shall include coverage for his/her activity in the municipality of North Myrtle Beach in the same manner and to the same extent provided by bonds of officers employed by the NMBPD. 3 COMPENSATION The NMBPD shall provide a fifty dollar ($50) per diem to each officer from the CPD transferred to the municipality of North Myrtle Beach pursuant to this Agreement. In addition, the NMBPD shall provide lodging for each officer from the CPD transferred to the municipality of North Myrtle Beach pursuant to this Agreement. The NMBPD shall also reimburse the CPD the rate of salary or the hourly rate of wages for each officer transferred from the CPD. Such reimbursement for each officer shall include any 28 -- 28 of 169 -- 4 overtime and any applicable state and federal taxes and SCPORS contributions. CPD shall submit an invoice to the NMBPD within thirty (30) days from May 26, 2025 regarding reimbursement for officers transferred pursuant to this Agreement. Reimbursement shall not include travel expenses. Other than the compensation to be paid to the CPD as indicated above, the NMBPD shall not be obligated to pay additional remuneration to the CPD however, in in the event any extraordinary cost is incurred by the CPD in the rendering of law enforcement services pursuant to this Agreement, the CPD may submit a request for compensation to off-set any extraordinary cost. The NMBPD shall not unreasonably withhold payment to the CPD for any extraordinary costs incurred by the CPD while rendering law enforcement services pursuant to this Agreement. The temporary transfer of officers from the CPD to the NMBPD pursuant to this Agreement shall in no manner affect or reduce the compensation, pension, or retirement rights of transferred or assigned officers and such officers shall continue to be paid by the City of Conway where such officers are permanently employed. 4. LIABILTY (a) To the extent permitted by law, and without waiving sovereign immunity, each agency shall be responsible for any and all claims, demands, suits, actions, damages and causes of action related to or arising out of or in any way connected with its own actions and the actions of its personnel in providing law enforcement services under this agreement. (b) The NMBPD and the City of North Myrtle Beach shall not be responsible for reimbursing any amounts paid or due as benefits to employees of the CPD or the City of Conway under the terms of the South Carolina Workers’ Compensation Act due to personal injury or death occurring while such employees are engaged in rendering aid under this Agreement. The NMBPD and the City of Conway shall be responsible for payment of compensation and benefits only to their respective employees. (c) All individuals retain all compensation, pension, retirement and disability rights while performing duties in accordance with this agreement, and all officers shall continue to be paid by the entity where they are permanently employed as of the dates services are rendered. (d) This Agreement shall not be construed as, or deemed to be, an agreement for the benefit of any third party or parties. No third party or parties shall have any right of action under this agreement for any cause of action whatsoever. 29 -- 29 of 169 -- 5 5. EQUIPMENT AND FACILITIES The CPD may utilize equipment from its own agency, if approved of by the Chief of Police for the NMBPD or his designee, in carrying out law enforcement services pursuant to this Agreement. 6. RECORDS In the event that it is necessary for any officer with the CPD to issue a uniform traffic ticket, prepare an incident report, traffic accident report, and/or prepare any document(s) necessary for the issuance of an arrest warrant, the originals of the above stated documents shall remain with and be maintained by the NMBPD. In the event it is necessary for an officer with the CPD to return to the City of North Myrtle Beach to aid in the prosecution of any traffic citation issued or arrest warrant obtained by, or with the assistance of, any officer from the CPD while he/she was performing law enforcement services pursuant to this Agreement, such officer shall reasonably cooperate with the NMBPD to return to North Myrtle Beach for the purpose of providing testimony if the matter is to be disposed of via bench trial or jury trial. The NMBPD shall pay for the officer’s mileage at the prevailing IRS mileage rate. 7. WORKSHOP: Twin Oaks Drive Annexation – Hucks informed Council that the applicant approached staff about the possibility of annexing property on Twin Oaks Drive. The proposed to be annexed property is contiguous to the Collins Jollie development, which is currently being developed as a conservation subdivision. The City’s utility service area ends at the start of Twin Oaks Drive, which is directly off Highway 65, with two parcels on one side of Twin Oaks within the utility service area (water and sewer). The property proposed to be annexed is contiguous via land, abutting one of the developments within the Collins Jollie Conservation Subdivision; however, it is not contiguous via travel way. The closest property on Highway 65 that is within the city limits is the Hainer Place development; approximately 2 miles from the property proposing annexation. Twin Oaks Drive is a dead-end road and there would not be any connection via the Collins Jollie development that would connect this property to Collins Jollie Road. Being that it’s not within the utility service area, future land use is not identified, although nearby properties that are within the service area are identified as Conservation Preservation (CP); likely due to either wetlands that are identified on those properties or flood zones that may exist. Council discussed the property being in the county versus being in the city, where the city would have control over the development. Council discussed the property being a Conservation Subdivision, creating a donut hole, service area, and access via roadways. ISSUE: Discussion of a request to amend the Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (f.n.a. Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). BACKGROUND: The Rivertown Landing Planned Development (PD) district, now Carsen’s Ferry, was originally created in 2007 out of 28.55 acres off Hwy 501 at Riverport Dr. The stated purpose was to “create a walkable, mixed-use community featuring multi-family residential, civic, commercial, and office space in the City of Conway.” Until 2015/2016, the only thing that had been developed in this community was the clubhouse and pool. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: Amended to increase the height allowance for Carsen’s Ferry multifamily project from 40 feet to 52 feet and reduce the total residential units from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: removed all commercial and multifamily from the rear most parcels and replaced them with single-family homes on 50 small individual lots. This created a traditional neighborhood layout / development style (i.e. The Village at Country Club) with 1 and 2-story traditional craftsman and low-country style homes spaced closely together, ranging from 1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft. 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres of a designated as commercial was amended and added to allow additional single-family residential, which now makes up phase 5 of the development, which contains an additional 18 single-family dwellings and with the same requirements as the previous 4 phases. This left approx. 1.5 acres of Commercial acreage for commercial development. 2022 amendment: amended the permitted uses in what was remaining of Commercial Tract B to include any use permitted in the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Proposed 2025 amendment: amend the permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, which includes approx. 4.24+/- acres, to allow a combination of residential, professional, and other limited commercial uses on the upland portion of the property, or mixed- use development, leaving the remainder as open space and a master-planned stormwater system. Current Zoning: The intent of the current zoning, a Planned Development (PD) district, per Section 3.3.2 of the UDO, is to provide for large-scale, quality development projects (3 acres and larger) with mixed land uses which create a superior environment through unified development and provide for the application of design ingenuity while protecting surrounding developments. 47 -- 47 of 169 -- COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies the subject property as Planned Development (PD) and Conservation Preservation (CP). Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the Conservation Preservation (CP) district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. PLANNING COMMISSION: The Technical Review Committee (TRC) is currently reviewing the proposed amendments. Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on the proposed amendments at their April 3, 2025 meeting. If a recommendation is provided at that time, it will be forwarded to Council for first reading. ISSUE: Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 8.5+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN’s 383-10-03-0020 and -0026) from the Planned Development (PD) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district, and a request to rezone 0.02+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN 383-10-03-0027) from the Planned Development (PD) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in March 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Planned Development (PD) district and Highway Commercial (HC). Two of the parcels include the University Suites Planned Development, with the small .02-acre parcel containing the pump station for University Suites. The other property, across Technology Blvd, is zoned Highway Commercial and is located directly behind the Food Lion shopping center. The applicant proposes to construct 24 multifamily units on the 1.75-acre parcel. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to High-Density Residential (R-3). Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: These parcels are located behind the Food Lion shopping center, which is zoned HC. It abuts an established single-family residential neighborhood (Coastal Heights), mostly zoned Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10); however, several lots within this development have been annexed into the city over the last few years and are zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The subject properties also abut property zoned Institutional (IN) that is owned by Horry-Georgetown Technical College (HGTC). The properties are within walking distance to a shopping center, several food establishments, medical offices, a hospital, and both HGTC and Coastal Carolina University (CCU). There are already sidewalks along Technology Blvd, and there are several outlets for vehicular access to Hwy 501. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on the request at their April 3rd meeting. ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (D) to rezone approximately 7.8+/- acres of property located on (North) Main Street and Chicora Blvd (PIN 338-03-02-0006) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in January 2025. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently vacant. The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3) in order to develop the property as multifamily; more specifically, a workforce housing community. Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) District: The subject property is also within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 3.4.2 of the UDO, the intent of the overlay district is to create a commercial corridor that is well planned and attractive through the implementation of consistent design standards. The provisions of this section will ensure that the design quality of new development in the city’s identified gateway corridors are held to high standards. This section (GCO) shall not apply to detached single-family residential dwellings being used for residential purposes. Per Section 6.5.2, A. – Purpose, of the UDO, the GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors are their primary means of access. Per Section 6.5.2, B. – Applicability, the GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of-way line on properties along these highways (90, 378, 501, 501 Bus., 701 (South and North), and 905). Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The subject property abuts the Chicora development, a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 (low/medium-density residential). Other properties beside and across from the subject property are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). There is no other property zoned R-3 (high-density residential) in the nearby surrounding area. The property on the opposite side of Chicora Blvd (currently vacant) had previously been proposed and approved for a grocery store (KJ’s) to be developed. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, 115 -- 115 of 169 -- reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their March 6th meeting and recommended disapproval of the request to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3), although it was not unanimous. Several residents of the Chicora neighborhood were present and gave public input, in opposition to the request. Their concerns included traffic along Chicora Blvd and Hwy 701, crime, stormwater drainage and flooding issues. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Workforce housing and affordable / attainable housing is needed in and around Conway. The costs of housing has increased significantly over the past several years; specifically post-Covid, with many people relocating to the area from other parts of the country, the shortage in housing supply, as well as inflation. Adequate housing is not always attainable for many individuals who work in and around our community, such as our teachers, nurses, police, firefighters, and others in similar professions, as these individuals make too much money to qualify for low-income housing and not enough money to purchase a home. While housing affordability is an issue, it is a much broader issue than just the zoning of property. Lack of affordability / attainability of housing cannot be solved just by rezoning properties to districts that allow higher density. Zoning districts which would allow higher densities could add to the housing supply if properties are developed as zoning (density) allows, but what must be considered when reviewing a request to rezone property is whether the requesting zoning is appropriate for the subject property. Staff must first consult the Comprehensive Plan to see if the proposed rezoning is consistent with the plan and the future land use map. This annexation includes all waterways, roads, and rights-of-way adjacent to the property. For a more specific description of said property, please see attached map. SECTION 2. APPLICATION OF ZONING ORDINANCE: The property is admitted as City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential District (R-1) area under the zoning laws of the municipality. SECTION 3. EFFECTIVE DATE: The annexation is effective as of the date of the final reading of this Ordinance. AND BE IT FURTHER ORDAINED that such changes shall be made on the Official Zoning Map.
