title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 3.17.2025
text: March 17, 2025 Page 1 of 9 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, MARCH 17, 2025 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Larry White. ABSENT: Justin Jordan STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director, Becky Graham, Human Resource Deputy Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Chris Weatherford, Public Utilities Deputy Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: Julie Hartman. There were approximately 25 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Matt Wilson of Ekklesia Christian Church gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (A) to rezone approximately 0.74+/- acres of property located on Sixteenth Avenue, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01-0049) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (B) to annex approximately 0.37+/- acres of property located at 116 Clemson Rd (PIN 383-10-01-0018) from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. C. Approval of Mutual Aid and Law Enforcement Support Agreement with the City of North Myrtle Beach D. Approval of February 18, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes E. Approval of FY 2025-2026 Budget Retreat Minutes F. Approval of the Appointments to the Grievance Committee -- 1 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 2 of 9 APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve the March 17, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Employee of the Month for March 2025 – Public Safety – Long presented Officer Vincent Taggart as the March 2025 Employee of the Month. B. Presentation of Longevity Awards – February 2025 – 5 Years: Jessica Stalvey, Recreation; 10 Years: Adam Emrick, Administration; 10 Years: Shane Carter, Police – Emrick and Goldfinch presented Stalvey and Carter with their longevity awards. Blain and Goldfinch presented Emrick with his longevity award. C. Presentation of Events for Autism Acceptance Month to be held in April – Recreation employees Patsy Baker and Veronica Ricardo presented Council with events for Autism Acceptance Month to be held in April. Blain stated that a Resolution for Autism Acceptance Month would be presented at the next Council meeting. D. Presentation by SK8Conway – Billy Staples gave a presentation to Council on the benefits and need for a skatepark in the city. Goldfinch stated that a skatepark had been discussed and would be included in the parks plan. E. Update on the Parks Master Plan – Jessica Wise of Greenberg Farrow and Keith Rodenhauser of Brandstetter Carroll gave an update on the progress of the Parks Master Plan. F. Discussion of a request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (f.n.a. Rivertown Landing PD), regarding the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated this this property is part of the Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development, which was created in 2007, and was originally called Rivertown Landing. The applicants are seeking to amend a portion of this Planned Development, for the tract known as Tract A on their master site plan. There have been several previous amendments to the Carsen’s Ferry PD; one in 2010, one in 2017, another in 2018 and in 2022. Most of these amendments included revisions to the commercial tracts that would permit additional single-family dwellings to be constructed. Tract A sits between the amenity parcel for the development and the existing restaurant that has frontage on Highway 501. Currently the permitted uses for Tract A are limited to baked goods stores, cafes, restaurants, candy or confectionery stores, or ice cream stores. The applicant would like to expand the list of permitted uses on this tract to include additional professional services and retail uses, such as a dance or fitness studio, pet spa, clothing or specialty store, or beauty salons. A true mixed-use style development would include buildings that contain commercial uses on the ground level of buildings and residential uses on upper floors of buildings. The amendment would allow for mixed use of the property, consisting of residential, professional and other commercial uses. Hucks -- 2 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 3 of 9 said that staff are reviewing the documents and site plan submitted with the request, and Planning Commission will hold a public hearing on the request at their April 3 meeting. G. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 8.53+/- acres located on Technology Blvd (PIN’s 383-10-03-0020, and -0026) from the Planned Development (PD) district and Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district, and a request to rezone 0.02+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN 383-10-03-0027) from the Planned Development (PD) district to the High- Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated that this request includes 3 parcels; 2 of which are known as the University Suites Planned Development, with one being the pump station parcel for the development. The other parcel is currently vacant and currently zoned Highway Commercial. The applicant is requesting to rezone these 3 parcels to the High- Density Residential District (R-3) in order to construct 24 additional units on the vacant property zoned Highway Commercial, across from the University Suites development. The applicant did include a site plan with their rezoning application that illustrates the proposed development. Rezoning the existing Planned Development to R-3 allows not only for the vacant parcel currently zoned HC to apply to be rezoned to R-3 and not be considered spot zoning or having to request a future land use map amendment, but it also removes the nonconformity of the Planned Development, in that PD’s are required to contain a mix of uses, both residential and commercial, and this PD is strictly residential, with no commercial uses on the property. Hucks said that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this request at their April 3 meeting. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (A) to annex approximately 1.42+/- acres located on Bohemia Court and Century Circle in the Atlantic Center Industrial Park (PIN 383-11-02-0003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Planned Unit Development (PUD) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated that this property is located within the Atlantic Center Industrial Park and is currently zoned Horry County Planned Unit Development. The property is currently vacant, but the application was likely submitted because there is intent to develop the site. The applicant is requesting to rezone the property Light Industrial upon annexation, which is consistent with other properties in the industrial park that are within the city limits. The city’s future land use map also identifies the property as Light Industrial. Hucks said that Planning Commission considered the request at their March 17 meeting and recommended approval. Staff also recommends approval of the request to annex and rezone the property as Light Industrial. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (B) to annex approximately 0.17+/- acres located at 1073 Waccamaw Drive (PIN 368-13-03-0004), and request to rezone from the Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF10), district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated that this annexation request was submitted as a result of a name change to the city utility account. The property was transferred to the current owner in February of 2025. There is an existing -- 3 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 4 of 9 residential structure on the property. The property is currently zoned Horry County MSF10 – which is a residential district that requires a minimum lot size of 10,000 sq. ft. and that allows manufactured homes. The requested zoning upon annexation is R-1 (low-medium density residential). This property was considered for annexation in January of 2023 for the same reasons as it is again being considered for annexation. The city’s future land use map identifies this property, along with adjoining properties, as conservation preservation (CP) being that this entire area is within a flood zone. Hucks said that staff continues to recommend against annexation of the properties along Waccamaw Drive that contain residential uses due to the flood zones these structures are located in. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by White to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (B). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (C) to annex approximately 0.18+/- acres located at 629 University Forest Circle (PIN 383-02-01-0018), and request to rezone from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10), district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated that this request was submitted in accordance with the requirements to connect to city utilities. The property was transferred into the current owner’s name in February of this year. The property is within the University Forest subdivision and there is an existing single-family structure on the property. There has been a restrictive covenant on file for this property since 1988. The current zoning is Horry County SF10 district, which allows site-built homes only on a minimum lot size of 10,000 sq. ft. The requested zoning upon annexation would be R-1, or low/medium-density residential; although the city’s future land use map identifies the properties within the University Forest subdivision as Medium-Density Residential, or R-2. Hucks said that no other properties within this subdivision have been annexed, and staff recommended against annexation. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Butler to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (C). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (D) to rezone approximately 7.8+/- acres located on North Main Street (Hwy 701 N) and Chicora Blvd (PIN 338-03-02-0006) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated that this request was received in January of this year. The property is currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC), which is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. This property is also located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay, which is an overlay that provides standards, in addition to the general standards for development, related to appearance, accessibility, and safety for projects that utilize highway corridors as their primary means of access. The property abuts the Chicora subdivision, an established single-family neighborhood zoned R-1, or low/medium-density residential. On either side is property zoned Highway Commercial. The property on the other side of Chicora Blvd was previously approved to be developed as a grocery store. -- 4 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 5 of 9 The applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the high-density residential district (R-3) to allow for multifamily development. Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their March 6 meeting. Several people spoke in opposition to the request. Their concerns included traffic on Highway 701 and Chicora Blvd, stormwater drainage and flooding, and crime. Ultimately, Planning Commission recommended disapproval of the request to rezone to R-3; however, it was not a unanimous decision. Hucks said that the applicant has stated that the intended use of the property is multifamily but would be workforce housing. Staff certainly agrees that not only workforce housing, but affordable and attainable housing is very much needed in the community, given the increased cost associated with housing; especially since the Covid pandemic. However, what staff must consider when reviewing a request to rezone property is whether the requested zoning district is appropriate for the property. Staff’s foremost responsibility is to the comprehensive plan, and whether the request is consistent with the plan. Additional factors can include how the rezoning will affect nearby properties, whether existing infrastructure is adequate and if not – what is needed, environmental and economic impacts there could be, past decisions that have been made for similar requests and the recommendation of Planning Commission. In the case of this property, which is zoned Highway Commercial, all surrounding properties with frontage on Highway 701 are also zoned HC. The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies these properties as HC as well. There is no other property in the vicinity that is zoned R-3. The closest to this would be properties on Boundary Street zoned R-2; however, these properties do not have frontage on Highway 701. Additionally, while there are no identified flood zones on this property, portions of the property on the other side of Chicora Blvd are within a flood zone, and Highway 701 has been prone to flooding very close to the subject property. Hucks said that there is strong opposition to the request, with the concerns that were previously mentioned. In the past, previous annexation or rezoning request for zoning along the major corridors other than what is identified on the city’s future land use map have not been successful. Hucks stated that Planning Commission recommended disapproval of this request and staff also recommended disapproval. There was some discussion regarding affordable housing in R-3, the need for affordable housing in Conway, suitable locations, Gateway Corridor, flooding, future land use map, area plans, and Highway Commercial versus R-3 zoning uses. The applicant stated that he would be open to a workshop. There is a tax credit in the process that has to be followed and would need rezoning in place by May 19, 2025 to be able to submit a final application for tax credits. Goldfinch asked for the income threshold for this proposed budget. The applicant stated that the highest income served would be 70% of the area median income, so for a family of four it would be a little over $55,000 annual income. The applicant said that the terminology is workforce housing. Blain asked if the rent would be subsidized. The applicant stated that they would not subsidize rent but would accept vouchers if people had them. -- 5 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 6 of 9 Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Blain to defer first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (D) to a workshop. Vote: Blain, Goldfinch, White, Helms, Butler voted yes. Hardwick voted no. Motion carried with a 5-1 vote E. First Reading of Ordinance#ZA2025-04-07 (E) to annex approximately 2.72+/- acres located at 966 West Cox Ferry Rd (PIN 382-07-01-0011), and request to rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks said that staff received this application a couple of weeks ago, as a result of the requirement to submit an annexation petition when a connection to city utilities is requested, either a new connection or a new account. The property is currently zoned Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture and the requested zoning upon annexation is R-1 (low/medium-density residential). There is an existing residential structure on the property. A restrictive covenant was recorded on March 4, 2025. This property became contiguous after the adjacent parcel – which fronts on West Cox Ferry Rd, was annexed in 2022. Horry County Code Enforcement notified staff that they had received a permit application for a proposed accessory dwelling to be constructed on the property and recently, a 2,000 sq. ft. detached metal garage had been erected on the property as well, which received its final inspection; also, on March 4. The city’s future land use map identifies the property as Conservation Preservation (CP). Hucks stated that since no other properties on this side of Weldon Lane are within the city limits, the county’s requirements for accessory dwelling units are likely different from the city’s requirements, the future land use designation of Conservation Preservation, addressing issues and the substandard condition of a portion of Weldon Lane, staff recommends against annexation at this time. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms to deny first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-04-07 (E). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSIDERATION: A. Consideration of approval of the name of a new subdivision located on John Doctor Rd / Hwy 905 (PIN 339-00-00-0013), called “Clearbrook” – Hucks stated that the proposed development is located on Highway 905 and John Doctor Road. It is a conservation subdivision, currently being reviewed by TRC. It will consist of 230 single- family homes on approximately 127 acres. The Unified Development Ordinance requires that all new subdivisions be reviewed and adopted by City Council. The proposed name of this subdivision is Clearbrook. Hucks said that staff does recommend approval. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve the subdivision name called Clearbrook. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Consideration of applications for the Redevelopment of Existing Vacant Commercial Buildings 25,000 Sq. Ft. or Greater Incentive Program for RP Coastal Centre LLC, located at 1610 and 1612 Church Street. (PINS 338-11-04-0029, 338-10-02-0015, 338- 10-02-0016, 338-10-02-0013). Dennis stated that these requests are for the four parcels listed which include the old Winn-Dixie, K-Mart, and Goody’s parcels as well as the Belk -- 6 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 7 of 9 parcel. The applicant is requesting all approved incentives offered under the Redevelopment of an Existing Vacant Commercial Building 25,000 Sq. Ft. or greater incentive program. This includes reimbursement of the following: Building Permit Fees, Up to ½ of water and sewer capital recovery fees, Business License Fees for 5 Years, Hospitality Fess for 5 Years, and Property Taxes for 10 Years. The applicant is proposing a redevelopment of the shopping center and is currently working with TRC on plan approvals. Upon approval and completion of the project these four parcels alone would include over 240,000 square feet of approximate redeveloped tenant space. This does not include any of the out parcels or smaller buildings also included within the scope of the project. Dennis said that staff does recommend approval. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve the applications for the Redevelopment of Existing Vacant Commercial Buildings 25,000 Sq. Ft. or Greater Incentive Program as submitted. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: There was no public input. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: − Emrick thanked Council for a very productive Budget Retreat, City of Rock Hill for some amazing hospitality and gave kudos to Rock Hill for their top-notch facilities. − Emrick asked Jenerette to come up and talk about an event he is heading up. Jenerette said that the Solid Waste Department along with the Horry County Solid Waste Authority would be having an Earth Day Celebration on April 22 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Collins Park. − Emrick said that Wednesday morning, the Mayor, Mayor Pro Tem Goldfinch and he will be attending Coffee with Council, produced by Coastal Carolina Association of Realtors. This is a way that CCAR hopes to make local government more accessible to the public. − Emrick announced that on Friday he and Mary Catherine will be in Columbia as the State Board of Archives and History will review the City’s application to expand the National Register Downtown Historic District. This expansion will increase the number of properties listed by 54 buildings and 5 structures. This is a tremendous increase in the City’s district which will allow the owners of the newly named historic properties to receive state and federal tax credits if they rehabilitate their properties. − Emrick said that next week he has a meeting scheduled with the new HCS Superintendent to discuss the City’s proposed TIF District. This is the first time in speaking with the HCS about the TIF since the new Superintendent has come on board and Emrick expects this to be just an introduction and the first of several meetings needed to get the school district’s approval. − Emrick said that last week, several senior staff members from the city met with some of the senior County Staff members to coordinate plans as they relate to growth. It’s vital -- 7 of 9 -- March 17, 2025 Page 8 of 9 that we do not duplicate efforts and that we cooperate as the entire County faces unprecedented expansion. − Staff met with the City’s Bond Attorneys regarding the potential letting of a Public Utilities Bond to address the 701 N Widening Project. The city attorneys believe there might be a possibility of an additional cost share from SCDOT on this project and recommended we consult with one of our local attorneys on the matter. Emrick hopes to have a fuller report shortly. − Department head reports tonight is from Recreation, Technology Services and Construction Services. Helms asked about the $2 M from Kevin Hardee, SC House Ways and Means Committee. Emrick said that the city requested money from the state government for acquisition of conservation property, which would be along Kingston Lake and would allow the city to make sure that the property is not built upon. Emrick said it would also allow public use for trails and pathways. Staff have also asked for money to expand the police facility. Recreation – Smith updated Council on the following items: - 400 new members were signed on during the month of February with now 5285 total members - The pool will be closed the month of April to replaster the pool and put the pool humidifier. - Smith Jones pool will open May 23. - There are a total of 1408 participants in the Spring Sports with a revenue of $94, 115. - Held 33 tournaments collecting rental fees of $15,950. - Fall concessions brought in $15,783 - Lots of events are on schedule. - The city will hold the largest Easter Egg Hunt with 75,000 candy filled eggs and thanked CMC for all their support. Construction Services – Cooper stated that the Facilities Maintenance division has completed several projects this past year including a pirate ship, gondola, building improvements in Public Utilities, Public Works and Hospitality & Beautification, electronic kiosks, prep for riverwalk expansion, 20-foot snowman, marina store remodel, build and wire market stalls, 20-foot chimney, various other Styrofoam pieces, rewiring of Town Green, as well as general maintenance and other small projects. Cooper said that a CNC Machine was purchased which has allowed staff to build even more props for holidays and create signage for the city. Cooper stated that the building inspectors have also been very busy and issued 88 more single family dwelling permits than this time last year. Blain commended Construction Services for a phenomenal job. Technology Services – Leveille told Council that the first digital kiosk is installed across the street from City Hall. This digital kiosk will provide event schedules, information and maps to visitors downtown. It is managed by a central server which has a Content Management System. This provides a central interface to upload and change slides, videos, and music. This central server can control multiple kiosks with the same or different information depending on the location. Leveille gave an update on South Carolina Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Program. Leveille said that the public restrooms are now a part of the access control system -- 8 of 9 -- -- 9 of 9 --

BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in January 2025. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently vacant. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3) in order to develop the property as multifamily. Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) District: The subject property is also within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 3.4.2 of the UDO, the intent of the overlay district is to create a commercial corridor that is well planned and attractive through the implementation of consistent design standards. The provisions of this section will ensure that the design quality of new development in the city’s identified gateway corridors are held to high standards. This section (GCO) shall not apply to detached single-family residential dwellings being used for residential purposes. Per Section 6.5.2, A. – Purpose, of the UDO, the GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors are their primary means of access. Per Section 6.5.2, B. – Applicability, the GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of-way line on properties along these highways (90, 378, 501, 501 Bus., 701 (South and North), and 905). Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The subject property abuts the Chicora development, a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 (low/medium-density residential). title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 2.18.2025
text: February 18, 2025 Page 1 of 6 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 18, 2025 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan, Larry White. ABSENT: Julie Hardwick STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality and Beautification Director; Jason Perzan, Deputy Fire Chief; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: Hillary Howard. There were approximately 25 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Joel Wilson of Ekklesia Christian Church gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (A) to annex approximately 1.4 acres of property located at 2837 Long Avenue Ext (PIN 32410040003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF40) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (B) to annex approximately 0.92 acres of property located at 4154 Long Avenue Ext (PIN 294-12-02-0006), and request to rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. C. Approval of a Resolution honoring the Conway Kiwanis Club for their 60th Annual Pancake Breakfast and Supper D. Approval of February 3, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve the February 18, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. INTRODUCTION OF NEW HIRES: Blain introduced the following new hires: -- 1 of 6 -- February 18, 2025 Page 2 of 6 − Billy Drayton, Public Works Right of Way Technician − William Gray, Public Works Construction Technician − Kent Smith, Public Works Construction Technician − Dean Tipton, Public Utilities Pump Mechanic − Jonathan Sandford, Public Utilities Tradesworker − David Johnson, Public Utilities Pump Mechanic − Seth Lara-Bell, Public Utilities Water Meter Technician − Landon Ward, Public Utilities Tradesworker − Alton “Dale” Ray, Solid Waste Equipment Operator I (absent) − Gregory Trapp, Light/Heavy Mechanic I SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of Employee of the Month for February 2025 – Public Works – Dudley presented Shawn Dawson as the February 2025 Employee of the Month. B. Presentation of a Resolution honoring the Conway Kiwanis Club for their 60th Annual Pancake Breakfast and Supper – Blain presented members of the Conway Kiwanis Club with a resolution honoring them for their 60th Annual Pancake Breakfast and Supper. C. Conway Downtown Alive Annual Visitor Center Update – Howard, Executive Director of Conway Downtown Alive updated Council on Events, Visitors Center, Fifth and Main, Social Media, Electronic Registration System, Staff & Ambassadors, Mural Guide, Rainy Day Guide, Community Events, Historic Tours, Visitor Parking Tag Program, Map Distribution, Downtown Marketing Campaign, Ad Placement, Geo-Fencing, Visitor Center Page, Gullah Geechee Community Day, Waccamaw Sportsmen’s Expo, and Groovin on the Green. D. Discussion of a request to rezone approximately 7.30+/- acres of property located on (North) Main Street and Chicora Blvd (PIN 338-03-02-0006) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated that this application was submitted last month. The property is currently zoned HC and is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The requested zoning is R-3. The property is also located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay. Staff discussed the proposed rezoning with the applicant, and it is staffs understanding that multifamily is proposed to be developed on the property. Adjacent uses include a single-family development, vacant property on the opposite side of Chicora Blvd, zoned HC, that was previously proposed to develop a KJ’s. Property across Main Street is zoned HC as well. Hucks said that Planning Commission is scheduled to hold the public hearing and consider the request at the March 6 meeting and that staff will forward their recommendation with first reading. SECOND/FINAL READING: Second Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (A), granting a non-exclusive franchise agreement to Project Smashburger Mobile Food Truck at the parking lot adjacent to Fourth Ave and Kingston Street (near Palmetto Taps). Hucks stated that this request received first reading on January 6 and second reading was deferred at the January 21 meeting due to concerns with a mobile food vendor securing parking spaces in an area with limited parking. The applicant -- 2 of 6 -- February 18, 2025 Page 3 of 6 is still requesting permission to utilize this location but has amended the request to Fridays and Saturdays from 3-9 p.m., alternating days each week. Additionally, two different locations are now shown on the revised site plan if the parks in one of the locations are in use when the vendor arrives on those days. If approved, the agreement would be for a 6-month probationary period and would require the applicant to come back for approval of the full term of the franchise agreement in August of this year. Council had concerns about traffic and the lack of parking in that area. Blain asked for staff’s recommendation. Hucks said that staff also had concerns with parking issues in this area and did not recommend approval of the franchise agreement. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to deny second reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Goldfinch asked if this would preclude the applicant from bringing another request to be located in a different spot. Hucks said no. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (A) to rezone approximately 0.74+/- acres of property located on Sixteenth Avenue, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01-0049) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Hucks stated that this request was discussed at the January 21 Council meeting. The applicant is requesting to rezone the property to NC, which is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The property is currently zoned R-1 and is also within the Village Corridor Overlay district. Abutting uses include a cosmetology school, which is on property zoned R-1, a vacant split zoned parcel, split between R-1 and Highway Commercial, and another vacant parcel zoned R-1. Across from the property is a small vacant parcel zoned Highway Commercial as well as a R-1 parcel that contains a single-family residence. Hucks said that Planning Commission held the public hearing at their February 6 meeting, and recommended approval of the request. The request is consistent with the future land use map and well exceeds the minimum lot size for the NC district. Additionally, the NC district is more restrictive in terms of permitted uses than the HC district. Hucks said that staff recommended approval. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Blain to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (B) to annex approximately 0.37+/- acres of property located at 116 Clemson Rd (PIN 383-10-01-0018) from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed, (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated that this request was submitted as a result of the requirements to connect to city utility services. The property was transferred into the current owner’s name in December of last year. The property is within the Coastal Heights subdivision, where several other parcels have been required to request annexation over the last few years. Coastal Heights is a relatively large development that also contains a golf course, with parcels stretching from Highway 544 to Technology Blvd. The city’s future land use map identifies the property as R-1. There is -- 3 of 6 -- February 18, 2025 Page 4 of 6 an existing single-family residence on the property. Hucks said that staff does recommend approval of the annexation. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-03-17 (B). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: There was no public input. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: − Emrick thanked Jack Cooper and Tanner Stroud, the official Conway Gondoliers and thanked all the folks that made the gondola rides happen. − Emrick reminded council that the Budget Retreat is in Rock Hill arriving on March 5 and leaving on March 7. − Emrick said that department head reports tonight is from Timmy Williams in Hospitality and Beautification and from Chief Hendrick from the Fire Department. − Emrick stated that there is one workshop item regarding a request to develop a parcel contiguous to the city limits. Hospitality and Beautification – Williams gave Council a copy of the Annual Report for Keep Conway Beautiful. Williams said that the irrigation system inside Riverfront Park should be completed by April 1. Williams stated that the parking lot improvements at the Dog Park should be started at the beginning of the summer. Williams informed Council that from October 19- November 23 there were 20 volunteers that helped with the holiday season decorations for a total of 480 hours. Fire Department – Hendrick updated Council on the Emergency Management saying that staff is preparing for an update to the Emergency Operations Plan that mostly will be general housekeeping items. Hendrick said that staff are preparing for the upcoming hurricane season. Hendrick said that with the recent snow event there were 6+ inches in Conway with no issues throughout the city as staff did not activate the EOC, but did move to OPCON 2 which is a readiness state. Hendrick said that our area could have possible freezing rain on Wednesday night, but no issues are expected. Perzan updated Council with the following information: Department Update o Two vacancies o 15,582.80 hours of training in 2024 o Training center has been used consistently – logged about 160 hours of use at the facility in 2024. o Fire apparatus order should be delivered September 2026 Call Volume o 3,796 incidents in 2023 vs. 4,240 incidents in 2024, which is an 11% increase -- 4 of 6 -- February 18, 2025 Page 5 of 6 EMT Update o 32 of 38 current EMT’s o 3 currently in class o 3 slated to go in April 2025 o All the original employees have completed the course, are currently enrolled; all new employees are required to successfully complete the course. COUNCIL INPUT: Helms thanked Smith and staff for the Father Daughter Dance and said that it gets better and better. Helms said that she and Blain represented Conway and attended the Gamecock Women’s Basketball game where they met Dawn Staley. Butler announced that the Conway High School boys’ basketball team is the region champs and encouraged all to attend the playoffs at home this Friday. White stated that Coach Hopkins, the head coach of the Conway High boys’ basketball team was named the Region 6-AAAAA Coach of the Year. Goldfinch said that he missed the Riverwalk Extension ribbon cutting but that it looked great, and that Conway was well represented. Goldfinch then talked about quality-of-life events and said that Porchfest, the one Howard talked about earlier, would be a quality-of-life event. Blain echoed Helms delight in the Father Daughter Dance and bragged on the decorations. Blain said that the Riverwalk Extension ribbon cutting with the lights, fanfare, decorations, the entrance, gondola, along with everything else that staff continue to put together was great. Blain also thanked the volunteers. Blain said that she was asked to write a Proclamation for Black History month, and she said that she didn’t respond like she should have, and time was an issue. Blain asked that this group be aware of the fact that this is Black History Month. WORKSHOP: Twin Oaks Drive Annexation – Hucks informed Council that the applicant approached staff about the possibility of annexing property on Twin Oaks Drive. The proposed to be annexed property is contiguous to the Collins Jollie development, which is currently being developed as a conservation subdivision. The City’s utility service area ends at the start of Twin Oaks Drive, which is directly off Highway 65, with two parcels on one side of Twin Oaks within the utility service area (water and sewer). The property proposed to be annexed is contiguous via land, abutting one of the developments within the Collins Jollie Conservation Subdivision; however, it is not contiguous via travel way. The closest property on Highway 65 that is within the city limits is the Hainer Place development; approximately 2 miles from the property proposing annexation. Twin Oaks Drive is a dead-end road and there would not be any connection via the Collins Jollie development that would connect this property to Collins Jollie Road. Being that it’s not within the utility service area, future land use is not identified, although nearby properties that are within the service area are identified as Conservation Preservation (CP); likely due to either wetlands that are identified on those properties or flood zones that may exist. Aside from CP, other properties are identified as Rural Residential. Hucks said that the applicant has mentioned developing the property as a conservation subdivision, which staff supports any development -- 5 of 6 -- -- 6 of 6 --

According to Horry County Register of Deed’s website, the deed was transferred into the owner’s name on December 17 of 2024. The property is within the Maple Hill subdivision off of Hwy 813. This is the only property on Hagwood Circle that is not currently within the city limits. The intent of the R-1 District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. This annexation is part of a broader enforcement issue related to the subject property that has been ongoing for a few years now. The applicant relocated his business, H&H Builders, from another property on Hwy 501 (in county’s jurisdiction) to this location, which has been owned by the applicant for some time. Both properties are still in the county’s jurisdiction; however, there were and continue to be issues related to business licensing, unpermitted structures, and uses on the subject properties, in that the county’s zoning compliance approval for the sales office is solely for a sales office only and not for any outdoor display, and a large metal building (more than 3,000 sq. ft.) in size, was erected on one of the parcels without a building permit (aerial photograph from April 2024 included in packet). Complicating matters, the properties were one parcel before being split in 2007 (plat book 221, pg. 175). The railroad right-of-way separates the two parcels. Now that they are separated, they cannot be recombined, due to the right-of-way that exists. However, both parcels include the use of manufactured homes sales, and in order for the manufactured home sales business to be compliant, the sales office, parking, etc., must be located on the same property as the display models are located; otherwise, the use is considered outdoor storage, which is prohibited except in conjunction with a permitted use. The applicant was attempting to become compliant with Horry County’s requirements; however, in order for them to do so, they would need to provide water to the unpermitted metal building on the same parcel as the displays (manufactured home units) are located on. Being that it would be an extension of (water) service, or a new service if none currently exists, the requirement to annex becomes applicable. The issue for staff is that if the property is annexed under the current condition, then the city is inheriting a use on a property that was never legally permitted on the property as well as structures that were never issued a building permit. Yet, the only way for the property to comply would include the requirement for city water to be extended to the property, which requires the applicant to request annexation. Staff has been working with the applicant’s attorney on the issues and has agreed that if Council chose to annex the properties, that they would be given the opportunity to request variances for some of the 14 -- 14 of 114 -- outstanding issues without the threat of further enforcement, pending the outcome of the variance requests, as they cannot request any variances (from the City’s requirements) until and unless the property has been annexed. If Council chooses not to annex, the applicant would need to comply with the requirements for the county. While manufactured home sales is the current use of one of the properties, the applicant has stated that they would be phasing that use out in the near future and would pursue approval to develop mini-storage and/or other commercial / industrial uses. The requested zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial (HC) (0.47-acre parcel with frontage on Hwy 501) and Light Industrial (LI) (7.15-acre tract with frontage on E. Cox Ferry Rd). Per Section 3.2.13 – Light Industrial (LI), the intent of the LI district is to provide areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: Adjacent properties in the city limits are zoned Light Industrial (LI) and Heavy Industrial (HI), as these properties are located within the Commerce Plaza industrial park. Property fronting Hwy 501 in the county’s jurisdiction is zoned Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. BACKGROUND: Since early 2023, city staff has been going through the UDO to identify inconsistencies, typos, and other items that may be lacking within each Article of the UDO. Sec 8-5-2 Prohibitions 58 -- 58 of 114 -- Except as otherwise provided in this code, it is unlawful to operate an off-highway vehicle upon public rights-of-way, utility rights-of-way or easements, public highways, streets, sidewalks, trails, parks and roads or upon private or public property without the written consent of the owner thereof; provided, however, that the prohibitions contained in this section shall not apply to any agent or employee of any public authority on public property or within public rights-of-way; the agent, employee or contractor for any public or private utility on property of the public or private utility or within its rights-of-way or easements; any law enforcement agency or public safety agency or any fire department, hospital or ambulance service while providing or exercising official duties and powers; or to the operation of off-highway vehicles on private property owned by the operator or for which the operator has written permission from the owner. Sec 8-5-3 Owner’s and operator’s responsibilities It is unlawful for the owner or operator of an off-highway vehicle to permit its operation on private or public property without permission of the owner or occupant; within public rights-of-way except as provided by law; or within rights-of-way of public or private utilities without the written consent of such utilities. All vehicles, including off- highway vehicles for which state statutes require liability insurance coverage shall be insured in accordance with liability insurance requirements for motor vehicles under South Carolina Statues and laws. Any owners and operators must also comply with South Carolina Code of Laws Title 50, Chapter 26, also known as “Chandler’s Law”. ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) to amend Article 9-Landscaping and Buffering, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding Landscape, Buffer, and Tree Preservation requirements. BACKGROUND: Staff is proposing an amendment to Article 9 that would allow for a more clarification on commonly misinterpreted aspects of the Tree Preservation Ordinance, penalties for violations of the ordinance, as well as a more appropriate course of action for Tree Board appeals. Staff is proposing the following. 1. Codify the Tree Preservation Ordinance into the UDO. Then the Tree Ordinance falls under the purview of the Planning & Development Dept. 2. Designate that the Community Appearance Board (CAB) will continue to act as the Tree Board; however, appeals of the decisions of the Tree Board would be directed to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). 3. Amend the Tree Preservation Ordinance, including the Appeals Section (Sec. 3-4-15 – Appeals), items (b) and (c) that directs appeals of the Tree Board to Conway City Council, and amend to direct appeals of the Tree Board decision to Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). This would ensure a proper appeal process, as the appellant would then appeal decisions of the BZA to circuit court instead of City Council. 4. Begin collecting an application fee ($250) for Tree Board Appeals. Staff proposes to begin charging $250 for Tree Appeal applications. Should applicants seek to overturn the decision of the Tree Board, and these requests go to BZA, the property will need to be posted, the appeal would need to be advertised, letters would need to be sent to adjacent property owners, and decisions from the BZA would need to be mailed certified to interested parties. 5. Upon the request of tree board, staff have made some housekeeping changes throughout the ordinance to ensure a more uniform and concise understanding of the processes and terminology used throughout the ordinance. These items include clarity of the process of tree mitigation, implementation of higher penalties for improper removal of protected or landmark trees, and clarification on definitions that were commonly misinterpreted. 6. Addition and deletion, upon the request of the tree board, of trees from the protected tree list. The tree board asked to remove non-native trees, Crepe Myrtle and Dawn Redwoods, from the protected list but to rather include native trees, such as a Tulip tree, Red Cedar, and a Tupelo tree. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) regarding the proposed amendments to the Tree Preservation Ordinance. 108 -- 108 of 114 -- ORDINANCE #ZA2025-02-18 (C) AMENDING ARTICLE 9 – LANDSCAPING AND BUFFERING, OF THE CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO), REGARDING REVISIONS TO VARIOUS ITEMS CONTAINED WITHIN THIS ARTICLE REGARDING LANDSCAPE, BUFFER AND TREE PRESERVATION REQUIREMENTS. State Code 6-29-760; and WHEREAS, Article 9 of the UDO contains information related to landscaping, buffering, and tree preservation and the requirements applied; and WHEREAS, the amendment is a part of a broader cleanup initiative of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) by staff to provide more concise and up-to-date information as well as remove inconsistencies or repetitiveness throughout the Article; and WHEREAS, following a review by the Planning Commission and the required public hearing, it has been determined that the UDO should be amended relative to revisions to various items within Article 9 of the UDO. Therefore, be it ORDAINED, by Conway City Council, in council duly assembled, that the UDO be shall be amended as attached hereto; and be it further ORDAINED, that all ordinances or parts of ordinances inconsistent with this Ordinance are hereby repealed to the extent of such inconsistency. ISSUE: First reading of Ordinance #2025-02-18 (D) to amend Title 3- Public Works, Chapter 4-Tree Preservation, and Title 5-Planning and Development of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, regarding the Tree Preservation Ordinance. BACKGROUND: Chapter 4 of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances assigns the duties of the Conway Tree Board to be the responsibility of the appointed members of the Community Appearance Board (CAB). The issue that faces the current Tree Board is that there is no clear direction as to the appeals process regarding their decisions. There are 3 appeals options listed in the Tree Preservation Ordinance: (a) Denial of a protected tree removal permit from City Arborist. The applicant may appeal to the Tree Board. It must be filed within 10 working days of the denial of the permit. (b) The arborist cannot grant a permit to remove a landmark tree. If the tree is determined to be a landmark tree, the applicant must request permission to remove from the Tree Board. IF the Tree Board denies the applicant a permit to remove a landmark tree, they may appeal their decision to City Council. It must be filed within 10 working days of the denial of the permit. (c) Appeal of the penalty assessed by the Tree Board. If the applicant wishes to appeal the penalty (or mitigation amount) that was assessed by the Tree Board, they may appeal to City Council. It must be filed within 10 days of the Board’s decision (or assessment). Staff has explored a couple of different options regarding the Tree Board and the appropriate Board for protected tree removal requests to be considered. In our research, staff has concluded that because Conway is a “Tree City USA”, there must be a designated “Tree Board” OR a “Tree Department”, and even with a Tree Dept., it is the opinion of the City Arborist, as well as other Cities / Towns with certified arborists that a Tree Board would still be necessary. Additionally, staff researched several cities / towns that are also a Tree City USA, and of the ones we found – all had a Tree Protection Ordinance and either a Tree Board, or in some cases, a Tree Commission. As such, staff has reached the following conclusions and suggestions for the Tree Preservation Ordinance and the appeals authority to ensure that the City does not lose its Tree City USA status and continues to strengthen its efforts in tree preservation and protection: 1. Codify the Tree Preservation Ordinance into the UDO. Then the Tree Ordinance falls under the purview of the Planning & Development Dept. 111 -- 111 of 114 -- 2. Designate that the Community Appearance Board (CAB) will continue to act as the Tree Board; however, appeals of the decisions of the Tree Board would be directed to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). 3. Amend the Tree Preservation Ordinance, including the Appeals Section (Sec. 3-4-15 – Appeals), items (b) and (c) that directs appeals of the Tree Board to Conway City Council, and amend to direct appeals of the Tree Board decision to Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). This would ensure a proper appeal process, as the appellant would then appeal decisions of the BZA to circuit court instead of City Council. 4. Begin collecting an application fee ($250) for Tree Board Appeals. Staff proposes to begin charging $250 for Tree Appeal applications. Should applicants seek to overturn the decision of the Tree Board, and these requests go to BZA, the property will need to be posted, the appeal would need to be advertised, letters would need to be sent to adjacent property owners, and decisions from the BZA would need to be mailed certified to interested parties. 5. Remove associated fees for penalties and mitigation. To preserve the intent of the Tree Preservation Ordinance and the increase in penalties staff proposes to remove the portion of the Fee Schedule that references Tree Penalties, Violations, and Protected or Landmark Tree Sizes outlined in Title 5 Planning and Development, Chapter 1, Section 5-1-4 Permit Fees, of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances. This will ensure compliance with the newly amended Tree Preservation Ordinance within the UDO. title: CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 2.3.2025
text: February 3, 2025 Page 1 of 5 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, FEBRUARY 3, 2025 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain, Mayor Pro Tem William Goldfinch, Amanda Butler, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan, Larry White. STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Dale Long, Police Chief; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Lynn Smith, Human Resources Director; Kym Wilkerson, Planning and Development Deputy Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Braxton Fleming, Public Works Deputy Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 20 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain called the meeting to order. Brandon Wilson of Ekklesia Christian Church gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-03 (A) to annex approximately 1.06 acres of property located at 4100 Hagwood Circle (PIN 324-04-02-0006), and request to rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). B. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-03 (B) to annex approximately 7.62+/- (total) acres of property located at 1705 Highway 501 and on East Cox Ferry Road (PINs 383-01-02-0030 & 383-01-03-0002), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and High Bulk Retail (RE4) districts to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) and Light Industrial (LI) districts. C. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-03 (C) to amend Article 11- Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for signs. D. Final Reading of Ordinance #2025-02-03 (D) to amend Title 8 Motor Vehicles and Traffic, Chapter 5 Off-Highway Vehicles, of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances. E. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (F), to annex approximately 4.50 acres of property located on Highway 501, near Conbraco Circle (PIN 399-08-01-0001), and -- 1 of 5 -- February 3, 2025 Page 2 of 5 rezone from the Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. F. Approval of January 21, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by White to approve the February 3, 2025 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Recognition of 2024 Retirees – Blain, Emrick and Butler recognized the following 2024 retirees: Anthony Collins – 19 Years, Shop; James Friday – 9 Years, Public Utilities; John Friestad – 8 Years, Public Utilities; John Rabon – 15 Years, Solid Waste; and Joseph “Andy” Roumillat (absent) – 8 Years, Solid Waste. B. Presentation of January 2025 Longevity Awards – 5 Years: Derick Carter, Public Utilities; 10 Years: Hayden Witt, Fire; 10 Years: Theodore “Teddy” Bryant, Public Utilities; 20 Years: Jamie Givens, Public Utilities; 25 Years: Jeannie Quilimaco, Police – Blain and Emrick presented the January 2025 longevity awards. C. Presentation of the 2024 City of Conway Audit Report - Nathan Skipper, Smith Sapp CPAs – Nathan Skipper of Smith Sapp CPAs gave a brief overview of the independent auditor’s report regarding the City’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. Skipper stated that there are no non-compliance issues to report and that there is no better audit report that can be issued than the one that he is issuing for the City. Skipper said that the annual reporting that the city finance department does go far beyond what is required and has received the Government Finance Officers Associate (GFOA) Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in financial reporting for 30 years and Skipper said that it is expected to continue. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (A) to annex approximately 1.4 acres of property located at 2837 Long Avenue Ext (PIN 32410040003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF40) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Wilkerson stated that this annexation application was submitted as a requirement to connect to city utility services. The property is within the Long Farm subdivision and there is an existing single-family home on the property. Wilkerson said that staff recommended approval of first reading. Motion: White made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (B) to annex approximately 0.92 acres of property located at 4154 Long Avenue Ext (PIN 294-12-02-0006), and request to rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Wilkerson stated that this annexation application was submitted by the personal representative of the -- 2 of 5 -- February 3, 2025 Page 3 of 5 deceased property owner as a requirement to alter the name on the city utilities services account. There is an existing single-family home located on the property. Wilkerson said that staff recommended approval of first reading. Motion: Hardwick made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (B). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) to amend Article 9 – Landscape and Buffering, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for landscaping, buffering, and tree preservation. This Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) and the next Ordinance #2025-02-18 (D) were combined. Dennis stated that staff are proposing an amendment to Article 9 of the UDO and Title 3, 4 and 5 of the City’s Code of Ordinances. The changes are to include updated terminology, definition clarification, increased landmark tree size, clarification on penalties assessed by the Tree Board, removal of fines from the fee schedule, updated process of appeals and other housekeeping items to provide a concise and streamlined process for protected and landmark tree removal. Dennis said that these changes have been recommended for approval by the Tree Board, Planning Commission and were discussed previously in workshop and at a special presentation with Council. There was some discussion regarding the appeal fee and the state law. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve first reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-02-18 (C) and Ordinance #2025-02-18 (D). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First Reading of Ordinance #2025-02-18 (D) to amend Title 3 – Public Works, Chapter 4 – Tree Preservation of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, to repeal this section in its entirety as it relates to the Tree Preservation Ordinance. See previous motion. PUBLIC INPUT: There was no public input. Motion: Blain made a motion, seconded by Jordan to close public input. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: • Emrick said he would like to start tonight with Valentine’s Day, and he gave an overview of what decorations are back and what staff have added along with the events that are scheduled. Emrick said that the big draw this year is the Gondola rides being sponsored by Conway Medical Center where you can take a short free ride with your special person. • Emrick informed Council of the increased number of visitors for the holidays comparing 2017 with 2024. Emrick said that the big goal here is for the city to become known as the place to be all year round and said that this calendar year, for the first time ever, the city is likely to hit 2 million visitors to Downtown. Emrick said that Conway is the destination and that is why staff invest in seasonal decorations. -- 3 of 5 -- February 3, 2025 Page 4 of 5 • Emrick told Council that due to the success of the unique way that the city has accomplished these holidays, Emrick has been invited to present at the 2025 South Carolina Rural Summit on March 3 and the topic of his presentation is “How holidays changed the face of Conway and scared its way to success.” • Emrick announced that the Riverwalk expansion ribbon cutting is this Thursday at 6:00 p.m. behind the former Ocean Fish Market site. Emrick said that this is the best connection that the city has ever had from the river to the downtown, something that was identified as the primary goal of the 2017 Masterplan. • Emrick reminded Council that the Budget Retreat will be in Rock Hill this year arriving on March 5 and leaving on March 7. • Emrick said that staff have had reports of people going door to door in the city selling water filtration systems and fraudulently telling people that they are working with the city. Door- to-door sales are illegal, and the city is not doing any business with this outfit or any other like it. Staff are sending something out to our customers and putting something on social media to alert the public. • Emrick said that staff are working with Rogers Lewis to add properties to the existing Historic District. The Department of Archives and History is reviewing the City’s application on March 21 and if approved it will add nearly 50 properties to the historic district. • Emrick stated that the Police Department is testing some new technology that is causing a little buzz on social media. Throughout the city gunshot detectors have been installed on black poles and the police are notified if one has been detected. • Emrick stated that there is one workshop item and no executive session. That item is a review of Title 4 of the Code of Ordinances with some recommended updates and housekeeping. Blain asked how many new businesses are interested in being in Conway and how the city has grown that way. Howard stated that in 2019 there were 50 empty storefronts and that is not the case now. Howard said that Conway Downtown Alive keeps a list of approximately 20 businesses that are interested in moving into the downtown district and as soon as a property comes available, they are notified so that they may rent that property. She stressed that more retail spaces are needed and Conway Downtown Alive supports the push for new construction. Goldfinch said that he would like to discuss at budget retreat an incentive that would encourage retail and the food and beverage industries to downtown. Hardwick added that she would like to balance the professional versus the retail and the restaurants. White asked what would be done with the Highway 378 properties that the city is buying. Emrick said that live oaks are planted to beautify the corridor and then they are put back on the market for viable businesses. COUNCIL INPUT: Hardwick thanked staff for their hard work and looks forward to seeing Valentines and having the Riverwalk open. Jordan thanked staff for working out in the snowstorm. -- 4 of 5 -- -- 5 of 5 --

ISSUE: Second Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (B), granting a non-exclusive franchise agreement to Randall’s Culinary Creations Mobile Food Truck at the parking lot located at 7 Elm Street. BACKGROUND: Section 5.1.16-Mobile Vending of the UDO sets forth regulations for mobile vending in Conway. This ordinance allows franchise mobile vending on public property in the CBD, CC, WRD zoning districts and City parks, but only with a franchise agreement approved through City Council. A franchise is an extension of the privilege to use the streets, parking and other City owned amenities for which the franchisee does not have a legal right without permission from the governing body. The franchise agreement allows the franchisee to use City property in the requested manner which exceeds or differs from the customary uses. The franchise agreement is a contract between the City and the franchisee which governs the use of the City property. The agreement does not give exclusive use to the franchisee. The hours of operations and approved locations are determined by City Council in the franchise agreement. A certificate of insurance, as well as a release and indemnification agreement, are also required for mobile vending on public property (which the applicant has obtained). Randall’s Culinary Creations has a valid City of Conway Business License and an approved Private Property Mobile Food Vending Permit for Coastal Carolina University. Randall’s Culinary Creations has requested a Franchise Agreement to operate the Mobile Food Truck at the following location: • The parking lot located at 7 Elm Street (PIN# 367-08-01-0001). The requested hours of operation are 12:00pm to 9:00pm or 7:00am to 7:00pm Monday through Friday. For a franchise agreement to be valid, it must receive two readings at City Council as an Ordinance. To satisfy the requirements of the City Code concerning franchise agreements, the applicant published a public notice in three (3) issues of a newspaper having general circulation in the city stating the nature of the franchise and the date on which the application is to be presented to Council. The public hearing has also been advertised as required. 4 -- 4 of 256 -- JANUARY 6, 2025 CITY COUNCIL MEETING: City Council had concerns about whether the location would be a good spot for the Mobile Food Truck to sell from. Out of concern for what the next one year to five years holds for the City of Conway, it was suggested to allow a Franchise Agreement for one (1) year instead of approving the location for five (5) years. No one spoke for Public Input. Council approved first reading of the franchise agreement for Randall’s Culinary Creations for a one (1) year term. At that time, the request would be revisited to decide if the applicant and Council are both happy with the location. RECOMMENDATION: Because of the unknown future plans of this area, staff recommends that the agreement be approved for one (1) year period, and in one (1) year, Council can revisit the issue and approve a more permanent agreement with Randall’s Culinary Creations if it desires. 5 -- 5 of 256 -- ORDINANCE #ZA2025-01-21 (B) AN ORDINANCE APPROVING A NON-EXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF CONWAY AND BENNY RANDALL, D.B.A. PROJECT RANDALL’S CULINARY CREATIONS, TO OPERATE A MOBILE VENDING UNIT IN THE PARKING LOT LOCATED AT 7 ELM STREET. According to Horry County Register of Deed’s website, the deed was transferred into the owner’s name on November 8, 2010. The property is within the Pine Valley Estates subdivision off Hwy 544. Thus far, five (6) properties in Pine Valley Estates have been annexed into the City limits. In 2023, Council denied annexation of a property within Pine Valley Estates – 600 Stanway Drive. Lesia Lane is the closest roadway to the entrance road coming into Pine Valley Estates, off Todd Blvd. The City’s Solid Waste Dept. currently provides service to six (6) other properties on Lesia Lane. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies this property as Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The intent of the Medium-Density District is to provide for areas for medium-density attached, detached, semi-attached and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway, and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the District. ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (H) to rezone approximately 0.70+/- total acres of property located at 1318 and 1320 Fourth Ave (PINs 368-04-01-0021 and -0022) from the Core Commercial (CC) and Medium- Density Residential (R-2) districts to the Core Commercial (CC) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant applied to rezone the subject properties following inquiring about leasing the building(s) for a beauty salon. One of the properties had been vacant for six (6) months or longer, triggering the requirement to bring the site into compliance with the current requirements of the UDO. Upon review, staff realized that the adjacent property (1320 Fourth Ave), owned by the same property owner, along with the property seeking to be utilized, was split-zoned CC and R-2. The parking lots for both properties are located behind the buildings and zoned R-2 (medium-density residential). As such, staff recommended that both properties be rezoned to remove the R-2 zoning designation and split zoning status of the properties, bringing the zoning into compliance. Per Section 3.2.4 – Medium Density Residential (R-2), the intent of the R-2 district is to provide for areas for medium density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway, and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the District. Per Section 3.2.11 – Core Commercial (CC), the intent of the CC district is to establish a thriving commercial and mixed-use district adjacent to the Central Business District that provides form and use of development compatible to that of the CBD, but not as strict with regards to design standards. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: A majority of the properties surrounding the subject properties are zoned CC, with one property that fronts on Fifth Ave zoned R-2. Surrounding businesses include professional services, such as financial institutions, insurance companies, legal services, accounting services, etc. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as being mixed-use and medium- density residential. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their December 12th meeting and recommended approval of the request to rezone the property to CC. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their January 6th meeting. ISSUE: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (I), to amend Article 2 – Definitions and Article 4 – Use Tables, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to various items within the Articles. BACKGROUND: Staff began a UDO clean up initiative earlier this year and have been slowly revising each article to provide a more correct and up to date version, based on proposed changes discussed at the Council budget retreat in 2023. These articles are being revised to coincide with previous changes made in other articles that impact them. Article 2 – Definitions, is being revised to meet new standard definitions as well as remove any repetitive definitions throughout. The Use Tables (Article 4) is proposed to be amended to provide a more inclusive umbrella of use types instead of very specific use types. For example, instead of specifying Barber shop/beauty salon, or Hair or Nail Salon the terms could be combined to Barber Shop/Beauty Salon and a new definition that is all encompassing would be created. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the proposed amendments and recommended approval, with minor revisions, at their December 12, 2024 meeting. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their January 6th meeting. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: All changes proposed to Articles 2 and 4 of the UDO are identified in the attached table. Some of the more recent revisions include the addition of definitions for Crematory, Funeral Home, relocation of the term “mural” to general definitions, additional language added to use of funeral homes in Article 4, and removal of certain uses in Article 4. Staff recommends approval of Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2025-01-21 (I). 72 -- 72 of 256 -- ORDINANCE #ZA2025-01-21 (I) AMENDING ARTICLE 2 – DEFINITIONS AND ARTICLE 4 – USE TABLES, OF THE CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO), REGARDING REVISIONS TO VARIOUS ITEMS CONTAINED WITHIN THESE ARTICLES. [ZA2020-09-21(A)] • External Access - access points provided along the boundaries of a development, to provide connection to the existing paved public roadways abutting the project. • Internal Access - access points provided to paved public roadways within a project. Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU): A housing unit not exceeding one thousand (1,000) square feet, with cooking facilities, sanitary facilities, and an independent means of access, either attached to a single-family detached dwelling or located on the same lot as a single-family detached dwelling. Accessory Structure: A subordinate structure, the use of which is incidental to and customary in connection with the principal structure or use, and which is located on the same lot with such principal structure or use. Accessory Use: A subordinate use which is incidental to and customary in connection with the principal structure or use and which is located on the same lot with such principal structure or use. Active Open Space: Areas where group or team activities take place with formal designated fields, outdoor courts (basketball, volleyball, tennis) and/or outdoor amenities (skate park, frisbee, golf, etc.) see Section 10.3.9 A.D.T. (Average Daily Trip): The average number of vehicles per day that pass over a given point. Amenity Center: A clubhouse or similar structure owned by a homeowners’ association, property owner’s association or development/property management company for use by residents of a specific apartment, condominium, or townhouse complex or a specific subdivision including recreational facilities, social rooms and other non-commercial activities. The structure shall fit with the residential character of the surrounding development. Armory: A building/structure where firearms and ammunition are stored, maintained and/or repaired by and for the express use of law enforcement and/or the US Armed Forces. [ZA2023-07-17(B)] Artisan: A person skilled in an applied art or artistic discipline (also known as Artist, Craftsman). Artists’ Studio & Gallery: An establishment for the preparation, display, and/or sale of individually crafted artwork, jewelry, furniture, sculpture, pottery, leathercraft, hand-woven articles, watercraft, baked or prepared food and drink, and similar items by one or more artisans (also known as Artisan Workshop) Assembly: The use of a building or structure, or a portion thereof, for the gathering of persons for purposes such as civic, social, or religious functions. Bail Bond Establishment: A building in which a “Professional bondsman” (any person who is approved and licensed under the provisions of the South Carolina Code of Laws; Statute 38-53-10) makes a business of furnishing bail in criminal cases or who furnishes bail in five or more criminal cases in any one year, whether for compensation or otherwise. Banquet Hall: An establishment used regularly for serving food and beverages to groups that, before the day of the event, have reserved the facility. Food shall be brought in from off-site.
