ISSUE: First Reading and Public Hearing of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (B), to amend the City’s Future Land Use Map (2019-2029) (FLUM) of the City of Conway Comprehensive Plan, relative to property located at 1926 Fulmer Street, (PIN 338-06-02-0038), consisting of approximately 0.32 acres, from the Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) zoning district to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. BACKGROUND: The South Carolina Planning Enabling Act of 1994 defines the Comprehensive Plan adoption process for all jurisdictions in South Carolina. This is to ensure consistency with the public hearing and revision process for Comprehensive Plans. Section 6-29-510 of the SC Code of Laws addresses re-evaluation of the Comprehensive Plan, stating that the "local planning commission shall develop and maintain a planning process which will result in the systematic preparation and continual re-evaluation and updating of those elements considered critical, necessary, and desirable to guide the development and redevelopment of its area of jurisdiction." Since updating the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan for the City in 2019, staff will occasionally review annexation and/or rezoning requests for zones that do not match the zone envisioned in the current Future Land Use Map (2019-2029). When a request is approved that is out of alignment with the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan, the map must be updated to reflect this change. In July 2021, Council passed an ordinance providing for a method by which the Comprehensive Plan, particularly the Future Land Use map, may be amended. Section 13.1.17 (E) of the UDO states that a proposed amendment to the Comprehensive Plan (the entire document or singular elements) may be initiated by the City of Conway City Council, Planning Commission, Board of Zoning Appeals, Zoning Administrator, or Planning Director. In the case of PIN 338-06-02-0038, currently zoned City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1), the city’s Future Land Use Map (2019-2029) also identifies the property as Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). The property is currently vacant, but a dilapidated residential structure was recently removed, and the property is directly behind Rivertown Child Development Center Inc., LLC at 1911 N Main Street (zoned Highway Commercial-HC). The applicants would like to rezone the property to Highway Commercial in order to combine with their property fronting Main Street in order to expand the existing child care facility. There are three other properties abutting the subject property that are currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC) one fronts Sessions Street and two that front on Main Street. Directly across Fulmer Street there is a property that is currently zoned Professional (P). 111 -- 111 of 230 -- Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. SURROUNDING USES / ZONING DISTRICTS: Surrounding properties are currently zoned R-1, HC, and P, and uses include vacant land, a gym, two existing daycare centers and a mini storage facility. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The CURRENT future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the entire parcel as being Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their October 3rd meeting and recommended to amend the City’s future land use map, from Low/Medium-Density Residential to Highway Commercial. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff supports the recommendation of Planning Commission as well as the policy positions of the American Planning Association (APA) and recommends amending the future land use map relative to PIN 338-06-02-0038. ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (C), to rezone approximately 0.32 acres of property located at 1926 Fulmer Street, (PIN 338-06-02-0038) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant is seeking to rezone the subject property to the Highway Commercial district in order to expand their daycare capabilities. The daycare is directly abutting this property, and fronts on Main Street (Hwy 701 N). This request to rezone the property will be accompanied by a Future Land Use Map amendment request. The property is currently vacant and zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R- 1). If the rezoning is granted, the applicant intends to combine the existing daycare property with the subject property, and a site plan submitted shows the proposed expansion, which includes an addition to the existing structure, and the subject property would be used for additional parking for staff and a playground. The site plan and proposed combination survey is included in the packet. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile-oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC), Professional (P), and Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Surrounding uses include single-family residential, a property containing a church which was rezoned to Professional a couple of years ago to allow a daycare to be established on the property, a HC property that contains a building that used to be an auto repair/garage, and also abuts the property on Main Street containing the existing daycare. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Per Section 3.2.3 of the UDO, the intent of the R-1 district is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. CITY COUNCIL: Staff presented the request to City Council during their September 16th meeting. There were concerns 118 -- 118 of 230 -- raised about further encroachment of commercial into the primarily residential area and whether there were more restrictive commercial zoning districts that the applicant could request that would still allow a daycare but not as of intense of uses that the HC district would permit. Staff subsequently relayed the concerns to the applicant and discussed the potential of rezoning the property as well as the property that the daycare is currently located on to the Professional (P) district. Should the applicant choose to go that route, the current application would need to be revised to include the other parcel in the request. However, properties along this portion of N. Main Street (Hwy 701 N) are primarily zoned Highway Commercial, including the property containing the daycare facility, as well as other surrounding property with frontage along Hwy 701 N./N. Main Street. Additionally, per the UDO, new construction in the Professional district is limited to a maximum building footprint of 30% of the total lot size, and no expansions of an existing building in the district shall cause the standards of the district to be exceeded (Sec. 6.3.2, A.1, 2). If there were no future expansions planned that could include an increase in the building footprint, the Professional district may be suitable to meet the needs to the applicant. If the properties are successfully rezoned to Professional, no expansions that would cause the standards within Section 6.3.2 to be exceeded would be permitted, which is why the Professional district was not recommended to the applicant at the time of application. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their October 3rd meeting. There was no public input. PC recommended approval of the request to rezone the property to HC and to amend the Future Land Use Map. Points to consider While there are similarities with this request compared to other requests, there are key differences to consider when comparing this request to those that were unsuccessful: 1. Other requests were closer to the downtown area, located within the Main Street Overlay (MSO), and included properties located in the Main Street Historic Design Review District. • Per Section 6.5.1, A., the standards of the Main Street Overlay (MSO) are applicable to properties fronting Main Street between 5th Ave and 16th Ave. These properties are also required to adhere to the residential/Main Street Corridor guidelines in the City of Conway Historic Design Review Districts: Community Appearance Guidelines. • Other properties located within the Main Street Overlay include mostly residential or professional-type businesses, with a few exceptions where properties contain a gas/service station. There are no properties in the Main Street Overlay or the Historic Design Review District that are zoned Highway Commercial. • With the exception of the Horry County Museum and Library property at the corner of Ninth 119 -- 119 of 230 -- Ave and Main Street, all properties directly abutting parcels that have frontage on Main Street are residentially zoned and contain residential uses. 2. The subject property on Fulmer Street is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), which includes properties within 500 feet from the right-of-way line on either side of the roadways within the GCO. • Per Section 6.5.2, A., of the UDO, the GCO was established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors as their primary means of access. The purpose is to provide opportunities to develop projects engineered to be compatible with the carrying capacity of highway corridors. • Any property or building that has any portion within the 500-ft overlay boundary shall comply with the regulations of the GCO. • Construction or renovation of any buildings located beyond the 500-ft overlay boundary shall be required if visible from the right-of-way. 3. Property located on the other side of Sessions Street, behind The Freeze restaurant, was rezoned from the R-1 (low/medium-density residential) district to the Highway Commercial District in 2022. The purpose of the rezoning was for the property owner to expand the parking area of The Freeze restaurant. It is located beside existing single-family homes and across from property containing two duplexes, which is not a permitted use in the R-1 district. 4. A majority of the parcels along this stretch of Hwy 701 N (N. Main Street) are zoned Highway Commercial, and the lots have more depth than the properties between Sessions and Oak Street, and several have parcels that do not have frontage along Hwy 701 N./N. Main Street that are either zoned Highway Commercial, or that contain a commercial use that is not zoned for that use. 5. The Tobacco shop at the corner of Hwy 701 N/N Main St is part of a commercial strip center. The Tobacco shop faces Hwy 701 N, but there are 2 other tenant spaces facing Sessions Street; one of which is a specialty food store. The property is split zoned, with a majority zoned Highway Commercial, and the remainder zoned R-1 (low/medium-density residential). 6. The subject parcel is located directly across from property zoned Professional, which also contains a child care facility in a structure that historically contained and was built for a church. It was rezoned in 2023 from R-1 to Professional to allow the church to be used for a child care facility. This also included a future land use map amendment. 7. The subject property is also directly adjacent to another property that had been legal nonconforming until it was rezoned to HC in 2022, which once contained an auto-related use. It has recently been renovated to be used for a fitness center, which is planned to open soon. The existing structure sits approximately 5-ft from the property line adjoining the subject property. 8. The property on the other side of the subject property on Fulmer Street is currently vacant. 120 -- 120 of 230 -- 1912, 1914, 1916 Fulmer Street contains at least 3 residential structures; 2 of which contain multiple units. It is also owned by a realty company. The use of the property in its current form is a nonconforming. 9. In a Community Needs Assessment Survey conducted by the United Way in 2021, respondents in the 29526 and 29527 zip codes identified a lack of safe, affordable full-time places for children to go as being one of the most overwhelming needs in the community. Additionally, 47% of Horry County is identified as a child care desert. 11. According to the Children’s Trust of South Carolina, a 2022 survey conducted by the SC Dept. of Employment and Workforce revealed that 27% of survey respondents stated that a lack of child care or the need to stay with a child as being their top barrier to work. 12. The American Planning Association (APA) Policy Guide states the following regarding the provision of child care: • Affordable, conveniently located, quality child care is one of the most pressing concerns of contemporary family life. • Increased zoning barriers add to the cost of child care and the lowering of quality in care. Child care centers are usually commercial land uses, thus making the cost and convenience of child care greater for neighborhood residents. • The impact of child care shortages is most acutely felt at the local level. • Accessible, affordable, and quality child care benefits the social and financial needs of parents and the educational and developmental needs of children. • Child care contributes to the local economy by supporting parents and local employers. • The location and availability of child care can affect other community development goals including smart growth and sustainability planning. Policy positions of the APA regarding child care include (but is not limited to) the following: • APA advocates the inclusion of child care policies as part of local planning policies; • APA encourages communities considering amending local zoning ordinances to remove obstacles to the provision of regulated group and family child care in all zoning districts, in locations that are appropriate and safe for children; • APA supports local legislation (zoning ordinances) which provide for child care in locations convenient to neighborhoods and in public facilities such as schools, recreation and social service centers, and subsidized housing projects. Procedures to locate child care facilities should not be overly burdensome and should be related to the size and land use impacts of the facility; • APA supports national and state legislation which moves toward the goal of providing 121 -- 121 of 230 -- adequate funding for safe, convenient and affordable child care opportunities for all children. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff supports the recommendation of Planning Commission as well as the policy positions of the American Planning Association and recommends approval of the rezoning request. While staff cannot require it, the owners would be seeking to delay final reading of the future land use map amendment and rezoning request until the combination survey has been completed, to combine the property containing the existing daycare with the vacant property. Once combination is complete, they would then request final reading. The property is split-zoned, with approximately 11.8 acres, including the highway frontage, zoned Horry County RE4 (High Bulk Retail), and the remaining acreage zoned Horry County CFA (Commercial Forest Agriculture). The property was previously approved for 5 buildings while in the County’s Jurisdiction with the understanding that once the Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.) was complete the property would be taken forward for second reading. The first 3 buildings have been built and there are currently no active permits in review or any buildings under construction on the property. This item is being considered by Planning Commission a second time due to a change in ownership that occurred between First Reading of the annexation / rezoning in 2022, and when the C.O. was issued on the existing buildings. Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the Light Industrial (LI) district is to provide for areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) District, Horry County High Bulk Retail (RE4), Horry County Highway Commercial (HC), Horry County Agricultural Community Services (AG3), Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF20) district, and Horry County Forest Agriculture (FA) district. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies a majority of the property as Low/Medium-Density Residential, and the remainder as Highway Commercial (HC). PLANNNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their October 3, 2024 meeting. There was no public input. PC recommended approval of the annexation and rezoning request. 135 -- 135 of 230 -- STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (D). ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (E), to annex approximately 3.07+/- total acres of property located on Hwy 378, near Airport Rd and 3191 Hwy 378 (PINs 370-04-01-0003, -0002, and 336-13-04- 0007), and rezone from the Horry County High Bulk Retail (RE4) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. BACKGROUND: Two (2) of the three properties under consideration for annexation are currently vacant, and one is an HVAC business looking to expand and redevelop (the existing use) on the properties, once combined. These parcels were recently rezoned in the county – to the High Bulk Retail (RE4) district, but since the properties adjacent to these parcels were annexed as the Brookhaven PD, with one of the properties at the corner of Hwy 378 and Airport Rd, these properties are now contiguous. Rather than running into a scenario where the property completes the rezoning process through the county and then upon plan submittal at the county, having to start over again through the city, the applicant is being proactive and starting the annexation process since these properties are within the city’s utility service area. The requested zoning district upon annexation is Light Industrial (LI). Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the Light Industrial (LI) district is to provide for areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Planned Development (PD) District, Horry County High Bulk Retail (RE4), Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF40) district, Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF40) district, and Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district. There are existing residential uses across the street from the subject properties and the Conway Airport is located behind the subject properties. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Industrial, although the future land use map does not distinguish between light and heavy industrial. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the request at their October 3rd meeting, and recommended approval of the request to annex and rezone to LI. ISSUE: First Reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (H), to amend Article B, Section 1-3-23-Notice Required, of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, relative to public notice requirements for granting a franchise, license or right to use any street or public property, or for the permanent closing of any abandoned street. BACKGROUND: In the past, “Private” Roads, Alleys and Paper Roads have always been closed via an ordinance by the City Council and a Road Closing Action through the Courts. It is staff’s opinion that taking “Private” Roads, Alleys or Paper Roads to City Council for an ordinance does not benefit the process for the applicant. An introduction of an ordinance granting the permanent closing of a “Private” Road, Alley or Paper Road by City Council merely establishes that the City does not claim the “Private” Road, Alley or Paper Road. Per State Code Section 57-9-10, “Any interested person, the State or any of its political subdivisions or agencies may petition a court of competent jurisdiction to abandon or close any street, road or highway whether opened or not. Prior to filing the petition, notice of intention to file shall be published once a week for three consecutive weeks in a newspaper published in the county where such street, road or highway is situated. Notice also shall be sent by mail requiring a return receipt to the last known address of all abutting property owners whose property would be affected by any such change, and posted by the petitioning party along the street, road, or highway, subject to approval of the location of the posting by the governmental entity responsible for maintenance of the street, road, or highway. The Department of Transportation shall promulgate regulations which once effective will establish the minimum mandatory size, language, and specific positioning of signs pursuant to this section.” An applicant wishing to close or abandon a “Private” Road, Alley or Paper Road would be better served to go directly to the courts to petition for the Road Closing Action. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (H). 188 -- 188 of 230 -- ORDINANCE #2024-11-04 (H) AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND ARTICLE B, SECTION 1-3-23-NOTICE REQUIRED, OF THE CITY OF CONWAY CODE OF ORDINANCES. WHEREAS, an ordinance by City Council for the closing or abandonment of a Private Road, Alley or Paper Road merely establishes that the City does not lay claim to said Private Road, Alley or Paper Road; WHEREAS, Section 5-27-150 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, as amended, grants authority to a municipal governing body to close and abandon public streets for the improvement and convenience of the City; WHEREAS, only the courts can establish who, if any person or entity has rights to a “Private” Road, Alley or Paper Road; WHEREAS, it is not beneficial to an applicant petitioning for the closure of a “Private” Road, Alley or Paper Road to be required to request an ordinance from City Council as well as petition the courts for said closure; ORDAINED by the City Council of the City of Conway, in Council duly assembled, that Section 1-2- 23 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Conway shall be amended accordingly, and be it further EFFECTIVE DATE: This ordinance shall become effective upon final reading. 189 -- 189 of 230 -- RATIFIED BY CITY COUNCIL, duly assembled this day of , 2024. Section 501(c)(3), (4), (6), (7), (8), (10) or (19). “Charitable Purpose” means a benevolent, philanthropic, patriotic, or eleemosynary purpose that does not result in personal gain to a sponsor, organizer, officer, director, trustee, or person with ultimate control of the organization. “Classification” means that division of businesses by NAICS codes subject to the same license rate as determined by a calculated index of ability to pay based on national averages, benefits, equalization of tax burden, relationships of services, or other basis deemed appropriate by the Council. “Council” means the City Council of the City of Conway, South Carolina. “Domicile” means a principal place from which the trade or business of a licensee is conducted, directed, or managed. For purposes of this ordinance, a licensee may be deemed to have more than one domicile. “Gross Income” means the gross receipts or gross revenue of a business, received or accrued, for one calendar or fiscal year collected or to be collected from business done within the Municipality. If the licensee has a domicile within the Municipality, business done within the Municipality shall include all gross receipts or revenue received or accrued by such licensee. If the licensee does not have a domicile within the Municipality, business done within the Municipality shall include only gross receipts or revenue received or accrued within the Municipality. In all cases, if the licensee pays a business license tax to another county or municipality, then the licensee’s gross income for the purpose of computing the tax within the Municipality must be reduced by the amount of revenues or receipts taxed in the other county or municipality and fully reported to the Municipality. Gross income for business license tax purposes shall not include taxes collected for a governmental entity, escrow funds, or funds that are the property of a third party. The value of bartered goods or trade-in merchandise shall be 194 -- 194 of 230 -- 2 included in gross income. The gross receipts or gross revenues for business license purposes may be verified by inspection of returns and reports filed with the Internal Revenue Service, the South Carolina Department of Revenue, the South Carolina Department of Insurance, or other government agencies. In calculating gross income for certain businesses, the following rules shall apply: A. Gross income for agents shall be calculated on gross commissions received or retained, unless otherwise specified. If commissions are divided with other brokers or agents, then only the amount retained by the broker or agent is considered gross income. B. Except as specifically required by S.C. Code § 38-7-20, gross income for insurance companies shall be calculated on gross premiums written. C. Gross income for manufacturers of goods or materials with a location in the Municipality shall be calculated on the lesser of (i) gross revenues or receipts received or accrued from business done at the location, (ii) the amount of income allocated and apportioned to that location by the business for purposes of the business’s state income tax return, or (iii) the amount of expenses attributable to the location as a cost center of the business. Licensees reporting gross income under this provision shall have the burden to establish the amount and method of calculation by satisfactory records and proof. Manufacturers include those taxpayers reporting a manufacturing principal business activity code on their federal income tax returns. “License Official” means a person designated to administer this ordinance. Notwithstanding the designation of a primary license official, the Municipality may designate one or more alternate license officials to administer particular types of business licenses, including without limitation for business licenses issued to businesses subject to business license taxes under Article 20, Chapter 9, Title 58, and Chapters 7 and 45, Title 38, of the South Carolina Code. “Licensee” means the business, the person applying for the license on behalf of the business, an agent or legal representative of the business, a person who receives any part of the net profit of the business, or a person who owns or exercises control of the business. “Municipality” means the City of Conway, South Carolina. “NAICS” means the North American Industry Classification System for the United States published under the auspices of the Federal Office of Management and Budget. “Person” means any individual, firm, partnership, limited liability partnership, limited liability company, cooperative non-profit membership, corporation, joint venture, association, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, syndicate, holding company, or other group or combination acting as a unit, in the singular or plural, and the agent or employee having charge or control of a business in the absence of the principal. “Real Estate Rental Business” means any persons deriving rental income from more than one real property Section 3. Purpose and Duration. The business license required by this ordinance is for the purpose of providing such regulation as may be required for the business subject thereto and for the purpose of raising revenue for the general fund through a privilege tax. Except as set forth 195 -- 195 of 230 -- 3 below for business licenses issued to contractors with respect to specific construction projects, each yearly license shall be issued for the twelve-month period of May 1 to April 30. A business license issued for a construction contract may, at the request of the licensee, be stated to expire at the completion of the construction project; provided, any such business license may require that the licensee file, by each April 30 during the continuation of the construction project, a statement of compliance, including but not limited to a revised estimate of the value of the contract. If any revised estimate of the final value of such project exceeds the amount for which the business license was issued, the licensee shall be required to pay a license fee at the then- prevailing rate on the excess amount. The provisions of this ordinance and the rates herein shall remain in effect from year to year as amended by the Council. Section 4. Business License Tax, Refund. A. The required business license tax shall be paid for each business subject hereto according to the applicable rate classification on or before the due date of the 30th day of April in each year, except for those businesses in Rate Class 8 for which a different due date is specified. Late payments shall be subject to penalties as set forth in Section 12 hereof, except that admitted insurance companies may pay before June 1 without penalty. B. A separate license shall be required for each place of business and for each classification or business conducted at one place. If gross income cannot be separated for classifications at one location, the business license tax shall be computed on the combined gross income for the classification requiring the highest rate. The business license tax must be computed based on the licensee’s gross income for the calendar year preceding the due date, for the licensee’s twelve-month fiscal year preceding the due date, or on a twelve-month projected income based on the monthly average for a business in operation for less than one year. The business license tax for a new business must be computed on the estimated probable gross income for the balance of the license year. A business license related to construction contract projects may be issued on a per- project basis, at the option of the taxpayer. No refund shall be made for a business that is discontinued. C. A licensee that submits a payment greater than the amount owed may request a refund. To be considered, a refund request must be submitted in writing to the Municipality before the June 1 immediately following the April 30 on which the payment was due and must be supported by adequate documentation supporting the refund request. The Municipality shall approve or deny the refund request, and if approved shall issue the refund to the business, within thirty days after receipt of the request. Section 5. Registration Required. A. The owner, agent, or legal representative of every business subject to this ordinance, whether listed in the classification index or not, shall register the business and make application for a business license on or before the due date of each year; provided, a new business shall be required to have a business license prior to operation within the Municipality, and an annexed business shall be required to have a business license within thirty (30) days of the annexation. A license for a bar (NAICS 722410) must be issued in 196 -- 196 of 230 -- 4 the name of the individual who has been issued the corresponding state alcohol, beer, or wine permit or license and will have actual control and management of the business. B. Application shall be on the then-current standard business license application as established and provided by the Director of the South Carolina Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office and shall be accompanied by all information about the applicant, the licensee, and the business deemed appropriate to carry out the purpose of this ordinance by the license official. Applicants may be required to submit copies of portions of state and federal income tax returns reflecting gross receipts and gross revenue figures. C. The applicant shall certify under oath that the information given in the application is true, that the gross income is accurately reported (or estimated for a new business) without any unauthorized deductions, and that all assessments, personal property taxes on business property, and other monies due and payable to the Municipality have been paid. D. The Municipality shall allow application, reporting, calculation, and payment of business license taxes through the business license tax portal hosted and managed by the South Carolina Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office, subject to the availability and capability thereof. Any limitations in portal availability or capability do not relieve the applicant or Licensee from existing business license or business license tax obligations. Section 6. Deductions, Exemptions, and Charitable Organizations. A. No deductions from gross income shall be made except income earned outside of the Municipality on which a license tax is paid by the business to some other municipality or county and fully reported to the Municipality, taxes collected for a governmental entity, or income which cannot be included for computation of the tax pursuant to state or federal law. Properly apportioned income from business in interstate commerce shall be included in the calculation of gross income and is not exempted. The applicant shall have the burden to establish the right to exempt income by satisfactory records and proof. B. No person shall be exempt from the requirements of the ordinance by reason of the lack of an established place of business within the Municipality, unless exempted by state or federal law. The license official shall determine the appropriate classification for each business in accordance with the latest issue of NAICS. No person shall be exempt from this ordinance by reason of the payment of any other tax, unless exempted by state law, and no person shall be relieved of liability for payment of any other tax or fee by reason of application of this ordinance. C. Wholesalers are exempt from business license taxes unless they maintain warehouses or distribution establishments within the Municipality. A wholesale transaction involves a sale to an individual who will resell the goods and includes delivery of the goods to the reseller. It does not include a sale of goods to a user or consumer. D. A charitable organization shall be exempt from the business license tax on its gross income unless it is deemed a business subject to a business license tax on all or part of its gross income as provided in this section. A charitable organization, or any affiliate of a charitable organization, that reports income from for-profit activities or unrelated 197 -- 197 of 230 -- 5 business income for federal income tax purposes to the Internal Revenue Service shall be deemed a business subject to a business license tax on the part of its gross income from such for-profit activities or unrelated business income. E. A charitable organization shall be deemed a business subject to a business license tax on its total gross income if (1) any net proceeds of operation, after necessary expenses of operation, inure to the benefit of any individual or any entity that is not itself a charitable organization as defined in this ordinance, or (2) any net proceeds of operation, after necessary expenses of operation, are used for a purpose other than a charitable purpose as defined in this ordinance. Excess benefits or compensation in any form beyond fair market value to a sponsor, organizer, officer, director, trustee, or person with ultimate control of the organization shall not be deemed a necessary expense of operation. Section 7. False Application Unlawful. It shall be unlawful for any person subject to the provisions of this ordinance to make a false application for a business license or to give or file, or direct the giving or filing of, any false information with respect to the license or tax required by this ordinance. Section 8. Display and Transfer. A. All persons shall display the license issued to them on the original form provided by the license official in a conspicuous place in the business establishment at the address shown on the license. A transient or non-resident shall carry the license upon his person or in a vehicle used in the business readily available for inspection by any authorized agent of the Municipality. B. A change of address must be reported to the license official within ten (10) days after removal of the business to a new location and the license will be valid at the new address upon written notification by the license official and compliance with zoning and building codes. Failure to obtain the approval of the license official for a change of address shall invalidate the license and subject the licensee to prosecution for doing business without a license. A business license shall not be transferable, and a transfer of controlling interest shall be considered a termination of the old business and the establishment of a new business requiring a new business license, based on old business income. Section 9. Administration of Ordinance. The license official shall administer the provisions of this ordinance, collect business license taxes, issue licenses, make or initiate investigations and audits to ensure compliance, initiate denial or suspension and revocation procedures, report violations to the municipal attorney, assist in prosecution of violators, produce forms, undertake reasonable procedures relating to the administration of this ordinance, and perform such other duties as may be duly assigned. 198 -- 198 of 230 -- 6 Section 10. Inspection and Audits. A. For the purpose of enforcing the provisions of this ordinance, the license official or other authorized agent of the Municipality is empowered to enter upon the premises of any person subject to this ordinance to make inspections and to examine and audit books and records. It shall be unlawful for any such person to fail or refuse to make available the necessary books and records. In the event an audit or inspection reveals that the licensee has filed false information, the costs of the audit shall be added to the correct business license tax and late penalties in addition to other penalties provided herein. Each day of failure to pay the proper amount of business license tax shall constitute a separate offense. B. The license official shall have the authority to make inspections and conduct audits of businesses to ensure compliance with the ordinance. Financial information obtained by inspections and audits shall not be deemed public records, and the license official shall not release the amount of business license taxes paid or the reported gross income of any person by name without written permission of the licensee, except as authorized by this ordinance, state or federal law, or proper judicial order. Statistics compiled by classifications are public records. Section 11. Assessments, Payment under Protest, Appeal. A. Assessments, payments under protest, and appeals of assessment shall be allowed and conducted by the Municipality pursuant to the provisions of S.C. Code § 6-1-410, as amended. In preparing an assessment, the license official may examine such records of the business or any other available records as may be appropriate and conduct such investigations and statistical surveys as the license official may deem appropriate to assess a business license tax and penalties as provided herein. B. The license official shall establish a uniform local procedure consistent with S.C. Code § 6-1-410 for hearing an application for adjustment of assessment and issuing a notice of final assessment; provided that for particular types of business licenses, including without limitation for business licenses issued to businesses subject to business license taxes under Article 20, Chapter 9, Title 58, and Chapters 7 and 45, Title 38, of the South Carolina Code, the Municipality, by separate ordinance, may establish a different procedure and may delegate one or more rights, duties, and functions hereunder to the Municipal Association of South Carolina. Section 12. Delinquent License Taxes, Partial Payment. A. For non-payment of all or any part of the correct business license tax, the license official shall impose and collect a late penalty of five (5%) percent of the unpaid tax for each month or portion thereof after the due date until paid. Penalties shall not be waived. If any business license tax remains unpaid for sixty (60) days after its due date, the license official shall report it to the municipal attorney for appropriate legal action. B. Partial payment may be accepted by the license official to toll imposition of penalties on the portion paid; provided, however, no business license shall be issued or renewed until the full amount of the tax due, with penalties, has been paid. 199 -- 199 of 230 -- 7 Section 13. Notices. The license official may, but shall not be required to, mail written notices that business license taxes are due. If notices are not mailed, there shall be published a notice of the due date in a newspaper of general circulation within the Municipality three (3) times prior to the due date in each year. Failure to receive notice shall not constitute a defense to prosecution for failure to pay the tax due or grounds for waiver of penalties. Section 14. Denial of License. The license official may deny a license to an applicant when the license official determines: A. The application is incomplete or contains a misrepresentation, false or misleading statement, or evasion or suppression of a material fact; B. The activity for which a license is sought is unlawful or constitutes a public nuisance per se or per accidens; C. The applicant, licensee, prior licensee, or the person in control of the business has been convicted within the previous ten years of an offense under a law or ordinance regulating business, a crime involving dishonest conduct or moral turpitude related to a business or a subject of a business, or an unlawful sale of merchandise or prohibited goods; D. The applicant, licensee, prior licensee, or the person in control of the business has engaged in an unlawful activity or nuisance related to the business or to a similar business in the Municipality or in another jurisdiction; E. The applicant, licensee, prior licensee, or the person in control of the business is delinquent in the payment to the Municipality of any tax or fee; F. A licensee has actual knowledge or notice, or based on the circumstances reasonably should have knowledge or notice, that any person or employee of the licensee has committed a crime of moral turpitude on the business premises, or has permitted any person or employee of the licensee to engage in the unlawful sale of merchandise or prohibited goods on the business premises and has not taken remedial measures necessary to correct such activity; or G. The license for the business or for a similar business of the licensee in the Municipality or another jurisdiction has been denied, suspended, or revoked in the previous license year. A decision of the license official shall be subject to appeal as herein provided. Denial shall be written with reasons stated. Section 15. Suspension or Revocation of License. When the license official determines: A. A license has been mistakenly or improperly issued or issued contrary to law; B. A licensee has breached any condition upon which the license was issued or has failed to comply with the provisions of this ordinance; C. A licensee has obtained a license through a fraud, misrepresentation, a false or misleading statement, or evasion or suppression of a material fact in the license application; D. A licensee has been convicted within the previous ten years of an offense under a law or ordinance regulating business, a crime involving dishonest conduct or moral turpitude 200 -- 200 of 230 -- 8 related to a business or a subject of a business, or an unlawful sale of merchandise or prohibited goods; E. A licensee has engaged in an unlawful activity or nuisance related to the business; or F. A licensee is delinquent in the payment to the Municipality of any tax or fee, the license official may give written notice to the licensee or the person in control of the business within the Municipality by personal service or mail that the license is suspended pending a single hearing before Council or its designee for the purpose of determining whether the suspension should be upheld and the license should be revoked. The written notice of suspension and proposed revocation shall state the time and place at which the hearing is to be held, and shall contain a brief statement of the reasons for the suspension and proposed revocation and a copy of the applicable provisions of this ordinance. Section 16. Appeals to Council or its Designee. A. Except with respect to appeals of assessments under Section 11 hereof, which are governed by S.C. Code § 6-1-410, any person aggrieved by a determination, denial, or suspension and proposed revocation of a business license by the license official may appeal the decision to the Council or its designee by written request stating the reasons for appeal, filed with the license official within ten (10) days after service by mail or personal service of the notice of determination, denial, or suspension and proposed revocation. B. A hearing on an appeal from a license denial or other determination of the license official and a hearing on a suspension and proposed revocation shall be held by the Council or its designee within ten (10) business days after receipt of a request for appeal or service of a notice of suspension and proposed revocation. The hearing shall be held upon written notice at a regular or special meeting of the Council, or, if by designee of the Council, at a hearing to be scheduled by the designee. The hearing may be continued to another date by agreement of all parties. At the hearing, all parties shall have the right to be represented by counsel, to present testimony and evidence, and to cross-examine witnesses. The proceedings shall be recorded and transcribed at the expense of the party so requesting. The rules of evidence and procedure prescribed by Council or its designee shall govern the hearing. Following the hearing, the Council by majority vote of its members present, or the designee of Council if the hearing is held by the designee, shall render a written decision based on findings of fact and conclusions on application of the standards herein. The written decision shall be served, by personal service or by mail, upon all parties or their representatives and shall constitute the final decision of the Municipality. C. Timely appeal of a decision of Council or its designee does not effectuate a stay of that decision. The decision of the Council or its designee shall be binding and enforceable unless overturned by an applicable appellate court after a due and timely appeal. 201 -- 201 of 230 -- 9 D. For business licenses issued to businesses subject to business license taxes under Article 20, Chapter 9, Title 58, and Chapters 7 and 45, Title 38, of the South Carolina Code, the Municipality may establish a different procedure by ordinance. Section 17. Consent, franchise, or license required for use of streets. A. It shall be unlawful for any person to construct, install, maintain, or operate in, on, above, or under any street or public place under control of the Municipality any line, pipe, cable, pole, structure, or facility for utilities, communications, cablevision, or other purposes without a consent agreement or franchise agreement issued by the Council by ordinance that prescribes the term, fees, and conditions for use. B. The annual fee for use of streets or public places authorized by a consent agreement or franchise agreement shall be set by the ordinance approving the agreement and shall be consistent with limits set by state law. Existing franchise agreements shall continue in effect until expiration dates in the agreements. Franchise and consent fees shall not be in lieu of or be credited against business license taxes unless specifically provided by the franchise or consent agreement. Section 18. Confidentiality. Except in accordance with proper judicial order or as otherwise provided by law, no official or employee of the Municipality may divulge or make known in any manner the amount of income or any financial particulars set forth or disclosed in any report or return required under this ordinance. Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit the publication of statistics so classified as to prevent the identification of particular reports or returns. Any license data may be shared with other public officials or employees in the performance of their duties, whether or not those duties relate to enforcement of this ordinance. Section 19. Violations. Any person violating any provision of this ordinance shall be deemed guilty of an offense and shall be subject to a fine of up to $500.00 or imprisonment for not more than thirty (30) days or both, upon conviction. Each day of violation shall be considered a separate offense. Punishment for violation shall not relieve the offender of liability for delinquent taxes, penalties, and costs provided for in this ordinance. Section 20. Severability. A determination that any portion of this ordinance is invalid or unenforceable shall not affect the remaining portions. To the extent of any conflict between the provisions of this ordinance and the provisions of the South Carolina Business License Tax Standardization Act, as codified at S.C. Code §§ 6-1-400 et seq., the standardization act shall control. Section 21. Classification and Rates. A. The business license tax for each class of businesses subject to this ordinance shall be computed in accordance with the current business license rate schedule, designated as Appendix A to this ordinance, which may be amended from time to time by the Council. B. The current business license class schedule is attached hereto as Appendix B. Hereafter, no later than December 31 of each odd year, the Municipality shall adopt, by ordinance, the latest standardized business license class schedule as recommended by the Municipal Association of South Carolina and adopted by the Director of the South Carolina Revenue 202 -- 202 of 230 -- 10 and Fiscal Affairs Office. Upon adoption by the Municipality, the revised business license class schedule shall then be appended to this ordinance as a replacement Appendix B. C. The classifications included in each rate class are listed with NAICS codes, by sector, sub- sector, group, or industry. The business license class schedule (Appendix B) is a tool for classification and not a limitation on businesses subject to a business license tax. The classification in the most recent version of the business license class schedule adopted by the Council that most specifically identifies the subject business shall be applied to the business. The license official shall have the authority to make the determination of the classification most specifically applicable to a subject business. D. text: October 21, 2024 Page 1 of 11 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY MONDAY, OCTOBER 21, 2024 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Pro Tem Larry White, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan. ABSENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; June Wood, Public Information Officer; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality & Beautification Director; Ted Dudley, Interim Public Utilities Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Kym Wilkerson, Planning and Development Deputy Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Ashley Smith, Parks and Recreation Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Braxton Fleming, Public Works Deputy Director; Rosanne Dates, Grants and Special Projects Division Chief; Kyle Hardee, Property Maintenance Inspector; Tammy Carter, Captain; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. Robert Bannan, Kingston Presbyterian gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. CONSENT AGENDA: A. INTRODUCTION OF NEW HIRES: White introduced and welcomed the following new hires: Jacob Shroba, Police Officer Patrol Andrew Wangstad, Senior Master Police Officer Matthew Carl Senior, Master Police Officer Titus Davis, Solid Waste Equipment Operator I Clayton Ricks, Public Utilities Tradesworker Joseph Durante, Public Utilities Tradesworker I Mason Johnson, Light Mechanic I Carolyn Wilson, Facilities Technician SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Presentation of a Proclamation Celebrating National Disability Employment Awareness Month – White presented the proclamation to CCU, the Coastal Life staff and students. B. Presentation of Employee of the Month for October 2024 – Public Service – Cooper presented Kyle Hardee with the employee of the month award. C. Discussion of a Proposed Amendment to Article 6 – Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) to remove El Bethel Road from the Village Corridor Overlay (VCO). Hucks stated that this item was initially discussed at Council’s budget retreat earlier this year. The VCO, or Village Corridor Overlay, is -- 2 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 3 of 11 intended to promote compact, pedestrian scale development with residential, neighborhood commercial, and professional uses. The current overlay includes properties with frontage along minor arterials and collector streets per the city’s zoning map. In addition to the typical zoning requirements, overlays add an additional layer of requirements for properties that are located within overlays. Some of the requirements for properties within the Village Corridor Overlay include access management, connectivity, additional landscaping & buffer standards, and sign limitations. With regard to El Bethel Road, the character of the road has changed over the last several years, with the rezoning of several properties to Institutional to allow for educational or medical facilities. Some of the standards of the overlay may create hardships for some of the properties yet to be developed, particularly with regard to height limitation and signage. Regardless of the zoning district, the maximum height for properties in the VCO is 40 ft., while the institutional zoning district allows a maximum height of 80 ft. Signs are limited to 24 sq. ft. for a single tenant, and 40 sq. ft. for a multi-tenant building. The new middle school requested and received a variance for the sign they have installed as it exceeded the square footage that was permitted – not in the zoning district or the type of sign, but due to the overlay. El Bethel Rd also has a wider right-of-way than other streets that are within the Village Corridor Overlay, with a right-of-way width of 150-ft. With the addition of the perimeter road, once completed, it will be a heavier traveled road for vehicles and tractor trailers to get from 701 north or west of Conway to 701 South and Hwy 501 Bypass. Hucks said that this item is for discussion only, and Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this amendment and make a recommendation to Council at their November 7 meeting. D. Discussion of a proposed amendment to Article 11 – Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for sign. Hucks said that the amendments proposed in Article 11 of the Unified Development ordinance stem from the 2023 budget retreat, in which a cleanup of the UDO was presented. This ordinance has been amended a few times over the years, and more recently, amendments to the EMC / LED section of the ordinance. However, Article 11 has not had a comprehensive review like other Articles of the UDO, and it remains to be one of the most misinterpreted ordinances, or that has different interpretations for the same requirements. Most of the variance requests that staff receives is for setback requirements and signage, and sign standards tend to be the most violated of all zoning requirements. Some of the items that are proposed to be amended include obsolete and abandoned sign standards, to make it clear that any sign deemed to be obsolete or abandoned cannot be re- established or reused and must be removed from the property in its entirety; illumination standards language; adding murals to the list of signs that are exempt from permitting procedures; standards for wall signs – particularly with regard to where a second wall sign is permitted if the property or building is located on a corner lot; as well as adding a minimum separation for EMC/LED signs from residential structures. Hucks said that Planning Commission is set to hold the public hearing at their November 7 meeting, and their recommendation on the proposed amendments will be forwarded to Council with first reading. There was some discussion regarding the separation requirement of 100 ft. for EMC/LED signs from residential structures. -- 3 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 4 of 11 SECOND/FINAL READING: Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-10-21 (C), to annex approximately 0.2 acres of property located at 628 Lesia Lane (PIN 382-12-01-0003), and rezone from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF6) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district. Dennis said that this is second reading for this request as a requirement to connect to city services. The property is located within the Pine Valley Estates subdivision, off Highway 544. There is an existing manufactured home with brick underpinning on the property. Council has annexed five other properties within the Pine Valley Estates Subdivision with the most recent being in 2023. Hucks stated that the future land use map does identify the property as R-1 and staff recommends approval. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve final reading of Ordinance #2024- 10-21 (C). Vote: Hardwick, Jordan, White, Butler, Helms voted yes. Goldfinch voted no. Motion carried with a 5-1 vote. PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST READING: A. Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (A) amending Title 5 Planning and Development, Section 5-1-4 Permit Fees of the City of Conway. Williams stated that the Stormwater Review Fee was previously discussed at budget retreat and the new fees are outlined in the issue paper. Williams said that staff recommends adopting the updated fees as proposed. Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Jordan to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (A). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Public Hearing and First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (B), to amend the City’s Future Land Use Map (2019-2029) (FLUM) of the City of Conway Comprehensive Plan, relative to property located at 1926 Fulmer Street, (PIN 338- 06-02-0038), consisting of approximately 0.32 acres, from the Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) zoning district to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. Hucks stated that this item and the next item are regarding the same parcel if Council would like to combine the two. Hucks said that this request was briefly discussed at a council meeting in September. The applicants are seeking to expand their existing childcare center, Rivertown Child Development, which is located at 1911 N. Main Street. The applicants purchased the subject property that adjoins the childcare center in order to combine it with the property containing the existing childcare center. However, the subject property is zoned R-1, or low/medium-density residential, and split zoning of property is not permitted. In order for the properties to be combined, the subject property would have to be rezoned to the Highway Commercial district, which is the same zoning of the property where the childcare center is located. The City’s future land use map was last updated in 2019. Staff will occasionally review annexation / rezoning requests for zones that do not match the zoning envisioned on the current future land use map. When a request to annex or rezone property is approved that does not align with the future land use map, it must be -- 4 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 5 of 11 updated to reflect the change. Council adopted an ordinance in 2021 providing a method in which the future land use map may be amended. Changes in the future land use map are also considered an amendment to the comprehensive plan, which requires two public hearings. The first public hearing was held by Planning Commission at their October 3 meeting. The second was advertised to be held at today’s council meeting. With regard to the rezoning request, the subject property is currently vacant, but until recently, it did contain a dilapidated residential structure, which contributed to neighborhood blight. The applicants’ plans include: (1) Combining the subject property with childcare center property; (2) Adding an addition to the existing childcare facility, which must meet a 20’ rear yard setback; (3) Relocating the playground to the property fronting Fulmer Street; and (4) Add parking for staff on property fronting Fulmer Street. Hucks stated that one of the concerns that was expressed during special presentation was the further encroachment of commercial uses into a residential neighborhood, and how that was different than previous requests that could be considered similar in nature. While there are similarities, there are also differences. A previous request to rezone properties closer to Laurel Street would have been a change in the character of the area in that where there were no previous requests to rezone properties in that area to commercial, this would have been the first attempt, on a street that was strictly residential and mostly single-family only. In the immediate area, there is no existence of nonconforming lots, structures or uses. There is no Highway Commercial zoning along Main Street until you get to North Main Street at the corner of Parkview Road and Oak Street. The subject property is located on Fulmer Street, one street over from North Main Street. Fulmer Street has a mix of uses and nonconforming lots or structures, including a property containing either a couple of duplex units or multi-family units and a single-family home on the same lot, a single-family home on a lot zoned neighborhood commercial. The property is across from a lot that was rezoned to Professional in 2023, given that the property contained a church and other than a church, the only other use that would have been permitted was a single-family home, which would have likely required that existing structure to be removed; and the subject property is adjacent to property zoned Highway Commercial. Until 2022, that property was zoned R-1 and at one time, contained an auto repair or auto body business. More recently, the property was improved but the structure remained, and the business looking to locate in that building is a fitness center. That building is approximately 5’ from the property line shared with this property. Hucks also noted that across Main Street, on the other side of Session Street, the Freeze sought and received approval to rezone the vacant parcel directly behind the restaurant to Highway Commercial in 2022 in order to expand their parking area. The possibility of the applicants seeking to rezone the property as Professional rather than Highway Commercial was mentioned as well. However, if they did so, it would prevent expansion of the building footprint, as the professional district limits the building footprint to 30% of the lot. Finally, while staff cannot require them to do so, the applicants are requesting that if first reading is approved, that final reading be delayed until the plat to combine the properties is recorded. Once recorded, they will seek final reading of the requests. Once the properties are combined, if they were ever proposed to be reseparated post construction of the addition to the childcare facility and the parking lot, both properties would have to comply with the requirements for the HC district, and no nonconformities could be created by the subdivision – for both lots. -- 5 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 6 of 11 Huck said that Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their October 3 meeting. There was no public input. Planning Commission recommended approval of both the future land use map amendment and the rezoning request and staff supports Planning Commission’s recommendations. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to close the public hearing. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Jordan to combine Ordinances #ZA2024- 11-04 (B) and #ZA2024-11-04 (C) and approve the first reading. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. FIRST READING: A. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (C) to rezone approximately 0.32 acres of property located at 1926 Fulmer Street (PIN 338-06-02-0038) from the Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. See previous motion. B. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (D) to annex approximately 20.7 acres of property located at 3633 Hwy 501, near Booth Circle (PIN 326-00-00-0024), and rezone from the Horry County High Bulk Retail (RE4) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) districts to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated that this property was first proposed to be annexed in 2022, when it was Pinnacle Storage. The annexation and rezoning requests received first reading in July 2022, but at that time, there was agreement to delay final reading until the county had issued certificates of occupancy for all buildings that had received permit approval from the county. Between then and now, three buildings have been constructed and the property has changed hands. Once staff was aware that there were no outstanding permits, we began the process of restarting the annexation due to the change in ownership. The property is currently split zoned between Horry County RE4 (high bulk retail) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) and the requested zoning upon annexation is Light Industrial. Hucks said that Planning Commission held the required public hearing at their October 3 meeting and recommended approval of the request. Staff also recommends approval. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (D). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. C. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (E) to annex approximately 3.07+/- total acres of property located on Hwy 378, near Airport Rd and 3191 Hwy 378 (PIN’s 370- 04-01-0002, -0003, and 336-13-04-0007), and request to rezone from the Horry County High Bulk Retail (RE4) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated that the applicant is requesting annexation and rezoning of three parcels on Highway 378 that became contiguous with the annexation of the property known as the Brookhaven Planned Development. It is across from the residential portion of the proposed development and is abutting the piece of the PD at the corner of Highway 378 and Airport -- 6 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 7 of 11 Road that will is proposed to have industrial and commercial uses. The applicant started the process of rezoning the properties in the county, and it is staffs understanding that it was successfully rezoned to RE4 (high bulk retail) recently; however, due to the requirement to connect to city utilities once development occurs, the applicant also applied for annexation and rezoning before submitting plans to the county for review. One of the parcels currently has an HVAC business that is looking to redevelop the existing business on the properties. There was a proposed site plan included in the packet. The existing structure would be removed. The site plan has not yet been reviewed by TRC. The requested zoning upon annexation is Light Industrial (LI), which is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. Hucks said that Planning commission considered the request at their October 3 meeting. There was no public input. PC recommended approval of the request and staff also recommends approval. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (E). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. D. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (F) to annex approximately 4.50 acres of property located on Hwy 501, near Conbraco Circle (PIN 399-08-01-0001), and request to rezone from the Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Dennis stated that the owner is requesting annexation and rezoning due to being within the City’s service area and now being contiguous to City limits with the most recent annexation of Lynn Ladder. The property is currently vacant with 2 storm water ponds and staff is unaware of any plans for development at this time. The applicant is requesting to rezone from Horry County Limited Industrial to the City of Conway Highway Commercial. The Future Land Use Map does identify this property as Highway Commercial. Dennis said that staff does recommend approval. Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Helms to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (F). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. E. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-11-04 (G), to rezone approximately 182+/- acres of property located on Waccamaw Drive, (PIN 382-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Conservation Preservation (CP) district. Dennis stated that this property is located off Waccamaw Drive and was formerly known as the Skipper tract owned by the Historic Ricefields Association. The property was transferred to the City of Conway last month and is currently zoned R-1. The City is seeking a rezoning to Conservation Preservation to follow the future land use map and preserve the environmentally sensitive nature of the property. Dennis said that staff does recommend approval. Motion: Helms made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (G). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. F. First Reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (H) amending Article B, Section 1-3-23 – Notice Required, of the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, relative to public notice -- 7 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 8 of 11 requirements for granting a franchise, license or right to use any street or public property, or for the permanent closing of any abandoned street. Wilkerson stated that this amendment was discussed at the last workshop. Wilkerson said that in the past private roads, streets and alleys whether open or not have always been closed via the ordinance by City Council and a road closing action through the courts. It is staffs opinion that taking private roads, streets and alleys to City Council for an ordinance does not benefit the process for the city or the applicant. An ordinance from City Council to close a private road, street or alley simply establishes that the city has no said claims to the private roads, street or alley. Should the applicant requesting the closing of a private road, street or alley may only be required a road closing action from the courts, this action would essentially accomplish the same outcome as an ordinance from City Council since an agent from the City of Conway must sign the road closing document stating that the City of Conway has no interest. The road closing action through the court requires the applicant to publish a notice of intention for three consecutive weeks, mail via returned receipt all adjacent property owners and road must be posted with specific signage per state code Section 57- 9-10. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Butler to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (H). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. G. First Reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (I) amending the City’s Professional and Business License Ordinance to update the definition of a Real Estate Rental Business. Williams said that this definition change was discussed at budget retreat and was presented as part of budget. Staff just needs to update the actual business license ordinance to reflect the new definition of real estate rental business as being any persons deriving rental income from more than one real property. Williams said that staff recommends first reading. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Hardwick to approve the first reading of Ordinance #2024-11-04 (I). Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSIDERATION: A. Consideration of a Special Event Request by Conway Downtown Alive – Conway’s New Year’s Eve – December 31, 2024 – Howard stated that Conway Downtown Alive has submitted a request for Conway’s New Year's Eve which is December 31 from 10:30 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. consisting of a fireworks display, DJ services and food trucks at the old tennis center. Howard said that no streets or parking areas will be closed as part of this request. Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Helms, to approve the special event as presented. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. B. Consideration of Approval of a Hydraulic Study for the Public Utilities Department. Dudley stated that as the community continues to grow it is crucial that the city adapts to meet the increasing demands of the city’s water system. To address these challenges staff recommends conducting a professional hydraulic study, which will serve as the first step in a plan necessary to restructure improvements. The Public Utilities Department -- 8 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 9 of 11 recommends hiring AECOM Engineering who is currently on retainer for the city to perform the hydraulic study. Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms, to approve the hydraulic study for the Public Utilities Department. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT: Emrick informed Council of the following: • Emrick stated that staff is working to create a Tax Increment Financing District and have asked the County and the School District to participate. This district will allow for the City to add some very major infrastructure to the downtown and riverfront areas, including a parking deck, all of the recreational amenities at the Santee Cooper properties that the city is acquiring, improved streets throughout the district… really all of the big things that the city hasn’t been able to do before given the limits of our budget. John Rogers isn’t here, he has left to go to the School Board meeting tonight and Emrick hopes to join him there at the conclusion of council meeting to ask the District to participate in this project, because of this, Emrick said that his report will be abbreviated. A final thought on the TIF, without the cooperation of the School District and the County, the TIF will not be successful, and the city will have no identified source of funding for this infrastructure. • Halloween has been an overwhelming success. Most of you have been downtown to see the staggering number of people coming to see what we have created. To add data to the experience, the city is up almost 35% in monthly visitors over last year. The data has a lag, so Emrick said that he did not have a full picture of this weekend, but last Saturday the city had over 16,000 people downtown, and 36,000 people were here just last weekend. On Friday the 18th, the city had almost 12,000 people. A normal Friday or Saturday night in any other month, data shows somewhere between 6k and 9k people. These extra people are here, walking downtown, shopping in stores, filling restaurants, and experiencing Conway in a new way. We focus a lot on what the hospitality fees that we gain from this month mean to Conway and to the restaurants, but we haven’t focused on the value of this. Conway is seen by our region as a cool place. A place that does wild, amazing things. It is seen by our younger residents as a place they want to live. It is seen by our graduating college students as a home, and not a stay. This is new and what we do at the holidays, especially Halloween, is the driver of this. Attracting and retaining young talent is the key to the success of any downtown, and we have unlocked a new way to do this. Now we just need downtown housing for them to live. • The city still has a number of new and great events to experience this month. This Friday at the Terrace, the movie is Arachnophobia, Saturday is the Conway Artisans Festival, Sunday is Scare on the Square, professional wrestling like its never been done before, Wednesday the 30th is Nightmare on Elm Street, a basketball crossover event with Coastal Carolina University. This will be on Elm Street between 2nd and 3rd Avenue. Staff is closing the road and painting a full-sized basketball court on the road. And of course, on Halloween night, It’s a Great Pumpkin Charlie Brown movie will be shown at the Terrace on loop for the Trick or Treating Hours. • Finally, Emrick invited all to participate in the magic of switching from Halloween to Christmas and said to meet at City Hall at 4 a.m. on the morning of the November 1. -- 9 of 11 -- October 21, 2024 Page 10 of 11 Goldfinch asked Emrick to explain the procurement issue that Conway Ford brought forward during public input.
