Definitions Section 2.2 – Definitions 2.2.1 General Definitions Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS). A device or station, containing one or more parking spaces that provide power to charge the batteries of an electric-powered vehicle (EV) or a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) through the use of an electric vehicle charger and/or electric vehicle service equipment (EVSE). There are 3 levels of EV charging: • Level 1 charging operates on a fifteen (15) to twenty (20) amp breaker on a one hundred twenty (120) volt AC circuit. • Level 2 charging operates on a forty (40) to one hundred (100) amp breaker on a two hundred eight (208) or two hundred forty (240) volt AC circuit. • Level 3 charging, or Direct-current fast charging (DCFC) operates on a sixty (60) amp or higher breaker on a four hundred eighty (480) volt or higher three phase circuit with special grounding equipment. DCFC stations can also be referred to as rapid charging stations that are typically characterized by industrial grade electrical outlets that allow for faster recharging of electric vehicles. Article 5. Specific Use Regulations Section 5.1 – Conditional Uses 5.1.36 Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) The purpose of this Section is to promote and encourage the use of electric vehicles by requiring the safe and efficient installation of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) with associated supply/service equipment through regulations and other standards contained herein; subject to the following: A. Level 1 and Level 2 chargers and/or charging stations are permitted as an accessory to any use in all zoning districts. B. Level 3 chargers, or Direct-Current Fast Chargers (DCFC) and/or stations are permitted as an accessory use in zoning districts that permit a gas/service station as a principal use (NC, HC, CC, LI, HI), provided that the property is not located within a CAB review district, in which case, Level 3 chargers are prohibited, regardless of zoning. Where installation of Level 3 chargers/charging stations are permitted, the following conditions apply: 1. Charging spaces / stations shall comply with ADA general accessibility requirements. 2. All chargers/charging stations and related service equipment shall meet a minimum 10-ft setback from all property lines and shall not be located within any sight triangles. 3. All service equipment associated with electric vehicle charging stations must be properly screened, in accordance with the standards set forth in Article 6. 4. Such charging spaces and/or stations shall be subject to site plan review and approval by the Planning Dept. and / or Construction Services (Building) Dept. All applicable zoning permits and/or building permits must be obtained prior to installation. 5. All conditions of prior approvals for the existing site and/or structure shall continue to be met. 6. Charging stations shall be compliant with all applicable building codes, fire codes, and all other applicable local, state, and federal laws regarding electric vehicle charging stations. 267 -- 267 of 296 -- U.S. Department of Energy - Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy Alternative Fuels Data Center Developing Infrastructure to Charge Electric Vehicles Consumers and fleets considering electric vehicles (EVs)—which include all-electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs)—need access to charging stations. For most drivers, this starts with charging at home (electricity_charging_home.html) or at fleet facilities. Charging stations at workplaces (electricity_charging_workplace.html) and public destinations (electricity_charging_public.html) may help bolster market acceptance by offering more flexible charging opportunities at commonly visited locations. Community leaders can find out more through EV readiness planning (/pev-readiness.html), including case studies (https://afdc.energy.gov/case/3101) of ongoing successes. The EVI-Pro Lite tool (/evi-pro-lite) is also available to estimate the quantity and type of charging infrastructure necessary to support regional adoption of EVs by state or city/urban area and to determine how EV charging will impact electricity demand. Charging the growing number of EVs in use requires a robust network of stations for both consumers and fleets. The Alternative Fueling Station Locator (/stations/#/find/nearest) allows users to search for public and private charging stations. Quarterly reports on EV charging station trends (/fuels/electricity_infrastructure_trends.html) show the growth of public and private charging and assess the current state of charging infrastructure in the United States. Report new charging stations for inclusion in the Station Locator using the Submit New Station (/stations/#/station/new) form. Suggest updates to existing charging stations by selecting “Report a change” on the station details page. Learn more about state electrification planning and funding (/fuels/electricity_infrastructure_state_planning.html), including information about the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. For information on currently available charging infrastructure models, see the Electric Drive Transportation Association’s GoElectricDrive website (https://www.goelectricdrive.org/charging-ev/charging-equipment-showroom) and Plug In America's Get Equipped publication (https://pluginamerica.org/get-equipped/), which include information on charging networks and service providers. For a list of ENERGY STAR certified chargers, see the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Product Finder list. (https://www.energystar.gov/products/ev_chargers) Charging Infrastructure Terminology The charging infrastructure industry has aligned with a common standard called the Open Charge Point Interface (https://evroaming.org/ocpi-background/) (OCPI) protocol with this hierarchy for charging stations: location, EV charging port, and connector. The Alternative Fuels Data Center and the Station Locator (/stations/) use the following charging infrastructure definitions: Station Location: A station location is a site with one or more EV charging ports at the same address. Examples include a parking garage or a mall parking lot. EV Charging Port: An EV charging port provides power to charge only one vehicle at a time even though it may have multiple connectors. The unit that houses EV charging ports is sometimes called a charging post, which can have one or more EV charging ports. EV charging ports are also sometimes referred to as electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) ports. Connector: A connector is what is plugged into a vehicle to charge it. Multiple connectors and connector types (such as CHAdeMO and CCS) can be available on one EV charging port, but only one vehicle will charge at a time. Connectors are sometimes called plugs. The Combined Charging System (CCS), also known as the SAE J1772 combo, charge port on a vehicle can be used to accept charge with Level 1, Level 2, or DC fast charging equipment. 268 -- 268 of 296 -- Charging Equipment Charging equipment for EVs is classified by the rate at which the batteries are charged. Charging times vary based on how depleted the battery is (i.e., state-of-charge), how much energy it holds (i.e., capacity), the type of battery, the vehicle's internal charger capacity, and the type of charging equipment (e.g., charging level, charger power output, and electrical service specifications). The charging time can range from less than 20 minutes using DC fast chargers to 20 hours or more using Level 1 chargers, depending on these and other factors. When choosing equipment (electricity_infrastructure_development.html) for a specific application, many factors, such as networking, payment capabilities, and operation and maintenance (electricity_infrastructure_maintenance_and_operation.html), should be considered. Level 1 Charging Approximately 5 miles of range per 1 hour of charging J1772 connector Alternating Current (AC) (/glossary.html#AlternatingCurrent) Level 1 equipment (often referred to simply as Level 1) provides charging through a 120 volt (V) AC plug. Most, if not all, EVs will come with a portable Level 1 cordset, so no additional charging equipment is required. On one end of the cord is a standard NEMA (/glossary.html#CommonNEMAOutlets) connector (for example, a NEMA 5-15, which is a common three-prong household plug), and on the other end is an SAE J1772 standard connector (often referred to simply as J1772, shown in the above image). The J1772 connector plugs into the car's J1772 charge port, and the NEMA connector plugs into a standard NEMA (/glossary.html#CommonNEMAOutlets) wall outlet. Level 1 charging is typically used when there is only a 120 V outlet available, such as while charging at home, but can easily provide charging for most of a driver's needs. For example, 8 hours of charging at 120 V can replenish about 40 miles of electric range for a mid-size EV. As of 2022, less than 1% of public EV charging ports in the United States were Level 1 (https://afdc.energy.gov/stations/#/analyze?country=US&fuel=ELEC&ev_levels=1). Assumes 1.9 kW charging power Level 2 Charging Approximately 25 miles of range per 1 hour of charging * * † 269 -- 269 of 296 -- J1772 connector J3400 (NACS) connector AC Level 2 equipment (often referred to simply as Level 2) offers charging through 240 V (typical in residential applications) or 208 V (typical in commercial applications) electrical service. Most homes have 240 V service available, and because Level 2 equipment can charge a typical EV battery overnight, EV owners commonly install it for home charging (/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html). Level 2 equipment is also commonly used for public and workplace charging (/fuels/electricity_charging_public.html) and can operate at 40 to 80 amperes (Amp). Most residential Level 2 chargers operate at up to 30 Amps, delivering 7.2 kW of power. These units require a dedicated 40-Amp circuit to comply with the National Electric Code requirements in Article 625. As of 2022, nearly 80% of public EV charging ports in the United States were Level 2 (https://afdc.energy.gov/stations/#/analyze? country=US&fuel=ELEC&ev_levels=2). Level 2 charging equipment uses the same J1772 connector that Level 1 equipment uses. All commercially available EVs in the United States have the ability to charge using Level 1 and Level 2 charging equipment. Vehicles with a J3400 (also referred to as NACS, or North American Charging Standard) connector (currently only Tesla vehicles) can use the connector for all charging levels, including Tesla's Level 2 Destination Chargers and chargers for home. All Tesla vehicles come with a J1772 adapter, which allows them to use non-Tesla Level 2 charging equipment. A Level 2 unit can range from 2.9 to 19.2 kW power output. DC Fast Charging Approximately 100 to 200+ miles of range per 30 minutes of charging CCS connector CHAdeMO connector J3400 (NACS) connector Direct-current (DC) (/glossary.html#DirectCurrent) fast charging equipment (typically a three-phase AC input) enables rapid charging along heavy traffic corridors at installed stations. As of 2022, more than 20% of public EV charging ports in the United States were DC fast chargers (https://afdc.energy.gov/stations/#/analyze?country=US&fuel=ELEC&ev_levels=dc_fast). The availability of DC fast charging is expected to increase as a result of federal funding to build a national EV charging network, such as the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Formula Program (https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/12744) or national Alternative Fuel Corridors grant program (https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/11675). Additionally, DC fast charging is projected to increase due to fleets adopting medium- and heavy-duty EVs (e.g., commercial trucks and vans and transit), as well as the installation of fast charging hubs for transportation network companies (e.g., Uber and Lyft) and other applications. There are three types of DC fast charging systems, depending on the type of charge port on the vehicle: SAE Combined Charging System (CCS), CHAdeMO, and J3400. † ‡ 270 -- 270 of 296 -- The CCS connector (also known as SAE J1772 combo) lets drivers use the same charge port with AC Level 1, Level 2, and DC fast charging equipment. The only difference is that the DC fast charging connector has two additional bottom pins. Most EV models on the market can charge using the CCS connector. The CHAdeMO connector is another common DC fast connector type among Japanese automakers. SAE International is standardizing the J3400 connector based on Tesla’s design for the NACS connector, which works for all charging levels, including Tesla's fast charging option, called a Supercharger. Although Tesla vehicles do not have a CCS or CHAdeMO charge port, they come with a limited CCS or CHAdeMO adapter that supports charging up to 19.2 kW. Several vehicle manufacturers have announced adopting the J3400 connector (https://driveelectric.gov/charging-connector) as early as 2025, which will allow non-Tesla EVs to charge at Tesla stations with the J3400 connector. A DC fast charging unit can range from 25 to 350 kW. Charging power varies by vehicle and battery state of charge. Additional Charging Options Another standard (SAE J3068 (https://www.sae.org/news/press-room/2018/04/sae-international-releases-new-specification-sae-j3068- for-charging-of-medium-and-heavy-duty-electric-vehicles)) was developed in 2018 for higher rates of AC charging using three-phase power, which is common at commercial and industrial locations in the United States. Some components of the standard were adapted from the European three-phase charging standards and specified for North American AC grid voltages and requirements. In the United States, the common three-phase voltages are typically 208/120 V, 480/277 V. The standard targets power levels between 6 kW and 130 kW. Extreme fast chargers (XFC), such as the SAE DC Level 2 standard, are capable of power outputs of up 350 kW and higher and are rapidly being deployed in the United States light-duty and select medium-duty applications (e.g., for in-route charging of electric buses). XFC will also support long-dwell overnight charging for medium- and heavy-duty vehicle applications. A 2022 report (https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/15/10/3788) looks at the requirements for charging stations that could support in-route charging for heavy-duty EVs. While XFC are currently available from several charging manufacturers, the U.S. Department of Energy's Vehicle Technologies Office is pursuing research that will bridge the technology gaps associated with implementing XFC networks in the United States. A 2017 report (https://energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2017/10/f38/XFC%20Technology%20Gap%20Assessment%20Report_FINAL_10202017.pdf) highlights technology gaps at the battery, vehicle, and infrastructure levels. In particular, many EVs on the roads today are not capable of charging at rates higher than 150 kW. However, vehicle technology is advancing, and most new EV models will be able to charge at higher rates, enabling the use of XFC. You can find additional resources on EV charging and advanced charging system research efforts (https://www.nrel.gov/transportation/project-ev-grid-integration.html) from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (https://www.nrel.gov/news/program/2020/advanced-charging-systems-research-moves-consumer-commercial-electric-vehicles-faster- further.html). text: January 2, 2024 CITY OF CONWAY CITY COUNCIL MEETING CONWAY CITY HALL 229 MAIN STREET, CONWAY TUESDAY, JANUARY 2, 2024 - 4:00 P.M. PRESENT: Mayor Barbara Jo Blain-Bellamy, Amanda Butler, William Goldfinch, Julie Hardwick, Beth Helms, Justin Jordan. Absent: Larry White STAFF: Adam Emrick, City Administrator; Mary Catherine Hyman, Deputy City Administrator; John Rogers, Deputy City Administrator; Jeff Leveille, Technology Services Director; Allison Williams, Finance Director; Timmy Williams, Hospitality & Beautification Director; Brandon Harrelson, Public Works Director; Reggie Jenerette, Solid Waste Director; Lynn Smith, Human Resource Director; Rock Rabon, Fleet Maintenance Director; Jessica Hucks, Planning and Development Director; Le Hendrick, Fire Chief; Ashley Smith, Recreation Director; Robert Cooper, Construction Services Director; Ted Dudley, Public Utilities Deputy Director; Kayla Fleming, Municipal Judge; Katie Dennis, Planning Concierge; and Alicia Shelley, City Clerk. OTHERS: There were approximately 50 others in attendance. CALL TO ORDER: Mayor Blain-Bellamy called the meeting to order. Rev. Richard Williams gave the invocation and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The requirements for posting notice of this meeting under South Carolina’s Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) were met. ADMINISTRATION OF OATHS OF OFFICE: Oaths of Office were administered during the swearing in ceremonies for the Council members that were elected/re-elected in the November 2023 election. Those included Mayor Barbara Jo Blain-Bellamy, Council Member Justin Jordan, and Council Member Julie Hardwick. There was a brief recess to welcome those Council members. APPROVAL OF AGENDA: Motion: Butler made a motion, seconded by Helms, to approve the January 2, 2024 meeting agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. CONSENT AGENDA: A. Final Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-01-02 (A) to annex approximately 0.23 acres located at 289 Wedding Lane (PIN 367-13-01-0025), and rezone from the Horry County Residential, including mobile homes (MSF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium Residential (R-1) district. B. Resolution accepting the dedication of roadways and drainage system in the Wild Wing, Phase 5B subdivision (Wood Stork Drive, Beechfield Court, Brick Point Court). C. Special Event – Waccamaw Sportsmen’s Expo – March 22 & 23, 2024 -- 1 of 12 -- January 2, 2024 D. Special Event – Shuckin’ on the Waccamaw – March 22, 2024 E. Approval to Replace Vehicle Maintenance Service Truck F. Approval of December 17, 2023 Emergency Meeting Minutes G. Approval of December 4, 2023 Council Meeting Minutes H. Declare that the State of Emergency relative to the December 2023 nor’easter has ended APPROVAL OF CONSENT AGENDA: Motion: Jordan made a motion, seconded by Blain- Bellamy to approve the January 2, 2024 consent agenda. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. ELECTION OF MAYOR PRO TEM FOR 2024: Motion: Goldfinch made a motion, seconded by Helms to defer this item to a future meeting. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT: There was no public input. Motion: Blain-Bellamy made a motion, seconded by Goldfinch, to close public input. Vote: Unanimous. Motion carried. SPECIAL PRESENTATION: A. Recognition of 2023 Employees of the Year – Emrick recognized the 2023 Employees of the Year – Allan Huggins, Public Safety; Tasha Sherman, Public Service; and Brandon Danser, Public Works. B. Presentation of Longevity Awards – December 2023 – 10 Years: Danner Thompson, Recreation – Emrick and Butler presented the longevity awards. C. Presentation of Future Plans for Jerry Cox Parking Lot and ERF #3 – Hyman said that the City-owned parking lot behind Jerry Cox is in disrepair and under-utilized, and as this area grows, so does the needs to improve this parking area. The recently completed Riverfront and Downtown Master Plan provided a conceptual design for gateway development at the corner of 4th Avenue and Kington Street. As stated in the plan, “crossing the Kingston Lake on Fourth Avenue and entering downtown, a bare city parking lot greets visitors and residents. This is a well-traveled road into the City of Conway and downtown and should reflect the City’s commitment to design.” Per recommendations from the plan, City staff has been working with Hanna Engineering to create a design that: reconfigures the parking for safety, provides a fun new gateway sign to anchor the parking lot, -adds lighting and landscaping to beautify and create a safer space, adds another ERF to clean up the area, creates a connection between downtown and the river, and upgrades sidewalks. The City was recently awarded the MASC Hometown Economic Development Grant to construct the ERF, which will also act as a gateway sign. The parking lot construction will be covered by Hospitality funds. Hyman said that since this design staff would like to see more green space. -- 2 of 12 -- January 2, 2024 D. Discussion of a request by Crunk Engineering, LLC, to annex approximately 8.96 acres of property located at the intersection of Mill Pond Rd and Hwy 501 (PIN 338- 10-01-0015), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. Hucks informed Council that the applicant is requesting to annex and rezone the 8.96-acre parcel, located at/near the corner of Hwy 501 & Mill Pond Rd as Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial. While the application does not specify the proposed use, discussions with the applicant indicates that the use will be a medical facility. This property will also be combined with the adjacent property, already in the city limits, zoned HC. The property abuts property on all but one side zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC), and surrounding uses include vacant property, a gas station/convenience store, and a restaurant. Hucks informed Council that the applicant is requesting to rezone the property at 610 Main Street to the Professional district. The property is currently zoned R-1, and currently contains 2 residential structures: a single-family home, which fronts Main Street, and a multifamily structure, which fronts on 7th Avenue However, the Building Official recently posted both structures as unsafe, and required that both structures be demolished. Because the property is within the Main Street Historic Design Review District, the applicant was required to obtain approval for demolition from the Community Appearance Board. The Board considered the request to demo the structures at their meeting on December 13th and approved demolition of the multifamily structure facing 7th Ave only, citing their desire to preserve the historic home. The Board cannot overrule the Building Official; however, the Building Official has stated that the rear, multifamily structure was the direst of the 2 and has made exceptions with regard to historical buildings or properties in the past. The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to Professional because they would like to market the property for sale as residential or commercial, and the Professional district allows both residential and commercial uses. If the property were rezoned to Professional, the existing home that fronts on Main Street could be rehabilitated and used as a commercial space, or it could be restored for residential use, depending on the wishes of the buyer. The City’s future land use map identifies the property as Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). However, property adjacent to the subject property is zoned Professional, and the request is consistent with the character of the surrounding properties which have frontage along Main Street. The request will be accompanied by a Future Land Use Map amendment; both of which will be considered by Planning Commission at a future meeting, unless the request is withdrawn. -- 3 of 12 -- January 2, 2024 Hucks said that following staff forwarding this request for discussion on this agenda, the applicant notified staff that they wish to defer the request at this time. Hucks said that in 2020, the state adopted a law requiring the inclusion of a resiliency element in the comprehensive planning process. The Resiliency Element promotes resilient planning, design and development and identifies goals and strategies for implementation of future policies and projects that are intended to increase Conway’s state of resilience. The City adopted its Resiliency Element in 2023. A couple of these goals were to: 1. “facilitate the preservation of the floodplain and the conservation of environmentally sensitive areas”; and 2. To “protect and restore natural flood mitigation features” Hucks said that staff supports the goals and strategies that were identified in the resiliency element of the comprehensive plan. Staff supports the future land use identified in the comprehensive plan of CP. First Reading of Ordinance #ZA2024-01-16 (F) of an amendment to Article 2 – Definitions and Article 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding the requirements for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) and associated equipment. (Hucks) Electric vehicles are gaining popularity across the nation, and with that, the need for infrastructure to support the demand for electric vehicles has increased. Cities and towns across South Carolina have drafted or adopted amendments to their ordinances regarding electric vehicle charging stations and related infrastructure. Several states offer incentives related to Electric vehicle charging stations, and some that also require EV ready infrastructure be installed when developing property. There are 3 charging levels for electric vehicles: (1) A Level 1 charger is typically what you would have installed in your home and uses 120-volt AC plug. It could take a full day or longer to fully charge an EV using a Level 1 charger. (2) A Level -- 7 of 12 -- January 2, 2024 2 charger uses a 240-volt AC plug, and is typically installed for commercial use. Level 2 chargers provide 10-20 miles of range per hour of charging; and (3) A Level 3 charger, also called Direct Current Fast Charger (DCFC), uses 480-volt AC plus that charges an EV – up to 80% - in approx. 30 minutes. These types of chargers are best for highway sites to enable longer vehicle trips. These types of charging stations are similar to those that you see at Coastal Grand Mall in Myrtle Beach, or along major highway corridors or interstates. Hucks said that currently, the UDO does not address EV’s or EV charging stations, however, we have begun receiving several inquiries regarding our requirements related to the use. The proposed amendment to the UDO will amend the definitions article of the UDO to include definitions for an Electric Vehicle Charging Station, as well as definitions for the 3 different charging levels. Additionally, the proposed amendment will provide standards for installation of electric vehicle charging stations, with Level 1 and 2 charging stations being permitted in all zoning districts, and additional conditions for Level 3 charging stations, including limiting the permitted locations for a Level 3 charging station to zoning districts which also permit a gas station; exception being if the property is within a Historic Design Review District, then a level 3 charger would not be permitted. The zoning districts that would permit the installation of a level 3 charging station include HC, NC, CC, LI and HI. Hucks said that Planning Commission considered the amendment at their November 27, 2023 meeting, as well as held the required public hearing, and recommended approval of the amendment to the UDO. Staff also recommends approval. Goldfinch had some concerns with a Level 3 charger not being allowed on a residential lot for personal use in the CBD district. Hucks explained as being similar to those you see at Coastal Grand Mall. Emrick said that it would be cost prohibitive to do so and would be the same as having a gas pump/station on your property for your own use. Emrick said that if they are not regulated in a way that makes sense today, the City could be opening up a can of worms for tomorrow. ISSUE: Quattlebaum Awards BACKGROUND: The C.P Quattlebaum Awards were created in honor of Conway’s first Mayor and the Quattlebaum family. The family was known for their associations and contributions to several of the oldest and most architecturally significant buildings in the City of Conway. City Council formed the Quattlebaum awards in 1999 in an effort to recognize those individuals who showcase and provide quality design and efforts in the City of Conway. The following award categories were created; • Outstanding Restoration of a Non-Residential Building • Outstanding Restoration of a Home • Outstanding New Construction of a Non-Residential Building • Outstanding New Construction of a Residential Building • Outstanding Landscape Project • Outstanding Design Effort • Outstanding Signage Project • Outstanding contribution to quality development, restoration, landscape or design by an organization or individual Nominees can be presented to city staff by citizens, city officials or by CAB members. The number of awards and the categories for which they are recognized is determined each year by the Community Appearance Board. However, the board cannot grant an award to more than two recipients in any given category and no group, organization, or individual can receive an award in more than one category each year. Staff reviews all nominees and projects from the previous calendar year and provides the CAB members with that list by category with supporting images. The board then makes their award decisions by a majority vote and the nominees are awarded at the following City Council meeting. Dennis gave an overview regarding the applicant requesting design changes to the building façade as well as the project site. The project was originally approved on April 26th, 2023. That approval was for the following façade improvements; • The proposal includes renovating the exterior structure of the main building using, Stucco main body master wall #500 EGG @30% lighter than standard for the main siding of the building, Stucco Trim/ master wall #500 EGG for trimming details around the building, Palmetto Brick in the color Oak Grove Queen size with mortar -- 2 of 9 -- CAB 9/9/2026 2 color being Ivory Buff along the bottom portions of the building on the front and sides, Using Sherwin Williams #0016 Billiard Green for the metal canopy, gutters, downspouts, and rear door, with composite trim and a parapet cap to match the Sherwin Williams #0016 Billiard Green color, and Bright Clear- Anodized or powder coated storefront frame windows and door along the front of the building. The applicant is also proposing to use the existing gas canopy and painting it to match the stucco master wall #500 EGG on the top of the canopy and bottom portions of the canopy structural poles and with paint to match the stucco master wall #500 EGG @ 30% lighter than standard on the bottom portions of the canopy and top portions of the canopy structural poles. Following this approval the applicant also received approval on July 23, 2025. That approval was for the following; • To install new signage for the proposed business located at 600 Main St. The applicant is proposing to replace the existing gas canopy with a new “ACM Fascia” canopy that will have custom lettering to spell “Sinclair” with halo back lighting on two sides of the canopy. The applicant is also proposing to install Sinclair branding on the two fuel pumps, and 4 trash cans. Following this approval the applicant also received approval on August 13, 2025. That approval was for the following; • To install a monument sign that measures 5.3’ (w) x 7.5’ (h), with the sign face measuring 5.3’ (w) x 4.5’ (h), totaling 23.85 sq. ft. Following these approvals the applicant continued with the TRC approval process. Through this process a few other items were identified including the need for a variance from two specific sections of the Unified Development Ordinance. The variance granted the approval for the applicant to not have to install certain landscaping requirements within the parking area to prevent the owner from having to remove the existing asphalt and to allow for adequate traffic flow. A variance was also granted for the dumpster location to be in the corner front yard due to the layout of the property site. The project site will also be resurfaced and restriped to match the approved site plan. As part of the review process CAB must also approve the revised landscape plan approved by TRC. There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property: This is an existing gas station which limits the amount of available space for landscaping and potential places to install dumpsters. 2. These conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. The conditions are particular to this piece of property as most parcels do not have an existing gas station on them. 3. Because of these conditions, the application of the ordinance to the particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property: The existing pavement precludes being able to install landscape islands and limits the space available to put a dumpster 4. The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or to the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by the granting of the variance: Granting of the variance will allow what has been an eye sore in the area for years to be cleaned up and make the area much more attractive. text: CAB 9/9/2026 Present: Absent: Staff: Other: CITY OF CONWAY COMMUNITY APPEARANCE BOARD MEETING WEDNESDAY, September 9, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Jacqueline Kurlowski; Coker Hall; Duc Watts; Jamie McLain Gerry Wallace; McKenzie Jordan; Troy Roehm Katie Dennis, Planner; Darlene Acevedo, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT; Quang Ho, IT Ashley Cowen; Hillary Howard I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Kurlowski called the meeting to order at approximately 4:00 p.m. U. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Watts made a motion to accept the minutes as written. It was seconded by McLain to approve August 26, 2026, minutes. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. I. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS A. 600 Main St (Sinclair Gas Station): The applicant, Diamond Shores LLC, is requesting approval of design changes for the building and project site located at 600 Main St. (PIN 338- 13-03-0005). Dennis gave an overview regarding the applicant requesting design changes to the building facade as well as the project site. The project was originally approved on April 26th, 2023. That approval was for the following facade improvements; . The proposal includes renovating the exterior structure of the main building using, Stucco main body master wall #500 EGG @30% lighter than standard for the main siding of the building, Stucco Trim/ master wall #500 EGG for trimming details around the building, Palmetto Brick in the color Oak Grove Queen size with mortar 1 CAB 9/9/2026 color being Ivory Buff along the bottom portions of the building on the front and sides, Using Sherwin Williams #0016 Billiard Green for the metal canopy, gutters, downspouts, and rear door, with composite trim and a parapet cap to match the Sherwin Williams #0016 Billiard Green color, and Bright Clear- Anodized or powder coated storefront frame windows and door along the front of the building. The applicant is also proposing to use the existing gas canopy and painting it to match the stucco master wall #500 EGG on the top of the canopy and bottom portions of the canopy structural poles and with paint to match the stucco master wall #500 EGG @ 30% lighter than standard on the bottom portions of the canopy and top portions of the canopy structural poles. Following this approval the applicant also received approval on July 23, 2025. That approval was for the following; ° To install new signage for the proposed business located at 600 Main St. The applicant is proposing to replace the existing gas canopy with a new “ACM Fascia” canopy that will have custom lettering to spell “Sinclair” with halo back lighting on two sides of the canopy. The applicant is also proposing to install Sinclair branding on the two fuel pumps, and 4 trash cans. Following this approval the applicant also received approval on August 13, 2025. That approval was for the following; . To install a monument sign that measures 5.3’ (w) x 7.5’ (h), with the sign face measuring 5.3’ (w) x 4.5” (h), totaling 23.85 sq. ft. The sign will be internally illuminated with only the lettering, gas price numbers, and logo visible during illumination. . The applicant will also be installing a retaining wall to match the same material as the building to provide the required landscaping needed for the monument sign while also meeting the required 5’ setback. Following these approvals the applicant continued with the TRC approval process. Through this process a few other items were identified including the need for a variance from two specific sections of the Unified Development Ordinance. The variance granted the approval for the applicant to not have to install certain landscaping requirements within the parking area to prevent the owner from having to remove the existing asphalt and to allow for adequate traffic flow. A variance was also granted for the dumpster location to be in the corner front yard due to the layout of the property site. The project site will also be resurfaced and restriped to match the approved site plan. Changes to the Plan: Due to trees that were originally proposed to remain for landscaping and buffering requirements being removed. The applicant had to submit a revised landscaping plan. This plan was ultimately approved by TRC in accordance with the UDO as weil as the approved variance requests and is included in the packet. As part of the review process CAB must also approve the revised landscape plan approved by TRC. The building fagade changes include architectural details along the roof line, midline of the building, window trim and style, door trim and style, and lower brickwork. The rear entrance has been relocated to the side of the building and the mechanical equipment along the rear of the building also provides the proper UDO required 6’ privacy fence for screening. CAB 9/9/2026 VIL The applicant has provided the plan showing that all materials are to be of the same color there are just a few slight architectural design changes. The applicant does have $6,000 in tree mitigation that is required to be paid prior to a CO being issued. The applicant, staff and board discussed at length. Kurlowski wanted to note on the record that CAB holds businesses to a high standard on windows within the HDRD. Landscape Plan: McLain made a motion to approve the revised landscape plan as presented. Hall seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Design Plan: McLain made a motion to approve the revised design plan as presented with the exception of the awning should be added back to the front fagade and be proportionally the same as the original approval. Watts seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT None BOARD INPUT Reminder regarding the continuing education credits need to be completed by December 31* for Board members. STAFF INPUT None ADJOURN There being no further business to come before the board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting at 4:28 p.m. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. Approved and signed this / fe ; day of EXD , 2026. > lowski, Chairperson Jacqueline

SPECIAL TAX ASSESSMENT AMENDMENT(S) A. 1311 Ninth Ave (Drew McElveen): The applicant, Drew McElveen, is requesting approval of a design change under the previously approved Historic Preservation Tax Incentive for the home located at 1311 Ninth Ave (338-14-03-0042). Dennis gave an overview that the applicant is requesting approval of an amendment to the previously approved Special Tax Assessment for the home located at 1311 9th Ave. Under the preservation tax incentive, any changes to the original preliminary approval must be presented to the board for additional approvals. The preliminary approval was granted back in December of last year and the applicant is requesting to relocate two existing windows. CAB previously approved the removal of two (2) of the four (4) windows on the front-left side of the home (to eliminate the appearance of a “wall of windows” on that side of the house). The applicant is now requesting approval for the removal of two (2) additional front windows (adjacent to the front door). With the intent to utilize these two (2) windows in place of the two remaining “standard order windows” located on the front-left side of the home (where the wall 1 CAB 5/13/2026 Iv. of windows used to be). This design change will result in two things: 1) more space for the placement of natural gas lanterns as previously approved adjacent to the front door and 2) a consistent window design across the entire front-facade of the home. The applicant is also requesting approval of the construction of an exterior fireplace on the lanai (left side of the home) as well as changing the color of shutters from black as previously approved to a beige/créme color. The applicant, staff and board discussed at length. Wallace made a motion to approve window and shutter changes as presented, the placement of the fireplace with the exception if they put in a masonry chimney that is visible from the street. The brick work must match the existing chimney and the same cap (brick cover). Watts seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The sign is to measure 60” (w) x 24” (h), totaling 10 Sq. Ft. and be affixed to a wall that measures 21.6’ (w) x 20’ (h), totaling 432 Sq. Ft. and allowing for a max coverage of 86.4 Sq. Ft. The proposed signage is compliant with the UDO, and renderings are included in your packet. The applicant, staff and board discussed at length. Roehm made a motion to approve as presented. text: CAB 3/25/2026 Present: Absent: Staff: Other: CITY OF CONWAY COMMUNITY APPEARANCE BOARD MEETING WEDNESDAY, March 25, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Jacqueline Kurlowski, Coker Hall, Jamie McLain, Duc Watts, Gerry Wallace, Troy Roehm McKenzie Jordan Katie Dennis, Planner; Darlene Acevedo, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Louis Smith, IT Hillary Howard; Jay Ham, Ryan Mandigo, Ruth Cronin, Andrew James, Stephen Ramos, Andrew Brown, Sarah Barnentine, Chaisty Whitlock, Joe Keenan, Chris Snyder, Susan McMillam, Marshall McMillan, and others I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Kurlowski called the meeting to order at approximately 4:00 p.m. Ii, APPROVAL OF MINUTES Watts made a motion to accept the minutes as written. It was seconded by McLain to approve February 25, 2026, minutes. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Il. CONCEPTUAL REVIEW A. 320 Kingston St (Conway Hotel): The applicant, Stephen Ramos is requesting conceptual review for proposed new construction of a hotel to be located at 320 Kingston St. (PIN 339-16- 04-0019 & 367-01-01-0066). Dennis provided the overview that the applicant is requesting to construct a new commercial structure along the riverfront. The proposed structure is to be a 69-room hotel with the entirety of the lower level being of commercial uses. The renderings provide images of the proposal and civil plans are currently under review with the TRC. The applicant will take all comments made today and include them with TRC comments to then revise the plans as needed and will resubmit them once they are further along in the TRC process. The applicant was present Mr. Ramos of Ramos Architectural and Design presented the renderings regarding the location and building site. The applicant, staff, and the board discussed in length. There was no action taken on the item as it was a conceptual review only. CAB 3/25/2026 IV. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS Board member McLain recused himself from voting on the item due to conflict of interest and did not participate in the decision-making process. A. 150 Laurel St (Peanut Warehouse): The applicant, Jamie McLain is requesting to install treated wood decking boards between brick pillars around the foundation for the building located at 150 Laurel St. (PIN 367-01-01-0058). Dennis gave an overview that the applicant is requesting approval for newly installed foundational fencing located below the building at 150 Laurel St. (The Peanut Warehouse) The fencing is constructed of wood material that will change color with time to match the existing siding of the building. The applicant, staff and board discussed at length. Hall made a motion to approve the item as presented. Wallace seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. V. PUBLIC INPUT Susan McMillan owner of the Jerry Cox’s building, presented concerns: e Staging is going to occur for the hotel building such as steel, concrete, delivery trucks, etc. e Kingston St being closed to traffic and the length of time for construction. e Delivery trucks on the 20 ft alley making their drops at the hotel will interfere with the public access to the riverwalk. e Parking is presently used by many of the downtown merchants. e We don’t want to drive away this popularity because parking becomes a nightmare. The building is beautiful and Conway would be proud to have it, but there is no space around it. Marshall McMillan husband of Susan McMillan owner of the Jerry Cox’s building he shares the same concerns as his wife. Parking being the most concern and questioned. He also questioned the setbacks on Kingston St and Fourth Ave, and if the storm water retention been looked at. VI. BOARD INPUT None VIL =STAFF INPUT Just another reminder of the South Carolina Historic Preservation Conference is coming up this year on Friday, April 24". Staff will be attending and we encourage the board to attend. We ask the Board members to notify our office by Friday March 27th to register for early registration. CAB 3/25/2026 VIN. ADJOURN There being no further business to come before the board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting at 4:32pm. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. uP ‘ Approved and signed this day of { , 2026. tet, Ro Dust: Tacqueliae Kurlowski, Chairperson

CALL TO ORDER Board member Coker Hall called the meeting to order at approximately 4:04pm. Hall mentioned the absence of the Chair, Jacqueline Kurlowski and Vice Chair, McKenzie Jordan. Hall continued by informing the board that the election of appointed chairperson in their absence was necessary. Watts made a motion to nominate Coker Hall, and it was seconded by McLain. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES McLain made a motion to accept the minutes as written. It was seconded by Roehm to approve January 28, 2026, minutes. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS A. 332 Main St. (Leone’s Italian Restaurant): The applicant, James Leone, is requesting to install a new detached structure for the building located at 332 Main St. (PIN 367-01-01-0028). Dennis provided that the applicant is requesting to install a prefab wooden shed measuring 10’ (W) X 16’ (L) behind their store front located at 332 Main St. The renderings provide an image of a sage green siding with white trim and a metal roof for the building. The building is proposed to be along the side wall of the neighboring building but in the rear of the restaurant. The applicant was not present. Staff and the board discussed the request in length. Wallace made a motion to deny the request. Watts seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 2 of 13 -- CAB 2/11/2026 2 B. 975 Second Ave: The applicant, Steve Strickland, is requesting approval of new commercial structure for the property at 975 Second Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0054). Dennis provided an overview of the applicant’s request and has been before the board on multiple occasions and to clarify the changes being made and the changes required by staff has consolidated the key moments from the approval process to illustrate the proposals change over time. March 13, 2019- The applicants received their first approval for the request with the condition that TRC approves the building to meet UDO standards. February 24, 2021- Approved following the 2019 approval and TRC the applicant submitted construction plans with a larger footprint that were different than what was approved by CAB with a portion of the rear of the building encroaching into the Riverwalk Easement triggering a re-review from the board. These changes included: • Relocation of the office entry to the left side • Changes to the main entrance to have a separate takeout door and adjust service doors. • Changes to the screen material on the rear and sides to glass to allow for year-round dining. • An increase in the area of vertical siding on the right side to screen all coolers and mechanical service equipment. • Changes to the access stairs and ramp on the front and sides to improve access to the restaurant. • Adjust the canopy on the left side to match the entrance. The board granted the request with the condition that on the riverside of the building there would be large clear glass and the entrance and take outdoors would come back for later approval. December 14, 2022- This review was Tabled and initiated following the applicant’s submittal in September of 2022 and their desire to create two restaurants within the building rather than one restaurant and office space as previously approved. Upon discovering a previously approved plat showing the updated property lines had not been recorded which resulted in the inability to fit the requested building footprint within the property boundaries the board voted to table the item until the applicant properly recorded the plat and executed the deed work. May 24, 2023- Approved w/ Conditions following the completion of the recording of the plat and executed deed work the applicant appeared before the board on January 25, 2023, and was asked by the board to; • Extend the porch along the length of the back of the building • Provide a symmetrical pitch or go back to the original design of the lower warehouse roof layout • Verify the roof pitch • Provide shed style porch roofs rather than gable end -- 3 of 13 -- CAB 2/11/2026 3 • Provide a zoomed in rendering of each entry way for board clarification • Show window details for each side of the building • Provide a size offset between the shed roofs to distinguish between the 2 tenants and entrances • Refer to the approved 2021 renderings The applicant returned on March 8th meeting and the requirements outlined by the board at the January 25th meeting. The board approved the revisions with the condition the applicant include a minimum of four (4) or more faux shutters on the street side of the building to mimic the look of the Riverwalk side, that the applicant uses all previously approved materials, and that the applicant return for board approval on the locations of the exhaust fans (vent hoods) At the May 24th meeting the applicant provided all the requested changes and was granted approval with condition the shutters are flat against the siding. August 28, 2024- The applicant was Approved following the May 24th approval the applicant began the review process with TRC. During the review it was determined that the proposed building was too large to meet certain code requirements, such as fire rating, and stairway placements. After discussions with staff the applicant elected to reduce the building size by 5’ or more on each side. The relocation of the staircase was requested by City Staff as it also did not meet fire requirements and the originally planned riverwalk connection was not going to be achievable due to underground utilities and stormwater. With the reduction the building exterior changed. The following changes were made and approved by the board; • The front takeout door on one unit was removed due to the reduction in the size of the building • The reduction of the building also affected the placement of some of the exit doors and the stage area on the interior of the building resulting in the need to shift the roll up window doors and the elimination of one rear door. • The stair well previously below the building was moved due to life safety as well as the reduction in the building size to meet fire code, and the location of utilities in the previous location. • Adjust the property lines on the street side of the building to encompass the ADA required ramp. Council will have the final determination for this but rather than having an open area between two property lines staff felt it necessary to include the ramp and/or steps within the property of the restaurant. The board voted to approve the changes to the building with the condition that all previously approved materials, colors, and designs are to remain the same and that all windows are to have 1 1/8” muttons that are a minimum of 1 ½” in depth. February 11, 2026 – The applicants request is due to the inability to incorporate all previously approved requirements from the board while achieving code compliance. The building was -- 4 of 13 -- CAB 2/11/2026 4 originally approved with the ADA ramp within the boundary lines, but this could not be accomplished without altering some of the exterior appearance changes. The key changes for this submittal include: • Relocation of the HVAC units and screening to the parking lot side of the building • Reduction in the number of faux shutters along the parking lot side of the building • Inclusion of the ADA ramp inside of the property lines • Removal of the lateral mechanical ventilation screening on the northeast side of the building. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. The window muttons are presented on the plan to be 3/8” in depth and 1/8” in width. Applicant explained that the building was conformed to be within the property lines. Wallace made a motion to approve as presented. McLain seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. IV. PUBLIC INPUT Hillary Howard from Conway Downtown Alive informed the board that the Coffee Movement will have their final inspection and the owner would like to welcome you to his soft opening next week. Also, she mentioned about Heresay and there has been movement on the building and we’re hoping to see some glass installed next week. V. BOARD INPUT None VI. STAFF INPUT None VII. title: APP 2.11.26 CAB MINUTES
text: CAB 2/11/2026 Present: Absent: Staff: Other: CITY OF CONWAY COMMUNITY APPEARANCE BOARD MEETING WEDNESDAY, February 11, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Coker Hall, Jamie McLain, Duc Watts, Gerry Wallace, Troy Roehm Jacqueline Kurlowski, McKenzie Jordan Katie Dennis, Planner; Darlene Acevedo, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT Hillary Howard; Sarah Barrentine; Steve Strickiand; Tripp Nealy I. CALL TO ORDER Board member Coker Hall called the meeting to order at approximately 4:04pm. Hall mentioned the absence of the Chair, Jacqueline Kurlowski and Vice Chair, McKenzie Jordan. Hall continued by informing the board that the election of appointed chairperson in their absence was necessary. Watts made a motion to nominate Coker Hall, and it was seconded by McLain. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES McLain made a motion to accept the minutes as written. It was seconded by Roehm to approve January 28, 2026, minutes. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. I. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS A. 332 Main St. (Leone’s Italian Restaurant): The applicant, James Leone, is requesting to install a new detached structure for the building located at 332 Main St. (PIN 367-01-01-0028). Dennis provided that the applicant is requesting to install a prefab wooden shed measuring 10’ (W) X 16’ (L) behind their store front located at 332 Main St. The renderings provide an image of a sage green siding with white trim and a metal roof for the building. The building is proposed to be along the side wall of the neighboring building but in the rear of the restaurant. The applicant was not present. Staff and the board discussed the request in length. Wallace made a motion to deny the request. Watts seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. CAB 2/11/2026 B. 975 Second Ave: The applicant, Steve Strickland, is requesting approval of new commercial structure for the property at 975 Second Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0054). Dennis provided an overview of the applicant’s request and has been before the board on multiple occasions and to clarify the changes being made and the changes required by staff has consolidated the key moments from the approval process to illustrate the proposals change over time. March 13, 2019- The applicants received their first approval for the request with the condition that TRC approves the building to meet UDO standards. February 24, 2021- Approved following the 2019 approval and TRC the applicant submitted construction plans with a larger footprint that were different than what was approved by CAB with a portion of the rear of the building encroaching into the Riverwalk Easement triggering a re-review from the board. These changes included: * Relocation of the office entry to the left side » Changes to the main entrance to have a separate takeout door and adjust service doors. * Changes to the screen material on the rear and sides to glass to allow for year-round dining. * An increase in the area of vertical siding on the right side to screen all coolers and mechanical service equipment. * Changes to the access stairs and ramp on the front and sides to improve access to the restaurant. « Adjust the canopy on the left side to match the entrance. The board granted the request with the condition that on the riverside of the building there would be large clear glass and the entrance and take outdoors would come back for later approval. December 14, 2022- This review was Tabled and initiated following the applicant’s submittal in September of 2022 and their desire to create two restaurants within the building rather than one restaurant and office space as previously approved. Upon discovering a previously approved plat showing the updated property lines had not been recorded which resulted in the inability to fit the requested building footprint within the property boundaries the board voted to table the item until the applicant properly recorded the plat and executed the deed work. May 24, 2023- Approved w/ Conditions following the completion of the recording of the plat and executed deed work the applicant appeared before the board on January 25, 2023, and was asked by the board to; + Extend the porch along the length of the back of the building * Provide a symmetrical pitch or go back to the original design of the lower warehouse roof layout * Verify the roof pitch * Provide shed style porch roofs rather than gable end CAB 2/11/2026 + Provide a zoomed in rendering of each entry way for board clarification * Show window details for each side of the building « Provide a size offset between the shed roofs to distinguish between the 2 tenants and entrances ° Refer to the approved 2021 renderings The applicant returned on March 8th meeting and the requirements outlined by the board at the January 25th meeting. The board approved the revisions with the condition the applicant include a minimum of four (4) or more faux shutters on the street side of the building to mimic the look of the Riverwalk side, that the applicant uses all previously approved materials, and that the applicant return for board approval on the locations of the exhaust fans (vent hoods) At the May 24th meeting the applicant provided all the requested changes and was granted approval with condition the shutters are flat against the siding. August 28, 2024- The applicant was Approved following the May 24th approval the applicant began the review process with TRC. During the review it was determined that the proposed building was too large to meet certain code requirements, such as fire rating, and stairway placements. After discussions with staff the applicant elected to reduce the building size by 5’ or more on each side. The relocation of the staircase was requested by City Staff as it also did not meet fire requirements and the originally planned riverwalk connection was not going to be achievable due to underground utilities and stormwater. With the reduction the building exterior changed. The following changes were made and approved by the board; * The front takeout door on one unit was removed due to the reduction in the size of the building ¢ The reduction of the building also affected the placement of some of the exit doors and the stage area on the interior of the building resulting in the need to shift the roll up window doors and the elimination of one rear door. * The stair well previously below the building was moved due to life safety as well as the reduction in the building size to meet fire code, and the location of utilities in the previous location. + Adjust the property lines on the street side of the building to encompass the ADA required ramp. Council will have the final determination for this but rather than having an open area between two property lines staff felt it necessary to include the ramp and/or steps within the property of the restaurant. The board voted to approve the changes to the building with the condition that all previously approved materials, colors, and designs are to remain the same and that all windows are to have 1 1/8” muttons that are a minimum of 1 4” in depth. February 11, 2026 — The applicants request is due to the inability to incorporate all previously approved requirements from the board while achieving code compliance. The building was 3 CAB 2/11/2026 VI. VII. originally approved with the ADA ramp within the boundary lines, but this could not be accomplished without altering some of the exterior appearance changes. The key changes for this submittal include: * Relocation of the HVAC units and screening to the parking lot side of the building * Reduction in the number of faux shutters along the parking lot side of the building * Inclusion of the ADA ramp inside of the property lines * Removal of the lateral mechanical ventilation screening on the northeast side of the building. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. The window muttons are presented on the plan to be 3/8” in depth and 1/8” in width. Applicant explained that the building was conformed to be within the property lines. Wallace made a motion to approve as presented. McLain seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC INPUT Hillary Howard from Conway Downtown Alive informed the board that the Coffee Movement will have their final inspection and the owner would like to welcome you to his soft opening next week. Also, she mentioned about Heresay and there has been movement on the building and we’re hoping to see some glass installed next week. BOARD INPUT None STAFF INPUT None ADJOURN There being no further business to come before the board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting at 4:44pm. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. Approved and signed this AD day of Kha 2026. Jacqueline Kurlowski, Chairperson

text: CAB 1/28/2026 Present: Absent: Staff: Other: CITY OF CONWAY COMMUNITY APPEARANCE BOARD MEETING WEDNESDAY, January 28, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Jacqueline Kurlowski, McKenzie Jordan, Coker Hall, Jamie McLain Duc Watts, Gerry Wallace, Troy Roehm Katie Dennis, Planner; Darlene Acevedo, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Louis Smith, IT Hillary Howard; Darya Suddreth; Steve Strickland; Darrell Blarton; Tripp Nealy; Abel Wilson; Andrew Brown; Jaughn Miller; Charles Perry I, CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Kurlowski called the meeting to order at approximately 4:21 p.m. Il APPROVAL OF MINUTES Jordan made a motion to accept the minutes as written. It was seconded by Hall to approve January 14, 2026, minutes. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. I. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS A. 911 Third Ave “The Olive Shoppe” (All American Homes): The applicant, Jaughn Miller of All American Homes, is requesting approval to install a new awning, repaint building exterior and other exterior improvements to the building located at 911 Third Ave (PIN 367-01-01- 0041). The applicant is proposing to install and paint new flower boxes. The flower boxes will be 96 inches in length, and the paint color is “Glidden Pro GPS2300”. The awning (trellis/pergola style): The applicant would also like to install a new trellis and pergola awning will be 28 feet in length. Small awning over entrance: The applicant is requesting to install a new awning over the door farthest to the right. The awning will be 4 feet wide. Color is black. Fabric type not provided. Signage is shown on awning. Compliance with the related standards in the UDO. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. CAB 1/28/2026 Jordan made a motion to approve as presented. McLain seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. 911 Third Ave (Surf Water Promotions): The applicant, Darya Suddreth, is requesting approval to install new window graphics on the windows of the building located at 911 Third Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0041). The applicant is proposing to install vinyl window graphics on the windows of the building located at 911 Third Ave. The proposed window vinyl will be applied to all 6 windowpanes located on the building face. The UDO permits window signage that does not exceed 25% of the windowpane(s), and a maximum of 24 sq. ft. for all windows. Upper Windowpane measurements: » Window 1: 6.13’ (L) x 1.54’ (H) = 9.44 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 2.36 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 3.5’ (L) x .67’ (H) = 2.35 sq. ft. * Window 2: 5.63’ (L) x 1.54’ (H) = 8.67 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 2.17 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 4.3” (L) x .67’ (H) = 2.88 sq. ft. * Window 3: 5.63’ (L) x 1.54’ (H) — 8.67 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 2.17 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 4.3’ (L) x .67’ (H) = 2.88 sq. ft. Lower Windows (larger) pane measurements: ¢ Window 1: 6.13’ (L) x 7.88’ (W) = 48.3 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 12.1 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 4.17’ (H) x 4’ (L) = 16.7 sq. ft. * Window 2: 5.63’ (L) x 7.88’ (W) = 44.36 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 11.09 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 5.2’ (H) x 4.25’ (L) = 22.1 sq. ft. * Window 3:5.63’ (L) x 7.88’ (W) = 44.36 sq. ft. Max coverage allowed: 11.09 sq. ft. Proposed graphics: 4.2’ (H) x 4’ (L) = 16.8 sq. ft. Total square footage of window graphics proposed, based on applicant’s submittal: 63.71 sq. ft. The proposed graphics exceed the overall allowance by 39.71 sq. ft. The proposed signage is not compliant with the UDO, as the decals exceed the maximum 25% window coverage, as well as the 24 sq. ft. maximum. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request. Staff will work with the applicant to slightly reduce the size of the decals to meet the 25% maximum coverage area. Hall made a motion to approve as presented as long as it complies with UDO measurements. Jordan seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. CAB 1/28/2026 C. 911 Third Ave (Reliable Signs): The applicant, Darrell Blarton of Reliable Signs, is requesting approval to install new signage (hanging / suspended sign) on the building located at 911 Third Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0041). The applicant is proposing to install a hanging sign for the business located at 911 Third Ave. The proposed sign will be a double-sided, sandblasted sign 24” (2”) x 32” (2.67’), totaling 5.34 sq. ft. (approx.) painted as shown in rendering and hanging from black metal sign bracket. The bottom of the hanging sign will be a min. of 8’ above the public right of way. Hanging signs may be a maximum of 8 sq. ft. The request is consistent with the requirements in the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. McLain made a motion to approve as presented. Hall seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. 1120 Third Ave (A Coffee Movement): The applicant, Abel Wilson, is requesting approval to install new window graphics on the windows of the building located at 1120 Third Ave (PIN 368-04-02-0107). The applicant proposes installing new vinyl graphics on the window for the business located at 1120 Third Ave. Per the applicant’s request, the proposed vinyl graphics will total approximately 5.1 sq. ft. overall. The window the sign is to be affixed to will measure 67” W X 55” H, totaling approximately 25.59 Sq. Ft. allowing for a max coverage of 6.4 sq. ft. The breakdown of measurement is as follows: Each mug (there are 4) is 10" x 8.5" (0.59sqft or 2.36sqft total) To-go cup is 6" x 12" (0.50sqft) Hand is 11" x 15" (1.15sqft) Leaf (2 total) is 6" x 4" (0.17sqft or 0.33sqft total) Coffee bean (5 total) is 2.25" x 1.5" (0.024sqft or 0.12sqft total) Dots (6 total) are 1" diameter (0.04sqft total) Text block is 14" x 6" (0.58sqft) CAB 1/28/2026 Iv. The request is consistent with the requirements in the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. Hall made a motion to approve as presented. Jordan seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. . 975 Second Ave: The applicant, Steve Strickland, is requesting approval of new commercial structure for the property at 975 Second Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0054). The applicant proposes to construct a new commercial structure, that is proposed to be two restaurants and proposed to include space for office use. This project has been reviewed multiple times by CAB and TRC, with multiple revisions made over the last several years. The project was originally reviewed as: “Under the Bridge Seafood, Steaks, and Spirits” in March, 2019. The proposed name was later changed to “Cowboys”, then to “Riverwalk Restaurant”, and per the architectural plans / renderings, is shown as two restaurant spaces: “Sunset Grille” and “Cowboys”. The applicant must obtain all applicable permits and any deviation from what is approved shall require a re-review from this board and subsequent approvals. In August 2024 the applicant did receive overall approval for the design, the materials, the colors. But since then, there has been a property line issue. The building has corrected the ADA ramp to fit inside of the property lines. They also corrected the air conditioner units, so they are accessible and comply with fire requirements that the Board and Building Department previously requested of the applicant. The material for the siding has been updated and has been corrected. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. Staff will provide the Board with a detailed explanation of all the things that have changed and as to why these changes need to happen for the building. This list will be provided for our next meeting on February 11”. Jordan made a motion to defer until next meeting. McLain seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. SPECIAL TAX ASSESSMENTS A. 1311 Ninth Ave: The applicant, Drew McElveen, requests preliminary approval of a special tax assessment, as well as approval of relevant work, for the property located at 1311 Ninth Ave., in accordance with the City of Conway’s Preservation Tax Incentive Program (PIN 338-14-03-0042). Dennis provided an overview indicating that the applicant is seeking preliminary approval, based off the Special Tax Assessment checklist and requirements. Under the preservation tax incentive, the applicant must make qualifying improvements to the home that exceed 25% of the fair market value within a 2-year time frame. In exchange, the applicant will receive a tax freeze for up to 15 years and fees waived for building permits and capital recovery fees. As a part of the preliminary certification City Council voted to deem the property as an eligible property -- 2 of 22 -- CAB 12/17/2025 2 for the preservation tax incentive at their November 17th Council meeting. Following this designation the applicant is now presenting the proposed improvements to the board in the hopes of receiving preliminary approval and beginning work following the issuance of necessary permits. This home has had many changes through the years, but the intent of the new owner is to preserve and restore as much of the existing home back to its original glory. Items proposed for improvement: • removal of a second story addition that was not a part of the original structure • adding one of the two chimneys that has been removed • restore an existing chimney to working order • replace the roof, rotten and damaged siding windows, shutters • An addition to the rear portion of the home • restoration of historical columns on the porches and the porch roofs themselves • enclose a covered outdoor area • structural foundation repairs • addition of time specific gas sconce lights • completion of the interior of the home as it has been ripped bare. Drawings, photos, applications, background information, appraisal and detailed contractors’ estimates are included in the packet. The applicant was not present. Staff, and the board discussed the request in length. Hall made a motion to grant preliminary approval for the special tax assessment. Wallace seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. CERTIFICATES OF APPROPRIATENESS A. 1016 Third Ave (Leroy Clewis): The applicant, Leroy Clewis, is requesting approval for exterior improvements to the building located at 1016 Third Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0020). Dennis provided an overview indicating that the applicant is proposing to paint the exterior portions of the metal framing around the windows and doors. Also remove the metal at the base of the windows to replace it with stucco and paint that area white to match the building. All over facade color would be Chantilly lace and trim color black. Renderings are included in the packet. The applicant was present to answer any questions. Jordan made a motion to approve as presented. McLain seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 3 of 22 -- CAB 12/17/2025 3 B. 1016 Third Ave (Coastal 980): The applicant, Joy Elias, is requesting approval to install new signage for the building located at 1016 Third Ave (PIN 367-01-01-0020). Dennis provided an overview indicating that the applicant request is for the signage for the business. Installing a PVC painted black flush mount wall sign that measures approximately 8 ft in width and 2 ft in height totaling 16 sq ft. The wall sign will be fixed to measure approximately 400 sq ft with a max coverage of 100 sq ft. The proposed signage is compliant with the UDO. The applicant, Joy Elias, was present to answer any questions. Wallace made a motion to approve as presented. Hall seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Dennis provided an overview indicating that the applicant would like to install a new 46 inch awning in the pattern “Paxton Dew” by Sunbrella. The applicant would also like to paint the building in Sherwin Williams “Alabaster” and the door in Sherwin Williams color “Mint Condition”. It will measure 1.31 ft in width and 1.64 ft in height totaling approximately 2.16 sq ft. The Interior of the sign will be birch wood paneling that will read a Coffee Movement in black, and the sign will be a minimum of 8 ft from the bottom of the sign to the top of the sidewalk. The proposed is compliant with the UDO and renderings are included in the packet. The applicant, Abel Wilson, was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. Applicant updated his proposal that the wood plate in the sign will not be birch. It will be powder coated white steel. The rest of it will remain black. Roehm made a motion to approve with the amended materials. Jordan seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 4 of 22 -- CAB 12/17/2025 4 E. 4 Elm St. (Conway Outpost): The applicant, Thomas Guido, is requesting approval of a new commercial structure located at 4 Elm St. (PIN 367-08-01-0003). The pavilion will be approximately 90 ft x 56 ft and will be made of wood with railings, a stage area, a bar area and a covered roof. All materials are within a flood zone and meet Technical Bulletin No. 2 and NFIP standards and Flood standards. Building is primarily open and will allow for the free flow of water the way they have designed it. They are proposing black shingles on the top with railings with then lattice under the very bottom of the structure. Renderings are included in the packet. The applicant, Thomas Guido, was present to answer any questions. Staff, applicant and the board discussed the request in length. Mr. Guido proposed a change that the building will have green shingles on the roof to match the existing building that is on the property and the color of the paint will be the same peach color to match existing building. Also, the proposed building will be positioned the same way as the other building to match side by side. Stage area of the proposed building will be facing the river. The handicap ramp is on the west side which will be on the parking lot side. Applicant was asked regarding trellis and lattice. He was open to boards input. McLain made a motion to defer to next meeting proposing finalized materials for building. Jordan seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. In exchange, the applicant will receive a tax freeze for up to 15 years and fees waived for building permits and capital recovery fees. As a part of the preliminary certification City Council voted to deem the property as an eligible property for the preservation tax incentive at their November 17 th Council meeting. Following this designation the applicant is now presenting the proposed improvements to the board in the hopes of receiving preliminary approval and beginning work following the issuance of necessary permits. This home has had many changes through the years, but the intent of the new owner is to preserve and restore as much of the existing home back to its original glory. Items proposed for improvement: • removal of a second story addition that was not apart of the original structure • adding one of the two chimneys that has been removed • restore an existing chimney to working order • replace the roof, rotten and damaged siding windows, shutters • An addition to the rear portion of the home • restoration of historical columns on the porches and the porch roofs themselves • enclose a covered outdoor area • structural foundation repairs • addition of time specific gas sconce lights • completion of the interior of the home as it has been ripped bare. S. dollars or in terms of financial arrangements comparable thereto; and (5) the price represents the normal consideration for the property sold unaffected by special or creative financing or sales concessions* granted by anyone associated with the sale. *Adjustments to the comparables must be made for special or creative financing or sales concessions.
