(PIN 383-07-01-0008) -- 2 of 232 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/24/26 2 V. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. (Requested Deferral) A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 12 – Nonconformities, for the property located at 2601 E US Hwy 501. (PIN 383-07-01-0008) B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 - Fences & Walls, for the property located at 2037 Sawyer Street. (PIN 368-10-01-0061) Wilkerson stated the applicant has applied for a fence permit to install a 6-ft white vinyl fence in the rear of their home; however, this parcel sits between Sawyer Street and Creel Street. The Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) classifies this area as a "Double Front Yard" rather than a "Rear Yard". The subject lot is considered a "Legal Nonconforming" parcel, as the current UDO prohibits the creation of new double- frontage lots. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 5.2.3 (Fences & Walls): A variance of 2-ft to allow a 6-ft privacy fence in the Double Front Yard instead of just a 4-ft fence permitted by the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.6.2 – Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling, and Trash Handling, for the property located at 1328 Cottage Lane. (PIN 338-10-02-0009) Wilkerson stated this project is currently undergoing formal review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Following the recombination of the three existing parcels, the newly established lot will feature a corner configuration, resulting in a Front Yard, a Corner Front Yard, a Rear Yard, and a single Side Yard. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: -- 3 of 232 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/24/26 3 • Section 6.6.2 (Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling, and Trash Handling): A variance from the required location of the dumpster facility to allow the dumpster facility to be located in the Corner Front Yard (at Cottage Lane). Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance, contingent upon approval of the combination plat combining the three lots. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.2 – Residential Dimensional Requirements, Dwelling Types & Design Standards, for the property located at 1308 Sixth Avenue. (PIN 338-13-04-0027) Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated the applicant contacted the Planning & Development Department regarding a proposed subdivision of 1308 Sixth Avenue. Staff located an existing plat (PB 25-31) for Lot 10 and reviewed the standard dimensional requirements for the R-1 zoning district. Based on this historical plat, staff determined that a lot depth variance would be the only relief required to proceed with the subdivision. Staff subsequently advised the applicant to secure an updated survey to provide the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) with exact, current measurements for the variance request. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.2 (Residential Dimensional Requirements, Dwelling Types & Design Standards): A 10- ft variance from the 100-ft minimum lot depth requirement to permit a minimum lot depth of 90-ft for the proposed parcel. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Steven Starbuck, Jerry McClellan, Cathy Andrew, Pete Andrew, and Jay Watford spoke during public input. -- 4 of 232 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/24/26 4 Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance on the basis that the application did not meet the required criteria. Altman seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.2 – Residential Dimensional Requirements, Dwelling Types & Design Standards, for the property located at 405 Greenwich Drive. (PIN 324-09-03- 0049) Wilkerson stated the applicant has applied for a building permit to construct a covered carport attached to the primary residential structure. The subject property is located within the R-4 zoning district, which requires a minimum 5-foot side yard setback. According to the submitted site plan, the proposed carport will encroach 3 feet into this setback, resulting in a 2-foot setback from the side property line. Due to the proposed proximity to the property line, staff consulted with Construction Services and the Fire Marshal regarding the International Residential Code (IRC) Section R302. Their review confirmed the following fire separation requirements based on the distance from the property line: • Less than 5 feet: Exterior walls must have a minimum 1-hour fire-resistance rating. • 3 feet to less than 5 feet: Wall openings (such as windows or doors) are restricted to a maximum of 25% of the total exterior wall area. • 5 feet or greater: No fire-resistance rating is required, and openings are unlimited. The applicant was notified of these regulations and has agreed to utilize fire-rated materials to satisfy all IRC compliance standards. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.2 (Residential Dimensional Requirements, Dwelling Types & Design Standards): A 3-ft variance from the 5-ft minimum side yard setback required to allow a 2-ft side yard setback for the construction of an open-air carport. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to deny the requested variance on the basis that the application did not meet the required criteria. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:13 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2026. ______________________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairman -- 6 of 232 -- IV.A Administrative Appeal 2601 E US Hwy 501 -- 7 of 232 -- Appeal: 2061 E Highway 501 DATE: October 22, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: An administrative appeal from the decision of the Zoning Administrator regarding Article 12 – Nonconformities for the property located at 2601 E US Hwy 501. (PIN 383-07-01-0008) BACKGROUND: In March 2026, a storm severely damaged a billboard located on the Fairfield by Marriott parcel. Because the damage extended beyond the sign face, causing the supporting structure to collapse, the billboard could no longer safely support or display a sign. Consequently, staff emailed Coastal Outdoors on March 16, 2026, advising that the extensive structural damage legally prohibited reconstruction. Staff sent a follow-up email on April 13, 2026. Mr. Pudge Roberts responded on behalf of Coastal Outdoors, claiming their internal assessment valued the damage at less than 50% of the total replacement cost. He also noted they were seeking approval from the South Carolina Department of Transportation (SCDOT). On April 28, 2026, staff issued a citation to Mr. Roberts for violating Section 12.1.6 C-3, which was sent via certified mail. That same evening, Coastal Outdoors emailed staff stating their intent to proceed with repairs, attaching an SCDOT storm-damage approval. Staff immediately clarified that SCDOT approval does not substitute for local municipal authorization. Because the City of Conway's regulations can be more restrictive than state guidelines, staff explicitly stated that a City permit was strictly required. During this time, amendments to Article 12 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), which included specific revisions to nonconforming sign regulations, were already moving through the adoption process. These amendments became effective on May 4, 2026, the same day Coastal Outdoors applied for a sign permit. On May 18, 2026, the City denied the permit based on the physical condition of the billboard and the nonconforming sign provisions. At the applicant's request, staff scheduled a meeting on May 27, 2026, with representatives from Coastal Outdoors, the Planning Director, and the Zoning Administrator. Staff explained the denial and advised the applicant of their right to appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). Coastal Outdoors subsequently submitted an appraisal on June 21, 2026. Following a review of the appraisal, staff reiterated to Coastal Outdoors on June 25, 2026, that an administrative appeal to the BZA remained their only appropriate recourse. Ultimately, the permit denial is upheld regardless of whether the pre-amendment or post-amendment UDO standards are applied: • Pre-Amendment Standards (Prior to May 4, 2026): Section 12.1.6 C-3. Nonconforming Advertising Signs: Once a nonconforming advertising sign is removed, taken down, or destroyed (i.e., receiving damage to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of the replacement cost at the time of destruction), such sign shall not be replaced with another sign unless such sign is in conformance with this Unified Development -- 8 of 232 -- Appeal: 2061 E Highway 501 Ordinance. Such damaged sign shall not be expanded or relocated. Such sign shall not be reconstructed or moved without complying in all respects with the provisions of this Article. • Post-Amendment Standards (Effective May 4, 2026): Section 12.1.6 C-3. Nonconforming Advertising Signs: Ordinary Maintenance and Repair - No structural alteration, relocation, or expansion of a nonconforming advertising sign permitted. A nonconforming advertising sign may undergo ordinance maintenance and repair, provided such work does not: a. Increase the size, height, or number of sign faces; b. Involve replacement of structural components; c. Extend the useful life of the sign beyond its original design; or d. Result in any expansion or intensification of the nonconformity. Based on the extensive damage, the applicant is proposing entirely reconstructing the billboard rather than repairing it. Per staff interpretation, a project that requires erecting new poles, constructing a new frame, installing new lighting, and attaching a new sign face constitutes a total reproduction, not a partial repair. Furthermore, because each side of the billboard constitutes its own individual sign—rather than a single, two- sided structure—the applicant is not repairing a fraction of an existing sign. Instead, they are completely reconstructing a destroyed, nonconforming structure. APPEAL REQUESTED: “Reverse the Zoning Administrator’s decision and direct issuance of the permit for a like-kind repair – no increase in size, height, number of faces or degree of nonconformity.” The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals where it is alleged the City Zoning Administrator or their designee erred in an order, requirement, decision, or determination. In such cases, the Board may reverse or affirm, wholly or in part, the City Zoning Administrator or their designee’s action. The Board shall have all the powers of the City Zoning Administrator or their designee in such cases and may direct the issuance of a permit. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the appeal and affirm, reverse, or modify the administrative decision, in whole or in part. -- 9 of 232 -- -- 10 of 232 -- -- 11 of 232 -- -- 12 of 232 -- -- 13 of 232 -- -- 14 of 232 -- DATE PLANNING TIMELINE OF EVENTS 2026-03-16 Email sent from Zoning Administrator to Coastal Outdoors regarding the clean up of the destroyed billboard debris. 2026-04-13 Follow up email from Zoning Administrator regarding the cleanup of the billboard debris with notation that a citation would be issued. 2026-04-13 Email received from Mr. Pudge Roberts stating the damage is not more than 50% of the replacement cost & that they are working with SCDOT for approval to repair the billboard. 2026-04-13 Email from Zoning Administrator quoting the UDO for nonconforming advertising signs. 2026-04-14 Email from Mr. Pudge Roberts stating that their determination is the damage is not more than 50% and that they are working with SCDOT. O’Bryan Martin Re: Billboard Denial - Coastal Outdoor Advertising | 2061 East Highway 501 (PIN# 38307010008) Dear Mr. Martin: This letter serves as official notice that the sign permit application (PS26-0046) submitted by Coastal Outdoor Advertising was denied by Zoning on May 18, 2026. A system-generated comment letter detailing the specific reasons for denial was emailed to the applicant on that date. Pursuant to city policy, the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO)—amended and effective as of May 4, 2026—applied to this review because the evaluation was completed after the amendment date. Under my determination as Zoning Administrator, the billboard has lost its legal non-conforming status. Per UDO Section 12.1.6 (4b), a sign loses this status if it is "removed, taken down, destroyed, collapsed, or otherwise no longer capable of safely supporting or displaying the sign face and the proposed work involves reconstruction, replacement of structural components, relocation, expansion, or other work beyond maintenance." I have attached photographic evidence documenting the current physical state of the structure that supports this finding. Planning Director, Jessica Hucks and I met in person with Mr. Pudge Roberts and Ms. Nancy Dunn on May 27, 2026. We explained the Billboard Sign Replacement Program option and the right to appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). If the applicant wishes to challenge this administrative decision, an appeal may be filed with the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). The BZA is empowered to hear and decide appeals where it is alleged there is an error in any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by the Zoning Administrator. For your convenience, I have attached the BZA application forms and the upcoming meeting schedule. Sincerely, Kym Wilkerson Zoning Administrator/Deputy Director -- 19 of 232 -- -- 20 of 232 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 12 – Nonconformities 12-5 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended November 3, 2025 12.1.5 Nonconforming Lots of Record Any lot created prior to the adoption of this Unified Development Ordinance that does not comply with the minimum lot area and lot width requirements as set forth in Section 6.2 shall nonetheless be approved for use provided all other applicable requirements of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance are met. If the owner of such nonconforming lot owns one or more adjacent lots, the combination of the nonconforming lot and the adjacent lot(s) shall be required in order to create lot(s) that comply with the minimum requirements set forth in Section 6.2. 12.1.6 Nonconforming Signs A. In cases where signs exist as nonconforming uses on property and/or exceed the total allowable sign area, no additional signs shall be permitted for an establishment. If the size, configuration, or use of a parcel (or building) is changed, signs on the resulting properties shall be required to conform to the sign regulations applicable to the newly created parcel or parcels at the time such change becomes effective. B. All nonconforming signs shall be maintained and repainted and shall not be maintained in such a manner as to increase the degree of nonconformity. In cases where a “cabinet” nonconforming sign exists with Plexiglas faces, these faces may be changed if damaged or if sign message is desired to be changed. Wooden pole signs with single wooden surfaces may only be changed by painting the surface and the face. C. Nonconforming advertising signs shall be allowed to continue as provided as follows: 1. No structural changes to the support structure or changes to the sign face itself except message changes, which do not renew or extend the life of said sign shall be allowed. 2. Maintenance of nonconforming advertising signs shall be limited to painting and repair of the existing sign. 3. Once a nonconforming advertising sign is removed, taken down, or destroyed (i.e., receiving damage to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of the replacement cost at the time of destruction), such sign shall not be replaced with another sign unless such sign is in conformance with this Unified Development Ordinance. Such damaged sign shall not be expanded or relocated. Such sign shall not be reconstructed or moved without complying in all respects with the provisions of this Article. D. Nonconforming business or identification signs shall be allowed to continue provided as follows: 1. Signs which are nonconforming with respect to size or illumination requirements may be repaired and/or repainted or re-lettered provided the nonconformance (e.g. area) is not increased. 2. Signs which are nonconforming with respect to location or number permitted shall not be altered in any way except to make such sign comply with the provisions of this Article. E. Signs for Nonconforming Uses. Signs associated with a legal nonconforming use of a structure or land shall be allowed to continue provided as follows: 1. Nonconforming signs associated with a nonconforming use of a structure or land shall not be changed except to make such signs comply with the applicable sign regulations for the district in which said use or land is located. Nonconforming signs shall be brought into compliance if a use change occurs or if a building is vacant for over 180 days. 2. Replacement signs for a legal nonconforming use of a structure or land shall be permitted in accordance with the applicable sign regulations for the district in which said use or land is located. C. General Provisions Nonconforming signs that were lawfully established prior to the adoption or amendment of this Ordinance may continue, subject to the provisions of this section. Where a property or use is modified, subdivided, or otherwise altered, all signage shall be brought into compliance with the requirements of this Ordinance for the new or modified use or parcel. B. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. -- 199 of 232 -- Variance: 2061 E Highway 501 STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 200 of 232 -- IV.C Variance Request 300 Victory Lane -- 201 of 232 -- Variance: 300 Victory Lane (HGTC) DATE: October 22, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: IV.C ISSUE: A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay, for the property located at 300 Victory Lane. (PIN 338-00-00-0037) BACKGROUND: • Proposed: Rivertown ER – Wall Sign • Zoning: Highway Commercial (HC) & Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) PROJECT OVERVIEW: The applicant has requested sign permits for the upcoming Rivertown ER located at 1720 Church Street. Due to the building's orientation, the primary emergency room entrance is situated on the west side rather than facing Church Street. Consequently, the applicant is seeking a variance to place the wall sign on the Church Street façade and increase the maximum allowable sign size. UDO REQUIREMENT: Section 11.4.1 - Walls Signs • Location and Number Permitted: Only one (1) wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at the Public Entrance. • Size: Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached. REQUEST & JUSTIFICATION: The west side of the emergency room is not visible to traffic traveling in either direction on Church Street. Placing the sign on the public entrance side would severely obstruct the facility's visibility from the property's primary roadway. Therefore, the proposed wall sign location utilizes the building elevation that offers maximum visibility from Church Street. SPECIFIC VARIANCES REQUESTED: Section 11.4.1 - Walls Signs • A variance to allow the installation of a wall sign on the Church Street façade rather than at the designated public entrance. • A 73.75-square foot variance to allow a 277-square foot wall sign covering 20.44% of the building face instead of the 15% limit. -- 216 of 232 -- Variance: 1720 Church Street (Rivertown ER) CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. ADJOURN (Requested Deferral (( )ll (R (( equested Deferral)ll -- 1 of 46 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 1 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, AUGUST 27, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman Absent: Sandra James, Paul Lawson, Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Louis Smith, IT. Others: Ralph Thompson, Reese Quick, Kevin Brown, Mark Avant, Magdy Hanna, Brett Callaghan, Cassidy Callaghan, Nathan Williamson, Gerry Wallace, Cameron Parker, Alberta Bellamy, Lucille Moses. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Hagen called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Alman to approve June 25 th , minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Hagen read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 8.2.12 – Parking Requirements for Specific Uses, for the property located at 1911 Ninth Avenue. (PIN 368-02-04-0015) -- 2 of 46 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 2 Wilkerson stated Venture Engineering has submitted plans to construct a new building containing 16 one- bedroom apartment units on the subject parcel. Staff’s review determined the proposed site plan does not meet the minimum parking requirements. The UDO requires 121 total parking spaces for the expanded site, while the proposed layout provides 92 spaces, resulting in a 29-space deficit. The 16 proposed one-bedroom units are designated for senior residents (aged 60 and older). According to data provided by the Chairman of the EME Board of Trustees, only 24 of the current households own vehicles. Because the actual vehicle ownership rate is low, the applicant contends that the existing 92 spaces will comfortably accommodate both current residents and the proposed senior housing expansion without creating a parking shortage. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements: A variance of 29 parking spaces to allow 92 parking spaces where 121 spaces are required. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Alberta Bellamy spoke during public input. Hagen made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 5.2.1 – Accessory Structures, for the property located at Victory Lane and Highway 501. (PIN 383-00-00-0132) Donna Baxley recused herself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated in 2023, staff identified unpermitted accessory structures on PIN 383-00-00-0132, owned by HGTC. Following notification, the Planning & Development department received an initial submittal later that month. Staff and the project engineer (DRG) have since engaged in an ongoing comment review process. On January 22, 2026, HGTC petitioned the BZA for a variance regarding the size of three proposed monument signs. The BZA granted two of the variances but tabled the third—located on this parcel—until -- 3 of 46 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 3 a combination plat could be completed to establish a principal structure. (the HGTC Automotive Technology Bldg). A combination plat was subsequently recorded on April 22, 2026, to combine this parcel with PIN 383-10- 01-0021. However, because the applicant has not finalized the necessary deedwork, the formal lot combination is not yet legally complete. Per the UDO, accessory structures require an established principal structure and must be located exclusively in the side or rear yards. Deed work is forthcoming to legally combine PIN 383-00-00-0132 and PIN 383-10-01-0021. This consolidation will formally establish a primary building on the combined parcel. Due to unique parcel topography and the existing layout, meeting the strict UDO location requirement is physically impossible. Strict enforcement of the ordinance would deny the property owner reasonable use of the land. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 5.2.1 (B) – Accessory Structures: A variance to allow the location of the Accessory Structures to be forward of the Principal Structure. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hagen made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 6.5.2 – Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at Highway 501 and University Drive as well as Highway 544 and University Drive. (PIN 383-00-00-0382 & 382-00-00-0039) Wilkerson stated due to the Highway 501 widening project and the subsequent realignment of University Boulevard, the applicant is requesting a variance from the maximum allowable sign face area for three (3) proposed monument signs. The subject property is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) district. Staff notes that this variance request is substantially similar to a prior variance granted to Horry- Georgetown Technical College (HGTC) in January 2022. The applicant is proposing monument signs with an aggregate sign area of ninety-five (95) square feet each, thereby necessitating the variance request. -- 4 of 46 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 4 SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.5.2 (M) – Gateway Corridor Overlay-Signs: A 35-sq ft variance to allow the three proposed Monument Signs to have an aggregate sign area of 95-sq ft each. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 6.5.3 – Village Corridor Overlay (VCO), for the property located at 1219 Sixteenth Avenue. (PIN 338-11-04-0034) Wilkerson stated the applicant recently relocated his business from Coastal Centre after purchasing the property at 1219 Sixteenth Avenue. He is requesting a 20-foot pole sign to match the existing signage of neighboring businesses. However, these surrounding signs are “legal non-conforming”. If any of those existing signs are removed for any reason, they cannot be reinstalled. Any new signage for those tenants would be required to comply fully with the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.5.3 (K) – Village Corridor Overlay-Signs: A variance to allow a pole sign that does not comply with the overlay district's standard restrictions on sign type, height, and total area. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to deny the requested variance on the basis that the application did not meet the required criteria. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 5 of 46 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 5 E. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2026. ______________________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairman -- 6 of 46 -- V.B -- 7 of 46 -- Variance: 2037 Sawyer Street DATE: September 24, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: V.B ISSUE: A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 - Fences & Walls, for the property located at 2037 Sawyer Street. (PIN 368-10-01-0061) BACKGROUND: • Location: Magnolia Bay Phase 2 (Lot 10) • Zoning: R1 (Low Density Residential) • Existing Land Use: Single-Family Residential • Adjacent Property: R1 (Low Density Residential) PROJECT OVERVIEW: The applicant has applied for a fence permit to install a 6-ft white vinyl fence in the rear of their home; however, this parcel sits between Sawyer Street and Creel Street. The Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) classifies this area as a "Double Front Yard" rather than a "Rear Yard". The subject lot is considered a "Legal Nonconforming" parcel, as the current UDO prohibits the creation of new double-frontage lots. UDO REQUIREMENT: • Section 5.2.3 (Fences and Walls): Only fences with a maximum height of 4-ft are permitted within a Double Front Yard. • Article 2 (Definitions): A Double Front Yard is defined as "a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. REQUEST & JUSTIFICATION: Strict application of the UDO restricts the applicant to a 4-ft fence along the Creel Street frontage, which functions as their backyard. The applicant is requesting a variance to allow a 6-ft fence based on the following factors: • Neighborhood Consistency: The adjacent properties on both sides of the subject lot feature existing 6-ft privacy fences. Granting this request would maintain visual continuity along the streetscape. • HOA Approval: While external to city jurisdiction, the Magnolia Bay Homeowners Association (HOA) has reviewed and formally approved the proposed 6-ft privacy fence at this location. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 5.2.3 (Fences & Walls): A variance of 2-ft to allow a 6-ft privacy fence in the Double Front Yard instead of just a 4-ft fence permitted by the UDO. -- 8 of 46 -- Variance: 2037 Sawyer Street CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 9 of 46 -- -- 10 of 46 -- -- 11 of 46 -- -- 12 of 46 -- SAWYER STREET CREEL STREET -- 13 of 46 -- -- 14 of 46 -- BACKSIDE OF 2037 SAWYER STREET -- 15 of 46 -- CREEL ST NEW RD FOURTH AVE WATSON ST SAWYER ST DEWBERRY DR ROSEHAVEN DR JAMES AVE JORDAN CIR JASMINE DR BUTLER DR SWEET PINE DR RAY LN EDGEWOOD CIR HWY 701 S TEMPLE ST MIMOSA CT CAUSEY ST Date: 8/17/2026 Time: 2:07 PM Path: \\Coc-fs01\Folder Redirects$\cpetty\My Documents\ArcGIS\Projects\ZONING MAP 8 X 10\ZONING MAP 8 X 10.aprx PIN #: 368-10-01-0061 2037 SAWYER ST ³ Disclaimer: This map is a graphic representation only. (PIN 338-10-02-0009) BACKGROUND: • Location: Adjacent to Burger King on Church Street • Proposed: 7Brew Drive Thru Coffee • Zoning: Highway Commercial (HC) | Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) • Adjacent Property: Highway Commercial (HC) • TRC Requirement: PIN#s 33810020009, 33810020008 & 33810020007 must be combined via a minor plat prior to Civil Plan approval PROJECT OVERVIEW: This project is currently undergoing formal review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Following the recombination of the three existing parcels, the newly established lot will feature a corner configuration, resulting in a Front Yard, a Corner Front Yard, a Rear Yard, and a single Side Yard. UDO REQUIREMENT: • Section 6.6.2 (Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling, and Trash Handling): The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street. REQUEST & JUSTIFICATION: Due to the unique configuration of this corner lot, the site features a Corner Front Yard rather than a traditional second side yard. This dual-frontage constraint significantly restricts compliant areas for a dumpster facility. Additionally, the facility must be positioned to ensure safe, efficient, and unobstructed access for sanitation vehicles. The proposed location represents the only viable placement without severely compromising the site's overall functionality, traffic circulation, and safety. The dumpster facility will be fully enclosed by an 8-foot-tall opaque screen fence as well as screening from landscaping. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.6.2 (Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling, and Trash Handling): A variance from the required location of the dumpster facility to allow the dumpster facility to be located in the Corner Front Yard (at Cottage Lane). -- 19 of 46 -- Variance: 1328 Cottage Lane CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. (PIN 338-13-04-0027) BACKGROUND: • Location: Corner of Sixth Avenue and Burroughs Street • Proposed: Subdivision of Lot 10 into two residential parcels • Zoning: R-1 (Low Density Residential) • Adjacent Property: R-1 (Low Density Residential) & R-2 (Medium Density Residential) PROJECT OVERVIEW: The applicant contacted the Planning & Development Department regarding a proposed subdivision of 1308 Sixth Avenue. Staff located an existing plat (PB 25-31) for Lot 10 and reviewed the standard dimensional requirements for the R-1 zoning district. Based on this historical plat, staff determined that a lot depth variance would be the only relief required to proceed with the subdivision. Staff subsequently advised the applicant to secure an updated survey to provide the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) with exact, current measurements for the variance request. UDO REQUIREMENT: • Section 6.2 (Residential Dimensional Requirements, Dwelling Types & Design Standards): The minimum lot depth for a newly created parcel zoned R-1 is 100-ft. REQUEST & JUSTIFICATION: Because the existing single-family residence is situated close to Sixth Avenue, the applicant intends to subdivide and develop the remaining vacant portion of the property along Burroughs Street. The proposed subdivision will yield one additional single-family residential homesite. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Rear is Residential (R1). PROJECT OVERVIEW: The applicant recently relocated his business from Coastal Centre after purchasing the property at 1219 Sixteenth Avenue. He is requesting a 20-foot pole sign to match the existing signage of neighboring businesses. However, these surrounding signs are “legal non-conforming”. If any of those existing signs are removed for any reason, they cannot be reinstalled. Any new signage for those tenants would be required to comply fully with the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). UDO REQUIREMENT: • Per Section 6.5.3 - Village Corridor Overlay (VCO) of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), “Monument and Freestanding Post Signs are the only freestanding signs allowed in the VCO.” The maximum height is eight (8) feet and the maximum size is twenty-four (24) square feet. • Per Section 11.2.2 – Prohibited Signs of the UDO, “Pole Signs and Pylon Signs” are listed as prohibited. • Per Section 12.1.6 – Nonconforming Signs & Sign Structures of the UDO states, “Nonconforming advertising signs may continue in accordance with this section but shall not be enlarged, relocated, or structurally altered except as expressly permitted herein. The display face or message of a nonconforming advertising sign may be changed, provided such change does not increase the size, height, or degree of nonconformity”. • Per Section 11.4.9 – EMC/LED Signs of the UDO states, “The size of the EMC / LED sign shall be no greater than the sign area allotted by the sign type”. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.5.3 (K) – Village Corridor Overlay-Signs: A variance to allow a pole sign that does not comply with the overlay district's standard restrictions on sign type, height, and total area. -- 46 of 78 -- Variance: 1219 Sixteenth Avenue (Conway Pharmacy) CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, AUGUST 27, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman Absent: Sandra James, Paul Lawson, Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Louis Smith, IT. Others: Ralph Thompson, Reese Quick, Kevin Brown, Mark Avant, Magdy Hanna, Brett Callaghan, Cassidy Callaghan, Nathan Williamson, Gerry Wallace, Cameron Parker, Alberta Bellamy, Lucille Moses. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Hagen called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Alman to approve June 25", minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. II. CRITERIA Hagen read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; ° Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; © Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance, IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 8.2.12 — Parking Requirements for Specific Uses, for the property located at 1911 Ninth Avenue. (PIN 368-02-04-0015) Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 Wilkerson stated Venture Engineering has submitted plans to construct a new building containing 16 one- bedroom apartment units on the subject parcel. Staff’s.review determined the proposed site plan does not meet the minimum parking requirements. The UDO requires 121 total parking spaces for the expanded site, while the proposed layout provides 92 spaces, resulting in a 29-space deficit. The 16 proposed one-bedroom units are designated for senior residents (aged 60 and older). According to data provided by the Chairman of the EME Board of Trustees, only 24 of the current households own vehicles. Because the actual vehicle ownership rate is low, the applicant contends that the existing 92 spaces will comfortably accommodate both current residents and the proposed senior housing expansion without creating a parking shortage. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements: A variance of 29 parking spaces to allow 92 parking spaces where 121 spaces are required. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Alberta Bellamy spoke during public input. Hagen made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 5.2.1 — Accessory Structures, for the property located at Vietory Lane and Highway 501. (PIN 383-00-00-0132) Donna Baxley recused herself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated in 2023, staff identified unpermitted accessory structures on PIN 383-00-00-0132, owned. by HGTC. Following notification, the Planning & Development department received an initial submittal later that month. Staff and the project engineer (DRG) have since engaged in an ongoing comment review process. On January 22, 2026, HGTC petitioned the BZA for a variance regarding the size of three proposed monument signs. The BZA granted two of the variances but tabled the third—located on this parcel—auntil Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 a combination plat could be completed to establish a principal structure. (the HGTC Automotive Technology Bldg). A combination plat was subsequently recorded on April 22, 2026, to combine this parcel with PIN 383-10- 01-0021. However, because the applicant has not finalized the necessary deedwork, the formal lot combination is not yet legally complete. Per the UDO, accessory structures require an established principal structure and must be located exclusively in the side or rear yards. Deed work is forthcoming to legally combine PIN 383-00-00-0132 and PIN 383-1 0-01-0021. This consolidation will formally establish a primary building on the combined parcel. Due to unique parcel topography and the existing layout, meeting the strict UDO location requirement is physically impossible. Strict enforcement of the ordinance would deny the property owner reasonable use of the land. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Section 5.2.1 (B) - Accessory Structures: A variance to allow the location of the Accessory Structures to be forward of the Principal Structure. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hagen made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 6.5.2 — Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at Highway 501 and University Drive as well as Highway 544 and University Drive. (PIN 383-00-00-0382 & 382-00-00-0039) Wilkerson stated due to the Highway 501 widening project and the subsequent realignment of University Boulevard, the applicant is requesting a variance from the maximum allowable sign face area for three (3) proposed monument signs. The subject property is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) district. Staff notes that this variance request is substantially similar to a prior variance granted to Horry- Georgetown Technical College (HGTC) in January 2022. The applicant is proposing monument signs with an aggregate sign area of ninety-five (95) square feet each, thereby necessitating the variance request. Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: ¢ Section 6.5.2 (M) - Gateway Corridor Overlay-Signs: A 35-sq ft variance to allow the three proposed Monument Signs to have an aggregate sign area of 95-sq ft each. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 6.5.3 — Village Corridor Overlay (VCO), for the property located at 1219 Sixteenth Avenue. (PIN 338-1 1-04-0034) Wilkerson stated the applicant recently relocated his business from Coastal Centre after purchasing the property at 1219 Sixteenth Avenue. He is requesting a 20-foot pole sign to match the existing signage of neighboring businesses. However, these surrounding signs are “legal non-conforming”. If any of those existing signs are removed for any reason, they cannot be reinstalled. Any new signage for those tenants would be required to comply fully with the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: Section 6.5.3 (K}— Village Corridor Overlay-Signs: A variance to allow a pole sign that does not comply with the overlay district's standard restrictions on sign type, height, and total area. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to deny the requested variance on the basis that the application did not meet the required criteria, Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 8/27/26 E. (Requested Deferral to September 24) An administrative appeal from the decision of the Zoning Administrator with regard to Article 12 - Nonconformities for the property located at 2601 E US Hwy 501. (PIN 383-07-01-0008) Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m. Approved and signed this TA. day ot Spend , 2026. PaulLaysSon, Chajrman

According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. text: PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT 196 Laurel Street | Post Office Box 1075 | Conway, South Carolina 29528-1075 | Telephone (843) 488-9888 | www.ConwaySC.gov MAYOR Barbara Jo Blain M AYOR P RO TEM Beth Helms COUNCIL M EMBERS Amanda Butler William M. CALL TO ORDER II. APPROVAL OF MAY 28, 2026 MINUTES III. CRITERIA IV. PUBLIC HEARING – VARIANCE REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 – Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at 1717 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-06-01-0017) V. ADJOURN -- 1 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 1 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, MAY 28, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Sandra James, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson, Catherine Dingle, Lesley Hill Absent: Donna Baxley Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT. Others: Collins Corbett, Edna Erazo, Brantle M Green, Clint Richardson, BJ & Tony Burkhart, Richard Hogan, Yvette Boyd, Forest Beverly, David Schwerd, Scott Davis, Daniel Ben- Yisrael. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the April 23rd , minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 – Landscaping & Buffer Requirements, for the property located at 1818 Main Street. (PIN 338-06-03-0078) Wilkerson stated due to parcel size constraints and to meet the parking requirements for the use, the applicant requests a variance to omit the 5-foot Type A Landscape Buffer along the southern property line -- 2 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 2 where it conflicts with the proposed parking lot. The development will meet all other UDO landscaping requirements. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • UDO Table 9.2 (Landscaping Rate Chart): Omission of the 5-foot landscape buffer along the southern property line, restricted to the parking lot area only. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 – Landscaping & Buffer Requirements, for the property located at 2776 Church Street. (PIN 337-00-00-0034) Wilkerson stated due to existing asphalt and site constraints, the applicant requests to omit the 5-foot physical buffer strip along the new shared property line, except for the first 30.22 linear feet. In its place, the applicant proposes relocating 100% of the required buffer plantings across both project sites. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • UDO Table 9.2 (Landscaping Rate Chart): Relief from the 5-foot physical landscape buffer width requirement along the shared property line (with the exception of the first 30.22 linear feet), with a condition to distribute 100% of the required planting units across both subject parcels. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. -- 3 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 3 Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 - Gateway Corridor Overlay and Article 11 - Signage, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN 338-11-04-0052) Wilkerson provided background on the property, noting that it is located at 1600 Church Street (intersection of Church Street and Sixteenth Avenue). She stated that the site is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). The proposal includes the Parker’s Kitchen outparcel development within the redeveloped Coastal Centre. She also noted that the surrounding properties are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). Granting this variance will allow Parker’s Kitchen to provide clear and consistent wayfinding for its customers, enhancing the overall safety and accessibility of the site. The additional signage on the left and right elevation, along with the requested monument sign height and reader board relief, will directly serve the community by ensuring motorists can easily locate and navigate to the property, reducing traffic disruptions and improving customer experience. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.5.2-M.4.a - Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO)-Signs-Height-Monument Signs: A 3-foot variance to allow two (2) monument signs at a height of 13 feet instead of the permitted 10- feet. • Section 11.4.13-B - Gasoline Pricing Signs-Size: A 4-inch variance to allow 16-inch digital reader board numbers instead of the permitted 12-inches. • Section 11.4.1-A – Walls Signs-Location & Number Permitted: A variance to allow four (4) total wall signs instead of the permitted maximum of two (2) signs. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance for the four (4) Wall Signs as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 4 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 4 Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance for the Gasoline Pricing Signs-Size as presented. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to deny the height requested variance for the two (2) monument signs. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1001 Winding Road. (PIN 339-09-01-0025) Wilkerson stated that the applicant has applied for a building permit proposing the construction of a 33-ft by 12-ft open porch addition to the existing single-family residence. The existing primary structure is classified as legally nonconforming. Per UDO Article 12 (Nonconformities), a structure is deemed legally nonconforming if it was lawfully established prior to the adoption, amendment, or jurisdictional changes of the current ordinance, but no longer complies with current dimensional standards. The home was constructed in 1951, pre-dating the adoption of the current UDO in 2011. Because the existing house does not meet current setbacks, any modern additions require variance relief if they encroach into the current setbacks. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Table 6.1: Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: An 8-foot variance to allow for a 12-ft rear setback to accommodate the proposed open porch. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.3.1 – Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards, for the property located at 2393 Church Street. (PIN 337-00-00-0024) Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. -- 5 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 5 Wilkerson stated that the applicant has applied for a building permit proposing the construction of a 7,000 sq ft Metal Building to use as an Automotive Repair Shop (not open to the general public). The applicant cited existing metal buildings on-site. However, these structures sit within unincorporated Horry County jurisdictions, not the City of Conway. Building 2 is a metal structure classified as a “legal nonconforming”. Google Earth imagery shows it has existed since 2008, likely permitted by Horry County prior to city annexation. Building 7 lacks any record of a City of Conway building permit and was also likely established under county jurisdiction. Recent developments on the property—specifically the Commercial Vehicle Center and the new front façade of Building 1, fully comply with current City of Conway architectural standards. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.3.1-D (Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards) & Section 5.2.1-B.6 (Non- Residential Accessory Structures): A variance to permit an external metal wall system for a proposed 7,000-square-foot structure, departing from the standard non-residential building material and design requirements. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at Little Bay Drive (Rivertown Row North-Phase 2). (PIN 326-00-00-0048 & 337-04-02-0079) Wilkerson stated that in January 2026, the applicant and the property owners of Rivertown Row North, Phase 1, jointly requested a variance to eliminate the required perimeter landscape buffer, which would otherwise encumber the rear yards of individual parcels. The Board of Zoning Appeals granted the variance for Phase 1 because those homes were already constructed and sold. However, the variance was not granted for Phase 2, as that phase has not yet been subdivided. -- 6 of 31 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 6 The R-2 zoning district mandates a minimum lot depth of 120-ft. To prevent the Phase 1 buffer issue from recurring, the applicant seeks a lot depth reduction specifically for Lots 105 through 120 on the western boundary of Phase 2. This variance would allow the required 10-ft landscape buffer to be platted as a separate open space area owned and maintained by the Homeowners Association (HOA), rather than encroaching into private rear yards. Currently, the shallowest proposed lot depth in this section is 122.32 ft. Excluding the 10-ft buffer area from the private lot boundaries reduces the platted lot depth to 112.32 ft, requiring a variance of 7.68 ft from the 120-ft UDO standard. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Table 6.1: Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts-Lot Depth: A variance to reduce the minimum required lot depth from 120-ft to 112.32-ft (a 7.68-ft reduction) for Lots 105–120. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Edna Erazo spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:51 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2026. Paul Lawson, Chairman Catherine Dingle, Vice Chairman -- 7 of 31 -- Variance: 1717 Fourth Avenue DATE: June 25, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 – Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at 1717 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-06-01-0017) BACKGROUND: • Location: 1717 Fourth Avenue (Waccamaw Flooring) • Zoning: Highway Commercial (HC) within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) • Existing Land Use: Multi Units with uses such as Waccamaw Flooring, Holmes Flooring, Elite Esthetics Spa, etc. • Adjacent Property: Highway Commercial (HC) PROJECT OVERVIEW: ASL Sign Services, acting as the property owner’s agent, submitted a permit application for a new 12-foot monument sign. The Planning & Development Department denied the request, citing the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) restriction that limits monument sign heights to 10 feet within the Gateway Corridor Overlay. Although the permit was never approved, the applicant stated that fabrication had already begun and the sign framework is complete at 12 feet. UDO REQUIREMENT: • Per Section 6.5.2 M-4 (Gateway Corridor Overlay) Monument Signs: The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for multi-tenants (more than 3). • Per Article 2-Definitions (Shopping Center): A unified commercial development consisting of four (4) or more retail, service, or professional establishments occupying common or adjacent buildings and having shared access, internal circulation, and parking areas intended to serve all multiple uses of the site. The development shall contain a total gross floor area of 100,000 square feet or greater. (Based on Horry County Land Records, the building is 11,200 square feet) • Per Article 2-Definitions (Sign Height): The vertical distance measured from the average finished grade at the base of the sign to the highest point top of the sign or supporting structure. Where a sign is located on a berm or artificial raised grade, height shall be measured from the average surrounding natural grade. • Per Section 12.1.6 D (Nonconforming Signs & Sign Structures): Nonconforming business or identification signs that do not comply with current standards for size, illumination, location, or number may continue provided that: 1. The sign is not expanded or modified in a manner that increases the degree of nonconformity. 2. Any alteration to the sign shall bring the sign into greater conformity where feasible. 3. No additional nonconforming signage shall be installed. -- 8 of 31 -- Variance: 1717 Fourth Avenue STAFF ANALYSIS: • Hardship: The sign company's misinterpretation of permit details does not establish a legal hardship (see attached). • Overlay Allowance: The Gateway Corridor Overlay restricts multi-tenant freestanding post signs to a maximum height of 20 feet. • UDO Restriction: The UDO explicitly prohibits replacing a legal nonconforming use, structure, site, or sign with another nonconforming element. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: • Section 6.5.2-M (Gateway Corridor Overlay): A variance of 2-ft to allow for a 12-ft multi-tenant monument sign vs the 10-ft allowed by the UDO. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 9 of 31 -- -- 10 of 31 -- -- 11 of 31 -- -- 12 of 31 -- -- 13 of 31 -- -- 14 of 31 -- -- 15 of 31 -- -- 16 of 31 -- -- 17 of 31 -- -- 18 of 31 -- -- 19 of 31 -- -- 20 of 31 -- -- 21 of 31 -- -- 22 of 31 -- -- 23 of 31 -- -- 24 of 31 -- &LW\RI&RQZD\ /DXUHO6WUHHW&RQZD\6& 3KRQH   6LJQ3HUPLW   36   0\UWOH%HDFK6& +Z\6 $6/6,*16  +:<* /2&$7,21 2:1(5 &2175$&725 :RUN'HVFULSWLRQ 6WLSXODWLRQV /('&KDQQHO/HWWHUVRQ5DFHZD\ $PRQJRWKHULQVSHFWLRQV\RXPXVWUHTXHVWDILQDOEXLOGLQJDQGDILQDO]RQLQJLQVSHFWLRQWRSURSHUO\FORVHRXWWKH SHUPLW 3KRQH 3KRQH ,19(670(1762)0%//& 8QLW 0\UWOH%HDFK6& 3(50,7 ,668(' (;3,5(6 =RQLQJ )HH&DWHJRU\ )HH'HVFULSWLRQ 4XDQWLW\ ,WHP7RWDO =RQLQJ&RPSOLDQFH&KDUJH 6WDQGDUG,WHP   &RP%XLOGLQJ)HH 6WDQGDUG,WHP    )HH7RWDO $PRXQW3DLG  %DODQFH'XH  5(48,5(',163(&7,216 6HWEDFNV )LQDO(OHFWULFDO )LQDO%XLOGLQJ )RXQGDWLRQ )RRWLQJ 5RXJK(OHFWULFDO =RQLQJ )LQDO%XLOGLQJ 6LJQ3HUPLW +:<* $6/6,*16 -- 25 of 31 -- -- 26 of 31 -- -- 27 of 31 -- -- 28 of 31 -- FOURTH AVE CHURCH ST APPLE LN WOODWARD DR ALSTON ST CHURCH ST Date: 5/15/2026 Time: 9:00:35 AM Path: \\Coc-srv2\4310\BZA\MEETINGS\2026\6.25.26\IV.A - 1717 FOURTH AVENUE (WACCAMAW FLOOR COVERING)\GIS\FUTURE LAND USE MAP FOR 1717 FOURTH AVE WACCAMAW FLOOR COVERING.mxd PIN #: 368-06-01-0017 WACCAMAW FLOOR COVERING 1717 FOUTH AVE ³ Disclaimer: This map is a graphic representation only.
