A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 — Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at 1717 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-06-01-0017) Wilkerson stated ASL Sign Services, acting as the property owner’s agent, submitted a permit application for a new 12-foot monument sign. The Planning & Development Department denied the request, citing the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) restriction that limits monument sign heights to 10 feet within the Board of Zoning Appeals 6/25/26 Gateway Corridor Overlay. Although the permit was never approved, the applicant stated that fabrication had already begun and the sign framework is complete at 12 feet. UDO REQUIREMENT: e Per Section 6.5.2 M-4 (Gateway Corridor Overlay) Monument Signs: The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for multi-tenants (more than 3). e Per Article 2-Definitions (Shopping Center): A unified commercial development consisting of four (4) or more retail, service, or professional establishments occupying common or adjacent buildings and having shared access, internal circulation, and parking areas intended to serve all multiple uses of the site. The development shall contain a total gross floor area of 100.000 square feet or greater. (Based on Horry County Land Records, the building is 11,200 square feet) e Per Article 2-Definitions (Sign Height): The vertical distance measured from the average finished grade at the base of the sign to the highest point top of the sign or supporting structure. Where a sign is located on a berm or artificial raised grade, height shall be measured from the average surrounding natural grade. e Per Section 12.1.6 D (Nonconforming Signs & Sign Structures): Nonconforming business or identification signs that do not comply with current standards for size, illumination, location, or number may continue provided that: 1. The sign is not expanded or modified in a manner that increases the degree of nonconformity. 2. Any alteration to the sign shall bring the sign into greater conformity where feasible. 3. No additional nonconforming signage shall be installed. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Section 6.5.2-M (Gateway Corridor Overlay): A variance of 2-ft to allow for a 12-ft multi-tenant monument sign vs the 10-ft allowed by the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to deny the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 6/25/26 Vv. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:46 p.m. Approved and signed this C 4 ‘ day of Jy st , 2026. A iS Kevin Hagen, Zi erson

APPROVAL OF MINUTES Lawson made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the March 26th , minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.2 - Non-Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 209 Waltrip Street. (PIN 383-02-04-0002) Ponder stated that the subject property was originally zoned Production, Service, Industry (PSI). When the City adopted the current UDO on December 12, 2011, all PSI parcels were rezoned to either Light Industrial (LI) or Heavy Industrial (HI). -- 2 of 81 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 4/23/26 2 Under the previous PSI zoning, the required side setback was 15-ft. Following the 2011 rezoning to Heavy Industrial (HI), the required side setback increased significantly to 30-ft. The applicant is currently seeking a permit for a non-residential accessory structure. Per the UDO Section 5.2.1-B, accessory structures must adhere to the setbacks of their primary zoning district. Because the existing primary building was constructed under the old standards and does not meet the current 30-ft HI side setback, placing the new accessory structure in compliance with current code is physically unfeasible. Variance(s) requested: • Section 5.2.1-B (Accessory Structures):  A variance to allow an accessory structure that does not meet the standard 30-foot Heavy Industrial side setback. • Table 6.2 – Non-Residential Zoning Districts:  A 7-foot variance from the required 30-foot side setback, allowing the structure to be placed at a 23-foot setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. STAFF INPUT Wilkerson informed the Board of a proposed amendment for Special Exceptions that is scheduled to come before the BZA. This amendment has already been presented to City Council. It received first reading on April 2 and is scheduled for second reading on May 4. VI. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Currently, the shallowest proposed lot depth in this section is 122.32 ft. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, MAY 28, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Sandra James, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson, Catherine Dingle, Lesley Hill Absent: Donna Baxley Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT. Others: Collins Corbett, Edna Erazo, Brantle M Green, Clint Richardson, BJ & Tony Burkhart, Richard Hogan, Yvette Boyd, Forest Beverly, David Schwerd, Scott Davis, Daniel Ben- Yisrael. I, CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. If. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the April 23, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. Il. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; ° Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 — Landscaping & Buffer Requirements, for the property located at 1818 Main Street. (PIN 338-06-03-0078) Wilkerson stated due to parcel size constraints and to meet the parking requirements for the use, the applicant requests a variance to omit the 5-foot Type A Landscape Buffer along the southern property line 1 Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 where it conflicts with the proposed parking lot. The development will meet all other UDO landscaping requirements. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: « UDO Table 9.2 (Landscaping Rate Chart): Omission of the 5-foot landscape buffer along the southern property line, restricted to the parking lot area only. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 — Landscaping & Buffer Requirements, for the property located at 2776 Church Street. (PIN 337-00-00-0034) Wilkerson stated due to existing asphalt and site constraints, the applicant requests to omit the 5-foot physical buffer strip along the new shared property line, except for the first 30.22 linear feet. In its place, the applicant proposes relocating 100% of the required buffer plantings across both project sites. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: ¢ UDO Table 9.2 (Landscaping Rate Chart): Relief from the 5-foot physical landscape buffer width requirement along the shared property line (with the exception of the first 30.22 linear feet), with a condition to distribute 100% of the required planting units across both subject parcels. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 - Gateway Corridor Overlay and Article 11 - Signage, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN 338-11-04-0052) Wilkerson provided background on the property, noting that it is located at 1600 Church Street (intersection of Church Street and Sixteenth Avenue). She stated that the site is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). The proposal includes the Parker’s Kitchen outparcel development within the redeveloped Coastal Centre. She also noted that the surrounding properties are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). Granting this variance will allow Parker’s Kitchen to provide clear and consistent wayfinding for its customers, enhancing the overall safety and accessibility of the site. The additional signage on the left and right elevation, along with the requested monument sign height and reader board relief, will directly serve the community by ensuring motorists can easily locate and navigate to the property, reducing traffic disruptions and improving customer experience. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Section 6.5.2-M.4.a - Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO)-Signs-Height-Monument Signs: A 3-foot variance to allow two (2) monument signs at a height of 13 feet instead of the permitted 10- feet. e Section 11.4.13-B - Gasoline Pricing Signs-Size: A 4-inch variance to allow 16-inch digital reader board numbers instead of the permitted 12-inches. e Section 11.4.1-A — Walls Signs-Location & Number Permitted: A variance to allow four (4) total wall signs instead of the permitted maximum of two (2) signs. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance for the four (4) Wall Signs as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance for the Gasoline Pricing Signs-Size as presented. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to deny the height requested variance for the two (2) monument signs. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1001 Winding Road. (PIN 339-09-01-0025) Wilkerson stated that the applicant has applied for a building permit proposing the construction of a 33-ft by 12-ft open porch addition to the existing single-family residence. The existing primary structure is classified as legally nonconforming. Per UDO Article 12 (Nonconformities), a structure is deemed legally nonconforming if it was lawfully established prior to the adoption, amendment, or jurisdictional changes of the current ordinance, but no longer complies with current dimensional standards. The home was constructed in 1951, pre-dating the adoption of the current UDO in 2011. Because the existing house does not meet current setbacks, any modern additions require variance relief if they encroach into the current setbacks. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Table 6.1: Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: An 8-foot variance to allow for a 12-ft rear setback to accommodate the proposed open porch. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.3.1— Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards, for the property located at 2393 Church Street. (PIN 337-00-00-0024) Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 Wilkerson stated that the applicant has applied for a building permit proposing the construction of a 7,000 sq ft Metal Building to use as an Automotive Repair Shop (not open to the general public). The applicant cited existing metal buildings on-site. However, these structures sit within unincorporated Horry County jurisdictions, not the City of Conway. Building 2 is a metal structure classified as a “legal nonconforming”. Google Earth imagery shows it has existed since 2008, likely permitted by Horry County prior to city annexation. Building 7 lacks any record of a City of Conway building permit and was also likely established under county jurisdiction. Recent developments on the property—specifically the Commercial Vehicle Center and the new front fagade of Building 1, fully comply with current City of Conway architectural standards. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Section 6.3.1-D (Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards) & Section 5.2.1-B.6 (Non- Residential Accessory Structures): A variance to permit an external metal wall system for a proposed 7,000-square-foot structure, departing from the standard non-residential building material and design requirements. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at Little Bay Drive (Rivertown Row North-Phase 2). (PIN 326-00-00-0048 & 337-04-02-0079) Wilkerson stated that in January 2026, the applicant and the property owners of Rivertown Row North, Phase 1, jointly requested a variance to eliminate the required perimeter landscape buffer, which would otherwise encumber the rear yards of individual parcels. The Board of Zoning Appeals granted the variance for Phase 1 because those homes were already constructed and sold. However, the variance was not granted for Phase 2, as that phase has not yet been subdivided. Board of Zoning Appeals 5/28/26 The R-2 zoning district mandates a minimum lot depth of 120-ft. To prevent the Phase 1 buffer issue from recurring, the applicant seeks a lot depth reduction specifically for Lots 105 through 120 on the western boundary of Phase 2. This variance would allow the required 10-ft landscape buffer to be platted as a separate open space area owned and maintained by the Homeowners Association (HOA), rather than encroaching into private rear yards. Currently, the shallowest proposed lot depth in this section is 122.32 ft. Excluding the 10-ft buffer area from the private lot boundaries reduces the platted lot depth to 112.32 ft, requiring a variance of 7.68 ft from the 120-ft UDO standard. SPECIFIC VARIANCE REQUESTED: e Table 6.1; Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts-Lot Depth: A variance to reduce the minimum required lot depth from 120-ft to 112.32-ft (a 7.68-ft reduction) for Lots 105-120. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Edna Erazo spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:51 p.m. Approved and signed this day o { eed , 2026. Catherine H. Digitally signed by Catherine H. Others: Dr. Daniel Falk, Linda Koretic, Terrie Grout, O’Bryan Martin and Josh Hughes. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the February 26 th , minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Reconsideration of a Previously Denied Variance Request…M. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes, is requesting a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047), previously denied at the November 20, 2025, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) Meeting. -- 2 of 25 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 2 Wilkerson stated that the parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017 (Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E)). At the time of annexation, the application identified the existing structure as "Vacant." Simultaneously, the adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0044) was rezoned to the Institutional (IN) district to facilitate the development of The Wren Coastal Student Living. Civil plans for that project were approved on July 30, 2018. The current leasing office for The Wren was established at 706 Highway 544 without City of Conway approval or a valid City of Conway Business License. The modular structure was occupied without a commercial review, and subsequent additions were constructed without building permits. Under UDO Section 12.1.2 (G), legal nonconforming status is only granted to structures or uses that were "legally in existence prior to annexation." Because the structure was vacant upon annexation, the current commercial use does not qualify for nonconforming protections. Furthermore, UDO Section 9.1.3 (B) mandates that any change in use to a completely different type must comply with the landscaping provisions of Article 9. On March 27, 2025, the Board granted a "use" variance (Section 6.4.3) allowing the office to remain contingent upon the applicant obtaining a business license and meeting all site requirements. While the applicant has achieved signage compliance, the following deficiencies remain: • Unpermitted Structures: A permit for an existing covered porch was denied due to insufficient documentation. The applicant has failed to provide the site plan requested on January 21, 2026. • Site Improvement Deficiencies: The applicant has not submitted the site plan required by Article 12 to secure a business license. Outstanding compliance items include:  Nonconforming buffer yards  Landscaping and screening  Parking standards  Street access compliance While the applicant cites the proposed Coastal Carolina University (CCU) pedestrian bridge as a hardship, the bridge would be located on an adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0048) and does not impact site improvements for The Wren Leasing Office. To achieve compliance, the applicant must submit a platting action to ensure the structure meets required setbacks and the drive-cut is correctly positioned on the subject parcel. This request was previously denied on November 20, 2025. On January 22, 2026, the Board voted unanimously to reconsider the application. -- 3 of 25 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 3 Variance requested: • Section 12.1.4 - Nonconforming Sites: A variance to allow the business to operate without the required site improvements. Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. O’Bryan Martin, agent, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to deny the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements and Table 6.2 – Non-Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1501 Ninth Avenue. (PIN# 338-14-03-0031). Chairperson Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item due to a conflict of interest and did not participate in the decision-making process. The board appointed Kevin Hagen to serve in his place for this item. Wilkerson stated that in 2023, the applicant (Dr. Falk) acquired the adjacent parcel (PIN 338-14-03-0032) and recorded a combination plat (Plat Book 312-319). Both parcels are zoned Professional (P), which permits both residential and commercial uses. The applicant proposes to expand his existing practice by constructing a commercial addition to connect the two existing structures. The completed facility will total 7,444 square feet. Under UDO Table 8.3, a medical/dental office (3,722 sq ft) requires one (1) parking space per 250 sq ft and administrative office (3,722 sq ft) requires one (1) parking space per 300 sq ft totaling 28 required spaces. The applicant currently has or is securing the following parking plan: • On-site: 5 existing spaces. • Leased: 7 spaces on PIN 338-14-03-0022 (Charley Ray). • Shared: 10 proposed spaces on PIN 338-14-03-0021 (Dr. Horowitz) via a shared parking agreement. • Total: 22 spaces (6 spaces short of the 28-space requirement). Additionally, the UDO requires at least 75% of required parking to be located on the same premises for which the primary use is located. -- 4 of 25 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 4 Finally, a review of the sketch plan identified an unpermitted shed on the property. While a 2017 variance allowed a 3.5-ft setback for two smaller sheds, the current larger shed requires the same 3.5-ft setback, a variance of 11.5-ft from the 15-ft corner front setback. Variance(s) requested: • Off-Street Parking (Article 8):  A variance of six (6) spaces to allow for 22 total spaces instead of the required 28.  A variance from the 75% on-site parking requirement to allow for a combination of leased and shared off-site parking. • Setback Requirements (Table 6.2):  An 11.5-ft variance from the 15-ft corner front setback to allow a 3.5-ft setback for an existing shed. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Dr. Daniel Falk was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:32 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2026. ____________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairperson -- 5 of 25 -- Variance: 209 Waltrip Street DATE: April 23, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.2 - Non-Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 209 Waltrip Street. (PIN 383-02-04-0002) BACKGROUND: The subject property was originally zoned Production, Service, Industry (PSI). When the City adopted the current UDO on December 12, 2011, all PSI parcels were rezoned to either Light Industrial (LI) or Heavy Industrial (HI). Under the previous PSI zoning, the required side setback was 15-ft. Following the 2011 rezoning to Heavy Industrial (HI), the required side setback increased significantly to 30-ft. The applicant is currently seeking a permit for a non-residential accessory structure. Per the UDO Section 5.2.1-B, accessory structures must adhere to the setbacks of their primary zoning district. Because the existing primary building was constructed under the old standards and does not meet the current 30-ft HI side setback, placing the new accessory structure in compliance with current code is physically unfeasible. Variance(s) requested: • Section 5.2.1-B (Accessory Structures):  A variance to allow an accessory structure that does not meet the standard 30-foot Heavy Industrial side setback. • Table 6.2 – Non-Residential Zoning Districts:  A 7-foot variance from the required 30-foot side setback, allowing the structure to be placed at a 23-foot setback. The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. -- 6 of 25 -- Variance: 209 Waltrip Street CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 4/23/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, APRIL 23, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Sandra James, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson, Donna Baxley, Catherine Dingle Absent: Lesley Hill Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Louis Smith, IT. Others: Erin Gossett and Jovan Fisher I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. I. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Lawson made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the March 26", minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.2 - Non-Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 209 Waltrip Street. (PIN 383-02-04-0002) Ponder stated that the subject property was originally zoned Production, Service, Industry (PSI). When the City adopted the current UDO on December 12, 2011, all PSI parcels were rezoned to either Light Industrial (LI) or Heavy Industrial (HI). Board of Zoning Appeals 4/23/26 Under the previous PSI zoning, the required side setback was 15-ft. Following the 2011 rezoning to Heavy Industrial (HD), the required side setback increased significantly to 30-ft. The applicant is currently seeking a permit for a non-residential accessory structure. Per the UDO Section 5.2.1-B, accessory structures must adhere to the setbacks of their primary zoning district. Because the existing primary building was constructed under the old standards and does not meet the current 30-ft HI side setback, placing the new accessory structure in compliance with current code is physically unfeasible. Variance(s) requested: e Section 5.2.1-B (Accessory Structures): > A variance to allow an accessory structure that does not meet the standard 30-foot Heavy Industrial side setback. e Table 6.2 — Non-Residential Zoning Districts: » A 7-foot variance from the required 30-foot side setback, allowing the structure to be placed at a 23-foot setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was present. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. STAFF INPUT Wilkerson informed 'the Board of a proposed amendment for Special Exceptions that is scheduled to come before the BZA. This amendment has already been presented to City Council. It received first reading on April 2 and is scheduled for second reading on May 4. Vi. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:40 p.m. : L Approved and signed this Z or day of Wa A , 2026. Paul Lawson,

Others: David Deitz, Jennifer Poindexter, Justin Poindexter, Kim Lafler, and Rondu Jackson I. CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the January 22nd, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Reconsideration of a Previously Denied Variance Request…M. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes, is requesting a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047), previously denied at the November 20, 2025, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) Meeting. DEFERRAL TO MARCH 26, 2026, MEETING REQUESTED BY AGENT. -- 2 of 67 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 2 B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements, for the property located at 1403 Ninth Avenue. (PIN# 338-14-03-0034). Wilkerson stated that the subject parcel is zoned Professional (P) which permits a mic of both commercial and residential uses. Originally constructed in 1895 as a four-room side-gable residence, the structure has a long history of adaptive reuse. It served as a physician’s office for two generations before being relocated to its current site in 1935. Following renovations in the 1930s and 1980s, the building most recently functioned as a single- family dwelling. The applicants, Justin and Jennifer Poindexter, have submitted a commercial sketch plan to transition the property back to commercial use for Poindexter Counseling. Per Table 8.3 of the UDO, “Professional and Business Offices” require one (1) parking space per 300 square feet of gross floor area. Based on the building's square footage, a minimum of ten (10) off-street parking spaces is required. Due to existing lot dimensions and site constraints, the proposed sketch plan provides three (3) parking spaces, including one ADA-compliant stall. Variance requested: Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements: A variance of seven (7) spaces from the required ten (10) spaces, to allow for a total of three (3) on-site parking spaces. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Justin Poindexter and Jennifer Poindexter, the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and applicants discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. Previously Deferred…This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts) for the property located at 2103 Seventh Avenue. (PIN# 368-07-02-0070). Wilkerson stated that the above PIN# is zoned R1 (Low/Medium Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Rear & 10-ft Sides. The applicant purchased the PIN# in February 2025. Based on the deed (DB 4907-1246), this PIN# is two lots of record and references the plat (PB 2-118). The original lot line of record in PB 2-118 ran parallel to Seventh Avenue which would be directly through the existing house. -- 3 of 67 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 3 The applicant is seeking to subdivide the PIN# to build a house on the proposed “Parcel 2” shown on the recent plat that was submitted for review in December 2025. The existing house does not meet the side setback requirement of 10-ft and proposed Parcel 2 does not meet the lot depth requirement of 100-ft. The applicant is seeking the following variances. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: • A variance of 4-ft from the 10-ft side setback requirement for a side setback of 6-ft on Parcel 1. • A variance of 1-ft from the 100-ft lot depth requirement for a lot depth of 99-ft on Parcel 2. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Rondu Jackson, the property owner, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Previously Deferred…A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 – Fences & Walls, for the property located at 905 Hickory Circle. (PIN# 338-14-04-0020). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 905 Hickory Circle, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a corner front on Ninth Avenue and a Double Front on Friendship Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Vinyl Fence in the Double Front Yard and partially in the Corner Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 – Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard and a 6-ft Fence is permitted in the Corner Front Yard, provided it meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. Per Article 2 – Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. A Corner Front Yard is the area “lying between the primary structure and the intersecting street”. -- 4 of 67 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 4 Staff recommends that, should the variance be granted, the 6-ft vinyl fence at Ninth Avenue must comply with the 10-ft setback requirement to maintain the required sight triangle. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 – Fences & Walls: • A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Friendship Street. • A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Corner Front Yard at Ninth Avenue without meeting a 10-ft setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Kim Lafler, the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Altman made a motion to approve the requested variance with the condition that the 10ft setback and 4ft fence on Hickory Circle match the 9th Avenue requirements. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:58 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2026. ____________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairperson -- 5 of 67 -- IV.A 706 HIGHWAY 544 -- 6 of 67 -- Variance: 706 Highway 544 (Wren) DATE: March 26, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: A request for a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047) BACKGROUND: The subject parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017 (Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E)). At the time of annexation, the application identified the existing structure as "Vacant." Simultaneously, the adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0044) was rezoned to the Institutional (IN) district to facilitate the development of The Wren Coastal Student Living. Civil plans for that project were approved on July 30, 2018. COMPLIANCE HISTORY: The current leasing office for The Wren was established at 706 Highway 544 without City of Conway approval or a valid City of Conway Business License. The modular structure was occupied without a commercial review, and subsequent additions were constructed without building permits. Under UDO Section 12.1.2 (G), legal nonconforming status is only granted to structures or uses that were "legally in existence prior to annexation." Because the structure was vacant upon annexation, the current commercial use does not qualify for nonconforming protections. Furthermore, UDO Section 9.1.3 (B) mandates that any change in use to a completely different type must comply with the landscaping provisions of Article 9. CURRENT STATUS: On March 27, 2025, the Board granted a "use" variance (Section 6.4.3) allowing the office to remain contingent upon the applicant obtaining a business license and meeting all site requirements. While the applicant has achieved signage compliance, the following deficiencies remain: • Unpermitted Structures: A permit for an existing covered porch was denied due to insufficient documentation. The applicant has failed to provide the site plan requested on January 21, 2026. • Site Improvement Deficiencies: The applicant has not submitted the site plan required by Article 12 to secure a business license. Outstanding compliance items include:  Nonconforming buffer yards  Landscaping and screening  Parking standards  Street access compliance While the applicant cites the proposed Coastal Carolina University (CCU) pedestrian bridge as a hardship, the bridge would be located on an adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0048) and does not impact site improvements for The Wren Leasing Office. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. -- 8 of 67 -- -- 9 of 67 -- -- 10 of 67 -- -- 11 of 67 -- -- 12 of 67 -- -- 13 of 67 -- -- 14 of 67 -- -- 15 of 67 -- -- 16 of 67 -- -- 17 of 67 -- -- 18 of 67 -- -- 19 of 67 -- -- 20 of 67 -- -- 21 of 67 -- Property Annexed in 2017 and zoned Mixed Use, for Commercial Retail Development January 2019 (Use not a Leasing Office) May 2019 January 2022 -- 22 of 67 -- 706 HIGHWAY 544 – THE WREN LEASING OFFICE TIMELINE:  Oct 2017: Property annexed as "Vacant" and zoned Mixed-Use for a planned residential/retail development.  Dec 2017: Initial project submittal received for Wren Student Housing (Todd Blvd).  July 2018: Site plans approved for The Wren (formerly Hughes Student Housing).  May 2019: The applicant opened an unauthorized modular leasing office. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, MARCH 26, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Sandra James, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson, Donna Baxley Absent: Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner, Louis Smith, IT. Others: Dr. Daniel Falk, Linda Koretic, Terrie Grout, O’Bryan Martin and Josh Hughes. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the February 26", minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. I. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; ¢ Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Reconsideration of a Previously Denied Variance Request...M. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes, is requesting a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047), previously denied at the November 20, 2025, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) Meeting. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 Wilkerson stated that the parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017 (Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E)). At the time of annexation, the application identified the existing structure as "Vacant." Simultaneously, the adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0044) was rezoned to the Institutional (IN) district to facilitate the development of The Wren Coastal Student Living. Civil plans for that project were approved on July 30, 2018. The current leasing office for The Wren was established at 706 Highway 544 without City of Conway approval or a valid City of Conway Business License. The modular structure was occupied without a commercial review, and subsequent additions were constructed without building permits. Under UDO Section 12.1.2 (G), legal nonconforming status is only granted to structures or uses that were "legally in existence prior to annexation." Because the structure was vacant upon annexation, the current commercial use does not qualify for nonconforming protections. Furthermore, UDO Section 9.1.3 (B) mandates that any change in use to a completely different type must comply with the landscaping provisions of Article 9. On March 27, 2025, the Board granted a "use" variance (Section 6.4.3) allowing the office to remain contingent upon the applicant obtaining a business license and meeting all site requirements. While the applicant has achieved signage compliance, the following deficiencies remain: e Unpermitted Structures: A permit for an existing covered porch was denied due to insufficient documentation. The applicant has failed to provide the site plan requested on January 21, 2026. e Site Improvement Deficiencies: The applicant has not submitted the site plan required by Article 12 to secure a business license. Outstanding compliance items include: > Nonconforming buffer yards > Landscaping and screening > Parking standards > Street aceess compliance While the applicant cites the proposed Coastal Carolina University (CCU) pedestrian bridge as a hardship, the bridge would be located on an adjacent parcel (PIN 382-05-04-0048) and does not impact site improvements for The Wren Leasing Office. To achieve compliance, the applicant must submit a platting action to ensure the structure meets required setbacks and the drive-cut is correctly positioned on the subject parcel. This request was previously denied on November 20, 2025. On January 22, 2026, the Board voted unanimously to reconsider the application. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 Variance requested: e Section 12.1.4 - Nonconforming Sites: A variance to allow the business to operate without the required site improvements. Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. O’Bryan Martin, agent, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to deny the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements and Table 6.2 — Non-Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1501 Ninth Avenue. (PIN# 338-14-03-003 1). Chairperson Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item due to a conflict of interest and did not participate in the decision-making process. The board appointed Kevin Hagen to serve in his place for this item. Wilkerson stated that in 2023, the applicant (Dr. Falk) acquired the adjacent parcel (PIN 338-14-03-0032) and recorded a combination plat (Plat Book 312-319). Both parcels are zoned Professional (P), which permits both residential and commercial uses. The applicant proposes to expand his existing practice by constructing a commercial addition to connect the two existing structures. The completed facility will total 7,444 square feet. Under UDO Table 8.3, a medical/dental office (3,722 sq ft) requires one (1) parking space per 250 sq ft and administrative office (3,722 sq ft) requires one (1) parking space per 300 sq ft totaling 28 required spaces. The applicant currently has or is securing the following parking plan: e On-site: 5 existing spaces. e Leased: 7 spaces on PIN 338-14-03-0022 (Charley Ray). e Shared: 10 proposed spaces on PIN 338-14-03-0021 (Dr. Horowitz) via a shared parking agreement. e Total: 22 spaces (6 spaces short of the 28-space requirement). Additionally, the UDO requires at least 75% of required parking to be located on the same premises for which the primary use is located. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/26/26 Finally, a review of the sketch plan identified an unpermitted shed on the property. While a 2017 variance allowed a 3.5-ft setback for two smaller sheds, the current larger shed requires the same 3.5-ft setback, a variance of 11.5-ft from the 15-ft corner front setback. Variance(s) requested: e Off-Street Parking (Article 8): > A variance of six (6) spaces to allow for 22 total spaces instead of the required 28. > A variance from the 75% on-site parking requirement to allow for a combination of leased and shared off-site parking. e Setback Requirements (Table 6.2): > An 11.5-ft variance from the 15-ft corner front setback to allow a 3.5-ft setback for an existing shed. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Dr. Daniel Falk was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:32 p.m. Approved and signed this ZS day of Apa { . 2026.

The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Lawson made a motion to nominate Dingle as Vice Chairperson, seconded by Hagen. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. V. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Beverly Home, agent for the property owners, request a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 – Landscaping, Buffering & Tree Preservation Standards, for several parcels located in the Rivertown Row North Subdivision off Cultra Road. (Beverly Home PIN#’s 326-13-01-0019, 326-13-01-0021, 326-13-01-0023, 326- 13-04-0010, 326-13-03-0010, 326-13-03-0011, 326-13-03-0013, 326-13-02-0052, 326-13-02- 0053, 326-13-02-0054, 326-13-02-0055, 326-13-02-0056, 326-13-02-0057, 326-13-02-0058, 326- 13-02-0059, 326-13-02-0069, 326-13-02-0070, 326-13-04-0011, 326-13-04-0012, 326-13-04- 0013, 326-13-04-0014, 326-13-04-0015, 326-00-00-0048). Wilkerson stated that the plat for Rivertown Row North Phase 1 was approved on December 22, 2022. The lots are zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). At that time, Section 6.5.3 - Village Corridor Overlay (VCO) of the UDO required a side and rear perimeter 25-ft vegetive buffer for new single-family residential (over 5 units) or multi-family developments. The 25-ft Private Vegetative Landscape Buffer was platted as an easement instead of fee-simple to meet the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for the R2 zoning district. Though this buffer was platted, the landscape buffer does not exist. On May 15, 2023, Ordinance ZA2023-05-15 (B) was passed by City Council to eliminate this requirement from the VCO and require developers to adhere to Article 9 – Landscaping and Buffering (now Landscaping, Buffering and Tree Preservation Standards). Table 9.1 – Landscaping Rate Chart requires a Type B Landscape Buffer. This buffer must be a minimum 15-ft in width. While the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer only required that the existing vegetation (including ANY trees) remain undisturbed, the Type B Buffer would require, from Article 9, the installation of two (2) canopy trees, three (3) understory trees and twenty (20) “tall” shrubs per 100 linear feet, as well as irrigation. Requiring this 15-ft buffer would still encumber the property owner’s rear yard since nothing is allowed to be constructed in the 15- buffer, with or without landscaping. If the variance is approved, a plat will be required to eliminate the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer and must be signed by all property owners. -- 3 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 3 • Article 9: A variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer on the individual lots. Also, a variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer from being required in Phase 2 of Rivertown Row North. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott Davis, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Brad Littlefield and Linda Heyser spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve variance request for Phase 1 as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to deny variance request for Phase 2 as presented. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. (Individual Owners PIN#’s 326-13-01-0013, 326-13-01-0018, 326-13-02-0067, 326-13-01-0016, 326-13-01-0015, 326-13-01-0011, 326-13-01-0017). The 25-ft Private Vegetative Landscape Buffer was platted as an easement instead of fee-simple to meet the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for the R2 zoning district. Though this buffer was platted, the landscape buffer does not exist. On May 15, 2023, Ordinance ZA2023-05-15 (B) was passed by City Council to eliminate this requirement from the VCO and require developers to adhere to Article 9 – Landscaping and Buffering (now Landscaping, Buffering and Tree Preservation Standards). Table 9.1 – Landscaping Rate Chart requires a Type B Landscape Buffer. This buffer must be a minimum 15-ft in width. While the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer only required that the existing vegetation (including ANY trees) remain undisturbed, the Type B Buffer would require, from Article 9, the installation of two (2) canopy trees, three (3) understory trees and twenty (20) “tall” shrubs per 100 linear feet, as well as irrigation. Requiring this 15-ft buffer would still encumber the property owner’s rear yard since nothing is allowed to be constructed in the 15- buffer, with or without landscaping. -- 4 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 4 If the variance is approved, a plat will be required to eliminate the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer and must be signed by all property owners. • Article 9: A variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer on the individual lots. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott Davis, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Brad Littlefield and Linda Heyser spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variances for all pin numbers as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 – Fences & Walls, for the property located at 905 Hickory Circle. (PIN# 338-14-04-0020). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 905 Hickory Circle, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a corner front on Ninth Avenue and a Double Front on Friendship Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Vinyl Fence in the Double Front Yard and partially in the Corner Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 – Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard and a 6-ft Fence is permitted in the Corner Front Yard, provided it meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. Per Article 2 – Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. A Corner Front Yard is the area “lying between the primary structure and the intersecting street”. Staff recommends that, should the variance be granted, the 6-ft vinyl fence at Ninth Avenue must comply with the 10-ft setback requirement to maintain the required sight triangle. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 – Fences & Walls: • A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Friendship Street. • A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Corner Front Yard at Ninth Avenue without meeting a 10-ft setback. -- 5 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 5 Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was not present. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Winifred Anderson spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to defer the requested variance to the February 26th meeting. James seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN# 338-11-04-0052). Wilkerson stated that the first full submittal for Parker’s Kitchen was completed and comments returned. One of the comments was regarding the parking count. The applicant is seeking a variance to increase the number of parking spaces allowed for the use. Per Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements, the “use” would fall under “Service Establishments”. The proposed building is 5,204 square feet, which based on Table 8.3, would allow a maximum parking count of 28 parking spaces. The applicant is seeking a variance to allow for 38 parking spaces. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 8.3 – Parking Requirements: • A variance to allow for a maximum parking count of 38 parking spaces vs the 28 parking spaces allowed per the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Daniel Ben-Yisrael and Patrick Monaghan, agents for the property owner, were present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the variance request as presented. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6 – Design Standards for three (3) lots being created in Elmhurst Subdivision; Phase VI. (PIN# 338-00-00-0036). -- 6 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 6 Wilkerson stated that the final plat for Elmhurst Phase 4C was approved on March 16, 2021. Upon layout of Elmhurst Phase 6, adjacent to Phase 4C, it was determined by Diamond Shores, that the ROW line shown on PB 298-28 was approximately 19-feet from its actual location. As a result of this error in 2021, the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for parcels zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential) cannot be met for Lots 148, 149 and 150. The applicant is seeking a variance on the lot depth requirement for these three lots to properly shift Dandy Lane, which runs parallel to Medlen Parkway. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: • A variance to allow a lot depth for Lots 148, 149 & 150 from 120-ft to ranges of 100-ft to 119.9- ft. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. David Schwerd, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. James made a motion to approve the variance request as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts) for the property located at 2103 Seventh Avenue. (PIN# 368-07-02-0070). Wilkerson stated that the above PIN# is zoned R1 (Low/Medium Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Rear & 10-ft Sides. The applicant purchased the PIN# in February 2025. Based on the deed (DB 4907-1246), this PIN# is two lots of record and references the plat (PB 2-118). The original lot line of record in PB 2-118 ran parallel to Seventh Avenue which would be directly through the existing house. The applicant is seeking to subdivide the PIN# to build a house on the proposed “Parcel 2” shown on the recent plat that was submitted for review in December 2025. The existing house does not meet the side setback requirement of 10-ft and proposed Parcel 2 does not meet the lot depth requirement of 100-ft. The applicant is seeking the following variances. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: -- 7 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 7 • A variance of 4-ft from the 10-ft side setback requirement for a side setback of 6-ft on Parcel 1. • A variance of 1-ft from the 100-ft lot depth requirement for a lot depth of 99-ft on Parcel 2. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Rondu Jackson, the property owner, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Daniel Grice, Alberta Bellamy, and Gloria Lance spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to defer the requested variance to the February 26th meeting. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3–Fences & Walls, for the property located at 1804 Brown St. (PIN# 368-02-01-0058). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 1804 Brown Street, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a Double Front on Rhue Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Privacy Fence in the Double Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 – Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard. Per Article 2 – Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 – Fences & Walls: A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Rhue Street. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Jamilah Swinton, property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request as presented, with a minimum setback of 20 feet from Rhue Street. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. H. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development -- 8 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 8 Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay, for the property located at 2050 Highway 501 East and 2451 Highway 501 East. (PIN# 383-00-00-0377, 383-00-00-0132, 383- 11-03-0004). Wilkerson stated that Horry Georgetown Technical College is seeking a variance on three (3) monument signs for the following locations: • PIN# 383-00-00-0377 (2050 Hwy 501 East) – Main Campus • PIN# 383-00-00-0132 (No Address) – Parking & Lineman Yard • PIN# 383-11-03-0004 (2451 Hwy 501 E) – Beside Ekklesia Christian Church The first two parcels are zoned Institutional (IN) and the third is zoned Planned Development (PD). All three parcels are in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), Monument Signs shall be a maximum of sixty (60) square feet, and the maximum height shall be ten (10) feet. Section 6.5.2 furthers states, “a property that contains more than one road frontage shall be permitted an additional monument sign. This additional monument sign shall not front the Gateway Corridor and shall meet the requirements in Section 11.4.6”. The applicant is seeking a variance to install three (3) signs that are 149.2-sq ft sign area and is 8.5-ft in height but proposed to set upon a landscape berm that is 2-ft in height. Per Article 2-Definitions, Sign Height: “The vertical distance measured from the lowest adjacent street crown grade to the top of the sign face or sign structure, whichever is greater.” This would make the sign height 10.5-ft. Per Article 2-Definitions, Monument Sign: “A sign in which the entire bottom of the sign face is in contact with a solid and continuous structure which is attached to the ground and made of brick, stone, or other material architecturally compatible with the principal building on the lot with which it pertains.” Based on the definitions of Article 2, PIN# 383-00-00-0132 does not have a principal building and therefore has no address which would prevent a Monument Sign on this parcel. Also based on Article 2, a 2-ft berm does not meet the definition for a Monument Sign. The applicants are requesting the following variances: • Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs: A 1/2-ft variance on the height of the sign to allow for an 8.5-ft sign (without the 2-ft berm). An 89.2-sq ft variance on the area of the sign to allow for an 149.2 sq ft sign. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Derrick Mozingo, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. -- 9 of 87 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 9 The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. -- 13 of 87 -- -- 14 of 87 -- -- 15 of 87 -- -- 16 of 87 -- -- 17 of 87 -- -- 18 of 87 -- -- 19 of 87 -- -- 20 of 87 -- -- 21 of 87 -- -- 22 of 87 -- -- 23 of 87 -- -- 24 of 87 -- -- 25 of 87 -- -- 26 of 87 -- -- 27 of 87 -- PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT 196 Laurel Street  Post Office Box 1075 Conway, South Carolina 29528-1075 Telephone (843) 488-9888 www.ConwaySC.gov MAYOR Barbara Jo Blain MAYOR PRO TEM William M. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1.
