title: APPD-BZA MINUTES 2.26.26
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 26, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Sandra James, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman, Catherine Dingle Absent: Paul Lawson, Donna Baxley Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator, Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Charlie Crosby, IT. Others: David Deitz, Jennifer Poindexter, Justin Poindexter, Kim Lafler, and Rondu Jackson I. CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. JI. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the January 22nd, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. IN. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Reconsideration of a Previously Denied Variance Request...M. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes, is requesting a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544, (PIN 382-05-04-0047), previously denied at the November 20, 2025, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) Meeting, DEFERRAL TO MARCH 26, 2026, MEETING REQUESTED BY AGENT. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 B. A variance request from the strict application of the City.of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements, for the property located at 1403 Ninth Avenue. (PIN# 338-14-03-0034). Wilkerson stated that the subject parcel is zoned Professional (P) which permits a mic of both commercial and residential uses. Originally constructed in 1895 as a four-room side-gable residence, the structure has a long history of adaptive reuse. It served as a physician’s office for two generations before being relocated to its current site in 1935. Following renovations in the 1930s and 1980s, the building most recently functioned as a single- family dwelling. The applicants, Justin and Jennifer Poindexter, have submitted a commercial sketch plan to transition the property back to commercial use for Poindexter Counseling. Per Table 8.3 of the UDO, “Professional and Business Offices” require one (1) parking space per 300 square feet of gross floor area. Based on the building's square footage, a minimum of ten (10) off-street parking spaces is required. Due to existing lot dimensions and site constraints, the proposed sketch plan provides three (3) parking spaces, including one ADA-compliant stall. Variance requested: Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements: A variance of seven (7) spaces from the required ten (10) spaces, to allow for a total of three (3) on-site parking spaces. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Justin Poindexter and Jennifer Poindexter, the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and applicants discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. Previously Deferred...This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts) for the property located at 2103 Seventh Avenue. (PIN# 368-07-02-0070). Wilkerson stated that the above PIN# is zoned R1 (Low/Medium Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Rear & 10-ft Sides. The applicant purchased the PIN# in February 2025. Based on the deed (DB 4907-1246), this PIN# is two lots of record and references the plat (PB 2-118). The original lot line of record in PB 2-118 ran parallel to Seventh Avenue which would be directly through the existing house. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 The applicant is seeking to subdivide the PIN# to build a house on the proposed “Parcel 2” shown on the recent plat that was submitted for review in December 2025. The existing house does not meet the side setback requirement of 10-ft and proposed Parcel 2 does not meet the lot depth requirement of 100-ft. The applicant is seeking the following variances. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: e A variance of 4-ft from the 10-ft side setback requirement for a side setback of 6-ft on Parcel 1. e A variance of 1-ft from the 100-ft lot depth requirement for a lot depth of 99-ft on Parcel 2. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Rondu Jackson, the property owner, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Previously Deferred...A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls, for the property located at 905 Hickory Circle. (PIN# 338-14-04-0020). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 905 Hickory Circle, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a corner front on Ninth Avenue and a Double Front on Friendship Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Vinyl Fence in the Double Front Yard and partially in the Corner Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 — Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard and a 6-ft Fence is permitted in the Corner Front Yard, provided it meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. Per Article 2 — Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. A Corner Front Yard is the area “lying between the primary structure and the intersecting street”. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/26/26 Staff recommends that, should the variance be granted, the 6-ft vinyl fence at Ninth Avenue must comply with the 10-ft setback requirement to maintain the required sight triangle. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls: e Avariance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Friendship Street. e A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Corner Front Yard at Ninth Avenue without meeting a 10-ft setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Kim Lafler, the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Altman made a motion to approve the requested variance with the condition that the 10ft setback and 4ft fence on Hickory Circle match the 9th Avenue requirements. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:58 p.m. Approved and signed this Z 6 day of Mad. , 2026. \ Paul i Nssod Facile erson

(PIN# 383-00-00-0377, 383-00-00-0132, 383-11-03-0004) BACKGROUND: Horry Georgetown Technical College is seeking a variance on three (3) monument signs for the following locations: • PIN# 383-00-00-0377 (2050 Hwy 501 East) – Main Campus • PIN# 383-00-00-0132 (No Address) – Parking & Lineman Yard • PIN# 383-11-03-0004 (2451 Hwy 501 E) – Beside Ekklesia Christian Church The first two parcels are zoned Institutional (IN) and the third is zoned Planned Development (PD). All three parcels are in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), Monument Signs shall be a maximum of sixty (60) square feet, and the maximum height shall be ten (10) feet. Section 6.5.2 furthers states, “a property that contains more than one road frontage shall be permitted an additional monument sign. This additional monument sign shall not front the Gateway Corridor and shall meet the requirements in Section 11.4.6”. The applicant is seeking a variance to install three (3) signs that are 149.2-sq ft sign area and is 8.5-ft in height but proposed to set upon a landscape berm that is 2-ft in height. Per Article 2-Definitions, Sign Height: “The vertical distance measured from the lowest adjacent street crown grade to the top of the sign face or sign structure, whichever is greater.” This would make the sign height 10.5-ft. Per Article 2-Definitions, Monument Sign: “A sign in which the entire bottom of the sign face is in contact with a solid and continuous structure which is attached to the ground and made of brick, stone, or other material architecturally compatible with the principal building on the lot with which it pertains.” Based on the definitions of Article 2, PIN# 383-00-00-0132 does not have a principal building and therefore has no address which would prevent a Monument Sign on this parcel. Also based on Article 2, a 2-ft berm does not meet the definition for a Monument Sign. The applicants are requesting the following variances: • Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs: A 1/2-ft variance on the height of the sign to allow for an 8.5-ft sign (without the 2-ft berm). An 89.2-sq ft variance on the area of the sign to allow for an 149.2 sq ft sign. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, JANUARY 22, 2026 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Sandra James, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson Absent: Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT. Others: Daniel Grice, Rondu Jackson, Ken Jennison, Dan Phillips, Brad Littlefield, Peter DeLuca, Patrick Monaghan, Jamilah Swinton, Jeff Keller, Cathy Noteware, Josh Hughes, Alberta Bellamy, Sharon Miller, Frank Miller, David Schwerd, Marilyn Fore, Scott Davis, Gloria Lance, Derrick Mozingo, Daniel Ben-Yisrael, Winifred Anderson, Linda Heyser and others. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Hl, ELECTION OF OFFICERS James made a motion to nominate Lawson to serve as Chairperson, seconded by Hill. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Lawson made a motion to nominate Dingle as Vice Chairperson, seconded by Hagen. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. TI. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hagen made a motion to reconsider Variance Request Item A for property owner PQ, located at 706 Highway 544, from the November 20, 2025 meeting, to be heard at the February 26, 2026 meeting. Lawson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Hill made a motion to approve the November 20, 2025 minutes as written, with the noted change regarding the reconsideration of the variance request. James seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. IV. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; © Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e¢ Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. V. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Beverly Home, agent for the property owners, request a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 — Landscaping, Buffering & Tree Preservation Standards, for several parcels located in the Rivertown Row North Subdivision off Cultra Road. (Beverly Home PIN#’s 326-13-01-0019, 326-13-01-0021, 326-13-01-0023, 326- 13-04-0010, 326-13-03-0010, 326-13-03-0011, 326-13-03-0013, 326-13-02-0052, 326-13-02- 0053, 326-13-02-0054, 326-13-02-0055, 326-13-02-0056, 326-13-02-0057, 326- 13-02-0058, 326- 13-02-0059, 326-13-02-0069, 326-13-02-0070, 326-13-04-0011, 326-13-04-0012, 326-13-04- 0013, 326-13-04-0014, 326-13-04-0015, 326-00-00-0048). Wilkerson stated that the plat for Rivertown Row North Phase 1 was approved on December 22, 2022. The lots are zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). At that time, Section 6.5.3 - Village Corridor Overlay (VCO) of the UDO required a side and rear perimeter 25-ft vegetive buffer for new single-family residential (over 5 units) or multi-family developments. The 25-ft Private Vegetative Landscape Buffer was platted as an easement instead of fee-simple to meet the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for the R2 zoning district. Though this buffer was platted, the landscape buffer does not exist. On May 15, 2023, Ordinance ZA2023-05-15 (B) was passed by City Council to eliminate this requirement from the VCO and require developers to adhere to Article 9 — Landscaping and Buffering (now Landscaping, Buffering and Tree Preservation Standards). Table 9.1 —- Landscaping Rate Chart requires a Type B Landscape Buffer. This buffer must be a minimum 15-ft in width. While the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer only required that the existing vegetation (including ANY trees) remain undisturbed, the Type B Buffer would require, from Article 9, the installation of two (2) canopy trees, three (3) understory trees and twenty (20) “tall” shrubs per 100 linear feet, as well as irrigation. Requiring this 15-ft buffer would still encumber the property owner’s rear yard since nothing is allowed to be constructed in the 15- buffer, with or without landscaping. If the variance is approved, a plat will be required to eliminate the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer and must be signed by all property owners. Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 e Article 9: A variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer on the individual lots. Also, a variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer from being required in Phase 2 of Rivertown Row North. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott Davis, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Brad Littlefield and Linda Heyser spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve variance request for Phase | as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to deny variance request for Phase 2 as presented. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9 — Landscaping, Buffering & Tree Preservation Standards, for several parcels located in the Rivertown Row North Subdivision off Cultra Road. (Individual Owners PIN#’s 326-13-01-0013, 326-13-01-0018, 326-13-02-0067, 326-13-01-0016, 326-13-01-0015, 326-13-01-0011, 326-13-01-0017). Wilkerson stated that the plat for Rivertown Row North Phase 1 was approved on December 22, 2022. The lots are zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). At that time, Section 6.5.3 - Village Corridor Overlay (VCO) of the UDO required a side and rear perimeter 25-ft vegetive buffer for new single-family residential (over 5 units) or multi-family developments. The 25-ft Private Vegetative Landscape Buffer was platted as an easement instead of fee-simple to meet the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for the R2 zoning district. Though this buffer was platted, the landscape buffer does not exist. On May 15, 2023, Ordinance ZA2023-05-15 (B) was passed by City Council to eliminate this requirement from the VCO and require developers to adhere to Article 9 — Landscaping and Buffering (now Landscaping, Buffering and Tree Preservation Standards). Table 9.1 — Landscaping Rate Chart requires a Type B Landscape Buffer. This buffer must be a minimum 15-ft in width. While the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer only required that the existing vegetation (including ANY trees) remain undisturbed, the Type B Buffer would require, from Article 9, the installation of two (2) canopy trees, three (3) understory trees and twenty (20) “tall” shrubs per 100 linear feet, as well as irrigation. Requiring this 15-ft buffer would still encumber the property owner’s rear yard since nothing is allowed to be constructed in the 15- buffer, with or without landscaping. Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 If the variance is approved, a plat will be required to eliminate the 25-ft Private Vegetative Buffer and must be signed by all property owners. e Article 9: A variance to eliminate the requirement for a perimeter landscape buffer on the individual lots. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott Davis, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Brad Littlefield and Linda Heyser spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variances for all pin numbers as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls, for the property located at 905 Hickory Circle. (PIN# 338-14-04-0020). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 905 Hickory Circle, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a corner front on Ninth Avenue and a Double Front on Friendship Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Vinyl Fence in the Double Front Yard and partially in the Corner Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 — Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard and a 6-ft Fence is permitted in the Corner Front Yard, provided it meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. Per Article 2 — Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”, A Corner Front Yard is the area “lying between the primary structure and the intersecting street”. Staff recommends that, should the variance be granted, the 6-ft vinyl fence at Ninth Avenue must comply with the 10-ft setback requirement to maintain the required sight triangle. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls: e A variance to allow a 6-ft Viny! Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Friendship Street. e A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Corner Front Yard at Ninth Avenue without meeting a 10-ft setback. Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Applicant was not present. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Winifred Anderson spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to defer the requested variance to the February 26" meeting. James seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN# 338-1 1-04-0052). Wilkerson stated that the first full submittal for Parker’s Kitchen was completed and comments returned. One of the comments was regarding the parking count. The applicant is seeking a variance to increase the number of parking spaces allowed for the use. Per Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements, the “use” would fall under “Service Establishments”. The proposed building is 5,204 square feet, which based on Table 8.3, would allow a maximum parking count of 28 parking spaces. The applicant is seeking a variance to allow for 38 parking spaces. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 8.3 — Parking Requirements: e A variance to allow for a maximum parking count of 38 parking spaces vs the 28 parking spaces allowed per the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Daniel Ben-Yisrael and Patrick Monaghan, agents for the property owner, were present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Hill made a motion to approve the variance request as presented. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6 — Design Standards for three (3) lots being created in Elmhurst Subdivision; Phase VI. (PIN# 338-00-00-0036). Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 Wilkerson stated that the final plat for Elmhurst Phase 4C was approved on March 16, 2021. Upon layout of Elmhurst Phase 6, adjacent to Phase 4C, it was determined by Diamond Shores, that the ROW line shown on PB 298-28 was approximately 19-feet from its actual location. As a result of this error in 2021, the lot depth requirement of 120-ft for parcels zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential) cannot be met for Lots 148, 149 and 150. The applicant is seeking a variance on the lot depth requirement for these three lots to properly shift Dandy Lane, which runs parallel to Medlen Parkway. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: e A variance to allow a lot depth for Lots 148, 149 & 150 from 120-ft to ranges of 100-ft to 119.9- ft. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. David Schwerd, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. James made a motion to approve the variance request as presented. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. This variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts) for the property located at 2103 Seventh Avenue. (PIN# 368-07-02-0070). Wilkerson stated that the above PIN# is zoned R1 (Low/Medium Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Rear & 10-ft Sides. The applicant purchased the PIN# in February 2025. Based on the deed (DB 4907-1246), this PIN# is two lots of record and references the plat (PB 2-118). The original lot line of record in PB 2-118 ran parallel to Seventh Avenue which would be directly through the existing house. The applicant is seeking to subdivide the PIN# to build a house on the proposed “Parcel 2” shown on the recent plat that was submitted for review in December 2025. The existing house does not meet the side setback requirement of 10-ft and proposed Parcel 2 does not meet the lot depth requirement of 100-ft. The applicant is seeking the following variances. Variances requested (per site plan): Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 e A variance of 4-ft from the 10-ft side setback requirement for a side setback of 6-ft on Parcel 1. e A variance of 1-ft from the 100-ft lot depth requirement for a lot depth of 99-ft on Parcel 2. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Rondu Jackson, the property owner, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Daniel Grice, Alberta Bellamy, and Gloria Lance spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to defer the requested variance to the February 26" meeting. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls, for the property located at 1804 Brown St. (PIN# 368-02-01-0058). Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located at 1804 Brown Street, is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential). This parcel has a Double Front on Rhue Street. The applicant is seeking a variance to install a 6-ft Privacy Fence in the Double Front Yard. The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Per Section 5.2.3 — Fences and Walls, a 4-ft Fence only is permitted in the Double Front Yard. Per Article 2 — Definitions, a Double Front Yard is “a space extending across the full width of the lot between the rear of the principal building and the adjacent street”. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls: A variance to allow a 6-ft Vinyl Fence to be installed in the Double Front Yard at Rhue Street. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Jamilah Swinton, property owners, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request as presented, with a minimum setback of 20 feet from Rhue Street. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. H. A variance request from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development 7 Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay, for the property located at 2050 Highway 501 East and 2451 Highway 501 East. (PIN# 383-00-00-0377, 383-00-00-0132, 383- 11-03-0004). Wilkerson stated that Horry Georgetown Technical College is seeking a variance on three (3) monument signs for the following locations: e PIN# 383-00-00-0377 (2050 Hwy 501 East) — Main Campus e PIN# 383-00-00-0132 (No Address) — Parking & Lineman Yard e PIN# 383-11-03-0004 (2451 Hwy 501 E) — Beside Ekklesia Christian Church The first two parcels are zoned Institutional (IN) and the third is zoned Planned Development (PD). All three parcels are in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), Monument Signs shall be a maximum of sixty (60) square feet, and the maximum height shall be ten (10) feet. Section 6.5.2 furthers states, “a property that contains more than one road frontage shall be permitted an additional monument sign. This additional monument sign shall not front the Gateway Corridor and shall meet the requirements in Section 11.4.6”. The applicant is seeking a variance to install three (3) signs that are 149.2-sq ft sign area and is 8.5-ft in height but proposed to set upon a landscape berm that is 2-ft in height. Per Article 2-Definitions, Sign Height: “The vertical distance measured from the lowest adjacent street crown grade to the top of the sign face or sign structure, whichever is greater.” This would make the sign height 10.5-ft. Per Article 2-Definitions, Monument Sign: “A sign in which the entire bottom of the sign face is in contact with a solid and continuous structure which is attached to the ground and made of brick, stone, or other material architecturally compatible with the principal building on the lot with which it pertains.” Based on the definitions of Article 2, PIN# 383-00-00-0132 does not have a principal building and therefore has no address which would prevent a Monument Sign on this parcel. Also based on Article 2, a 2-ft berm does not meet the definition for a Monument Sign. The applicants are requesting the following variances: e Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs: A 1/2-ft variance on the height of the sign to allow for an 8.5-ft sign (without the 2-ft berm). An 89.2-sq ft variance on the area of the sign to allow for an 149.2 sq ft sign. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Derrick Mozingo, agent for the property owners, was present to answer any questions. Board of Zoning Appeals 1/22/26 The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion to table the variance request for the Parking and Lineman yard, PIN 383-00-00- 0132, until such time as additional information is available. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Hill made a motion to approve the requested variance for PIN 383-00-00-0377 (2050 Hwy 501 East — Main Campus) and 383-11-03-0004 (2451 Hwy 501 East — beside Ekklesia Christian Church), as presented. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. VI. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 7:17 p.m. Approved and signed this Ale day of __/ Z Dry ar) _, 2026. ADJOURN -- 1 of 25 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 10/23/25 1 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, October 23, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Paul Lawson, Sandra James Absent: Andy Altman, Lesley Hill, Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Charlie Crosby, IT Others: Roxanne Kwiatek I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the September 25th, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Roxanne Kwiatek, the property owner, request a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1–Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1216 Dunraven Court. (PIN 369-06-03- 0009). -- 2 of 25 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 10/23/25 2 Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located in the New Castle subdivision, is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 10-ft Sides and 20-ft Rear. The applicant applied for a permit to add an addition to the existing single-family home. Unlike accessory structures, additions to existing homes must meet the setbacks for the zoning district. Upon review of the site plan, it was determined that the proposed addition encroaches into the side setback. Therefore, the permit cannot be approved by Planning, and the applicant is requesting the following variance: • Table 6.1: A 3.5-ft variance to allow a side setback of 6.5-ft (instead of 10-ft) in order to add an addition to the existing home. Roxanne Kwiatek, the property owner, was present to answer any questions. The board discussed the request at length. No public input. Lawson made a motion, seconded by Hagen to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to deny the requested variance, citing that the request did not meet the criteria for an extraordinary condition. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:41 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2025. ____________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairperson -- 3 of 25 -- IV.A 706 HIGHWAY 544 -- 4 of 25 -- Variance: 706 Highway 544 (Wren) DATE: November 20, 2025 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: A request for a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047) BACKGROUND: The above parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017 per Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E). At that time, the applicants requested the Mixed Use (MU) zoning district in order to support residential housing built over retail commercial use. PIN 382-05-04-0044 was annexed and rezoned at the same time to the City of Conway Institutional (IN) zoning district to accommodate student housing. The civil plan set for the student housing project was approved on July 30, 2018 for what is now The Wren Coastal Student Living. The leasing office for The Wren, located at 706 Highway 544, was established without approval from the City of Conway and therefore, has never received a City of Conway Business License. The modular structure was opened as a Leasing Office (with no commercial review), unpermitted signs installed and additions added to the structure with no building permits issued. On March 27, 2025, the applicant requested a “use” variance “to allow the continued operation of a leasing and property management office on the subject property, which is currently zoned as mixed use. Strict enforcement of zoning restrictions prohibiting this use would impose an undue hardship of the property owner by forcing the closure of a legitimate and necessary business”. The “use” variance was granted on March 27, 2025 and the motion was stated as follows: “A variance from the requirements of Section 6.4.3 of the UDO, allowing a single commercial use to remain operating on this parcel with the condition that the business obtains a City of Conway Business License as well as all necessary permits and conditions required by the City of Conway”. The only progress the applicant has made to come into compliance is two sign permits. Staff has never received a site plan illustrating the necessary improvements as required by the UDO to obtain a City of Conway Business License. Per Article 12 of the UDO, the following site improvements are required: • Nonconforming Buffer Yard • Nonconforming Landscaping and Screening • Nonconforming Parking • Nonconforming Street Access Furthermore, the applicant had an A-frame porch built onto the front of the modular structure without a building permit. The Building Official has stated that a building permit is required. -- 5 of 25 -- Variance: 706 Highway 544 (Wren) Variance requested: • Section 12.1.4 - Nonconforming Sites: A variance to allow the business to operate without the currently required site improvements at this time. The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. -- 6 of 25 -- -- 7 of 25 -- -- 8 of 25 -- PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT 196 Laurel Street  Post Office Box 1075 Conway, South Carolina 29528-1075 Telephone (843) 488-9888 www.ConwaySC.gov MAYOR Barbara Jo Blain MAYOR PRO TEM William M. (PIN 382-05-04-0047) Dear Applicant(s): After consideration of the evidence and arguments presented at the March 27, 2025 meeting, the Board made the following findings of fact and conclusions: 1. Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. -- 9 of 25 -- 196 Laurel Street  Post Office Box 1075 Conway, South Carolina 29528-1075 Telephone (843) 488-9888 www.ConwaySC.gov THE BOARD, THEREFORE, ORDERED the request for a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU) and Section 4.2-Use Tables, for the property located at 706 Highway 544 was granted as follows: • Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU): A variance from the requirements of Section 6.4.3 of the UDO, allowing a single commercial use to remain operating on this parcel with the condition that the business obtains a City of Conway Business License as well as all necessary permits and conditions required by the City of Conway. • Article 4-Use Tables: A variance from the “conditions” required from the Use Table (found in Section 6.4.3). title: APPD-BZA MINUTES 11.20.25
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 11/20/25 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, November 20, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Sandra James, Lesley Hill, Catherine Dingle Absent: Andy Altman, Paul Lawson, Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Darlene Acevedo, Planning & Development Assistant; Marcus Cohen, IT Others: None I. CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:32 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the October 23rd, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. IIL. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; ¢ Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. M. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes, is requesting a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1 - Nonconformities, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047). Board of Zoning Appeals 11/20/25 Wilkerson stated that the parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017 per Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E). At that time, the applicants requested the Mixed Use (MU) zoning district in order to support residential housing built over retail commercial use. PIN 382-05-04-0044 was annexed and rezoned at the same time to the City of Conway Institutional (IN) zoning district to accommodate student housing. The civil plan set for the student housing project was approved on July 30, 2018 for what is now The Wren Coastal Student Living. The leasing office for The Wren, located at 706 Highway 544, was established without approval from the City of Conway and therefore, has never received a City of Conway Business License. The modular structure was opened as a Leasing Office (with no commercial review), unpermitted signs installed and additions added to the structure with no building permits issued. On March 27, 2025, the applicant requested a “use” variance “to allow the continued operation of a leasing and property management office on the subject property, which is currently zoned as mixed use. Strict enforcement of zoning restrictions prohibiting this use would impose an undue hardship of the property owner by forcing the closure of a legitimate and necessary business”. The “use” variance was granted on March 27, 2025 and the motion was stated as follows: “A variance from the requirements of Section 6.4.3 of the UDO, allowing a single commercial use to remain operating on this parcel with the condition that the business obtains a City of Conway Business License as well as all necessary permits and conditions required by the City of Conway”. The only progress the applicant has made to come into compliance is two sign permits. Staff has never received a site plan illustrating the necessary improvements as required by the UDO to obtain a City of Conway Business License. Per Article 12 of the UDO, the following site improvements are required: ¢ Nonconforming Buffer Yard e Nonconforming Landscaping and Screening e Nonconforming Parking e Nonconforming Street Access Furthermore, the applicant had an A-frame porch built onto the front of the modular structure without a building permit. The Building Official has stated that a building permit is required. Variance requested: « Section 12.1.4 - Nonconforming Sites: A variance to allow the business to operate without the currently required site improvements at this time. Staff recommends denial of this variance request. The owner’s repeated disregard for zoning requirements undermines the intent of the ordinance and would set a precedent that compliance is optional. Furthermore, staff believes the request does not satisfy the required findings for a variance and is not in the best interest of the City of Conway. Board of Zoning Appeals 11/20/25 Applicant was not present. The board and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. James made a motion to deny the requested variance, citing that the request did not meet the criteria for an extraordinary condition. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. 2026 BZA MEETING SCHEDULE James made a motion to approve the 2026 meeting schedule, seconded by Hagen. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. VI. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:42 p.m. Approved and signed this Ll, of <== ee > \\ a) P. awson, Qhairperson

ADJOURN -- 1 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 1 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 25, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Lesley Hill, Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson Absent: Sandra James Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Louis Smith, IT Others: Daniel Ben-Yisrael, David Schwerd, Robert Collins, Paul Scheuer, Christopher Sacawa, Jim Clemons, Tyler Thomas, Jay Sellers, Khrystal Suggs, Jon Grzwa and others. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the August 28th, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: x Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; x Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; x Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; x Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Joshua Cox with Foresite Group LLC, agent for the property owner, RP Coastal Center, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.6.2 – Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN 338-11-04-0052). -- 2 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 2 Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located on the corner of Church Street and Sixteenth Avenue, is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is located in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). This parcel is part of the Coastal Centre redevelopment and is proposed to be a Parker’s Kitchen. Upon sketch review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), staff made the comment that the Dumpster Facility must be located in the rear or side yards per Section 6.6.2-Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling as well as Section 6.3.5 B-1-Highway Commercial (HC). Due to the multiple frontages and the need for underground storage tanks, the applicants are requesting the following variance: x Section 6.6.2: “All mechanical equipment (including HVAC units, generators and other mechanical equipment) and trash handling facilities shall be located on the same lot as the use served unless shared facilities are approved. The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street.” x Section 6.3.5: “Electrical boxes, communication equipment and all other mechanical or utility equipment shall be located on the side or rear of the building and not visible on the front façade. All refuse storage areas shall be located to the rear or side yard of the property and screened with a finished exterior surface.” Per the UDO, all ground level mechanical equipment and trash-handling facilities must be completely screened from the public right-of-way and adjacent properties. Section 6.6.2 also gives staff the ability to require additional screening through the use of landscaping: “Appropriate screening includes: A wall OR opaque fence (excluding chain-link), a minimum of six (6) feet in height and constructed of materials approved by TRC. Shrubs, earth berm, and/or understory trees may be required in conjunction with a fence/wall to further obscure such facilities.” All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Daniel Ben-Yisrael, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, was present and further explained the request. The board discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Altman seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Sellers General Construction, the property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.6.2 – Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling, for the property located at Westridge Blvd. (337-13-03- 0056). -- 3 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 3 Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential) and the applicants are proposing an In-Common Development. The UDO defines an In-Common Development as “A development where any mix of single-family homes, multifamily, duplex or townhome developments are located on commonly owned property and ownership of the land is collectively held by all owners of the dwelling units and governed by a property regime.” Upon sketch review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), staff made the comment that the Dumpster Facility must be located in the rear or side yards per Section 6.6.2-Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling. Section 6.6.2: “All mechanical equipment (including HVAC units, generators and other mechanical equipment) and trash handling facilities shall be located on the same lot as the use served unless shared facilities are approved. The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street.” The Sanitation Director is requiring a Dumpster Facility instead of individual roll carts since the turnaround of the Sanitation Truck would be impossible. Per the UDO, all ground level mechanical equipment and trash-handling facilities must be completely screened from the public right-of-way and adjacent properties. Section 6.6.2 also gives staff the ability to require additional screening through the use of landscaping: “Appropriate screening includes: A wall OR opaque fence (excluding chain-link), a minimum of six (6) feet in height and constructed of materials approved by TRC. Shrubs, earth berm, and/or understory trees may be required in conjunction with a fence/wall to further obscure such facilities.” Due to the lot size and configuration, the applicants are requesting the following variance: x Section 6.6.2: A variance to allow the Double Dumpster Facility to be located in the front yard, along Westridge Boulevard. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Dingle. Tyler Thomas, agent for Sellers General Construction, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. James Clemens, the property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.1 – Accessory Structures, for the -- 4 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 4 property located at 910 Pine Street. (PIN 338-14-02-0042). Wilkerson stated that the parcel is located on the corner of Pine Street and Ninth Avenue, is zoned R1 (Low- Medium Density Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Corner Front, 10-ft Side and 20-ft Rear. After being issued a “Stop Work Order” by Construction Services, the applicant submitted a permit application for a 24-ft x 20-ft Detached Garage. Upon review of the site plan, staff made the applicant aware that Detached Garages are permitted in the rear or the side yards only per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures. Section 5.2.1(A-1): “Location: Shall be located in the rear yard only. Detached garages and garden structures may also be located in the side yard.” Upon a site visit by staff, it was determined that the parcel is almost fully screened from Tenth Avenue with an undisturbed landscape buffer. The placement of the Detached Garage was based on the existing cement slab. The structure meets the setbacks for the zoning district of 20-ft Front and 20-ft Corner Front. Due to the parcel being a corner lot and the existing cement slab, the applicant is requesting the following variance: x Section 5.2.1: A variance to allow the Detached Garage to be located in the corner front yard instead of the side or rear yards. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. James Clemens, property owner, was present and further explained the request. Khrystal Suggs spoke during public input. Hagen made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Diamond Shores LLC, agent for property owner, Alfronso Sangtian, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located on Technology Boulevard. (PIN 383-10-03-0020). Catherine Dingle recused herself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R3 (High Density Residential) and construction plans are currently in review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) for the expansion of University Suites at Coastal. The initial submittal was received on July 7, 2025 and on July 21, 2025, City Council approved a revision to the Residential Dimensional Requirements for In-Common Developments. -- 5 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 5 The setbacks for the R3 zoning district are 15-ft Front, 20-ft Rear and 5-ft Sides; however, the revision approved for In-Common Developments created a required 25-ft building setback from all exterior boundaries. Table 6.1 - Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, footnote #5 states “Single-family detached, Duplex, Townhome and Multi-family in-common developments are permitted in the R-2 and R-3 districts. In such developments, a 25-ft building setback shall be required, from all exterior project boundaries”. Upon review of the plans, staff made the applicant aware that a 25-ft building setback shall be required from all exterior project boundaries. Due to the project being fully designed prior to the new setbacks receiving approval from City Council, the applicant is requesting the following variances: x Table 6.1: A 5-ft variance from the rear setback to allow for a 20-ft rear setback and a 10-ft variance from the left side setback to allow for a 15-ft left side setback. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. David Schwerd, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. Theresa Snow with Ware Malcomb, agent for property owner, Santi Jimongkonkul, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.2 – Non-Residential Zoning Districts and Table 9.1 – Required Landscaping Type, for the property located at 748 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0046). Wilkerson stated that the applicants discussed with city staff the plan to develop half of the above PIN# and build a Scooter’s Coffee. The parcel is serviced by City of Conway Water as well as being contiguous to property within the City of Conway. Annexation and rezoning to City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district was approved by City Council on August 4, 2025. Once the parcel was annexed, the applicants submitted a subdivision plat. Without subdividing, the entire parcel would have to come into compliance with the new commercial project. A minor subdivision plat was submitted for review. The minor plat met all of the requirements for a parcel zoned HC with the exception of the Existing Building on Parcel B. The setbacks for the HC zoning district are 30-ft Front, 20- ft Rear and 15-ft Sides. The Existing Building is 12.9-ft from the proposed property line. -- 6 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 6 The commercial plans were reviewed by the City’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) concurrently with the minor plat. Staff made the following comment upon review of the commercial plans: Type A Landscape Buffer (against the proposed new property line) does not meet the landscape requirements of 5-ft width & included per 100 linear feet: x 2 understory trees: 1-in caliper & 6 to 8-ft in height at time of planting; x 18 shrubs: 1.5-ft in height & 3-gallon min. at time of planting. The applicant is requesting the following variances: x Table 6.2 - Non-Residential Zoning Districts: A 2.3-ft variance from the proposed property line to allow for a 12.9 side setback instead of the required 15-ft side setback. x Table 9.1 – Required Landscaping Type: A 5-ft variance from the required 5-ft landscape buffer to eliminate landscaping against the proposed property line. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Jon Grzwa, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the setback variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to table the variance request to allow the applicant additional time to work with staff on a solution for the landscape buffer. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. Joshua Cox with Foresite Group, LLC, agent for property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 9.8 – Tree Preservation, for the property located at 3500 West Highway 501. (PIN 326-09-03-0008). Wilkerson stated that an appeal has been requested regarding the strict application of Section 9.8 – Tree Preservation of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), pertaining to the property located at 3500 West Highway 501 (PIN 326-09-03-0008). On February 18, 2025, City Council approved an ordinance to redirect appeals of the Conway Tree Board from City Council to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). In December 2024, the applicant submitted a request to prune a 36-inch Landmark Live Oak Tree. The applicant stated the pruning was needed due to overhead powerlines. Based on the approved plans for -- 7 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 7 Parker’s Kitchen, the request was denied as staff was unable to find where the tree would interfere with the powerlines as depicted on the plans. Parker’s Kitchen then appealed staff’s decision to the City of Conway Tree Board. The meeting was held on Wednesday, January 8, 2025. The real estate development manager for Parkers Kitchen as well as an agent for Horry Electric were both present at the meeting. A motion was made and carried unanimously stating “Require a certified arborist to submit a pruning plan to staff prior to the issuance of the pruning permit and the commencement of pruning activities. The plan should explain the process being used, ensure that the pruning practices adhere to ANSI A300 standards, and confirm that the practices will not be detrimental to the tree. A mitigation penalty will be imposed if the pruning is not conducted according to the approved plan.” Staff never received the pruning plan that was requested by the Tree Board and on February 4, Horry Electric trimmed the tree with no approvals from the City. Staff met an ISA Certified Arborist on site and based on her inspection, she concluded “this live oak was not pruned according to ANSI A300 Standards for proper pruning techniques”. Due to Horry Electric’s actions, the property owner was assessed a penalty. The penalty assessed being appealed to the Board of Zoning Appeals. x Mitigation Penalty: Plant a total of 27 canopy trees at a minimum of 4-inch caliper or pay a fee-in- lieu of $22,950, or a combination of the two. Because the penalty would hold up the Certificate of Occupancy (CO), Parker’s Kitchen planted 10 of the 27 trees which left a penalty of $14,450. Staff has the check from Parker’s Kitchen; however, per Section 9.8.16-Appeals of the UDO, they are appealing the penalty since the pruning/trimming of the 36-inch Landmark Live Oak Tree was done by a third party and not contracted or hired by Parker’s Kitchen. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Daniel Ben-Yisrael, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. After considerable discussion and in recognition of the property owner’s circumstances, including their limited involvement in the pruning of the tree and their prompt mitigation efforts through the planting of ten replacement trees, Lawson made a motion to remove the mitigation fee. The motion was contingent upon the property owner’s acknowledgment that, should the tree die in the future, the Tree Board will revisit the matter as it pertains to this specific tree. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. Paul Scheuer with Image360 Myrtle Beach, agent for property owner, Conway Hospital Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), -- 8 of 19 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 8 Section 11.4.6 – Monument Signs, for the property located at 300 Singleton Ridge Road. (PIN 383-00- 00-0317). Wilkerson stated that a variance has been requested from the strict application of Section 11.4.6 – Monument Signs of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), concerning the property located at 300 Singleton Ridge Road (PIN 383-00-00-0317). The current Conway Medical Center monument sign located on the corner of Highway 501 and Singleton Ridge Road is being removed because of the Highway 501 widening project. The applicants would like to relocate the sign to the hospital entrance at Myrtle Trace Road. The sign is considered “Nonconforming” based on its current location because it is an offsite sign. The parcel at 300 Singleton Ridge Road is zoned Institutional (IN) and per Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs, the maximum height shall be 8-ft and the maximum area shall be 40-sq ft. The existing sign is 13-ft tall with an area of 221-sq ft. The applicants are requesting the following variances: Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs: x A 5-ft variance on the height of the sign to allow for a 13-ft sign. x A 181-sq ft variance on the area of the sign to allow for a 221-sq ft sign. Paul Scheuer with Image360 Myrtle Beach, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Christopher Sacawa spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 7:00 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2025. ____________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairperson -- 9 of 19 -- /s͘ ϭϮϭϲhEZsEKhZd -- 10 of 19 -- Variance: 1216 Dunraven Court DATE: October 23, 2025 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: A request for a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 – Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1216 Dunraven Court. (PIN 369-06-03-0009) BACKGROUND: The parcel, located in the New Castle subdivision, is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 10-ft Sides and 20-ft Rear. The applicant applied for a permit to add an addition to the existing single- family home. Unlike accessory structures, additions to existing homes must meet the setbacks for the zoning district. Upon review of the site plan, it was determined that the proposed addition encroaches into the side setback. Therefore, the permit cannot be approved by Planning, and the applicant is requesting the following variance: x Table 6.1: A 3.5-ft variance to allow a side setback of 6.5-ft (instead of 10-ft) in order to add an addition to the existing home. The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. -- 11 of 19 -- Variance: 1216 Dunraven Court CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R (Low-Medium Density Residential) and was annexed into the City of Conway on May 15, 2023, per Ordinance ZA2023-05-15(E). The applicant has since applied for the fence/wall permit and included a letter from an engineer stating the fence/wall meets minimum requirements of the IRC (International Residential Code); however, the height does not meet the requirements of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). Though the parcel is odd in shape, the UDO states that the “Front Yard” is “a space extending the full width of the lot between any building and the front lot line.” Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the UDO limits Front Yard fences/walls to 4-ft in height. The owner of the property is requesting the following variance: • Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls: A variance of 2-ft in order to allow the 6-ft fence/wall in the front yard.
