title: APPD-BZA MINUTES 9.25.25
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 25, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Lesley Hill, Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson Absent: Sandra James Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Louis Smith, IT Others: Daniel Ben-Yisrael, David Schwerd, Robert Collins, Paul Scheuer, Christopher Sacawa, Jim Clemons, Tyler Thomas, Jay Sellers, Khrystal Suggs, Jon Grzwa and others. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the August 28th, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous, and the motion carried. Il. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE/APPEAL REQUEST(S) A. Joshua Cox with Foresite Group LLC, agent for the property owner, RP Coastal Center, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.6.2 — Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling, for the property located at 1600 Church Street. (PIN 338-11-04-0052). Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 Wilkerson stated that the parcel, located on the corner of Church Street and Sixteenth Avenue, is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is located in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). This parcel is part of the Coastal Centre redevelopment and is proposed to be a Parker’s Kitchen. Upon sketch review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), staff made the comment that the Dumpster Facility must be located in the rear or side yards per Section 6.6.2-Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling as well as Section 6.3.5 B-1-Highway Commercial (HC). Due to the multiple frontages and the need for underground storage tanks, the applicants are requesting the following variance: e Section 6.6.2: “All mechanical equipment (including HVAC units, generators and other mechanical equipment) and trash handling facilities shall be located on the same lot as the use served unless shared facilities are approved. The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street.” e Section 6.3.5: “Electrical boxes, communication equipment and all other mechanical or utility equipment shall be located on the side or rear of the building and not visible on the front fagade. All refuse storage areas shall be located to the rear or side yard of the property and screened with a finished exterior surface.” Per the UDO, all ground level mechanical equipment and trash-handling facilities must be completely screened from the public right-of-way and adjacent properties. Section 6.6.2 also gives staff the ability to require additional screening through the use of landscaping: “Appropriate screening includes: A wall OR opaque fence (excluding chain-link), a minimum of six (6) feet in height and constructed of materials approved by TRC. Shrubs, earth berm, and/or understory trees may be required in conjunction with a fence/wall to further obscure such facilities.” All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Daniel Ben-Yisrael, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, was present and further explained the request. The board discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Altman seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously, B. Sellers General Construction, the property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.6.2 — Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling and Trash Handling, for the property located at Westridge Blvd. (337-13-03- 0056). Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R2 (Medium Density Residential) and the applicants are proposing an In-Common Development. The UDO defines an In-Common Development as “A development where any mix of single-family homes, multifamily, duplex or townhome developments are located on commonly owned property and ownership of the land is collectively held by all owners of the dwelling units and governed by a property regime.” Upon sketch review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), staff made the comment that the Dumpster Facility must be located in the rear or side yards per Section 6.6.2-Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling. Section 6.6.2: “All mechanical equipment (including HVAC units, generators and other mechanical equipment) and trash handling facilities shall be located on the same lot as the use served unless shared facilities are approved. The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street.” The Sanitation Director is requiring a Dumpster Facility instead of individual roll carts since the turnaround of the Sanitation Truck would be impossible. Per the UDO, all ground level mechanical equipment and trash-handling facilities must be completely screened from the public right-of-way and adjacent properties. Section 6.6.2 also gives staff the ability to require additional screening through the use of landscaping: “Appropriate screening includes: A wall OR opaque fence (excluding chain-link), a minimum of six (6) feet in height and constructed of materials approved by TRC. Shrubs, earth berm, and/or understory trees may be required in conjunction with a fence/wall to further obscure such facilities.” Due to the lot size and configuration, the applicants are requesting the following variance: © Section 6.6.2: A variance to allow the Double Dumpster Facility to be located in the front yard, along Westridge Boulevard. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Dingle. Tyler Thomas, agent for Sellers General Construction, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. James Clemens, the property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.1 — Accessory Structures, for the Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 property located at 910 Pine Street. (PIN 338-14-02-0042). Wilkerson stated that the parcel is located on the corner of Pine Street and Ninth Avenue, is zoned R1 (Low- Medium Density Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Corner Front, 10-ft Side and 20-ft Rear. After being issued a “Stop Work Order” by Construction Services, the applicant submitted a permit application for a 24-ft x 20-ft Detached Garage. Upon review of the site plan, staff made the applicant aware that Detached Garages are permitted in the rear or the side yards only per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures. Section 5.2.1(A-1): “Location: Shall be located in the rear yard only. Detached garages and garden structures may also be located in the side yard.” Upon a site visit by staff, it was determined that the parcel is almost fully screened from Tenth Avenue with an undisturbed landscape buffer. The placement of the Detached Garage was based on the existing cement slab. The structure meets the setbacks for the zoning district of 20-ft Front and 20-ft Corner Front. Due to the parcel being a corner lot and the existing cement slab, the applicant is requesting the following variance: e Section 5.2.1: A variance to allow the Detached Garage to be located in the corner front yard instead of the side or rear yards. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. James Clemens, property owner, was present and further explained the request. Khrystal Suggs spoke during public input. Hagen made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously D. Diamond Shores LLC, agent for property owner, Alfronso Sangtian, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1 — Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located on Technology Boulevard. (PIN 383-10-03-0020). Catherine Dingle recused herself from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R3 (High Density Residential) and construction plans are currently in review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) for the expansion of University Suites at Coastal. The initial submittal was received on July 7, 2025 and on July 21, 2025, City Council approved a revision to the Residential Dimensional Requirements for In-Common Developments. Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 The setbacks for the R3 zoning district are 15-ft Front, 20-ft Rear and 5-ft Sides; however, the revision approved for In-Common Developments created a required 25-ft building setback from all exterior boundaries. Table 6.1 - Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, footnote #5 states “Single-family detached, Duplex, Townhome and Multi-family in-common developments are permitted in the R-2 and R-3 districts. In such developments, a 25-ft building setback shall be required, from all exterior project boundaries”. Upon review of the plans, staff made the applicant aware that a 25-ft building setback shall be required from all exterior project boundaries. Due to the project being fully designed prior to the new setbacks receiving approval from City Council, the applicant is requesting the following variances: e Table 6.1: A 5-ft variance from the rear setback to allow for a 20-ft rear setback and a 10-ft variance from the left side setback to allow for a 15-ft left side setback. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. David Schwerd, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. Theresa Snow with Ware Malcomb, agent for property owner, Santi Jimongkonkul, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.2 — Non-Residential Zoning Districts and Table 9.1 — Required Landscaping Type, for the property located at 748 Highway 544, (PIN 382-05-04-0046). Wilkerson stated that the applicants discussed with city staff the plan to develop half of the above PIN# and build a Scooter’s Coffee. The parcel is serviced by City of Conway Water as well as being contiguous to property within the City of Conway. Annexation and rezoning to City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district was approved by City Council on August 4, 2025. Once the parcel was annexed, the applicants submitted a subdivision plat. Without subdividing, the entire parcel would have to come into compliance with the new commercial project. A minor subdivision plat was submitted for review. The minor plat met all of the requirements for a parcel zoned HC with the exception of the Existing Building on Parcel B. The setbacks for the HC zoning district are 30-ft Front, 20- ft Rear and 15-ft Sides. The Existing Building is 12.9-ft from the proposed property line. Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 The commercial plans were reviewed by the City’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) concurrently with the minor plat. Staff made the following comment upon review of the commercial plans: Type A Landscape Buffer (against the proposed new property line) does not meet the landscape requirements of 5-ft width & included per 100 linear feet: e 2understory trees: 1-in caliper & 6 to 8-ft in height at time of planting; e 18 shrubs: 1.5-ft in height & 3-gallon min. at time of planting. The applicant is requesting the following variances: e Table 6.2 - Non-Residential Zoning Districts: A 2.3-ft variance from the proposed property line to allow for a 12.9 side setback instead of the required 15-ft side setback. e Table 9.] — Required Landscaping Type: A 5-ft variance from the required 5-ft landscape buffer to eliminate landscaping against the proposed property line. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Jon Grzwa, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Dingle made a motion to approve the setback variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to table the variance request to allow the applicant additional time to work with staff on a solution for the landscape buffer. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. F. Joshua Cox with Foresite Group, LLC, agent for property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 9.8 — Tree Preservation, for the property located at 3500 West Highway 501. (PIN 326-09-03-0008). Wilkerson stated that an appeal has been requested regarding the strict application of Section 9.8 — Tree Preservation of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), pertaining to the property located at 3500 West Highway 501 (PIN 326-09-03-0008). On February 18, 2025, City Council approved an ordinance to redirect appeals of the Conway Tree Board from City Council to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). In December 2024, the applicant submitted a request to prune a 36-inch Landmark Live Oak Tree. The applicant stated the pruning was needed due to overhead powerlines. Based on the approved plans for Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 Parker’s Kitchen, the request was denied as staff was unable to find where the tree would interfere with the powerlines as depicted on the plans. Parker’s Kitchen then appealed staff's decision to the City of Conway Tree Board. The meeting was held on Wednesday, January 8, 2025. The real estate development manager for Parkers Kitchen as well as an agent for Horry Electric were both present at the meeting. A motion was made and carried unanimously stating “Require a certified arborist to submit a pruning plan to staff prior to the issuance of the pruning permit and the commencement of pruning activities. The plan should explain the process being used, ensure that the pruning practices adhere to ANSI A300 standards, and confirm that the practices will not be detrimental to the tree. A mitigation penalty will be imposed if the pruning is not conducted according to the approved plan.” Staff never received the pruning plan that was requested by the Tree Board and on February 4, Horry Electric trimmed the tree with no approvals from the City. Staff met an ISA Certified Arborist on site and based on her inspection, she concluded “this live oak was not pruned according to ANSI A300 Standards for proper pruning techniques”. Due to Horry Electric’s actions, the property owner was assessed a penalty. The penalty assessed being appealed to the Board of Zoning Appeals. ¢ Mitigation Penalty: Plant a total of 27 canopy trees at a minimum of 4-inch caliper or pay a fee-in- lieu of $22,950, or a combination of the two. Because the penalty would hold up the Certificate of Occupancy (CO), Parker’s Kitchen planted 10 of the 27 trees which left a penalty of $14,450. Staff has the check from Parker’s Kitchen; however, per Section 9.8.16-Appeals of the UDO, they are appealing the penalty since the pruning/trimming of the 36-inch Landmark Live Oak Tree was done by a third party and not contracted or hired by Parker’s Kitchen. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Daniel Ben-Yisrael, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. After considerable discussion and in recognition of the property owner’s circumstances, including their limited involvement in the pruning of the tree and their prompt mitigation efforts through the planting of ten replacement trees, Lawson made a motion to remove the mitigation fee. The motion was contingent upon the property owner’s acknowledgment that, should the tree die in the future, the Tree Board will revisit the matter as it pertains to this specific tree. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. Paul Scheuer with Image360 Myrtle Beach, agent for property owner, Conway Hospital Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), 7 Board of Zoning Appeals 9/25/25 Section 11.4.6 —- Monument Signs, for the property located at 300 Singleton Ridge Road. (PIN 383-00- 00-0317). Wilkerson stated that a variance has been requested from the strict application of Section 11.4.6 — Monument Signs of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), concerning the property located at 300 Singleton Ridge Road (PIN 383-00-00-0317). The current Conway Medical Center monument sign located on the corner of Highway 501 and Singleton Ridge Road is being removed because of the Highway 501 widening project. The applicants would like to relocate the sign to the hospital entrance at Myrtle Trace Road. The sign is considered “Nonconforming” based on its current location because it is an offsite sign. The parcel at 300 Singleton Ridge Road is zoned Institutional (IN) and per Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs, the maximum height shall be 8-ft and the maximum area shall be 40-sq ft. The existing sign is 13-ft tall with an area of 221-sq ft. The applicants are requesting the following variances: Section 11.4.6-Monument Signs: e A 5-ft variance on the height of the sign to allow for a 13-ft sign. e A 181-sq ft variance on the area of the sign to allow for a 221-sq ft sign. Paul Scheuer with Image360 Myrtle Beach, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Christopher Sacawa spoke during public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 7:00 p.m. Approved and signed this day of __( » , 2025. A Paul \Lawson, Chairperson ~ }

CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hagen made a motion, seconded by Altman to approve the May 22nd and June 26th , 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE REQUEST(S) A. Benny R. Pigg Jr, agent for the property owner, Ramos Marta Romos, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1- Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1009 Live Oak Street. (PIN 368-01-03-0065) -- 2 of 75 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 7/24/25 2 Wilkerson stated that Benny R Pigg Jr., agent for the property owner request a variance from the strict application of the city of Conway’s UDO table 6.1 dimensional requirements for residential zoning districts for the property located at 109 Live Oak Street. The parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) and is located on the corner of Live Oak Street and Bayside Avenue; therefore, having a double front. The setbacks for the R1 zoning district are 20-ft Front (Live Oak Street), 20-ft Corner Front (Bayside Avenue), 20-ft Rear and 10-ft Side. The contractor applied for a permit (PB25-0317) to install a front and rear covered porch. The one-story house is already “Legal Nonconforming” since it does not meet the current setbacks for the zoning district. Rooftop vents, used for ventilation purposes, may be exempt from these requirements at the recommendation of TRC. G. Access Management All properties within this corridor shall meet the requirements of the City of Conway’s access management standards in Section 7.2.1. 1. Inter-parcel Access. Provide inter-parcel vehicle access points between all contiguous non-residential properties. A system of joint use driveways and cross access easements shall be used to promote connectivity in the GCO. This requirement may be waived by the TRC only if it is demonstrated that an inter-parcel connection is not feasible due to traffic safety, topographic, or environmental concerns. 2. Shared Access Points. Shared access points should be located along a common property boundary. The first thirty (30’) feet of a driveway shall be paved with impervious or pervious surfaces including concrete pavers or similar materials. The TRC shall approve the paving surface of the first thirty (30’) feet. 3. Where shared access or service driveways occur, an access agreement shall be required by the City of Conway. The agreement must be signed by all affected property owners and must be registered with the Horry County Register of Deeds. H. Connectivity 1. Pedestrian/Bike Access. Pedestrian and bicycle access must be provided to individual developments and each establishment within the development. Pedestrian walkways must be designed and located in a manner that does not require pedestrians to walk through parking lots or cross driveways. 2. Pedestrian Walkways. Pedestrian walkways, a minimum of five (5) feet in width, must be clearly defined and provide a direct connection from the street to the main entrance, and to abutting properties. 3. Trails. If a parcel is located within five hundred (500) feet of a proposed pathway/bike trail, a minimum eight (8’) feet wide trail connection shall be provided. 4. Sidewalks. Sidewalks shall be installed on all public streets the parcel(s) abuts or match existing sidewalk. Sidewalks shall meet the design requirements in Article 7. 5. Bicycle Lanes. Bicycle lanes shall meet the street design requirements in Article 7. I. Utilities All new utility lines (electric, telephone, CATV, etc.) shall be placed underground. All junction and access boxes shall be screened with sufficient vegetation so as to completely obscure it from view. All utility pad features and meters should be shown on the development site plan. J. Landscaping and Buffer Requirements 1. Non-Residential Front Buffers. a. Parking Lots up to 30,000 square feet: The front buffer for commercial and office establishments shall be ten (10’) feet along corridor rights-of-way, both public and private. This buffer is intended for aesthetics, rather than screening purposes. The buffer shall contain the following minimum ornamental plantings per one hundred (100) linear feet of frontage: i. Two (2) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. ii. Two (2) understory trees six (6) --eight (8) feet height minimum. iii. Eighteen (18) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. -- 71 of 75 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-44 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 b. Parking Lots over 30,000 square feet: The front buffer for non-residential establishments shall be fifteen (15’) feet along corridor rights-of-way, both public and private. This buffer is intended for aesthetics, rather than screening purposes. The buffer shall contain the following minimum ornamental plantings per one hundred (100) linear feet of frontage: i. Three (3) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. ii. Three (3) understory trees six (6) – eight (8) feet height minimum. iii. Twenty (20) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. 2. Non-Residential Side and Rear Buffers. Side and rear buffers shall meet the requirements set forth in Article 9. 3. Residential Front Buffers. A fifty (50’) feet buffer shall be provided along the frontage of any new single-family residential development (over five new units) or multi-family development across the street from any use or zoning other than single-family residential. The fifty (50) feet front buffer shall contain the following minimum planting per one hundred (100) linear feet when existing vegetation is not sufficient: a. Eight (8) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. b. Twelve (12) understory trees six (6) – eight (8) feet minimum c. Fifty (50) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. 4. Residential Side and Rear Buffers. Side and rear buffers shall meet the requirements set forth in Article 9. 5. Required Screening for Loading Zones. Structures shall be oriented so that loading areas are in no manner visible from residential districts, from existing public or private rights-of-way, or from planned future public rights-of-way. Loading areas may be oriented toward adjoining developed properties, which are commercially zoned, or toward adjoining properties eligible for future commercial development if and only if they are entirely screened from view by the use of solid fencing or appropriate landscaping. 6. Dumpster screens. Garbage dumpsters shall be screened and buffered with an eight (8) foot high opaque fence or walls on four (4) sides. Dumpster screens shall be reviewed by the TRC. 7. Fencing materials. Chain linked fencing (with and without barbed wire) in the GCO shall be prohibited. K. Site Design and Parking 1. Up to twenty-five percent (25%) of the required parking spaces for any development may be reduced in total area, width, or depth for designated compact vehicle parking. Each compact vehicle parking space shall not be less than eight-feet (8’) in width and seventeen-feet (17’) in depth. L. Height Requirements 1. Building height shall be limited to fifty (50) feet above base floor elevations, with the following exception: a. Parcels zoned Highway Commercial in the GCO along Highway 501 between Lake Busbee and Carolina Forest Blvd. shall be limited to sixty-five (65) feet above base floor elevations. b. Multifamily developments on parcels zoned High-Density Residential (R-3) shall be limited to sixty-five (65) feet above base floor elevations, subject to applicable fire codes. M. Signs Off premise signs, portable signs, and temporary signs shall be prohibited within the GCO corridor. Monument and freestanding post signs are the only freestanding signs allowed in the GCO. Signs in the GCO shall be as permitted in Article 11 of this Unified Development Ordinance, except that compliance with the following regulations shall be required. -- 72 of 75 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-45 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 1. Materials. All signs shall be compatible with the architectural design of associated building, including colors and materials. 2. Setback. All monument and freestanding post signs shall meet the setback requirements in Section 11.1.7. 3. Size. a. Monument Signs: The maximum sign face area shall be sixty (60) square feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign face area shall be eighty (80) square feet for multi-tenants (more than three) except in Shopping Centers as referenced in Section 11.4.17. [amended 8-15-16 ZA3201508-15(A)] b. Freestanding Post Signs: The maximum sign-face area shall be sixty (60) square feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign face area shall be eighty (80) square feet for multi-tenants (more than three) except in Shopping Centers as referenced in Section 11.4.17. [Amended ZA2016-08-15(A)] 4. Height. a. Monument Signs: The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for multi-tenants (more than three). b. Freestanding Post Signs: The maximum sign height shall be sixteen (16) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be twenty (20) feet for multi-tenants (more than three (3) businesses). 5. Location. A property that contains more than one road frontage shall be permitted an additional monument sign. This additional monument sign shall not front the gateway corridor and shall meet the requirements in Section 11.4.6. 6. Incentive. For any monument sign request, the TRC can consider reducing the street yard and sign landscaping requirements. -- 73 of 75 -- 1065 Pitch Landing Rd Elevations will be available at the BZA Meeting on 8.28.25 for the board to view. -- 74 of 75 -- Deadline Meeting Date December 23, 2024 January 23, 2025 January 28, 2025 February 27, 2025 February 25, 2025 March 27, 2025 March 25, 2025 April 24, 2025 April 22, 2025 May 22, 2025 May 27, 2025 June 26, 2025 June 24, 2025 July 24, 2025 July 29, 2025 August 28, 2025 August 26, 2025 September 25, 2025 September 23, 2025 October 23, 2025 October 21, 2025 November 20, 2025 November 10, 2025 December 10, 2025 December 23, 2025 January 22, 2026 CITY OF CONWAY 2025 Board of Zoning Appeals - 5:30 pm **December 10, 2025 meeting falls on a Wednesday** -- 75 of 75 --

text: Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, AUGUST 28, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Lesley Hill, Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Andy Altman, Paul Lawson Absent: Sandra James Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Jessica Hucks, Planning & Development Director; Anne Bessant, Planning Coordinator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Marcus Cohen, IT Others: Rob Shelton, Lindsey Fleming, Rachel Fleming, Ryan Gengo, Stephen Grengo, Vonna Grengo, Nancy McMillan, Gen Sellers, Jay Sellers, Tyler Thomas, Eric Curtis, Shawn Butler, Larry Ruby, Mike Battle & others I, CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Altman to approve the July 24, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. If. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; « Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; e Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE REQUEST(S) A. Jay Sellers, property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls, for the property located 1 Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 at 216 Buchanan Lane. (PIN 324-16-01-0005) Paul Lawson and Catherine Dingle, both recused themselves from this agenda item. Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R (Low-Medium Density Residential) and was annexed into the City of Conway on May 15, 2023, per Ordinance ZA2023-05-15(E). After annexation, the property owner built a 6-ft fence/wall in order to help with drainage and keep the runoff from the adjacent property. The 6-ft fence/wall was erected without a permit. The applicant has since applied for the fence/wall permit and included a letter from an engineer stating the fence/wall meets minimum requiréments of the IRC (International Residential Code); however, the height does not meet the requirements of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). Though the parcel is odd in shape, the UDO states that the “Front Yard” is “a space extending the full width of the lot between any building and the front lot line.” Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the UDO limits Front Yard fences/walls to 4-ft in height. The owner of the property is requesting the following variance: e Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls: A variance of 2-ft in order to allow the 6-ft fence/wall in the front yard. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship only if it makes and documents, in writing, findings that satisfy all four required criteria. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Hagen. Mike Battle, agent for property owners, was present and further explained the request. Rob Shelton, Ryan Gengo, Nancy McMillan, and Jay Sellers spoke during public input. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Altman seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Eric Curtis, agent for the property owner, Serenity Point Recovery LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2 — Accessory Uses & Structures, for the property located at 2121 Oak Street. (338-06-01-0004) Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) and is currently the home of Serenity Point Recovery. Mr. Curtis would like to install a 10-ft x 20-ft “Accessory Structure” on the parcel. The parcel is triangular in shape with a ROW on two (2) sides (Elm Street & Oak Street) creating a double front parcel. Per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Accessory Structures shall be located in the rear yard only, with the exception of detached garages and garden structures. Also, in the rear yard, the “Accessory Structure” only has to meet a 5-ft setback from the property line. In the side yard, the setback from the zoning district must be met. The setbacks for the R1 zoning district are 20-ft Front, 10-ft Sides and 20-ft Rear. Based on the plat attached, the “Accessory Structure” will be approximately 13.25-ft from the property line at Elm Street. Staff feels if the variance is granted, that a 20-ft setback from Elm Street would be a safer alternative. The owner of the property is requesting the following variance: © Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structure: A variance to allow an Accessory Structure to be located in one of two front yards (Elm Street). According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship only if it makes and documents, in writing, findings that satisfy all four required criteria. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Eric Curtis, agent for the property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested with the condition the accessory structure meets a required 20-foot front setback from Elm Street. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. Shawn Gregory Butler, property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2.3 — Fences & Walls, for the property located at 1501 Oconee Avenue. (PIN 338-14-01-0018) Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 Wilkerson stated that the parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) with setbacks of 20-ft Front, 20-ft Corner Front, 20-ft Rear and 10-ft Sides. Mr. Butler’s property is situated on the corner of Oconee Avenue and Church Street creating a corner front. He has applied for a fence permit to install a 6-ft Privacy Fence along Church Street. Per Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), a 6-ft privacy fence may be installed in the corner front provided a 10-ft setback from the property line is met. The property owner is proposing a 4-ft setback from the property line at Church Street for the 6-ft fence. The owner of the property is requesting the following variance: e Section 5.2.1-Fences & Walls: A 6-ft variance to allow a 6-ft privacy fence to be installed 4-ft from the corner front property line (along Church Street). According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship only if it makes and documents, in writing, findings that satisfy all four required criteria. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Lawson. Shawn Butler, property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Larry Ruby spoke during public input. Dingle made a motion to grant the variance as requested with the condition it remains out of the site triangle. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Douglas W. and Rose E. Hardwick, property owners, request a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 5.2 — Accessory Uses & Structures, for the property located at 3015 Jasmine Drive. (PIN 368-10-04-0039) Wilkerson stated that the property owners have applied for an “Accessory Structure Permit” to install a 26- ft x 26-ft metal building with 8-ft overhangs and wrapped in vinyl on their property at 3015 Jasmine Drive. The rear of the applicant’s house is adjacent to New Road which is considered a “Double Front”. Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 Per Section 6.1.9 of the UDO: “In the case of any lot that adjoins two or more streets, yards abutting streets shall be treated as front yards.” The applicant’s lot is considered “Legal Nonconforming” since it is a nonconforming lot of record. Double Front lots are not allowed to be created per the current UDO. Table 9.1 of the UDO states: “Residential developments containing lots with double frontage shall adhere to the Type B Landscape Buffer Requirements, or install a berm, as specified in Section 9.3.1, J. Buffer / berm must be located behind the lots that would otherwise have double frontage and be platted separately as a landscape buffer / berm, to be owned and maintained by the HOA/POA.” The applicants currently have two (2) Existing Accessory Structures in their yard and per Section 5.2.1- Accessory Structure, would only be allowed to permit one (1) additional structure. According to the site plan submitted by the applicants, the proposed building would replace one of the existing accessory structures. Per Section 5.2.1 — Accessory Structures of the UDO: 1. Location: Shall be located in the rear yard only. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 5.2.1 — Accessory Structures: e A variance to allow an Accessory Structure to be permitted in the Double Front Yard (adjacent to New Road). According to Section 14.1035, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are “to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship only if it makes and documents, in writing, findings that satisfy all four required criteria. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Wilkerson informed the board that the applicants were unable to attend due to a family emergency but had requested that the variance be considered in their absence. The board and staff discussed the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 A. Tyler Thomas with Sellers General Construction, agent for the property owner, Ceppetelli Storage Solutions LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.3.1 — Non-Residential Design Standards and Section 6.5.2 — Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), for the property located at 1065 Pitch Landing Road. (PIN 381-08-01-0006) Wilkerson stated that this parcel (Tract S-Commercial) is part of the Warden Station tract that was Annexed and Rezoned to City of Conway Planned Development (PD) on January 2, 2024, per Ordinance #ZA2023- 10-02(B). The Warden Station PD document was recorded on January 27, 2024, in Deed Book 4779 at Page 653. This parcel is also located in the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). A Mini-Storage Facility has been reviewed for this parcel and is close to Civil Plan approval. Part of the review process includes elevations and building materials. The Warden Station PD Document states that “All commercial development within the PD shall comply with the City’s Non-Residential Design Standards in effect at the time of plan and/or permit submittal, and, where applicable the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO).” Section 6.3.1-Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards of the UDO states that “No portion of a building constructed of unadorned concrete masonry units or corrugated metal, sheet metal, exposed metal, and / or manufactured panelized metal wall systems shall be visible in any manner from adjoining developed properties, from existing public rights-of-way, or from adjoining properties which are eligible for future development.” Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) of the UDO states that “The Planning Department shall ensure compliance with the architectural design standards that are identified in Section 6.3.1”. The contractor for this project, Sellers General Construction, proposes using brick fagade on the side of the buildings that face the Highway and the interior buildings be a standard colored metal building panel. The PD document does require a 25-ft Commercial PD Perimeter Buffer. The facility will also be enclosed behind a 6-ft wooden fence. The following variance is requested: e Section 6.3.1-Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards: A variance to allow the use of Metal Building Panels within the Mini Storage Facility with the sides of buildings facing the Highway being covered with brick facade. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board of Zoning Appeals 8/28/25 Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship only if it makes and documents, in writing, findings that satisfy all four required criteria. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Paul Lawson recused himself from this agenda item. All individuals who spoke regarding this request were sworn in by Dingle. Tyler Thomas, agent property owner, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:33 p.m. Approved and signed this Z S day of Spl A ye 2025. ' Paul Lawson, Chhizperson

Pigg Jr., agent for the property owner, Ramos Marta Romos, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1009 Live Oak Street. (PIN 368-01-03-0065). -- 2 of 29 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 2 ADMINISTRATIVE APPEALS REQUEST(S) B. Brooks Marlowe, agent for Lamar Outdoor, requests an appeal of the Zoning Administrator’s interpretation of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1.6- Nonconforming Signs and Section 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off- Premises Signs, regarding the repair of an existing billboard located within the SCDOT ROW at Highway 378 and Rhue Street. Wilkerson stated that the billboard located at the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street within the SCDOT ROW was damaged in a recent storm. The applicant came to the office to inquire about permitting repairs to the billboard. The applicant was advised that billboards are considered “Legal Non-Conforming” and staff could not permit repairs. 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs A. All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited, and no permit shall be granted for construction of any billboard or off-premises sign, except in accordance with the Billboard Sign Replacement Program (Section 12.1.6, F) B. Existing traditional billboards and off-premises signs shall be nonconforming. The applicant sites Article 12-Nonconformities, Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions as their reasoning for the billboard to be authorized for repairs: “Nonconforming structure shall be permitted to be rebuilt or be repaired after sustaining damage less than fifty (50%) percent of the appraised value as shown in the Horry County Tax records and/or a Certified South Carolina Appraiser and approved by the City of Conway Building Department”. The applicant provided a quote for a new billboard as well as a quote for the billboard repairs. The applicant also provided an SCDOT Encroachment Permit from 1973. The Zoning Administrator’s interpretation is as follows…. Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.1 states: “Nonconforming structures or uses may be continued provided they conform to the provisions of this section”. The “Section” is 12.1-Nonconformities, not 12.1.2-General Provisions. “General Provisions” provides a foundation for a broader set of regulations. Therefore, the applicant must then refer to 12.1.6-Nonconforming Signs (see attached) where all provisions would apply. The applicant later submitted an updated SCDOT Encroachment Permit from this year; however, number 12 of the permit states “Please notify the owner of one pole in the right of way. They will need to move the sign back on the property”. The billboard is no longer approved in the SCDOT ROW. Mr. Marlowe also provided a Designation of Agent form signed by the adjacent property owner, Mr. Kenneth W. Bellamy. With the relocation of the billboard to private property, this becomes a new submittal, and 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs applies (All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited). Staff discussed 12.1.6 (F)-Billboard Sign Replace Program with Mason, from the Columbia office for Lamar. The program requires three (3) legal nonconforming billboards to be removed from within the City -- 3 of 29 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 3 limits in order to permit one (1) digital billboard on Highway 501 Bypass / Church Street. The billboard that was removed from the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street will count as one of the three. Appeal requested: • 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions: Grant the appeal based on 12.1.2 (F) which allows nonconforming structures to be repaired when damage is less than 50% of the appraised value. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in the Criteria written above. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Brooks Marlowe, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance due to the sign’s relocation to a new area, where the ordinance's updated rules apply. Additionally, granting the variance under these conditions would not satisfy all four required criteria. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:32 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the April 24, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE REQUEST(S) A. Defered…Benny R. Pigg Jr., agent for the property owner, Ramos Marta Romos, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1009 Live Oak Street. (PIN 368-01-03-0065). -- 2 of 50 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 2 ADMINISTRATIVE APPEALS REQUEST(S) B. Brooks Marlowe, agent for Lamar Outdoor, requests an appeal of the Zoning Administrator’s interpretation of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1.6- Nonconforming Signs and Section 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off- Premises Signs, regarding the repair of an existing billboard located within the SCDOT ROW at Highway 378 and Rhue Street. Wilkerson stated that the billboard located at the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street within the SCDOT ROW was damaged in a recent storm. The applicant came to the office to inquire about permitting repairs to the billboard. The applicant was advised that billboards are considered “Legal Non-Conforming” and staff could not permit repairs. 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs A. All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited, and no permit shall be granted for construction of any billboard or off-premises sign, except in accordance with the Billboard Sign Replacement Program (Section 12.1.6, F) B. Existing traditional billboards and off-premises signs shall be nonconforming. The applicant sites Article 12-Nonconformities, Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions as their reasoning for the billboard to be authorized for repairs: “Nonconforming structure shall be permitted to be rebuilt or be repaired after sustaining damage less than fifty (50%) percent of the appraised value as shown in the Horry County Tax records and/or a Certified South Carolina Appraiser and approved by the City of Conway Building Department”. The applicant provided a quote for a new billboard as well as a quote for the billboard repairs. The applicant also provided an SCDOT Encroachment Permit from 1973. The Zoning Administrator’s interpretation is as follows…. Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.1 states: “Nonconforming structures or uses may be continued provided they conform to the provisions of this section”. The “Section” is 12.1-Nonconformities, not 12.1.2-General Provisions. “General Provisions” provides a foundation for a broader set of regulations. Therefore, the applicant must then refer to 12.1.6-Nonconforming Signs (see attached) where all provisions would apply. The applicant later submitted an updated SCDOT Encroachment Permit from this year; however, number 12 of the permit states “Please notify the owner of one pole in the right of way. They will need to move the sign back on the property”. The billboard is no longer approved in the SCDOT ROW. Mr. Marlowe also provided a Designation of Agent form signed by the adjacent property owner, Mr. Kenneth W. Bellamy. With the relocation of the billboard to private property, this becomes a new submittal, and 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs applies (All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited). Staff discussed 12.1.6 (F)-Billboard Sign Replace Program with Mason, from the Columbia office for Lamar. The program requires three (3) legal nonconforming billboards to be removed from within the City -- 3 of 50 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 3 limits in order to permit one (1) digital billboard on Highway 501 Bypass / Church Street. The billboard that was removed from the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street will count as one of the three. Appeal requested: • 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions: Grant the appeal based on 12.1.2 (F) which allows nonconforming structures to be repaired when damage is less than 50% of the appraised value. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in the Criteria written above. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Brooks Marlowe, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance due to the sign’s relocation to a new area, where the ordinance's updated rules apply. Additionally, granting the variance under these conditions would not satisfy all four required criteria. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, May 22, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Lesley Hill, Sandra James, Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Andy Altman Absent: Paul Lawson, Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator, Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Louis Smith, IT Others: Brooks Marlowe, Ty Singleton I. CALL TO ORDER Vice Chairperson Dingle called the meeting to order at approximately 5:32 p.m. I. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the April 24, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Tl. CRITERIA Dingle read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; © Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. PUBLIC HEARING VARIANCE REQUEST(S) A. Defered...Bemny R. Pigg Jr., agent for the property owner, Ramos Marta Romos, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, for the property located at 1009 Live Oak Street. (PIN 368-01-03-0065). Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 ADMINISTRATIVE APPEALS REQUEST(S) B. Brooks Marlowe, agent for Lamar Outdoor, requests an appeal of the Zoning Administrator’s interpretation of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 12.1.6- Nonconforming Signs and Section 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off- Premises Signs, regarding the repair of an existing billboard located within the SCDOT ROW at Highway 378 and Rhue Street. Wilkerson stated that the billboard located at the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street within the SCDOT ROW was damaged in a recent storm. The applicant came to the office to inquire about permitting repairs to the billboard. The applicant was advised that billboards are considered “Legal Non-Conforming” and staff could not permit repairs. 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs A. All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited, and no permit shall be granted for construction of any billboard or off-premises sign, except in accordance with the Billboard Sign Replacement Program (Section 12.1.6, F) B. Existing traditional billboards and off-premises signs shall be nonconforming. The applicant sites Article 12-Nonconformities, Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions as their reasoning for the billboard to be authorized for repairs: “Nonconforming structure shall be permitted to be rebuilt or be repaired after sustaining damage less than fifty (50%) percent of the appraised value as shown in the Horry County Tax records and/or a Certified South Carolina Appraiser and approved by the City of Conway Building Department”. The applicant provided a quote for a new billboard as well as a quote for the billboard repairs. The applicant also provided an SCDOT Encroachment Permit from 1973. The Zoning Administrator’s interpretation is as follows... Section 12.1-Nonconformities, 12.1.1 states: “Nonconforming structures or uses may be continued provided they conform to the provisions of this section”. The “Section” is 12.1-Nonconformities, not 12.1.2-General Provisions. “General Provisions” provides a foundation for a broader set of regulations. Therefore, the applicant must then refer to 12.1.6-Nonconforming Signs (see attached) where all provisions would apply. The applicant later submitted an updated SCDOT Encroachment Permit from this year; however, number 12 of the permit states “Please notify the owner of one pole in the right of way. They will need to move the sign back on the property”. The billboard is no longer approved in the SCDOT ROW. Mr. Marlowe also provided a Designation of Agent form signed by the adjacent property owner, Mr. Kenneth W. Bellamy. With the relocation of the billboard to private property, this becomes a new submittal, and 11.4.14-Traditional Billboards, Digital Billboards and Off-Premises Signs applies (All traditional billboards, digital billboards and off-premises signs are prohibited). Staff discussed 12.1.6 (F)-Billboard Sign Replace Program with Mason, from the Columbia office for Lamar. The program requires three (3) legal nonconforming billboards to be removed from within the City Board of Zoning Appeals 5/22/25 limits in order to permit one (1) digital billboard on Highway 501 Bypass / Church Street. The billboard that was removed from the corner of Highway 378 and Rhue Street will count as one of the three. Appeal requested: © 12.1.2 (F)-General Provisions: Grant the appeal based on 12.1.2 (F) which allows nonconforming structures to be repaired when damage is less than 50% of the appraised value. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in the Criteria written above. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Brooks Marlowe, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Dingle made a motion to deny the requested variance due to the sign’s relocation to a new area, where the ordinance's updated rules apply. Additionally, granting the variance under these conditions would not satisfy all four required criteria. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:57 p.m. a day of AL , 2025. Catherine Dingle, Vice Chairperson Approved and signed this
