CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the February 27, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. M. O’Bryan, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes., requests a “use” variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU) and Section 4.2-Use Tables, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047. -- 2 of 21 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 2 Wilkerson stated that the parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017, per Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E). At that time, the applicants requested the Mixed Use (MU) zoning district in order to support residential housing built over retail commercial use. PIN 382-05-04-0044 was annexed and rezoned at the same time to the City of Conway Institutional (IN) zoning district in order to accommodate student housing. The civil plan set for the student housing project was approved on July 30, 2018, for what is now The Wren Coastal Student Living. The leasing office for The Wren, located at 706 Highway 544, has never been approved by the City of Conway and has never had a City of Conway business license. Based on the zoning district requested in 2017, Mixed Use (MU), the leasing office could not be approved on this parcel without a mix of uses (residential, commercial and professional). Prior to a business license being issued, the site would have to come into compliance with the current UDO; however, that is not possible in the current zoning district because of the singular use. Staff has discussed rezoning the parcel (as well as the adjacent parcel) to Highway Commercial (HC), which would allow for the “use”. The applicant prefers not to rezone because of future plans with the parcel. The applicant contends that the property has been used for some type of non-residential use, including a church, prior to being a leasing office; however, Article 12 of the UDO states that “A nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use shall not be changed to any other nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use”. Based on Section 14.2.1 Duties and Powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals of the UDO, “an affirmative vote of two-thirds (2/3) of the Board members present and voting shall be required before a variance may be granted for a “use” of land, a building or a structure that is prohibited in a given district, provided however that City Council may overrule the decision of the Board within thirty (30) days following the decision of the Board. In order to grant a “use” variance, the following finding must be determined and made part of the record: the use requested can be documented to have been a past use of the property; however, historic use alone may not be sufficient to grant a use variance. The fact that property may be utilized more profitably, should a variance be granted, may not be considered grounds for any variance”. Variance requested: • Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU): A variance from the requirements of Section 6.4.3 of the UDO, allowing a single commercial use to remain operating on this parcel. • Article 4-Use Tables: A variance from the “conditions” required from the Use Table (found in Section 6.4.3). Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. -- 3 of 21 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 3 There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance as requested, contingent upon obtaining the business license and complying with all other requirements established by the city within a reasonable timeframe. James seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Margie Yarton-Higgins with Massa Multimedia Architecture, agent for the property owner, Wal- Mart Real Estate Business Trust, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 2709 Church Street, Unit A. (PIN 337-00-00-0031) Wilkerson stated Based on Horry County Land Records; the above parcel has been the home to Walmart since 1998. We have recently received permit applications for interior/exterior renovations as well as a small expansion and updated signage. The current building signage is 640.26 square feet and the updated proposed building signage is 399.09 square feet. The existing signage is considered “legal non-conforming” since it does not meet the current UDO requirements. Per Article 12-Nonconformities of the UDO, “Nonconforming business or identification signs shall be allowed to continue provided as follows: Signs which are nonconforming with respect to location or number permitted shall not be altered in any way except to make such sign comply with the provisions of this Article”. Though the proposed building signage is considerably less in square feet, “A nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use shall not be changed to any other nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use”. Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO limits the wall signage. “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed on a different facade if the building is located on a corner lot or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space. to one per tenant unless the building is on a corner lot or if there is a second entrance.” Walmart is allowed two (2) wall signs and is requesting a variance for an additional nine (9) wall signs. Also requested is quantity one (1) - 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner attached to a light pole. Per Section 11.2.2- Prohibited Signs of the UDO, pole signs are prohibited. Additionally, Walmart did receive a variance on number of wall signs in 2018; however, that variance was based on the sign ordinance in effect at that time. Variance requested: • Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow nine (9) additional wall signs beyond the two (2) that the UDO currently allows. • Section 11.2.2-Prohibited Signs: A variance to allow one (1) – 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner to be attached to a light pole creating a pole sign. -- 4 of 21 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 4 In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Edward Danza, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. Nichole Blackmon Lee with Tyson Sign Company, agent for the property owner CHS of 1995 Investments LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 424 Main Street. (PIN 338-13-03-0021) Wilkerson stated that the above parcel was the location of the old Bank of America. This site & structure are in the process of being remodeled and renovated to be the home of Anderson Brothers Bank. The applicant has applied for a sign permit (PS25-0012) to install a non-illuminated hanging sign on the old arm post used by Bank of America. The Bank of America sign was considered “Legal Non- Conforming” since it did not meet the requirements found in Section 11.4.8-Arm Post Sign of the UDO. Per this section, “The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be twenty-four (24) square feet”. The sign that the applicant has applied for is twenty-one (21) square feet; however, the arm post is 15-ft in height. Also, according to Google Maps, the Bank of America sign appears to have been removed sometime in 2021. Per Section 11.1.5-Obsolete and Abandoned Signs of the UDO: “Any sign which advertises or pertains to a business, product, service, activity, or purpose which is no longer conducted or that has not been in use for sixty (60) days, or which is no longer imminent, or any sign structure that no longer displays -- 5 of 21 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 5 any sign copy shall be deemed to be an obsolete or abandoned sign. Such signs shall not be permitted to be re-established or re-used in any manner and must be removed in its entirety”. If the variances are granted by this board, the signage must still be presented to the Community Appearance Board (CAB) for their approval prior to a permit being issued. Variance requested: • Section 11.4.8-Arm Post Sign: A 7-ft variance to allow the existing 15-ft arm post to be used for new signage. • Section 11.1.5-Obsolete and Abandoned Signs: A variance to allow the existing nonconforming arm post to be re-used for ABB signage, though it has not been used for signage in sixty (60) days or longer with the condition that if the sign/structure is removed, whatever is proposed would have to comply with the current UDO standards for signage. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Richard Carol, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the 7ft. variance to allow the 15ft. arm post to stay for new signage as requested. James seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance allowing the existing nonconforming arm post to be reused for ABB signage, with the stipulation that if the sign or structure is removed, any new proposal must comply with the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) standards for signage, as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m. Approved and signed this ___________ day of __________________, 2025. _________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairperson -- 6 of 21 -- IV.A 3191 Highway 378 -- 7 of 21 -- Variance: 3191 Highway 378 (Long HVAC) DATE: April 24, 2025 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: Diamond Shores, agent for the property owner, ASL Properties LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 - Gateway Corridor Overlay, for the property located at 3191 Highway 378. (PIN 370-04-01-0003 & 370-04-01-0002) BACKGROUND: The above parcels, as well as PIN 336-13-04-0007, were annexed into the City of Conway on November 4, 2024. The zoning district is Light Industrial (LI) and the parcels are also located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). The center parcel is the home to Long HVAC. The two above PIN#’s are currently in commercial review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) to enlarge the business as well as enhance the site. Per Section 6.5.2 (J-7) - Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), “Chain linked fencing (with and without barbed wire) in the GCO shall be prohibited”. The side and rear of the parcel are to be used for a Gravel Storage Yard. Per Section 5.1.18 – Open Air Storage, only parcels zoned Highway Commercial (HC) are required to shield Open Air Storage from the public view on all sides by an opaque fence or wall. The applicant is requesting a variance to allow “Chain Link Fencing with Vinyl Slats” on the sides and rear of the property, just inside the required landscaping with a “6-ft tall Wooden Screening Fence” running parallel to Highway 378. Variance requested: • Section 6.5.2 (J-7)-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO): A variance to allow 6-ft Chain Link Fencing with vinyl slats along the rear and sides of the proposed Open Air Storage. -- 8 of 21 -- Variance: 3191 Highway 378 (Long HVAC) The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Explain: -- 11 of 21 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-42 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 6.5.2 Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) A. Purpose The GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multi-family residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors as their primary means of access. The purpose is to provide unified development that promotes a sense of place and provides opportunities to develop projects engineered to be compatible with the carrying capacity of highway corridors. B. Applicability The boundaries of the GCO shall be as shown on a map titled Gateway Corridor Overlay Zone which is hereby adopted and made a part of the UDO, and which may be amended from time to time in accordance with the procedures established in the UDO. The boundaries of the GCO include all those major roadways entering the city along Highways 90, 378, 501, 501 Business, 544, 701, and 905. The GCO district shall include all properties fronting on a thoroughfare or highway designated on the overlay zone map. Properties annexed into the City of Conway shall be required to conform to the GCO regulations. The GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of way line on properties along these highways. Any property or building that has any portion within the 500-feet overlay boundary shall comply with these regulations. Construction or renovation of any buildings located beyond the 500-feet overlay boundary shall be required if visible from the corridor. Parcels zoned CC and single-family developments (less than 5 homes) are exempt from the overlay district standards. Renovated or newly constructed commercial, industrial, multi-family residential, or office developments that are located partially or completely within the boundaries indicated above shall comply with the regulations established below. Renovation is defined as: Work that modifies or expands a structure or business where the improvements are equal to or greater than fifty percent (50%) of the property’s assessed value or the value of the property as determined by an independent appraisal. [Amended 9-20- 21, ZA#2021-09-20 (E)] C. Permitted Uses All uses permitted by right or as Conditional Uses by the underlying zoning district shall be similarly permitted under the GCO. D. Accessory Structures Size Accessory structures for all nonresidential uses shall not exceed twenty-five (25) percent of the area of the principal structure. Residential use of accessory structures shall be prohibited except for owner/business operators. E. Buildings 1. Building Massing and Modulation. The massing of building facades oriented to public streets shall incorporate modulation with horizontal breaks at least every fifty (50) feet. Massing and modulation changes could include changes in height, horizontal plane, building projections/recessions, roof form, and/or other architectural elements. 2. Building materials. The Planning Department shall ensure compliance with the architectural design standards that are identified in Section 6.3.1. -- 12 of 21 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-43 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 F. Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment whether ground level, raised, or rooftop shall be shielded and screened from public view through the use of a parapet wall or other decorative feature. The public view includes front facades, and side and rear facades visible from public right(s)-of-way, adjacent properties, and residential uses or districts. Rooftop vents, used for ventilation purposes, may be exempt from these requirements at the recommendation of TRC. G. Access Management All properties within this corridor shall meet the requirements of the City of Conway’s access management standards in Section 7.2.1. 1. Inter-parcel Access. Provide inter-parcel vehicle access points between all contiguous non-residential properties. A system of joint use driveways and cross access easements shall be used to promote connectivity in the GCO. This requirement may be waived by the TRC only if it is demonstrated that an inter-parcel connection is not feasible due to traffic safety, topographic, or environmental concerns. 2. Shared Access Points. Shared access points should be located along a common property boundary. The first thirty (30’) feet of a driveway shall be paved with impervious or pervious surfaces including concrete pavers or similar materials. The TRC shall approve the paving surface of the first thirty (30’) feet. 3. Where shared access or service driveways occur, an access agreement shall be required by the City of Conway. The agreement must be signed by all affected property owners and must be registered with the Horry County Register of Deeds. H. Connectivity 1. Pedestrian/Bike Access. Pedestrian and bicycle access must be provided to individual developments and each establishment within the development. Pedestrian walkways must be designed and located in a manner that does not require pedestrians to walk through parking lots or cross driveways. 2. Pedestrian Walkways. Pedestrian walkways, a minimum of five (5) feet in width, must be clearly defined and provide a direct connection from the street to the main entrance, and to abutting properties. 3. Trails. If a parcel is located within five hundred (500) feet of a proposed pathway/bike trail, a minimum eight (8’) feet wide trail connection shall be provided. 4. Sidewalks. Sidewalks shall be installed on all public streets the parcel(s) abuts or match existing sidewalk. Sidewalks shall meet the design requirements in Article 7. 5. Bicycle Lanes. Bicycle lanes shall meet the street design requirements in Article 7. I. Utilities All new utility lines (electric, telephone, CATV, etc.) shall be placed underground. All junction and access boxes shall be screened with sufficient vegetation so as to completely obscure it from view. All utility pad features and meters should be shown on the development site plan. J. Landscaping and Buffer Requirements 1. Non-Residential Front Buffers. a. Parking Lots up to 30,000 square feet: The front buffer for commercial and office establishments shall be ten (10’) feet along corridor rights-of-way, both public and private. This buffer is intended for aesthetics, rather than screening purposes. The buffer shall contain the following minimum ornamental plantings per one hundred (100) linear feet of frontage: i. Two (2) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. ii. Two (2) understory trees six (6) --eight (8) feet height minimum. iii. Eighteen (18) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. -- 13 of 21 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-44 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 b. Parking Lots over 30,000 square feet: The front buffer for non-residential establishments shall be fifteen (15’) feet along corridor rights-of-way, both public and private. This buffer is intended for aesthetics, rather than screening purposes. The buffer shall contain the following minimum ornamental plantings per one hundred (100) linear feet of frontage: i. Three (3) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. ii. Three (3) understory trees six (6) – eight (8) feet height minimum. iii. Twenty (20) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. 2. Non-Residential Side and Rear Buffers. Side and rear buffers shall meet the requirements set forth in Article 9. 3. Residential Front Buffers. A fifty (50’) feet buffer shall be provided along the frontage of any new single-family residential development (over five new units) or multi-family development across the street from any use or zoning other than single-family residential. The fifty (50) feet front buffer shall contain the following minimum planting per one hundred (100) linear feet when existing vegetation is not sufficient: a. Eight (8) canopy trees two and one-half (2 1/2) inches caliper minimum. b. Twelve (12) understory trees six (6) – eight (8) feet minimum c. Fifty (50) shrubs, three (3) gallon minimum. 4. Multifamily developments on parcels zoned High-Density Residential (R-3) shall be limited to sixty-five (65) feet above base floor elevations, subject to applicable fire codes. M. Signs Off premise signs, portable signs, and temporary signs shall be prohibited within the GCO corridor. Monument and freestanding post signs are the only freestanding signs allowed in the GCO. Signs in the GCO shall be as permitted in Article 11 of this Unified Development Ordinance, except that compliance with the following regulations shall be required. -- 14 of 21 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 6 – Design Standards 6-45 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 1. Materials. All signs shall be compatible with the architectural design of associated building, including colors and materials. 2. Setback. All monument and freestanding post signs shall meet the setback requirements in Section 11.1.7. 3. Size. a. Monument Signs: The maximum sign face area shall be sixty (60) square feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign face area shall be eighty (80) square feet for multi-tenants (more than three) except in Shopping Centers as referenced in Section 11.4.17. [amended 8-15-16 ZA3201508-15(A)] b. Monument Signs: The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be ten (10) feet for multi-tenants (more than three). b. Freestanding Post Signs: The maximum sign height shall be sixteen (16) feet for a single tenant. The maximum sign height shall be twenty (20) feet for multi-tenants (more than three (3) businesses). 5. Location. text: Board of Zoning Appeals 4/24/25 Present: Absent: Staff: Others: CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, April 24, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Paul Lawson, Lesley Hill, Sandra James, Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley Andy Altman Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Marcus Cohen, IT David Schwerd I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Baxley to approve the March 27, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. Diamond Shores, agent for the property owner, ASL Properties LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.5.2 - Gateway Corridor Overlay, for the property located at 3191 Highway 378. (PIN 370-04-01-0003 & 370-04-01-0002) Board of Zoning Appeals 4/24/25 Wilkerson stated that the above parcels, as well as PIN 336-13-04-0007, were annexed into the City of Conway on November 4, 2024. The zoning district is Light Industrial (LI) and the parcels are also located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). The center parcel is the home to Long HVAC. The two above PIN#’s are currently in commercial review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) to enlarge the business as well as enhance the site. Per Section 6.5.2 (J-7) - Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), “Chain linked fencing (with and without barbed wire) in the GCO shall be prohibited”. The side and rear of the parcel are to be used for a Gravel Storage Yard. Per Section 5.1.18 — Open Air Storage, only parcels zoned Highway Commercial (HC) are required to shield Open Air Storage from the public view on all sides by an opaque fence or wall. The applicant is requesting a variance to allow “Chain Link Fencing with Vinyl Slats” on the sides and rear of the property, just inside the required landscaping with a “6-ft tall Wooden Screening Fence” running parallel to Highway 378. Variance requested: Section 6.5.2 (J-7)-Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO): A variance to allow 6-ft Chain Link Fencing with vinyl slats along the rear and sides of the proposed Open Air Storage. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. David Schwerd, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. . AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:36 p.m. Board of Zoning Appeals 4/24/25 Approved and signed this DP? day of (ae 32025; Catherine Dingle, Vice Chairperson

(PIN 368-03-03- 0064) Wilkerson stated that the applicant currently has plans in review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) for a future healthcare facility. (PIN 337-00-00-0031) BACKGROUND: Based on Horry County Land Records, the above parcel has been the home to Walmart since 1998. We have recently received permit applications for interior/exterior renovations as well as a small expansion and updated signage. The current building signage is 640.26 square feet and the updated proposed building signage is 399.09 square feet. The existing signage is considered “legal non-conforming” since it does not meet the current UDO requirements. Per Article 12-Nonconformities of the UDO, “Nonconforming business or identification signs shall be allowed to continue provided as follows: Signs which are nonconforming with respect to location or number permitted shall not be altered in any way except to make such sign comply with the provisions of this Article”. Though the proposed building signage is considerably less in square feet, “A nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use shall not be changed to any other nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use”. Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO limits the wall signage. “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed on a different facade if the building is located on a corner lot or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space. to one per tenant unless the building is on a corner lot or if there is a second entrance.” Walmart is allowed two (2) wall signs and is requesting a variance for an additional nine (9) wall signs. Also requested is quantity one (1) - 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner attached to a light pole. Per Section 11.2.2-Prohibited Signs of the UDO, pole signs are prohibited. Additionally, Walmart did receive a variance on number of wall signs in 2018; however, that variance was based on the sign ordinance in effect at that time. Variance requested: • Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow nine (9) additional wall signs beyond the two (2) that the UDO currently allows. • Section 11.2.2-Prohibited Signs: A variance to allow one (1) – 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner to be attached to a light pole creating a pole sign. -- 43 of 62 -- Variance: 2709 Church Street (Walmart) The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. title: APPD. BZA MINUTES 3.27.25
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 Present: Absent: Staff: Others: CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, March 27, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Paul Lawson, Lesley Hill, Andy Altman, Sandra James Catherine Dingle, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlie Crosby, IT Edward Danza, Margie Yarton-Higgins, O’ Bryan Martin, Debbie Jenkins, Richard Carroll, Carol Piento, Tammy Carter, Maryann Piento, Hubert Greene I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES James made a motion, seconded by Hill to approve the February 27, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. II. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. M. O’Bryan, agent for the property owner, Pete Hughes., requests a “use” variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU) and Section 4.2-Use Tables, for the property located at 706 Highway 544. (PIN 382-05-04-0047. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 Wilkerson stated that the parcel was annexed and rezoned to the City of Conway Mixed Use (MU) zoning district on October 2, 2017, per Ordinance ZA2017-08-21(E). At that time, the applicants requested the Mixed Use (MU) zoning district in order to support residential housing built over retail commercial use. PIN 382-05-04-0044 was annexed and rezoned at the same time to the City of Conway Institutional (IN) zoning district in order to accommodate student housing. The civil plan set for the student housing project was approved on July 30, 2018, for what is now The Wren Coastal Student Living. The leasing office for The Wren, located at 706 Highway 544, has never been approved by the City of Conway and has never had a City of Conway business license. Based on the zoning district requested in 2017, Mixed Use (MU), the leasing office could not be approved on this parcel without a mix of uses (residential, commercial and professional). Prior to a business license being issued, the site would have to come into compliance with the current UDO; however, that is not possible in the current zoning district because of the singular use. Staff has discussed rezoning the parcel (as well as the adjacent parcel) to Highway Commercial (HC), which would allow for the “use”. The applicant prefers not to rezone because of future plans with the parcel. The applicant contends that the property has been used for some type of non-residential use, including a church, prior to being a leasing office; however, Article 12 of the UDO states that “A nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use shall not be changed to any other nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use”. Based on Section 14.2.1 Duties and Powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals of the UDO, “an affirmative vote of two-thirds (2/3) of the Board members present and voting shall be required before a variance may be granted for a “use” of land, a building or a structure that is prohibited in a given district, provided however that City Council may overrule the decision of the Board within thirty (30) days following the decision of the Board. In order to grant a “use” variance, the following finding must be determined and made part of the record: the use requested can be documented to have been a past use of the property; however, historic use alone may not be sufficient to grant a use variance. The fact that property may be utilized more profitably, should a variance be granted, may not be considered grounds for any variance”. Variance requested: ¢ Section 6.4.3-Mixed Use Flexible Zone (MU): A variance from the requirements of Section 6.4.3 of the UDO, allowing a single commercial use to remain operating on this parcel. e Article 4-Use Tables: A variance from the “conditions” required from the Use Table (found in Section 6.4.3). Staff'recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. O’Bryan Martin, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance as requested, contingent upon obtaining the business license and complying with all other requirements established by the city within a reasonable timeframe. James seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Margie Yarton-Higgins with Massa Multimedia Architecture, agent for the property owner, Wal- Mart Real Estate Business Trust, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 2709 Church Street, Unit A. (PIN 337-00-00-003 1) Wilkerson stated Based on Horry County Land Records; the above parcel has been the home to Walmart since 1998. We have recently received permit applications for interior/exterior renovations as well as a small expansion and updated signage. The current building signage is 640.26 square feet and the updated proposed building signage is 399.09 square feet. The existing signage is considered “legal non-conforming” since it does not meet the current UDO requirements. Per Article 12-Nonconformities of the UDO, “Nonconforming business or identification signs shall be allowed to continue provided as follows: Signs which are nonconforming with respect to location or number permitted shall not be altered in any way except to make such sign comply with the provisions of this Article”. Though the proposed building signage is considerably less in square feet, “A nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use shall not be changed to any other nonconforming use, structure, or characteristic of use”. Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO limits the wall signage. “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed on a different facade if the building is located on a corner lot or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space. to one per tenant unless the building is on a corner lot or if there is a second entrance.” Walmart is allowed two (2) wall signs and is requesting a variance for an additional nine (9) wall signs. Also requested is quantity one (1) - 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner attached to a light pole. Per Section 11.2.2- Prohibited Signs of the UDO, pole signs are prohibited. Additionally, Walmart did receive a variance on number of wall signs in 2018; however, that variance was based on the sign ordinance in effect at that time. Variance requested: e Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow nine (9) additional wall signs beyond the two (2) that the UDO currently allows. e Section 11.2.2-Prohibited Signs: A variance to allow one (1) — 2-ft x 5-ft “Pickup” banner to be attached to a light pole creating a pole sign. Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Edward Danza, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. Nichole Blackmon Lee with Tyson Sign Company, agent for the property owner CHS of 1995 Investments LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 424 Main Street. (PIN 338-13-03-0021) Wilkerson stated that the above parcel was the location of the old Bank of America. This site & structure are in the process of being remodeled and renovated to be the home of Anderson Brothers Bank. The applicant has applied for a sign permit (PS25-0012) to install a non-illuminated hanging sign on the old arm post used by Bank of America. The Bank of America sign was considered “Legal Non- Conforming” since it did not meet the requirements found in Section 11.4.8-Arm Post Sign of the UDO. Per this section, “The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be twenty-four (24) square feet”. The sign that the applicant has applied for is twenty-one (21) square feet; however, the arm post is 15-ft in height. Also, according to Google Maps, the Bank of America sign appears to have been removed sometime in 2021. Per Section 11.1.5-Obsolete and Abandoned Signs of the UDO: “Any sign which advertises or pertains to a business, product, service, activity, or purpose which is no longer conducted or that has not been in use for sixty (60) days, or which is no longer imminent, or any sign structure that no longer displays Board of Zoning Appeals 3/27/25 any sign copy shall be deemed to be an obsolete or abandoned sign. Such signs shall not be permitted to be re-established or re-used in any manner and must be removed in its entirety”. If the variances are granted by this board, the signage must still be presented to the Community Appearance Board (CAB) for their approval prior to a permit being issued. Variance requested: e Section 11.4.8-Arm Post Sign: A 7-ft variance to allow the existing 15-ft arm post to be used for new signage. © Section 11.1.5-Obsolete and Abandoned Signs: A variance to allow the existing nonconforming arm post to be re-used for ABB signage, though it has not been used for signage in sixty (60) days or longer with the condition that if the sign/structure is removed, whatever is proposed would have to comply with the current UDO standards for signage. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Richard Carol, agent for the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the 7ft. variance to allow the 15ft. arm post to stay for new signage as requested. James seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance allowing the existing nonconforming arm post to be reused for ABB signage, with the stipulation that if the sign or structure is removed, any new proposal must comply with the current Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) standards for signage, as requested. Hill seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. . AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m. a a Approved and signed this a Stn day of Vy, WV , 2025. Sean Flynn with Thomas and Hutton, agent for the property owner, Health Care Partners of SC Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 1500 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-03-03-0064) B. David Buckel, agent for the property owner, RP Coastal Centre LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 8-Off-Street Parking and Loading and Article 9-Landscaping and Buffering, for the property located at 1610 Church Street and 1612 Church Street. ADJOURN -- 1 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 1 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, DECEMBER 19, 2024 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Paul Lawson, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Lesley Hill Absent: Andy Altman, Sandra James, Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Anne Bessant, Planning & Development Coordinator; Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Officer Kipp McDowell; Corporal Tyres Nesmith, Support Services Supervisor; Charlie Crosby, IT Others: Diane Adams, Esti Simson, Jen Dauberman, Todd Dauberman, Sean Flynn, Collins Corbett, Keith Skinner, Edna B. Dewitt, David Wellons, Mike Goldson, Jean Spedden Goldson, Alice A. Smith, Toni Mulkey, Randy Mulkey, Robert Ralph, Ronald Conwell, Wanda Conwell, Mike Garrilis, SeeMone Billingsley, Clara Wilson, David Sligh I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the October 24, 2024, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: • Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; • Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; • Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; • Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. -- 2 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 2 IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. Remanded back to BZA by Circuit Court……Keith Skinner, owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards and Section 5.2-Accessory Uses & Structures, for the property located at 1003 and 1005 Creel Street. (PIN 369-05-02-0005 & 06) Wilkerson stated that this variance request was originally heard at the July 27, 2023, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) meeting. At that meeting, the board unanimously voted to table the request to give the applicant time to revise his site plan. The case was then heard at the August 24, 2023, BZA meeting and the request was denied. Mr. Skinner appealed against the board’s decision to Circuit Court. Circuit Court has remanded the case back to the BZA due to deficiencies in the record related to the Board's findings. Mr. Skinner owns the residential home at 1005 Creel Street as well as the vacant parcel at 1003 Creel Street. In September of 2022, Staff was made aware of a structure that was built behind the residential home without a permit. This unpermitted structure does not meet the requirements for a Residential Accessory Structure per Section 5.2.1 of the Unified Development Ordinance (hereinafter “UDO”). The size of a residential accessory structure shall not exceed 50% of the primary structure on the same lot. Based on the minor plat that Mr. Skinner submitted for review, the unpermitted accessory structure is approximately 2,400 sq. ft and the primary structure (house) is 1,300 sq. ft. Upon notification via email of this violation, Mr. Skinner requested a meeting with Staff. At the January 5, 2023 meeting, Mr. Skinner made staff aware of his proposal for a commercial project on the vacant parcel at 1003 Creel Street. In this meeting, he also explained that he planned to add the unpermitted accessory structure to the commercial parcel via a platting action. This unpermitted accessory structure would be a “childcare covered shelter” for use in conjunction with the daycare. Back in 2023, Mr. Skinner submitted a commercial sketch plan for review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) as well as a minor plat adding the unpermitted accessory structure to the vacant parcel for future commercial use. At that time, Staff explained to Mr. Skinner that variances would be required since the accessory structure would not meet setbacks from the new property line and per Section 5.2.1 of the UDO, non-residential accessory structures may be located in the rear and side yards only. Also, the “Childcare Covered Shelter” can only be permitted as an accessory to a principal use. Based on the commercial sketch plan submitted, the “Childcare Covered Shelter” is forward of the “Proposed Childcare Annex Building” and is, therefore, in the front yard. Furthermore, the accessory structure would not have a principal structure until the project is completed. No additional plans were submitted to City staff in 2024. Both parcels are zoned Professional (P). The Professional zoning district has the same setbacks for residential and commercial uses. The setbacks are 20-ft Front, 15-ft Rear and 10-ft Sides. -- 3 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 3 Variance Requested: • Table 6.2 – A variance of 6.2-ft from the side setback of 10-ft for the unpermitted accessory structure on the commercial parcel. • Table 6.1 – A variance of 11.2-ft from the rear setback of 15-ft for the existing accessory structures on Parcel B shown on the minor plat. • Section 5.2.1 – A variance to allow the “Childcare Covered Shelter” to be located in the Front Yard. • Section 5.2.1 – A variance to allow an accessory structure to be located on a parcel without a principal structure. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Keith Skinner, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Randy Mulkey spoke in opposition of the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. Lawson made a motion to deny the request for a variance of 6.2-ft from the side setback of 10-ft for the unpermitted accessory structure on the commercial parcel, a variance of 11.2-ft from the rear setback of 15- ft for the existing accessory structures on Parcel B shown on the minor plat, a variance to allow the “Childcare Covered Shelter” to be located in the Front Yard and a variance to allow an accessory structure to be located on a parcel without a principal structure for the property located at 1003 & 1005, Conway, South Carolina (PIN 369-05-02-0005 & -0006). Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Chad Dauberman, agent for the property owner, Jennifer Dauberman, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 5-Specific Use Regulations and Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 300 Twelfth Avenue. (PIN 339-09-01-0003) Wilkerson stated that the applicant lives on a parcel that is triangular with a property line adjacent Twelfth Avenue and two property lines adjacent Snowhill Drive. Based on the definitions found in the UDO, the applicant has a Front Yard, a Corner Front Yard and a Double Front Yard. When the house was purchased by the current owner of record, there was a 6-ft privacy fence already in place as well as a storage shed. Based on Google Maps, which only goes back to 2013, the fence and shed existed in 2013. Staff has been unable to locate a permit for the existing 6-ft privacy fence or storage shed and can only speculate that both existed prior to the adoption of the UDO in 2011. The applicant has applied for a fence permit to replace the existing 6-ft fence and install an 8-ft fence from the furthest front portion of the house, adjacent to Snowhill Drive, along the property lines. Per Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the UDO, the height of the fence in the corner front yard is only allowed -- 4 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 4 to be 6-ft in height, provided the fence meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. The applicant also is requesting a variance to replace the existing non-conforming storage shed. Per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures of the UDO, structures which are accessory to the principal use of the property shall be located in the rear yard only. Per Section 12.1-Nonconformities of the UDO, a nonconforming use, structure or site shall not be extended, enlarged, or intensified except in conformity. The applicant and owner were made aware of Section 5.2.6-Parking, Storage & Use of Recreational Equipment of the UDO which states that “No major recreational equipment shall be parked or stored on any lot, on any right of way owned by the City of Conway, or upon any street in a residential district except, 1) in a carport or enclosed building 2) rear yard 3) side yard”. The applicant and owner were also made aware of a variance that was granted in 2018. In 2018, the property owner of record at that time requested a variance from Section 5.2.6-Parking, Storage & Use of Recreational Equipment. The variance was granted on June 4, 2018 stating “has been approved to permit your recreational vehicle to be parked on the side where your garage is located, but shall not protrude past the front façade of the house”. Variances granted by the Board of Zoning Appeals run with the land regardless of the property owner. The owner and applicant continued to disregard the City of Conway’s Unified Development Ordinance and therefore, a citation was issued to the property owner on October 21, 2024 for continuing to violate the ordinance. The applicant has verbally agreed to keep all recreational equipment inside the 8-ft fence should the variance be granted. The applicant has requested a variance to have the definition of “Corner Front Yard” removed from pertaining to his parcel in the future. This request cannot be accepted as a variance since a zoning variance is a request to deviate from zoning regulations to allow a property owner to use their land in a way that would otherwise be prohibited. A variance is a waiver from the zoning ordinance, not a change to the zoning law itself. Variance Requested: • Section 5.2.3: A variance to allow an 8-ft fence to be installed on the property lines in the corner front yards, adjacent Snowhill Drive. • Section 5.2.1: A variance to allow a storage shed to be permitted in the corner front yard, replacing the existing storage shed. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Todd Dauberman, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Mike Goldson spoke on opposition of the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. -- 5 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 5 Lawson made a motion that the request for a variance to allow an eight (8) foot fence to be installed on the property lines in the corner front yards, adjacent Snowhill Drive and a variance to allow a storage shed to be permitted in the corner front yard, replacing the existing storage shed be granted with the following conditions: An eight (8) foot fence is allowed along the same footprint as the existing fence with the exception of the fence section running parallel to the front façade of the residence. This section of fence must be six (6) feet in height instead of eight (8) feet. Also, where the fence meets at the tip of the triangular parcel, a ten (10) foot setback must be met because of the sight triangle. Hill seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. C. Sean Flynn with Thomas and Hutton, agent for the property owner, Health Care Partners of SC Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 8-Off-Street Parking & Loading, for the property located at 1500 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-03-03-0064) Wilkerson stated that the applicant currently has plans in review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) for a future healthcare facility. The parcel is zoned Core Commercial (CC) and must meet the requirements of Section 6.3.6-Core Commercial of the City of Conway’s UDO. Upon the initial review, it was determined that the parking count for the new site exceeds the maximum number of parks allowed per Table 8.3-Parking Requirements of the UDO. Table 8.3 lists a minimum and a maximum parking count based on the proposed use. Doctor & Dentist Offices are allowed a maximum of 1 space per 150 square feet of gross floor area. The overall site plan for the project states the building size as 27,895 square feet. This would allow for a maximum of 186 parking spaces. The site plan proposes 205 parking spaces; therefore, the applicant is seeking a variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186-maximum allowed by the UDO. Variance Requested: • Table 8.3-Parking Requirements: A variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186- maximum allowed for the use. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Sean Flynn, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186-maximum allowed for the use. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Alice Smith, property owner and Dennis McCray, contractor, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 449 Thompson Street. (PIN 368-02-03-0038) -- 6 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 6 Wilkerson stated that the DLM Construction Inc. applied for a building permit to construct a new house at 449 Thompson Street. The parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density) and is considered “Legal Non- Conforming” since it does not meet the residential dimensional standards of the current UDO. Per Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, parcels created today that are zoned R1 must be 7,500 square feet in size, have 75-feet of lot width at the right-of-way and 100-feet of lot depth. Ms. Smith’s parcel is approximately 4,444 square feet in size, has 50-feet of lot width at the right-of-way and is 90-feet deep. The parcel is also located on the corner of Thompson Street (SCDOT ROW) and Court Drive (City ROW) which makes the property line at Court Drive a corner front with setbacks of 20-feet Front (Thompson Street), 20-feet Rear, 10-feet Side and 20-feet Corner Front (Court Drive). Based on the site plan provided by the contractor, a 6-feet variance is needed for the Corner Front setback requirement of the UDO in order for the proposed house to fit on the “Legal Non-Conforming” parcel. Variance Requested: • Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A 6-ft variance at the Corner Front, along Court Drive, allowing for a 14-ft setback instead of a 20-ft setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Alice Smith, the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance with a 6-ft variance at the Corner Front, along Court Drive, allowing for a 14-ft setback instead of a 20-ft setback. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. Deferred per applicant…Dan Sennema with Venture Engineering, agent for the property owner, GBS2, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9-Landscaping & Buffering, for the property located at Highway 501 and University Forest Drive. (PIN 383-01-02-0022) F. David T. Wellons Jr, agent for the property owner, Jasper Dewitt, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6- Design Standards, for the property located at Cherry Street and Eagles Street. (PIN 368-01-04- 0015) Wilkerson stated that Mr. Wellons is proposing to build a house on the parcel located at the corner of Cherry Street and Eagles Street. The parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density) and is considered “Legal Non-Conforming” since it does not meet the residential dimensional standards of the current UDO. -- 7 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 7 Per Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, parcels created today that are zoned R1 must be 7,500 square feet in size and have 75-feet of lot width at the right-of-way. Per the sketch plan provided by the applicant, the parcel is approximately 3,923 square feet in size and has 38.4- feet of lot width at the right-of-way. The parcel is also located on the corner of Cherry Street and Eagles Street (both City ROWs) which makes the property line at Eagles Street a corner front with setbacks of 20-feet Front (Cherry Street), 20-feet Rear, 10-feet Side and 20-feet Corner Front (Eagles Street). Based on the sketch plan, a variance is needed for the Front, the Corner Front and the Side setback requirements of the UDO in order for the proposed house to fit on the “Legal Non-Conforming” parcel. Variance Requested: • Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A 1.5-ft variance on the Front Setback, a 6-ft variance on the Side Setback and a 16-ft variance at the Corner Front Setback allowing for a 18.5-ft Front Setback, a 4-ft Side Setback and a 4-ft Corner Front Setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. David Wellons, the applicant, was present to answer any questions. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant a 1.5-ft variance on the Front Setback, a 6-ft variance on the Side Setback and a 16-ft variance at the Corner Front Setback allowing for an 18.5-ft Front Setback, a 4-ft Side Setback and a 4-ft Corner Front Setback. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. Anchor Signs, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 3500 W Highway 501. (PIN 326-09-03-0008) Wilkerson stated that Parker’s Kitchen has been approved at the above address. It will be located on the corner of Highway 501 and Four Mile Road. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO, “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed and shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed if the building is located on a corner lot, installed on another facade or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space”. The applicant is allowed two wall signs since the parcel is located on a corner lot; however, the applicant is seeking a variance to allow three wall signs. The signs are proposed for the front of the building (along Highway 501), the right elevation (along Four Mile Road) and the left elevation. -- 8 of 59 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 8 Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO also states, “Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached.” Based on the applicant’s drawings, all three wall signs are only 10% of the building face where they are attached. Variance Requested: • Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow for a total of three wall signs instead of the two permitted by the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. Collins Corbett, agent for applicant, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. (PIN 338-09-02-0002) BACKGROUND: The applicant has applied for a sign permit to install a monument sign and two (2) wall signs at the approved Scooter’s Coffee location. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO, “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at a public entrance.” This business does not have a “public entrance”, only a drive-up window. The business name is proposed to be located at the drive-up window. The applicant is requesting a second wall sign to be located on the front elevation of the building. The UDO defines a sign as “any device designed to attract the attention of the public for commercial or advertising purposes that is attached, painted or otherwise affixed to, or a part of a building, structure, material, surface, vehicle, or object”.” Therefore, the smiley face drinking coffee would be considered a second wall sign. Variance requested: • Section 11-4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow two (2) wall signs on the Scooter’s Coffee building instead of one. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. -- 31 of 59 -- Variance: 1727 Church Street 1. (PIN 337-11-01-0080) BACKGROUND: The parcel above was created on September 1, 2022 with the recording of plat book 307-18. The project went through the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) and received conditional approval on December 2, 2020. The subdivision is zoned High Density Residential (R-3) which requires 5,000 sq ft lots with 50-ft minimum lot width and 100-ft minimum lot depth. Per Section 6.1.10 of the UDO, “lots zoned Medium Density Residential (R-2), and High Density Residential (R-3) that front on curved streets must have at least 40-feet of frontage”. The setbacks for the zoning district are 15-ft Front, 20-ft Rear, 5-ft Side and 10-ft Corner Front. There is a 10-ft non-exclusive perpetual utility easement that extends along the front of all lots with the development parallel to the road right-of-way (see Note 10 on the plat). The applicant has applied for a building permit (PB24-1052) for a new Single-Family home. Upon review, the residential reviewer determined that the proposed house does not meet setbacks for the zoning district (R3) and encroaches into the 10-ft Utility Easement. The applicant submitted a second plot plan that removed the house from the 10-ft Utility Easement; however, the rear setback is unable to be met. In lieu of making the home smaller, the applicant was advised that the only option is a variance. Staff have received several emails in opposition to building a home on this parcel; however, this parcel is a buildable lot. The variance is only for the rear setback requirement. Variance requested: • Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A variance of 10-ft from the rear setback requirement to allow a 10-ft rear setback instead of a 20-ft setback. The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. -- 43 of 59 -- Variance: 2458 Campton Loop According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance.
