title: APPD. BZA MINUTES 2.27.25
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 Present: Absent: Staff: Others: CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, February 27, 2025 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Paul Lawson, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Andy Altman, Sandra James, Catherine Dingle Lesley Hill Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlie Crosby, IT Nick Bruno, JD Bell, Velma Suggs, Joe Dore, Sean Flynn, Kelly Wagnor, Sam Berry, Charles Perry, Alberta Bellamy, Jennifer Flowers. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. ELECTION OF OFFICERS James made a motion to nominate Dingle to serve as Vice Chairperson, seconded by Hill. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. James made a motion to nominate Lawson as Chairperson, seconded by Baxley. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. Ill. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Lawson made a motion, seconded by James to approve the December 19, 2024, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. IV. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 V. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT . Sean Flynn with Thomas and Hutton, agent for the property owner, Health Care Partners of SC Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 1500 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-03-03- 0064) Wilkerson stated that the applicant currently has plans in review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) for a future healthcare facility. The parcel is zoned Core Commercial (CC) and must meet the requirements of Section 6.3.6-Core Commercial of the City of Conway’s UDO. Upon review of the second submittal of the project by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), it was determined that the dumpster location had been moved from the original location shown on the first submittal to a location not permitted by the UDO. According to Section 6.6.2 of the UDO, “All mechanical equipment (including HVAC units, generators, and other mechanical equipment) and trash handling facilities shall be located on the same lot as the use served unless shared facilities are approved. The location of all utilities and trash handling facilities shall be in the rear or side yards. No such facilities shall be located in any yard adjacent to a public street.” This site has a Double Front (Fifth Avenue) and a Corner Front (Powell Street). The proposed location for the dumpster facility is along Fifth Avenue; however, there will not be a drive-cut at Fifth Avenue. The applicant intends to meet the required screening and dumpster enclosure specifications. Additionally, the Sanitation Director, Reggie Jenerette, does not have any issues with the new location. Variance requested: e Section 6.6.2-Mechanical Equipment, Dumpster, Recycling, and Trash Handling: A variance to allow the dumpster facility to be located in the Double Front at Fifth Avenue. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Flynn, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request to allow the dumpster facility to be located in the Double Front at Fifth Avenue as requested. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 . Kelly Wagnor, agent for the property owner, RP Coastal Centre LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 8-Off-Street Parking and Loading and Article 9-Landscaping and Buffering, for the property located at 1610 Church Street and 1612 Church Street. (PIN 338-10-02-0016, 338-10-02-0015 and 338-10-02-0013) Wilkerson stated that the applicant is proposing to redevelop the current Coastal Centre located on Church Street. This project will be completed in multiple phases. Upon designing the site plan to be submitted for review by the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC), the applicant found several items in the UDO that will require variances. Prior to submitting for a full review, the applicant is requesting variances to allow the full submittal process to be as streamlined as possible. According to Section 14.2.1, the duties of the Board of Zoning Appeals include hearing and deciding appeals for variances in specific cases where the strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship. Approval of such variances must not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that a property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address the location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it provides and explains in writing all of the criteria met by the variance request. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Kelly Wagoner, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Jennifer Flowers spoke during public input. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request for the One-Way Traffic Flow Aisle Width: 20-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 16.45-ft, Angular Parking Dimension: 19-ft, Center to Center: 58-ft, as presented. Dingle seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request for the Two-Way Traffic Flow Aisle Width: 25-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 16.45-ft, Angular Parking Dimension: 19-ft, Center to Center: 63-ft, as presented. James seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request to eliminate the requirement for wheelstops on-site, citing them as tripping hazards. ADA signs will be protected with bollards as presented. Hagen seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request to redesign of the parking area, allowing more than twelve (12) consecutive parking spaces in a row without a landscape island or peninsula, to maintain consistency with the existing parking area that is not being designed as presented. Dingle seconded the motion, which was unanimously approved. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request to eliminate the 2-ft wide area between the curb and the parking space for the new parking lots, in order to maximize the landscape consistency with existing structures as presented. Baxley seconded the motion, which was unanimously approved. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance request for the change from every 3rd to every 4th for new parking lots in order to have the island located in front of the vestibule for ADA path, as presented. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. . Nick Bruno with Grand Strand Visuals, agent for Coffee Holding 3 LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 1727 Church Street. (PIN 338-09-02-0002) Wilkerson stated that the applicant has applied for a sign permit to install a monument sign and two (2) wall signs at the approved Scooter’s Coffee location. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO, “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed, and it shall be located at a public entrance.” This business does not have a “public entrance”, only a drive-up window. The business name is proposed to be located at the drive-up window. The applicant is requesting a second wall sign to be located on the front elevation of the building. The UDO defines a sign as “any device designed to attract the attention of the public for commercial or advertising purposes that is attached, painted or otherwise affixed to, or a part of a building, structure, material, surface, vehicle, or object”.” Therefore, the smiley face drinking coffee would be considered a second wall sign. Variance requested: e Section 11-4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow two (2) wall signs on the Scooter’s Coffee building instead of one. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Nick Bruno, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to approve the variance to allow Two (2) wall signs on the Scooter’s Coffee building instead of one as requested. Altman seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. Joseph Dore with Dreamfinder Homes, agent for H&H Constructors of Fayetteville LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 2458 Campton Loop. (PIN 337-11-01-0080) Wilkerson stated that the parcel above was created on September 1, 2022, with the recording of plat book 307-18. The project went through the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) and received conditional approval on December 2, 2020. The subdivision is zoned High Density Residential (R-3) which requires 5,000 sq ft lots with 50-ft minimum lot width and 100-ft minimum lot depth. Per Section 6.1.10 of the UDO, “lots zoned Medium Density Residential (R-2), and High Density Residential (R-3) that front on curved streets must have at least 40-feet of frontage”. The setbacks for the zoning district are 15-ft Front, 20-ft Rear, 5-ft Side and 10-ft Corner Front. There is a 10-ft non-exclusive perpetual utility easement that extends along the front of all lots with the development parallel to the road right-of-way. The applicant has applied for a building permit (PB24-1052) for a new Single-Family home. Upon review, the residential reviewer determined that the proposed house does not meet setbacks for the zoning district (R3) and encroaches into the 10-ft Utility Easement. The applicant submitted a second plot plan that removed the house from the 10-ft Utility Easement; however, the rear setback is unable to be met. In lieu of making the home smaller, the applicant was advised that the only option is a variance. Staff have received several emails in opposition to building a home on this parcel; however, this parcel is a buildable lot. The variance is only for the rear setback requirement. Variance requested: e Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A variance of 10-ft from the rear setback requirement to allow a 10-ft rear setback instead of a 20-ft setback. In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29- 800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Joseph Dore, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. VI. Board of Zoning Appeals 2/27/25 The board and the applicant and staff discussed the request at length There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to deny the request for a 10-ft variance from the rear setback requirement, which would allow a 10-ft rear setback instead of the required 20 foot. James seconded the motion, which was unanimously approved. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:07 p.m. Approved and signed this

(PIN 338-10-02-0016, 338-10-02-0015 and 338-10-02-0013) BACKGROUND: The applicant is proposing to redevelop the current Coastal Centre located on Church Street. This project will be completed in multiple phases. Upon designing the site plan to be submitted for review by the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC), the applicant found several items in the UDO that will require variances. Prior to submitting for a full review, the applicant is requesting variances to allow the full submittal process to be as streamlined as possible. VARIANCE REQUESTS 1) 8.2.4 Minimum Parking Space and Aisle Dimensions – Sixty (60) Degree Parking: One-Way Traffic Flow per the UDO Requested One-Way Traffic Flow Variance Aisle Width: 18-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 19-ft Angular Parking Dimension: 21-ft, Center to Center: 60-ft Aisle Width: 20-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 16.45-ft Angular Parking Dimension: 19-ft, Center to Center: 58-ft Two-Way Traffic Flow per the UDO Requested Two-Way Traffic Flow Variance Aisle Width: 22-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 19-ft Angular Parking Dimension: 21-ft, Center to Center: 64-ft Aisle Width: 25-ft, Stall Dimensions: 9-ft x 16.45-ft Angular Parking Dimension: 19-ft, Center to Center: 63-ft -- 19 of 30 -- Variance: 1610 & 1612 Church Street 2) 8.2.6 Wheelstop Requirements Wheelstops per the UDO Requested Wheelstop Variance Wheelstops shall be required in all handicapped parking spaces. Wheelstops shall be required in all parking spaces that abut sidewalks and parking spaces that abut landscape areas where the parking area does not contain curbing. Wheelstop requirements can be waived if the sidewalk in front of the parking space is at least six (6) feet in width and is raised at least four (4) inches. Eliminate any Wheelstops to be required on-site as these are tripping hazards. Also, the ADA signs will be protected with bollards. 3) 9.3.4 Landscape Requirements for the Interior of Parking Areas Per the UDO Requested Variances C) A maximum of twelve (12) consecutive parking spaces in a row shall be permitted without a landscape island or peninsula. F) For parking spaces adjacent to a landscape island, a two (2) feet distance is required between the parking space and curb/gutter. G) Every third group of rows of parking spaces shall be separated from one another by a six (6) feet landscape island that extends the entire length of the row of parking spaces. Such landscape island shall contain one (1) canopy tree and ten (10) shrubs per one hundred (100) linear feet. C) For the parking area that is being redesigned, allow more than twelve (12) consecutive parking spaces in a row without a landscape island or peninsula in order to stay consistent with the parking area that is not being redesigned. F) Eliminate the 2-ft wide area between the curb and parking space for the new parking lots in order to maximize the landscape and be consistent with the existing center. G) Change from every 3rd to every 4th for new parking lots in order to have the island located in front of the vestibule for ADA path. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. -- 20 of 30 -- Variance: 1610 & 1612 Church Street According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:35 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hagen made a motion, seconded by Altman to approve the September 26, 2024 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. -- 2 of 99 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 2 IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. Previously Deferred….Cheryl Wingard, agent for the property owner, Castles Real Estate Properties, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 1701 Husted Road. (PIN 383-02-01-0005) Wilkerson stated that when Commerce Plaza was created in 2000 via PB 168-244, the parcel was zoned Production, Service & Industry (PSI) in the City of Conway with setbacks of 30-ft Front, 15-ft Side, 25-ft Rear and 25-ft Corner Front. In 2011, the Unified Development Ordinance was adopted, and parcels zoned PSI were rezoned to Heavy Industrial (HI) with setbacks of 50-ft Front, 30-ft Side, 50-ft Rear and 50-ft Corner Front. The applicant has provided a site plan illustrating development with PSI setbacks vs HI setbacks. Based on the site plan, it would be impossible to develop the parcel meeting HI setbacks. Also, HI requires a minimum lot area of 25,000 SF where PSI only required a minimum lot area of 21,780 SF. Therefore, two of the existing lots (9 & 12) are considered “legal non-conforming” based on the current UDO. The applicant is requesting variances from the setback requirements for the HI zoning district and to adhere to the original setbacks for the PSI zoning district. If granted, the applicant must go through a full commercial review by the Technical Review Committee prior to submitting for any building permits. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 6.3 - Non-Residential Design Stands / Table 6.2 – Non-Residential Zoning Districts: • A variance of 20-ft on the Front setback • A variance of 15-ft on the Side setback • A variance of 25-ft on the Rear setback • A variance of 25-ft on the Corner Front setback Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott McNew, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 3 of 99 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 3 B. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 11 of 99 -- Variance: 1003 & 1005 Creel Street If the Board chooses to grant the requested variances, staff recommends the following conditions be placed on the board order: • A deadline be established for the project’s completion of the childcare facility in order for the accessory structure aka “Childcare Covered Shelter” to remain without a principal structure, to include a stipulation that allows the applicant to request additional time for unforeseen issues; • A requirement that all necessary building permits, inspections and fees for the “Childcare Covered Shelter” be brought into compliance within 30-days of this meeting date; and • That the “Childcare Covered Shelter” be used as an accessory structure in conjunction with the childcare center only. When the house was purchased by the current owner of record, there was a 6-ft privacy fence already in place as well as a storage shed. Based on Google Maps, which only goes back to 2013, the fence and shed existed in 2013. Staff has been unable to locate a permit for the existing 6-ft privacy fence or storage shed and can only speculate that both existed prior to the adoption of the UDO in 2011. The applicant has applied for a fence permit to replace the existing 6-ft fence and install an 8-ft fence from the furthest front portion of the house, adjacent to Snowhill Drive, along the property lines. Per Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the UDO, the height of the fence in the corner front yard is only allowed to be 6-ft in height, provided the fence meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. The applicant also is requesting a variance to replace the existing non-conforming storage shed. Per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures of the UDO, structures which are accessory to the principal use of the property shall be located in the rear yard only. Per Section 12.1- Nonconformities of the UDO, a nonconforming use, structure or site shall not be extended, enlarged, or intensified except in conformity. Staff has received multiple complaints about the applicant storing various recreational vehicles on the parcel, several of which are located in the front yard, adjacent to Twelfth Avenue. The applicant and owner were made aware of Section 5.2.6-Parking, Storage & Use of Recreational Equipment of the UDO which states that “No major recreational equipment shall be parked or stored on any lot, on any right of way owned by the City of Conway, or upon any street in a residential district except, 1) in a carport or enclosed building 2) rear yard 3) side yard”. The applicant and owner were also made aware of a variance that was granted in 2018. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. (PIN 326-09-03-0008) BACKGROUND: A Parker’s Kitchen has been approved at the above address. It will be located on the corner of Highway 501 and Four Mile Road. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO, “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed and shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed if the building is located on a corner lot, installed on another facade or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space”. The applicant is allowed two wall signs since the parcel is located on a corner lot; however, the applicant is seeking a variance to allow three wall signs. The signs are proposed for the front of the building (along Highway 501), the right elevation (along Four Mile Road) and the left elevation. Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO also states, “Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached.” Based on the applicant’s drawings, all three wall signs are only 10% of the building face where they are attached. Variance requested: • Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow for a total of three wall signs instead of the two permitted by the UDO. The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.2.1, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning -- 87 of 99 -- Variance: 3500 W Highway 501 ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. title: APPD-BZA MINUTES 12.19.24
text: Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, DECEMBER 19, 2024 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Paul Lawson, Kevin Hagen, Donna Baxley, Lesley Hill Absent: Andy Altman, Sandra James, Catherine Dingle Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Anne Bessant, Planning & Development Coordinator; Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Officer Kipp McDowell; Corporal Tyres Nesmith, Support Services Supervisor; Charlie Crosby, IT Others: Diane Adams, Esti Simson, Jen Dauberman, Todd Dauberman, Sean Flynn, Collins Corbett, Keith Skinner, Edna B. Dewitt, David Wellons, Mike Goldson, Jean Spedden Goldson, Alice A. Smith, Toni Mulkey, Randy Mulkey, Robert Ralph, Ronald Conwell, Wanda Conwell, Mike Garrilis, SeeMone Billingsley, Clara Wilson, David Sligh I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 p.m. Il. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hill made a motion, seconded by Hagen to approve the October 24, 2024, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: e Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property: e Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; ¢ Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; e Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. Remanded back to BZA by Circuit Court...... Keith Skinner, owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards and Section 5.2-Accessory Uses & Structures, for the property located at 1003 and 1005 Creel Street. (PIN 369-05-02-0005 & 06) Wilkerson stated that this variance request was originally heard at the July 27, 2023, Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) meeting. At that meeting, the board unanimously voted to table the request to give the applicant time to revise his site plan. The case was then heard at the August 24, 2023, BZA meeting and the request was denied. Mr. Skinner appealed against the board’s decision to Circuit Court. Circuit Court has remanded the case back to the BZA due to deficiencies in the record related to the Board's findings. Mr. Skinner owns the residential home at 1005 Creel Street as well as the vacant parcel at 1003 Creel Street. In September of 2022, Staff was made aware of a structure that was built behind the residential home without a permit. This unpermitted structure does not meet the requirements for a Residential Accessory Structure per Section 5.2.1 of the Unified Development Ordinance (hereinafter “UDO”). The size of a residential accessory structure shall not exceed 50% of the primary structure on the same lot. Based on the minor plat that Mr. Skinner submitted for review, the unpermitted accessory structure is approximately 2,400 sq. ft and the primary structure (house) is 1,300 sq. ft. Upon notification via email of this violation, Mr. Skinner requested a meeting with Staff. At the January 5, 2023 meeting, Mr. Skinner made staff aware of his proposal for a commercial project on the vacant parcel at 1003 Creel Street. In this meeting, he also explained that he planned to add the unpermitted accessory structure to the commercial parcel via a platting action. This unpermitted accessory structure would be a “childcare covered shelter” for use in conjunction with the daycare. Back in 2023, Mr. Skinner submitted a commercial sketch plan for review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) as well as a minor plat adding the unpermitted accessory structure to the vacant parcel for future commercial use. At that time, Staff explained to Mr. Skinner that variances would be required since the accessory structure would not meet setbacks from the new property line and per Section 5.2.1 of the UDO, non-residential accessory structures may be located in the rear and side yards only. Also, the “Childcare Covered Shelter” can only be permitted as an accessory to a principal use. Based on the commercial sketch plan submitted, the “Childcare Covered Shelter” is forward of the “Proposed Childcare Annex Building” and is, therefore, in the front yard. Furthermore, the accessory structure would not have a principal structure until the project is completed. No additional plans were submitted to City staff in 2024. Both parcels are zoned Professional (P). The Professional zoning district has the same setbacks for residential and commercial uses. The setbacks are 20-ft Front, 15-ft Rear and 10-ft Sides. Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 Variance Requested: © Table 6.2 — A variance of 6.2-ft from the side setback of 10-ft for the unpermitted accessory structure on the commercial parcel. e Table 6.1—A variance of 11.2-ft from the rear setback of 15-ft for the existing accessory structures on Parcel B shown on the minor plat. © Section 5.2.1 — A variance to allow the “Childcare Covered Shelter” to be located in the Front Yard. © Section 5.2.1 — A variance to allow an accessory structure to be located on a parcel without a principal structure. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Keith Skinner, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Randy Mulkey spoke in opposition of the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. Lawson made a motion to deny the request for a variance of 6.2-ft from the side setback of 10-ft for the unpermitted accessory structure on the commercial parcel, a variance of 11.2-ft from the rear setback of 15- ft for the existing accessory structures on Parcel B shown on the minor plat, a variance to allow the “Childcare Covered Shelter” to be located in the Front Yard and a variance to allow an accessory structure to be located on a parcel without a principal structure for the property located at 1003 & 1005, Conway, South Carolina (PIN 369-05-02-0005 & -0006). Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Chad Dauberman, agent for the property owner, Jennifer Dauberman, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 5-Specific Use Regulations and Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 300 Twelfth Avenue. (PIN 339-09-01-0003) Wilkerson stated that the applicant lives on a parcel that is triangular with a property line adjacent Twelfth Avenue and two property lines adjacent Snowhill Drive. Based on the definitions found in the UDO, the applicant has a Front Yard, a Corner Front Yard and a Double Front Yard. When the house was purchased by the current owner of record, there was a 6-ft privacy fence already in place as well as a storage shed. Based on Google Maps, which only goes back to 2013, the fence and shed existed in 2013. Staff has been unable to locate a permit for the existing 6-ft privacy fence or storage shed and can only speculate that both existed prior to the adoption of the UDO in 2011. The applicant has applied for a fence permit to replace the existing 6-ft fence and install an 8-ft fence from the furthest front portion of the house, adjacent to Snowhill Drive, along the property lines. Per Section 5.2.3-Fences & Walls of the UDO, the height of the fence in the corner front yard is only allowed Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 to be 6-ft in height, provided the fence meets a 10-ft setback from the property line. The applicant also is requesting a variance to replace the existing non-conforming storage shed. Per Section 5.2.1-Accessory Structures of the UDO, structures which are accessory to the principal use of the property shall be located in the rear yard only. Per Section 12.1-Nonconformities of the UDO, a nonconforming use, structure or site shall not be extended, enlarged, or intensified except in conformity. The applicant and owner were made aware of Section 5.2.6-Parking, Storage & Use of Recreational Equipment of the UDO which states that “No major recreational equipment shall be parked or stored on any lot, on any right of way owned by the City of Conway, or upon any street in a residential district except, 1) in a carport or enclosed building 2) rear yard 3) side yard”. The applicant and owner were also made aware of a variance that was granted in 2018. In 2018, the property owner of record at that time requested a variance from Section 5.2.6-Parking, Storage & Use of Recreational Equipment. The variance was granted on June 4, 2018 stating “has been approved to permit your recreational vehicle to be parked on the side where your garage is located, but shall not protrude past the front facade of the house”. Variances granted by the Board of Zoning Appeals run with the land regardless of the property owner. The owner and applicant continued to disregard the City of Conway’s Unified Development Ordinance and therefore, a citation was issued to the property owner on October 21, 2024 for continuing to violate the ordinance. The applicant has verbally agreed to keep all recreational equipment inside the 8-ft fence should the variance be granted. The applicant has requested a variance to have the definition of “Corner Front Yard” removed from pertaining to his parcel in the future. This request cannot be accepted as a variance since a zoning variance is a request to deviate from zoning regulations to allow a property owner to use their land in a way that would otherwise be prohibited. A variance is a waiver from the zoning ordinance, not a change to the zoning law itself. Variance Requested: ¢ Section 5.2.3: A variance to allow an 8-ft fence to be installed on the property lines in the corner front yards, adjacent Snowhill Drive. e Section 5.2.1: A variance to allow a storage shed to be permitted in the corner front yard, replacing the existing storage shed. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Todd Dauberman, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Mike Goldson spoke on opposition of the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 Lawson made a motion that the request for a variance to allow an eight (8) foot fence to be installed on the property lines in the corner front yards, adjacent Snowhill Drive and a variance to allow a storage shed to be permitted in the corner front yard, replacing the existing storage shed be granted with the following conditions: An eight (8) foot fence is allowed along the same footprint as the existing fence with the exception of the fence section running parallel to the front fagade of the residence. This section of fence must be six (6) feet in height instead of eight (8) feet. Also, where the fence meets at the tip of the triangular parcel, a ten (10) foot setback must be met because of the sight triangle. Hill seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously. C. Sean Flynn with Thomas and Hutton, agent for the property owner, Health Care Partners of SC Inc., requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 8-Off-Street Parking & Loading, for the property located at 1500 Fourth Avenue. (PIN 368-03-03-0064) Wilkerson stated that the applicant currently has plans in review with the City of Conway’s Technical Review Committee (TRC) for a future healthcare facility. The parcel is zoned Core Commercial (CC) and must meet the requirements of Section 6.3.6-Core Commercial of the City of Conway’s UDO. Upon the initial review, it was determined that the parking count for the new site exceeds the maximum number of parks allowed per Table 8.3-Parking Requirements of the UDO. Table 8.3 lists a minimum and a maximum parking count based on the proposed use. Doctor & Dentist Offices are allowed a maximum of 1 space per 150 square feet of gross floor area. The overall site plan for the project states the building size as 27,895 square feet. This would allow for a maximum of 186 parking spaces. The site plan proposes 205 parking spaces; therefore, the applicant is seeking a variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186-maximum allowed by the UDO. Variance Requested: e Table 8.3-Parking Requirements: A variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186- maximum allowed for the use. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Sean Flynn, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance to allow 19 parking spaces beyond the 186-maximum allowed for the use. Hill seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. Alice Smith, property owner and Dennis McCray, contractor, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 449 Thompson Street. (PIN 368-02-03-0038) Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 Wilkerson stated that the DLM Construction Inc. applied for a building permit to construct a new house at 449 Thompson Street. The parcel is zoned R1 (Low-Medium Density) and is considered “Legal Non- Conforming” since it does not meet the residential dimensional standards of the current UDO. Per Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, parcels created today that are zoned R1 must be 7,500 square feet in size, have 75-feet of lot width at the right-of-way and 100-feet of lot depth. Ms. Smith’s parcel is approximately 4,444 square feet in size, has 50-feet of lot width at the right-of-way and is 90-feet deep. The parcel is also located on the corner of Thompson Street (SCDOT ROW) and Court Drive (City ROW) which makes the property line at Court Drive a corner front with setbacks of 20-feet Front (Thompson Street), 20-feet Rear, 10-feet Side and 20-feet Corner Front (Court Drive). Based on the site plan provided by the contractor, a 6-feet variance is needed for the Corner Front setback requirement of the UDO in order for the proposed house to fit on the “Legal Non-Conforming” parcel. Variance Requested: ¢ Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A 6-ft variance at the Corner Front, along Court Drive, allowing for a 14-ft setback instead of a 20-ft setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Alice Smith, the applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance with a 6-ft variance at the Corner Front, along Court Drive, allowing for a 14-ft setback instead of a 20-ft setback. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. Deferred per applicant...Dan Sennema with Venture Engineering, agent for the property owner, GBS2, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9-Landscaping & Buffering, for the property located at Highway 501 and University Forest Drive. (PIN 383-01-02-0022) F. David T. Wellons Jr, agent for the property owner, Jasper Dewitt, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6- Design Standards, for the property located at Cherry Street and Eagles Street. (PIN 368-01-04- 0015) Wilkerson stated that Mr. Wellons is proposing to build a house on the parcel located at the corner of Cherry Street and Eagles Street. The parcel is zoned RI (Low-Medium Density) and is considered “Legal Non-Conforming” since it does not meet the residential dimensional standards of the current UDO. Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 Per Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts, parcels created today that are zoned R1 must be 7,500 square feet in size and have 75-feet of lot width at the right-of-way. Per the sketch plan provided by the applicant, the parcel is approximately 3,923 square feet in size and has 38.4- feet of lot width at the right-of-way. The parcel is also located on the corner of Cherry Street and Eagles Street (both City ROWs) which makes the property line at Eagles Street a corner front with setbacks of 20-feet Front (Cherry Street), 20-feet Rear, 10-feet Side and 20-feet Corner Front (Eagles Street). Based on the sketch plan, a variance is needed for the Front, the Corner Front and the Side setback requirements of the UDO in order for the proposed house to fit on the “Legal Non-Conforming” parcel. Variance Requested: e Table 6.1-Dimensional Requirements for Residential Zoning Districts: A 1.5-ft variance on the Front Setback, a 6-ft variance on the Side Setback and a 16-ft variance at the Corner Front Setback allowing for a 18.5-ft Front Setback, a 4-ft Side Setback and a 4-ft Corner Front Setback. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. David Wellons, the applicant, was present to answer any questions. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant a 1.5-ft variance on the Front Setback, a 6-ft variance on the Side Setback and a 16-ft variance at the Corner Front Setback allowing for an 18.5-ft Front Setback, a 4-ft Side Setback and a 4-ft Corner Front Setback. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. G. Anchor Signs, agent for the property owner, Drayton-Parker Companies LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 3500 W Highway 501. (PIN 326-09-03-0008) Wilkerson stated that Parker’s Kitchen has been approved at the above address. It will be located on the corner of Highway 501 and Four Mile Road. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and is within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO, “Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed and shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed if the building is located on a corner lot, installed on another facade or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space”. The applicant is allowed two wall signs since the parcel is located on a corner lot; however, the applicant is seeking a variance to allow three wall signs. The signs are proposed for the front of the building (along Highway 501), the right elevation (along Four Mile Road) and the left elevation. Board of Zoning Appeals 12/19/24 Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO also states, “Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached.” Based on the applicant’s drawings, all three wall signs are only 10% of the building face where they are attached. Variance Requested: e Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs: A variance to allow for a total of three wall signs instead of the two permitted by the UDO. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. The board and the applicant discussed the request at length. Collins Corbett, agent for applicant, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Hill made a motion to grant the variance to allow for a total of three (3) wall signs instead of the two (2) permitted by the UDO. Baxley seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. 2025 BZA MEETING SCHEDULE Hagen made a motion, seconded by Baxley to approve the 2025 meeting schedule as presented. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. VI. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:45p.m. - (ae -— ; Approved and signed this a a \ , 2025.

Hugh Smith, agent for the property owner, Walter Smith, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 2200 Main Street. (PIN 338-06-02-0010) Wilkerson stated above address is the location of Conway Feed & Grain. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial and is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay. The current Wall Sign meets the requirements of the City of Conway’s Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) pertaining to Wall Signs. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.1035, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are “to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 31 of 65 -- -- 32 of 65 -- -- 33 of 65 -- -- 34 of 65 -- ECOXFERRYROAD 60'PublicR/W HUSTEDROAD 66'PublicR/W POCONOSTREET 50'PublicR/W PIN#383-02-04-0006 JAYNEBJOHNSON PIN#383-02-01-0003 OMNIINVESTMENTPROPERTIES EX.20'DRAINAGEEASEMENT WALTRIPCOURT 50'PublicR/W BUILDING 10,000SF LOADINGDOCK 100' 100' 30' 24' 8' 80' 5' 6' 5' 50'ARTERIAL SETBACK 50'REAR SETBACK 30'SIDE SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 25'SIDE SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 30'SIDE SETBACK 50'ARTERIAL SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 50'SIDE SETBACK 50'REAR SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 25'ARTERIAL SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 25'ARTERIAL SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 5'LANDSCAPE STRIP(TYP.) text: Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 CITY OF CONWAY BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS MEETING THURSDAY, OCTOBER 24, 2024 BUILDING & PLANNING DEPARTMENT 196 LAUREL STREET Present: Sandra James, Paul Lawson, Kevin Hagen, Andy Altman Absent: Donna Baxley, Catherine Dingle, Lesley Hill Staff: Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Vicki Stone, Zoning Officer, Anne Bessant, Planning & Development Coordinator; Jeff Leveille, IT Others: Monroe Thompkins, Vernon Thompkins, Angelia Thompkins, Jamie Steele, Matthew Norris, Scott McNew L CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:35 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hagen made a motion, seconded by Altman to approve the September 26, 2024 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. Til. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT A. Previously Deferred....Chery] Wingard, agent for the property owner, Castles Real Estate Properties, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 6-Design Standards, for the property located at 1701 Husted Road. (PIN 383-02-01-0005) Wilkerson stated that when Commerce Plaza was created in 2000 via PB 168-244, the parcel was zoned Production, Service & Industry (PSI) in the City of Conway with setbacks of 30-ft Front, 15-ft Side, 25-ft Rear and 25-ft Corner Front. In 2011, the Unified Development Ordinance was adopted, and parcels zoned PSI were rezoned to Heavy Industrial (HI) with setbacks of 50-ft Front, 30-ft Side, 50-ft Rear and 50-ft Corner Front. The applicant has provided a site plan illustrating development with PSI setbacks vs HI setbacks, Based on the site plan, it would be impossible to develop the parcel meeting HI setbacks. Also, HI requires a minimum lot area of 25,000 SF where PSI only required a minimum lot area of 21,780 SF. Therefore, two of the existing lots (9 & 12) are considered “/egal non-conforming” based on the current UDO. The applicant is requesting variances from the setback requirements for the HI zoning district and to adhere to the original setbacks for the PSI zoning district. If granted, the applicant must go through a full commercial review by the Technical Review Committee prior to submitting for any building permits. Variances requested (per site plan): Section 6.3 - Non-Residential Design Stands / Table 6.2 — Non-Residential Zoning Districts: e A variance of 20-ft on the Front setback e A variance of 15-ft on the Side setback eA variance of 25-ft on the Rear setback eA variance of 25-ft on the Corner Front setback Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Scott McNew, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance as requested. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 B. (PIN’s 326-00-00-0025, 326-09-01-0002, & 326-09- 01-0001) Wilkerson stated that the applicant currently has commercial plans in review for a new car dealership at the above location. The parcels are zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and fall within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). The three (3) parcels are to be combined via a platting action to create one parcel. Per Section 6.5.2-Gateway Corridor Overlay - Parking Lots over 30.000 sqft: The front buffer for non- residential establishments shall be 15-ft along corridor rights-of-way. This buffer is intended for aesthetics, rather than screening purposes. The buffer shall contain the following minimum ornamental plantings per 100-linear feet of frontage: 3-canopy trees, 3-understory trees & 20-shrubs Per Section 9.3.4-Landscape Requirements for the Interior of Parking Areas - Each landscape island or peninsula shall contain a minimum of 1-eanopy tree & 5-shrubs. The applicant is concerned about the visibility as well as increased maintenance of the future dealership’s automobile displays based on the UDO’s landscape requirements. The applicant is requesting a reduction in the GCO front landscape buffer requirements as far as Canopy and Understory Trees. The applicant would also like to use Understory Trees in lieu of Canopy Trees in 9 of the parking islands at the front & to the south side of the project. The applicant is, however, proposing 4 additional Canopy Trees in the landscape island to the south of Building B. (see attached sketch plan) The applicant is also proposing a Commercial Center on the remainder of the combined parcels. The frontage for the Commercial Center will meet the GCO front landscape buffer requirements. There is also a private commercial drive separating the 2 commercial projects (Phase 1 & Phase 2). The applicant is proposing Canopy Trees on both sides of this Private Commercial Drive (which would not be required by the UDO). Variances requested: Section 6.5.2 — Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO): e A variance to reduce the number of Canopy Trees from eight (8) to two (2) and reduce the number of Understory Trees from eight (8) to four (4) in the front GCO landscape buffer on the dealership side of the property only. Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 Section 9.3.4 — Landscape Requirements for the Interior of Parking Areas: e A variance to replace Canopy Trees with Understory Trees in nine (9) of the landscape islands on the dealership side of the property only. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Matthew Norris, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. Monroe Thompkins spoke in opposition of the request. The board and applicant discussed the request at length. Lawson made a motion to deny the variance request. Hagen seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. E. Diamond Shores LLC, agent for MR Investment Group, LLC, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 9-Landscaping & Buffering, for the property located at 1312 Second Avenue. (PIN 368-04-03-0021) Wilkerson stated that the applicant is in the last stages of the construction of a 7-unit commercial project at 1312 Second Avenue. The parcel is zoned Core Commercial (CC) but is not within the Historic Design Review District (HDRD) and does not require CAB (Community Appearance Board) review and/or approval. On July 27, 2023 a 2-ft variance was granted on the 5-ft landscape buffer required along the eastern property line (against the existing building), adjacent to 1310 Second Avenue (DDG Investments LLC). Per the applicant, “based on the required 6-inch of additional road base width and existing concrete flume which extends from the adjacent building, we can not provide the 3-ft landscape strip required along the eastern property line.” Instead of the 3-ft landscape buffer along the easter property line, the applicant is proposing instead an 8- inch wide open space area along the eastern property line. The 8-inch wide open space area will accommodate the concrete flume that conveys storm water drainage from the adjacent building’s roof and along the adjacent building’s foundation. The applicant is requesting the following variances... Variances requested: Board of Zoning Appeals 10/24/24 e Table 9.1-Required Landscaping: A variance from the perimeter landscape requirement along the eastern property line only and allowing an 8-inch wide open space area to accommodate water runoff. Jamie Steele, agent for applicant, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. After much discussion, Lawson made a motion to defer the variance request to next month’s meeting to give the applicant and staff time to obtain some additional information. James seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 6:03 p.m. Approved and signed this q i” of Decenb- , 2024. Ne i Paul Lawson, Chairman

Disabato Jr., Dennis J. Disabato Sr. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairman Lawson called the meeting to order at approximately 5:31 p.m. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Hendrick made a motion, seconded by James to approve the June 27, 2024 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous and the motion carried. Lawson swore in the applicants and staff. III. CRITERIA Lawson read the following four criteria required to be met in order for the Board to grant a variance: Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property; Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity; Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property; Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to the adjacent property or the public good and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. IV. VARIANCE REQUESTS/PUBLIC INPUT -- 2 of 80 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 7/25/24 2 A. Dennis J. Disabato Jr., agent for DD&G, LLC, property owner, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Section 8.2.7-Entrance and Exit Curb Cuts & Article 9-Landscaping and Buffering, for the property located at 1809 & 1817 Lonestar Street. (PIN 383- 02-03-0010) Wilkerson stated that both addresses are zoned Heavy Industrial (HI) and are located in Commerce Plaza. The two parcels, 1809 and 1817 Lonestar Street, were combined via a platting action and recorded on 2.2.2024 in plat book 319-210. The property owner submitted Commercial Plans to add an additional building to the site. One side of the new building would be for another business to lease, and the other side would be for the property owner’s business storage. Submittal of the Commercial Plans triggered requirements from the UDO. The plans were approved by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) on 5.31.2024 and a Zoning Compliance was signed on 6.3.2024 A building permit for the additional building has been applied for through the Building Department by Homewood Metal Works. The property owner is seeking a variance to have a larger drive-cut than what is allowed per the UDO. Lonestar Street is a City Maintained ROW and Public Works does not have an issue with this variance request. Per Section 8.2.7 – Entrance and Exit Curb Cuts: All curb cuts on public streets shall meet the following requirements: A. Maximum. A maximum of one (1) driveway per lot shall be permitted. Additional driveways may be permitted with the approval of the TRC and/or SCDOT. Curb cuts shall not exceed forty (40) feet in width. Variance requested: • A variance of 20-ft to allow for a 60-ft curb cut vs the 40-ft maximum allowed by the UDO. -- 3 of 80 -- Board of Zoning Appeals 7/25/24 3 The property owner is also seeking a variance on Landscape Requirements. The property to the rear of this Heavy Industrial (HI) parcel is zoned R3 (High Density Residential). Per Article 9 – Landscaping & Buffering: The required landscaping type between HI and R3 is a Type D Landscape Buffer. A Type D Landscape Buffer must be 25-ft in width and contain 4-Canopy Trees, 8-Understory Trees and 30-Tall Shrubs per 100 linear feet on center. Typically, Landscape Buffers are installed close to the property line; however, this parcel has a 40-ft Drainage Easement running across the rear as well as a 10-ft Maintenance and Access Easement. (illustrated on the following plat) Variance requested: • A variance to require no rear landscaping or in the alternative, a variance to reduce the Type D Landscape Buffer to a Type A Landscape Buffer. A Type A Landscape Buffer must be 5-ft in width and contain 2-Understory Trees and 18-Tall Shrubs per 100 linear feet on center. Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. Dennis J. Disabato Jr. and Dennis J. Disabato Sr. , property owners, were present and further explained the request at length. There was no public input. Lawson made a motion to grant the 20-ft to allow for a 60-ft curb cut variance as requested. Dingle seconded the motion and the motion carried unanimously. Lawson made a motion to grant the variance to reduce the Type D Landscape Buffer to a Type A Landscape Buffer as requested with the condition to also install a fence. James seconded the motion and the motion carried unanimously. V. AJOURN There being no further business to come before the Board, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 5:46 p.m. Approved and signed this _________ day of ____________, 2024. __________________________ Paul Lawson, Chairman -- 4 of 80 -- VARIANCE REQUEST IV.A – 2200 MAIN STREET -- 5 of 80 -- Variance: 2200 Main Street DATE: September 26, 2024 AGENDA ITEM: IV.A ISSUE: Hugh Smith, agent for the property owner, Walter Smith, requests a variance from the strict application of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Article 11-Signage, for the property located at 2200 Main Street. (PIN 338-06-02-0010) BACKGROUND: The above address is the location of Conway Feed & Grain. The parcel is zoned Highway Commercial and is located within the Gateway Corridor Overlay. The current Wall Sign meets the requirements of the City of Conway’s Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) pertaining to Wall Signs. The applicant is seeking a variance in order to add additional Wall Signage to the front façade of the building. Per Section 11.4.1-Wall Signs of the UDO: A. Location and Number Permitted. Only one Wall Sign per tenant will be allowed and shall be located at the Public Entrance. B. Size. Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached. Based on the renderings provided by the applicant, the additional Wall Signage will be 59 square feet larger than the 15% maximum allowed. Variances requested: • A variance to allow additional Wall Signage which would consist of eight (8) words, twelve (12) inches in height. • A variance to allow the Wall Signage to exceed the 15% maximum allowed with the addition of the eight (8) words, twelve (12) inches in height. -- 6 of 80 -- Variance: 2200 Main Street The applicant cites the following reasons for which a variance should be granted: **See attached application. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.1035, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are “to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 7 of 80 -- -- 8 of 80 -- -- 9 of 80 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 11 – Signage Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended June 4 , 2024 Article 11. These include channel letters made out of wood, metal or plastic. Wall signs may be painted on a wall, or on a board that is attached to a wall. Wall signs should be oriented to achieve balanced composition and harmony with other architectural elements of a building façade. Wall signs should be placed on a flat building surface and should not be placed over or otherwise obscure architectural building features. CITY OF CONWAY UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE (UDO) & ANALYSIS In Section 14.2.1 of the UDO, the duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals reflect Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. According to Section 14.1035, the Board of Zoning Appeals duties are “to hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary Conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the BZA conduct a thorough review of the request and determine if a legal hardship exists and if the best interests of the City of Conway would be served by granting the request. -- 30 of 80 -- -- 31 of 80 -- -- 32 of 80 -- -- 33 of 80 -- ECOXFERRYROAD 60'PublicR/W HUSTEDROAD 66'PublicR/W POCONOSTREET 50'PublicR/W PIN#383-02-04-0006 JAYNEBJOHNSON PIN#383-02-01-0003 OMNIINVESTMENTPROPERTIES EX.20'DRAINAGEEASEMENT WALTRIPCOURT 50'PublicR/W BUILDING 10,000SF LOADINGDOCK 100' 100' 30' 24' 8' 80' 5' 6' 5' 50'ARTERIAL SETBACK 50'REAR SETBACK 30'SIDE SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 25'SIDE SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 30'SIDE SETBACK 50'ARTERIAL SETBACK 50'FRONT SETBACK 50'SIDE SETBACK 50'REAR SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 25'ARTERIAL SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 25'ARTERIAL SETBACK 20'REAR SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 30'FRONT SETBACK 20'SIDE SETBACK 5'LANDSCAPE STRIP(TYP.)
