(Rezoning) PLANNING COMMISSION MTG DATE: July 9, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: V.A.5. ISSUE: Request to rezone approximately 10.51+/- acres of property located at 1151 Hwy 501 Business, upon annexation into the City of Conway, from Horry County Commerial Forest Agriculture (CFA) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. APPLICANT(S): Diamond Shores, LLC & FC 501, LLC PIN(s): 367-00-00-0010 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) & Highway Commercial (HC) PROPOSED ZONING: Light Industrial (LI) BACKGROUND: The annexation application was submitted in accordance with City requirements for connection to City utilities; specifically, a name change for the city utility services account. The subject property fronts both Highway 501 Business and Highway 90 and contains an existing commercial building and outdoor display/storage areas currently occupied by a heavy equipment sales and rental business. The site was previously operated as Altman Tractor Equipment, a tractor sales and service facility, while under Horry County jurisdiction. The current business was established while the property remained in Horry County’s jurisdiction and was issued a Horry County business license prior to the request for annexation being submitted. The request for City utility service triggered the requirement for annexation into the City. City Council approved first reading of the ordinance annexing the subject property at their June 15, 2026 meeting. DEFINITION / INTENT OF PROPOSED ZONING: Per Section 3.2.13 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the LI District is to provide areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: Properties surrounding the subject property remain within the jurisdiction of Horry County and are zoned Highway Commercial (HC), Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA), and Heavy Industrial (HI). Directly across Highway 501 Business is an approximately 32.62-acre vacant parcel located within the city limits and zoned Forest Agriculture (FA). -- 91 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT 1151 Hwy 501 Bus. (Rezoning) The City’s Future Land Use Map designates the property as Highway Commercial (HC). The HC designation generally supports automobile-oriented commercial activity along major corridors. Although the Light Industrial zoning does not directly match the parcel’s HC Future Land Use designation, staff finds that LI zoning is appropriate based on the property’s longstanding use for tractor and heavy equipment sales and service, the current heavy equipment sales and rental operation, and the presence of nearby properties designated for industrial uses. The proposed LI zoning would avoid creating a legal nonconforming use upon annexation and would provide a zoning classification that more accurately reflects the existing and historic use of the property. Further, the City generally tries to reduce nonconformities, not create new ones. STAFF ANALYSIS: The City’s Future Land Use Map designates the subject property as Highway Commercial. Staff recognizes that Council has generally expressed a preference for Highway Commercial zoning along the Hwy 501 corridors due to their visibility, access, and importance as major commercial gateways. However, the subject property has historically operated as a tractor and heavy equipment sales and service facility. The current use is substantially similar, if not identical to, the prior use of the property and was established while the property remained under Horry County jurisdiction. The City recently amended the UDO to define Heavy Equipment and to identify the zoning districts in which the use (Heavy equipment sales and service) is appropriate. Based on those amendments, heavy equipment sales and service is more appropriately classified as a light industrial use rather than a typical highway commercial use. If the property were annexed and zoned HC, the existing heavy equipment sales and rental business would become a legal nonconforming use. This would allow the use to continue but would limit the property owner’s ability to expand or modify the use in the future. Staff does not believe creating a legal nonconforming use upon annexation is the most appropriate zoning outcome when the existing use is longstanding, legally established, and more closely aligned with the Light Industrial district. While the Future Land Use Map designates this specific parcel as HC, nearby (and adjacent) properties are designated for industrial uses, and the surrounding areas includes a mix of commercial, industrial, and agricultural properties. RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 92 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT 1151 Hwy 501 Bus. ISSUE: Request to rezone approximately 4.08+/- acres of property located on Country Club Dr. and Graham Rd, identified as PIN 324-16-03-0045, from the Low-Density Residential (R) district to the Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district, and approx. 0.58+/- acres consisting of PIN 324-16-04-0082 and a portion of PIN 324-16-04-077 from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. The purpose of the rezoning is to accommodate revisions to the approved open space configuration within the Riverwood at Sherwood Forest subdivision. APPLICANT(S): Amber Wall, Wall Eng. (agent) PIN(s): 324-16-03-0045, 324-16-04-0082 and a portion of PIN 324-16-04-0077 CURRENT ZONING: Low-Density Residential (R) and Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) PROPOSED ZONING: Low-Density Residential (R) BACKGROUND: The subject properties are part of the Riverwood at Sherwood Forest residential subdivision. The applicant proposes to revise the configuration of the subdivision’s open space incorporating approx. a 10-ft strip from Lot 88 into the existing open space tract. To maintain consistent zoning across the revised open space area, the applicant also proposes to rezone the adjacent landscape buffer parcels from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. The request originally proposed rezoning the existing 4.08-acre open space tract from the R district to the R-1 district. Following discussions with City staff, the application was been revised to instead: • Rezone approx. a 10-ft strip of Lot 88 from R-1 to R; • Rezone the adjacent landscape buffer area(s) from R-1 to R; and • Incorporate those areas into the existing open space tract. These revisions maintain consistent zoning throughout the expanded open space area while avoiding the need to rezone the existing open space tract to a higher-density residential tract. The request does not authorize additional residential lots, increase residential density, or modify the number of dwelling units previously approved for the subdivisions. DEFINITION / INTENT OF PROPOSED ZONING: Per Sec. 3.2.17 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low-density, detached single-family residential development in -- 103 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT Riverwood at Sherwood Forest (Rezoning) the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the district. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: The properties surrounding the subject property are – for the most part, zoned R-1 (Low/Medium-Density Residential). There are some properties in and around the subject property that remain in Horry County’s jurisdiction. The area is primarily residential in nature. STAFF ANALYSIS: The revised request is primarily intended to align zoning district boundaries with the proposed configuration of the subdivision’s open space and landscape buffer area. Staff believes the revised proposal is preferable to the original request because it: • Maintains the open space tract within the Low-Density Residential (R) district; • Creates a single, consistent zoning district across the expanded open space and landscape buffer areas; • Avoids split zoning of the open space tract; • Does not increase residential density; • Does not authorize additional residential lots; and • Does not alter the approved development pattern of the subdivision. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: While the Future Land Use Map identifies the area as Low/Medium-Density Residential, the proposed rezoning affects only open space and landscape buffer areas that are not intended for residential development. Therefore, staff does not believe the request will alter the planned residential character or development intensity contemplated by the Comprehensive Plan. The revised request also eliminates split zoning between the expanded open space tract and the adjacent landscape buffer area(s), resulting in a more logical and administratively consistent zoning pattern. RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. APPLICANT(S): Kingston Engineering, agent PIN(s): 337-00-00-0023 CURRENT ZONING: Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PROPOSED ZONING: Medium Density Residential (R-2) and Conservation Preservation (CP) districts BACKGROUND: City Council approved first reading of the annexation ordinance for the subject property at its May 4, 2026 meeting. Planning Commission is now being asked to hold the required public hearing and provide a recommendation to City Council regarding the appropriate zoning upon annexation. The subject property contains approx. 120.71+/- acres and is located along Hwy 378, and is currently within Horry County’s jurisdiction, where it is zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). The property is located within the City’s utility service area, and future development of the property will require connection to City water and sewer services. Concurrent with the annexation request, the applicant has submitted a Development Agreement outlining the proposed development of the property. The applicant intends to develop the site for single-family residential purposes and is requesting Medium-Density Residential (R-2) zoning for the developable portions of the property. The associated Development Agreement is being considered separately and establishes the proposed development framework, public benefits, and other obligations associated with the project. Portions of the property contain mapped flood hazard areas, wetlands, and other environmentally sensitive features. Consistent with the City’s policy of protecting floor-prone and environmentally sensitive areas that may be unsuitable for residential development, staff recommends that these areas be zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation. DEFINITION / INTENT OF PROPOSED ZONING: Per Sec. 3.2.4 of the UDO, the Medium-Density Residential District is intended to provide areas for medium density attached, detached, semi-attached and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway, -- 112 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT Hwy 378 (Rezoning) while prohibiting uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the District. Per Sec. 3.2.15 of the UDO, the CP district is intended to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood-prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. SURROUNDING USES/ZONING: The subject property is adjacent to a mix of institutional, residential, commercial, and undeveloped land, including: • To the rear: Conway High School (Institutional – IN) and two vacant parcels zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) • Along Radio Lane: properties zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and Low/Medium-Density (R-1); and • All other adjacent properties are located in the County’s jurisdiction and zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). COMPREHENSIVE PLAN / FUTURE LAND USE MAP: The City’s future land use map designates the majority of the property as Medium-Density Residential, with a portion of the Highway 378 frontage identified as Highway Commercial (HC). The requested R-2 zoning is generally consistent with the Future Land Use Map for the majority of the property and reflects the applicant’s intent to develop the site for residential purposes. The proposed CP zoning for flood-prone and environmentally sensitive areas is also consistent with the City’s policy of protecting areas that may be unsuitable for residential development. Planning Commission should note that the Hwy 378 frontage is identified as HC on the Future Land Use Map. However, the applicant is not currently proposing commercial development as part of the zoning request or associated Development Agreement. Planning Commission may consider whether the proposed R-2 zoning is appropriate for the frontage based on the applicant’s stated residential development intent, surrounding conditions, and the overall zoning framework proposed upon annexation. STAFF ANALYSIS: The proposed R-2 zoning would allow a range of residential housing types and is generally consistent with the Medium-Density Residential designation shown on the Future Land Use Map for a majority of the property. The proposed CP zoning for flood-prone and environmentally-sensitive areas would provide additional protection for portions of the site that may be unsuitable for development. -- 113 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT Hwy 378 (Rezoning) Although a portion of the Hwy 378 frontage is designated Highway Commercial (HC) on the Future Land Use Map, the applicant has indicated an intent to develop the property for residential purposes. The associated Development Agreement is also being reviewed in connection with the proposed residential development of the site. Because negotiations related to the Development Agreement remain ongoing, the zoning request should be reviewed based on the appropriate zoning designations upon annexation, while recognizing that specific development obligations may continue to be refined through the Development Agreement process. Staff finds that R-2 zoning for the developable portions of the property, together with the CP zoning for flood-prone or environmentally sensitive areas, provides a reasonable zoning framework upon annexation. RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council regarding the appropriate zoning(s) upon annexation. APPLICANT(S): Kingston Engineering, agent PIN(s): 337-00-00-0023 BACKGROUND: City Council approved first reading of the annexation ordinance for the subject property at its May 4, 2026 meeting. In conjunction with annexation and zoning of the property, the City and Developer have been discussing a proposed Development Agreement pursuant to the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act. The proposed development agreement is intended to establish rights and obligations of the City and Developer related to development of the property, including vested development rights, infrastructure responsibilities, environmental protection, public improvements, and negotiated public benefits. The property is proposed to be developed primarily for residential purposes, with flood-prone and environmentally sensitive portions of the property proposed to be zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation. Negotiations between the City and the developer remain ongoing, and several provisions of the Agreement have not been finalized. Among the outstanding issues are the scope of transportation improvements, which cannot be finalized until completion of the Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA), and the extent of the Developer’s obligations regarding the construction of the proposed Greenway trail improvements, and the extent to which the negotiated tree preservation and mitigation provisions will modify or satisfy the requirements of the Tree Preservation Ordinance. Accordingly the Agreement presented to Planning Commission should be considered a working draft that may include additions revisions prior to City’s Council’s consideration. DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT OVERVIEW: Pursuant to the SC Local Government Development Agreement Act (S.C. Code Ann. § 6-31-10 et seq.), local governments may enter into Development Agreements with property owners or developers to establish the terms and conditions under which property may be developed. Development Agreements are intended to provide certainty regarding applicable development regulations while allowing local governments to negotiate public benefits, infrastructure improvements, environmental protections, and other obligations that serve the public interest. -- 126 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT Development Agreement for property on Hwy 378 Under the Act, the initial term of a Development Agreement depends on the size of the property. Because the subject property contains approx. 120.71 acres, the Agreement is limited to an initial term of 5 years, unless extended in accordance with the Act and the terms of the Agreement. The proposed Development Agreement is being considered concurrently with the requested annexation and zoning and is intended to establish the respective rights and obligations of the City and Developer should the property be annexed and developed. The law requires that the Planning Commission conduct a public hearing and make a recommendation to City Council prior to Council’s consideration of the proposed Agreement. City Council is the governing body authorized to approve, modify, or deny the Development Agreement following the required public hearing process. KEY PROVISIONS: The draft Development Agreement currently proposes or contemplates provisions including: • Vesting certain development rights for the property pursuant to the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act; • Assigning responsibility for construction of public infrastructure serving the project; • Requiring transportation improvements identified through the Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) or otherwise required by the City or SCDOT; • Providing roadway and utility stub-outs to adjacent undeveloped properties; • Conveyance of approx. 21 acres to the City for public park and greenway (trail) purposes; • Protection of environmentally sensitive and flood-prone areas through Conservation Preservation (CP) zoning; • Annual compliance review requirements; and • Other provisions governing future development approvals, environmental protection, and implementation of the Project. Staff notes that negotiations remain ongoing regarding certain public benefits, including whether the Developer will construct the Greenway Trail improvements or convey only the land upon which the City would construct those improvements. STAFF ANALYSIS: Staff continues to work with the developer to negotiate the terms of the proposed Development Agreement. While substantial progress is being made, several material provisions remain under discussion and may change prior to City Council’s consideration. In particular: -- 127 of 198 -- STAFF REPORT Development Agreement for property on Hwy 378 • The review of roadway and transportation improvements cannot be finalized until completion of the TIA; • The parties continue to negotiate to what extent the developer will construct the trail improvements or instead only convey the land for future construction by the City; and • The parties continue to negotiate the extent to which the developer will receive relief from the City’s Tree Preservation Ordinance and mitigation requirements in exchange for the public benefits provided under the Agreement. Planning Commission’s review should focus on the overall framework of the proposed Agreement, whether the proposed Agreement is consistent with the City’s Comprehensive Plan, and whether the public benefits being negotiated are appropriate for the vested development rights proposed to be granted. In addition to the original draft provided by the applicant, there is another draft in the packet that includes the original language of the Agreement (in black) and staff’s recommended revisions in red. Also attached is a document outlining the key provisions and a summary of revisions. A5 www.myhorrynews.com Local author shares tale of betrayal, heartbreak and finding true love A STORY ‘ONLY GOD COULD HAVE WRITTEN’ SHANNON KEITH info@myhorrynews.com Marti Schutte said the front porch of her “little county home” in Aynor is where she feels closest to God. “That’s my peace ... I can sit there and see how his designs on my life have come true,” she said Schutte, 50, a Physical Education teacher with Horry County Schools, lives an admittedly “sim- ple” life, with and her husband, Jon, occupying about seven acres of the 50-acre farm she grew up in. However, Schutte said her 2,200 square foot home is her “fairytale” and her “happily ever after” and that the story of her life could only have been written by one author. “My story is one that only God could have writ- ten,” Schutte said. “I look back on my life and I can see his grand design so clearly. I know that God always had plans for me.” Schutte, a native of Del- aware, moved to South Carolina when she was in the fifth grade, raised on a 50-acre farm in Aynor, the same farm she came back to about a decade ago. “My life has come full circle,” Schutte said. “God’s plan took me across the country and took many years ... but he gave me the storybook ending every girl dreams of.” Last month, Schutte published ‘The Porch God Promised’ .. which chroni- cles her struggles through her first marriage, which ended in divorce but ulti- mately led her to “the man God intended for me” ... her husband, Jon. “I wrote this book because God wanted me to,”, Schutte said. “I think it can give people hope and peace.” “It was a fairytale ... If you didn’t look too close” Schutte met her first husband, who she renamed Trevor in her book, while attending col- lege in 1995. “I talk about it in my book ... It was like a fairy- tale,” she said. “It was textbook ... We both grew up in Christian homes, we shared the same values ... I thought I was living the dream.” Schutte said Trevor was a successful businessman, which allowed her to be a stay-at-home mother after the birth of their first two sons. “We had it all. On paper, our life was perfect,” Schutte said. “It was fairy- tale ... If you didn’t look too close.” Schutte said that even through the early, happy, years of their marriage, Trevor always begrudged her one thing. “Before I had my porch, I had a balcony,” Schutte said of the home she shared with her first husband. “That’s where I found peace ... where I could truly pray and hear God’s voice. Trevor never liked that I had such a place... He resented it even. It wasn’t until many years later that I learned, that people who carry secrets cannot sit quietly in the presence of peace.” While she was pregnant with her third son, Schutte said Trevor’s secrets start- ed to unveil. Eight months into her pregnancy with her third child, Schutte said “the cracks in our foundation appeared.” “I saw a message on my husband’s phone from someone he worked with and I listened to it,” she said “it was like, ‘hey handsome, you’re proba- bly working on that beau- tiful body of yours’ ... I was devastated.” Schutte said that although her husband ini- tially denied the affair, her marriage would never be the same. “That was the beginning of the end,” Schutte said. “But even then, God was telling me to move forward ... I just didn’t know where he was leading me.” “I DON’T LOVE YOU ANY- MORE” Shortly after the birth of her third son, Schutte said Trevor announced that he was taking a job in Las Vegas, Nevada, tearing her from her family and friends in South Carolina. “I was scared for myself and my family” she said. “But I still moved forward, because I believed God had a plan for me.’ Shortly before leaving for his new job, Schutte said her husband said five words to her that changed her life. “Trevor said that I prob- ably shouldn’t move to Vegas,” she said. “He told me, ‘I don’t love and you anymore’ ... that absolute- ly devastated me.” Schutte said that even though her husband recanted his statement and purchased a “mil- lion-dollar” home in Las Vegas with a balcony, the disconnect in their mar- riage continued to grow. “He had taken away my balcony ...my peace,” she said. “Still, I knew, God had moved me all the way across the country for a reason.” About two years after she moved to Las Vegas, Schutte said she met the man that would change her life. “SIMPLY ELECTRIC” Schutte said she was first introduced to Jon through mutual friends. She was 32 at the time and he was 25. Although she was married, Schutte said the “spark” upon meeting Jon was undeniable. “I can’t begin to describe it ... It was simply electric,” she said. “We both felt it, but we didn’t know where it would lead at the time.” Schutte said that after a few interactions with Jon, he admitted to having feelings for her, yet urged her to try and save her marriage. “He told me he couldn’t be friends with me because of the way he felt about me,” Schutte said. “And he told me that mar- riage was forever and that we have to honor God. “I mean, what kind of a man does that?” She asked. “They just don’t make men like Jon any- more.” Schutte said she tried to make her marriage work through the next several months, but she knew in her heart that it was over. “I tried,” she said. “I tried for my family ... I tried for my children ... I tried for God. But nothing helped in the end.’ “SHELTER IN THE STORM” About two years after moving to Las Vegas, Schutte said Trevor admit- ted to having a five-year affair and that he was leav- ing her. “I sensed it was coming,” she said. “It started out with things like him sug- gesting we have an open marriage. Later, he even offered me $200,000 to leave him. One day, he just told me he was leaving me ... and walked out casually like he was going to the gym.” Devastated, Schutte said she called on family and friends for support, then called on Jon. Their friendship eventually turned to “absolute true love.” “I don’t know what made me call him,” she said. “But somehow I knew he was the person I needed. I just knew he was my shel- ter in the storm.” Over the next few months, Schutte and Jon started dating, eventually marrying and having a daughter together. “The thing that almost broke me ended up lead- ing me to the best thing that ever happened to me,” Schutte said. “I didn’t know it at the time, but now I see God’s vision clearly. He had a plan for me all along.” “FULL CIRCLE” About two years after they were married, still liv- ing in Las Vegas, Schutte said she and Jon visited her family farm in Aynor, a visit she calls a “God wink.” “I had taken some pic- tures of the farm and posted them on Facebook, saying I missed South Car- olina and didn’t want to leave,” Schutte said. “Jon saw the post and imme- diately told me that he wanted to bring me back home to South Carolina. I knew in that moment that God had brought me full circle ... everything that happened to me was him guiding me back home.” Shortly after moving back to South Carolina, Schutte and her family took over about seven acres of her childhood farm and built their cur- rent home. And in place of the balconies of her past, Jon replaced them with a front porch .. the porch God had always promised her, Schutte said. It’s amazing to look back on it now,” she said. “I couldn’t see his vision when I was a mother of three crying on the floor because her world had shattered. But now I’m able to see God’s plan full scope.” Schutte said she hopes her readers can find peace ... and hope ... in her story. “When I first started writing my story, it was more of a steamy romance,” she said. “About a year and a half ago, I started to rewrite my story from the perspective of someone who has seen God’s plan for me come to life. “I just want people to have hope,” she said. “Hope that even in the worst moments of your life, God is preparing you for the best parts of your life.”The Porch God Prom- ised” is available through Amazon and is download- able on Amazon Kindle. Significant provisions include the following: Public Benefits 1. Requires conveyance of approx. 21 acres to the City for public park and greenway purposes. 2. Requires the developer to design, permit, construct, and dedicate the greenway trail system and associated improvements at the developer’s sole expense. 3. Requires roadway and utility stub-outs to adjacent undeveloped properties to facilitate future connectivity. 4. Requires all roadway and transportation improvements identified through the TIA or required by the City or SCDOT. 5. Requires environmentally sensitive and flood-prone areas to be zoned CP upon annexation. Infrastructure and Public Improvements 1. Clarifies that the Developer is responsible for designing, permitting, constructing, funding, and completing all infrastructure necessary to serve the project. 2. Requires all public streets to be constructed to City standards unless otherwise approved in accordance with the UDO. 3. Establishes requirements for acceptance, warranties, and dedication of public improvements. 4. Clarifies ownership and maintenance responsibilities for stormwater facilities. Environmental Protection 1. Requires wetlands, flood-prone areas, and Conservation Preservation lands to remain protected. 2. Prohibits wetlands from being incorporated into residential lots, consistent with the UDO. 3. Requires environmentally sensitive lands to remain in common areas, buffers, open space, or CP zoning. Tree Preservation and Mitigation 1. Establishes that the negotiated Public Benefits provided by the Developer serve as the agreed- upon tree mitigation for the project in lieu of the standard mitigation requirements. 2. Clarifies that tree mitigation credit is unique to this Development Agreement and does not establish precedent for future developments or development agreements. 3. Confirms that the agreement does not waive compliance with any federal, state, or local environmental regulations, including wetland permitting, floodplain regulations, or other natural resource protection requirements. 4. Preserves the City’s enforcement rights should the Developer fail to satisfy the obligations required under the Development Agreement. -- 159 of 198 -- Vested Rights 1. Clarifies the specific development rights vested by the Agreement. 2. Preserves the City’s authority to apply updated building codes, fire codes, engineering standards, utility standards, and other regulations authorized under the Development Agreement Act. 3. No statement, action or agreement hereafter made shall be effective to change, amend, waive, modify, discharge, terminate or effect an abandonment of this Agreement in whole or in part unless such statement, action or agreement is in writing and signed by the party against whom such change, amendment, waiver, modification, discharge, termination or abandonment is sought to be enforced except as otherwise provided in the Act. Proposed revision: MODIFICATION OF AGREEMENT. This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument executed by the City and the Developer in accordance with the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act. No waiver or modification to shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. No amendment shall become effective until approved by City Council and executed by the parties in accordance with the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act. 19. BENEFIT. The benefits and burdens of this Agreement are binding upon the parties hereto and shall run with the land and inure to all successors in interest or assigns of the parties hereto. -- 183 of 198 -- RED-LINED COPY WITH PROPOSED REVISIONS (STAFF EDITS) 23 Proposed revision: BENEFIT. The rights, obligations, benefits, and burdens of this Agreement shall run with the Property and shall be binding upon, and inure to the benefit of, the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. 20. SEVERABILITY. If any provision herein or the application of any provision herein is held invalid, such invalidity shall apply only to such invalid provision, and the remaining provisions of the Agreement, and the application of this Agreement or any other provision of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. Proposed revision: SEVERABILITY. If any provision of this Agreement is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable, such determination shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions which shall remain in full force and effect. 21. NOTICES. Any notice, demand, request, consent, approval or communication which a signatory party is required to or may give to another signatory party hereunder shall be in writing and shall be delivered or addressed to the other at the address below set forth or to such other address as such party may from time to time direct by written notice given in the manner herein prescribed, and such notice or communication shall be deemed to have been given or made when communicated by personal delivery or by independent courier service or by facsimile or if by mail on the fifth (5th) business day after the deposit thereof in the United States Mail, postage prepaid, registered or certified, addressed as hereinafter provided. All notices, demands, requests, consents, approvals or communications to the City shall be addressed to the City at: Proposed revision: NOTICES. Any notice required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed given upon personal delivery, delivery by a nationally recognized overnight courier, or deposit in the United States Mail by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed to the parties at the addresses set forth below, or to such other address as either party may designate by written notice. All notices, demands, requests, consents, approvals or communications to the City shall be addressed to the City at: To the City at: City of Conway _________________________ _________________________ _________________________ _________________________ Attention: City Manager With a copy to: _________________________ _________________________ _________________________ And to the Developer at: Ashton Charleston Residential L.L.C. _________________________ _________________________ _________________________ Attention: E-Mail: -- 184 of 198 -- RED-LINED COPY WITH PROPOSED REVISIONS (STAFF EDITS) 24 With a copy to: George Bullwinkel, III Maynard Nexsen PC 205 King Street, Suite 400 Charleston, SC 29401 Email: gbullwinkel@maynardnexsen.com 22. GENERAL. (A) Subsequent Laws. In the event state or federal laws or regulations are enacted after the execution of this Agreement or decisions are issued by a court of competent jurisdiction which prevent or preclude compliance with the Act or one or more provisions of this Agreement (“New Laws”), the provisions of this Agreement shall be modified or suspended as may be necessary to comply with such New Laws. Immediately after enactment of any such New Law, or court decision, a party designated by Developer and the City shall meet and confer in good faith to agree upon such modification or suspension based on the effect such New Law would have on the purposes and intent of this Agreement. During the time that these parties are conferring on such modification or suspension or challenging the New Laws, the City may take reasonable action to comply with such New Laws. Should these parties be unable to agree to a modification or suspension, either may petition a court of competent jurisdiction for an appropriate modification or suspension of this Agreement. Proposed revision: Subsequent Laws. If any state or federal law, regulation, or final court decision enacted or issued after the Effective Date of this Agreement renders any provision of this Agreement unlawful or unenforceable, the parties shall meet in good faith to consider such amendments as may be necessary to comply with applicable law while preserving, to the greatest extent practicable, the intent and purposes of this Agreement. Pending resolution, the City may take such actions as reasonably necessary to comply with applicable law. If the parties be unable to reach agreement, either party may seek appropriate relief from a court of competent jurisdiction. (B) Estoppel Certificate. The City or any Developer may, at any time, and from time to time, deliver written notice to the other applicable party requesting such party to certify in writing, within Thirty (30) days of such written notice, that this Agreement is in full force and effect, that this Agreement has not been amended or modified, or if so amended, identifying the amendments, whether, to the knowledge of such party, the requesting party is in default or claimed default in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement, and, if so, describing the nature and amount, if any, of any such default or claimed default, and whether, to the knowledge of such party, any event has occurred or failed to occur which, with the passage of time or the giving of notice, or both, would constitute a default and, if so, specifying each such event. (C) Entire Agreement. This Agreement sets forth, and incorporates by reference all of the agreements, conditions and understandings between the City and the Developer relative to the Property and its development and there are no promises, agreements, conditions or understandings, oral or written, expressed or implied, among these parties relative to the matters addressed herein other than as set forth or as referred to herein. (D) No Partnership or Joint Venture. Nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture between the City or any Developer or to render such party liable in any manner for the debts or obligations of another party. (E) Exhibits. All exhibits attached hereto and/or referred to in this Agreement are incorporated herein as though set forth in full. -- 185 of 198 -- RED-LINED COPY WITH PROPOSED REVISIONS (STAFF EDITS) 25 Proposed revision: Exhibits. All exhibits attached to or referenced in this Agreement are incorporated herein as though fully set forth herein. (F) Construction. The parties agree that each party and its counsel have reviewed and revised this Agreement and that any rule of construction to the effect that ambiguities are to be resolved against the drafting party shall not apply in the interpretation of this Agreement or any amendments or exhibits hereto. (G) Transfer of Title. Transfers of title to the Property, in whole or in part, may be made, at any time and to any person or entity, without the consent of the City. Proposed revision: Transfer of Title. The Developer may transfer all or any portion of the Property without obtaining prior consent of the City, provided that such transfer shall remain subject to the provisions of Sections 7 and 8 of this Agreement regarding assignment, assumption of obligations, and notice to the City. No transfer shall relieve the transferring Developer of obligations that accrued prior to the transfer unless expressly released by City Council through a written amendment to this Agreement. (H) Binding Effect. The parties hereto agree that this Agreement shall be binding upon their respective successors and/or assigns. (I) Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of South Carolina, and the parties further agree that venue shall be proper, without regards to any conflict of law principals, in a court of competent jurisdiction in Horry County, or such other jurisdiction in South Carolina as is appropriate and necessary under the circumstances. Proposed revision: Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of South Carolina. Venue for any action arising under this Agreement shall lie in a court of competent jurisdiction in Horry County, South Carolina, unless otherwise required by applicable law. (J) Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in several counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and such counterpart shall constitute but one and the same instrument. (K) Eminent Domain. Nothing contained in this Agreement shall limit, impair or restrict the City’s right and power of eminent domain under the laws of the State of South Carolina. (L) No Third Party Beneficiaries. The provisions of this Agreement may be enforced only by the City and the Developer. No other persons shall have any rights hereunder, unless specified in this Agreement. (M) Release of Developer. Subject to Section 7.B, in the event of conveyance of all or a portion of the Property, the Developer shall be released from any obligations and liabilities with respect to this Agreement as to the portion of Property so transferred, and the transferee shall be substituted as the Developer under the Agreement as to the portion of the Property so transferred; provided, however, the transferee(s) of the one acre contemplated for subdivision and conveyance under Section 7.B shall not be deemed to succeed to any Development Rights and Obligation of Developer under this Agreement. Proposed revision: Release of Developer. Except as otherwise expressly provided herein, a transfer of all or a portion of the Property shall not relieve the Developer of obligations that accrued prior to the transfer unless City Council expressly releases the transferring Developer through a written amendment -- 186 of 198 -- RED-LINED COPY WITH PROPOSED REVISIONS (STAFF EDITS) 26 to this Agreement. Any successor owner assuming development responsibilities shall be bound by the applicable obligations of this Agreement relating to the transferred property. (N) Assignment. Either party may assign any right or interest or delegation of any duty, responsibility, or obligation under this Agreement without the written consent of the other party. Proposed revision: Assignment. Either party may assign its rights under this Agreement only in accordance with applicable law and provisions of Section 7 and 8 of this Agreement. (O) City Cooperation and Support. The City agrees to reasonably cooperate and support the Developer’s efforts that are necessary for the Project, including, but not limited to, any efforts with respect to right of way acquisitions or land swaps. Proposed revision: Cooperation. The City agrees to reasonably cooperate with the Developer in processing applications, permits, reviews, inspections, and other governmental actions necessary to implement this Agreement, provided such cooperation is consistent with applicable law, this Agreement, the City’s UDO, and the City’s governmental responsibilities. Nothing contained herein shall obligate the City to approve any application or exercise its legislative or governmental authority in a manner inconsistent with applicable law. ADD: (P) Integration with Exhibits. If a conflict exists between the text of this Agreement and an exhibit, the text of this Agreement shall control unless the exhibit expressly states otherwise. 23. DESCRIPTION OF LOCAL DEVELOPMENT PERMITS NEEDED. The development of the Property shall be pursuant to this Agreement, the UDO, and Code of Ordinances, as amended; provided, however, in the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the UDO, and/or the Code of Ordinances, the provisions of this Agreement shall control. Necessary permits include, but may not be limited to, the following: building permits, zoning compliance permits, sign permits (permanent and temporary), temporary use permits, accessory use permits, driveway/encroachment/curb cut permits, clearing/grading permits, and land disturbance permits. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the City acknowledges that City Planning and Zoning Director or the City Planning Commission approval of plats will be given if any such plats are materially consistent with the Master Plan of the Project, subject to any Master Plan Revisions. It is specifically understood that the failure of this Agreement to address a particular permit, condition, term or restriction does not relieve the Developer of the necessity of complying with the law governing the permitting requirements, conditions, terms or restrictions. It is expressly understood and acknowledged by all parties to this Agreement that any portions of the Property donated or sold by any Developer to the City shall not be subject to any private declaration of restrictions or property owners association(s) created by any Developer for any subsequent subdivision of the Property. Proposed revision: DESCRIPTION OF LOCAL DEVELOPMENT APPROVALS REQUIRED. Development of the Property shall proceed in accordance with this Agreement, the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act, the City’s UDO, and City of Conway Code of Ordinances, and all other applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and the UDO, or the Code of Ordinances, the provisions of this Agreement shall control only to the extent authorized by the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act. The Developer shall obtain all necessary permits, approvals, authorizations, and development approvals required by applicable law, including but not limited to: annexation approvals; rezoning approvals; subdivision approvals; construction plan approvals; building permits; zoning compliance permits, land -- 187 of 198 -- RED-LINED COPY WITH PROPOSED REVISIONS (STAFF EDITS) 27 disturbance permits; stormwater permits; temporary use permits, driveway/encroachment/curb cut permits, clearing/grading permits; utility permits; sign permits; Certificates of Occupancy, and any other approvals required by applicable law. Nothing contained herein shall be construed as granting approval of any subdivision plat, construction plan, engineering plan, permit, or other development approval. Such approvals shall be reviewed by the City for consistency with this Agreement, the approved Master Plan, and all applicable technical and engineering standards in effect pursuant to this Agreement. Failure of this Agreement to specifically address any permit, approval, condition, standard, or restriction shall not relieve the Developer of the obligation to comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing development of the property. The parties further acknowledge and agree that any property conveyed or dedicated to the City pursuant to this Agreement, including, but not limited to, public rights-of-way, easements, Greenway (trail) improvements or Park Property, shall not be subject to any private declaration of covenants, restrictions, homeowners’ or property owners association(s), or similar private encumbrance unless expressly accepted in writing by the City. 24. STATEMENT OF REQUIRED PROVISIONS. In compliance with Section 6-31-60(A) of the Act, the Developer and the City represent that this Agreement includes all the specific mandatory and required provisions required by the Act, addressed elsewhere in this Agreement. Proposed revision: STATEMENT OF REQUIRED PROVISIONS. In accordance with Section 6-31-60(A) of the South Carolina Local Government Development Agreement Act, the City and the Developer acknowledge that this Agreement contains each of the mandatory provisions required by the Act, all of which are addressed throughout this Agreement. title: APPD MINUTES (7.9.26)
text: PC 7/9/2026 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, JULY 9, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: George Ulrich, Allan Cornell, Thomas J. Anderson III, Kendall Brown, Stacy Knotts, Jessica Wise, David Sligh Absent: Greg Bryson Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT Others: Clint Richardson, John Danford, Carlee N. Vieux, George Debusk, Jason Collins, Al Patanr, Scott Davis, Barry Cates, Libby Cates David Schwerd I. CALL TO ORDER Il. Il. IV. Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Cornell to approve the June 4, 2026, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT Wise made a motion to open public input. No one spoke during public input. Wise made a motion to close public input, seconded by Ulrich and the motion carried unanimously. SUBDIVISIONS A. Maple Grove, Phase 10 - The applicant is requesting approval of a revised master plan for Phase 10 of the Maple Grove subdivision, along with street name approval for roadways within the revised portion of the subdivision, part of the Collins Jollie conservation subdivision (PIN 295-00-00-0037). Hucks stated the item is a request for Planning Commission approval of a revised Master Plan for Phase 10 of the Maple Grove subdivision, which is part of the larger Collins Jollie development. The applicant is also requesting approval of two new street names associated with this phase. PC 7/9/2026 The overall Collins Jollie Development Agreement and Concept Plan were approved by City Council in 2023. Since that time, Planning Commission has reviewed several revisions to the Maple Grove Master Plan as the applicant has refined the design of Phase 10. Originally, Phase 10 was proposed with townhomes, then revised to in-common duplex units, later back to townhomes, and now the applicant is proposing 94 semi-attached duplex units on individual fee-simple lots. This latest revision actually reduces the overall intensity of the development. The previously approved Master Plan contained 692 dwelling units and approximately 70.8 acres of open space. The revised Master Plan proposes 606 total dwelling units while increasing the amount of open space to approximately 80.25 acres. Because the duplexes are now proposed on individual fee-simple lots, each lot must meet the dimensional standards of the R-2 zoning district and have frontage on a public street resulting in two new street names proposed for Planning Commission approval: Whirlybird and Maple Syrup Tree. If approval is granted, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval by the Technical Review Committee. The applicant, John Danford, was present. Wise made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Anderson III. The motion carried unanimously. B. Oak Haven Subdivision - The applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval of a proposed (in-common) single-family development, located on Westridge Blvd, which includes a request to pay an alternative fee-in-lieu amount for a portion of the required open space, in accordance with Sec. 10.3.9 of the UDO (PIN 337-13-03-0056). Hucks stated the request is for an in-common single-family residential development located off Westridge Boulevard. The property is zoned Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The applicant is proposing 10 single- family detached homes on approximately 1.6 acres. Unlike a traditional subdivision, these homes will remain on a single parcel under common ownership rather than being subdivided into individual lots. Access to the development is proposed from a single driveway connecting to an internal parking and circulation area providing 22 parking spaces. As part of the City's in-common single-family regulations adopted last year, developments are required to provide open space. Because this development is relatively small and does not require a full acre of open space, the applicant is utilizing the fee-in-lieu option authorized by the Unified Development Ordinance. The revised site plan provides both active and passive open space on-site, including a floating dock that qualifies as an active open space amenity. The remaining open space requirement will be satisfied through the payment of the required fee-in-lieu, calculated in accordance with the ordinance adopted by City Council in June. Staff has reviewed the proposal and finds it to be consistent with the City's recently adopted regulations for in- common single-family developments. PC 7/9/2026 If approval is granted, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval by the Technical Review Committee. The applicant was present. Sligh made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Cornell. The motion carried unanimously. C. South Oaks, Phase 2 - The applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval of Phase 2 of the South Oaks subdivision, located on South Oaks Drive, which includes a request to pay a fee- in-lieu of providing open space, in accordance with Sec. 10.3.9 of the UDO (PIN 369-12-02- 0065). Hucks stated that the applicant was seeking preliminary plan approval for phase 2 of the South Oaks Subdivision. The request includes four additional single-family lots that would be served by existing streets in the original South Oaks subdivision. The property is zoned R-1 and the proposed lot sizes range from 0.40 acres to 1.3 acres. The applicant is requesting to pay the fee-in-leu of the required on site open space in accordance with the rate determined by the UDO totaling $36,000. If approval is granted, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval by the Technical Review Committee. The applicant was present. Wise made a motion to approve the request as presented, seconded by Anderson. The motion carried unanimously. D. Collins Walk, Phase 2 - The applicant is requesting a reduction and renewal in the infrastructure letter of credit for Phase 2 of the Collins Walk subdivision, located off Church Street. Hucks stated that this phase of the Collins Walk development consists of 57 townhome lots. The existing Letter of Credit is set to expire on July 23, 2026, and is currently in the amount of approximately $349,276. Since the Letter of Credit was originally established, the developer has completed the majority of the required public improvements. The remaining work consists primarily of final landscaping, sidewalks, and the final asphalt surface course within Phase 2. Based on the remaining improvements, staff has recalculated the amount necessary to secure completion of the outstanding work. The applicant is requesting that the Letter of Credit be reduced to $79,770 and extended for one additional year. If approval is granted, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval by the Technical Review Committee. The applicant, Schwerd, was present. Wise made a motion to approve the request as presented, seconded by Ulrich. The motion carried unanimously. PC 7/9/2026 PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Requesting Deferral...Request to rezone approximately 1.54+/- acres of property located at 906 Covery Lane (PIN 382-12-04-0005), from the Horry County Neighborhood Commercial (NC) and Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10) districts to the City of Conway Planned Development (PD) district upon annexation; and Request to rezone approximately 5.27+/- acres of property located at the intersection of Hwy 544 and Buccaneer’s Cove (PIN: 382-12-04-0006), from the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district to the Planned Development (PD) district. Hucks stated that the applicant has requested this item be deferred until the August 6" meeting. The applicant was not present. Ulrich made a motion to defer public input and the rezoning request, seconded by Anderson III. The motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone approximately 0.58 +/- acres of property located at 921 Buccaneers Cove (PIN: 382-13-01-0007), from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-20) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that The property is currently located in Horry County and is zoned Residential (SF-20). Upon annexation, the applicant is requesting Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) zoning. The property contains an existing single-family residence, and the annexation request was submitted in accordance with the City's utility policies requiring annexation for connection to City utility services. The surrounding area is predominantly developed with single-family residential uses. The parcel directly behind the property is located within the City and is zoned Institutional, containing student-oriented multifamily housing. The remainder of Buccaneers Cove is primarily single-family residential. The City's Future Land Use Map designates the property as Low/Medium-Density Residential, and the proposed R- 1 zoning is consistent with both the Future Land Use Map and the surrounding development pattern. Staff recommends that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and forward a recommendation to City Council regarding the proposed R-1 zoning upon annexation. Wise made a motion to open public input. Carlee N. Vieux spoke during public input. Wise made a motion to close public input, seconded by Ulrich and the motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Sligh. The motion was carried unanimously. PC 7/9/2026 3. Request to rezone approximately 0.24 +/- acres of property located at 500 West Cox Ferry Road (PIN: 382-04-04-0012), from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-20) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that This request is for zoning upon annexation of approximately 0.24 acres located at 500 West Cox Ferry Road. The property is currently in Horry County and is zoned Residential, no mobile homes allowed, SF-20. Upon annexation, the applicant is requesting City of Conway Low/Medium- Density Residential, R-1 zoning. The property contains an existing single-family residence, and the annexation request was submitted in accordance with the City’s utility policies due to a name change on the City utility service account. The surrounding area is primarily zoned residential, and the City’s future land use map identifies the property as R-1, consistent with the requested classification. Wise made a motion to open public input. No one spoke during public input. Wise made a motion to close public input, seconded by Ulrich and the motion carried unanimously. The applicant was not present. Ulrich made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Anderson. The motion was carried unanimously. 4, Request to rezone approximately 1.28 +/- acres of property located at 158 Gardner Lacy Road (PIN: 399-01-04-0005), from the Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district upon annexation. Hucks stated the request is for for zoning upon annexation of approximately 1.28 acres located at 158 Gardner Lacy Road. The property is currently in Horry County and is zoned Limited Industrial. Upon annexation, the applicant is requesting City of Conway Light Industrial zoning. The property contains an existing commercial building occupied by Southern Sun Awnings, a long-established metal fabrication and shade solutions business that has operated at this location for many years. The proposed Light Industrial zoning closely corresponds to the property’s existing County zoning and reflects the property’s longstanding industrial use. Surrounding properties include a mix of City and County Highway Commercial and Limited/Light Industrial zoning, with nearby commercial uses along Gardner Lacy Road and Highway 501. The City’s Future Land Use Map designates this property as Light Industrial, and staff finds the proposed LI zoning consistent with the Future Land Use Map, the existing use of the property, and the surrounding zoning pattern. PC 7/9/2026 Wise made a motion to open public input. No one spoke during public input. The applicant was not present. Wise made a motion to close public input, seconded by Ulrich and the motion carried unanimously. Anderson III made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Ulrich. The motion was carried unanimously. 5. Request to rezone approximately 10.51 +/- acres of property located at 1151 Hwy 501 (PIN: 367-00-00-0010), from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) districts to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that the property consists of approximately 10.5 acres and is located on Hwy 501 Business, near the intersection with Hwy 90. The property is currently in the County’s jurisdiction, split-zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture and Highway Commercial. The applicant is requesting to zone the property Light Industrial upon annexation into the City. The annexation was triggered by a name change on the City’s utilities account. The current business is a heavy equipment sales and rental business and was established while the property was still in the County’s jurisdiction and received an Horry County business license prior to the annexation being requested. However, this property has historically operated in a similar manner, previously operated by Altman Tractor Equipment, which also sold heavy equipment. Staff recognizes that the City generally prefers Highway Commercial zoning along the Highway 501 corridor, However, this property is somewhat unique because the existing and historic use is not a typical highway commercial use. The City recently updated the Unified Development Ordinance to define Heavy Equipment sales and service and determined that this type of use is more appropriately located in the Light and Heavy Industrial zoning districts. If the property were annexed and zoned Highway Commercial, the existing business would become legally nonconforming. Staff generally tries to avoid creating new nonconformities when there is a reasonable zoning option that better reflects the existing lawful use of the property. The Light Industrial district reflects the property’s historic use, the current use, and the surrounding development pattern, which includes a mix of commercial, industrial, and agricultural properties. Wise made a motion to open public input. No one spoke during public input. Wise made a motion to close public input, seconded by Ulrich and the motion carried unanimously. 6 t PC 7/9/2026 The applicant, David Shwerd, was present. Ulrich made a motion to approve the request, seconded by Anderson III. The motion was carried unanimously. 6. Request to rezone approximately 4.08 +/- acres of property located on Graham Road and Country Club Drive, identified as PIN 324-16-03-0045, from the Low-Density Residential (R) district to the Low/Medium Density (R-1) district, and approximately 0.58+/- acres consisting of PIN: 324-16-04-0082 and a portion of PIN: 324-16-04-0077 from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. Hucks stated that the purpose of the rezoning request is to accommodate a revision to the Riverwood at Sherwood Forest subdivision’s approved open space configuration. The applicant is proposing to incorporate a small strip of land from Lot 88 (approx. 10-ft) and adjacent landscape buffer areas into the existing open space tract. The request originally proposed rezoning the existing open space tract from Low-Density Residential, R, to Low/Medium-Density Residential, R-1. After discussions with staff, the request was revised so that the smaller areas being added to the open space tract would instead be rezoned from R-1 to R. Staff believes the revised approach is preferable because it maintains the open space tract in the lower- density R district, creates one consistent zoning district across the expanded open space area, and avoids split zoning. This request does not create additional lots, increase density, or change the approved residential development pattern of the subdivision. What it does is take a portion of 3 different parcels and essentially downzone them to the R district to match the zoning of the entire development, with the exception of the portion that was already zoned R-1 at the time the property was annexed into the City. Conway Downtown Alive’s “Groov- in’ on the Green” series is back, start- ing this Friday, May 1. Each Friday from 7:30 p.m. to 9 p.m., a different musical group will perform on the Town Green at 200 Laurel Street. This Friday will begin the series with the band City Lights breaking in the action. “What began in 2021 as an oppor- tunity for the community to come together after Covid, has transformed into a May Friday night tradition,” said Hillary Howard, executive director of Conway Downtown Alive. “Friends, old and new, not only enjoy fabulous musical acts but immerse themselves in the culture that has transformed Conway — residents loving where they live.” Groovin’ on the Green is a free event. Attendees are invited to bring blankets or chairs to enjoy the con- cert. Chicora Car Club will also host a classic car cruise-in with a People’s Choice trophy. Schedule May 1: City Lights May 8: Trae Pierce & The T-Stones May 15: Chocolate Chip & Compa- ny Band May 22: Whiskey Run May 29: Special Blend Experience Band APRIL 30, 2026 | LOCAL | THE HORRY INDEPENDENT | CONWAY, S.C. A3 www.myhorrynews.com STATE HOUSE FROM A2 Groovin’ on the Green returns to Conway with May concert series FARRIER, FROM A1 Horry County, is one of South Carolina’s old- est and most significant communities with a nationally recognized historic downtown that offers an authentic and immersive setting for public celebrations. It’s tree-lined streets, pre- served architecture, and walkable core provide an ideal backdrop for year round destina- tion-quality holiday programming; and Whereas, over the past several years, Conway has earned statewide recognition for its excep- tional holiday celebrations, seasonal décor, and festive programming that have become central to the city’s cultural and economic life. These initiatives include large-scale public art instal- lations, immersive downtown environments, themed markets, parades, concerts, and family friendly celebrations tied to major holidays and seasons. While Conway’s Halloween festivities have become its most visible and widely recog- nized example, it is part of a broader and delib- erate strategy to activate the downtown year round through high-quality experiences; and Whereas, Conway’s dedication to preserving historic spaces while transforming them into vibrant holiday destinations creates a welcom- ing and memorable experience for all who visit generating regional and national media atten- tion and attracting visitors beyond the local region. Local businesses, hospitality providers, and civic organizations credit these efforts with increased visitation, extended stays, and enhanced community pride; and Whereas, Conway’s holiday programming and seasonal attractions have generated sig- nificant economic benefits, welcoming some 2.8 million visitors in 2025. In October alone, more than 472,000 visitors came to experience Halloween-related events such as “Boo-Jangles,” with another 270,000 visitors in December for its “Bo-Jingles” celebration. These numbers directly correlate to a citywide increase in hospitality fee collections and higher restaurant sales, tangi- ble gains that directly support essential public services and infrastructure improvements that enhance the quality of life for residents and vis- itors alike. In addition, social media influencers regularly travel to Conway during each holiday season, using the city as a backdrop to build their platforms while extending Conway’s reach to regional and national audiences at no cost to taxpayers; and Whereas, the city’s holiday programing has produced outcomes rarely seen in communities of similar sizing. Commercial vacancies have been effectively eliminated throughout the down- town and are now minimal across the entire city, a direct result of consistent foot traffic, strong branding, and private sector confidence. Busi- nesses now plan annual operations and staffing around the city’s holiday seasons rather than rely- ing solely on the traditional summer peak; and Whereas, Conway’s holiday programming offers experiences for all ages, cultures, and backgrounds, from family-oriented celebrations to immersive artistic installations. The city actively partners with schools, churches, civic organizations, local businesses, and the Latino community to ensure broad participation and shared ownership of events; and Whereas, designation of Conway as the Hol- iday Capital of South Carolina would serve as a statewide marketing asset, promoting the Palmetto State’s tourism, hospitality, and arts sectors. It also would encourage other munici- palities to pursue complementary seasonal pro- gramming, strengthening cultural tourism and economic vitality across the state. Now, therefore, Be it resolved by the House of Representatives, the Senate concurring: That the members of the South Carolina Gen- eral Assembly, by this resolution, dedicate the City of Conway in Horry County as the Holiday Capital of South Carolina. Be it further resolved that a copy of this resolu- tion be presented to Conway Mayor Barbara Jo Blain and City Administrator Adam Emrick. “Our historic downtown, our tree lined streets, and our shared pride have created something that reaches far beyond our city limits. In 2025 alone, millions of visitors expe- rienced Conway during the holidays, drawn in by something you help create every single year. This designation is more than a title. It is a reflection of who we are and what we con- tinue to build together,” the City of Conway posted on Facebook following the resolutions passing. PHOTO PROVIDED BY CITY OF CONWAY Members of Conway City Council and city staff accepted a resolution recognizing Con- way as the Holiday Capital of South Carolina on Tuesday, April 28 at the South Carolina State House. and still has to physically know how and where to nail the shoe onto the hoof. “I get my shoes and tools from S.C. Tool Company,” Ward said. “I’ve been getting supplies from them since I was 16 or so. It’s more cost-effective time wise.” He has a truck full of tools and shoes he takes everywhere he goes. His love of his work shines through as he goes through the process of taking caring of a horse’s hoof. He can tell you exactly what it takes to make a horse comfortable, knowledge that has come from years of experience. Ward says trimming the hoof is the most important part of the process. He points to such minute details of making sure the hoof is aligned with the horse’s shoulder angle, not something you probably would have heard many years ago in a blacksmith shop. “You have to be able to read the horse,” he said. “The horse will let you know when something isn’t right.” His client base covers much of upper South Carolina and eastern North Carolina with some having been on board for 15 years or more. Many of the clients are on a five to six-week rotation, “mostly for maintenance.” If the horse is well-mannered, Ward says he can do all four hooves in about 45 minutes. Some days, that means 5-7 horses in a day’s work. That equates to about 200 horses he takes care of a year. Being a farrier can be hard on the body, especially dealing with bending, lifting, the heat and bugs. Ward laughed that a good tool for a farrier is knowing a good chiropractor. Another horse passion that Ward has had since he was a small kid in Leland is barrel racing, something that he con- tinues today and has passed on to his two kids. “I started running barrel races when I was 5 years old,” he said. “My daddy strapped me to the saddle on my pony. I was 8 when I rode my first real barrel horse.” Today, folks far and wide come to Ward to have him train their barrel horses. It seems there a lot more barrel racers around than most people realize. Ward says he loves training the horses and the young riders. “The main thing I try to teach them is to love what they do,” he said. “The competition can be intense and I tell them to just enjoy it and have fun.” Son Waymon, 15, and daughter Aaliyah, 14, have followed in dad’s footsteps when it comes to barrel racing. Both have qualified for the Youth World Championships. Proud mom Tina said they qualified last year, too, and made the finals on their first try. “They were so proud to win those buckles,” she added. Today, dad and the kids still compete in area rodeos and shows. “They’re so competitive against each other,” Tina laughed. Ward said horse shoeing has opened up “so many doors” for him over the years. “It’s more than just a career,” he said. “It’s a passion. Former Seahawk and Clemson star Adam Randall was selected by the Baltimore Ravens in the fifth round of the NFL Draft on Saturday. The 6-foot-3, 232-pound running back was the 174th player taken in the 2026 NFL Draft. Randall, a converted wide receiver, led Clemson with 814 yards and 10 touchdowns rushing in the 2025 season. He became just the fourth player in Clemson history to have 750 yards rushing and 750 yards receiving for a career. The others are Tra- vis Zachery, C.J. Spiller and Travis Etienne. In the 2026 season, Randall caught 36 passes for 254 yards and 3 touchdowns. Injuries slowed Randall earlier in his career at Clem- son, including torn ACL in 2022, a broken left hand in 2023 and a toe stress fracture in 2024. Randall will be competing for the No. 3 running back slot on the Ravens’ depth chart, according to espn.com. A stellar high school career at Myrtle Beach, including a state championship in 2018, elevated Randall’s status. In his senior year, Randall caught 65 passes for 1,267 yards and 16 touchdowns. The Shrine Bowl selection had 325 yards rushing on 45 car- ries for the Seahawks. Randall is the first Horry County football player drafted into the NFL since Socastee’s Hunter Renfrow was drafted by the Las Vegas Raiders in 2019.
