These standards are intended to address subject use-specific characteristics and a determination by the Planning Director that such use(s) conform(s) to all potential site impacts that are not full addressed by base district regulations. Uses subject to this Article shall comply with all applicable regulations standards set forth herein in addition to the regulations of for that specific use and the zoning district in which such the use is proposed to be located. Applications to construct or alter conditional uses shall be processed in accordance with the standards set forth herein for permitted uses. Uses subject to Supplemental Use Standards are identified Applicable conditional uses shall be shown in Article 4, Use Tables. Where expressly stated, certain uses or site In addition to the conditions may require administrative review or special exception approval by the Board of Zoning Appeals in order to evaluate and mitigate site-specific impacts set forth in this Article, the Planning Director and/or the Technical Review Committee (TRC) may require additional provisions reasonable as deemed necessary to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the general public. Such review shall be limited to the criteria identified in the applicable section(s) of this Article. 5.1.1 Adult Entertainment Establishments Adult entertainment establishments include, but are not limited to: cabarets, bookstores, drive-in theaters, theaters, peep shows, adult model studios, sexual encounter centers, escort services and motels, as defined herein, and any other establishment which contains activities characterized by the performance, depiction or description of “specified sexual activities”, or “specified anatomical areas”. Adult entertainment establishments shall be permitted as conditional uses in the Light Industrial (LI) and Heavy Industrial (HI) districts provided the following requirements standards are met: A. Number. No more than one (1) adult use as classified above shall be located on any lot. B. Location. Adult entertainment establishments shall not be located closer than: 1. 1,000 feet from residential zoning districts or residential use in the City of Conway (R, RA, RR, R-1, R-2, R- 3, R-4, or residential within a MU or PD Zoning District) or equivalent residential zoning districts or use in Horry County. [ZA2018-12-17(A)] 2. 1,000 feet from any religious institution, day care facilities, public or private education facility, Community Support Services / Facility, Outpatient Treatment Facility, public park, public library, cemetery, or any motion picture establishment which shows G or PG rated movies to the general public on a regular basis. [ZA2019-04-01(D)] 3. 2,000 feet from any other adult use, provided that this shall not apply to any establishment or cabaret that does not provide adult entertainment more than twelve (12 times per calendar year). 4. Measurements of distance separation shall be in a straight line from the closest points of the buildings in which the adult uses are located. C. Ownership Disclosure. If a person who applies to operate an adult entertainment business is an individual, he must sign the application for a permit as applicant. If a person who applies to operate an adult entertainment business is other than an individual, each individual who has a ten (10%) percent or greater interest in the business must sign the application for a permit and/or license as applicant. If a corporation is listed as owner of an adult business, or as entity which wishes to operate such business, each individual having a ten (10%) percent or greater interest in the corporation must sign the application for a permit and/or license as applicant. All corporate officers shall also sign the application. The fact that a person possesses other types of state or county permits and/or licenses does not exempt him from the requirements of obtaining a sexually oriented business permit and/or license. D. Sale and/or Consumption of Alcohol Prohibited. The sale and/or consumption of alcoholic beverages in -- 85 of 137 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 5 –Specific Supplemental Use Regulations and Development Standards 5-4 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended November 3,2025 conjunction with any adult entertainment establishment shall be prohibited. E. An adult entertainment establishment shall neither employ nor permit the admittance / patronage of any person who is under 18 years of age. F. Inspections. The management of any adult entertainment establishment shall permit representatives of the Police, Fire, Construction Services, Planning/Development Department or other City or State Agencies to inspect the premises at any time it is open for business. G. Revocation of Zoning Compliance. The Planning Director shall revoke a Certificate of Zoning Compliance, thereby suspending the operation of any adult entertainment establishment, for any of the following: 1. The giving of false or misleading information by the applicant at any time in the application process; 2. For the illegal sale of any controlled substance on the premises; 3. For the arrest and conviction of any owner or employee (unless said employee is discharged immediately) for any violation of Title 44 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, 1976 as amended, relating to controlled substances; and/or violation of any State or Federal crime involving moral turpitude and/or violation of Title XVI, Chapters 3, 15, 23, and 25 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, 1976, as amended; and/or for the arrest and conviction of any owner or employee for any violation of Title 16 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, 1976, as amended; 4. Failure to permit inspections by authorized City and State agencies or personnel; 5. Violation of the age restrictions as set forth herein. H. Exterior Portions of Regulated Establishments. 1. It shall be unlawful for an owner or operator of a regulated establishment to allow the merchandise or activities of the regulated establishment to be visible from any point outside such regulated establishment. 2. It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of a regulated establishment to allow the exterior portions of the regulated establishment to have flashing lights, or any words, lettering, photographs, silhouettes, drawings, or pictorial representations of any manner except to the extent permitted by the signage provisions of this section and Article 11. 3. It shall be unlawful for the owner or operator of a regulated establishment to allow exterior portions of the regulated establishment to be painted any color other than a single achromatic color. This provision shall not apply to any regulated establishment if the following conditions are met: a. The regulated establishment is a part of a commercial multi-unit center; b. The exterior portions of each individual unit in the commercial multi-unit center, including the exterior portions of the regulated establishment are painted the same color as one another or are painted in such a way so as to be a component of the overall architectural style or pattern of the commercial multi-unit center. 4. Nothing set forth herein shall be construed to require the painting of an otherwise unpainted exterior portion of a regulated establishment. I. Signage. 1. The parking pad shall be located on the adjacent parcel, paved with concrete and include the following: 1. A van accessible ADA space and access aisle with appropriate signage 2. ADA compliant sidewalk ramp(s) at adjacent sidewalk(s). 3. A minimum of four (4) parking spaces, in accordance with the parking design standards of Article 8. 4. Wheelstops shall be installed in all parking spaces. C. The sales office / model home shall obtain a certificate of occupancy (CO) from the Construction Services Department prior to being open to the public. -- 128 of 137 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 5 –Specific Supplemental Use Regulations and Development Standards 5-47 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended November 3,2025 Section 5.3 – Temporary Uses 5.3.1 Temporary Uses Requiring a Temporary Certificate This section establishes a process for review and approval of certain uses that are intended to be of limited duration of time and that will not permanently alter the character or physical facilities of the property where they occur. The Zoning Administrator shall be authorized to issue a Temporary Certificate of Zoning Compliance for the following temporary uses: A. Carnivals, circuses, and/or fairs, for a period not to exceed ten (10) days (including setup and takedown) in any commercial district, subject to the approval of the City Council. B. Religious meetings / revivals in a tent or other temporary structure located in any district for a period not to exceed seven (7) days, including setup and takedown. C. Open lot sale of Christmas trees in any commercial district for a period not to exceed forty-five (45) days. Sales are limited to Christmas trees and associated holiday fare. D. Real estate sales offices associated with new developments or subdivisions, in any district, for a period not to exceed one (1) year, provided no cooking or sleeping accommodations are maintained in the structure. E. Contractor’s office and equipment shed, in any district, for a period not to exceed one (1) year, provided such office or shed is located on the property to which such office or shed is appurtenant. F. Public Educational and Public Higher Education Facilities may utilize portable classrooms and offices in any district for a period not to exceed five (5) years. Up to ten (10) structures are permitted as accessory structures to a permanent education facility. G. Accessory Residential Uses. Residential uses accessory to any of the above permitted temporary uses are prohibited, unless expressly permitted by the Zoning Administrator at the time of issuing the Temporary Certificate of Zoning Compliance. 5.3.2 Temporary Uses During a Declared Emergency A. Temporary Public Safety Uses during a Natural Disaster or Emergency. In the case of a natural disaster or other citywide emergency event, all public safety and/or public health land uses of a temporary nature that the city deems as necessary to serve the city during a time of need, as declared by the Mayor or City Council, shall be exempt from requiring a Temporary Certificate. This includes, but is not limited to: 1. Temporary emergency tents or shelters; 2. Triage care centers; 3. Mobile communications units or similar staging and care equipment; 4. Temporary structures needed to house displaced city departments and/or services. B. Private Temporary Uses during a Natural Disaster or Emergency. Private temporary uses in the case of a citywide declared emergency shall require Temporary Certificate of Zoning Compliance allowing the temporary use for a period of ninety (90) days. The Zoning Administrator may issue an extension of up to sixty (60) days if deemed necessary. The following are private temporary uses that will be considered for a temporary Certificate: 1. Mobile homes or on-site RVs and campers for displaced residents; 2. Portable storage units; 3. Dumpsters; 4. Portable toilets; 5. Other uses related to home repair or residential displacement related to said emergency. C. Additional Requirements. The Zoning Administrator may impose any additional requirements including -- 129 of 137 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 5 –Specific Supplemental Use Regulations and Development Standards 5-48 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended November 3,2025 landscape buffers and restrictions necessary to insure the public health, safety, comfort, and convenience. The Zoning Administrator shall have the authority to renew any Temporary Certificate of Zoning Compliance with just cause shown; however, any request by a public educational facility or public higher education facility to maintain more than 10 temporary classrooms or offices or to maintain any portable facilities for more than five (5) years is subject to review and approval by the Conway City Council. Section 5.4 – Prohibited Uses 5.4.1 Mobile Home Mobile homes shall not be permitted in any district for residential or other use, except as permitted as Temporary Uses under Section 5.3. --Reserved for additional prohibited uses-- -- 130 of 137 -- STAFF REPORT Amendment(s) to Articles 2 – Definitions, 4 – Use Tables, and 14 – Boards & Procedures PLANNING COMMISSION MTG DATE: February 5, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: V.B.2 ISSUE: Amendments to Article 2 – Definitions, Article 4 – Use Tables, and Article 14 – Boards & Procedures, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding the adoption of a special exception process and uses in which a special exception will be required. BACKGROUND: This amendment is a companion amendment to the other amendment being considered regarding specific uses in certain zoning districts (Articles 2, 4 and 5 – item V.B.1. on this agenda). One of the options included the adoption of a special exception process, which would be required to be obtained by the Board of Zoning Appeals for certain uses that are otherwise permitted in a particular zoning district but which may be a use that attracts more traffic, generates more noise or that needs additional, reasonable restrictions than what the ordinance requires to ensure that the use is compatible with the neighborhood and the adjacent owners will be protected. In essence, a special exception is an added layer of approval for a particular use. A special exception: • Is not a variance from dimensional or development standards; • Does not permit prohibited uses; • Is granted only upon a finding that the use will be compatible with surrounding properties; • Will not adversely affect public health, safety, or welfare; and • Complies with all specific standards applicable to the use and zoning district. Uses that were discussed in which a special exception may be required include: bed & breakfasts establishments, outpatient treatment facilities, payday/title loan establishments, adult entertainment establishments, body piercing / tattoo parlors, vape/smoke/tobacco shops, taverns/bars/nightclubs, gas/service stations, etc. Adoption of a special exception process would require a use, when specified, to apply to go before the Board of Zoning Appeals for review and approval, which would include a public hearing on the request. In granting a special exception, the board may attach to it such conditions regarding the location, character, or other features of the proposed building, structure, or use as the board may consider advisable to protect established property values in the surrounding areas, or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission review the proposed amendments and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 131 of 137 -- Section 14.2 – Board of Zoning Appeals 14.2.1 Duties and Powers Duties and powers of the Board of Zoning Appeals are derived from Section 6-29-800 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. A. To hear and decide appeals where it is alleged the City Zoning Administrator or their designee, erred in an order, requirement, decision, or determination. In such cases, the Board may reverse or affirm, wholly or in part, the City Zoning Administrator or their designee’s action. The Board shall have all the powers of the City Zoning Administrator or their designee in such cases and may direct the issuance of a permit. B. To hear and decide appeals for variances in specific cases when a strict application of the zoning ordinance would cause an unnecessary hardship, and approval of such variance would not be contrary to public interest or undermine the spirit of the zoning ordinance. The fact that property may be used more profitably if a variance is granted is not grounds for a variance. The Board may attach conditions to a variance that address location, character, or other features of a proposed building, structure, or use, in order to protect the established property values in the surrounding area or to promote the public health, safety, or general welfare of the community. The Board may grant a variance for an unnecessary hardship if it makes and explains in writing all of the following findings. 1. Extraordinary conditions: There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property. 2. Other Property: The extraordinary and exceptional conditions do not generally apply to other property in the vicinity. 3. Utilization: Because of the extraordinary or exceptional conditions, the application of the ordinance to a particular piece of property would effectively prohibit or unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property. 4. Detriment: The authorization of a variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property or the public good, and the character of the district will not be harmed by granting a variance. C. An affirmative vote of two-thirds (2/3) of the Board members present and voting shall be required before a variance may be granted for a use of land, a building or a structure that is prohibited in a given district, provided however that City Council may overrule the decision of the Board within thirty (30) days following the decision of the Board. In order to grant a use variance, the following finding must be determined and made part of the record: the use requested can be documented to have been a past use of the property; however, historic use alone may not be sufficient to grant a use variance. The fact that property may be utilized more profitably, should a variance be granted, may not be considered grounds for any variance. D. Special Exceptions 1. To hear and decide Special Exception requests, which is required for certain uses within a particular zoning district, as outlined in Article 4 – Use Tables, but due to the size, location, design or potential impacts of the proposed use, additional review and approval is required to ensure that the use complies with the standards for such use in this Ordinance and is compatible with surrounding uses. The Board of Zoning appeals shall consider the following criteria when evaluating a request for a special exception: a. The special exception complies with all applicable specific use regulations in Article 5 of this ordinance; b. The special exception is consistent with the character and intent of the zoning district in which it will be located; -- 132 of 137 -- c. The special exception is compatible with the existing uses in the vicinity and will not adversely affect the general welfare or character of the immediate community; d. Adequate provision is made for such items as setbacks, buffering, and sufficient screening to protect adjacent properties; e. The special exception will not result in nuisances or other adverse disturbances such as noise, odor, dust, vibrations, glare, overcrowding, or excessive traffic, in excess of what is anticipated for the zoning district or area; f. The use complies with all applicable rules, regulations, laws and standards of this ordinance; g. The use will not hinder or endanger vehicular or pedestrian movements on adjacent streets; 2. In granting a special exception, the Board may impose reasonable and additional stipulations, conditions, or safeguards as, in its judgement, will enhance and protect public safety, health and general welfare. 3. The Board may include, as a condition of approval, a time limit within which the action for which the special exception approval is required shall begin or be completed, or both. Failure to comply with the time limit imposed shall void the special exception approval. 14.2.2 Procedure for Appeals, and Variances and Special Exceptions A. Application: Any person aggrieved by an administrative action or decision or seeking relief from a requirement in the Zoning Ordinance, shall make a formal request on an application supplied by the City Zoning Administrator or their designee. Such application shall be completed in full and returned to the office of the City Planning & Development Department or emailed to Planning@ConwaySC.gov. B. Stay of proceedings: An appeal shall stay all legal proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from, unless the officer from whom the appeal is taken certifies to the Board, after the notice of appeal is filed that by reason of facts stated in the certificate, a stay would, in the opinion of the officer, cause imminent peril to life or property. In that case, proceedings shall not be stayed except by a restraining order which may be granted by the Board of Zoning Appeals or by a court of record on application, on notice to the officer from whom the appeal is taken and on due cause shown. C. Notice of hearing: Notice of regularly scheduled meetings of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall be published in a general circulation newspaper fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the meeting. D. Posting of lot: In cases involving variance requests, a notice of a variance request, special exception request or appeal shall be posted on or adjacent to the affected property in a conspicuous place fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the scheduled meeting. One such notice shall be visible from each public right-of-way that abuts the property. E. Decisions of the Board: All final decisions and orders of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall be in writing and be permanently filed in the office of the Board as a public record. All findings of fact and conclusions of law must be separately stated in final decisions or orders of the Board of Zoning Appeals, which must be addressed to parties or interest by certified mail. 14.2.3 Appeal of Board of Zoning Appeals Decision to Court Appeal of the Board of Zoning Appeals is derived from Section 6-29-820 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. A. Any person or persons jointly or severally aggrieved by a final decision of the Board of Zoning Appeals may present to a court of record a petition duly verified setting forth that the decision of the Board of Zoning Appeals is illegal, in whole or in part, specifying the grounds of the illegality. Such petition shall be presented to the court within thirty (30) days after the filing of such decision of the Board. -- 133 of 137 -- B. Upon the filing of the appeal, the clerk of court shall give immediate notice of such appeal to the City Zoning Administrator, and within thirty (30) days from the time of the notice, the City Zoning Administrator shall file with the clerk a certified copy of the proceedings held before the Board of Zoning Appeals, including transcript of the evidence heard before it, if any, and the decision to the Board including its findings of fact and conclusions. C. The filing of an appeal from a decision of the Board of Zoning Appeals shall not ipso facto act as a supersedes, but the judge of the court may, in his at their discretion, grant a supersedes upon such terms and conditions as may seem reasonable and proper. 14.2.4 Organization The rules of procedure are adopted pursuant to S.C. Code § 6-29-790 for the City of Conway Board of Zoning Appeals which consists of members appointed by the City Council. A. Officers. The officers of the Board shall be a chairman and vice-chairman elected for one (1) year terms at the first meeting of the Board in each calendar year. Such officers shall be eligible to succeed themselves. Vacancies in office shall be filled immediately for unexpired terms by regular election procedures. The Board shall appoint a member of the staff of the City of Conway as secretary of the Board B. Chairman. 1. The chairman shall be a voting member of the Board and shall: 2. Call meetings of the Board; 3. Preside at meetings and hearings; and swear in witnesses; 4. Act as spokesperson for the Board; 5. Sign documents for the Board; 6. Have orders of the Board served on parties; and 7. Perform other duties approved by the Board. C. Vice-Chairman. The vice-chairman shall exercise the duties of the chairman in the absence, disability, or disqualification of the chairman. In the absence of the chairman and vice-chairman, an acting chairman shall be elected by the members present. D. Planning Staff. The secretary shall: 1. Provide and publish notice of appeals and meetings; 2. Prepare the meeting agenda; 3. Assist the chairman in preparation of agenda’ 4. See that property involved in appeals for variances is properly posted; 5. Keep recordings and minutes of meetings and hearings; 6. Maintain Board records as public records; 7. Serve Board decisions on parties; 8. Attend to Board correspondence; and 9. Perform other duties as needed. 14.2.2 Meetings A. Time and Place. An annual schedule of regular meetings shall be adopted, published and posted in the City of Conway Planning & Development Department in December of each year. Special meetings may be called by the -- 134 of 137 -- chairman upon 24 hours’ notice, posted and delivered to all members and local news media. Meetings shall be held at the place stated in the notices and shall be open to the public. B. Agenda. A written agenda shall be furnished by City Staff to each member of the Board and the news media and shall be posted at least five (5) days prior to each regular meeting, and at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to a special meeting. Items may be removed from the agenda or postponed at a meeting by a majority vote. C. Quorum. A majority of the members of the Board shall constitute a quorum. A quorum shall be present before any business is conducted other than rescheduling the meeting. A recusal by a member does not affect the quorum, which is determined by the membership present. D. Rule of Order. Robert’s Rules of Order, Revised, shall govern the conduct of meetings except as otherwise provided by these Rules of Procedure. 14.2.3 Appeals Procedure A. Form of Appeal. Appeals from administrative decisions and applications for variances or special exceptions shall be filed on forms approved by the Board and provided to applicants by City Staff. B. Time for Appeal. An appeal from an administrative decision must be filed within fifteen (15) days after actual notice of the decision by delivery of the approved appeal form to the Planning & Development Staff of the Board who shall notify the official appealed from. C. Calendar. Appeals and applications shall be marked with the date of receipt and placed on the hearing calendar in the order in which received. Appeals shall be heard in the order on the calendar unless otherwise set by the Board for good cause shown. D. Withdrawal of Appeal. Any appeal or application may be withdrawn by written notice delivered to the Zoning Administrator or their designee prior to action by the Board. An appeal from an administrative decision which is withdrawn may not be re-filed after the fifteen (15) day time for appeal has expired. Withdrawn applications for variances may be refilled after six (6) months and shall be placed on the calendar according to the date re-filed. E. Continuances. The hearing of an appeal or application may be continued one time by the Board for good cause shown. F. Notice. Public notice of hearing of the Board shall be published in a local newspaper and posted on or adjacent to the property affected at least fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing. The notice shall contain a description of each matter to be heard and identify the applicant and property affected. -- 135 of 137 -- 14.2.4 Hearing Procedure A. Appearances. The applicant or any party in interest may appear in person or by agent or attorney. The Board may postpone or proceed to dispose of a matter on the records before it in the absence of an appearance on behalf of an applicant. B. Witnesses. Parties in interest may present testimony under oath. Witnesses may be compelled to attend by subpoena requested at least ten (10) days prior to a hearing and signed by the chairman. The Board may call its own witness when deemed appropriate. C. Cross Examination. No party shall have the right to cross-examine witnesses; however, the opportunity to examine opposing witnesses may be freely extended when conducted in an orderly manner. Intimidation of witnesses will not be allowed. D. Evidence. Relevant documents, photographs, maps, plans, and drawings will be received in the record without authentication in the form of legible copies. Relevant testimony which is not cumulative, or hearsay will be received. The chairman will rule on all evidentiary matters. Evidence may be placed in the record with or without an objection noted. 14.2.5 Conduct of Hearing A. Conduct of Hearing. The normal order of hearing, subject to modification by the chairman, shall be: 1. Statement of matter to be heard (chairman or secretary); 2. Presentation by the City Zoning Administrator; 3. Presentation by applicant; 4. Presentation by official appealed; or 5. Presentation by opponents; 6. Rebuttal by applicant; 7. Unsworn public comment when appropriate; 8. The Board may question participants at any point during the hearing; 9. Matter in which additional time is granted may be moved to the end of the agenda. B. Disposition. The Board may deliberate and make a final disposition of a matter by a majority vote of the members present at the hearing and qualified to vote; provided that not less than a quorum is qualified to vote. The vote may be taken at the same or a subsequent meeting. A member may not vote on a matter which the member has not heard. Deliberations and voting shall be conducted in public. C. Form of Order. An order shall be issued disposing of a matter by granting or denying relief with such conditions may be deemed necessary; or affirming, modifying, or reversing an administrative decision. A matter may be dismissed for lack of jurisdiction or prosecution. Findings of fact and conclusions of law shall be separately stated in an order. D. Service of Order. City Staff shall deliver a copy of an order to each party in interest by certified mail immediately upon execution of the order by the chairman. -- 136 of 137 -- E. Rehearing. The Board may grant a rehearing of an application which has been dismissed or denied upon written request filed with the Zoning Administrator or their designee within fifteen (15) days after delivery of the order accompanied by new evidence which could not reasonably have been presented at the hearing, or evidence of a clerical error or mutual mistake of fact affecting the outcome. 14.2.6 Records A. Minutes. The City Staff shall record all meetings and hearings of the Board which shall be preserved until final action is taken on all matters presented. The City Staff shall prepare minutes of each meeting for approval by the Board at the next regular meeting. Minutes shall be maintained as public records. B. Orders and Documents. The City Staff shall assist in the preparation and service of all orders of the Board in appropriate form. Copies of all notices, correspondence, documentary evidence, orders and forms shall be maintained as public records. -- 137 of 137 --

text: PC 2/5/2026 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 2026 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Greg Bryson, Allan Cornell, Thomas J. Anderson III, Absent: Kendall Brown, David Sligh Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Charlie Crosby, IT Others: Jimmy Beh, Tim White Il. Il. IV. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Bryson to approve the December 11, 2025 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input and the motion carried unanimously. SUBDIVISIONS A. Woodside Crossing, Phase 1. The applicant(s) is requesting reduction and renewal of the infrastructure Letter of Credit for phase one (1) of the Woodside Crossing subdivision, located on Four Mile Rd. Hucks gave an overview of the request regarding the financial guarantee for phase 1 of the Woodside Crossing subdivision on Four Mile Rd. Phase 1 proposed 143 single-family lots and an amenity center. The amount of the current letter of credit is $1,468,647 and now that many of the homes in phase 1 are complete, along with other major infrastructure improvements, the applicants are requesting to reduce the letter of credit to $445,729 and extend it for an additional year. Since it is the second time it is being renewed, Planning Commission is required to approve the renewal. The Technical Review Committee reviewed the request and approved the reduction. The applicant was not present. Ulrich made a motion to approve the requested reduction and renewal, Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Homestead (FKA Rivers Edge Village). The applicant is requesting approval of revised street names for the proposed development, “Homestead”, formerly known and approved as Rivers Edge Village (PIN 339-00-00-0025). PC 2/5/2026 Hucks gave an overview and stated that the applicant has requested to reserve the street names: Homestead, Fox Hound, Setter, and Spaniel. These names have been approved by Horry County emergency services. The applicant was not present. Wise made a motion to approve the street name change request; Ulrich seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.43+/- acres of property located at 1322 and 1324 Cottage Lane (PINs 338-10-02-0005 and -0006) upon annexation, from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district, or alternatively, the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that these properties are located on Cottage Lane and both are currently zoned Horry County Highway Commercial. Recently, property at the corner of Church Street and Cottage Lane was rezoned to Highway Commercial as well, which was already in the City. These 2 parcels are 2 of 4 total that remain in the County’s jurisdiction but these properties are arguably one of the biggest donut holes that remain within the City limits. The applicant is having to request annexation as a requirement to connect to City utilities. There is an existing single-family dwelling on each of the parcels. The county’s version of Highway Commercial permits single-family residential, so under the current zoning, the use is allowed. The applicant is requesting to be zoned low/medium-density residential (R-1) upon annexation. However, the City’s future land use map identifies the property as Highway Commercial, which is also consistent with the zoning of the surrounding property. Because City ordinance does not allow property to be rezoned in contrast to the future land use map or inconsistent with the zoning of surrounding property when the subject property is less than 3 acres, which could be considered spot zoning, should Planning Commission recommend the R-1 district, or any district aside from Highway Commercial, an amendment to the future land use map of the comprehensive plan will be required. Alternatively, if the property is annexed as Highway Commercial, the existing structures can remain. However, expansion of the use would not be permitted, in accordance with the Nonconformities section of the UDO. For this reason, the advertisement for this particular request was worded to give Planning Commission flexibility to recommend the Highway Commercial district in lieu of the R-1 district, rather than denial of the requested zoning. City Council approved first reading of an ordinance annexing these properties at their January 5th meeting. Planning Commission’s recommendation, if provided, will be forwarded to Council for consideration of first reading at their February 17th meeting. PC 2/5/2026 The applicant, Jimmy Beh, was present to answer questions. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to approve the rezoning request to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) District. Anderson II] seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone 0.22+/- acres of property located at 1326 Cottage Lane (PIN 338-10-02-0007) upon annexation, from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that this parcel is directly adjacent to the other parcels that were just discussed and directly behind the parcel that was rezoned to Highway Commercial within the last few months. It is currently vacant. The applicant is requesting to zone the property Highway Commercial for future commercial development. The requested zoning is consistent with the City’s future land use map and the zoning of surrounding property. Council approved first reading of an ordinance annexing the property at their January 20% meeting. Planning Commission’s recommendation of the zoning upon annexation, if provided, will be forwarded for consideration of first reading at the February 17" Council meeting. The applicant, Tim White, was present to answer questions. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to approve the rezoning request to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) District. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Request to rezone approximately one (1)+/- acre(s) of property located at 3000 Hwy 378 (PIN 337-16-04-0011) upon annexation, from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that is property is the location of what used to be a used car dealership. The property was transferred to the current owners in October 2025, and restrictive covenants were recorded for this property in 1991. In order to connect to City utilities, the new owners must request annexation, in accordance with City requirements. The rear adjacent property as well as the property on one side is within the City limits. The city’s future land use map identifies the property as Highway Commercial, and the requested zoning upon annexation is also HC. Council approved first reading of an ordinance annexing the subject property at their January 5th meeting. Planning Commission’s recommendation of the requested zoning, if provided, will be forwarded for consideration of first reading at the February 17" Council meeting. The applicant was not present. PC 2/5/2026 There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Ulrich made a motion to approve the rezoning request to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) District. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Previously Deferred...Amendment(s) to Article 2 — Definitions, Article 4— Use Tables and Article 5 — Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) regarding revisions to Permitted and Conditional uses in various zoning districts. The proposed amendment(s) would establish new or additional standards and restrictions for new and/or existing regulated commercial uses, including, but not limited to, vape/smoke/tobacco shops, alternative financial services (i.e. payday loan/title loan/cash advance services), gas/service stations (with or without a convenience store), outdoor event facilities/spaces, and other high impact uses in the City of Conway. 2. Previously Deferred...Amendment(s) to Article 2 — Definitions, Article 4— Use Tables, and Article 14 — Boards and Procedures, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) regarding the adoption of a special exception process and uses in which a special exception will be required. Hucks explained that this amendment has been discussed at previous Planning Commission meetings, and it has grown since staff began drafting the amendment. Whereas previously, it only included certain uses that warranted additional regulation, the amendment was advertised this time to include other items, such as “Outdoor Event Facilities / Spaces”, which was previously its own amendment. There have also been issues that have arose over the last couple of months that staff felt needed to be addressed in this amendment. The intent of this amendment, which will include Article 2, 4, 5 and 14 of the UDO is to restrict certain uses that have had secondary negative impacts to surrounding properties, or that there may be a proliferation of in certain areas; particularly when these uses are in close proximity to residential uses. Whereas previously, the amendment focused on uses in Highway Commercial and the Industrial districts, the amendment has evolved into a focus on uses, and all the districts in which the use is currently permitted, and where the use is permitted, but with additional standards. Some of these uses will also require special exception approval from the Board of Zoning appeals under certain circumstances. This amendment also provided staff the ability to correct administrative errors, make housekeeping revisions, define terms that are already used throughout the UDO, or that would be necessary as part of the other amendments being proposed. One of the biggest changes proposed is to the Use Tables, which will have different codes than currently. Whereas, conditional uses were identified with a “C”, they will now be uses in which supplemental standards will apply and will be coded with an “S”. Accessory uses will be identified with an “A” rather than Pa. Special Exceptions, where required, will be identified with an SE in the table. A note was also expanded, note 5 in Section 4.1 of the Use table, to clarify that the absence of a use from the Use Tables shall not be interpreted as permission to establish a use.... if there is no code in a specific block, the use is not permitted in that district. 4 PC 2/5/2026 However, staff retains the ability to consider a proposed use that is similar in nature to uses that are listed. There were several instances where a use was listed as being permitted but then listed in Article 5 as a conditional use in the same zoning district, or the zoning district was listed under a specific use, but then not listed in the Use Table for that zoning district, so these amendments sought to clean that up as well. Article 5 will be renamed to Supplemental Use and Development Standards, to be in line with the intent of Article 5 and the Use Tables of Article 4. The biggest issue with the “conditional use” language is that it implies that a conditional use permit is given for certain uses, which is not the case. The proposed amended title of Article 5 better reflects what the Article actually does: it establishes additional, site-specific standards that apply to certain uses beyond those of the base zoning district, clarifies what uses can be approved administratively, without additional review, or those that are subject to needing a special exception when additional review is needed. Because there will be uses that will require special exception approval under certain situations, using the term “conditional use” could blur standards and expose decisions to being challenged. Additionally, these changes align with modern UDO best practices that have moved away from the term “conditional use” and in favor of supplemental standards, use-specific criteria, and clearly defined review triggers. So, the biggest changes to Article 5 include the addition of restricting certain uses by adopting supplemental use standards for those uses, which include the requirement for them to receive special exception approval based on proximity to residential uses or residential zoning districts. These uses include: : Tobacco/Vape/Smoke Shops - Alternative Financial Service establishments, such as payday loan/title/loan/ or other deferred payment loan establishments - Gas/Service Stations with or without convenience stores - And a new use: Outdoor Event facilities / spaces. This particular use will be permitted via special exception only in certain zoning districts. There have been some changes made since you received the packet, including a table being inserted for Location Based Standards for the Outdoor Event Facilities or Spaces, and removing subsection G all together. You should have a revised table of changes, with the changes made since you received it last highlighted in light pink. Also, before Council will consider this amendment, it will be discussed at their upcoming budget retreat, so if, in the event, Planning Commission would like more time to review these amendments, we do have time. They would not go for first reading until the March 16th Council meeting. This amendment, and the next one on the agenda, for the creation of a special exception process, go hand in hand, so if you choose to defer this amendment, you would need to defer that amendment as well. The special exception amendment would officially adopt a special exception process, and define what it is, as well as add the requirement for a particular use listed in Article 5 to be granted a special exception. As discussed at the previous Planning Commission meeting, a special exception process provides an additional layer to certain uses under certain criteria, which includes a public hearing and a review by the board of zoning appeals who can then attach conditions to the use. A special exception: 5 PC 2/5/2026 - Is not a variance from dimensional standards - It does not prohibit uses - Is granted only upon a finding that the use will be compatible with surrounding properties - Will not adversely affect public health, safety, or welfare, and - Complies with all specific standards applicable to the use and the zoning district in which it is proposed. This amendment has been discussed at previous Planning Commission meetings, and it began with the issue of limiting certain uses that we see a lot of in the Highway Commercial district, and possibly limiting those uses to just the LI and HI districts. Other options included the adoption of different conditions based on the zoning district, adopting conditions that would apply to the use regardless of the zoning district — the condition would apply to the use if permitted in the district, as well as adopting a special exception process, that in certain situations, would require that certain uses obtain special exception approval from the board of zoning appeals. While the UDO already lists certain uses that can be considered to have secondary negative impacts as being conditional uses, meaning that the use must meet certain conditions in a zoning district in order to be permitted at a particular location, there are other uses that were either outright permitted with no specific conditions or that were not addressed in the UDO. While there may be other uses that are not mentioned or included, the top 3 that have been identified for which there are currently no conditions in place include vape/smoke or tobacco shops, payday loan/title loan establishments, which are a form of alternative financial service establishments, and gas / service stations with or without a convenience store component. As part of this amendment, there were other revisions that are included in Article 5, such as amending Section 5.1.3 — Banquet Halls to instead be Indoor event facilities and Banquet Halls, or cleaning up language in other parts of Article 5 that are not consistent with current city policy or other articles of the UDO — for instance, the Use Tables in Article 4 lists certain uses as either being permitted or conditional uses, but when you go to Article 5 to review the standards for the use that was listed as a conditional use, the district is not listed as one of the districts in which the use is allowed, or the opposite — the use if permitted outright which means that the conditions listed for a particular use in Article 5 (for example, religious institutions), would not be applicable to properties that are zoned a certain way while those conditions would be applicable to properties zoned another way, which is NOT unusual, but staff wanted to point those out because this amendment is an opportunity to determine if the conditions should apply to the use regardless of the zoning district. Another use — bars, taverns, nightclubs listed a condition that implied that Planning Commission must approve the use. I believe another use required that a conditional use permit be obtained, which is not something we currently do. When it comes to a special exception process, what we don’t want to do is create a situation where a use has specific conditions that are applicable to a site, and then even though those conditions are satisfied, they still have to go through another approval process. A special exception should be triggered by specific factors; meaning that the special exception should not apply to the use universally but only when certain factors exist. What those factors are is something that can be determined for each use. The most common one being the distance to residentially zoned property or residential uses. When the special exception is required, staff must be able to say that even when objective standards are met, certain uses may still create location-specific 6 PC 2/5/2026 VI. Vil. VII. IX. impacts that require additional review, such as traffic circulation, noise, lighting spillover, neighborhood compatibility or operational characteristics; all of which are not fully captured by setting appropriate lot sizes or separation requirements for a specific use. With that in mind, staff made some revisions to the text since the packet was sent last week, which you should have a copy of in front of you. The uses that required the most amendments to Article 5 were the vape/smoke shops, alternative financial services, and gas/service stations. The highlights of the proposed standards for each of those uses are highlighted here (PowerPoint). They include restrictions on location, such as separation requirements, instances in which a special exception would be required, and other conditions for approval. Staff would prefer that after discussion, or any public input we have, those comments be taken into consideration and used to refine the amendments, if needed, before an official recommendation is made unless Planning Commission is comfortable with the changes that have been discussed. Some of the uses that commonly require special exception approval, such as outpatient treatment facilities or adult entertainment establishments, would not require a special exception with this amendment, unless there are site specific situations that could be added that warrant additional review by the board of zoning appeals, and that could change the conditions that we currently have in place that seem to be working as intended. After much discussion, Wise made a motion to combine agenda items B.1 and B.2, seconded by Anderson. The motion carried unanimously. Wise made second motion to defer the request and public input until next month’s meeting. As well as hold a workshop for the board to further discuss the text amendments before the March 5" meeting. Ulrich seconded the motion and the motion carried unanimously. DISCUSSTION ITEMS None BOARD INPUT None STAFF INPUT None ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 5:59 pm. Approved and signed this > - oy of VAKeAA _, 2026. Tease wi pence \ > \

ADJOURNMENT -- 2 of 119 -- BY JOE WEDRA JOE.WEDRA@MYHORRYNEWS.COM Construction issues at tennis courts at three Horry County Schools may impact local tennis teams’ abilities to practice and compete as planned. According to documents received by MyHorryNews, HCS is holding a contractor — Contract Construction Inc. of Irmo — responsible for deficiencies in court surfaces and issues with asphalt instal- lation. The issues exist at the Aynor, North Myrtle Beach and St. James high school ten- nis courts. On Dec. 10, HCS Superin- tendent Clifford Jones sent an email to board members making them aware of the issues. After receiving input from a consultant and receiv- ing independent testing, it was documented that seven of the eight asphalt core sam- ples at the newly installed courts at Aynor High School failed compaction standards, Jones wrote. Additional analysis found issues with uniformity, sur- face preparation and aggre- gate gradation, which is the utilization of various size particles in the asphalt mix to fill voids. After receiving findings from project engineer CHA Consulting, Inc. of Myrtle Beach, the district sent a note to Contract Construction, letting the company know that HCS believes the per- formance issues are “directly attributable to improper construction means and methods and inadequate construction quality control/ assurance.” In his letter to the board, Jones said that HCS will continue to work with “CHA and legal counsel” to ensure compliance with contract requirements and to “protect the district’s financial and operational interests.” It is unclear when the ten- nis court issues will be fixed. According to the South Caro- lina High School League, boys tennis practice can begin on Feb. 2, and matches can be played starting Feb. 20. Girls tennis is a fall sport. My Horry News reached out to the district with ques- tions including when the issues were found, if Contract Construction was the lowest bidder for the project and if HCS is going to have the com- pany perform improvements on the courts. The district’s spokes- person, Lisa Bourcier, sent back a statement: “Horry County Schools is working closely with our construc- tion partners regarding the new tennis courts at several of our schools. As with any construction project, we are confident that we will be able to rectify any issues that may occur during the construction process.” Because the district found the issues to be construc- tion-related, HCS denied Contract Construction’s change order request and is not authorizing any addition- al compensation to the com- pany at this time. HCS had budgeted $5.5 million for the contractor to pave and improve the tennis courts at the three high schools at issue, plus Socastee High School. The contract also includes parking improvements at North Myr- tle Beach and St. James. In a letter, HCS made Con- tract Construction aware that they expect the company to proceed according to the con- tract’s corrective/remedial obligations for nonconform- ing work and coordinate with both the district and CHA on the approved remediation scope. CHA recommended to HCS the removal and replacement of asphalt courts placed to date at Aynor, North Myrtle Beach and St. James. The next steps and time- line of the status of courts at all three schools is currently unclear. MyHorryNews reached out to Contract Construction for comment, but the company had not responded by the time of publication. DECEMBER 18, 2025 | LOCAL | THE HORRY INDEPENDENT | CONWAY, S.C. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Greg Bryson, Allan Cornell, Thomas J. Anderson III, David Sligh, Kendall Brown Absent: Ellen Watkins Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Marsha Ponder, Assistant Zoning Administrator; Nancy Alvarez, Assistant Planner; Charlotte Peterson, Assistant Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT Others: Kenny Walsh, Joey Singleton, Dennis Disebato, Matt McCourry, Charles Rietman, Seth June & others I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Anderson to approve the November 6, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. PUBLIC INPUT No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. IV. SUBDIVISIONS A. The Reserve at Elmhurst – The applicant(s) is requesting approval of: The Reserve at Millpond, a 125- single-family lot, three phase development and the associated street names for the project (PIN 338-00- 00-0004). Hucks gave an overview of the request stating that the applicant is seeking preliminary plan approval for The Reserve at Elmhurst, located off of Oak Street. The proposed development will contain a total of 125 single- family lots in 3 phases. This development is part of a larger development, Elmhurst, which has 4 previous phases that began development in 1998, with phase 4 approved in 2021. Although not yet developed, what is considered as Phase 5 of Elmhurst received preliminary plan approval in 2024. Also requested is street name approval for 3 proposed street names: Everly Pass, Hartwell Drive, and Winslow Bend, which has been reserved for this development by Horry County. If Planning Commission recommends approval, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval of the Technical Review Committee. The applicant, Kenny Walsh, was present and further explained the request. -- 4 of 119 -- PC 12/11/2025 2 Wise made a motion to give PC approval and street name approval contingent upon all TRC comments being addressed. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Country Manor Phase 8 – The applicant, Matthew McCourry, is requesting a reduction to the required amount of open space as well as a waiver for suitability standards (PIN 326-07-03-0068). Hucks gave an overview of the request stating that the applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval for phase 8 of Country Manor, along with a request in the reduction of the amount of required open space as well as a waiver in the suitability requirements for the proposed open space. Country Manor is located off of Four Mile Rd. The first 7 phases of Country Manor were developed between 2001 and 2006. Phase 8 received preliminary plan approval in 2008; however, vested rights have long expired with no site improvements installed for phase 8. The most recent plans for phase 8 propose to include 11 lots across approx. 2.62 acres. Last year, Planning Commission approved a design modification to waive the access management standards that the UDO now requires that limits the number of lots or units which can be accessed on one entrance, to allow the development of the additional 11 lots. By doing so, it allows the completion of Hamilton Way and Murphy Way, which was never completed in previous phases, leaving 3 dead-ends in this development and no appropriate (dust-free) turnarounds for emergency vehicles, as well as preventing one lot in phase 5 from being developed due to the road not being installed in front of the property. In addition to preliminary plan approval, the applicant is seeking a design modification from the open space requirements, including 2 modifications: 1) a reduction in the amount of required open space, along with the elimination of the fee-in-lieu requirement; and 2) a modification in the suitability requirements for open space. Under the current open space requirements, which were amended last year, developments are required to provide 1,000 sq. ft. of open space per lot or unit. What didn’t change was the requirement for the developer to pay a fee in lieu of providing open space when less than 1 acre of open space is calculated as being required. The caveat being that they could opt to install open space rather than paying that fee in lieu, but it had to be a minimum of 1 acre in size and meet all of the applicable criteria for open space. Based on the number of lots (11), 11,000 sq. ft. is what would be required short of the requirement of it being a min. of 1 acre in size, with 2,750 sq. ft. of that required to be active open space (25% of the total amount of open space to be provided must be “active” open space). What the developer is proposing is to provide 8,519 sq. ft. of wooded area as open space (which will be considered “passive”). The plans also show that an additional 610 sq. ft. will be conveyed to the city to enlarge an existing pump station site. If Planning Commission approves the requested design modifications, there will be 8,519 sq. ft. of open space provided, which would be considered passive, and the fee in lieu would no longer be applicable with the acceptance of the reduction in the amount of open space to be provided. If Planning Commission approves the applicant’s requests, including the design modifications and preliminary plan approval, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval of the TRC. -- 5 of 119 -- PC 12/11/2025 3 Jamie Steele, agent for applicant, was present and further explained the request. The board, applicant, and staff discussed the request at length. Ulrich made a motion to approve the design modifications from the open space requirements, including a reduction to the amount of required open space and a modification to the open space suitability requirements. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.44+/- acres of property located on Main Street (PIN 325-13- 01-0013), from the City of Conway Low/ Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that this property is currently zoned R-1 (Low/Medium-Density Residential) and the applicant is seeking to rezone the property to Highway Commercial for future potential development. The request is consistent with the city’s future land use map, which also identifies the property as Highway Commercial, a district that is intended to accommodate auto-dependent commercial development. The HC district is typically located along major arterial and highway corridors where auto-dependent development can occur, while also promoting orderly growth, coordinated access, and functional corridor aesthetics, such as those that are listed in the City’s Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), which this property will be subject to if developed commercially. Property on either side of this property is zoned HC. Property across from it is zoned Horry County Heavy Industrial. Property located behind the subject property is the Ivy Glen development, which is zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential. The requested zoning will be forwarded to Council for consideration of First reading at their January 5th meeting, along with Planning Commission’s recommendation. The applicant, Joey Singleton, was present to answer any questions. Sligh recused himself from this item. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Bryson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Brown seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone approximately 0.15+/- acres of property located at 182 Quail Run (PIN 383- 09-04-0040) from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-10) district to the City of Conway Low/ Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that this property is within the Quail Creek subdivision, and annexation is being required as a condition of receiving city utilities, due to a change in property ownership, and in accordance with restrictive covenants that were filed in 2010. The current zoning is Horry County SF10, and the requested zoning upon annexation is R-1, low/medium-density residential. The city’s future land use map identifies -- 6 of 119 -- PC 12/11/2025 4 the property, along with the surrounding lots within Quail Creek, as medium-density residential; however, the other properties that have been annexed over the years were annexed as low/medium-density residential, so the requested zoning district is consistent with the zoning of surrounding properties. Eight other properties within Quail Creek have been annexed into the City, with the adjacent parcel annexed in 2023, making the subject property contiguous. Council approved first reading of the annexation of the property at their November 3rd meeting, and the requested zoning upon annexation will be forwarded to Council for consideration of First Reading at their January 5th meeting, along with Planning Commission’s recommendation. The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Brown to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Bryson made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Request to rezone approximately 0.4+/- acres of property located at 5007 Presbyterian Dr. (PIN 383-08-02-0010), from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-10) district to the City of Conway Low/ Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that this property is within the College Park subdivision, and annexation is now being required as a condition of receiving city utilities, due to a change of ownership of the property, and in accordance with restrictive covenants that were recorded in 1998. The property contains a single-family dwelling. The requested zoning is consistent with the City’s future land use map, which also identifies the property as low/medium-density residential (R-1). The requested zoning upon annexation will be forwarded to Council for consideration of First Reading at their January 5th meeting, along with Planning Commission’s recommendation. The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Bryson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Cornell made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 4. Request to rezone approximately 0.37+/- acres of property located at 801 Donald St. (PIN 369- 12-04-0002), from the Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF-20) district to the City of Conway Low/ Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district upon annexation. Hucks stated that annexation of this property is being required as a condition of receiving city utilities, due to a change in ownership of the property and a new utility account in the name of the property’s -- 7 of 119 -- PC 12/11/2025 5 personal representative, according to Probate documentation that was submitted in conjunction with the annexation. There have been restrictive covenants on file for this property since 1987. 11 other properties in this neighborhood have been annexed, with the neighboring property annexed in 2023. The current zoning is Horry County SF10 and the requested zoning upon annexation is R-1, low/medium- density residential, which is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. Council approved first reading of an ordinance to annex the subject property at their November 17th meeting. The requested zoning upon annexation will be forwarded to council for consideration of first reading at their January 5th meeting, along with Planning Commission’s recommendation. The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Ulrich made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. VI. DISCUSSION ITEMS Huck provided a discussion on the proposed amendments to the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). Her remarks addressed revisions to the permitted and conditional uses within the Highway Commercial (HC), Light Industrial (LI), and Heavy Industrial (HI) zoning districts, proposed regulations concerning the operation and allowance of outdoor event spaces, and the adoption of a special exception process for designated uses. VII. BOARD INPUT None VIII. STAFF INPUT Hucks introduced the new staff members to the Planning & Development Dept. IX. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:37 pm. Approved and signed this ___________ day of _____________, 2026. ____________________________________ Jessica Wise, Chairperson -- 8 of 119 -- STAFF REPORT University Suites PLANNING COMMISSION MTG DATE: January 8, 2025 AGENDA ITEM(S): IV.A. and IV.B. ISSUE(S): 1. The applicant is requesting P.C. approval of the: University Suites Expansion, a multi-family project located along Technology Boulevard, directly across from the existing University Suites; 2. The applicant is requesting that Planning Commission waive the requirement of a post- development appraisal and instead recommend the acceptance of an alternative valuation for the open space fee-in-lieu amount; and 3. The applicant is requesting that the Planning Commission recommend approval of a reduced fee- in-lieu to City Council for consideration. APPLICANT(S): Diamond Shores Surveying LLC (representing: Alfonso Sangtian) PIN(s): 383-10-03-0020 BACKGROUND: July 2025 The initial preliminary plans were submitted for review on the 7th July 2025 City Council amended setbacks for all in common developments to 25-ft from all exterior project boundaries on the 21st Sep. 2025 a variance granted, by the Board of Zoning Appeals, to reduce the rear setback and one side-yard setback for the project Dec. 2025 This application for a design modification was submitted ANALYSIS: Issue #1 The project is located on a: 1.75-acre parcel, zoned: R-3 (High Density Residential). The proposed development consists of: 2-two story buildings, containing: 12-two bedroom units in each structure (24-units total). (843) 488 -9888 ph (84 3) 4 88-98 90 fax 2940 JERRY BARNHILL BLVD - CONWAY, SC 2 9527 PIN #: 367-13-01-0031 Legend UTILITY SERVICE AREA PARCELS -- 28 of 119 -- -- 29 of 119 -- -- 30 of 119 -- -- 31 of 119 -- STAFF REPORT Amendments to Articles 2 – Definitions, 4 – Use Tables, and 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the UDO PLANNING COMMISSION MTG DATE: January 8, 2026 AGENDA ITEM: V.B.1 ISSUE: Amendments to Article 2 – Definitions, Article 4 – Use Tables, and Article 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to Permitted and Conditional Uses in various zoning districts. The proposed amendments would establish additional standards and restrictions for certain regulated commercial uses, including, but not limited to, vape/smoke/tobacco shops, cash advance/payday loan establishments, and other high impact uses in the City of Conway. BACKGROUND: Over the past several months, staff has been researching various options for limiting or restricting certain uses in some of the City’s commercial zoning districts; particularly in the Highway Commercial district. This came as a result of a request to rezone a property, already zoned HC, which sought to rezone to a district that allowed multifamily development and was ultimately denied; however, the concern of the existing zoning of HC directly adjacent to an established single-family residential neighborhood and the potential uses that could be established remained. Therefore, staff was asked to look at the uses and ways to limit them when adjacent to residential areas. Staff began looking at the Use Table in Article 4 of the UDO to determine which uses did not currently have specific conditions associated with the use, including those that there have been a proliferation of over the past several years, and which often have secondary negative impacts on surrounding properties. Staff researched how other cities and towns regulated these uses, if at all, and explored options for additional regulation in the City of Conway of certain uses; particularly, vape shops/smoke shops/tobacco shops and payday/title loan establishments, known as “alternative financial services.” Other uses considered were gas stations/convenience stores and the proximity to residential areas where the use is directly abutting a residentially zoned property or use. Options discussed with Planning Commission the past couple of months included separation requirements, sunset clause/amortization, adoption of a special exception process, and removing certain uses from the HC district entirely and limiting these uses to the LI and HI districts only, or a combination of the aforementioned options. The proposed amendments that have been included are a multiprong solution, with some uses becoming more limited or restricted, such as establishing separation requirements, as well as the requirement of some uses to obtain a special exception in certain instances. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission review the proposed amendments and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 32 of 119 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 2 – Definitions 2-1 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended November 3, 2025 Article 2.
