Providers shall provide documentation demonstrating exemption through DSS licensure or proof of registration, as applicable. d. Maximum Number of Children. No more than six (6) children may be cared for at any one time, -- 93 of 98 -- ARTICLE 5 – Specific Use Regulations, Section 5.1.7 including the provider’s own children under the age of 12, unless otherwise licensed or permitted by the state (DSS). e. Neighborhood Compatibility. The use shall not produce noise, traffic, or activity that disrupts the residential character of the neighborhood. No signs advertising the use shall be permitted. f. Home-Based Business Requirements. Except as modified herein, such programs shall comply with the applicable standards for Home-Based Businesses, as set forth in Section 5.2.4 of this ordinance. -- 94 of 98 -- Issue Brief: Child Care Licensing Requirements Child Care Licensing sets standards to promote and protect the health and safety of children receiving care and to protect the employees and staff providing care. Child care providers must be licensed or registered if they: • Operate 4 or more hours a day • Operate more than 2 days a week • Care for children in your home and you care for more than 1 family not related to you Types of Care: All South Carolina child care programs are required to be one of the following: licensed, registered, approved, or legally exempt. Requirements are determined by provider type. The state defines four types of child care: • Child Care Center—A center that is licensed for 13 or more children can be commercial, faith-based, or school-based. • Group Child Care Home—A facility within a residence occupied by the operator that cares for 7 to 12 children; The number includes those living in the residence and children who are related to the operator, must be licensed. • Family Child Care Home—A facility within a residence occupied by the operator that cares for no more than 6 children; The number includes those living in the residence and children who are related to the operator; Family Child Care Centers must be registered but may choose to be licensed. • Legally-Exempt Operations—Child care center-based programs open less than 4 hours a day and/or open on school holidays; Not allowed for Family Child Care Homes or Group Child Care Homes. NOTE: Many parents rely on family members, friends, or neighbors who provide care. These types of care are not registered or licensed but are regulated. How to Become a Licensed Child Care Provider: Step 1. Attend Orientation. Interested parties will receive an application packet prior to orientation that will have all the required forms needed to apply. In addition, they will be able to ask any questions related to the process and provide resources specific to the county/town where the facility may be located. Interested parties should review the dates and times of orientation meetings available, on our website and call the Region that will monitor their location at the telephone number assigned to their specific regional office at scchildcare.org/ providers/new-applicant-orientation/ to attend orientation. Step 2. If required, submit architectural plans to the Chief Fire Marshal at the DSS Child Care Licensing Central Office: SC Department of Social Services Child Care Licensing Attn: Chief Fire Marshal P.O. Box 1520 Columbia, SC 29202-1520 Step 3. After attending orientation and the architectural plans have been approved by the Chief Fire Marshal at Child Care Licensing, the applicant must submit the Zoning Approval letter or form, the application to apply, and the fire and health inspection request to the local Child Care Licensing Regional Office that will monitor the location of the child care facility. Step 4. Once the above items have been submitted to Child Care Licensing, they will be assigned a Licensing DSS Brochure 501 (JAN 24) -- 95 of 98 -- Specialist and must complete the additional required documents located in the application packet. Those items should be completed and submitted for Child Care Licensing review. Step 5. During the review of the application, the Fire and Health Inspector and Child Care Licensing will contact them for an inspection visit. If everything meets the regulatory requirements, their application will be submitted for approval. When approved, a provisional license will be issued. Step 6. After the provisional license has been issued and the child care facility has operated with 13 or more children enrolled for at least 45 days, Child Care Licensing will re-visit to complete their full evaluation. If no deficiencies, the application will be submitted for a regular license. How SC Licensing Works: Licensing is managed by the SC Division of Early Care and Education at the SC Department of Social Services (SCDSS). Child Care Licensing regulates approximately 2,400 child care providers, through four regional offices. There are several key functions that build safe, healthy environments for children: 1. Inspections: These help to ensure that providers comply with state laws and regulations through a yearly unannounced inspection. All regulated child care providers including legally-exempt and Family, Friend and Neighbor providers will receive the required annual health and safety inspections. 2. State and Federal Comprehensive Background Checks: As required by state law, federal and state background checks must be conducted on all child care staff members who work in child care facilities. More information on background checks can be found at scchildcare.org/providers/in-state-background-check- requirements. Required background checks include: • SC Child Abuse and Neglect Central Registry & Database checks and out of state Abuse and Neglect checks if child care staff lived out of SC in the past 5 years. o For all center-based care, licensed, registered, and legally exempt o Licensed and registered home child care facilities o Family, Friend, and Neighbor checks for providers enrolled in the SC Scholarship Program • In-state and National Sex Offender Database checks for all child care facility types, including legally exempt child care facilities and Family, Friend and Neighbor providers • State and Federal fingerprinting for all child care facility types, including legally exempt child care facilities and Family, Friend and Neighbor providers The State of South Carolina uses a digital fingerprint service. Find the complete information at sc.state.identogo.com. 3. Investigations: Child Care Licensing investigates complaints against regulated facilities and reports of facilities or individuals operating without a license or registration. 4. Regulation: A state Advisory Committee is responsible for reviewing the regulations regarding their improvement. Staff to Child Ratios: The following staffing ratios apply at all times children are present on the premises at a child care center and during activities away from the center. Age Staff-to-Child Ratios Birth to one year 1:5 One to two years 1:6 Two to three years 1:8 Three to four years 1:12 Four to five years 1:17 Five to six years 1:20 Six to twelve years 1:23 DSS Brochure 501 (JAN 24) -- 96 of 98 -- EXCERPT FROM THE 2.6.25 PC MTG MINUTES -- 97 of 98 -- -- 98 of 98 --

title: APPD_8.7.25 PC MINUTES
text: PC 8/7/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, August 7, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Allan Cornell, Thomas J. Anderson III, David Sligh, Greg Bryson Absent: Ellen Watkins, Kendall Brown Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Marcus Cohen, IT; Sydney Livingston, Summer Intern Others: Vicki Smink, John Powell, Denise Linderson, Ellen Powell, Justin Carter, Sue Taylor, Robert Wilfong, Belinda Weeks, Cheryl Raven, Deb Malfara, Thomas Aniello, Sharon Aniello, Ernestine Fabrizzi, David Bartus, John Danford, Orion Loftis, Frank Derosa, James Baldwin and Others. I. CALL TO ORDER Il. Ill. IV. Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Cornell to approve the July 10, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT John Powell, Ellen Powell, Justin Carter, Sue Taylor spoke during public input. Sligh made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. SUBDIVISIONS A. DESIGN MODIFICATIONS 1. Brookhaven Planned Development (PD). The applicant, Thomas & Hutton Eng., is requesting a waiver from the access management standards for several phases of the Brookhaven PD, and approval of street names for said development. Hucks stated that the applicant, Thomas & Hutton, has submitted a request for a waiver from access management standards applicable to several phases of a proposed Planned Development. Additionally, the applicant seeks approval of street names associated with the project. The Commission previously held a workshop in November 2023 to review the potential annexation, rezoning, and development agreement for multiple adjacent tracts totaling approximately 486 acres. In August 2024, the Commission recommended approval for rezoning 446 acres to Planned Development (PD) and endorsed the Development Agreement. These tracts were subsequently annexed into the city and rezoned to PD. City Council approved the Development Agreement. 1 PC 8/7/2025 Following this: e March 2025: Initial Master Phase Plan submitted; comments returned. e June 2025: Revised Master Phase Plan submitted; further comments provided. e July 2025: Application for Design Modification submitted. Phase Development Overview: e Phase 1; 83 lots with one access point via Hwy 378; includes a 3-lane entrance and an all-weather emergency access (~1,400 ft +) connecting to Juniper Bay Road. e Phase 2: Adds 79 lots; total of 162 lots accessed through Phase 1's entrance. e Phase 3: 78 lots accessed solely from Juniper Bay Road; connection to Hwy 378 entrance planned for Phase 4. e Phase 4: 77 lots accessed via Dunn Shortcut Road; secondary access to be constructed in Phase 15 through Victorinox Road (St. Johns Ridge stub-out). The applicant is requesting approval of street names included in the issue paper for this meeting. Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, should the Planning Commission recommend approval of the applicant’s requests, staff advises that such approval be made contingent upon the final review and approval by the Technical Review Committee (TRC). The applicant, John Danford, Thomas & Hutton, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Bryson made a motion to approve the request for the street names for the proposed development as presented. Wise seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to approve the Phase 1 request for one point of access in the all-weather emergency access onto Juniper Bay. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried 4-2 with Ulrich and Bryson voting in opposition to the approval. Wise made a motion to deny the Phase 2 request to create an additional 79 units without providing another entrance. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried 5-1 with Sligh voting in opposition to the denial. Wise made a motion to approve the Phase 3 request, allowing one access point on Juniper Bay Road for the proposed 78 lots. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried 5-1 with Bryson voting in opposition to the approval. Wise made a motion to approve the Phase 14 request as presented, noting its similarity to request numbers | and 3. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Vv. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) PC 8/7/2025 1. Request to annex 1.34+/- acres of property located behind the Coastal Centre Mall and at the end of Elizabeth Street (off 16" Ave) (PIN 338-10-02-0018), and rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the applicant, Sam Berry, RP Coastal Centre LLC, submitted an annexation and rezoning application for the subject property earlier this month when it was discovered that the parcel, which will be used for stormwater purposes, was not yet in the city limits. Following staffs review of the site plans, the applicant was informed that the parcel was still within Horry County’s jurisdiction but would need to be annexed and combined with the overall site so that the stormwater is not considered to be off-site. Like the rest of the Coastal Centre parcels, the parcel is proposed to be zoned Highway Commercial (HC) upon annexation. The property is surrounded by property that is currently vacant, zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) or Highway Commercial (HC), or directly adjacent to the Coastal Centre property, also zoned HC. The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Conservation Preservation (CP); likely due to the property being used to hold stormwater for the Coastal Centre. Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, “the intent of the CP district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district.” Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The board and staff discussed the request at length. No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The applicant was not present. Sligh made a motion to approve the rezoning request as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried. 2. Request to annex 1.08+/- (total) acres of property located on Cypress Circle, within the Conway Medical Center (CMC) campus (PIN’s 383-15-02-0024, -0025, -0026, -0027, - 0028), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Institutional (IN) district. Board member Anderson submitted a Recusal Statement form and abstained from voting on this item due to a declared conflict of interest. Anderson did not participate in the discussion or decision-making process. PC 8/7/2025, Hucks stated the applicant, Conway Medical Center (CMC), is requesting to annex these parcels into the City limits and rezone the properties Institutional (IN) upon annexation for the broader purpose of expanding parking on the Conway Medical Center (CMC) campus and seek approval of a master parking plan from Planning Commission, once annexed. The CMC campus is made up of several parcels, with these being the only remaining ones that are not yet in the city limits. These properties are located within the CMC campus and are surrounded by other medical facilities; also zoned City of Conway Institutional (IN). The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies these parcels as Institutional (IN). Per Section 3.2.8 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), “the intent of the IN district is to provide areas for the development of medical, educational, and higher educational facilities in a campus- like setting. More specifically, the district is intended to accommodate the development styles, uses, and accessory uses associated with these facilities. This district is not intended for businesses engaging in retail sales, except for those businesses that are clearly accessory to and specifically provide services to the permitted principal use.” Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mig. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, James Baldwin was present to answer any questions. No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board, staff and applicant discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the rezoning request as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Request to annex approximately 0.35+/- acres of property located at 152 Lander Drive (PIN 383-15-01-0046), and rezone from the Horry County Residential (SF10) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks stated the property was transferred to the current owners in May of 2024. It is unknown as to why annexation has not been required until now; however, in instances where property receives city utilities and is contiguous to the city limits, annexation must be requested at the time services are requested. If the property is not yet contiguous at the time in which city services are requested, a restrictive covenant is typically required to be recorded, which bounds current and future owners to annexation requirements should the property become contiguous in the future. The legal residence of the current owners is not a local address. The property is located within the Coastal Heights subdivision. The abutting property was annexed in 2018 and property directly across the road was annexed in 2013, making this property contiguous. There are 3 other lots on Lander Drive that are within the City limits and 20 other lots on Clemson Rd that have been amnexed into the City, to date; all of which are within the Coastal Heights subdivision. PC 8/7/2025 The Coastal Heights subdivision is a single-family neighborhood, containing single-family detached dwellings on roughly quarter-acre parcels. The CCU Hackler Course abuts the homes within the subdivision, which is not in the city limits. Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mtg. Staffrecommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the rezoning request as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 4. Request to rezone approximately 109.13 +/- acres of property located at or near the commer of Cultra Rd. and Oak Street (PIN 325-00-00-0011) from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Medium-Density Residential (R-2) district upon annexation into the City of Conway. Board member Anderson submitted a Recusal Statement form and abstained from voting on this item due to a declared conflict of interest. Anderson did not participate in the discussion or decision-making process. Hucks stated the subject property is proposed to be annexed into the City for residential development. The property is within the city’s utility service area, thus requiring annexation to be requested. Surrounding developments — Rivertown Row North, Kingston Bay and Elmhurst, are also zoned Medium-Density Residential (R-2). Midtown Village, which directly abuts this property, is zoned High- Density Residential (R-3). A large portion of the subject property is located within the AE flood zone, which runs through the middle of the parcel (see attached maps). While development is permitted within flood zones, provided the affected property meets the required elevation, staff does not support rezoning portion(s) of property within a flood zone to a district that would permit residential development. In 2023, Council adopted an ordinance that permits parcels containing environmentally sensitive areas to be split-zoned, which is otherwise prohibited, with such areas being zoned Conservation Preservation (CP) upon annexation of property or when property is proposed to be rezoned. Given that there is a small portion of the property within the floodway, in which no development can occur, and that the general area has been prone to flooding, should annexation proceed, this would be an opportunity to discuss the possibility of zoning the portions within a flood zone / floodway to CP with the applicant. In this instance, the applicant would need to submit a survey showing the areas within the flood zone / floodway so that they could be mapped accordingly should the split zoning be preferred. Surrounding in-City zoning includes Neighborhood Commercial (NC), High-Density Residential (R-3), Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), and Medium-Density Residential (R-2). The area is primarily single-family residential, with limited established commercial uses. There is a gas station/convenience PC 8/7/2025 store (Sun House) with a few tenant spaces containing limited commercial uses, including a dog grooming business, immediately adjacent to the subject property. Surrounding County zoning includes mostly residential, including Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF20) on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes, and Residential, including mobile homes (MSF20), also on 20,000 sq. ft. min. lot sizes. Abutting property is also zoned Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA). The John T. Henry Auction location is near the subject property, which is also zoned CFA. Horry Electric is also nearby, on the opposite side of Cultra Rd, which is zoned Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI). The City’s future land use map provides three (3) future land use designations for the subject property. For the portion with frontage along Cultra Rd, the future land use is shown as Neighborhood Commercial (NC). Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small-scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. A larger portion of the property is shown as Conservation Preservation (CP) on the city’s future land use map. Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the CP district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The portion abutting Midtown Village and Conway Christian School is shown as High-Density Residential on the future land use map. Per Section 3.2.5 of the UDO, the intent of the high-density residential district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was present to answer questions. Vicky Smith, John Powell and Ellen Powell spoke during public input. Sligh made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board, staff and applicant discussed the request at length. Sligh made a motion to defer the rezoning request until the September 4th meeting. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 5. Requesting Deferral...Request to rezone approximately 10.97+/- acres of property at 1808 Rhue Street (PIN 368-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Institutional (IN) district. PC 8/7/2025 Ulrich made a motion to defer the rezoning request. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Reguesting Deferral...Amendments to Article 6 — Design Standards, Article 13 — Administrative Agencies and Functions, and Article 14 — Boards and Procedures, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for annexation and amendments to the City’s Official Zoning Map. Wise made a motion to defer the amendment request. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Amendments to Article 2 — Definitions and Article 5 — Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for Educational Facilities. Hucks provided an overview of the request, which stemmed from a request to rezone property where the former Whittemore Middle School from the current zoning of Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) to the Institutional (IN) district, so that the school district could utilize the property to house their Conway area Adult Education Center, to include a limited childcare function, a therapeutic learning center for students, the districts JROTC program, Administrative offices, etc. The complex will be known as the HCS Rivertown Complex. However, due to public concerns regarding the uses that would be permitted if rezoned to IN, should the school district choose to move the facility or sell the property in the future, staff began looking at ways the proposed uses could be permitted as accessory uses to a public educational facility, or amend the permitted uses to allow the proposed uses when the buildings are used by a public school. The proposed amendments seek to redefine what an educational facility is (Art. 2 — Definitions) and amend the specific use regulations (conditions) in Sec. 5.1.9 (attached). There are 4 options provided for redefining what an educational facility is; one of which is differentiated between public and private educational facilities. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council regarding the proposed amendments. Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mtg. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. PC 8/7/2025 Ulrich made a motion to approve the amendment for Option Number 2, as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Ulrich amended his original motion and moved to approve Option Number 2, along with the amendments to Article 5.1.9 as noted. Wise seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Amendments to Article 2 — Definitions, Article 4 — Use Tables, Article 5 — Specific Use Regulations, and Article 6 — Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for Day Care Facilities. Hucks provided an overview of the request, which was initially discussed at the February 2025 Planning Commission meeting. The issue arose out of an inquiry from a prospective childcare provider, looking to open a part-time child-care facility in a strip mall setting. Currently, the City’s ordinance does not address part-time childcare, or any other type of childcare which the state deems to be “/egally exempt”, meaning the childcare center / program is open less than four (4) hours per day, no more than two (2) days per week, and on an irregular schedule, such as on school holidays. Upon closer review, staff looked at ways to include more options for childcare within the UDO, compliant with state law, without compromising the safety and security of children. There were several factors considered when drafting the proposed amendments: e According to a 2024 article from the Children’s Trust of South Carolina, one of the most significant reasons for the lack of workforce participation is the shortage of childcare. Childcare challenges center around three primary factors: access, affordability, and quality. e Access: 42% of South Carolinians live in a childcare “desert”, meaning there are 3 young children for every licensed “spot.” e Affordability: the low supply of available slots drive up costs. The average cost for center-based childcare for an infant (in 2024) is approximately $9,000 per year. e Quality: finding high-quality childcare can be a challenge due to the high (employee) turnover rates and poor employee compensation. Disparities relating to childcare (cost; access) disproportionately affect low-income and minority families because they limit workforce participation, and exacerbate inequalities in education, health and economic opportunities. Even middle-income families struggle to afford high-quality childcare, and subsidy programs often have long waiting lists or strict eligibility requirements. e Many localities include childcare regulations in their ordinances that create a barrier to home- based providers, such as requirements for home modifications, and zoning codes — including Conway’s, have not been updated to accommodate home-based care. These requirements also disproportionately affect minority or low-income women, who are most likely to seek licensing for an in-home childcare program. e Lack of centralized coordination between the multiple agencies who provide oversight of childcare (i.e. DSS, First Steps, DHEC) contribute to the gaps in service, inefficiencies, and frustration of families and providers trying to navigate the complex systems in place. What changes are advocated by the American Planning Association? e Reviewing current regulations regarding childcare facilities and amend, as needed, to remove barriers to parents entering or re-entering the workforce. e Support legislation (i.e. zoning amendments) which provide for childcare in locations convenient 8 VI. PC 8/7/2025 to neighborhoods and in public facilities such as schools, recreation centers and social service centers. Procedures should not be overly burdensome and should be related to size and land use impacts associated with the proposed facility. e Remove obstacles to group and family childcare in all zoning districts, in safe and appropriate locations for children. e Support legislation (local or state) which provides for small childcare homes as permitted land uses in all zoning districts without standard home occupation restrictions. e Support federal, state and local legislation providing for childcare needs assessments and for planning to be performed at the state and local level. Where the proposed amendments included in the proposed ordinance could make a real impact: e Permits family and group child care homes in residential areas as conditional uses, removing a major zoning barrier; Provides economic opportunities for individuals looking to become a family or group child care home provider; Aligns local definitions and use standards with DSS categories, helping to prevent conflicts; Helps small providers navigate compliance without confusion; Helps reduce regulatory burdens for home-based providers. Please review the attached amendments to Section 5.1.7 of the UDO and the Table (attached) breaking down the proposed amendments. While the proposed amendments are a first step in addressing child care disparities at a local regulatory level, there are still opportunities to strengthen equity impacts for low-income families, minority entrepreneurs, and working parents with nontraditional schedules. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council regarding the proposed amendments. Additional information can be found in the packet for the August 7, 2025 PC mig. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. Sligh made a motion to recommend approval of the text amendment set forth in item B3 with the following exceptions. Under the childcare home, it will be permitted in zoning RA, RR and P only. Sligh also incorporated Huck’s change to the name of the agency of the department and the changes that we were provided that had to do with the fencing. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. BOARD INPUT None VII. VIII. PC 8/7/2025 STAFF INPUT Hucks shared recent guidance provided to staff by the Municipal Association. In accordance with this guidance, annexation and zoning matters will now be processed through two separate ordinances. City Council will be responsible for reviewing and deciding on annexation requests. The Planning Commission will review zoning proposals, specifically evaluating the zoning map in relation to the future land use map and the comprehensive plan. The annexation ordinance will be presented to City Council for a first reading. If Council approves the annexation, the matter will then be forwarded to the Planning Commission for zoning review. If Council denies the annexation, the Planning Commission will not need to review the zoning, and no public advertisement will be required. After Planning Commission review, the zoning ordinance will be sent to City Council for its own first reading. At a subsequent Council meeting, both the annexation ordinance and the zoning ordinance will appear together on the agenda for final approval. Hucks clarified that Planning Commission board members are limited in their authority to making official changes to the zoning map, and such changes must be consistent with the future land use map. Additionally, Hucks noted that a list of other amendments is being prepared and will be brought before the Board at a later date for review and consideration. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:32 pm. Approved and signed this A day of ARFERRER, 2025. Jessica Wise, Chairperson 10

text: PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA Thursday, July 10, 2025 | 5:30 p.m. Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street I. CALL TO ORDER – 5:30 p.m. II. MINUTES A. Approval of the June 5, 2025 Planning Commission Meeting Minutes III. PUBLIC INPUT IV. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Previously Tabled…Request to annex approximately 1.43+/- acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and request to rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. 2. Request to annex approximately 0.79+/- acres of property located at 150 Amber Lane (PIN 367-14-04-0004), and rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. 3. Request to annex approximately 1.4+/- acres of property located at the corner of Hwy 544 and Todd Blvd (720, 730 and 748 Hwy 544) (PIN 382-05-04-0046), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. 4. Request to annex approximately 22.88+/- (total) acres of property located on Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN’s 399-01-02-0001 & 399-00-00-0001), and rezone from the Horry County Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI) district to the City of Conway Low-Density Residential (R) district. 5. Conference Room 196 Laurel St. VIII. ADJOURNMENT -- 2 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 1 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, June 5, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Allan Cornell, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III Absent: Greg Bryson, Kendall Brown, David Sligh, Danny Hardee Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Marcus Cohen, IT; Sidney Livingston, Intern Others: Priscilla Fuller, Ashley Cowen, Edna Dewitt, Beverly Marlowe, Collin Brogan, Bob Stevens, Andy Christenson, Celia Sands, Vallerie Jordan, Fran Dixson, Anthony Brooks, Edward McQueen, Olga Hays, Craig Anderson, Joan Anderson, Russ Mehl, Annette Blondeau, Mack Hutson. I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Cornell to approve the May 1, 2025, minutes, with the correction to Public Input under item IV.B., to state “Andy Christenson, applicant, spoke with the people in opposition to the request”. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. IV. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 2.22+/- acres of property located on 1091 E Hwy 501 and Amber Ln. (PIN 367-14-04-0003, 0002 & 0001), and request to rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the request was being considered as a result of a requirement to annex by Public Utilities. The subject property, known as South Atlantic Monument Company, is currently on the same water meter as the residential property located at 150 Amber Lane. As a result of the requirement for the -- 3 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 2 property to have a separate meter, annexation must be requested by the property owner, which also requires that all surrounding property owned by the applicant be subject to annexation. The residential property on Amber Lane will be considered for annexation at a future council meeting. The requested zoning upon annexation for all three properties with frontage on Hwy 501 is Highway Commercial, which is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The intent of the HC District is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the city. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Mack Hutson, was present to answer any questions. He expressed his desire not to be annexed into the city limits. Beverly Marlowe spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. There was discussion as to whether this property would be serviced by City of Conway or GSWSA. Ulrich made a motion to recommend disapproval of the request to rezone the 2.22 acres of property as presented. However, if the council proceeds with annexation, the annexation should comply with the highway commercial designation outlined in the future land use map for the city of Conway. Cornell seconded the motion, the motion carried 4-1, with Wise voting in opposition to the denial. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.33+/- acres of property at 1307 Grainger Rd (PIN 368-01-02-0007) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that the applicants were requesting to rezone the subject property from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district in order to construct a single-family dwelling. The property has an older commercial structure, previously used as an auto garage, and is currently classified as being storage/warehousing, and the legal nonconforming residence that once existed has been demolished or removed. Per the legal description of the property, the property is described as being lots 20 & 21 from a plat recorded in 1941. Should the rezoning request be approved, the applicant may be required to provide a new plat formally combining the two lots into one and to demo the older commercial structure. -- 4 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 3 The current zoning map and future land use map identify the property as Highway Commercial, along with several other properties with frontage on Grainger Rd; however, some of these properties contain a residence while others are vacant. The intent of the requested zoning, Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Celia Sands, was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Cornell made a motion to approve the request as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone approximately 10.97+/- acres of property at 1808 Rhue Street (PIN 368-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Institutional (IN) district. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that the applicant, Horry County Schools, is requesting to rezone the former site of Whittemore Park Middle School, currently zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) to the Institutional (IN) district in order to utilize the property as the school districts Rivertown Complex, which will house the Conway Adult Education program, a therapeutic learning center for students of HCS, and the districts JROTC program, along with administrative offices. The request is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The intent of the IN District is to provide areas for the development of medical, educational, and higher educational, facilities in a campus-like setting. More specifically, the district is intended to accommodate the development styles, uses, and accessory uses associated with these facilities. This district is not intended for businesses engaged in retail sales, except for those businesses that are clearly accessory to and specifically provide services to the permitted principal use. The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Institutional (IN). -- 5 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 4 During presentation of the request at the June 2nd council meeting, there was discussion as to whether or not the applicant could operate the proposed uses in a zoning district other than Institutional (IN). Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. Edna Dewitt and Priscilla Fuller spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Ulrich made a motion to defer the request as presented to allow for an additional public hearing to give the planning department an opportunity to discuss the matter with the school district, to invite them to a future public meeting, and encouraged the district to engage with neighboring residents before the next planning meeting. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (aka Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated that this request to amend the PD for Carsen’s Ferry (a.k.a. Rivertown Landing Planned Development) (PD) district, was discussed at the April and May Planning Commission meetings, where public hearings were held at each meeting regarding the request. Currently, the only uses permitted on Tract A, as one of the 2 remaining “commercial” tracts, are a baked goods store, café or restaurant, candy or confectionary store and an ice cream shop. The PD was originally created in 2007, with the intent of developing a mixed-use community on 28.5 acres, to consist of multifamily, office and retail space, and civic use space. Since that time, the PD has been amended four other times – in 2010, 2017, 2018, and in 2022. The 2017 amendment permitted 50 single-family detached homes in lieu of the multifamily initially proposed on 11.4 acres of the PD, with narrow lots, reduced setbacks, and some portions having rear loaded garaged that were accessed via an alley. The 2017 amendment also removed approximately 5 acres from the PD, which was commercial tract C, and rezoned it to R-2, now part of the Rivertown Row subdivision. In 2018, Commercial tract B was amended to reduce the commercial acreage and added to -- 6 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 5 the residential portion of the PD in order to permit additional single-family homes, now phase 5 of Carsen’s Ferry. The applicant held a community meeting with the residents of Carsen’s Ferry in April, who were concerned with the mixed-uses proposed for Tract A, the potential for increased traffic, as well as the location and proximity of residential units overlooking the amenities for Carsen’s Ferry. Due to concerns of the community with the proposed mixed-use nature of Tract A, the applicant revised the request to allow only single-family residential as the permitted use, similar to the homes within the Carsen’s Ferry development. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Ashley Cowen, Diamond Shores LLC, was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Wise made a motion to approve the request, ensuring a maximum of six (6) (residential) dwellings. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Amendment(s) to Article 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements Mobile Food Vending. Hucks gave an overview of the proposed amendment(s), stating that this amendment was discussed at Council’s budget retreat earlier in the year. Since the city adopted standards for mobile food vending in 2018, the number of requests that staff receives each year nearly doubles. In 2018, staff received six applications for mobile vending. In 2022/2023, that number increased to more than 20 applications. Last year, staff processed more than 50 applications for mobile food vending. For comparison, the City of Myrtle Beach offers 20 mobile vending permits each year, and Horry County has a cap of 50 mobile vending permits each year for the entire county. The application process for mobile vending is very time-consuming for both staff and the applicant, and due to state regulations for licensing, requirements for approvals by property owners, coordination with other city departments, required inspections, the business license process, related enforcements, and the process for obtaining approval of a franchise agreement with the city (to operate on city-owned property), it has become a fulltime job for one staff member a large portion of the year. Staff proposes to cap the number of mobile food vending permits to 40 per year, to be issued on a first- come, first-serve basis. Business licenses, in addition to the vending permit, must be renewed each year; however, many of them are not renewed yet the vendors continue to operate, which has caused -- 7 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 6 enforcement issues for staff. The cap of 40 per year would include the three different types of mobile vending – transient mobile vending, mobile vending on private property, and franchise agreements. However, the cap would not include mobile vendors operating under an approved special event permit for specific dates, or other types of franchise agreements that the city enters into, such as Peel Scooters or H2O Excursions (both nonfood-related vendors). Having a limit on the number of mobile vending permits each year not only benefits the brick-and-mortar establishments that are located within the city limits, but it also incentivizes those who were previously licensed to have their mobile vending permits current and to renew each year, on time so that they do not lose their ability to operate in the city limits if the cap is reached before they have submitted their renewal application and have it approved. Staff presented the proposed amendment to Council at the June 2nd mtg., and they asked that there be language added that excluded brick-and-mortar dining establishments in the city limits who may engage in mobile food vending from the cap. That change was added to the proposed amendment. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. Priscilla Fuller spoke during public input and stated that the information for mobile vending should be publicly available so that people knew what the rules were. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. After much discussion, Cornell made a motion to approve the request with the recommendation to cap the number of permitted mobile trucks to a maximum of 20 per year, excluding the brick-and-mortar restaurants. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Amendment(s) to Article 6 – Design Standards, of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for single-family in-common development. Hucks stated that this topic was previously discussed at a council workshop earlier in the year, following a request received to review a single-family in-common development, which has been receiving more interest from developers. While still considered a typical single-family development, the homes would be built on one single parcel rather than on separate lots, like a traditional subdivision is (or fee simple). Currently, the UDO does not contain standards for single-family in-common development, and the proposed amendments would include standards for minimum separation, off-sets from internal/external roadways, spacing requirements from project boundaries, ingress/egress, zoning requirements, landscaping/buffer requirements, among other standards. This type of development is similar to a -- 8 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 7 townhome development, which are considered “single-family attached”, and can be built in-common, with standards for doing so already in the UDO; however, single-family detached does not currently have such standards. “In-common” development is a more unconventional pattern of ownership, for single-family homes, is the Condominium form of ownership. This style of ownership, if transferred, conveys to the grantee, an individual unit, consisting of the interior surfaces of the perimeter walls, floors and ceilings, while the underlying and surrounding real property is common area, to be owned by either a Horizontal Property Regime or a property management group. Hucks briefly went over the sections of the UDO that were proposed to be amended, with the proposed changes. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council regarding the proposed amendments. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Wise made a motion to approve the request to amend as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Amendment(s) to Article 15 – Enforcement, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding penalties for violations of the UDO. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that over the last year or so, staff has been issuing more citations for violations of the UDO that end up requiring court appearances and decisions from Municipal Court, which led to discussions regarding misdemeanor offenses and those who are found guilty of violating the UDO; specifically, because the UDO does not provide specific language as to penalties for such violations. City Council had approved a previous amendment to Article 15 in 2024 that outlined the penalty for those actions deemed punishable as a civil infraction, which related to signs illegally placed in rights-of- way. Staff reached out to the Municipal Association for guidance, and while their legal counsel is of the opinion that 1 – while the contents of the UDO are not contained within the general code; only referenced to say that the UDO “is adopted in accordance with state law under the Planning Enabling Act of 1994”, and 2 – there are a few sections in the city’s general code regarding penalties for violations that include any section of the city’s general code and one section in particular that states “any ordinance of the city, or any rule or regulation promulgated by any officer or agency of the city”, staff proposes to amend -- 9 of 85 -- PC 6/5/2025 8 Article 15 to specify that “the penalties for violations of the UDO are a misdemeanor offense that are subject to the penalties in the city’s code of ordinances” for the sake of consistency. The proposed amendment would simply add “subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances” to the end of each sentence in Art. 15 that references violations of the UDO. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff briefly discussed the proposed amendment. Wise made a motion to approve the proposed amendment(s) to Article 15. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. BOARD INPUT None VI. STAFF INPUT Hucks introduced Sydney Livingston, the city’s summer intern. Sydney is a rising senior at the University of South Carolina. VII. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:55 pm. Approved and signed this ___________ day of ______________, 2025. Jessica Wise, Chairperson -- 10 of 85 -- DATE: JULY 10, 2025 ITEM: IV.A.1. ISSUE: Previously Tabled…. Request to annex approximately 1.43 acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd, (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. BACKGROUND: On August 27th of 2024, the applicant went to the City’s Water Dept. to apply for water services on the subject property. The applicant was informed at that time that because the property is contiguous to property in the City limits, they would have to request annexation. Upon review of the property, staff noticed that per County land records, there were permits pending for the subject property. The only thing holding up permit issuance at that point was the requirement for the applicant to provide proof that City utilities would be connected. The permit was applied for at Horry County on February 27, 2024. The use specified on the permit was for a new auto shop. At the time the permit was applied for at the county, the subject property was NOT contiguous. However, the adjacent parcel, the Founders National Golf property, was currently going through the annexation process and had received First Reading on February 19th. Final Reading occurred on March 18th, subsequently making this parcel contiguous to City limits. As such, staff informed the County at the time that no permits could be issued for the property due to the requirement to annex before permitting, which would then need to occur once the property is annexed and would be issued by the City. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Limited Industrial (LI). Adjacent uses include the property containing the former entrance road for the MB National Golf Course, a gas station (fronting Hwy 501), Southern Sun Awnings, and Domino’s Pizza is located across Gardner Lacy Rd. The zoning designation applied for on the annexation and rezoning paperwork is the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile-oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the entire parcel as Highway Commercial (HC). CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved first reading of the annexation and rezoning at their September 3rd meeting. -- 11 of 85 -- However, during a workshop at their September 16, 2024 meeting, staff made council aware that the applicant has received his stormwater approval, DHEC approval and SCDOT encroachment permits, and the civil plans had already been approved through the County. If the applicant were forced to start this process over in the City’s jurisdiction, it would create an unnecessary financial hardship that may be impossible for the property owner and business owner to overcome. For this reason, staff preferred tabling final reading at the time until the county issued Certificate of Occupancies for the property. Update – July 2025: The structure is still in the process of being constructed. Council still has the ability to defer or table final reading of the annexation, should they choose to do so. Regardless, the request is required to receive a recommendation from Planning Commission with regard to the proposed zoning upon annexation. Additionally, property directly across from this property was annexed into the city limits in January 2025 (former Wolverine Brass properties) as Light Industrial (LI). STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. ISSUE: Request to annex approximately 0.79 acres located at 150 Amber Lane (PIN 367-14-04-0004), and rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. BACKGROUND: The annexation application was submitted by the property owners, as a requirement for connection to city services. According to Horry County Land Records, the property was transferred into the owner’s names on July 24, 2024. The property contains an existing brick single-family home as well as a mobile home. A restrictive covenant was recorded on April 17, 2025. As part of the required review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), all were asked to comment on the request for annexation. Below are their comments: Building: recommends disapproval – This is not an area we normally patrol with property maintenance and the building inspectors are too busy as it is. Flood: Approved Fire: Approved GIS: NA Police: recommends disapproval – We currently have few properties nearby and creates a reverse donut hole where we generally do not patrol the area. It also brings us closer to another school, and we are at capacity for our SRO program. If all contiguous properties associated with this owner come in, we will have Hwy 501 corner and frontage access, which takes us away from the school and into a more commercial area. Public Utilities: Approved Public Works: Approved Sanitation: Approved CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies this property as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The intent of the R-1 District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their June 16th meeting. -- 28 of 85 -- STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. ISSUE: Request to annex approximately 22.88+/- (total) acres of property located on Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN’s 399-01-02-0001 & 399-00-00-0001), and request to rezone from the Horry County Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI) district to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. BACKGROUND: The applicants are requesting to annex the subject properties located on Gardner Lacy Rd, and rezone the properties to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. The properties are currently vacant. Per Section 3.2.17 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: One of the properties abuts a Santee Cooper distribution facility. Both properties are adjacent to the railroad right-of-way. The other side is property owned by Myrtle Beach National Property Owner’s Association (POA), as well as the Southcreek development. Southcreek, in Horry County’s jurisdiction, is zoned SF10, which is single-family residential, no mobile homes allowed, with minimum lot sizes of 10,000 sq. ft. The proposed zoning upon annexation is the city’s default zoning of R, which also requires a minimum lot size of 10,000 sq. ft. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Professional (P). Per Section 3.2.7 of the UDO, the intent of the P district is to accommodate office, institutional, and residential uses in areas whose character is neither exclusively business nor residential in nature. This district is intended to establish areas that provide professional services to the public, which do not materially detract from nearby residential areas. More specifically, the P district serves as a transitional zone between more intensive commercial uses and residential areas. The P district is not intended for businesses that engage in retail sales. CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their June 16th meeting. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. ISSUE: Request to annex approximately 224+/- acres of property located on E. Hwy 501, New Road, Ash Pond Road, Marina Drive, Elm Street, and Laurel Street (PIN’s 368-00-00-0008 and -0015), and rezone from the Horry County Heavy Industrial (HI) district, City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district and City of Conway High-density Residential (R-3) district to the City of Conway Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD) (1) (2). BACKGROUND: The City is seeking to annex and rezone these properties that were recently acquired to the Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD). The WRD districts, 1 & 2, are considered a special use district; similar to that of a Planned Development (PD) district or the Mixed Use (MU) Flexible Zone district. Section 3.3.1 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) defines the WRD as the following: The intent of the WRD District is to provide for the proper physical, social, and economic development of the City’s riverfront area in order to protect, promote and improve the public health, safety, morals, convenience, order, appearance, prosperity, and general welfare, including but not limited to: safeguarding the cultural, scenic, economic, environmental, and social heritage of the Waccamaw Riverfront on behalf of the City, Horry County and South Carolina; providing for adequate light, air, and public open space; encouraging efficient and economic practices in the process of development and redevelopment; making adequate provision for pedestrian and vehicular traffic; supporting the wise and efficient expenditures of public funds promoting safe and proper drainage; protecting lives and properties from the hazards of flooding; safeguarding water quality; promoting attractive and economically beneficial community and architectural appearance; protecting valuable wetlands trees, and other vegetation; encouraging natural and environmentally sound shoreline stabilization, promoting economic prosperity for the district and the City, and providing for adequate public access to the river and its shores. The Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD) is broken down into two (2) sub-districts for zoning purposes: WRD-1 and WRD-2. The only difference between the two is that WRD-1 has specific requirements for certain uses in new buildings, and limitations on multifamily residential – in that it may only occupy second (upper) floors of buildings, not ground floors. There is also a distinction between 1 & 2 in terms of being on the river side of the railroad and the town side of the railroad. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: While most of these properties are vacant, or containing ponds, there are still a couple of buildings on one of the properties, where the smoke stacks were once located, which is zoned Horry County Heavy Industrial (HI). BACKGROUND: The applicant, Horry County Schools, is requesting to rezone the former site of Whittemore Park Middle School, which is currently zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The property and building will be the HCS Rivertown Complex, which will house the Conway area Adult Education and its programs, including a limited childcare function, as well as a therapeutic learning center for students, the districts JROTC program, and other staff. The intent of the IN District is to provide areas for the development of medical, educational, and higher educational, facilities in a campus-like setting. More specifically, the district is intended to accommodate the development styles, uses, and accessory uses associated with these facilities. This district is not intended for businesses engaged in retail sales, except for those businesses that are clearly accessory to and specifically provide services to the permitted principal use. June 5th Planning Commission mtg. Planning Commission deferred the request to the July meeting, as the applicant was not present. There were people in attendance who were opposed to the request to rezone the property to Institutional, due to the potential uses that could occur should the school district stop using the property and/or sell the property to then be utilized as the Institutional zoning district would permit. Alternative to rezoning: Staff is currently working on drafting a text amendment regarding educational facilities and accessory uses for such facilities, as well as an ordinance to address current requirements for child care (daycare) facilities. These amendment(s) seek address the uses that are proposed for the property, thus eliminating the need for the property to be rezoned. Per an email from Mr. Burch, Executive Director of Capital Projects for Horry County Schools, the uses proposed for the subject property include: • Conway Adult Education Center – adult ed classes and assistance, GED administration and minimal part-time childcare support for adults during certain class times, which is limited to 4 hours per day. • Therapeutic Learning Center – includes HCS students from most grade levels who need specialized assistance for special education needs, during normal daytime school hours. • Several district administration functions, including JROTC administration offices for district and Building Services administration offices. • Occasional meeting space for district meetings as needed. -- 72 of 85 -- CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Institutional (IN). STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that the request be deferred once again in order for staff to draft the amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) addressing accessory uses to educational facilities and the requirements for child care facilities. (Church Street), known as Lake Busbee, from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Conservation Preservation (CP) district. BACKGROUND: The City is seeking to rezone the property formerly known as Lake Busbee from Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) to Conservation Preservation (CP) district, the CP district is described: The intent of the CP District is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. This property is commonly known as the former Lake Busbee that was allowed to be restored to its natural form as a biodiverse and flood prone ecosystem following multiple natural disasters. This was done with the intent of preserving and protecting the property and surrounding properties from the devastation of flooding as much as possible. Allowing the ecosystem to act on its own provides a true scenic beauty to the area as it is intended by nature to be, but it also provides the ability to reduce the flood risk for surrounding properties. Conservation Preservation (CP) is also consistent with the zoning classification of the future land use map. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: While most of the surrounding properties are vacant, or contain environmentally sensitive areas themselves, most are owned by the City of Conway except for a few properties. Surrounding zoning includes City of Conway Conservation Preservation (CP), City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA), and Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10). Uses around this property include residential, a community dog park, a waste treatment facility, and another property is vacant except for a large pond. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Conservation Preservation (CP). STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council.
