text: PC 7/10/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, July 10, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Allan Cornell, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III, David Sligh Absent: Greg Bryson, Kendall Brown Staff: Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Kym Wilkerson, Zoning Administrator; Charlie Crosby, IT; Sydney Livingston, Summer Intern Others: Fred Archer, Beverly Marlowe, Ann Hutson, Mack Hutson, Andreas Hoppe, Cecil Brown, Monica Brown, Ruth Cronin, Charles Pency I. CALL TO ORDER Il. Til. IV. Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Cornell to approve the June 5, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Previously Tabled ... Request to annex approximately 1.43+/- acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and request to rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Dennis stated on August 27" of 2024, the applicant went to the City’s Water Dept. to apply for water services on the subject property. The applicant was informed at that time that because the property is contiguous to property in the City limits, they would have to request annexation. Upon review of the property, staff noticed that per County land records, there were permits pending for the subject property. The only thing holding up permit issuance at that point was the requirement for the applicant to provide proof that City utilities would be connected. The permit was applied for at Horry County on February 27, 2024. The use specified on the permit was for a new auto shop. At the time the permit was applied for at the county, the subject property was NOT contiguous. However, the adjacent parcel, the Founders 1 PC 7/10/2025 National Golf property, was currently going through the annexation process and had received First Reading on February 19'". Final Reading occurred on March 18", subsequently making this parcel contiguous to City limits. As such, staff informed the County at the time that no permits could be issued for the property due to the requirement to annex before permitting, which would then need to occur once the property is annexed and would be issued by the City. _ Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Limited Industrial (LI). Adjacent uses include the property containing the former entrance road for the MB National Golf Course, a gas station (fronting Hwy 501), Southern Sun Awnings, and Domino’s Pizza is located across Gardner Lacy Rd. The zoning designation applied for on the annexation and rezoning paperwork is the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile-oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. City Council approved first reading of the annexation and rezoning at their September 3" meeting. However, during a workshop at their September 16, 2024 meeting, staff made council aware that the applicant has received his stormwater approval, DHEC approval and SCDOT encroachment permits, and the civil plans had already been approved through the County. If the applicant were forced to start this process over in the City’s jurisdiction, it would create an unnecessary financial hardship that may be impossible for the property owner and business owner to overcome. For this reason, staff preferred tabling final reading at the time until the county issued Certificate of Occupancies for the property. Update — July 2025: The structure is still in the process of being constructed. Council still has the ability to defer or table final reading of the annexation, should they choose to do so. Regardless, the request is required to receive a recommendation from Planning Commission with regard to the proposed zoning upon annexation. Additionally, property directly across from this property was annexed into the city limits in January 2025 (former Wolverine Brass properties) as Light Industrial (LI. Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Fred Archer, was present to answer any questions. No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PC 7/10/2025 The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the annexation and rezoning request to city of Conway Highway commercial district. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to annex approximately 0.79+/- acres of property located at 150 Amber Lane (PIN 367-14-04-0004), and rezone from the Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) district to the City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district. Dennis stated the annexation application was submitted by the property owners, as a requirement for connection to city services. According to Horry County Land Records, the property was transferred into the owner’s names on July 24, 2024. The property contains an existing brick single-family home as well as a mobile home. A restrictive covenant was recorded on April 17, 2025. As part of the required review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC), all were asked to comment on the request for annexation. Below are their comments: Building: recommends disapproval — This is not an area we normally patrol with property maintenance and the building inspectors are too busy as it is. Flood: Approved Fire: Approved GIS: NA Police: recommends disapproval — We currently have few properties nearby and creates a reverse donut hole where we generally do not patrol the area. It also brings us closer to another school, and we are at capacity for our SRO program. If all contiguous properties associated with this owner come in, we will have Hwy 501 corner and frontage access, which takes us away from the school and into a more commercial area. Public Utilities: Approved Public Works: Approved Sanitation: Approved The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies this property as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The intent of the R-1 District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their June 16" meeting. Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Ann Hutson and Beverly Marlowe, was present to answer any questions. 3 PC 7/10/2025 Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mtg. Sligh made a motion to recommend that the city council deny the request to annex/rezone the 2.22 acres of property as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, the motion carried 5-1, with Wise voting in opposition to the denial. 3. Request to annex approximately 1.4+/- acres of property located at the corner of Hwy 544 and Todd Blvd (720, 730 and 748 Hwy 544) (PIN 382-05-04-0046), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Dennis stated the applicant’s submitted annexation and rezoning applications on June 6" for the subject property. The applicant is seeking to redevelop the property and construct a Scooters Coffee on the site. Currently, the property contains a produce stand, a State Farm office and a cell tower. The requested zoning upon annexation is the Highway Commercial (HC) district. The property is currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC) in Horry County. The intent of the HC District is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the city. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: Surrounding properties are a mix of commercial, institutional and residential. Abutting property is Mixed-Use (MU) and Institutional (IN). Property across Todd Blvd is Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF6) and currently contains a single-family residence. Property located across Hwy 544 is zoned Institutional and is owned by the University. The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. 4 PC 7/10/2025 No public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Ulrich made a motion to approve as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 4, Request to annex approximately 22.88+/- (total) acres of property located on Gardner Lacy Rd (PIN’s 399-01-02-0001 & 399-00-00-0001), and rezone from the Horry County Office/Professional/Institutional (OPI) district to the City of Conway Low-Density Residential (R) district. Dennis stated the applicants are requesting to annex the subject properties located on Gardner Lacy Rd, and rezone the properties to the Low-Density Residential (R) district. The properties are currently vacant. Per Section 3.2.17 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: One of the properties abuts a Santee Cooper distribution facility. Both properties are adjacent to the railroad right-of-way. The other side is property owned by Myrtle Beach National Property Owner’s Association (POA), as well as the Southcreek development. Southcreek, in Horry County’s jurisdiction, is zoned SF10, which is single-family residential, no mobile homes allowed, with minimum lot sizes of 10,000 sq. ft. The proposed zoning upon annexation is the city’s default zoning of R, which also requires a minimum lot size of 10,000 sq. ft. City Council approved First Reading of the ordinance at their June 16" meeting. Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mig. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. Andreas Hoppe spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. 5 PC 7/10/2025 Sligh made a motion to approve the annexation of the 22.88 acres and rezoning from Horry County office Professional Institutional to city of Conway Professional as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 5. Request to annex approximately 224+/- acres of property located on E. Hwy 501, New Road, Ash Pond Road, Marina Drive, Elm Street, and Laurel Street (PIN’s 368-00-00-0008 and - 0015), and rezone from the Horry County Heavy Industrial (HI) district, City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district and City of Conway High-density Residential (R-3) district to the City of Conway Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD) (1) (2). Dennis stated the City is seeking to annex and rezone these properties that were recently acquired to the Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD). The WRD districts, 1 & 2, are considered a special use district; similar to that of a Planned Development (PD) district or the Mixed Use (MU) Flexible Zone district. Section 3.3.1 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) defines the WRD as the following: The intent of the WRD District is to provide for the proper physical, social, and economic development of the City’s riverfront area in order to protect, promote and improve the public health, safety, morals, convenience, order, appearance, prosperity, and general welfare, including but not limited to: safeguarding the cultural, scenic, economic, environmental, and social heritage of the Waccamaw Riverfront on behalf of the City, Horry County and South Carolina; providing for adequate light, air, and public open space; encouraging efficient and economic practices in the process of development and redevelopment; making adequate provision for pedestrian and vehicular traffic; supporting the wise and efficient expenditures of public funds promoting safe and proper drainage; protecting lives and properties from the hazards of flooding; safeguarding water quality; promoting attractive and economically beneficial community and architectural appearance; protecting valuable wetlands trees, and other vegetation; encouraging natural and environmentally sound shoreline stabilization, promoting economic prosperity for the district and the City, and providing for adequate public access to the river and its shores. The Waccamaw Riverfront District (WRD) is broken down into two (2) sub-districts for zoning purposes: WRD-1 and WRD-2. The only difference between the two is that WRD-1 has specific requirements for certain uses in new buildings, and limitations on multifamily residential — in that it may only occupy second (upper) floors of buildings, not ground floors. There is also a distinction between 1 & 2 in terms of being on the river side of the railroad and the town side of the railroad. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: While most of these properties are vacant, or containing ponds, there are still a couple of buildings on one of the properties, where the smoke stacks were once located, which is zoned Horry County Heavy Industrial (HT). Property across Hwy 501 on New Rd zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), Conservation Preservation (CP), Light Industrial (LI) and Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA) PC 7/10/2025 The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies a majority of the property as Conservation Preservation (CP) and a small portion, where the smoke stacks and other structures were once located, as Light Industrial (LI). Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mig. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, the City of Conway staff, was present to answer any questions. Cecil Brown spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the rezoning request as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Previously Deferred...Request to rezone approximately 10.97+/- acres of property at 1808 Rhue Street (PIN 368-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Institutional (IN) district. Katie stated that staff is requesting that this item be deferred so staff can develop a text amendment that could eliminate the need to rezone the property. Staff’s goal is to have the proposed amendment before the board at the August Planning Commission meeting for consideration and the school district has no issue with the deferral. The applicant, Horry County Schools, provided a quote that states, “We want to be good neighbors to everyone who lives near our facilities and we understand the concerns from some residents. While we have no plans to do anything with the Rivertown complex other than utilize it for educational purposes, we want to give the residents peace of mind for the future. Therefore, we support a text amendment to address the childcare question and are fine with deferral of the rezoning request to that end. Additionally, if the text amendment to address those questions is approved, we will withdraw our rezoning requests. We appreciate the city’s continued assistance with our various Conway area educational facilities and their unique needs”. Ulrich made a motion to defer the request as presented. Wise seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. PC 7/10/2025 2. Request to rezone approximately 533+/- acres of property (PIN 368-00-00-0014) located on Hwy 501 E. (Church Street), known as Lake Busbee, from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Conservation Preservation (CP) district. Dennis gave an overview of the request, stating that the City is seeking to rezone the property formerly known as Lake Busbee from Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) to Conservation Preservation (CP) district, the CP district is described: The intent of the CP District is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses, and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. This property is commonly known as the former Lake Busbee that was allowed to be restored to its natural form as a biodiverse and flood prone ecosystem following multiple natural disasters. This was done with the intent of preserving and protecting the property and surrounding properties from the devastation of flooding as much as possible. Allowing the ecosystem to act on its own provides a true scenic beauty to the area as it is intended by nature to be, but it also provides the ability to reduce the flood risk for surrounding properties. Conservation Preservation (CP) is also consistent with the zoning classification of the future land use map. Surrounding Zoning / Uses: While most of the surrounding properties are vacant, or contain environmentally sensitive areas themselves, most are owned by the City of Conway except for a few properties. Surrounding zoning includes City of Conway Conservation Preservation (CP), City of Conway Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1), Horry County Commercial Forest Agriculture (CFA), and Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10). Uses around this property include residential, a community dog park, a waste treatment facility, and another property is vacant except for a large pond. Additional information can be found in the packet for the July 10, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, the City of Conway staff, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Sligh made a motion to approve of the rezoning from R1 (Low-Medium Density Residential) to CP (Conservation Preservation). Anderon seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 8 PC 7/10/2025 VY. BOARD INPUT None VI. STAFF INPUT None VII. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:08 pm. Approved and signed this 4 day of _ KOCK , 2025. Jessica Wise, Chairperson

ADJOURNMENT -- 2 of 74 -- PC 5/1/2025 1 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, May 1, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Greg Bryson, George Ulrich, Kendall Brown, Allan Cornell Absent: Danny Hardee, David Sligh, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Marcus Cohen, IT Others: Kenneth Barnes, Ashley Cowen, Annette Blondeau, Russ Mehl, Robert Stevens, Andy Christenson, Craig Anderson, Sheri Walton, Amy Hill, Phillip McLean, Carla Rector, Susan Douthat, Karen Santa, Kate Hartson I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Bryson to approve the April 3, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. IV. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Deferred… Request to rezone approximately 18.78+/- total acres of property located at the corner of Oak Street and Mill Pond Road (PIN 338-00-00-0019) from the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district to High-Density Residential (R-3) district. 2. Request to rezone approximately 1.4+/- total acres of property located at the corner of Davidson Road and East Highway 501 (PIN’s 383-08-02-0003 & 383-08-02-0002) from the Professional (P) district to Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject properties on April 1, 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Professional (P). These properties are lots 1 and 2 on block 8 of the College Park subdivision (see attached plat of College Park). The lots are currently vacant; however, they are encumbered by power transmission line easements, as are several other surrounding lots, which will restrict any type of development. Lot 1 (PIN 383-08-02-0003) is approx. 0.74 acres and Lot 2 (PIN 383-08-02-0002) is approx. 0.66 acres. The proposed use of the property is not known at this time. The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning -- 3 of 74 -- PC 5/1/2025 2 district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestion, and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. These parcels front Hwy 501. Lot 1 is a corner lot, adjacent to Davidson Road. There is nothing on either side of these lots, and properties on either side are zoned Professional. Properties directly behind the subject property is zoned R-1; also, part of the College Park Subdivision. While developed in the county, several parcels were annexed into the city limits over the years, including the lots that front Hwy 501. University Baptist Church is located on lots 1-4 on block 9 of College Park. Staff was recently made aware of the existence of restrictive covenants for the College Park Subdivision, from when the development was originally created in 1967, recorded in Deed Book 371 at Page 517 (at Horry County Register of Deeds). Building regulations provided in the restrictions is limited to single-family dwellings only, not to exceed two stories in height. Uses are limited to private family residences together with appropriate and approved outbuildings. Further, the restrictions strictly prohibit commercial activity within the College Park subdivision. The restrictions described within the Declaration of Restrictive Covenants are in effect for an initial 20-year period, and then automatically extended for successive periods of 5 years each, unless an instrument signed by the then owners of a majority of lots within the subdivision has been recorded, agreeing to change in the covenants, limitations or restrictions – in whole or in part. There was such an amendment filed in 1996 for lots 1-4 of block 9 of the subdivision, which subsequently allowed a church with amenities to be constructed on said lots. However, the amendment did not include any revisions to any of the other lots within College Park. In fact, page 3 of the amendment specifically states that “except as changed, amended, or modified herein, the subdivision Declaration of Restrictions, and any amendment thereto, shall remain in full force, virtue and effect.” While deed restrictions / restrictive covenants are a civil matter, and it is not required by the local planning agency to determine whether such restrictions exist, once we have received notice of their existence, the local planning agency does have the ability to deny plans that would otherwise violate such restrictions. However, they are not enforced by the local planning agency. More specifically: SC Code of Laws, Section § 6-29-1145. Determining existence of restrictive covenant; effect. A. In an application for a permit, the local planning agency must inquire in the application or by written instructions to an applicant whether the tract of land or parcel of land is restricted by any recorded covenant that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity. B. If a local planning agency has actual notice of a restrictive covenant on a tract or parcel -- 4 of 74 -- PC 5/1/2025 3 of land that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity: 1. In the application for the permit; 2. From materials or information submitted by the person or persons requesting the permit; or 3. From any other source including, but not limited to, other property holders, The local planning agency must not issue the permit unless the local planning agency receives confirmation from the applicant that the restrictive covenant has been released for the tract or parcel of land by action of the appropriate authority or property holders or by court order. C. As used in this section: 1. “actual notice” is not constructive notice of documents filed in local offices concerning the property and does not require the local planning agency to conduct searches in any records offices for filed restrictive covenants. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Kenneth Barnes, C21 McAlpine & Associates was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Phillip McLean, Amy Hill and Sheri Walton spoke in opposition of the request during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Brown to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to deny the request to rezone from Professional to Highway Commercial, explaining to the applicant that, given the covenants and restrictions, she would consider a rezoning if there were an aspect that facilitated movement on the property, particularly given its location on Highway 501 and its potential viability. She further stated that, under the current circumstances, she was not comfortable supporting a rezoning. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. -- 5 of 74 -- PC 5/1/2025 4 B. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Previously deferred… Request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (aka Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated that the Rivertown Landing Planned Development (PD) district, now known as the Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development, was originally created in 2007 out of 28.55 acres off Hwy 501 at Riverport Dr. The stated purpose was to “create a walkable, mixed-use community featuring multi-family residential, civic, commercial, and office space in the City of Conway.” Until 2015/2016, the only thing that had been developed in this community was the clubhouse and pool. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: Amended to increase the height allowance for Carsen’s Ferry multifamily project from 40 feet to 52 feet and reduce the total residential units from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: removed all commercial and multifamily from the rear most parcels and replaced them with single-family homes on 50 small individual lots. This created a traditional neighborhood layout / development style (i.e. The Village at Country Club) with 1 and 2-story traditional craftsman and low- country style homes spaced closely together, ranging from 1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft. 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres of a designated as commercial was amended and added to allow additional single-family residential, which now makes up phase 5 of the development, which contains an additional 18 single-family dwellings and with the same requirements as the previous 4 phases. This left approx. 1.5 acres of Commercial acreage for commercial development. 2022 amendment: amended the permitted uses in what was remaining of Commercial Tract B to include any use permitted in the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Proposed 2025 amendment: amend the permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, which includes approx. 4.24+/- acres, to allow a combination of residential, professional, and other limited commercial uses on the upland portion of the property, or mixed-use development, leaving the remainder as open space and a master-planned stormwater system. -- 6 of 74 -- PC 5/1/2025 5 A more comprehensive description of previous amendments has also been provided by staff, which has been recommended to be included in the proposed amendment, should the amendment be approved. The intent of the current zoning, a Planned Development (PD) district, per Section 3.3.2 of the UDO, is to provide for large-scale, quality development projects (3 acres and larger) with mixed land uses which create a superior environment through unified development and provide for the application of design ingenuity while protecting surrounding developments. The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies the subject property as Planned Development (PD) and Conservation Preservation (CP). Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the Conservation Preservation (CP) district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The applicant held a community meeting with residents of Carsen’s Ferry on April 24, 2025 at the clubhouse in the Carsen’s Ferry development. It is staffs understanding, from an email staff received by the applicant following this meeting, that the community will only support single- family residential on Tract A, not mixed use. Currently, staff does not have an updated PD narrative or master plan that is required to accompany any PD requests or PD amendments. The applicant has stated that they intend to provide additional information at the upcoming meeting on May 1st . Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. BACKGROUND: The Rivertown Landing Planned Development (PD) district, now Carsen’s Ferry, was originally created in 2007 out of 28.55 acres off Hwy 501 at Riverport Dr. The stated purpose was to “create a walkable, mixed-use community featuring multi-family residential, civic, commercial, and office space in the City of Conway.” Until 2015/2016, the only thing that had been developed in this community was the clubhouse and pool. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: Amended to increase the height allowance for Carsen’s Ferry multifamily project from 40 feet to 52 feet and reduce the total residential units from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: removed all commercial and multifamily from the rear most parcels and replaced them with single-family homes on 50 small individual lots. This created a traditional neighborhood layout / development style (i.e. The Village at Country Club) with 1 and 2-story traditional craftsman and low-country style homes spaced closely together, ranging from 1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft. 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres of a designated as commercial was amended and added to allow additional single-family residential, which now makes up phase 5 of the development, which contains an additional 18 single-family dwellings and with the same requirements as the previous 4 phases. This left approx. 1.5 acres of Commercial acreage for commercial development. 2022 amendment: amended the permitted uses in what was remaining of Commercial Tract B to include any use permitted in the Highway Commercial (HC) district. (UPDATED) Proposed 2025 amendment: amend the permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, which includes approx. 4.24+/- acres, to allow up to six (6) single-family dwellings to be constructed a combination of residential, professional, and other limited commercial uses on the upland portion of the property, or mixed-use development, leaving the remainder as open space and a master-planned stormwater system. Current Zoning: The intent of the current zoning, a Planned Development (PD) district, per Section 3.3.2 of the UDO, is to provide for large-scale, quality development projects (3 acres and larger) with mixed land uses which create a superior environment through unified development and provide for the application of design ingenuity while protecting surrounding developments. -- 33 of 74 -- COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies the subject property as Planned Development (PD) and Conservation Preservation (CP). Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the Conservation Preservation (CP) district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. PLANNING COMMISSION: Planning Commission held the required public hearing on the proposed amendments at their April 3rd and May1st meetings. Residents of Carsen’s Ferry were present at both meetings to express their concerns with the request, which included increased traffic, the possibility of commercial with residential on upper floor units that would overlook the pool amenity area, use of the pool by residents staying in the proposed mixed-use buildings, and commercial uses encroaching closer to residential areas. The applicants held a community meeting in late April with residents of Carsen’s Ferry. As a result of that meeting, in which the residents were adamant that they would only be supportive of single-family units on that parcel, the applicants have since revised their request to propose up to six (6) single-family detached dwellings to be constructed on Tract A of the PD, similar to what was constructed in the Carsen’s Ferry development, even though the current PD allows some commercial uses, including a restaurant. Planning Commission will consider the revised request at their June 5th meeting. Their recommendation will be forwarded to Council with first reading of the request. HISTORY Carsen’s Ferry (aka Rivertown Landing PD) was originally created in 2007 with the intent of developing a mixed-use development on 28.55 acres of land, consisting of multifamily condominium units, office and retail space, as well as civic use space. The multifamily tract would have consisted of 108 condominium units as well as 16,800 sq. ft. of retail space within 3 buildings located along the main entrance road into the community, with the retail space on the bottom floors used for various different specialty shops. The proposed commercial/office park portion of the development was intended to consist of four, 3- story buildings that would house 5,600 sq. ft. of retail space on the first floor and 11,200 sq. ft. on the remaining 2 floors. Upon completion of the development, as originally proposed, there would have been 44,800 sq. ft. of retail space and 89,600 sq. ft. of office/commercial space, located adjacent to the entrance road. The original master plan also included a 12,000 sq. ft. stand-alone restaurant on a 1.6-acre parcel, overlooking the existing pond. Additionally, the original master plan included a 4.6-acre tract that was intended to be used by a civic organization, to contain a 10,000 sq. ft. banquet hall, overflow parking and a small park to accommodate the community. BACKGROUND: Mobile Food Trucks have become extremely popular as a way of generating income. The number of Mobile Food Vending Permits issued has more than doubled from this time last year. Staff spends a great deal of time assisting Mobile Vendors with their submittals for review to ensure that all required documentation is accounted for. This is year-round. A Mobile Food Vending Permit may be issued in February only to expire on April 30th and the whole process starts over again. Staff must also enforce the renewal of Mobile Food Vending Permits. Most vendors will receive their initial permit and never renew but continue to operate in the City limits. Between Franchise Agreements and Private Property vendors, keeping up with Mobile Food Vendors has almost become a full time job. This is time that could be spent completing all other reviews including but not limited to commercials, residential, signs, plats, etc. as well as focusing on zoning violations within the City. After researching, staff has determined that the City of Myrtle Beach only offers 20 Mobile Food Vending Permits each year. Horry County has a cap of 50 Mobile Food Vendors each year. With the continued growth in the City of Conway, a cap would limit the number of Mobile Food Vendors going forward and allow staff to focus on other duties and responsibilities that require our attention. Mobile Food Vending Permits expire each year on April 30 when the City of Conway Business License expires. Prior to renewing their Business License, the Mobile Food Vendor must resubmit all necessary documents to Planning for review as well as schedule an inspection with the Fire Marshal. As of May 8, 2025, nineteen (19) Mobile Food Vendors had renewed. There were thirty-seven (37) Mobile Food Vendors permitted in the 2024-2025 license year. Staff would like to see a cap of forty (40) Mobile Food Vendors allowed to be permitted each year. This would keep the number at a reasonable amount that current staff would be able to oversee and enforce. Any more than forty (40) will require limited time in other areas of review and enforcement by staff. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City A. Mobile vending shall be permitted with the following conditions. 1. Mobile Food Vending Permits are limited to a cap of forty (40) issued per year (May 1 st – April 30 th ), on a first-come, first-serve basis. The vendor shall obtain and carry at all times any SCDHEC (South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control) food handler and / or other applicable health safety licenses. 3. If the vendor wants to operate on public property or on private property under a special event permit, he or she shall obtain notarized written permission from the owner to conduct business. 4. The vendor shall obtain and carry at all times a valid City of Conway Business License. Vendors must obtain an annual zoning compliance. Food truck permits issued under this ordinance will be valid beginning on date of this Ordinance’s enactment until June 30 of the ensuing year. In the following year, a permit shall be from May 1 until April 30 of the ensuing year. [Amended 4-16-18 ZA# 2018-04-16 (B)] 5. The vendor can operate through an approved City of Conway Special Event Permit. Mobile vendors shall not be permitted to operate in the location of Special Event activities without the permission of the Special Event permit holder. 6. The vendor is subject to a background check by the Conway Police Department prior to issuance of a zoning permit. 7. The vendor shall provide a list of the items to be sold and shall be limited to selling food and non- alcoholic beverages. 8. All sales shall be made to pedestrians and bikers only. Vendors may not solicit or conduct business with persons in motor vehicles. 9. The vendor may use only music or bells to attract attention but shall not violate the noise ordinance regulations (City of Conway Code of Ordinances Sec. 9-1-21). 10. The vendor shall not operate in any manner that blocks, obstructs or restricts the free passage of vehicles or pedestrians in the lawful use of the sidewalks or highways or ingress or egress to the abutting property. Vending units shall be in compliance with all ANSI (American National Standards Institute) regulations. 12. The vendor shall be actively engaged in vending operations at all times while occupying any property. 13. BACKGROUND: Typically, detached single-family units are transferred as an affixture to a lot, the conveyance would include: a front yard, side yards, a rear yard, the residence and the underlying property. This pattern of ownership is called: fee simple. Our regulations use dimensional standards to govern such things like: o project density: through minimum lot sizes & open space requirements, o intensity: through minimum lot widths, o building separation: through side yard setbacks, o off-set from internal roadways: through front yard setbacks and o spacing from project boundaries; through rear setbacks as well as landscape buffering A more unconventional pattern of ownership, for single-family homes, is the Condominium form of ownership. This style of ownership, if transferred, conveys to the grantee, an individual unit, consisting of the interior surfaces of the perimeter walls, floors and ceilings, while the underlying and surrounding real property is common area, to be owned by either a Horizontal Property Regime or a property management group. Duplexes can currently be owned: fee-simple (as a semi-detached development) or condominium style (Duplex), but only one duplex per lot in the R-2 and R-3 zoning districts. ANALYSIS: An in-common style of development would use different tools to govern items like: o project density: through minimum parking & open space requirements, o intensity and building separation: through the adoption of building separation requirements, o off-set from internal roadways: through dimensional standards for parking if provided via individual driveways and o spacing from project boundaries: through the adoption of a perimeter setback as well as landscape buffering In many in-common single-family & duplex developments, there is the added complexity of providing residents with privacy and personal space outside of the units in which they own. Often this is resolved by delineating “Limited Common Area” for each unit. This distinction would allow for the owners of the units to practice more control of amenities that are appurtenant to their specific unit (i.e: driveways, -- 63 of 74 -- front porches, patios, etc.…) via the restrictive covenants which would dictate such provisions and/or constraints. However, these: Limited Common Areas would not be required by the political body and should not be counted toward meeting the mandatory Passive or Active Open Space required for the development. Also, required parking may be provided through individual driveways/ garages or through the use of a parking lot style/vehicle use area. If the development chooses to utilize common vehicle use area(s), the amount of required parking would be based on the number of bedroom units (as parking for: apartments are calculated). Since this development is designed for medium to high density, the R-2 and R-3 zoning districts seem the most appropriate, as these districts currently allow: multi-family and townhome in-common developments already and the side setbacks, for standard fee-simple developments are consistent with the proposed building separation. This type of development is convenient for both: short-term & long-term rentals as well as age-restricted communities, as the maintenance of the sites would be the responsibility of the Horizontal Property Regime or property management group, not the owner of the individual unit. The highlighted text and additional images on the following pages are some of the amendments needed to properly govern in-common single-family and duplex developments.
