In addition to façade material requirements, structures shall contain a minimum of two (2) architectural details on front facades, a minimum of one (1) on side facades, and a minimum of one (1) on rear facades that are visible from public rights-of-way, and which must be provided on building elevations at the time of permit submittal: a. Vertical columns or pillars; b. Stonework detailing on columns (if applicable); -- 68 of 74 -- c. Decorative / ornamental window design (i.e. window trim, recesses, adding bay windows, shutters, grids, etc.); d. Decorative (front) door design; e. Decorative / ornamental garage door design (i.e. glass/windows, carriage hardware, etc.); f. Decorative roofline elements, such as roof brackets or dormers; g. Porch (front) or covered entry features; h. Decorative belly band trim; i. Other decorative ornamentation/feature or design technique that meets the intent of this section, with the approval of the Planning Department. 4. Attached Garages and/or Carports. The following standards are applicable to single-family residential structures that contain attached garages and/or carports: a. Attached garages and/or carports shall have a mix of orientations within the development. b. Garage dominant houses (i.e. snout houses), or those in which the garage and/or carport protrudes past the front façade by more than 10 feet, are prohibited in instances where the garage faces the front yard or public street(s). c. Front-load garages, or garages facing a public street, shall contain decorative windows or other acceptable decorative / ornamental feature (standard squares on garage doors do not count). 5. Parking. a. When parking is to be provided via parking lot style/vehicle use area(s), in-common developments shall adhere to the minimum required and maximum allowed parking standards for an “Apartment”, as cited in Article 8, Table 8.3: Parking Requirements and the Handicapped Accessible Parking Requirements of Section 8.2.3. 6. Sidewalks. A sidewalk or walkway, constructed of concrete or decorative pavers, a minimum of three (3) feet in width, shall be installed connecting the front door to the street-front sidewalk or driveway. 7. Overhangs. A minimum overhang/eave of 12-inches shall be required on all sides of all new single- family construction. a. Applicable Building and Fire codes shall apply. 8. Shingles. Where shingles are proposed to be installed, architectural shingles shall be used. Three-tab shingles are prohibited. 9. Roof Pitch. The minimum roof pitch for single-story dwellings shall not be less than 6:12. 10. Chimneys located on an exterior elevation of the dwelling must extend to the ground and be clad in masonry or same as adjacent materials. -- 69 of 74 -- DATE: JUNE 5, 2025 ITEM: IV.D.3 ISSUE: Amendment to Article 15 – Enforcement, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding penalties for violations of the UDO. BACKGROUND: Recently, a case being heard in Municipal Court involved violations of both the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) and Building Code. In addition, there was discussion between Municipal Court and Planning & Development staff regarding the authority to issue judgements for those found guilty of misdemeanor offenses in violations of the UDO. The Construction Services Dept. (formerly Building Dept.) has a Code Enforcement Officer, who is able to issue a Uniform Ordinance Summons, in accordance with SC Code § 56-7-80, in addition to Law Enforcement Officers; however, only sworn Law Enforcement Officers are able to issue both a uniform ordinance summons AND a uniform traffic ticket. Code Enforcement Officers cannot issue uniform traffic tickets because they do not have the power to arrest. Because Planning & Development does not have an employee “designated” or employed as a Code Enforcement Officer, staff reached out to the Municipal Associations General Counsel for advice. Furthermore, Article 15 – Enforcement, of the UDO, does not include language referencing the penalties for such violations of the UDO. Currently, with regard to violations, the UDO states the following: Section 15.1.3 Remedies “A violation of any section of the UDO shall constitute a misdemeanor, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction.” Section 15.1.4 Penalties for Violation “Violation of the UDO or failure to comply with any requirements states herein shall be a misdemeanor, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction.” There is no language specifying the penalty for the offense other than it being a misdemeanor or a civil infraction. Last year, an ordinance was adopted to amend Article 15 to include civil infractions and the penalties for such infractions, which was recommended by the Municipal Association. In this instance, the Municipal Association has stated that while the UDO does not cover the issue of an exact penalty, the general code provides language that would include “any ordinance or resolution of the city, or rule or regulation or order promulgated by any officer or agency of the city under authority duly vested in him or it, any act is prohibited or is declared to be unlawful or an offense or misdemeanor…” as stated in Title 1, Ch. 3, Art. C, Sec. 1-3-48: General Penalty; continuing violations of the city’s general code. The Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) is not contained within the city’s general code; however, it is referenced in Title 5 of the general code. Title 5 – Planning & Development, only includes Building -- 70 of 74 -- Regulations, which also includes a subsection (Sec. 5-1-7 – Violations and penalties) that specifies the penalties for violations of building codes, citing the following: Sec. 5-1-7. – Violations and penalties “Any person, firm, corporation or agent who shall violate a provision of these codes, or fail to comply therewith, or with any of the requirements thereof, or who shall erect, construct, alter, install, demolish or move any structure, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, or has erected, constructed, altered, repaired, moved or demolished a building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, in violation of a detailed statement or drawing submitted and permitted thereunder, and in like manner, any condition which is permitted to exist after notice to abate, discontinue, or remove such condition, duly given by the Building Official shall constitute a misdemeanor. Each such person shall be considered guilty of a separate offense for each and every day or portion thereof during which any violation of any of the provisions of these codes is committed or continued, and upon any conviction of any such violation such person shall be punished within the limits as provided by the ordinances of the City of Conway or the laws of the State of South Carolina.” Ch. 5, Sec. 5-5-1. – Unified Development Ordinance, of the general code, only specifies that the UDO is adopted herein, in accordance with Title 6, Ch. 29 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina 1976, amended as “South Carolina Local Government Comprehensive Enabling Act of 1994.” For the sake of consistency and clarity, staff proposes amending Article 15 – Enforcement, of the UDO to include language specifying that violations of the UDO are a misdemeanor offense that is subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances (general code). With regard to the authority of staff in Planning & Development to issue uniform ordinance summons, staff was advised that there is very little as to what qualifications are necessary to be appointed as a code enforcement officer, and the only statute on the matter in SC Code of Laws (§ 5-7-32) states “A municipality may appoint and commission as many code enforcement officers as may be necessary for the proper security, general welfare, and convenience of the municipality.” Planning & Development staff may be appointed as code enforcement officers so that they could issue uniform ordinance summons as a way to have control of the ticketing process through the Planning & Development Dept. Staff believes that through the authority given within the UDO, this has been satisfied. Staff can provide additional information from the City’s general code if needed that provides the entire sections referenced in this report. RECOMMENDATION: Provide guidance to staff on how to proceed. -- 71 of 74 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 15 - Enforcement 15-1 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 Article 15. Enforcement Article 15 Contents Section 15.1 – Enforcement • 15.1.1, Violations • 15.1.2, Complaints Regarding Violations • 15.1.3, Remedies • 15.1.4, Penalties for Violation • 15.1.5, Legal Status Provisions -- 72 of 74 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 15 - Enforcement 15-2 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 Section 15.1 – Enforcement 15.1.1 Violations If the Planning Director or other designated administrative officer shall find that any of the provisions of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance are being violated, they shall notify in writing the owner or tenant of the property, indicating the nature of the violation and order the action necessary to correct it. They shall order discontinuance of illegal use of land, buildings, or structures; removal of illegal buildings, structures, additions, alterations, or structural changes; discontinuance of any illegal work being done; or shall take any other action authorized by the UDO to ensure compliance with, or to prevent violation of its provisions. 15.1.2 Complaints Regarding Violations Whenever a violation of the UDO occurs, or is alleged to have occurred, any person may file verbal complaint. The complaint stating fully the causes and basis thereof, shall be filed with the Planning Director or other designated administrative officer. They shall record the complaint properly, investigate promptly, and take action thereon as provided by the UDO. 15.1.3 Remedies A. It shall be unlawful to construct, reconstruct, alter, demolish, change the use of or occupy any land, building, or other structure without first obtaining the appropriate permit or permit approval. No permit shall be issued or approved unless the requirements of the UDO are complied with. It shall be unlawful for other officials to issue any permit for the use of any land, building, or structure, or the construction, conversion, demolition, enlargement, movement, or structural alteration of a building or structure without the approval of the Planning Director or other designated administrative officer. A violation of any section of the UDO shall constitute a misdemeanor offense and is subject to penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction. In case a building, structure, or land is or is proposed to be used in violation of any requirements set forth herein, the Planning Director or other appropriate administrative officer, or adjacent or neighboring property owner who would be directly damaged by the violation may in addition to other remedies, institute injunction, mandate, or other appropriate action or proceeding to prevent the unlawful erection, construction, reconstruction, alteration, conversion, maintenance, or use, or to correct or abate the violation, or to prevent the occupancy of the building, structure, or land. Each day the unlawful erection, construction, reconstruction, alteration, conversion, maintenance, or use continues shall be considered a separate offense. B. In case a building, structure, or land is or is proposed to be used in violation of the UDO adopted pursuant to this chapter, the Planning Director or other designated administrative officer may in addition to other remedies issue and serve upon a person pursuing the activity or activities a stop order requiring that entity stop all activities in violation of the UDO. 15.1.4 Penalties for Violation In case any building or structure is erected, constructed, reconstructed, altered, repaired, converted, or maintained; or any structure or land is used in violation of this chapter; or there is a violation of any condition or requirement in connection with variances under the terms of the UDO, that violation shall constitute a misdemeanor offense and is subject to penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction. -- 73 of 74 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 15 - Enforcement 15-3 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended February 3, 2025 Violations of the UDO or failure to comply with any requirements stated herein shall be a misdemeanor offense, subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances, except where specified throughout the UDO as being a civil infraction. Each day such violation continues after due notice to discontinue such violation shall be considered a separate offense. The owner or tenant of any building, structure, premises, or part thereof, and/or any architect, surveyor, builder, engineer, contractor, agent, or other person who commits, participates in, assists in, or maintains that violation may each be found guilty of a separate offense and suffer the penalties herein provided. Nothing herein contained shall prevent the City of Conway from taking such other lawful action as is necessary to prevent or remedy any violation. A. Civil Infractions. Where penalties of the UDO are specified as being a civil infraction, such penalty for violation shall be fifty dollars ($50). 15.1.5 Legal Status Provisions A. Conflict with Other Laws: Whenever the regulations of the UDO require a greater width or size of yards or require a greater percentage of lot to be left unoccupied or impose other more restrictive standards than are required in or under any other statue, the requirements of the UDO shall govern. Whenever the provisions of any other statute require more restrictive standards than are required by this Ordinance, the provisions of such statute shall govern. B. Severability: If any section or provision of the UDO should be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court or competent jurisdiction, such declaration shall not affect the validity of the UDO as a whole or any part thereof which is not specifically declared to be invalid or unconstitutional. C. Repeal of Conflicting Ordinances: All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are repealed to the extent necessary to give the UDO full force and effect. D. Effective Date: The UDO shall take effect and be in force from and after the date of its adoption by the City Council of the City of Conway. -- 74 of 74 --

title: APPD_6.5.25 PC MINUTES
text: PC 6/5/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, June 5, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, George Ulrich, Allan Cornell, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III \ Absent: Greg Bryson, Kendall Brown, David Sligh, Danny-Hardee_ OM -- WAERMWSD: Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Marcus Cohen, IT; Sidney Livingston, Intern Others: Priscilla Fuller, Ashley Cowen, Edna Dewitt, Beverly Marlowe, Collin Brogan, Bob I. Til. IV. Stevens, Andy Christenson, Celia Sands, Vallerie Jordan, Fran Dixson, Anthony Brooks, Edward McQueen, Olga Hays, Craig Anderson, Joan Anderson, Russ Mehl, Annette Blondeau, Mack Hutson. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Cornell to approve the May 1, 2025, minutes, with the correction to Public Input under item IV.B., to state “Andy Christenson, applicant, spoke with the people in opposition to the request”. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 2.22+/- acres of property located on 1091 E Hwy 501 and Amber Ln. (PIN 367-14-04-0003, 0002 & 0001), and request to rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the request was being considered as a result of a requirement to annex by Public Utilities. The subject property, known as South Atlantic Monument Company, is currently on the same water meter as the residential property located at 150 Amber Lane. As a result of the requirement for the 1 PC 6/5/2025 property to have a separate meter, annexation must be requested by the property owner, which also requires that all surrounding property owned by the applicant be subject to annexation. The residential property on Amber Lane will be considered for annexation at a future council meeting. The requested zoning upon annexation for all three properties with frontage on Hwy 501 is Highway Commercial, which is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The intent of the HC District is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the city. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Mack Hutson, was present to answer any questions. He expressed his desire not to be annexed into the city limits. Beverly Marlowe spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. There was discussion as to whether this property would be serviced by City of Conway or GSWSA. Ulrich made a motion to recommend disapproval of the request to rezone the 2.22 acres of property as presented. However, if the council proceeds with annexation, the annexation should comply with the highway commercial designation outlined in the future land use map for the city of Conway. Comell seconded the motion, the motion carried 4-1, with Wise voting in opposition to the denial. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.33+/- acres of property at 1307 Grainger Rd (PIN 368-01-02-0007) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Low/Medium- Density Residential (R-1) district. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that the applicants were requesting to rezone the subject property from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district in order to construct a single-family dwelling. The property has an older commercial structure, previously used as an auto garage, and is currently classified as being storage/warehousing, and the legal nonconforming residence that once existed has been demolished or removed. Per the legal description of the property, the property is described as being lots 20 & 21 from a plat recorded in 1941. Should the rezoning request be approved, the applicant may be required to provide a new plat formally combining the two lots into one and to demo the older commercial structure. PC 6/5/2025 The current zoning map and future land use map identify the property as Highway Commercial, along with several other properties with frontage on Grainger Rd; however, some of these properties contain a residence while others are vacant. The intent of the requested zoning, Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) District is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mig. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Celia Sands, was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Cornell made a motion to approve the request as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone approximately 10.97+/- acres of property at 1808 Rhue Street (PIN 368-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Institutional (IN) district. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that the applicant, Horry County Schools, is requesting to rezone the former site of Whittemore Park Middle School, currently zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) to the Institutional (IN) district in order to utilize the property as the school districts Rivertown Complex, which will house the Conway Adult Education program, a therapeutic learning center for students of HCS, and the districts JROTC program, along with administrative offices. The request is consistent with the city’s future land use map. The intent of the IN District is to provide areas for the development of medical, educational, and higher educational, facilities in a campus-like setting. More specifically, the district is intended to accommodate the development styles, uses, and accessory uses associated with these facilities. This district is not intended for businesses engaged in retail sales, except for those businesses that are clearly accessory to and specifically provide services to the permitted principal use. The Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Institutional (IN). PC 6/5/2025 During presentation of the request at the June 24 council meeting, there was discussion as to whether or not the applicant could operate the proposed uses in a zoning district other than Institutional (IN). Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed. recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. Edna Dewitt and Priscilla Fuller spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Ulrich made a motion to defer the request as presented to allow for an additional public hearing to give the planning department an opportunity to discuss the matter with the school district, to invite them to a future public meeting, and encouraged the district to engage with neighboring residents before the next planning meeting. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (aka Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated that this request to amend the PD for Carsen’s Ferry (a.k.a. Rivertown Landing Planned Development) (PD) district, was discussed at the April and May Planning Commission meetings, where public hearings were held at each meeting regarding the request. Currently, the only uses permitted on Tract A, as one of the 2 remaining “commercial” tracts, are a baked goods store, café or restaurant, candy or confectionary store and an ice cream shop. The PD was originally created in 2007, with the intent of developing a mixed-use community on 28.5 acres, to consist of multifamily, office and retail space, and civic use space. Since that time, the PD has been amended four other times — in 2010, 2017, 2018, and in 2022. The 2017 amendment permitted 50 single-family detached homes in lieu of the multifamily initially proposed on 11.4 acres of the PD, with narrow lots, reduced setbacks, and some portions having rear loaded garaged that were accessed via an alley. The 2017 amendment also removed approximately 5 acres from the PD, which was commercial tract C, and rezoned it to R-2, now part of the Rivertown Row subdivision. In 2018, Commercial tract B was amended to reduce the commercial acreage and added to PC 6/5/2025 the residential portion of the PD in order to permit additional single-family homes, now phase 5 of Carsen’s Ferry. The applicant held a community meeting with the residents of Carsen’s Ferry in April, who were concerned with the mixed-uses proposed for Tract A, the potential for increased traffic, as well as the location and proximity of residential units overlooking the amenities for Carsen’s Ferry. Due to concerns of the community with the proposed mixed-use nature of Tract A, the applicant revised the request to allow only single-family residential as the permitted use, similar to the homes within the Carsen’s Ferry development. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Ashley Cowen, Diamond Shores LLC, was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Wise made a motion to approve the request, ensuring a maximum of six (6) (residential) dwellings. Cornell seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Amendment(s) to Article 5 — Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements Mobile Food Vending. Hucks gave an overview of the proposed amendment(s), stating that this amendment was discussed at Council’s budget retreat earlier in the year. Since the city adopted standards for mobile food vending in 2018, the number of requests that staff receives each year nearly doubles. In 2018, staff received six applications for mobile vending. In 2022/2023, that number increased to more than 20 applications. Last year, staff processed more than 50 applications for mobile food vending. For comparison, the City of Myrtle Beach offers 20 mobile vending permits each year, and Horry County has a cap of 50 mobile vending permits each year for the entire county. The application process for mobile vending is very time-consuming for both staff and the applicant, and due to state regulations for licensing, requirements for approvals by property owners, coordination with other city departments, required inspections, the business license process, related enforcements, and the process for obtaining approval of a franchise agreement with the city (to operate on city-owned property), it has become a fulltime job for one staff member a large portion of the year. Staff proposes to cap the number of mobile food vending permits to 40 per year, to be issued on a first- come, first-serve basis. Business licenses, in addition to the vending permit, must be renewed each year; however, many of them are not renewed yet the vendors continue to operate, which has caused 5 PC 6/5/2025 enforcement issues for staff. The cap of 40 per year would include the three different types of mobile vending — transient mobile vending, mobile vending on private property, and franchise agreements. However, the cap would not include mobile vendors operating under an approved special event permit for specific dates, or other types of franchise agreements that the city enters into, such as Peel Scooters or H20 Excursions (both nonfood-related vendors). Having a limit on the number of mobile vending permits each year not only benefits the brick-and-mortar establishments that are located within the city limits, but it also incentivizes those who were previously licensed to have their mobile vending permits current and to renew each year, on time so that they do not lose their ability to operate in the city limits if the cap is reached before they have submitted their renewal application and have it approved. Staff presented the proposed amendment to Council at the June 2™ mtg., and they asked that there be language added that excluded brick-and-mortar dining establishments in the city limits who may engage in mobile food vending from the cap. That change was added to the proposed amendment. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The board and staff briefly discussed the request. Priscilla Fuller spoke during public input and stated that the information for mobile vending should be publicly available so that people knew what the rules were. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. After much discussion, Cornell made a motion to approve the request with the recommendation to cap the number of permitted mobile trucks to a maximum of 20 per year, excluding the brick-and-mortar restaurants. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Amendment(s) to Article 6 — Design Standards, of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for single-family in-common development. Hucks stated that this topic was previously discussed at a council workshop earlier in the year, following a request received to review a single-family in-common development, which has been receiving more interest from developers. While still considered a typical single-family development, the homes would be built on one single parcel rather than on separate lots, like a traditional subdivision is (or fee simple). Currently, the UDO does not contain standards for single-family in-common development, and the proposed amendments would include standards for minimum separation, off-sets from internal/external roadways, spacing requirements from project boundaries, ingress/egress, zoning requirements, landscaping/buffer requirements, among other standards. This type of development is similar to a 6 PC 6/5/2025 townhome development, which are considered “single-family attached”, and can be built in-common, with standards for doing so already in the UDO; however, single-family detached does not currently have such standards. “In-common” development is a more unconventional pattern of ownership, for single-family homes, is the Condominium form of ownership. This style of ownership, if transferred, conveys to the grantee, an individual unit, consisting of the interior surfaces of the perimeter walls, floors and ceilings, while the underlying and surrounding real property is common area, to be owned by either a Horizontal Property Regime or a property management group. Hucks briefly went over the sections of the UDO that were proposed to be amended, with the proposed changes. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council regarding the proposed amendments. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Wise made a motion to approve the request to amend as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Amendment(s) to Article 15 — Enforcement, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding penalties for violations of the UDO. Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that over the last year or so, staff has been issuing more citations for violations of the UDO that end up requiring court appearances and decisions from Municipal Court, which led to discussions regarding misdemeanor offenses and those who are found guilty of violating the UDO; specifically, because the UDO does not provide specific language as to penalties for such violations. City Council had approved a previous amendment to Article 15 in 2024 that outlined the penalty for those actions deemed punishable as a civil infraction, which related to signs illegally placed in rights-of- way. Staff reached out to the Municipal Association for guidance, and while their legal counsel is of the opinion that 1 — while the contents of the UDO are not contained within the general code; only referenced to say that the UDO “is adopted in accordance with state law under the Planning Enabling Act of 1994”, and 2 — there are a few sections in the city’s general code regarding penalties for violations that include any section of the city’s general code and one section in particular that states “any ordinance of the city, or any rule or regulation promulgated by any officer or agency of the city”, staff proposes to amend 7 VI. VII. PC 6/5/2025 Article 15 to specify that “the penalties for violations of the UDO are a misdemeanor offense that are subject to the penalties in the city’s code of ordinances” for the sake of consistency. The proposed amendment would simply add “subject to the penalties specified in the City of Conway Code of Ordinances” to the end of each sentence in Art. 15 that references violations of the UDO. Additional information can be found in the packet for the June 5, 2025 PC mtg. Staff recommended that Planning Commission hold the required public hearing and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Cornell to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff briefly discussed the proposed amendment. Wise made a motion to approve the proposed amendment(s) to Article 15. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. BOARD INPUT None STAFF INPUT Hucks introduced Sydney Livingston, the city’s summer intern. Sydney is a rising senior at the University of South Carolina. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:55 pm. dayof SOX 2095. \O Jessica Wise, Chairperson Approved and signed this

ISSUE: Request to rezone approximately 1.4+/- acres of property located at the corner of Davidson Rd and Hwy 501 (PIN’s 383-08-02-0003 & -0002) from the Professional (P) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject properties on April 1, 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Professional (P). These properties are lots 1 and 2 on block 8 of the College Park subdivision (see attached plat of College Park). The lots are currently vacant; however, they are encumbered by power transmission line easements, as are several other surrounding lots, which will restrict any type of development. Lot 1 (PIN 383-08-02-0003) is approx. 0.74 acres and Lot 2 (PIN 383- 08-02-0002) is approx. 0.66 acres. The proposed use of the property is not known at this time. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to the Professional (P) zoning district. Per Section 3.2.7 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the P district is to accommodate office, institutional, and residential uses in areas whose character is neither exclusively business nor residential in nature. This district is intended to establish areas that provide professional services to the public, which do not materially detract from nearby residential areas. More specifically, this district should serve as a transitional zone between more intensive commercial areas and residential areas. This district is not intended for businesses that engage in retail sales. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: These parcels front Hwy 501. Lot 1 is a corner lot, adjacent to Davidson Road. There is nothing on either side of these lots, and properties on either side are zoned Professional. Properties directly behind the subject property is zoned R-1; also, part of the College Park Subdivision. While developed in the county, several parcels were annexed into the city limits over the years, including the lots that front Hwy 501. University Baptist Church is located on lots 1-4 on block 9 of College Park. Declaration of Restrictive Covenants Staff was recently made aware of the existence of restrictive covenants for the College Park Subdivision, from when the development was originally created in 1967, recorded in Deed Book 371 at Page 517 (at Horry County Register of Deeds). Building regulations provided in the restrictions is limited to single- family dwellings only, not to exceed two stories in height. Uses are limited to private family residences together with appropriate and approved outbuildings. Further, the restrictions strictly prohibit commercial activity within the College Park subdivision. The restrictions described within the Declaration of Restrictive Covenants are in effect for an initial 20- year period, and then automatically extended for successive periods of 5 years each, unless an instrument signed by the then owners of a majority of lots within the subdivision has been recorded, agreeing to change in the covenants, limitations or restrictions – in whole or in part. There was such an amendment filed in 1996 for lots 1-4 of block 9 of the subdivision, which subsequently allowed a church with amenities to be constructed on said lots. However, the amendment did not include any revisions to any of the other lots -- 9 of 45 -- within College Park. In fact, page 3 of the amendment specifically states that “except as changed, amended, or modified herein, the subdivision Declaration of Restrictions, and any amendment thereto, shall remain in full force, virtue and effect.” While deed restrictions / restrictive covenants are a civil matter, and it is not required by the local planning agency to determine whether such restrictions exist, once we have received notice of their existence, the local planning agency does have the ability to deny plans that would otherwise violate such restrictions. However, they are not enforced by the local planning agency. More specifically: SC Code of Laws, Section § 6-29-1145. Determining existence of restrictive covenant; effect. A. In an application for a permit, the local planning agency must inquire in the application or by written instructions to an applicant whether the tract of land or parcel of land is restricted by any recorded covenant that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity. B. If a local planning agency has actual notice of a restrictive covenant on a tract or parcel of land that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity: 1. In the application for the permit; 2. From materials or information submitted by the person or persons requesting the permit; or 3. From any other source including, but not limited to, other property holders, the local planning agency must not issue the permit unless the local planning agency receives confirmation from the applicant that the restrictive covenant has been released for the tract or parcel of land by action of the appropriate authority or property holders or by court order. C. As used in this section: 1. “actual notice” is not constructive notice of documents filed in local offices concerning the property and does not require the local planning agency to conduct searches in any records offices for filed restrictive covenants. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: Amended to increase the height allowance for Carsen’s Ferry multifamily project from 40 feet to 52 feet and reduce the total residential units from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: removed all commercial and multifamily from the rear most parcels and replaced them with single-family homes on 50 small individual lots. This created a traditional neighborhood layout / development style (i.e. The Village at Country Club) with 1 and 2-story traditional craftsman and low-country style homes spaced closely together, ranging from 1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft. 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres of a designated as commercial was amended and added to allow additional single-family residential, which now makes up phase 5 of the development, which contains an additional 18 single-family dwellings and with the same requirements as the previous 4 phases. HISTORY Carsen’s Ferry (aka Rivertown Landing PD) was originally created in 2007 with the intent of developing a mixed-use development on 28.55 acres of land, consisting of multifamily condominium units, office and retail space, as well as civic use space. The multifamily tract would have consisted of 108 condominium units as well as 16,800 sq. ft. of retail space within 3 buildings located along the main entrance road into the community, with the retail space on the bottom floors used for various different specialty shops. The proposed commercial/office park portion of the development was intended to consist of four, 3- story buildings that would house 5,600 sq. ft. of retail space on the first floor and 11,200 sq. ft. on the remaining 2 floors. Upon completion of the development, as originally proposed, there would have been 44,800 sq. ft. of retail space and 89,600 sq. ft. of office/commercial space, located adjacent to the entrance road. The original master plan also included a 12,000 sq. ft. stand-alone restaurant on a 1.6-acre parcel, overlooking the existing pond. title: APPD_5.1.25 PC MINUTES
text: IL. Il. Iv. PC 5/1/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, May 1, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Greg Bryson, George Ulrich, Kendall Brown, Allan Cornell Absent: Danny Hardee, David Sligh, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner, Marcus Cohen, IT Others: Kenneth Barnes, Ashley Cowen, Annette Blondeau, Russ Mehl, Robert Stevens, Andy Christenson, Craig Anderson, Sheri Walton, Amy Hill, Phillip McLean, Carla Rector, Susan Douthat, Karen Santa, Kate Hartson CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Bryson to approve the April 3, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Deferred... Request to rezone approximately 18.78+/- total acres of property located at the comer of Oak Street and Mill Pond Road (PIN 338-00-00-0019) from the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district to High-Density Residential (R-3) district. Request to rezone approximately 1.4+/- total acres of property located at the corner of Davidson Road and East Highway 501 (PIN’s 383-08-02-0003 & 383-08-02-0002) from the Professional (P) district to Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject properties on. April 1, 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Professional (P). These properties are lots 1 and 2 on block 8 of the College Park subdivision (see attached plat of College Park). The lots are currently vacant; however, they are encumbered by power transmission line easements, as are several other surrounding lots, which will restrict any type of development. Lot 1 (PIN 383-08-02-0003) is approx. 0.74 acres and Lot 2 (PIN 383-08-02-0002) is approx. 0.66 1 PC 5/1/2025 acres. The proposed use of the property is not known at this time. The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestion, and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. These parcels front Hwy 501. Lot I is a corner lot, adjacent to Davidson Road. There is nothing on either side of these lots, and properties on either side are zoned Professional. Properties directly behind the subject property is zoned R-1; also, part of the College Park Subdivision. While developed in the county, several parcels were annexed into the city limits over the years, including the lots that front Hwy 501. University Baptist Church is located on lots 1-4 on block 9 of College Park. Staff was recently made aware of the existence of restrictive covenants for the College Park Subdivision, from when the development was originally created in 1967, recorded in Deed Book 371 at Page 517 (at Horry County Register of Deeds). Building regulations provided in the restrictions is limited to single-family dwellings only, not to exceed two stories in height. Uses are limited to private family residences together with appropriate and approved outbuildings. Further, the restrictions strictly prohibit commercial activity within the College Park subdivision. The restrictions described within the Declaration of Restrictive Covenants are in effect for an initial 20-year period, and then automatically extended for successive periods of 5 years each, unless an instrument signed by the then owners of a majority of lots within the subdivision has been recorded, agreeing to change in the covenants, limitations or restrictions — in whole or in part. There was such an amendment filed in 1996 for lots 1-4 of block 9 of the subdivision, which subsequently allowed a church with amenities to be constructed on said lots. However, the amendment did not include any revisions to any of the other lots within College Park. In fact, page 3 of the amendment specifically states that “except as changed, amended, or modified herein, the subdivision Declaration of Restrictions, and any amendment thereto, shall remain in full force, virtue and effect.” While deed restrictions / restrictive covenants are a civil matter, and it is not required by the local planning agency to determine whether such restrictions exist, once we have received notice of their existence, the local planning agency does have the ability to deny plans that would otherwise violate such restrictions. However, they are not enforced by the local planning agency. More specifically: SC Code of Laws, Section § 6-29-1145. Determining existence of restrictive covenant; effect. A. In an application for a permit, the local planning agency must inquire in the application or by written instructions to an applicant whether the tract of land or parcel of land is 2 PC 5/1/2025 restricted by any recorded covenant that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity. B. Ifa local planning agency has actual notice of a restrictive covenant on a tract or parcel of land that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the permitted activity: 1. In the application for the permit; 2. From materials or information submitted by the person or persons requesting the permit; or 3. From any other source including, but not limited to, other property holders, The local planning agency must not issue the permit unless the local planning agency receives confirmation from the applicant that the restrictive covenant has been released for the tract or parcel of land by action of the appropriate authority or property holders or by court order. C. As used in this section: 1. “actual notice” is not constructive notice of documents filed in local offices concerning the property and does not require the local planning agency to conduct searches in any records offices for filed restrictive covenants. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Kenneth Barnes, C21 McAlpine & Associates was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. Phillip McLean, Amy Hill and Sheri Walton spoke in opposition of the request during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Brown to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to deny the request to rezone from Professional to Highway Commercial, explaining to the applicant that, given the covenants and restrictions, she would consider a rezoning if there were an aspect that facilitated movement on the property, particularly given its location on Highway 501 and its potential viability. She further stated that, under the current PC 5/1/2025 circumstances, she was not comfortable supporting a rezoning. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Previously deferred... Request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (aka Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). Hucks stated that the Rivertown Landing Planned Development (PD) district, now known as the Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development, was originally created in 2007 out of 28.55 acres off Hwy 501 at Riverport Dr. The stated purpose was to “create a walkable, mixed-use community featuring multi-family residential, civic, commercial, and office space in the City of Conway.” Until 2015/2016, the only thing that had been developed in this community was the clubhouse and pool. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: = Amended to increase the height allowance for Carsen’s Ferry multifamily project from 40 feet to 52 feet and reduce the total residential units from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: — removed all commercial and multifamily from the rear most parcels and replaced them with single-family homes on 50 small individual lots. This created a traditional neighborhood layout / development style (i.e. The Village at Country Club) with 1 and 2-story traditional craftsman and low- country style homes spaced closely together, ranging from 1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft. 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres of a designated as commercial was amended and added to allow additional single-family residential, which now makes up phase 5 of the development, which contains an additional 18 single-family dwellings and with the same requirements as the previous 4 phases. This left approx. 1.5 acres of Commercial acreage for commercial development. 2022 amendment: amended the permitted uses in what was remaining of Commercial Tract B to include any use permitted in the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Proposed 2025 amendment: amend the permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, which includes approx. 4.24+/- acres, to allow a combination of residential, professional, and other limited commercial uses on the upland portion of the property, or mixed-use development, leaving the remainder as open space and a master-planned stormwater system. 4 PC 5/1/2025 VI. A more comprehensive description of previous amendments has also been provided by staff, which has been recommended to be included in the proposed amendment, should the amendment be approved. The intent of the current zoning, a Planned Development (PD) district, per Section 3.3.2 of the UDO, is to provide for large-scale, quality development projects (3 acres and larger) with mixed land uses which create a superior environment through unified development and provide for the application of design ingenuity while protecting surrounding developments. The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies the subject property as Planned Development (PD) and Conservation Preservation (CP). Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the Conservation Preservation (CP) district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. The applicant held a community meeting with residents of Carsen’s Ferry on April 24, 2025 at the clubhouse in the Carsen’s Ferry development. It is staffs understanding, from an email staff received by the applicant following this meeting, that the community will only support single- family residential on Tract A, not mixed use. Currently, staff does not have an updated PD narrative or master plan that is required to accompany any PD requests or PD amendments. The applicant has stated that they intend to provide additional information at the upcoming meeting on May 1%. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Ashley Cowen, Diamond Shores LLC was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant briefly discussed the request. 7 UNT Andy Christens , Robert Stevens, Annette Blondeau, Kate Hartson, and Russ Mehl spoke during-public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to defer the request to amend the existing Carsen’s Ferry Plan Development district. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Absent: Staff: Others: Jessica Wise, Greg Bryson, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III, George Ulrich, David Sligh (Left Early) Danny Hardee, Kendall Brown Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlie Crosby, IT Rachel Sullivan, Nate Brown-Fulks, Julie Hartman, Elizabeth Orlando, Kent Gunter, Robert Wiley, Katherine Wiley, JoAnn Trujillo, Tara Ostrander, James Allman, Kimberley Daily I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Anderson made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to approve the February 6, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. IV. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 1.42+/- acres of property located on Bohemia Court and Century Circle in the Atlantic Center Industrial Park (PIN 383-11-02-0003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Planned Unit Development (PUD) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated this property is located within the Atlantic Center Industrial Park and is currently zoned Horry County Planned Unit Development. The property is currently vacant, but the application was likely submitted because there is an intent to develop the site. The applicant is requesting to zone the property Light Industrial upon annexation, which is consistent with other properties in the industrial park that are within the city limits. The city’s future land use map also identifies the property as Light Industrial. Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the LI district is to provide areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: -- 3 of 53 -- PC 3/6/2025 2 There are two properties on the opposite side of Bohemia Court that are in the city limits, both of which are also zoned Light Industrial (LI). One was annexed in 2013 and the other was annexed in 2022. Across Century Circle is a parcel, also in the city limits and zoned LI, owned by the United Way of Horry County. The surrounding uses are consistent with the LI zoning district. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Kent Gunter, FBI Construction was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Anderson made a motion to approve the request as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 7.8+/- acres of property located on (North) Main Street and Chicora Blvd (PIN 338-03-02-0006) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High- Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in January 2025. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently vacant. The property is located at the corner of North Main Street (also referred to as Hwy 701 North) and Chicora Blvd. It is currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC), which is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. Adjacent uses include the Chicora development, which is a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 to the rear of the subject property. Properties on either side of the subject property and across the road are all zoned HC. Any development on the property will also be subject to the requirements of the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), which extends 500-ft from the right of way lines of Hwy 701 N. / Or N. Main Street. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3) in order to develop the property as multifamily. Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) District: The subject property is also within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 3.4.2 of the UDO, the intent of the overlay district is to create a commercial corridor that is well planned and attractive through the implementation of consistent design standards. The provisions of this section will ensure that the design quality of new development in the city’s identified gateway corridors are held to high standards. This section (GCO) shall not apply to detached single-family residential dwellings being used for residential purposes. Per Section 6.5.2, A. – Purpose, of the UDO, the GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors are their primary means of access. -- 4 of 53 -- PC 3/6/2025 3 Per Section 6.5.2, B. – Applicability, the GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of-way line on properties along these highways (90, 378, 501, 501 Bus., 701 (South and North), and 905). Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The subject property abuts the Chicora development, a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 (low/medium- density residential). Other properties beside and across from the subject property are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). There is no property zoned R-3 (high-density residential) in the nearby surrounding area. The property on the opposite side of Chicora Blvd (currently vacant) had previously been proposed and approved for a grocery store (KJ’s) to be developed. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Nate Broman-Fulks, Taft Mills Group was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. Julie Hartman, Elizabeth Orlando, Katherine Wiley and Kimberly Daily spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Sligh made a motion to recommend that the city council deny the request to rezone the 7.0 acres of property as presented. Anderson seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously, with Ulrich voting in opposition to the denial. C. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Amendment to Article 10- Subdivision Design and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for the renaming of existing streets. Hucks stated that last year, city staff received a few requests from the public inquiring about the process for renaming a public street (owned by/dedicated to the City). Currently, the City has no defined process for renaming existing streets that have been dedicated to the city or naming an unnamed street, with the exception of those being created in conjunction with the development of property. However, staff has received a few requests from different residents of the city to rename a city street in which they resided; the most recent one being a resident of McCray Alley, who inquired about renaming the alley to a different name, which they claimed was for public safety reasons. Changing of a street name that has been dedicated to the City should be limited and rare, as doing so may have a negative impact on emergency response. However, in the very rare instances that may warrant a street name change, it would be beneficial to have a process in which such requests may be facilitated. Staff reached out to Horry County about their process of renaming county roads. Horry County requires a public hearing to be held for any proposed road name changes. In addition, the property (road) must be posted, written notification must be provided to affected addressees, and if approved, a plat must be submitted renaming the road and a new street sign must be installed; all of which incur costs. The proposed amendment includes a process for the renaming of a City street, which would require a public hearing to be held by Planning Commission, followed by a recommendation, and two (2) readings by City Council will also be required. -- 5 of 53 -- PC 3/6/2025 4 Staff recommend, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the request as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. BOARD INPUT None VI. STAFF INPUT None VII. ISSUE: A request to amend the Carsen’s Ferry Planned Development (PD) district (Rivertown Landing PD), to amend the list of permitted uses on Commercial Tract “A”, consisting of approximately 4.24+/- acres of property located on Riverport Drive (PIN 337-05-02-0004). BACKGROUND: The Rivertown Landing Planned Development (PD) district, known today as Carsen’s Ferry due to the residential development of the same name within the PD, was originally created in 2006-2007 out of 28.55 acres off Hwy 501 at Riverport Dr. The stated purpose was to “create a walkable, mixed-use community featuring multi-family residential, civic, commercial, and office space in the City of Conway.” Until 2015/2016, the only thing that had been developed in this community was the clubhouse and pool. Since its creation, the PD has been amended four (4) other times. 2010 amendment: Amended the ‘multifamily’ tract to allow multifamily buildings to be 4 stories in height (40’ to 52’) and remainder of tract to allow 50 single-family attached (townhome) units. Also changes to minimum lot size for multifamily tract, revisions to street widths, minor open space amendments. Total number of units reduced from 108 to 86. 2017 amendment: Amend the multifamily tract (renamed to Residential Tract) to allow 50 single- family ‘detached’ dwellings on small, fee simple lots to create a traditional neighborhood design. Design standards were included in this amendment for the single-family homes, such as square footage requirements (1,400 to 2,200 sq. ft.), rear loading garages, porches 12’ behind the walk line, etc. Commercial Tract ‘C’, consisting of approx. 4.94 acres, was removed from this PD and rezoned to R-2 for another development (Rivertown Row). 2018 amendment: 3.5 acres removed from Commercial Tract ‘B’ and added to the Residential Tract in order to construct an additional 18 single-family homes of the same design/style as permitted in previous phases/amendments. Approx. 1.5 acres of Commercial Tract ‘B’ remained. Some of the design standards for the Residential Tract were removed from the PD with this amendment. Setbacks were also revised to be 5’ on all sides for the residential dwellings. 2022 amendment: Commercial Tract ‘B’ was amended to include any use permitted in the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Parking requirements to comply with the UDO for the proposed use. Proposed 2025 amendment: amend Commercial Tract “A”, which includes approx. 4.24+/- acres, to a Mixed-Use tract, and to allow a combination of residential, professional, and limited commercial uses on the upland portion of the property, leaving the remainder as open space and a master-planned stormwater system. -- 32 of 53 -- Current Zoning: The intent of the current zoning, a Planned Development (PD) district, per Section 3.3.2 of the UDO, is to provide for large-scale, quality development projects (3 acres and larger) with mixed land uses which create a superior environment through unified development and provide for the application of design ingenuity while protecting surrounding developments. For reference only, the definition of “Mixed-Use Flexible Zone” per the UDO is provided below: Per Section 3.3.3 of the UDO, the intent of the Mixed-Use Flexible Zone is to encourage a mix of residential, professional, and limited commercial development throughout the City of Conway that does not create excessive demands for vehicular parking. The requirements of the district are designed to promote mixed uses and provide a transition between residential and commercial properties and minimizing adverse effects to adjoining properties. COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the comprehensive plan identifies the subject property as Planned Development (PD) and Conservation Preservation (CP). Per Section 3.2.15 of the UDO, the intent of the Conservation Preservation (CP) district is to provide needed open space for general outdoor and indoor recreational uses and to protect environmentally sensitive areas and flood prone areas from the encroachment of any residential, commercial, industrial, or other uses capable of adversely affecting the relatively undeveloped character of the district. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. First reading of this request could occur as soon as May 5, 2025. -- 33 of 53 -- Carsen’s Ferry PD and PD Amendments Original PD (2007) 2010 amendment 2017 amendment 2018 amendment 2022 amendment 2025 amendment Tract acreage 28.55 (total) 28.55 28.55 (-4.94 acres) = 23.61 acres (with removal of Tract C from PD) 23.61 acres 23.61 acres 23.61 acres?? title: APPD_4.3.25 PC MINUTES
text: PC 4/3/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, APRIL 3, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Greg Bryson, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III, George Ulrich, Kendall Brown Absent: Danny Hardee, David Sligh Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Brent Gerald, Planner Marcus Cohen, IT Others: David Schwerd, Daniel Stacy, Lorraine Birbilis, Russ Mehl, Robert Stevens, Moreen Hettinger, Craig Anderson CALL TO ORDER IL. lI. Iv. Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Wise made a motion to approve the minutes with two amendments discussed. Anderson seconded the motion. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. All amendments have been made in accordance with the board’s request and are contained herein. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. SUBDIVISIONS 1. Kingston Preserve Phase 1- applicant(s) requesting approval of the project layout and street names for the internal streets. (PIN 369-00-00-0044). Hucks stated that the master plan for this project, initially submitted under the name Pelican Pointe’ in October 2023, was reviewed and approved with a design modification by the Planning Commission. The modification granted (a) the use of an emergency access easement and road for Phase 1, and (b) permission to develop the project in multiple phases. Hucks further explained that the first full set of preliminary plans and plats were submitted for review in April 2024. The applicant is requesting approval of the following street names. Horry County has reserved these names for this development (the suffixes have been intentionally omitted): e Greenhouse e Kings Branch ® Monarch e Nature Haven e Tycoon _ PC 4/3/2025 This first phase of development proposes: 134 single-family lots, whereas the master plan originally presented to Planning Commission proposed 182-lots in the initial phase. Access to this phase will be provided via an enlarged (three-lane) entrance off Hwy 378 and a secondary all-weather emergency access off of Tampa Lane, which is consistent with the design originally presented to Planning Commission. To be compliant with the conditions of the design modification, as well as the current Conservation Subdivision ordinance, the applicant will be required to dedicate the mandatory conservation easements for the entire project development area, before final approval of the phase 1 subdivision plat. Staff recommends a thorough review of the applicant’s request. If the Planning Commission approves the applicant’s requests, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval of the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Future phases for Kingston Preserve will also be subject to PC review and approval. The applicant was not present. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the project layout and street names contingent upon addressing all the TRC comments, seconded by Bryson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 20.4+/- acres of property located on Hwy 501 (PIN’s 326-15-03- 0002, 326-00-00-0042 and 337-03-01-0026) and request to rezone from Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest and Agriculture (CFA) zoning district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated the applicant submitted the annexation and rezoning application for the subject property on March 3, 2025. The properties are currently in the county’s jurisdiction, zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and Commercial Forest and Agriculture (CFA). The property is currently vacant. The applicant is requesting to assign Highway Commercial (HC) zoning to the properties upon annexation. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The parcel with PIN 337-03-01-0026 is located across from Squeaky’s Towing, which is zoned HC within the City limits of Conway creating the continuity for the remaining two parcels. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC) and Low/ Medium Density Residential (R-1). Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PC 4/3/2025 The applicant, Daniel Stacy, Oxner and Stacy PA, was present to answer any questions. The board, staff and the applicant discussed the request at length. Anderson made a motion to approve the request to annex 20.4 acres as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 8.5+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN’s 383- 10-03-0020 and -0026) from the Planned Development (PD) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts to the High-Density Residential (R-3) district, and a request to rezone 0.02+/- acres of property located on Technology Blvd (PIN 383-10-03-0027) from the Planned Development (PD) district to the High- Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in March 2025. The properties are already in the city limits, zoned Planned Development (PD) district and Highway Commercial (HC). Two of the parcels include the University Suites Planned Development, with the small .02-acre parcel containing the pump station for University Suites. The other property, across Technology Blvd, is zoned Highway Commercial and is located directly behind the Food Lion shopping center. The applicant proposes to construct 24 multifamily units on the 1.75-acre parcel. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the properties to High-Density Residential (R-3). Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high- density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: These parcels are located behind the Food Lion shopping center, which is zoned HC. It abuts an established single-family residential neighborhood (Coastal Heights), mostly zoned Horry County Residential, no mobile homes allowed (SF10); however, several lots within this development have been annexed into the city over the last few years and are zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). The subject properties also abut property zoned Institutional (IN) that is owned by Horry-Georgetown Technical College (HGTC). The properties are within walking distance to a shopping center, several food establishments, medical offices, a hospital, and both HGTC and Coastal Carolina University (CCU). There are already sidewalks along Technology Blvd, and there are several outlets for vehicular access to Hwy 501. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was much discussion regarding traffic along Technology Blvd and the need for a traffic study with the proposed residential development. Ulrich made a motion to approve the request to rezone as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Cc. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AMENDMENT(S) 1. The board concurred and agreed to proceed. Hucks provided a concise overview of the request, which seeks to amend the permitted uses for Commercial Tract A. This tract encompasses approximately 4.24 acres, the majority of which consists of a pond situated along Highway 501, adjacent to Jordan’s Nursery. Currently, the tract permits a very limited range of commercial uses. The applicant has proposed expanding the allowed uses to create a mixed-use development, combining commercial spaces on the lower floors with residential units on the upper floors. Several residents of Carsen’s Ferry spoke in regards to the request. Their concerns included increased traffic, residential uses on upper floors overlooking the pool amenity, and the location of proposed structures, among other concerns mentioned during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Watkins to close public input. Request to annex approximately 1.42+/- acres of property located on Bohemia Court and Century Circle in the Atlantic Center Industrial Park (PIN 383-11-02-0003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Planned Unit Development (PUD) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district.
