Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Kendall Brown, David Sligh, Greg Bryson, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III, George Ulrich Absent: Danny Hardee Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Marcus Cohen, IT; Louis Smith, IT; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant Others: None I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Sligh to approve the January 9, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. IV. SUBDIVISIONS A. Oak Tree Farm, Phase 3 - Letter of Credit extension / renewal. Hucks stated the Technical Review Committee originally approved plans for this development in 2019. Since that time, the project has been divided into 3 phases, in order to facilitate the development of the project, due to funding. Oak Tree Farm is an affordable housing community designed for individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. The project includes a total of 7 buildings, and 68 residential units. The project also includes a life skills center (with amenity center), a swimming pool and an on-site laundry facility. This letter of credit is to cover any remaining required infrastructure in Oak Tree Farm Phase 3, which in this instance includes remaining landscaping improvements and sidewalk/concrete finishing and is set to expire on February 8, 2025. Staff recommends extending the letter of credit for one more year in the original amount of $124,973.75 by SOS Health Care, LLC to financially guarantee the installation of the remaining required infrastructure. Anderson made a motion to approve the request as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Woodside Crossing, Phase 1 - Letter of Credit extension / renewal. -- 2 of 47 -- PC 2/6/2025 2 Hucks stated the letter of credit to cover any remaining infrastructure requirements for Phase 1 of Woodside Crossing include: concrete curb and gutter, roadway improvements, concrete sidewalk, landscaping and irrigation, street trees, amenity center (clubhouse and swimming pool amenity), and pond fountains, is set to expire on March 1, 2025. The amount of the current letter of credit is $1,719,067.00 and is from Conway National Bank, letter of credit number 3457. The reduced letter of credit amount is $1,468,647.00. Staff recommends extending the letter of credit for one more year, at the requested reduced amount of $1,468,647.00. Sligh made a motion to approve the request as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. V. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. WITHDRAWN……Request to rezone approximately 5.63+/- acres of property located on Shoffner Road (PIN 325-13-02-0002) from the Light Industrial (LI) district to the Heavy Industrial (HI) district. 2. Request to rezone approximately 0.74+/- acres of property located on Sixteenth Ave, between Elm Street and Elizabeth Street (PIN 338-11-01-0049) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Hucks gave the board an overview of the request, stating the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in late December 2024. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Low/Medium- Density Residential. The property is currently vacant. The proposed use of the property has not been disclosed by the applicant; however, the applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the NC district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. A portion of the property abuts property zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and abuts property zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential on one side that is used commercially (was occupied by a cosmetology school at one time) and the other side is also zoned R-1 but currently vacant. Behind the property is a split- zoned parcel, zoned R-1 and HC, with the frontage of that property being on Elizabeth Street. There is also a 10-ft construction easement that runs along one side of the subject property that appears to have been created when additional right-of-way was deeded to SCDOT in 2007. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Neighborhood Commercial. -- 3 of 47 -- PC 2/6/2025 3 Staff recommend, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. Paula Draper spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to recommend approval for rezoning the property from R1 to NC, summitting this request to City Council for their consideration, as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. A. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Previously Deferred…Amendments to Article 2 – Definitions and Article 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for Day Care Facilities. Hucks provided the board with an overview of the request, explaining that staff has received interest from individuals who wish to open a childcare center in a shopping center with "limited hours." The staff was informed that this type of childcare service is considered legally exempt from the state's licensing requirements for childcare centers. Staff reviewed state law regarding the requirements for childcare centers and found the following: SC Code of Laws, Ch. 13 – Childcare Facilities, Article 1, Sec. 63-13-20 defines a childcare facility as: "A facility which provides care, supervision, or guidance for a minor child who is not related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the owner or operator of the facility whether or not the facility is operated for profit and whether or not the facility makes a charge for services offered by it." This definition includes, but is not limited to, day nurseries, nursery schools, childcare centers, group childcare homes, and family childcare homes. The term "childcare facility" does not include facilities that operate for more than 4 hours a day in connection with a shopping center or similar facility, where the same children are cared for less than 4 hours a day AND not on a regular basis. These facilities cater to children whose parents or custodians are occupied on the premises or in the immediate vicinity and are immediately available. These types of facilities must meet local fire and sanitation requirements and maintain documentation of these requirements on file, accessible for public inspection. Currently, the UDO permits after school programs as a conditional use in most of the residential zoning districts; subject to requirements for proof of licensing or proof of exemption, limitations on hours of operation and no more than 4 consecutive hours per day, and fencing requirements for any designated play areas. After school programs are also permitted as an accessory use to all schools or religious institutions and daycare facilities in the Institutional and Professional zoning districts. The current requirements for after school programs restrict the ability for other types of facilities, such as part- -- 4 of 47 -- PC 2/6/2025 4 time childcare facilities in shopping centers, to be permitted under the city’s current ordinance, even though state law exempts such facilities from licensing requirements. This also limits the option for zoning, as such facilities are only allowed in Institutional or Professional zoning districts, as an accessory use to a church or school, or if proposed to operate from a residence. To align with state provisions, staff proposes allowing part-time childcare facilities in commercial districts. Even though these facilities would be considered "legally exempt," the owner or operator would still need to apply for legally exempt status. The state would determine this status, which must be provided prior to the issuance of any city business license. Staff recommend, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to table requested amendment to the City Council as presented. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. VI. BOARD INPUT None. VII. STAFF INPUT Hucks reminded the board that the next scheduled City Council meeting will be on February 18th, rather than the 17th as previously mentioned in the packet. VIII. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 5:56 pm. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in January 2025. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently vacant. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3) in order to develop the property as multifamily. Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) District: The subject property is also within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 3.4.2 of the UDO, the intent of the overlay district is to create a commercial corridor that is well planned and attractive through the implementation of consistent design standards. The provisions of this section will ensure that the design quality of new development in the city’s identified gateway corridors are held to high standards. This section (GCO) shall not apply to detached single-family residential dwellings being used for residential purposes. Per Section 6.5.2, A. – Purpose, of the UDO, the GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors are their primary means of access. Per Section 6.5.2, B. – Applicability, the GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of-way line on properties along these highways (90, 378, 501, 501 Bus., 701 (South and North), and 905). Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The subject property abuts the Chicora development, a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 (low/medium-density residential). Other properties beside and across from the subject property are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). There is no property zoned R-3 (high-density residential) in the nearby surrounding area. The property on the opposite side of Chicora Blvd (currently vacant) had previously been proposed and approved for a grocery store (KJ’s) to be developed. -- 18 of 47 -- Dimensional Standards / Other Requirements (comparison): Dimensional Standards Comparison Current Zoning (HC) Proposed Zoning (R-3) Min. The proposed site is well located to provide much needed housing affordable to residents serving vital roles in the community. High quality housing at affordable prices is becoming incredibly difficult to find in Conway, and other desirable places to live. Chicora Springs Trace is specifically designed to help meet that need in the community. The site is in a great location for a workforce community. It is near many employers, parks, retail options, service providers, schools, a library, and downtown shops. The proposed development, once completed, will represent an over $22 million-dollar investment in the community. Owner/Developer Overview Founded in Greenville, NC in 2014 by Tom Taft Sr. and Dustin Mills, Taft Mills Group (TMG) has established itself as one of the preeminent developers of affordable workforce housing in the southeast. Presently, TMG has more than 1,750 units in operation and almost 800 units under construction. Taft-Mills Group is led by its principals, Dustin T. Mills and C.J. Tyree, who bring a combined forty-five years of experience in the affordable housing field. Taft, Sr. Taft Family Ventures is a vertically integrated developer, builder, and manager that has developed over 5,000 multifamily units and over 800,000 square feet of commercial space. The experience and financial capacity of Taft Family Ventures combined with the affordable experience of Dustin and C.J. has led TMG to consistently be ranked as a top 50 affordable housing developer in the country. Location Overview The area immediately surrounding the proposed site features a great selection of parks, restaurants, grocery stores, retail shopping venues, doctor offices, and schools. Most of these amenities are within 1 mile from the Chicora Springs Trace site and all the amenities are just a short drive. In addition to these amenities, there are over 4,000 jobs within a 2-mile radius of the site for employees making wages that our community is designed to serve. -- 22 of 47 -- Project Benefits The development of Chicora Springs Trace will help address an extreme need that exists today in Conway for newly constructed high-quality affordable workforce housing units. As proposed, the community will consist of a mix of 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, and 3-bedroom units. The site will include four residential buildings and a clubhouse. The community will feature many amenities for our residents. The clubhouse will include an on-site management office, staffed with a full-time property manager, a community room, fitness center, and business center. The site will also include a covered patio area and a playground. Rents are expected to range from between $250 and $1,200 and will serve residents who have an average household income below 70% of Horry County’s Area Median Income, or $55,500 for a family of four. The community will not only benefit its residents and surrounding businesses, but it will also provide significant property tax revenue to the City of Conway. -- 23 of 47 -- Chicora Springs Trace Conway, SC A PROPOSED WORKFORCE HOUSING COMMUNITY BY: 3/6/25 -- 24 of 47 -- Overview • Principals at TMG have completed: • 100+ affordable communities • 5,000+ units • $850+ million in total development costs • Active in North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Maryland & Ohio • Consistently ranked top 50 workforce housing developer nationwide by Development Finance Magazine Residences at Railroad Square Brunswick, MD -- 25 of 47 -- PARKSIDE COMMONS GREENVILLE, NC (98 Units – Senior Housing) Completed Project - 2016 -- 26 of 47 -- Completed Project - 2017 Wakefield Commons Raleigh, NC (68 Family Units) -- 27 of 47 -- Completed Project - 2022 Eastbend Trace Greenville, NC (72 Family Units) -- 28 of 47 -- CRENSHAW TRACE WAKE FOREST, NC (68 Units – Senior Housing) Completed Project - 2022 -- 29 of 47 -- Residences at Railroad Square Brunswick, MD (45 family Units) TMG – Under Construction Visual -- 30 of 47 -- The Junction – Under Construction Frederick, MD (179 family units) -- 31 of 47 -- SITE Aerial View • 2503 N. BACKGROUND: Currently, the City has no defined process for renaming existing streets that have been dedicated to the city or naming an unnamed street, with the exception of those being created in conjunction with the development of property. However, staff has received a few requests from different residents of the city to rename a city street in which they resided; the most recent one being a resident of McCray Alley, who inquired about renaming the alley to a different name, which they claimed was for public safety reasons. Changing of a street name that has been dedicated to the City should be limited and rare, as doing so may have a negative impact on emergency response. However, in the very rare instances that may warrant a street name change, it would be beneficial to have a process in which such requests may be facilitated. Staff reached out to Horry County about their process of renaming county roads. Horry County requires a public hearing to be held for any proposed road name changes. In addition, the property (road) must be posted, written notification must be provided to affected addressees, and if approved, a plat must be submitted renaming the road and a new street sign must be installed; all of which incur costs. Staff presented the issue to City Council at a workshop last August, and they agreed with staff to create a process in which a resident / addressee may request a street be renamed. If approved, the fee schedule for the Planning & Development Dept. will also need to be amended to reflect a $250 fee in conjunction with such requests. The proposed amendment includes a process for the renaming of a City street, which would require a public hearing to be held by Planning Commission, followed by a recommendation, and two (2) readings by City Council will also be required. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: In addition to holding the required public hearing, staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 45 of 47 -- Article 10. Subdivision and Land Development Article 10 Contents Section 10.1 – General Guidelines for Subdivisions and Land Development • 10.1.1, Adoption and Amendment • 10.1.2, Land Development and Subdivision Defined • 10.1.3, Compliance • 10.1.4, Enforcement by City Staff • 10.1.5, Coordination of Plans • 10.1.6, Administrative Fee Section 10.2 –Review Procedures • 10.2.1, Approval Levels • 10.2.2, Land Development Types • 10.2.3, Approval Authority • 10.2.4, Plan and Plat Requirements • 10.2.5, Review Periods for Plan and Plat Submittals • 10.2.6, Appeals • 10.2.7, Effects of Approvals – Prerequisites Section 10.3 – Subdivision Design Standards • 10.3.1, General Standards • 10.3.2, Lots Must Comply with Zoning Requirements • 10.3.3, Design in Respect to Physical Conditions • 10.3.4, Connectivity and Appropriateness to Adjoining Property and Land Uses • 10.3.5, Reserve Strips, Half Streets, and Private Streets • 10.3.6, Intersections • 10.3.7, Blocks • 10.3.8, Lots and Building Sites • 10.3.9, Park and Open Space Dedication • 10.3.10, Reserved • 10.3.11, Construction in Public Right-of-Way and Easements • 10.3.12, Subdivision Street Design • 10.3.13, Storm Drainage in Streets • 10.3.14, Utility Easements • 10.3.15, Development Entrance Markers and Landscaped Medians • 10.3.16, Water and Sewer • 10.3.17, Wastewater Pump Stations • 10.3.18, Subdivision Naming • 10.3.19, Street Names • 10.3.20, Street Addresses • 10.3.21, Street Renaming -- 46 of 47 -- 10.3.21 Street Renaming To reduce any possible impediment in emergency response, during the transitional period, changing the name of an existing public street dedicated to the City of Conway should be limited and rare. Requests to rename a street dedicated to the City may be approved by City Council through adoption of an ordinance to rename the subject street(s), only after Planning Commission has made a recommendation and review by the Technical Review Committee (TRC). The following provisions shall apply: A. Other than the requested street name, alternative names shall be provided in the event that the requested name is not an available street name. Potential street names shall not: 1. Duplicate or be phonetically similar to any existing street name(s); 2. Be named after any person(s) unless such individual is of historical significance; 3. Include offensive, obscene, vulgar or profane language B. Street Renaming Process 1. Application and/or petition shall be completed and submitted with the applicable fee. a. The applicant must be an addressee on the subject street and have a compelling reason for such request; b. The signers of the application/petition must be addressees for individual properties, residents, or businesses located on the subject street. 2. Requested street name(s) must be reviewed by the Technical Review Committee (TRC) and shall be submitted to Horry County Addressing for availability and reservation (if approvable). 3. Public Hearing required. Once the proposed street name(s) has been reserved, the meeting date in which Planning Commission shall consider the request will be set, in accordance with public notice requirements, and as provided for herein: a. Public notice shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the city a minimum of fifteen (15) days prior to the public hearing in which the request will be considered; b. Individual notices shall be sent to the current addressees of the subject street, and such notice shall contain a description of the matter to be heard. 4. Following Planning Commission’s recommendation and the required public hearing, the request will be forwarded to City Council along with such recommendation from Planning Commission and the Technical Review Committee (TRC). Two (2) readings of such ordinance will be required. 5. Street Name Signs shall be the standard City of Conway, size and color and shall be mounted on steel posts with appropriate brackets. The applicant/petitioner shall be responsible for all materials and labor necessary for the street sign. 6. City of Conway GIS will assign new street addresses once sign installation is completed and will be done in accordance with the street addressing standards provided herein (Section 10.3.20). a. New street addresses shall not be assigned to reflect the name change until the street sign(s) have been replaced. b. Address verification letters may be provided by City of Conway GIS upon request; however, it is the responsibility of the affected addressees to notify all appropriate parties of their change of address (i.e. employer, utility providers, financial institutions, governmental agencies, etc.) -- 47 of 47 --

text: PC 3/6/2025 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, March 6, 2025 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Greg Bryson, Ellen Watkins, Thomas J. Anderson III, George Ulrich, David Sligh (Left Early) Absent: Danny Hardee, Kendall Brown Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant; Charlie Crosby, IT Breoman Others: Rachel Sullivan, Nate Brown-Fulks, Julie Hartman, Elizabeth Orlando, Kent Gunter, Robert Wiley, Katherine Wiley, JoAnn Trujillo, Tara Ostrander, James Allman, Kimberley Daily CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Anderson made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to approve the February 6, 2025, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried Il. I. PUBLIC INPUT unanimously. Iv. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 1.42+/- acres of property located on Bohemia Court and Century Circle in the Atlantic Center Industrial Park (PIN 383-11-02-0003), and request to rezone from the Horry County Planned Unit Development (PUD) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) district. Hucks stated this property is located within the Atlantic Center Industrial Park and is currently zoned Horry County Planned Unit Development. The property is currently vacant, but the application was likely submitted because there is an intent to develop the site. The applicant is requesting to zone the property Light Industrial upon annexation, which is consistent with other properties in the industrial park that are within the city limits. The city’s future land use map also identifies the property as Light Industrial. Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the LI district is to provide areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: PC 3/6/2025 There are two properties on the opposite side of Bohemia Court that are in the city limits, both of which are also zoned Light Industrial (LI). One was annexed in 2013 and the other was annexed in 2022. Across Century Circle is a parcel, also in the city limits and zoned LI, owned by the United Way of Horry County. The surrounding uses are consistent with the LI zoning district. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Kent Gunter, FBI Construction was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Anderson made a motion to approve the request as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 7.8+/- acres of property located on (North) Main Street and Chicora Blvd (PIN 338-03-02-0006) from the Highway Commercial (HC) district to the High- Density Residential (R-3) district. Hucks stated the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in January 2025. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Highway Commercial (HC). The property is currently vacant. The property is located at the corner of North Main Street (also referred to as Hwy 701 North) and Chicora Blvd. It is currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC), which is also consistent with the city’s future land use map. Adjacent uses include the Chicora development, which is a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 to the rear of the subject property. Properties on either side of the subject property and across the road are all zoned HC. Any development on the property will also be subject to the requirements of the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO), which extends 500-ft from the right of way lines of Hwy 701 N. / Or N. Main Street. Proposed Zoning of Property: The applicant is seeking to rezone the property to High-Density Residential (R-3) in order to develop the property as multifamily. Per Section 3.2.5 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), the intent of the R-3 district is to provide areas for high-density attached, detached, semi-attached, and multifamily residential development in the City of Conway and to prohibit uses that would substantially interfere with the development or continuation of residential structures in the district. Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO) District: The subject property is also within the Gateway Corridor Overlay (GCO). Per Section 3.4.2 of the UDO, the intent of the overlay district is to create a commercial corridor that is well planned and attractive through the implementation of consistent design standards. The provisions of this section will ensure that the design quality of new development in the city’s identified gateway corridors are held to high standards. This section (GCO) shall not apply to detached single-family residential dwellings being used for residential purposes. Per Section 6.5.2, A. — Purpose, of the UDO, the GCO is established to provide standards relative to accessibility, appearance, and safety in the development of commercial, industrial, multifamily residential, and office projects that utilize highway corridors are their primary means of access. PC 3/6/2025 Per Section 6.5.2, B. — Applicability, the GCO district shall extend 500 feet from the right-of-way line on properties along these highways (90, 378, 501, 501 Bus., 701 (South and North), and 905). Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The subject property abuts the Chicora development, a single-family neighborhood, zoned R-1 (low/medium- density residential). Other properties beside and across from the subject property are zoned Highway Commercial (HC). There is no property zoned R-3 (high-density residential) in the nearby surrounding area. The property on the opposite side of Chicora Blvd (currently vacant) had previously been proposed and approved for a grocery store (KJ’s) to be developed. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the HC district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant, Nate Broman-Fulks, Taft Mills Group was present to give a brief presentation and to answer any questions. Julie Hartman, Elizabeth Orlando, Katherine Wiley and Kimberly Daily spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Sligh made a motion to recommend that the city council deny rezone the 7.0 acres of property as presented. Anderson seconded the motion. The motion carrjéd unanimously, With Ulrich voting in opposition to the denial. : H-\ C. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. Amendment to Article 10- Subdivision Design and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for the renaming of existing streets. Hucks stated that last year, city staff received a few requests from the public inquiring about the process for renaming a public street (owned by/dedicated to the City). Currently, the City has no defined process for renaming existing streets that have been dedicated to the city or naming an unnamed street, with the exception of those being created in conjunction with the development of property. However, staff has received a few requests from different residents of the city to rename a city street in which they resided; the most recent one being a resident of McCray Alley, who inquired about renaming the alley to a different name, which they claimed was for public safety reasons. Changing of a street name that has been dedicated to the City should be limited and rare, as doing so may have a negative impact on emergency response. However, in the very rare instances that may warrant a street name change, it would be beneficial to have a process in which such requests may be facilitated. Staff reached out to Horry County about their process of renaming county roads. Horry County requires a public hearing to be held for any proposed road name changes. In addition, the property (road) must be posted, written notification must be provided to affected addressees, and if approved, a plat must be submitted renaming the road and a new street sign must be installed; all of which incur costs. The proposed amendment includes a process for the renaming of a City street, which would require a public hearing to be held by Planning Commission, followed by a recommendation, and two (2) readings by City Council will also be required. VI. VIL. PC 3/6/2025 Staff recommend, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the request as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. BOARD INPUT None STAFF INPUT None ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:38 pm. Approved and signed this 2 day of SPRL , 2025. Ogeacd Dug Jessica Wise, Chairperson

Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Kendall Brown, David Sligh, Greg Bryson, Ellen Watkins, Danny Hardee, Thomas J. Anderson III, George Ulrich Absent: None Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Brent Gerald, Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant Others: Kelvin Causey, Kelvin Chadwick, Jay Sellers, O’Brian Martin, Daniel Asmonga I. CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. ELECTION OF OFFICERS Ulrich made a motion to nominate Sligh to serve as Vice Chairman, seconded by Anderson. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. Ulrich made a motion to nominate Wise as Chairperson, seconded by Watkins. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. III. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Sligh made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to approve the December 12, 2024, minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. IV. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. V. DESIGN MODIFICATIONS A. Previously Tables… Buchanan Lane – The applicant, Sellers Construction, is requesting a design modification from the required street improvements and roadway design standards for future development of property located on an existing private roadway – Buchanan Lane (PIN 324-16-01- 0005), including the requirement for the property to have frontage onto a publicly maintained street. Wise stated that this request had been previously tabled and entertained a motion to untable. Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Watkins, and the motion carried unanimously. Hucks stated the 4.04-acre tract was annexed into the city limits in 2023 as Low-Density Residential (R). The property owner proposes to develop a single-family dwelling on the property at some point in the near future; however, no permits for the structure have been applied for at this time. Buchanan Lane is a 50’ unimproved right-of-way. -- 2 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 2 Per Section 10.5.2 – Street Improvements, of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), “all proposed streets shall be graded to the full width of the right-of-way and improved with a pavement width and standard curb and gutter and storm drainage section as required for the particular classification of street. All grading, pavement and curb and gutter shall be designed and installed in accordance with City of Conway standards and the approved construction plan”. Section 10.9.3 – Basic Design Requirements, provides several standards for construction of streets to be dedicated to the City upon completion, including right of way standards, drainage system/stormwater requirements, sub-grade/surface material requirements, underdrain requirements, standards for shoulders/ditches, etc. The applicant is seeking a design modification to allow Buchanan Lane to be improved to the same standards as Graham Rd; provided that the 24’ pavement width requirement is still met. Granting the modification would exempt the applicant from the requirement to install curb/gutter, sidewalks, and street trees along either side of Buchanan Lane. The design modification, if granted, will not exempt the applicant from having to comply with other construction standards, including base/binder course/subgrade requirements, surface course requirements, minimum paving tolerances, installation of street signage (if applicable), applicable drainage/stormwater improvements, etc. Public Works may also require that a geotechnical report and pavement design be provided if the native soil’s conditions are considered unsatisfactory or of questionable suitability. Additionally, Buchanan Lane will be required to be dedicated to the City for perpetual maintenance once the improvements have been completed AND before any permits for any construction on the property can be issued. The requirements of Section 10.5.2 (A) – Street Improvements, regarding the requirement for all lots to be directly connected to the public street system and not an “island”, are and will continue to be applicable to this property. Staff Recommendation, before this request was tabled at the July 2024, PC meeting, it was the understanding of staff that the applicant intended to dedicate the road to the city, once improvements were installed. However, the underlying owners of Buchanan Lane do not wish to dedicate the improvements to the City although they have no issue with the applicant installing the road improvements. The issue of the lot – already created and not fronting a public street – is an issue that has come up more frequently the past few years. Bill Mack Blvd, on the other side of Graham Rd, has several lots that do not access a public street and some of which rely on city services. Bill Mack is not paved, and residents are required to bring their roll carts to Graham Rd in order for sanitation trucks to empty. Other properties throughout the city either front unimproved rights of way that ARE owned by the city, county, or state – but not maintained, or the right-of- way doesn’t exist at all. Many of these properties are heirs’ property and even if the heir was willing to improve the right-of-way, they would likely not have the right to do so unless the underlying property owners were still alive and knew who they were. Planning Commission may be most familiar with property on Sixth Ave that was considered last year for similar reasons as Buchanan Lane. However, unlike Sixth Ave, in the case of Buchanan Lane, not knowing the ownership of the underlying property is not an issue. The underlying ownership is identified, and the owner also gets their access from Buchanan Lane. They too would benefit from the improvements proposed by the applicant. However, they do not wish to deed the portion of the road being improved to the City for perpetual maintenance. This does pose an issue with perpetual maintenance of Buchanan Lane. Ultimately, if -- 3 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 3 Planning Commission wishes to grant the design modification, the underlying owner will continue to own the private roadway, and maintenance of the road will be a civil issue. A possible solution may be to require a maintenance agreement to be recorded showing the roadway (as well as any realignments of the easement) that details the maintenance responsibilities of all tenants of Buchanan Lane. The applicant, Jay Sellers, Sellers General Construction, LLC was present to answer any questions. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Sligh made a motion to approve the design modification, allowing the road width, curb, and gutter requirements to be substantially similar to Graham Road, as opposed to the full requirements under the UDO. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried with Wise and Hardee voting no. VI. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 7.62+/- (total) acres of property located at 1705 Hwy 501 and on E. Cox Ferry Rd (PINs 383-01-02-0030 & 383-01-03-0002), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and High Bulk Retail (RE4) districts to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LI) and Highway Commercial (HC) districts. Hucks gave the board an overview of the request, stating that the applicant submitted an annexation and rezoning application for the subject properties November 2024. The property is located in the city’s water utility service area and is contiguous to property in the city limits. This annexation is part of a broader enforcement issue related to the subject property that has been ongoing for a few years now. The applicant relocated his business, H&H Builders, from another property on Hwy 501 (in county’s jurisdiction) to this location, which has been owned by the applicant for some time. Both properties are still in the county’s jurisdiction; however, there were and continue to be issues related to business licensing, unpermitted structures, and uses on the subject properties, in that the county’s zoning compliance approval for the sales office is solely for a sales office only and not for any outdoor display, and a large metal building (more than 3,000 sq. ft.) in size, was erected on one of the parcels without a building permit (aerial photograph from April 2024 included in packet). Complicating matters, the properties were one parcel before being split in 2007 (plat book 221, pg. 175). The railroad right-of-way separates the two parcels. Now that they are separated, they cannot be recombined, due to the right-of-way that exists. However, both parcels include the use of manufactured homes sales, and in order for the manufactured home sales business to be compliant, the sales office, parking, etc., must be located on the same property as the display models are located; otherwise, the use is considered outdoor storage, which is prohibited except in conjunction with a permitted use. The applicant was attempting to become compliant with Horry County’s requirements; however, in order for them to do so, they would need to provide water to the unpermitted metal building on the same parcel as the displays (manufactured home units) are located on. Being that it would be an extension of (water) service, or a new service if none currently exists, the requirement to annex becomes applicable. The issue for staff is that if the property is annexed under the current condition, then the city is inheriting a use on a property that was never legally permitted on the property as well as structures that were never issued -- 4 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 4 a building permit. Yet, the only way for the property to comply would include the requirement for city water to be extended to the property, which requires the applicant to request annexation. Staff has been working with the applicant’s attorney on the issues and has agreed that if Council chose to annex the properties, that they would be given the opportunity to request variances for some of the outstanding issues without the threat of further enforcement, pending the outcome of the variance requests, as they cannot request any variances (from the City’s requirements) until and unless the property has been annexed. If Council chooses not to annex, the applicant would need to comply with the requirements for the county. While manufactured home sales is the current use of one of the properties, the applicant has stated that they would be phasing that use out in the near future and would pursue approval to develop mini-storage and/or other commercial / industrial uses. The requested zoning upon annexation is Highway Commercial (HC) (0.47-acre parcel with frontage on Hwy 501) and Light Industrial (LI) (7.15-acre tract with frontage on E. Cox Ferry Rd). The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the larger tract fronting E. Cox Ferry Rd as being Industrial, and the smaller parcel with frontage on Hwy 501 as Highway Commercial (HC). The future land use map does not distinguish between light and heavy industrial, only “industrial”, but because Light Industrial (LI) is the requested zone for the larger parcel upon annexation, that district is defined below: Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. O’Brian Martin, agent for applicant, was present to answer any questions. The request was discussed at length. Bryson made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried with Hardee voting no. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to rezone approximately 5.63+/- acres of property located on Shoffner Road (PIN 325-13-02-0002) from the Light Industrial (LI) district to the Heavy Industrial (HI) district. Hucks provided the board with an overview of the request, stating that the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in December 2024. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Light Industrial (LI). The property is currently owned by UFP Real Estate, LLC. The current use / business on the subject property is UFP Mid-Atlantic, LLC, a building materials supplier (i.e. roof trusses, etc.). The use of the property is split onto 2 separate properties, which are zoned differently. The larger property that contains the main building (not part of the request) is zoned Heavy Industrial (HI). The other property, which is proposed to be rezoned, is currently zoned Light Industrial (LI). The applicant wishes to combine -- 5 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 5 the properties but because they are zoned differently, one of the properties must be rezoned to have the same zoning as the other property it’s proposed to be combined with. Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The applicant, Kelvin Causey was present to answer any questions. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Ulrich made a motion to defer the request. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. C. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. To be DEFFERED…Amendments to Article 2 – Definitions and Article 5 – Specific Use Regulations, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding requirements for Day Care Facilities. The above item was deferred. 2. Previously Deferred… Amendment(s) to Article 11 – Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for signs. Hucks stated that since early 2023, city staff has been going through the UDO to identify inconsistencies, typos, and other items that may be lacking within each Article of the UDO. The sign ordinance, although amended a few times through the years, has not had a comprehensive review of all sign requirements, and as part of the city’s UDO cleanup effort, staff is seeking to amend Article 11 to address several issues that have been identified through the years and/or that have caused confusion amongst staff and the sign community, as well as different interpretations. Some of the amendments include, but are not limited to: • Revisions to requirements for signage in residential zoning districts; • Addition of murals to signage that is considered to be exempt from permitting procedures, provided that it does not contain text or images that identify the business or business product(s) • Clarification of number of wall signs permitted on corner buildings or lots; • Removal of balloons as being ‘prohibited’ signage; • Revisions to requirements for EMC/LED signs – regarding distance to residential structures or properties; • Minor revisions to design requirements for monument signs (deletion of repetitive language); • Revisions to requirements for drive-thru signs (i.e. menu panel options); and • Housekeeping revisions to sign permit requirements -- 6 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 6 Staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the proposed amendments to Article 11 and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the requested amendment to City Council as presented. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Amendment(s) to Article 9 – Landscaping and Buffer Requirements, the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding Landscaping, Buffer, and Tree Preservation requirements. Hucks stated that staff is proposing an amendment to Article 9 that would allow for a more clarification on commonly misinterpreted aspects of the Tree Preservation Ordinance, penalties for violations of the ordinance, as well as a more appropriate course of action for Tree Board appeals, as well as other minor amendments to the landscaping requirements; part of the ongoing effort to cleanup articles of the UDO. Amendments include (but are not limited to) the following: 1. Codify the Tree Preservation Ordinance into the UDO. Then the Tree Ordinance falls under the purview of the Planning & Development Dept. 2. Designate that the Community Appearance Board (CAB) will continue to act as the Tree Board; however, appeals of the decisions of the Tree Board would instead be directed to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). 3. Amend the Tree Preservation Ordinance, including the Appeals Section (Sec. 3-4-15 – Appeals, that directs appeals of the Tree Board to Conway City Council, to direct appeals of the Tree Board decision to Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) instead of City Council. Decisions of BZA would be appealable to circuit court. 4. Adopt an application fee ($250) for Tree Board Appeals. Staff proposes to begin charging $250 for Tree Appeal applications. Should applicants seek to appeal the decision of the Tree Board, and these requests go to BZA, the property will need to be posted, the appeal would need to be advertised, letters would need to be sent to adjacent property owners, and decisions from the BZA would need to be mailed certified to interested parties. 5. Upon the request of tree board, staff has made some housekeeping changes throughout the ordinance to ensure a more uniform and concise understanding of the processes and terminology used throughout the ordinance. These items include clarity of the process of tree mitigation, implementation of higher penalties for improper removal of protected or landmark trees, and clarification on definitions that were commonly misinterpreted. 6. Addition and deletion, upon the request of the tree board, of trees from the protected tree list. The tree board asked to remove non-native trees, Crepe Myrtle and Dawn Redwoods, from the protected list but to rather include native trees, such as a Tulip tree, Red Cedar, and a Tupelo tree. -- 7 of 29 -- PC 1/9/2025 7 Staff recommends, in addition to holding the required public hearing, that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the proposed amendments and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the requested amendment to City Council as presented. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. VII. BOARD INPUT None. VIII. STAFF INPUT None. IX. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:54 pm. The property is currently vacant. The proposed use of the property has not been disclosed by the applicant; however, the applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the NC district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: A portion of the property abuts property zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and abuts property zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential on one side that is used commercially (was occupied by a cosmetology school at one time) and the other side is also zoned R-1 but currently vacant. Behind the property is a split-zoned parcel, zoned R-1 and HC, with the frontage of that property being on Elizabeth Street. There is also a 10-ft construction easement that runs along one side of the subject property that appears to have been created when additional right-of-way was deeded to SCDOT in 2007. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Neighborhood Commercial. BACKGROUND: Staff has received interest from individuals who would like to open a childcare center in a shopping center with “limited hours”. Staff was informed that this type of childcare service is considered legally exempt from the state’s licensing requirements for childcare centers. Staff looked at state law regarding the requirements for childcare centers, and found the following: SC Code of Laws, Ch. 13 – Childcare Facilities, Article 1, Sec. 63-13-20, defines a childcare facility as “a facility which provides care, supervision, or guidance for a minor child who is not related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the owner or operator of the facility whether or not the facility is operated for profit and whether or not the facility makes a charge for services offered by it.” This definition includes, but is not limited to, day nurseries, nursery schools, childcare centers, group childcare homes, and family childcare homes. The term does not include facilities that are operated for more than 4 hours a day in connection with a shopping center or service or other similar facility, where the same children are cared for less than 4 hours a day AND not on a regular basis while parents or custodians of the children are occupied on the premises or are in the immediate vicinity and immediately available. These types of facilities must meet local fire and sanitation requirements and maintain documentation on these requirements on file at the facility available for public inspection. Currently, the UDO permits after school programs as a conditional use in most of the residential zoning districts; subject to requirements for proof of licensing or proof of exemption, limitations on hours of operation and no more than 4 consecutive hours per day, and fencing requirements for any designated play areas. After school programs are also permitted as an accessory use to all schools or religious institutions and daycare facilities in the Institutional and Professional zoning districts. The current requirements for after school programs eliminate the ability for other types of facilities, such as a part-time childcare facility located within shopping centers, to be permitted under the city’s current ordinance, even though state law exempts such facilities from licensing requirements. It also eliminates the option as far as zoning because unless the proposed facility is in the Institutional or Professional -- 22 of 29 -- zoning districts, is an accessory use to a church or school, or is proposed to operate from a residence, the use is not allowed. To comply with how the state permits such facilities, staff would like to open the use in commercial districts as a “Part-Time Childcare Facility”. Even though such a facility would be considered “legally exempt”, the owner or operator of these facilities would still be required to apply for legally exempt status, meaning it would be determined by the state whether the facility is legally exempt, and this status would be required to be provided prior to the issuance of any city business license. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 23 of 29 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 2 – Definitions Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended August 19, 2024 Article 2. Oak Tree Farm, Phase 3 - Letter of Credit extension / renewal. Hucks stated the Technical Review Committee originally approved plans for this development in 2019. Since that time, the project has been divided into 3 phases, in order to facilitate the development of the project, due to funding. Oak Tree Farm is an affordable housing community designed for individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. The project includes a total of 7 buildings, and 68 residential units. The project also includes a life skills center (with amenity center), a swimming pool and an on-site laundry facility. This letter of credit is to cover any remaining required infrastructure in Oak Tree Farm Phase 3, which in this instance includes remaining landscaping improvements and sidewalk/concrete finishing and is set to expire on February 8, 2025. Staff recommends extending the letter of credit for one more year in the original amount of $124,973.75 by SOS Health Care, LLC to financially guarantee the installation of the remaining required infrastructure. Anderson made a motion to approve the request as presented. Bryson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. Woodside Crossing, Phase 1 - Letter of Credit extension / renewal. PC 2/6/2025 Hucks stated the letter of credit to cover any remaining infrastructure requirements for Phase 1 of Woodside Crossing include: concrete curb and gutter, roadway improvements, concrete sidewalk, landscaping and irrigation, street trees, amenity center (clubhouse and swimming pool amenity), and pond fountains, is set to expire on March 1, 2025, The amount of the current letter of credit is $1,719,067.00 and is from Conway National Bank, letter of credit number 3457. The reduced letter of credit amount is $1,468,647.00. Staff recommends extending the letter of credit for one more year, at the requested reduced amount of $1,468,647.00. Sligh made a motion to approve the request as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. WITHDRAWN...... Hucks gave the board an overview of the request, stating the applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in late December 2024. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Low/Medium- Density Residential. The property is currently vacant. The proposed use of the property has not been disclosed by the applicant; however, the applicant is requesting to rezone the property to the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Per Section 3.2.9 of the UDO, the NC district is intended to provide small scale retail and service uses for nearby residential areas. Dimensional requirements and design standards of the NC district are intended to promote compatibility to surrounding residential areas and accommodate pedestrian use and access. Strip commercial development, designed primarily to accommodate vehicular access and parking, and development that is insensitive or incompatible with the scale and character of the surrounding residential areas, is discouraged in this district. A portion of the property abuts property zoned Highway Commercial (HC) and abuts property zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential on one side that is used commercially (was occupied by a cosmetology school at one time) and the other side is also zoned R-1 but currently vacant. Behind the property is a split- zoned parcel, zoned R-1 and HC, with the frontage of that property being on Elizabeth Street. There is also a 10-ft construction easement that runs along one side of the subject property that appears to have been created when additional right-of-way was deeded to SCDOT in 2007. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Neighborhood Commercial. The term "childcare facility" does not include facilities that operate for more than 4 hours a day in connection with a shopping center or similar facility, where the same children are cared for less than 4 hours a day AND not on a regular basis. These facilities cater to children whose parents or custodians are occupied on the premises or in the immediate vicinity and are immediately available. These types of facilities must meet local fire and sanitation requirements and maintain documentation of these requirements on file, accessible for public inspection. After school programs are also permitted as an accessory use to all schools or religious institutions and daycare facilities in the Institutional and Professional zoning districts. Amendment(s) to Article 10 – Subdivision and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to the requirements for Conservation Subdivisions. Hucks stated that the conservation subdivision design is part of Article 10 of the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). This section of Article 10, along with open space requirements, was pulled from an overall cleanup of Article 10 that was recently adopted by Council, due to the comprehensive nature of the proposed amendments. A conservation subdivision design offers a flexible, cluster-style development that incentivizes eco-conscious design and preserves areas of environmental and historical value. This approach maintains the prorated density of residential units for the overall site while minimizing the impact on surrounding communities. Houses or lots in a conservation subdivision are typically located closer together, rather than spread throughout the development acreage. This results in higher density in one or more parts of the property while preserving larger portions of land. Additionally, conservation subdivisions generally have fewer environmental impacts than traditional developments, including reduced disturbed areas, minimized stormwater runoff, and less impervious surface. There are also economic benefits to conservation subdivisions, including higher property values, reduced maintenance costs, and lower stormwater management expenses. Current and former staff have advocated for the use of conservation subdivision design. The Council has previously approved amendments to the UDO concerning conservation subdivisions. This includes a requirement for proposed developments on parcels exceeding 50 acres to submit a site plan for a conservation subdivision alongside the preliminary development plans. This enables staff to assess whether a conservation subdivision design is appropriate for the proposed site. The first development that was approved as a conservation subdivision is Collins Jollie, a multi-neighborhood design containing several tracts being developed by different owners or builders. During the plan review process, staff discovered that although multi-neighborhood designs are allowed, the requirement for all conservation and open space areas to be platted and recorded simultaneously remained unchanged. This requirement applied regardless of whether all tracts were at the stage where final plats to create lots could be approved or not. The solution to this issue was a development agreement. The sole purpose of this agreement was to allow each tract to record the open space and conservation areas separately, provided that these areas coincided with wetlands delineated on a recent survey and aligned with the approved master plan. This amendment seeks to remedy this issue so that the requirements apply regardless of whether a multi- neighborhood or single-neighborhood design is proposed. -- 6 of 128 -- PC 12/12/2024 5 Other amendments, aside from reorganization of the requirements, include detailing what areas qualify for conservation areas, how maximum density is to be calculated, what areas may not count towards the net buildable area, the requirements for a Master Plan to be submitted, clarification on perimeter buffers and screening requirements, as well as appropriate instruments for the permanent protection of open space. This includes the requirement for such areas to be platted as a conservation easement either before or with the final subdivision plat. The city has seen an increase in the number of conservation subdivisions being proposed, with three different approved plans and two others currently being reviewed. In total, there are currently 1,766 lots or units proposed within conservation subdivisions. The proposed amendments will provide needed clarification and better guidance to applicants and staff when considering a conservation subdivision design. Hucks stated that several properties along Hwy 378 and Dunn Shortcut Rd have been annexed over the past couple of years. Notably, there have been two annexations in close proximity to the Conway-Horry County Airport. One of these annexations encompasses several hundred acres proposed for both commercial and residential development, known as the Brookhaven Planned Development. South Carolina Code of Laws requires the local governmental body or agency receiving requests for a planned development, plat approval or a building permit that is within an airport safety zone to provide the information to the division of airports for review. This was done last year with regard to the Brookhaven Planned Development in accordance with South Carolina code. There were no specific comments provided back to staff regarding the annexation request; however, the county attorney at the time recommended that the city defer to the county’s Airport Environs overlay in the county zoning ordinance. He also advised that a large national flight school associated with the Myrtle Beach airport's east coast campus has begun operations, and that there would likely be an increase in operations at the Conway airport. In general, development resulting in any density of significance near the ends of runways is generally discouraged. South Carolina Aeronautics Commission requires that developers submit an Obstacle Evaluation / Airport Airspace Analysis Form to the FAA. Once the developer receives the results of the analysis of the FAA, the findings should be submitted to the Local Permitting Authority, in this case – the city, in conjunction with their plan or permit submittals. From there, the appropriate city department, which could include Planning as well as Construction Services, would be required to submit a case to SCAC for further evaluation. The goal of this overlay is to provide a layer on the city’s GIS maps for current and future staff. When annexation requests, rezoning requests, plan submittals, or permit applications are received, staff can easily identify properties located within the overlay and determine when appropriate notifications are required. This overlay is not intended to provide decisions on whether specific developments or permits can be approved. Therefore, unlike the county’s airport environs overlay, no specific requirements are included; only the process for notification by developers and staff. This amendment will also define the overlay, provide a map of the overlay, outline the proper review authority and information relating to the Airport Approach Zones identified by the South Carolina Aeronautics Commission’s Compatible Land Use Evaluation Tool (CLUE) Analysis. BACKGROUND: The applicant submitted a rezoning application for the subject property in December 2024. The property is already in the city limits, zoned Light Industrial (LI). The property is currently owned by UFP Real Estate, LLC. The current use / business on the subject property is UFP Mid-Atlantic, LLC, a building materials supplier (i.e. roof trusses, etc.). The use of the property is split onto 2 separate properties, which are zoned differently. The larger property that contains the main building (not part of the request) is zoned Heavy Industrial (HI). The other property, which is proposed to be rezoned, is currently zoned Light Industrial (LI). The applicant wishes to combine the properties but because they are zoned differently, one of the properties must be rezoned to have the same zoning as the other property it’s proposed to be combined with. For Council’s knowledge, the existing use can be permitted in either the Light or Heavy Industrial districts. However, the other property is not part of the application and cannot be considered with this request. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: Adjacent properties in the city limits are zoned Heavy Industrial (HI), Professional (P) – which includes the city fire station and a dentist office, and Highway Commercial (HC), which includes the Food Lion shopping center. Property abutting the subject property is in the county’s jurisdiction, zoned Heavy Industrial (HI); however, there is no known use or structure on the property zoned HI in the county. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies the property as being industrial. Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the Light Industrial (LI) district is to provide areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely affected. Per Section 3.2.14 of the UDO, the intent of the Heavy Industrial (HI) district is to accommodate areas for heavy manufacturing, distribution and processing. ISSUE: Previously Deferred …Request of amendments to Article 11 – Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for signs. BACKGROUND: Since early 2023, city staff has been going through the UDO to identify inconsistencies, typos, and other items that may be lacking within each Article of the UDO. The sign ordinance, although amended a few times through the years, has not had a comprehensive review of all sign requirements, and as part of the city’s UDO cleanup effort, staff is seeking to amend Article 11 to address several issues that have been identified through the years and/or that have caused confusion amongst staff and the sign community, as well as different interpretations. Some of the amendments include, but are not limited to: • Revisions to requirements for signage in residential zoning districts; • Addition of murals to signage that is considered to be exempt from permitting procedures, provided that it does not contain text or images that identify the business or business product(s); • Clarification of number of wall signs permitted on corner buildings or lots; • Removal of balloons as being ‘prohibited’ signage; • Revisions to requirements for EMC/LED signs – regarding distance to residential structures or properties; • Minor revisions to design requirements for monument signs (deletion of repetitive language); • Revisions to requirements for drive-thru signs (i.e. menu panel options); and • Housekeeping revisions to sign permit requirements RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that Planning Commission conduct a thorough review of the proposed amendments to Article 11 and make an informed recommendation to City Council. -- 55 of 128 -- City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance Article 11 – Signage 11-1 Adopted December 12, 2011 Last Amended XXXX Article 11. ISSUE: Amendments to Article 9 – Landscaping and Buffering, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding Landscape, Buffer, and Tree Preservation requirements. BACKGROUND: Staff is proposing an amendment to Article 9 that would allow for a more clarification on commonly misinterpreted aspects of the Tree Preservation Ordinance, penalties for violations of the ordinance, as well as a more appropriate course of action for Tree Board appeals, as well as other minor amendments to the landscaping requirements; part of the ongoing effort to cleanup articles of the UDO. Amendments include (but are not limited to) the following: 1. Codify the Tree Preservation Ordinance into the UDO. Then the Tree Ordinance falls under the purview of the Planning & Development Dept. 2. Designate that the Community Appearance Board (CAB) will continue to act as the Tree Board; however, appeals of the decisions of the Tree Board would instead be directed to the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA). 3. Amend the Tree Preservation Ordinance, including the Appeals Section (Sec. 3-4-15 – Appeals, that directs appeals of the Tree Board to Conway City Council, to direct appeals of the Tree Board decision to Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) instead of City Council. Decisions of BZA would be appealable to circuit court. 4. Adopt an application fee ($250) for Tree Board Appeals. Staff proposes to begin charging $250 for Tree Appeal applications. Should applicants seek to appeal the decision of the Tree Board, and these requests go to BZA, the property will need to be posted, the appeal would need to be advertised, letters would need to be sent to adjacent property owners, and decisions from the BZA would need to be mailed certified to interested parties. 5. Upon the request of tree board, staff has made some housekeeping changes throughout the ordinance to ensure a more uniform and concise understanding of the processes and terminology used throughout the ordinance. These items include clarity of the process of tree mitigation, implementation of higher penalties for improper removal of protected or landmark trees, and clarification on definitions that were commonly misinterpreted. 6. Addition and deletion, upon the request of the tree board, of trees from the protected tree list. The tree board asked to remove non-native trees, Crepe Myrtle and Dawn Redwoods, from the protected list but to rather include native trees, such as a Tulip tree, Red Cedar, and a Tupelo tree. Purpose 9.1.1 Intent A. The requirement and regulation of landscaping in the City of Conway is a critical public concern. Requirements and regulations for landscaping are necessary in order to preserve and enhance the aesthetic beauty of the city and promote the safety and general welfare of its residents. More specifically, the intent of the landscape ordinance is to: 1. Provide buffering between non-compatible land uses. 2. Protect, preserve, and promote aesthetic appeal and scenic beauty. 3. Reduce noise pollution and air pollution. 4. Reduce storm water run-off. 5. Filter and reduce glare from artificial light sources. 6. Provide shaded areas along streets and in parking areas. 9.1.2 Interpretation In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this Unified Development Ordinance shall be held to be the minimum requirements necessary for the promotion and protection of the public health, safety, and aesthetic appeal of the City of Conway. This The provisions contained within this Article section shall be consistent with the City of Conway Section 9.8 – Tree Preservation, Ordinance and as well as Planting Guidelines. 9.1.3 Applicability A. Exemptions 1. Any R or R-1 zoned development shall be exempt from the buffering requirements herein. {Amended 6-15-15 #ZA2015-06-15 (D)} [Amended 12/17/18#ZA2018-12-17(A)] 2. Properties in the CBD are exempt only if property includes no off-street parking. 3. Portion of the property abutting railroad right-of-way and utility easements in excess of sixty (60) feet in width. 4. Portion of the property abutting dedicated street right-of-way which is undeveloped. B. Applicable Areas 1. New Principal Building or Use. Principal buildings or open uses of land constructed or established after the adoption of this Unified Development Ordinance. 2. Changes in Use. A change in use resulting in a completely different type of use shall be subject to the landscaping provisions in Article 9. This would include a use not found in the same general grouping. The requirements of this Article shall be applicable to the entire zoned lot. {Amended 6-15-15 #ZA2015-06-15 (D)} 3. Expansions or Reconstruction. Expansions or renovations to an existing building within a five-year period that exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the appraised value (as indicated by Horry County Tax Records). This includes all existing buildings or properties on the effective date of this Unified Development Ordinance. In such cases the landscaping requirements shall apply only to the expansion. 4. Publicly Owned Buildings.
