ISSUE: Request of amendments to Article 6 – Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) to remove El Bethel Road from the Village Corridor Overlay (VCO). BACKGROUND: The Village Corridor Overlay (VCO), per Section 3.4.3 of the UDO, is intended to promote compact, pedestrian-scale development with residential, neighborhood commercial, professional, and office uses. The VCO zoning includes properties fronting on minor arterials and collector streets designated on the city’s zoning map. The VCO extends 250 feet from the right-of-way line for properties along these streets, and any property or building that has any portion within the 250-ft overlay boundary is subject to the regulations of the VCO. Regulations within the VCO include building massing/modulation, access management, connectivity, landscaping and buffer requirements, site design and parking, and sign limitations. Currently, the following roads are subject to the requirements of the VCO: • El Bethel Rd (+/-150’ right-of-way width) • Cultra Rd (right-of-way width varies but majority is 66’) • Mill Pond Rd (right-of-way width varies from +/-80’ to +/-125’. A small portion of Mill Pond exceeds 150’ in right-of-way width) • Sixteenth Ave, between Main Street & Church St (Hwy 501) (right-of-way width varies from +/-60’ to +/-88’) • 16th Ave, between Church St (Hwy 501) & Hwy 378 (right-of-way width varies from +/-50’ to +/-80’) The El Bethel Rd right-of-way (150’) is wider than most of the other roadways within the VCO. Additionally, the landscape and character of El Bethel Rd has changed within the last few years, with several rezoning requests approved for institutional or medical uses. As such, there are some standards within the VCO that could be difficult for these types of uses to adhere to, with the potential for variances to be sought on signage, height limitation, connectivity requirements, landscaping/buffer requirements, etc. Horry County Schools applied for and was granted a variance on signage last year for the new Whittemore Park Middle School on El Bethel Rd. As such, staff proposes to amend Section 6.5.3 (B) – Applicability, of the VCO to exclude El Bethel Rd from the requirements of the VCO, therefore making the properties along El Bethel Rd subject to the standard requirements of the City’s Unified Development Ordinance. CITY COUNCIL: City Council will hear this item at their November 18, 2024 meeting and staff will forward Planning Commission’s recommendation with first reading of the proposed amendment(s). -- 25 of 41 -- Article 6. ISSUE: Request of amendments to Article 11 – Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for signs. BACKGROUND: Since early 2023, city staff has been going through the UDO to identify inconsistencies, typos, and other items that may be lacking within each Article of the UDO. The sign ordinance, although amended a few times through the years, has not had a comprehensive review of all sign requirements, and as part of our UDO cleanup effort, staff is seeking to amend Article 11 to address several issues that have been identified through the years and have caused confusion amongst staff and different interpretations. Some of the items that will be included in the amendment are in the sections listed below: • Sec. 11.1.4 – Signs in Disrepair and Unsafe Signs • Sec. 11.1.5 – Obsolete and Abandoned Signs - Language added to clarify that such signs must be removed and not be re-established • Sec. 11.1.6 – Area and Height Measurement • Sec. 11.1.8 – Illumination • Sec. 11.2.1 – Signs exempt from Permit Procedures - Added murals to the signs which are exempt from permit requirements • Sec. 11.2.2 – Prohibited Signs • Sec. 11.3.1 – Signs in Residential Zoning Districts • Sec. 11.3.2 – Signs in Non-Residential Zoning Districts • Sec. 11.4.1 – Wall Signs • Sec. 11.4.6 – Monument Signs • Sec. 11.4.7 – Freestanding Signs • Sec. 11.4.9 – Electronic Message Centers (EMC’s), Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) signs with digital/animated display - Amendment to require that such signs meet a minimum distance from existing residential structures • Sec. 11.4.16 – Drive-Thru Signs • Sec. 11.4.11 – Residential Subdivision and Multi-Family Signs • Sec. 11.5.1 – Sign Permit Requirements -- 28 of 41 -- CITY COUNCIL: City Council will hear this item along with Planning Commission’s recommendation at their November 18th meeting. No sign illumination system shall contain or utilize any beacon, spot, search or stroboscopic light, glaring light or reflector, which is visible from any public right-of-way or adjacent property, nor shall such lights be operated outside, under any circumstances, except by authorized public agencies. 18. Signs using the words “stop”, “danger” or any other word, phrase, symbol, or character in a manner that is misleading, confusing, or distracts a vehicle driver. 19. No sign shall display lights resembling by color and design or other characteristics customarily associated with danger or those used by police, fire, ambulance and other emergency vehicles or for navigation. Automotive warning or flashing signs shall not be utilized as commercial attention-seizing devices. 20. Any sign erected, altered, displayed, or changed without approval from the Planning Department, and a sign permit from the Building Department. 21. Any other type or kind of sign which does not comply with the terms, conditions, and provisions contained in this Article. -- 33 of 41 -- 22. Any sign considered to be an off-premises sign. Section 11.3 – Sign Standards by Zoning Districts 11.3.1 Signs in Residential Zoning Districts A. Signs Permitted in Residential Zoning Districts: See Section 11.4 for specific requirements. Additionally, some Conditional Uses in Article 5 include specific requirements for signage. B. Residential Subdivision and Multifamily Unit Signs: See Section 11.4.11. C. Religious Institutions, Educational Facilities, Cemeteries, Country Clubs, Parks, and Similar Recreational Uses located in residential districts: Shall be permitted one (1) wall sign or one (1) freestanding sign per street frontage. This shall not exceed a cumulative sign surface area of fifty (50) square feet. 1. Size a. Wall sign(s) and/or freestanding post sign(s) shall not exceed a sign surface area of fifty (50) square feet. The freestanding sign shall be a monument or freestanding post type and shall not exceed six (6) feet in height. b. Portions of signs containing an LED / EMC shall not exceed thirty-two (32) square feet sign surface area. 2. Illumination Requirements a. Such signs may be illuminated by any means consistent with Section 11.1.8. b. If signs with EMC’s/LED’s and/or digital display is desired, such signs shall comply with Section 11.4.9. Signs containing EMC’s / LEDs shall also comply with the illumination requirements in Section 11.4.9. 3. Setbacks a. Such signs, other than signs which contain and EMC / LED, shall be located a minimum of ten (10) feet from any adjoining property boundary. b. All signs containing EMCs / LEDs shall be located a minimum of 100 feet from any residentially zoned property and/or from an existing residential structure. [ZA2023-11-06(B)] 11.3.2 Signs in Non-Residential Zoning Districts A. Signs Permitted in Non-Residential Zoning Districts: See Section 11.4 for specific requirements. Some Conditional Uses in Article 5 also include specific requirements for signage. Additionally, some Conditional Uses in Article 5 include specific requirements for signage. B. Religious Institutions, Educational Facilities, Cemeteries, Country Clubs, Parks, and Similar Recreational Uses: See Section 11.4 for specific dimensions of signs permitted in non-residential districts. Section 11.4 – Sign Standards by Sign Type 11.4.1 Wall Signs Wall signs include most types of signage that are attached to the face of a building wall. These include channel letters made out of wood, metal or plastic. Wall signs may be painted on a wall, or on a board that is attached to a wall. Wall signs should be oriented to achieve balanced composition and harmony with other architectural elements of a building façade. Wall signs should be -- 34 of 41 -- placed on a flat building surface and should not be placed over or otherwise obscure architectural building features. Changeable copy signs are not permitted as a wall sign, except for cinemas, theaters, and auditoriums. A. Location and Number Permitted Only one wall sign per tenant will be allowed and it shall be located at the Public Entrance. A second wall sign will be allowed on a different facade if the building is located on a corner lot, installed on another facade or if there is a second public entrance. The maximum number of wall signs permitted is two (2) per tenant space. B. Size Wall signs may be a maximum of 15% of the building face where the sign is attached. The changeable copy if included in wall signs shall be limited to six (6) square feet. C. Illumination Wall signs may be illuminated by any means consistent with Section 11.1.8. D. Zoning Wall signs are allowed in all zoning districts. 11.4.6 Monument Signs Monument signs have a solid base that the sign face is installed upon. These signs should be designed so that the style of the sign and its base are consistent with the architecture of the buildings on the site. They are typically oriented perpendicular to the adjacent street and sidewalk and have a maximum of two parallel sign faces. Monument signs provide opportunities for landscaping to enhance their appearance. A. Location and Number Permitted Monument signs may be located in required street yards for any given zoning district. Only one monument sign is permitted per lot unless the lot has more than one street frontage. One additional sign (i.e. monument or other freestanding sign) may be approved if there are multiple street frontages. B. Size 1. P, NC, CC, CBD, MU and WRD Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be twenty-four (24) square feet for a single tenant. Where there are three (3) or more tenants, the maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be forty (40) square feet. 2. IN, CP, and FA Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be forty (40) square feet. 3. HC, LI, and HI Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be ten (10) feet, and the maximum area shall be sixty (60) square feet for a single tenant. Where there are three (3) or more tenants, the maximum height shall be ten (10) feet, and the maximum area shall be eight (80) square feet. 4. Overlay Districts: If located within an Overlay District, the sign standards of that district apply. C. Illumination If illumination of monument signs is desired, then external illumination or halo lighting is preferred. Internally illuminated cabinet signs must have a dark background with light lettering, per requirements set forth in Section 11.1.8. -- 35 of 41 -- D. Zoning Monument signs are permitted in all zoning districts throughout the City of Conway. E. Design Monument signs shall conform to the following standards: 1. All support structures, poles, and wiring related to a monument sign shall be enclosed within the base or sign face of said monument sign so that they are not visible. 2. The color of the base and the materials enclosing the base of a monument sign shall be consistent with the exterior color and materials of the building(s) on the property. 3. Monument signs having a base greater than 18-inches in height shall have a base that is constructed of the same materials and incorporates the same colors as the principle structure(s) on the property. Monument sign bases that are 18-inches or less in height may have a base constructed of the same material as the exterior of the sign cabinet. 4. Landscaping shall be installed around the base of the monument sign, in accordance with Section 9.3.8. 5. For any monument sign request in the HC, LI, or HI Zoning Districts, the TRC can consider reducing the street yard and sign landscaping requirements. 11.4.7 Freestanding Post Signs Freestanding post signs are similar to monument signs, except they do not have a base other than the support posts. The colors and materials used for the sign must be compatible with the associated building design. Lettering should be carved, routed or applied as opposed to painted on a flat board. A. Location and Number Freestanding post signs may be located in required street yards for any given zone. Only one freestanding post sign is permitted per lot unless the lot has more than one street frontage. One additional sign (i.e. monument or other freestanding sign) may be approved if there are multiple street frontages. B. Size 1. P, NC, CC, CBD, and WRD Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be twenty-four (24) square feet for a single tenant. Where there are three (3) or more tenants, the maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be forty (40) square feet. 2. IN, CP, and FA Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum area shall be forty (40) square feet. 3. HC, LI, and HI Zoning Districts: The maximum height shall be sixteen (16) feet, and the maximum area shall be sixty (60) square feet for a single tenant. Where there are three (3) or more tenants, the maximum height shall be twenty (20) feet, and the maximum area shall be eight (80) square feet. 4. Overlay Districts: If located within an Overlay District, the sign standards of that district apply. C. Illumination Freestanding post signs may be illuminated by any means consistent with Section 11.1.8. D. Zoning Freestanding post signs are allowed in all zoning districts. -- 36 of 41 -- E. Landscaping Landscaping shall be installed around the base of the Freestanding Post Sign, in accordance with Section 9.3.8. 11.4.9 Electronic Message Centers (EMC’s)/Light Emitting Diodes (L.E.D.) Signs with Digital/Animated Display Electronic message centers (EMCs) and L.E.D. digital signs come in different shapes and sizes and typically have informational messages. Messages shall not be intended to, nor shall they distract oncoming traffic. Should the Planning Department determine that the signage is distracting, the signage must be altered to remove the offending message or shall be in violation of this section. This section does not apply to Time and Temperature Signs (Section 11.4.12) or Gasoline Pricing Signs (Section 11.4.13). [ZA2019-03-18 (C)] A. Location and Number One (1) EMC / LED is permitted per parcel. B. Size The size of the EMC / LED shall be no greater than the sign area allotted by the sign type, as provided for in Section 11.4. C. Illumination 1. The EMC / LED shall not exceed 5,000 nits from sunrise to sunset, and it shall not exceed 500 nits from sunset to sunrise. 2. All EMCs / LEDs shall be equipped with a sensor or other auto-dimming technology that automatically determines the ambient illumination and programmed to automatically dim according to the requirements in this section. a. EMC’s/LEDs shall not exceed 0.3 footcandles over ambient lighting conditions when measured at the recommended distance, based on the EMC size. 3. Before issuing a Zoning Compliance/Permit, the sign company and/or applicant shall certify the illumination specifications for the proposed EMC / LED. D. Zoning Electronic Message Centers (EMC’s) or L.E.D. (Light Emitting Diode) signs with digital or animated displays are permitted as follows: 1. IN, IC and HC Zoning Districts. EMC’s / L.E.D. signs with digital/animated displays are permitted in the IN, IC, and HC zoning districts, and on properties zoned HC that are located on US HWY 501 Bypass, to include “Church Street.” 2. Theaters. Theaters, including buildings or structures (i.e. auditorium) that is designed for, permitted, and is intended for such use, and which contains audience seating, one or more screens and/or stage, and a lobby, for the purpose of showing motion pictures, performing live music, live plays, or other performance art(s), that is located outside of an HDRD, shall be permitted one (1) EMC / LED sign with digital/animated display. a. Theaters must be located on parcels that are zoned for such use. b. Theaters shall not include any adult entertainment uses as outlined in Section 5.1.1. c. Historic Design Review Districts (HDRD’s). Theaters located on properties within a HDRD shall be reviewed by the Community Appearance Board (CAB) for consideration of the installation of an EMC / LED sign digital/animated display. 3. Educational Facilities/Religious Institutions, as defined in Article 2 – Definitions, shall be permitted one (1) EMC / L.E.D. sign with digital/animated display, in compliance with the standards contained herein. -- 37 of 41 -- a. In addition to these standards, signage for educational facilities and religious institutions located in residential zoning districts shall adhere to the conditions in Section 11.3.1. 4. Public Recreational Facilities, as specified in Article 4 – Use Tables, shall be permitted one (1) EMC / L.E.D. sign with digital/animated display, in compliance with the standards contained herein. E. Setbacks from Residential. 1. All signs containing EMCs / LEDs shall be located a minimum of 100 feet from any residentially zoned property and/or from an existing residential structure. F. Additional Conditions 1. EMCs / LEDs shall only be incorporated into monument signs only. EMCs / LEDs are not permitted on buildings as wall signs. a. Theaters, as defined herein, shall be permitted to have EMCs/LEDs with digital / animated displays incorporated into wall signs. 2. The EMC / LED shall have a mechanism to turn it off if a malfunction occurs. 3. The displaying of videos shall be prohibited. 4. No audio speakers or any form of pyrotechnics shall be permitted. 5. EMCs / LEDs shall not change or alternate displays (words, symbols, figures or images) more frequently than once every fifteen (15) seconds, except that digital changeable copy signs may change or alternate displays as frequently as once every eight (8) seconds if: a. The sign displays public service announcements on a permanent basis once every sixty (60) second period; and, b. The sign operator displays as part of the normal advertising rotation, public emergency messages, hereinafter defined until such time as such message is no longer reasonably necessary. “Public emergency messages” shall mean: Amber Alert emergency information and information about terrorist attacks, natural disasters, public infrastructure failures and public safety emergencies. Public emergency messages shall be displayed in accordance with protocols developed by the City in conjunction with the issuing agencies and the qualified sign owners. For the purposes of this section, a public service announcement shall be any announcement for which no charge is made, and which promotes programs, activities, or services of federal, state or local governments or the programs, activities or services of non- profit organizations and other announcements regarded as serving community interests, excluding time signals, routine weather announcements and promotional announcements. 6. The images and messages displayed shall be complete in themselves, without continuation in content to the next message or image, or to any other sign. 7. The display shall not be configured to resemble a warning, danger signal, official signage used to control traffic, or to cause a viewer to mistake the sign for a warning or danger signal. [ZA2012-11-05 (A); ZA2016-08-01 (E); ZA2019-03-18 (C); ZA2023-06-05 (C); ZA2023-11-06(B)] 11.4.16 Drive-Thru Signs -- 38 of 41 -- Drive-Thru Signs are permitted for establishments that have an approved drive-thru. The color of such signs shall be similar to the main building or other signage for the development. A. Location and Number Drive-Thru signs may be free standing or may be fixed on an exterior wall if the building has no setback. Free standing drive-thru signs may include a clearance bar as well as a drive thru order canopy. B. Size 1. Drive-Thru Menu Panel signs a. Freestanding menu panel signs: on posts may shall be no larger than fifteen (15) twenty-four (24) square feet in area and six (6) feet in height. b. Menu panel signs affixed to wall: If located on a wall, the maximum size is ten (10) square feet in area. This does count on overall required signage. 2. Drive-Thru Canopies (ie. Clearance, Double Lanes, Business Name): shall be no larger than five (5) square feet in area and eleven (11) feet in height. This does count on overall required signage. C. Illumination Drive-Thru signs may be illuminated by any means consistent with Section 11.1.8 of this Article. D. Zoning Drive-Thru signs are allowed in all zoning districts where a drive-thru is permitted. 11.4.17 Shopping Center Identification Signs The purpose of shopping center identification signs is to identify the name of a shopping center as well as the tenants within the shopping center. Shopping center identification signs may consist of free standing or monument and must be compatible with the associated building design as specified in Section 6.3.1, Non-Residential Architectural Design Standards. The following standards apply to shopping centers only as defined in Article 2. All signs are subject to approval by Planning Department. A. Location and Number Sign(s) may be located in required buffer for any given zone, subject to the approval of the Planning Department and consistent with Section 11.1.7, Setbacks. One (1) shopping center identification sign may be permitted per major entrance as determined by the Planning Department. Individual tenants within shopping centers are permitted wall signage consistent with Section 11.4.1, Wall Signs. B. Size -- 39 of 41 -- 1. Freestanding post signs used to identify shopping centers shall have a maximum height of twenty-five feet (25) feet, and maximum sign area of three hundred (300) square feet. Monument-style signs used to identify shopping centers shall have a maximum height of twenty (20) feet and a maximum sign area of two hundred (200) square feet. 2. The sign area identifying the name of the shopping center shall not exceed 50 100 square feet (i.e. Coastal Mall, Bay Village, etc.) and does not apply to any wall signs used to identify the shopping center, which must be consistent with Section 11.4.1 regarding wall signs. 3. Individual tenant panels located on freestanding or monument signs shall not exceed 100 square feet and must be consistent with Section 11.3.1: Sign Standards by Zoning District; Table 11.1: Sign Standards by District. Tenant wall signs may be 15% of the wall façade where the sign will be affixed or 100 square feet, whichever is less, consistent with Section 11.4.1. 4. Sign structure design and size must be incorporated into the overall site development plans and approved by the TRC and/or Planning Department. C. Zoning Shopping center identification signs are permitted only in districts where shopping centers are allowed, per Article 4: Use Tables. Electronic Message Centers (EMCs) and/or LEDs may be utilized provided that the EMC/LED is consistent with the requirements in Section 11.4.9, Electronic Message Centers (EMCs)/Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) Signs with Digital/Animated Display and is located in a permissible location. If an Electronic Message Center is utilized it shall not exceed one hundred (100) square feet. Maximum one (1) per shopping center. D. Illumination Shopping Center Identification signage may be illuminated consistent with Section 11.1.8. Internally illuminated cabinet signs must have a dark background with light lettering, per requirements set forth in Section 11.1.8, 9. E. Additional Conditions 1. Landscaping for shopping center identification signs shall conform to Section 9.3.8. 2. Monument signs shall be consistent with the requirements of Section 11.4.6 (E) regarding sign design. [ZA2016-08-15 (A)] Section 11.5 – Sign Permits 11.5.1 Sign Permit Requirements A. Sign Permits Required: Unless otherwise provided for in this Article, no sign or sign structure, shall be erected, replaced, relocated, constructed, changed, or altered until such sign has been approved by the Planning Department and a permit has been issued by the Building Construction Services Department. B. Permit Applications: A City of Conway Sign Permit Application shall be submitted for a permit to erect, alter, or relocate any sign which requires a building permit. shall be made to the Planning Department upon a form provided by the Planning Department. The following information must be submitted via the City of Conway online portal at www.ConwaySC.gov: and shall include the following information: 1. Name, address, telephone number, and signature of the owner of premises (and occupant if different) granting permission for the construction, maintenance of, or display of the proposed signage. 2. Name, address, telephone number, and signature of sign contractor, if any. 3. The approximate value of the sign to be installed, including the installation cost. -- 40 of 41 -- 4. A site plan of the proposed signage drawn to scale, showing elevations of the sign as proposed on the building facade, awning, or canopy. In the case of a freestanding sign, a site plan of the property drawn to scale illustrating the proposed location of the sign. 5. Specifications and scaled drawings showing the materials, design, dimensions, structural supports, and electrical components of the proposed sign. 6. Any other information, specifications, photographs, or the like deemed necessary by the Planning Department in order to assure compliance with requirements set forth herein. C. Community Appearance Board (CAB): CAB review and approval is required if the property is located in a Historic Design Review District. D. Upon compliance with the requirements set forth herein, the Planning Department shall approve the application for a sign and forward the necessary information to the Building Construction Services Department where a permit may be issued. E. Failure to obtain a final satisfactory inspection within the permit period shall render the permit invalid and the applicant shall be required to reapply for a permit or remove the sign and sign structure. F. The Building Construction Services Department may make or require any inspections of any construction work to ascertain compliance with the provisions of this Ordinance and other laws which are in force and to ascertain that the sign is erected or displayed as indicated on the approved sign permit application. [ZA2021-08-16(C)] -- 41 of 41 --

title: APPD-11.7.24 PC MINUTES
text: PC 11/7/2024 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 7, 2024 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Kendall Brown, George Ulrich, Thomas J. Anderson III, David Sligh, Greg Bryson Absent: Danny Hardee, Ellen Watkins Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Brent Gerald, Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT; Anne Bessant, Planning & Development Coordinator; Marsha Ponder, Planning & Development Assistant Others: John Richards CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Anderson to approve the October 3, 2024 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. SUBDIVISIONS A. Maple Grove Subdivision, Phase 1, 2 &3 — The applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval for Phases 1, 2 & 3 of the Maple Grove subdivision, located on Collins Jollie Rd (PIN 295-00-00- 0037). Hucks stated that Maple Grove is one of the developments within the Collins Jollie Conservation Subdivision, located on Collins Jollie Rd. There are a total of 10 phases within the development, and the applicant is requesting preliminary plan approval for the first 3 phases, which contains a total of 176 lots — 53 in phase 1, 60 in phase 2 and 63 in phase 3. The master plan, street names and design modifications were approved by Planning Commission in March of this year. If approved, staff recommends that it be contingent upon final review and approval of the Technical Review Committee. John Richards, Thomas & Hutton, was present to answer any questions. The board, applicant, and staff discussed the request at length. Wise made a motion to approve the request as presented pending any further TRC review comments. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 1 PC 11/7/2024 B. Rivertown Row North, Phase J — Letter of Credit extension / renewal. Hucks stated that Phase 1 of Rivertown Row North contains 108 lots. The original letter of credit was approved in November 2022 for $1,249,500. The ordinance allows staff to renew and if necessary, reduce the original letter of credit amount the first time it is set to mature, which was done in 2023 for an additional year and reduced to $636 thousand. Ifthe letter of credit is to be extended for an additional year, Planning Commission must approve the extension along with the amount. 71 lots within Phase | are either vacant or currently under construction. Remaining work and infrastructure include sidewalks and street trees for the remaining lots, as well as landscaping, fencing, the surface layer of asphalt for the roads in Phase | and a percentage of the amenity center. The applicant is seeking to reduce the letter of credit to $430,999. Staff has performed a site visit and TRC has approved the proposed reduction. The applicant was not present. Sligh made a motion to approve the request as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 0.80+/- total acres of property located at 2689, 2691, 2693, 2695, 2697 and 2699 Oak Street (PIN 325-15-01-0010), and rezone from the Horry County Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district to the City of Conway Neighborhood Commercial (NC) district. Hucks gave the board an overview of the request, stating that the applicant has applied for annexation of the subject property as a requirement to connect to city utilities. There has been a restrictive covenant on file since 2009. When the property transferred to the current owner of the property, Summit Fuels, LLC in September of this year, and then application for a new utility account in the new owner’s name was made, the requirement to annex was triggered. The property contains two structures; one of which is the primary structure that includes several tenant spaces; the primary one being the gas station/convenience store. The smaller tenant spaces fronting on Oak Street include a pet grooming business, a restaurant, and the smaller structure in the rear of the property is used for storage. The property is currently zoned Horry County Neighborhood Commercial, and the City’s future land use map also identifies the property as neighborhood commercial. While the property is within the city’s utility service area and is identified on the future land use map, there are concerns that were noted by the city’s technical review committee regarding the annexation of this property, including a high call volume for the police dept., reoccurring violations related to business license and zoning — such as illegal vending, signage, and yard sales, and property maintenance violations. Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. PC 11/7/2024 The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. After much discussion, Bryson made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. TEXT AMENDMENT(S) 1. DEFFERED...Amendment(s) to Article 10 — Subdivision and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to the requirements for Conservation Subdivisions. 2. DEFERRED...Amendment(s) to Article 2— Definitions, Article 3— Zoning Districts, and Article 4 — Use Tables, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to various items within the Articles of the UDO. The above items were deferred. 3. Amendment(s) to Article 6 — Design Standards, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), to remove EI Bethel Road from the Village Corridor Overlay (VCO). Hucks stated the Village Corridor Overlay is intended to promote compact, pedestrian scale development with residential, neighborhood commercial, and professional uses. The current overlay includes properties with frontage along minor arterials and collector streets per the city’s zoning map. This includes 16 Ave, between Church St & Main St, Mill Pond Rd, Cultra Rd, and El Bethel Rd. In addition to the typical zoning requirements, overlays add an additional layer of requirements for properties that are located within them. The Village Corridor Overlay include requirements for access management, connectivity, landscaping & buffer standards that could be in addition to standard landscaping requirements, and sign limitations. The character of El Bethel Road has changed over the last several years, with the rezoning of several properties to Institutional to allow for educational or medical facilities. Some of the overlay’s standards may create hardships for some of the properties yet to be developed, particularly with regard to height limitation and signage. Regardless of the zoning district, the maximum height for properties in the VCO is 40’, while the institutional zoning district allows a maximum height of 80’. Signs are limited to a size of 24 sq. ft. for a single tenant and 40 sq. ft. for a multi-tenant building. More recently, the new middle school requested and received a variance for the sign they have installed as it exceeded the square footage that was permitted — not in the zoning district or the type of sign, but due to the property being within the overlay. El Bethel Rd also has a wider right-of-way than other streets that are within the Village Corridor Overlay, with a right-of-way width of 150-ft. With the addition of the perimeter road, once completed, it will be a heavier traveled road for vehicles and tractor trailers to get from 701 north or west of Conway to 701 South and Hwy 501 bypass. At that point, it could be considered more of a gateway corridor. 3 VI. Vi. PC 11/7/2024 Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously, Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 4. Amendments to Article 11 — Signage, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding general provisions, exempt and prohibited signs, sign standards by zoning district and sign type, and applications and permits for signs. Hucks stated that the sign ordinance has been amended a few times over the years, and more recently, amendments to the EMC / LED section of the ordinance. However, Article 11 has not had a comprehensive review like other Articles of the UDO, and it remains to be one of the most misinterpreted ordinances, or that has different interpretations for the same requirements. Most of the variance requests that staff receives is for setback requirements and signage, and sign standards tend to be the most violated of all zoning requirements. Some of the items that are proposed to be amended include adding language to clarify standards for signs in disrepair, unsafe, obsolete and abandoned signs, making it clear that any sign deemed to be obsolete or abandoned cannot be re-established or reused and must be removed from the property in its entirety, adding murals to the list of signs that are exempt from permitting procedures, clarifying requirements for signs in residential zoning districts, standards for wall signs — particularly with regard to where a second wall sign is permitted if the property or building is located on a corner lot, as well as adding a minimum separation for EMCI/LED signs from residentially zoned properties and/or structures, and several other housekeeping items. Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Anderson, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to defer the request until the next meeting to give staff time to revise the amendment relating to distances from EMC signs to residential properties/structures. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. DISCUSSION ITEMS None. BOARD INPUT Wise thanked everyone. VII. PC 11/7/2024 STAFF INPUT Hucks welcomed and introduced Marsha, the new Planning and Development Assistant. She also reminded the board that the December meeting was pushed back to the 12", due to the tree lighting ceremony and gave an overview of potential items for the upcoming meeting. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:25 pm. Approved and signed this 2 day of VCR 24. Jessica Wise, Chairperson

title: PC AGENDA 10.3.24
text: 196 Laurel Street | Post Office Box 1075 | Conway, South Carolina 29528-1075 | Telephone (843) 488-9888 | www.conwaysc.gov MAYOR Barbara Jo Blain MAYOR PRO TEM Larry A. White COUNCIL MEMBERS Amanda Butler William M. Goldfinch IV Julie Ann Hardwick Beth Helms Justin D. Jordan PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA Thursday, October 3, 2024 | 5:30 p.m. Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street I. CALL TO ORDER – 5:30 p.m. II. MINUTES A. Approval of the September 5, 2024, Planning Commission Meeting Minutes III. PUBLIC INPUT IV. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to Table…. Request to annex approximately 1.43 acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd, (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. 2. Conference Room – 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Ellen Watkins, George Ulrich, Thomas J. Anderson III, Greg Bryson, David Sligh, Danny Hardee, Kendall Brown Absent: none Staff: Jessica Hucks, Planning Director; Brent Gerald, Planner; Katie Dennis, Planner; Marcus Cohen, IT; Anne Bessant, Planning & Development Coordinator Others: Bill Taylor, Patty Taylor, Gene Johnson, Val Vaccano, Tommy Holt, Robert Smith, Rene Smith, Emma Howes, Lizzie Marlowe, Allen Springer, Angela Springer, Melissa Carr, Mary Childress, Scott Carr, Candace Klixbull, Gabe Klixbull, Lucas Klixbull, Brandon Truesdale, Shep Guyton, John Padgett, & others I. CALL TO ORDER Vice-Chairperson Wise called the meeting to order at approximately 5:30 pm. II. ELECTION OF OFFICERS Sligh made a motion to elect Wise as the Chairperson of the Planning Commission. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to elect Sligh as the Vice-Chairperson of the Planning Commission. Hardee seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. III. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich to approve the July 11, 2024 minutes with correcting the motion of item V.2. to state “the motion carried with Bryson voting no”. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. IV. PUBLIC INPUT Mary Childers, Bill Taylor, Joe Chianese, Liz Marlowe, Angela Springer, Candace Kilxbull, Lucas Kilxbull, Gabe Kilxbull, Melissa Carr, and Patty Taylor spoke in opposition of the rezoning request for Laurel Street. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. V. PUBLIC HEARINGS A. ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to annex approximately 3.02 acres of property located at 4908 Hwy 501 (PIN 399- 01-04-0010), and rezone from Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. -- 3 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 2 Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that the property has a restrictive covenant, signed in 2008, that was completed (and recorded) by the property owner in order to receive city water and/or sewer services. By signing the restrictive covenants, the property owner agreed that once the property became contiguous to the City limits, they or any future owners of the subject property would agree to petition for annexation into the City limits (per Section 5-3-150 (3) of the Code of Laws for the State of SC). The subject property became contiguous to the City limits earlier this year, and staff notified the property owner in June that annexation is now required. On August 3rd, 2024, the required signed annexation / rezoning applications were submitted. The property is currently zoned Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) and is currently the location of Lynn Ladder & Scaffolding Co. The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC), which is vacant land and Myrtle Beach International Golf Course entrance signage. Staff recommends that Planning Commission give a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Ulrich made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. REZONING REQUEST(S) Wise made a motion to combine all three rezoning requests to hear and vote as one. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.14 acres of property located at 1400 Laurel Street (portion of PIN 338-11-02-0022) from the City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district to the City of Conway Professional (P) district. 2. Request to rezone approximately 0.08 acres of property located at 1402 Laurel Street (portion of PIN 338-11-02-0023) from the City of Conway low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district to the City of Conway Professional (P) district. 3. Request to rezone approximately 0.11 acres of property located at 1404 Laurel Street (portion of PIN 338-11-02-0024) from the City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district to the City of Conway Professional (P) district. Hucks stated that the applicant is seeking to rezone these properties in order to expand the parking area of his establishment, an eye surgery center with frontage on Main Street, which directly abuts these parcels. All of the properties currently contain single-family residences. However, the applicant is proposing to demo portions of the structures that are contained on the parcels, and then subdivide a portion of them from the current property and combine with the property located at 1409 Main Street so that additional parking can be installed to accommodate his patients. The acreage contained within the request is a portion of each of the PIN numbers listed in the request. -- 4 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 3 A site plan and a survey showing the portions to be combined with PIN 338-11-02-0040 (1409 Main Street – Conway Ophthalmology Associates / Surgery Center of Conway). The site plan shows which structures on each of the residentially zoned lots are proposed to be demolished in order to accommodate the recombination of a portion of the lots into the 1409 Main Street property. Below are the amounts of each of the 3 parcels that are proposed to be combined with the Main Street property: 1400 Laurel St (PIN 338-11-02-0022): 0.14 acres (6,182 sq. ft.) 1402 Laurel St (PIN 338-11-02-0023): 0.08 acres (3,660 sq. ft.) 1404 Laurel St (PIN 338-11-02-0024): 0.11 acres (4,613 sq. ft.) Before any platting action combining a portion of these lots in the Main Street parcel could be approved, the structures that are shown to be demolished would have to be demolished and / or removed if they would otherwise encroach into property boundaries or not meet setbacks from the new property lines to be established, as nonconformities cannot be established with the creation or relocation of property lines. Properties on each side of the parcels as well as directly across from the parcels contain residential structures and uses; all zoned R-1 and identified as low/medium-density residential on the Future Land Use Map. Behind these parcels are professional/medical offices, on properties zoned Professional (P). The properties are identified as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) on the Future Land Use Map. The property that the acreage from each of the 3 parcels that is proposed to be combined with the abutting property (PIN 338-11-02-0040) is identified as Professional on the future land use map, the same as the current zoning of the property. While the requested zoning for a portion of these properties is different than what is shown on the future land use map, it is consistent with the zoning some of the surrounding properties, and if approved, the portions being rezoned will be added to property already zoned Professional. Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. Joe Chianse, Robert Smith, Bill Taylor, Angela Springer, Liz Marlowe, Patty Taylor, Mary Childers, Gene Johnson, Elvin House, & Scott Carr spoke in opposition of the request during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Sligh, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Tommy Holt, G3, Engineering, agent for owner, was present and further explained the request. The board discussed the request at length. Ulrich made a motion to recommend denial of the request to City Council, as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried, with 7 in votes in favor, and 1 abstention from Hardee. C. DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENTS 1. Amendment(s) to a previously approved land development agreement for the property known as the “Collins Jollie Conservation Subdivision”, located on Collins Jollie Rd, containing approximately 809 +/- acres, and which contains the following uses: single-family detached dwellings, single-family semi-attached dwellings (duplex) and/or single-family attached -- 5 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 4 dwellings (townhomes), as well as required Primary Conservation areas, Secondary Conservation areas, and Open Space (PINs 295-00-00-0010; 295-00-00-0035; 295-00-00- 0036; 295-00-00-0037; 295-00-00-0038; 295-00-00-0039 & 295-10-04-0001). Hucks gave an overview of the request, stating that Council approved a development agreement for the Collins Jollie Conservation Subdivision in February 2023, the sole purpose of which was to allow the master developer to record the wetlands, flood zones, and other conservation areas with each tract proposed to be developed, rather than all at one time, as the overall acreage was being developed by different entities. The conservation subdivision ordinance language currently requires that all open space and conservation areas within a conservation subdivision, regardless of whether it is a single neighborhood design or a multiple neighborhood design, be platted as an instrument of permanent protection, such as conservation easement or dedication to a third-party conservation group, prior to land disturbance. The reason being that some tracts will contain a majority of the conservation areas that are being utilized across all tracts to count towards the minimum requirements. With regard to Collins Jollie, there are at least 3 or 4 different developers involved, and whereas one developer may be ready to begin land disturbance, other developers may have just begun the plan review process and is several months away or longer from receiving approval for land disturbance; however, because of the wording of the current ordinance for a conservation subdivision, the only option is for the master developer to have the instrument of permanent protection platted across all tracts at the same time, which is why a development agreement was proposed and approved in 2023. That development agreement was never recorded, and staff realized that one of the property owners in effect at the time in which the original development agreement was proposed did not provide a signed joinder of the other owner’s form with the agreement, and since Council approved the original agreement, other tracts have been sold to the entities that will be developing them. Because of this staff felt it was necessary to take the agreement back through the process, and further, the owners have requested some revisions to language provided in the previously approved amendment. Staff has reviewed the proposed language and has sent comments back to the applicant. Two public hearings are required, and this will serve as the first of the second, with the next public hearing scheduled for the September 16th Council meeting, where final reading is also currently scheduled to occur. Staff did provide some alternative language which you have a copy of due to the concern of the timing in which the open space and conservation areas would be platted. Shep Guyton, agent, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Sligh made a motion, seconded by Wise, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the amendments to City Council as presented. Brown seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Amendment(s) to a previously approved land development agreement for the property known as “Warden Station”, a Planned Development (PD) District located at or near the corner of Pitch Landing Rd & Hwy 701 South, Kinlaw Lane & Hwy 701 South, and Pitch Landing Rd & Blaze Trail, containing approximately 1,763+/- acres, and which contains the following -- 6 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 5 uses: single-family detached dwellings, single-family semi-attached dwellings (duplex), single-family attached dwellings (townhomes), multifamily dwellings, as well as commercial and recreational uses (PINs 381-00-00-0003; 381-08-01-0006; 381-08-04-0009 and -0010; 380-00-00-0038; 403-00-00-0001, -0002, and -0022). Hucks stated that this is an amendment to a development agreement that was approved in January of this year & subsequently recorded at the Register of Deeds & comes down to one section of the agreement regarding Tree Preservation. Plans were submitted for review earlier this year for mass grading of the entire site. These plans could not be approved, in large part due to the language in the development agreement, that not only requires a tree survey to be provided for each tract within the PD at the time of plan submittal, before any land disturbance could be approved, but that the tree survey shall include any tree in excess of 6-inches in caliper. This would mean that any pine tree or other tree not protected per the city’s tree preservation ordinance would still be required to be shown on a tree survey. The applicant is seeking an amendment that specifies the more standard requirement, that a tree survey indicating the specimen, location and diameter at breast height of all protected and landmark trees, per the city’s tree preservation ordinance, to be submitted for each tract within the project at the time of plan submittal. The applicant has also included language in the revision to ensure that no land disturbance, including grading and clearing, will occur without staff approval nor without proper mitigation. Additionally, as with the current development agreement, the applicant has also agreed to be subject to the tree preservation ordinance that is in effect at the time of plan submittal. This item is also required two public hearings, this being the first and the second public hearing scheduled to occur at the September 16 th council meeting, where final reading is also scheduled to occur. Shep Guyton, agent, was present to answer any questions. There was no public input. Sligh made a motion, seconded by Wise, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Sligh made a motion to recommend approval of the amendments to City Council as presented. Anderson seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. D. TEXT AMENDMENTS 1. Previously Deferred…Amendment(s) to Article 10 – Subdivision and Land Development, of the City of Conway Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), regarding revisions to the requirements for Parks and Open Space Dedication. Hucks stated that currently, this amendment was originally discussed at the 2023 budget retreat, as a result of a park expansion plan, based on the National Recreation and Park Association guidelines for the quantities of park and recreation facilities related to population size. Staff was asked to research and come up with alternatives that would aid in expanding city park space, including through development of property that would require the dedication of open space. Two options were presented at that time: in lieu of a developer providing onsite open space, they could instead provide adequate area adjacent to the development that would be deeded to the city once improvements were installed, and the possibility of offering incentives to the developer for deeding the property to the city, such -- 7 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 6 as density bonuses. The other option was adding an additional percentage to the fee in lieu amount of open space dedication, based on the written appraisal of the property, such as an additional 25% fee on top of the appraised value, which is typically required to be based on what the value would be as if the development was completed, and all infrastructure was installed. Since then, staff had also been working on several amendments to the city’s subdivision and land development regulations in Article 10, and initially wanted to include the open space amendments within the amendment to Article 10; however, due to the complexity of the revisions to open space, staff opted to take it separately from the other amendments, which were officially adopted at the July 15 th Council meeting. A lot of the proposed amendment includes housekeeping items, but also rewording of some parts of the ordinance to provide much needed clarity with regard to open space requirements in general. Some of the more notable changes proposed include the amount of open space required, or how it's actually calculated. Currently, the amount of open space required is calculated by the number of lots, times the average household size per the latest US census, times .008, which is the recommended size of open space per person recommended by the national park service. Currently, the average household size is 2.6; or even 2.5; depending on what census source you look at, but that changes over time. It may be less the next time a census is done, or it could be more. Many places require a minimum square footage per lot or unit. The amendment before you proposes a minimum open space of 1,000 sq. ft. per lot or unit. Another area of major revisions is to the suitability section, which includes several criteria that is applicable to the different types of open space. Staff is proposing to break down each type of open space between active, passive and ancillary spaces, with suitability standards for each type. The criteria topics for each type remains the same, but what may be deemed suitable as passive open space would not be suitable for active open space, and this amendment provides clearer standards for each. Additionally, the fee-in-lieu section of the open space ordinance will be renamed Open Space Mitigation, which will include an additional option for providing open space, in that there would be a provision to allow a developer to locate the open space offsite, with certain conditions…one being that the offsite park would have to have access to external roadways AND also be accessible via pedestrian travel to the project that it will serve. It would additionally need to be deeded to the City of Conway once improvements are installed, along with a few other conditions. The appraisal requirements were also amended, which removes the different standards for PD’s as they now must meet the same standards for open space as any standard development, at a minimum, with the goal that if a PD is proposed, a better quality of open space would be provided. It also removes the ability to require a different method of determining the value of the property other than the requirement that it be performed by a licensed South Carolina Appraiser. Open space fee in lieu requests will still be required to be approved by PC and final approval by City Council. There were several other minor revisions, which were more housekeeping in nature, and some things were relocated throughout the ordinance so that it was more consistent and provided more clarity. There is one outstanding item that was not included in the amendment – regarding the additional fee on top of the appraisal value. Staff wanted to discuss it with PC because there are ultimately 2 different ways that could be calculated: -- 8 of 70 -- PC 9/5/2024 7 25% added to the property value as determined by the appraiser, or 25% added to what the fee-in-lieu amount would be, based on the property value. We thought this would be a good time to discuss the changes and go over any other revisions that PC would like to be considered, and then we could bring the amendment to you next month for a recommendation. Wise made a motion to recommend approval of the amendment to City Council as presented. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. VI. DISCUSSION ITEMS A. Tree Preservation Ordinance rewrite B. 104 Gardner Lacy Rd (annexation and rezoning) Hucks gave the board an overview of both items. VII. BOARD INPUT Wise thanked everyone and Bryson thanked Brent. VIII. STAFF INPUT None. IX. ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:45 pm. Request to annex approximately 1.43 acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd, (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. BACKGROUND: On August 27 th , the applicant went to the City’s Water Dept. to apply for water services on the subject property. The applicant was informed at that time that because the property is contiguous to property in the City limits, they would have to request annexation. Upon review of the property, staff noticed that per County land records, there were permits pending for the subject property. The only thing holding up permit issuance at that point was the requirement for the applicant to provide proof that City utilities would be connected. The permit was applied for at Horry County on February 27, 2024. The use specified on the permit was for a new auto shop. At the time the permit was applied for at the county, the subject property was NOT contiguous. However, the adjacent parcel, the Founders National Golf property, was currently going through the annexation process and had received First Reading on February 19 th . Final Reading occurred on March 18th , subsequently making this parcel contiguous to City limits. As such, staff informed the County that no permits may be issued for the property, as it would be required to be annexed before permits could be approved, which would need to be reviewed and approved by the city. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) and Horry County Limited Industrial (LI). Adjacent uses include the property containing the former entrance road for the MB National Golf Course, a gas station (fronting Hwy 501), Southern Sun Awnings, and Domino’s Pizza is located across Gardner Lacy Rd. The zoning designation applied for on the annexation and rezoning paperwork is the Highway Commercial (HC) district. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile-oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the entire parcel as Highway Commercial (HC). -- 10 of 70 -- CITY COUNCIL: City Council approved first reading of the annexation and rezoning at their September 3 rd meeting. During a workshop at their September 16th meeting, staff made council aware that the applicant has received his stormwater approval, DHEC approval and SCDOT encroachment permits, and the civil plans had already been approved through the County. If the applicant were forced to start this process over in the City’s jurisdiction, it would create an unnecessary financial hardship that may be impossible for the property owner and business owner to overcome. For this reason, staff would prefer that final reading be tabled until the county has issued the Certificate of Occupancies on the property. Council was in agreement with staff to delay final reading, which required no action from Council; it was informative only. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that Planning Commission table this request until a future meeting date in which the Certificate of Occupancy and final approvals have been issued by Horry County. Once that has occurred, staff will add the item to a future Planning Commission agenda for consideration. ISSUE: Request to amend the City’s Future Land Use Map (2019-2029) (FLUM) of the City of Conway Comprehensive Plan, relative to property located at 1926 Fulmer Street, (PIN 338-06-02-0038), consisting of approximately 0.32 acres, from the Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) zoning district to the Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. BACKGROUND: The South Carolina Planning Enabling Act of 1994 defines the Comprehensive Plan adoption process for all jurisdictions in South Carolina. This is to ensure consistency with the public hearing and revision process for Comprehensive Plans. Section 6-29-510 of the SC Code of Laws addresses re-evaluation of the Comprehensive Plan, stating that the "local planning commission shall develop and maintain a planning process which will result in the systematic preparation and continual re-evaluation and updating of those elements considered critical, necessary, and desirable to guide the development and redevelopment of its area of jurisdiction." Since updating the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan for the City in 2019, staff will occasionally review annexation and/or rezoning requests for zones that don't match the zone envisioned in the current Future Land Use Map (2019-2029). When a request is approved that is out of alignment with the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan, the map must be updated to reflect this change. In July 2021, Council passed an ordinance providing for a method by which the Comprehensive Plan, particularly the Future Land Use map, may be amended. Section 13.1.17 (E) of the UDO states that a proposed amendment to the Comprehensive Plan (the entire document or singular elements) may be initiated by the City of Conway City Council, Planning Commission, Board of Zoning Appeals, Zoning Administrator, or Planning Director. In the case of PIN 338-06-02-0038, currently zoned City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1), the city’s Future Land Use Map (2019-2029) shows the entire property as Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). The property is currently vacant and is directly behind the Rivertown Child Development Center INC LLC at 1911 N Main Street (zoned Highway Commercial-HC). The applicants would like to rezone the property with the intent to combine the parcel with the existing daycare facility property for future expansion. The applicant is requesting to rezone the subject property to the Highway Commercial (HC) district. If the rezoning is successful, any use permitted in the Highway Commercial district would be allowed on this property. There are three other properties abutting the subject property that are currently zoned Highway Commercial (HC) one fronts Sessions Street and two that front on Main Street. Directly across Fulmer Street there is a property that is currently zoned Professional (P). -- 51 of 70 -- Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. SURROUNDING USES / ZONING DISTRICTS: Surrounding properties are currently zoned R-1, HC, and P, and uses include vacant land, a gym, two existing daycare centers and a mini storage facility. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The CURRENT future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the entire parcel as being Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1). STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends that Planning Commission give a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. ISSUE: Request to rezone approximately 0.32 acres of property located at 1926 Fulmer Street, (PIN 338-06-02- 0038) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Highway Commercial (HC) district, to include a request to amend the City of Conway Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan. BACKGROUND: The applicant is seeking to rezone the subject property to the Highway Commercial district in order to expand their daycare capabilities. The daycare is directly abutting this property, and fronts on Main Street (Hwy 701 N). This request to rezone the property will be accompanied by a Future Land Use Map amendment request. The property is currently vacant and zoned Low/Medium-Density Residential (R- 1). Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile-oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. Surrounding uses/Zoning Districts: The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC), Professional (P), and Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Surrounding uses include single-family residential, a property containing a church which was rezoned to Professional a couple of years ago to allow a daycare to be established on the property, a HC property that contains a building that used to be an auto repair/garage, and also abuts the property on Main Street containing the existing daycare. CITY OF CONWAY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1). Per Section 3.2.3 of the UDO, the intent of the R-1 district is to provide for the preservation and expansion of areas for low to medium density, detached single-family residential development in the City of Conway. The district shall present a relatively spacious character, promote quiet, livable neighborhoods, and prohibit uses that are incompatible with the residential nature of the surrounding area. CITY COUNCIL: Staff presented the request to City Council during their September 16th meeting. There were concerns raised about further encroachment of commercial into the primarily residential area and whether there were more restrictive commercial zoning districts that the applicant could request that would still allow a daycare but not as of intense of uses that the HC district would permit. -- 54 of 70 -- Staff subsequently relayed the concerns to the applicant and discussed the potential of rezoning the property as well as the property that the daycare is currently located on to the Professional (P) district. Should the applicant choose to go that route, the current application would need to be revised to include the other parcel in the request. However, properties along N. Main Street are primarily zoned Highway Commercial, including the property containing the daycare facility, and the future land use map also identifies the properties along N. Main Street as Highway Commercial. Additionally, per the UDO, new construction in the Professional district is limited to a maximum building footprint of 30% of the total lot size, and no expansions of an existing building in the district shall cause the standards of the district to be exceeded (Sec. 6.3.2, A.1, 2). If there were no future expansions planned that could include an increase in the building footprint, the Professional district may be suitable to meet the needs to the applicant. If the properties are successfully rezoned to Professional, no expansions that would cause the standards within Section 6.3.2 to be exceeded would be permitted. PLANNING COMMISSION: Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. text: L IL Il. Iv. PC 10/3/2024 CITY OF CONWAY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING THURSDAY, OCTOBER 3, 2024 Planning & Building Dept. Conference Room — 196 Laurel Street Present: Jessica Wise, Ellen Watkins, George Ulrich, Thomas J. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Ulrich made a motion, seconded by Anderson to approve the September 5, 2024 minutes as written. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. PUBLIC INPUT There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. PUBLIC HEARINGS A, ANNEXATION/REZONING REQUEST(S) 1. Request to Table.... Request to annex approximately 1.43 acres of property located at 104 Gardner Lacy Rd, (PIN 399-01-04-0006), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) zoning district. Wise made a motion to table the request. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to annex approximately 20.7 acres located on Hwy 501 (PIN 326-00-00-0024) and zone from Horry County RE4 (High Bulk Retail) and Horry County CFA (Commercial Forest Agriculture) to City of Conway Light Industrial (LI). Hucks stated that PS Southeast Two LLC owns subject property on Hwy 501 near Booth Circle (formerly owned by Pinnacle Storage). The property is split-zoned, with approximately 11.8 acres, including the highway frontage, zoned Horry County RE4 (High Bulk Retail), and the remaining acreage zoned Horry County CFA (Commercial Forest Agriculture). PC 10/3/2024 The property was previously approved for 5 buildings while in the County’s Jurisdiction with the understanding that once the Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.) was complete the property would be taken forward for second reading. The first 3 buildings have been built and there are currently no active permits in review or any buildings under construction on the property. This item is being considered by Planning Commission a second time due to a change in ownership that occurred between First Reading of the annexation / rezoning in 2022, and when the C.O. was issued on the existing buildings. Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the Light Industrial (LI) district is to provide for areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan identifies a majority of the property as Low/Medium- Density Residential, and the remainder as Highway Commercial (HC). Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board discussed the request at length. Sligh made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 3. Request to annex approximately 4.50 acres of property located on Hwy 501, near Conbraco Circle (PIN 399-08-01-0001), and rezone from the Horry County Limited Industrial (LI) district to the City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC) district. Hucks stated that the subject property is currently vacant, containing two (2) ponds, and is directly adjacent to Lynn Ladder, which is currently in the process of annexation as well. The property is currently zoned Horry County Limited Industrial (LD, and the applicant is requesting the property to be zoned Highway Commercial (HC) upon annexation. Per Section 3.2.10 of the UDO, the intent of the Highway Commercial (HC) district is to provide compatible locations to serve the automobile oriented commercial activities in harmony with major highway developments, reduce traffic congestions and to enhance the aesthetic atmosphere of the City. The property abuts parcels zoned City of Conway Highway Commercial (HC), Horry County Highway Commercial and Horry County Limited Industrial (LI). The subject property is located between Lynn Ladder 2 PC 10/3/2024 & Scaffolding and PSI Molded Plastics and directly in front of the old Conbraco plant, now known as Aalberts Integrated Piping Systems. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Highway Commercial (HC). Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. The applicant was not present. Philip Bower spoke during public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Sligh made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried with Wise voting no. 4. Request to annex approximately 3.07+/- total acres of property located on Hwy 378, near Airport Rd and 3191 Hwy 378 (PINs 370-04-01-0003, -0002, and 336-13-04-0007), and rezone from the Horry County Highway Commercial (HC) district to the City of Conway Light Industrial (LD district. Hucks stated that two of the three properties under consideration for annexation are currently vacant, and one of the properties contain an HVAC business looking to expand and redevelop (the existing use) on the properties, once combined. These parcels are currently undergoing the rezoning process through Horry County, but since the properties adjacent to these parcels were annexed as the Brookhaven PD, with one of the properties at the corner of Hwy 378 and Airport Rd, these properties are now contiguous. Rather than running into a scenario where the property completes the rezoning process through the county and then upon plan submittal at the county, having to start over again through the city, the applicant is being proactive and starting the annexation process since these properties are within the city’s utility service area. The requested zoning district upon annexation is Light Industrial (LI). Per Section 3.2.13 of the UDO, the intent of the Light Industrial (LI) district is to provide for areas for light industrial uses, such as manufacturing, processing, repairing of goods, wholesaling, storage, packaging, distribution and retailing while ensuring adjacent and nearby properties are not adversely impacted. The future land use map of the Comprehensive Plan also identifies the property as Industrial, although the future land use map does not distinguish between light and heavy industrial. Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. PC 10/3/2024 David Schwerd, Diamond Shores, agent for owner, was present and further explained the request. There was no public input. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulrich, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. The board discussed the request at length. Anderson made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council, as presented. Ulrich seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. B. FUTURE LAND USE MAP AMENDMENT(S) Wise made a motion to combine items B.1 and C.1 to hear and vote as one. Sligh seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 1. Request to rezone approximately 0.14 acres of property located at 1400 Laurel Street (portion of PIN 338-11-02-0022) from the City of Conway Low/Medium Density Residential (R-1) district to the City of Conway Professional (P) district. C. Staff recommends that Planning Commission provide a thorough review of the request and make an informed recommendation to City Council. There was no public input. Watkins seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. 2. Request to rezone approximately 182+/- acres of property located on Waccamaw Drive, (PIN 382-00-00-0002) from the Low/Medium-Density Residential (R-1) district to the Conservation Preservation (CP) district. Wise made a motion, seconded by Ulirch, to close public input. Motion carried unanimously. Sligh made a motion to recommend approval of the request to City Council as presented. Ulirch seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. DISCUSSION ITEMS A. November PC items. Hucks gave the board an overview of potential items for the next two upcoming meetings. BOARD INPUT Ulrich thanked staff for all of their hard work. Wise thanked the board and the city for all the Halloween decorations. STAFF INPUT None ADJOURNMENT A motion was made to adjourn the meeting. The vote in favor was unanimous. The motion carried. The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:30 pm. Approved and signed this A day of WIKRE, 2024. Avsicalinie Jessicd Wise, Chairperson
